headings.text: Level A and AA — proposed baseline
Level AAA — select explicitly or assess as enhancements
Pointer, touch, voice, and motion input
Date, numeric, search, and input controls
Tables, grids, charts, and spatial interfaces
Mobile web, native apps, and kiosks
T04 — Mobile screen reader and touch
T06 — Text spacing and font changes
T08 — Forced colors, contrast preferences, and motion
T09 — Targets, cancellation, gestures, and dragging
T11 — Media, motion, and time limits

values: Titles identify page topic/purpose and distinguish similar pages, errors and meaningful client-side route changes.
Headings convey hierarchy and topic; visual headings expose semantics. Investigate skipped levels in context rather than treating every skip as an automatic failure.
Main content, navigation, header/footer and complementary regions are understandable in the accessibility tree; repeated region types have distinguishing labels where needed.
DOM and screen-reader order preserve meaning when flex/grid, columns, cards or responsive layouts rearrange the display.
Lists, quotations, definitions, control groups and tables expose relationships; spacing alone does not carry essential structure.
Default language and substantive language changes are identifiable programmatically; consider exceptions for names and technical terms.
Instructions such as “press the green button on the right” also identify the control without depending solely on sensory characteristics.
Meaningful pseudo-element text, icons and badges are available appropriately; decorative content does not create repetitive speech.
Hidden, collapsed, off-canvas and inert content is not misleadingly exposed or keyboard reachable; visible essential content is not hidden from AT.
Duplicate IDs and invalid relationships are investigated for actual label, state or interaction failures. Removed criterion 4.1.1 is not a WCAG 2.2 requirement.
Complete critical tasks without a pointer, including correction, cancellation and recovery controls.
Tab/Shift+Tab order preserves meaning and operability; visual rearrangement and positive tabindex do not cause disorienting jumps.
Native/custom controls activate with expected keys without duplicate submission; Space does not scroll during button activation.
Focus is visible on every interactive element in supported themes/states, including icons, inline links, embeds and shadow DOM.
Sticky bars, banners and overlays do not entirely obscure focused components at AA. Partial obscuring is an additional usability/AAA concern.
Users can leave components using a keyboard; nonstandard exit instructions are discoverable. Modal containment has a usable completion or dismissal path.
A mechanism bypasses repeated blocks. If using a skip link, verify focus visibility, destination and where subsequent keyboard navigation continues.
Focus remains meaningful after deletion, filtering, sorting, pagination, row insertion, banner dismissal and replacement of a focused element.
Dialogs, route changes and view transitions have deliberate contextual focus behavior; background updates do not repeatedly steal focus.
Single-character shortcuts can be disabled/remapped or only activate when the relevant component has focus; speech input does not trigger unwanted commands.
Link purpose is clear from text and permitted programmatic context. Repeated “read more” links are checked in context; standalone clarity is enhanced guidance.
Multiple ways to find pages in a set exist where required; document process-step/result exceptions. Repeated navigation and help remain predictably ordered.
Focus does not unexpectedly navigate, submit or open a context; input changes do not cause unannounced context changes.
Back/forward, deep links and in-page anchors preserve understandable position/state; restored focus does not land behind an overlay.
Pointer, touch, voice, and motion input
Visible label wording occurs within accessible names so voice users can target controls; hidden overrides do not replace the wording.
Pointer, touch, voice, and motion input
Multipoint/path-based gestures have a single-pointer operation without a path-based gesture unless essential; examine custom pinch and drawn gestures.
Pointer, touch, voice, and motion input
Dragging has a click/tap alternative without dragging unless an exception applies. A keyboard-only alternative alone does not satisfy this requirement.
Pointer, touch, voice, and motion input
Pointer actions permit cancellation, reversal or safe release under the applicable criterion; test down, move away, release and accidental activation.
Pointer, touch, voice, and motion input
Hit areas meet 24 by 24 CSS pixels or a valid 2.5.8 exception: spacing, equivalent, inline, user-agent control or essential presentation. Measure actual targets.
Pointer, touch, voice, and motion input
Dense toolbars, pagination, pins, calendar cells and adjacent destructive buttons remain usable by touch; consider 44 by 44 targets as an enhanced goal with its own exceptions.
Pointer, touch, voice, and motion input
Shaking, tilting or motion-actuated functions have UI alternatives and can be disabled unless an exception applies.
Pointer, touch, voice, and motion input
Hover-only, long-press, swipe-to-delete and context-menu actions have usable keyboard/touch alternatives where needed.
Normal text meets 4.5:1; qualifying large text meets 3:1. Large means at least 18 pt (24 CSS px), or 14 pt bold (about 18.67 CSS px), not 18/14 CSS px.
Measure text on actual backgrounds including gradients, photographs, overlays, opacity, placeholders and selection; document applicable exceptions.
Visual information needed to identify controls/states and meaningful graphics meets applicable 3:1 non-text contrast against adjacent colors; borders are not mandatory on every control.
Color is not the only visual cue for errors, selection, availability, links, required fields, chart series or change direction.
Text remains usable at 200% resize without loss of content/function; understand the criterion's caption/image-of-text exceptions.
Content reflows at 320 CSS pixel viewport width without loss or two-dimensional scrolling except qualifying two-dimensional content; test 256 CSS pixel height for vertical writing.
High zoom leaves menus, dialogs, tables, tooltips, sticky UI and error summaries reachable; fixed-height containers do not trap essential content.
Simultaneously override line height to 1.5 times font size, paragraph spacing to 2 times, letter spacing to 0.12 em and word spacing to 0.16 em without loss. Consider script-specific exceptions.
Portrait/landscape both work unless orientation is essential; design preference is not an essential restriction.
Forced colors and user contrast settings preserve names, selection, focus and meaningful icons. Classify usability findings separately when no specific criterion fails.
Font changes, minimum font settings and long translations do not hide essential content; text stays selectable where the task needs it.
Real text replaces images of text where possible; document customizable/essential exceptions, such as logotypes.
Hover/focus content is dismissible, hoverable and persistent under 1.4.13 conditions/exceptions; test magnification and moving into the popup.
Informative images have equivalent contextual alternatives, without filenames or needless repetition of surrounding text.
Decorative images are ignored appropriately; functional image alternatives identify action/destination rather than appearance alone.
Linked image/text combinations have useful non-repetitive names; icon-only controls and social links expose localized names.
SVG, canvas, background images, emoji and icon fonts convey meaningful information through accessible text or equivalent interfaces; test actual AT exposure.
Charts, maps, diagrams, scientific notation and infographics expose task-relevant values/relationships through structured descriptions, tables or equivalent controls.
CAPTCHA identifies its purpose and provides alternatives required by 1.1.1; assess authentication separately under 3.3.8. An audio fallback alone does not prove the process accessible.
Alternatives stay correct after localization, responsive-image swaps, CMS edits, user uploads and image failures.
Fields have meaningful accessible names and visible labels or adequate instructions where required; investigate disappearing placeholder-only context.
Group labels, legends, hints, units, formats, limits and required states are available at entry and associated programmatically where appropriate.
Applicable personal-data fields identify input purpose through standardized tokens; input type alone does not replace autocomplete purpose.
Password managers, autofill, paste, dictation and correction work; segmented codes assist whole-code entry and expose meaningful order/labels.
Login, MFA, recovery, step-up and identity challenges meet accessible-authentication conditions; examine cognitive tests, assistance and alternatives explicitly.
Errors identify field/problem in text, expose invalid state appropriately and suggest known corrections unless security/purpose would be compromised.
Submit errors become discoverable through a suitable summary, focus strategy or announcement, without duplicate speech or lost data.
Async validation handles pending/success/failure and stale responses; users are not repeatedly interrupted before finishing input.
Correcting an error preserves unrelated valid inputs; hidden conditional fields do not create unreachable validation blockers.
Data already entered/provided in the same process is auto-populated or selectable where 3.3.7 applies; document essential, security and no-longer-valid exceptions.
Legal/financial submissions, stored-user-data changes/deletions and test responses meet applicable reversible, checked or confirmed error-prevention conditions.
Review pages/receipts expose confirmation details; correction links return to usable fields and preserve other steps.
Disabled/read-only fields and unavailable actions expose understandable states and discoverable reasons; required completion is not hidden behind an unnamed disabled button.
Upload supports keyboard selection, constraints, progress, cancellation, failure, replacement and removal; drag-and-drop is not the sole path.
Prerecorded audio-only has an equivalent transcript; prerecorded video-only has an equivalent time-based or text alternative as applicable.
Prerecorded synchronized media has accurate synchronized captions covering speech and meaningful non-speech audio, unless the specific media-alternative exception applies.
Essential visual information in prerecorded synchronized media has audio description at AA; a transcript alone does not replace 1.2.5. Evaluate the distinct A-level alternative under 1.2.3.
Live synchronized media has live captions at AA; assess usability of accuracy, delay, speaker changes and essential events.
Alternatives are discoverable, synchronized where needed, localized as applicable and equivalent to the currently published version.
Player controls, tracks, volume, speed, fullscreen and picture-in-picture work with supported inputs/AT; controls do not hide captions.
Automatically playing audio lasting over three seconds has required pause/stop or independently adjustable volume.

Moving/blinking/scrolling content starting automatically, lasting over five seconds and presented alongside content can be paused/stopped/hidden unless essential; assess auto-updating information separately.
Time limits can be turned off, adjusted or extended under 2.2.1 or a documented exception applies; warnings and extension actions are reachable in time.
Flashing meets the three-flashes-or-below-threshold criterion; do not expose testers to suspected dangerous flashing merely to gather evidence.
Reduced motion suppresses unnecessary parallax, zoom and smooth scrolling as enhanced guidance; map interaction animation to AAA 2.3.3 where applicable.
Disabling animation does not leave hidden content or never-completing transitions; movement can also be controlled where A/AA requires it.
Custom controls expose name, role, state/value; expanded, checked, selected, pressed and busy changes reach AT.
ARIA references resolve after hydration, repetition and rerendering; ARIA does not contradict native semantics or visible wording.
Status messages such as counts, saved changes, progress and outcomes are available programmatically without focus where 4.1.3 applies.
Live regions announce meaningful updates once at suitable urgency; clocks, tokens, typing and progress increments do not flood speech.
SPA routes update title, context and focus appropriately; back/forward and loading/error paths work with virtual navigation.
Lazy loading, virtualization and infinite scroll permit discovery of task-relevant content and access beyond the list, including the footer.
Skeleton, empty, offline and server-error states explain outcome and next action; busy states do not freeze navigation indefinitely.
Shadow DOM, portals, iframes and embeds preserve relationships, reading order, focus transitions and return behavior across boundaries.
Delayed widgets, ad refresh and personalization do not unexpectedly reorder tasks or replace focused controls.
Repeated controls/help use consistent identification/order where required; icons with different functions are distinguishable.
Instructions explain prerequisites, steps, units and consequences before commitment; complex wording and abbreviations receive useful explanations as enhanced checks.
Multi-step tasks show understandable progress, permit correction, preserve work through reasonable interruptions and explain unrecoverable loss.
Alerts, upsells and chat invitations do not repeatedly interrupt reading or obscure correction controls; distinguish usability advice from criterion failures.
Accessible support/reporting is discoverable; reporting a barrier does not require completing the inaccessible process.
Ordinary site navigation uses links and disclosure buttons appropriately; a visual “menu” is not automatically an ARIA application menu requiring desktop-style keys.
Mobile drawers have a named opener, exposed expanded state, logical focus entry/exit and a reachable close control; collapsed links are not tabbable off screen.
Nested/mega navigation works by keyboard, pointer and touch; users can open subnavigation without being forced to follow its parent link.
Current page, breadcrumbs and in-page location are understandable without relying on color; repeated navigation regions can be distinguished.
Accordions expose button headings and expanded state; opening a section preserves focus, and collapsed contents do not receive focus. Test independent/multiple-open variants.
Pagination identifies current page and meaningful previous/next actions; switching pages communicates new results and preserves a sensible reading/focus position.
“Load more” reports appended content and permits users to reach it without traversing the entire preceding list again; loading failures leave retry usable.
Context/action menus expose their trigger, menu items, enabled/disabled states and expected keyboard exit; focus returns meaningfully after selection or dismissal.
A modal has an accessible name, suitable dialog semantics and initial focus that makes its purpose/content available; lengthy content is not read as one unusable description.

Modal focus stays in the active dialog, background interaction is unavailable as intended, and keyboard/screen-reader users can complete or dismiss it. Test actual modality rather than assuming every dialog element is modal.
Closing a dialog returns focus to its opener or a logical successor when the opener no longer exists; background scroll and reading position recover.
Nested dialogs, confirmations and provider overlays do not create competing focus loops, invisible active dialogs or accidental closure of both layers.
Short viewports, high zoom and virtual keyboards allow dialog content and actions to scroll into view; sticky action rows do not cover fields.
Nonmodal popovers do not trap focus as if modal; dismissal and return behavior match the chosen pattern, with no invisible focusable leftovers.
Tooltips supplement rather than replace a control's accessible name; they open on focus as appropriate and satisfy hover/focus-content conditions.
Toasts communicate relevant status without stealing focus; essential recovery actions remain available long enough or in a persistent location.
Checkboxes expose checked/unchecked/mixed state; clicking a label works; mixed-state parent behavior matches actual child selection.
Radio groups have a group name and understandable selected option; arrow navigation and focus entry follow the chosen native/custom pattern.
Switches and toggle buttons expose current state and keep stable names where appropriate; state changes are not conveyed by color alone.
Tabs expose tablist, tabs and associated panels; selection, focus, orientation and roving tabindex match the pattern; panel content remains reachable.
Automatic tab activation is usable without disruptive latency; manual activation supports expected activation keys. Removing/reordering tabs leaves a meaningful active tab.
Listboxes expose selected/focused options distinctly; single/multiselect keyboard behavior, labeling and selection updates are usable.
Comboboxes expose name, value and expanded state; popup navigation, selection, cancellation and editable-text keys do not conflict.
Autocomplete announces useful results/loading/no-results without excess speech; typed text is not silently overwritten, and manual entry remains usable where intended.
Multi-select chips have named remove actions, predictable focus after removal and understandable selection count; Backspace does not unexpectedly erase unrelated content.
Tree views expose hierarchy, expanded state and selection; parent/child traversal and lazy-loaded nodes work; hidden descendants do not remain reachable.
Toolbars have an intelligible name and navigation model; roving focus does not make controls undiscoverable or interfere with text/slider keys.
Date, numeric, search, and input controls
Date pickers provide usable typed entry where appropriate, clear localized format instructions, calendar navigation and announced month/year changes.
Date, numeric, search, and input controls
Calendar grids identify full dates, today, selection and unavailable dates without color alone; month/year crossing and focus return work.
Date, numeric, search, and input controls
Date ranges, timezones, daylight-saving boundaries and invalid end-before-start states have understandable feedback and correction.
Date, numeric, search, and input controls
Sliders expose name, current value, limits and useful value text; keyboard and non-drag single-pointer adjustment work, including touch screen-reader use.
Date, numeric, search, and input controls
Dual-thumb sliders identify each endpoint; thumbs remain distinguishable, values do not cross unexpectedly, and zoom does not hide their values.
Date, numeric, search, and input controls
Spinbuttons and quantity controls support direct entry or suitable alternatives, boundaries, invalid values and announced value changes without duplicate submissions.
Date, numeric, search, and input controls
Search supports submission, clearing, suggestion dismissal and no-results recovery; clear buttons are named and do not unexpectedly clear unrelated filters.
Date, numeric, search, and input controls
Password reveal exposes its action/state, preserves value/focus and does not break autofill; strength guidance is available without color or repeated intrusive announcements.
Date, numeric, search, and input controls
Rich-text editors expose editing area and formatting states; toolbar operation returns to the editing context and does not trap keyboard users in the editor.
Date, numeric, search, and input controls
Formatting, mentions, emoji, slash commands and link dialogs are available without inaccessible popups; authoring tools allow headings, lists and alternatives for published content.
Date, numeric, search, and input controls
Code editors expose a usable editing/reading mode, instructions for leaving Tab indentation mode, diagnostics and accessible equivalent interactions when needed.
Tables, grids, charts, and spatial interfaces
Data tables expose headers and associations for simple, row-header, multilevel and irregular layouts; captions/context explain their purpose.
Tables, grids, charts, and spatial interfaces
Sorting controls identify the column and current sort; sorting leaves focus stable and communicates the new state.
Tables, grids, charts, and spatial interfaces
Responsive tables/cards preserve header/value relationships and reading sequence; horizontal scrolling of a qualifying table does not force the whole page to scroll both ways.
Tables, grids, charts, and spatial interfaces
Interactive grids implement a deliberate cell/row navigation model; entering/exiting edit mode, selecting rows and operating cell controls are possible without a pointer.
Tables, grids, charts, and spatial interfaces
Virtualized grids expose row/column information accurately where supported; offscreen data can be reached and read; row recycling does not move focus to a different record silently.
Tables, grids, charts, and spatial interfaces
Bulk selection reports scope, including “all matching” versus “this page”; destructive bulk actions offer applicable checking/confirmation/reversal and retain meaningful focus.
Tables, grids, charts, and spatial interfaces
Charts provide a concise summary and equivalent task-relevant data/relationships; axes, units, legends, filters and series are understandable without color alone.
Tables, grids, charts, and spatial interfaces
Interactive chart tooltips and data points work through supported non-pointer paths without thousands of unusable Tab stops; chart filters also update accessible equivalents.
Tables, grids, charts, and spatial interfaces
Maps have task-equivalent address/search/list or other interfaces where possible; markers, zoom and directions are named and operable without drag-only panning.
Tables, grids, charts, and spatial interfaces
Diagram editors, whiteboards and canvas tools expose meaningful objects, selections and editing alternatives; distinguish genuinely essential path-dependent actions from ordinary controls.
Tables, grids, charts, and spatial interfaces
Math and scientific notation remain understandable with the selected AT and output formats; do not assume a screenshot, raw markup or alt text alone supports the required task.
Sortable lists and kanban cards support non-drag click/tap movement as well as keyboard access; item/destination/order changes are communicated.
Reordering an item preserves focus on that item or a useful control; undo and first/last positions work without impossible moves.
Carousels have named controls and understandable slide position; automatic rotation can be controlled where required and hidden slides do not contain stray focus stops.
Carousel changes preserve reading/focus appropriately; announcing every auto-rotating slide does not overwhelm speech.
Progress bars expose meaningful name/value where determinate; indeterminate activity is distinguishable from completed or failed work.
Skeletons are not repeated as fake content in AT; loading completion and failure leave the actual content and retry discoverable.
Alerts and error summaries have appropriate urgency and linking; focus and live-region strategies do not announce the same long message repeatedly.
Rating/review controls expose the scale, each option and selected value; hover preview is not the only way to determine the rating.
Steppers/wizards expose current/completed/available steps; returning to edit and moving forward preserves values and a sensible focus destination.
File drop zones expose a real selection mechanism; progress, per-file errors, previews and remove/cancel actions remain usable for large batches.
Color pickers expose usable named values or equivalent entry, selected state and non-drag adjustment; color alone does not identify saved swatches.
Audio recording and camera capture expose permission, start/stop, elapsed state, review, retry and alternate upload paths appropriate to the task.
Resizable panes have non-drag alternatives where required and do not hide critical controls at minimum size; splitters expose usable orientation/value if interactive.
Iframes have meaningful titles and usable content; focus can enter/exit provider controls without trapping, disappearing or skipping required fields.
Consent preference panels expose categories, states, links and save outcomes; all offered choices are operable and dismissal does not leave a blocked page.
Starred/saved items, reaction controls and counters distinguish action from current state and announce changes without replacing their accessible name unpredictably.
Notifications lists distinguish read/unread, provide meaningful timestamps and preserve position when items arrive or are dismissed.
Download/export controls identify relevant format/context and communicate queued, ready, expired and failed states; accessible data is not lost in the exported artifact.
Web components retain labels and focus indicators across shadow boundaries; slot changes, hydration and component upgrades do not break interaction.
Registration works from invitation/entry through validation, consent, verification and first login; activation email content and expired-link recovery are accessible.
Login works with password managers and paste; show-password, remember-me and alternative sign-in choices remain understandable and operable.
MFA handles paste/autofill, whole-code input, expiry, resend, alternative factor and unavailable-device recovery without unnecessary cognitive barriers.
Passkeys, SSO and cross-device redirects preserve context and provide usable failure/cancel/retry paths; record OS/provider boundaries explicitly.
Password reset and account recovery work without remembering inaccessible prior data or relying on a single sensory challenge.
Session warnings are announced and reachable; extension follows the selected criterion and documented exceptions. Reauthentication does not silently destroy work; separately assess AAA preservation.
Profile changes, email changes, logout, account export and deletion have usable verification and outcomes; destructive changes meet applicable error prevention.
Identity/document/biometric checks include a usable route for relevant impairments; examine camera alignment, movement, audio prompts and manual-review alternatives.
Users can discover products through search/navigation and operate filters, sorting, comparison and no-results recovery without pointer-only actions.
Variants, swatches, availability, price changes, subscription intervals and size guides are understandable without color or images alone.
Add-to-cart announces item/quantity outcome and supports continue-shopping or checkout without unexpected focus loss.
Cart quantity edits, removal, undo, coupons, errors and total changes are accessible; out-of-stock changes do not strand the user.
Guest/account checkout, saved addresses, address lookup/manual entry and billing/shipping reuse preserve information and expose errors.
Shipping options, fees, taxes, delivery dates and recurring terms are available before commitment and after changes.
Payment fields, provider iframes, wallet redirects and step-up challenges work through success, decline, timeout and cancellation. Use sandbox/test transactions where available.
Order review permits checking/correction under applicable error prevention; confirmation, receipt and order history are readable and accessible.
Refund, cancellation, subscription pause and returns are as testable as purchase; inaccessible support is not the only recovery route.
Booking calendars, availability grids, seat/room choices and timezones have equivalent nonvisual/non-drag operations; held-slot expiry is announced and recoverable.
Search supports query entry, suggestions, count, results, pagination and no-results actions; updated counts do not steal focus or overwhelm speech.
Articles/documentation expose meaningful heading structure, anchors, code snippets, footnotes, glossary and copy controls across narrow layouts.
Paywalls, newsletter overlays, age gates, ads and consent do not create traps or hide required reading/close controls at zoom.
Comments, reviews and user-generated media have accessible input, moderation feedback, reporting and authoring guidance for alternatives/captions.
Chat/support permits opening, composing, sending, reviewing history, attachments, closing and returning to the host task; incoming messages do not continuously interrupt.
Audio/video calls expose join, mute, captions, participant status, chat and device errors; assess accessible alternatives for essential communication tasks.
Email and transactional messages have logical order, meaningful links, readable contrast and alternatives; critical actions do not depend on image loading.
Notification settings, language choices, unsubscribe and support escalation work with keyboard, screen reader and mobile touch.
Onboarding/tutorials are skippable or otherwise usable, preserve context and do not require a visual spotlight or drag gesture to proceed.
Dashboards expose current metrics, time ranges, trends and equivalent data; refreshed data and filters keep summaries/tables synchronized.
Create/edit/delete records, inline editing, selection and bulk actions work across empty, large, filtered and permission-limited datasets.
Long forms/autosave communicate pending, saved, conflict and failed states; recovery does not require finding an invisible transient toast.
Import workflows expose column matching, row errors, progress, cancel/retry and accessible result reports; invalid files do not erase configuration.
Collaboration communicates edits, mentions, presence and conflicts without excessive announcements; focus does not follow other users' cursors.
Role/permission differences do not produce unnamed disabled controls, unreachable actions or silent authorization failures.
Settings changes, theme previews and personalization remain usable before and after saving; resetting settings can recover from a broken configuration.
Data exports, print views and generated reports preserve labels, reading order and data equivalence rather than flattening essential information into images.
Mobile web, native apps, and kiosks
Mobile screen-reader exploration/swiping reaches every required element; touch activation does not depend on inaccessible hover or custom gestures.
Mobile web, native apps, and kiosks
Virtual keyboards, safe-area insets, bottom sheets and browser chrome do not cover active inputs, errors or primary actions; scrolling reveals them.
Mobile web, native apps, and kiosks
Orientation changes and responsive breakpoints preserve entered data, current step, reading order and focused content.
Mobile web, native apps, and kiosks
Voice control can select visible controls by label; switch access has a practical scanning order and a usable route through composite controls.
Mobile web, native apps, and kiosks
Native app scope includes platform text scaling, AT semantics/actions, external keyboard, reduced motion, contrast and permission dialogs; commission platform-specific verification.
Mobile web, native apps, and kiosks
Webviews preserve semantics and focus across native/web boundaries; app links, external authentication and return-to-app failures have usable recovery.
Mobile web, native apps, and kiosks
Kiosk/hardware scope records physical reach, tactile/audio output, privacy, timeouts, payment hardware and accessible assistance; a web-only pass cannot settle these requirements.
Inventory PDFs, office files, slide decks, spreadsheets, certificates, tickets, invoices and attachments required by a task; identify authoring and export owners.
PDFs have correct tags, language, title, reading order, headings, lists, links, alternatives and table associations; verify with AT, not only a checker.
Scanned documents receive accurate recognition and structure as needed; OCR alone does not prove usable headings, order, tables or form fields.
Fillable documents expose names, instructions, logical tab order, error handling and signatures; submitting, saving and reopening preserve usability.
Office files use meaningful styles, slide order, alt text, table structure and labels; spreadsheet meaning does not depend on color, merged cells or unexplained coordinates alone.
Accessible HTML or other alternatives are equivalent, current and discoverable before an inaccessible download; record when additional PDF/UA or document standards are in scope.
Generate and inspect artifacts from realistic long, localized and missing-data records; a manually repaired sample does not prove the export generator is fixed.
Prompt input, attachment, send, stop, retry, edit and regenerate are named and operable; submitting does not erase the only accessible copy of the prompt.
Streaming responses have a readable final structure and useful completion/error feedback; token-by-token announcements do not overwhelm speech.
Auto-scroll respects users reading earlier content; history, references and newly generated controls remain discoverable without forced focus jumps.
Generated tables, code, citations, math and images expose usable structure/alternatives; copy and export preserve task-relevant meaning.
Generated choices, tool approvals, refusals, rate limits and connection failures expose clear outcomes and recovery without color or hidden affordances alone.
Speech input/output has usable text alternatives and controls as applicable; microphone permissions, playback, interruption and errors are understandable.
Model outputs do not silently overwrite user-provided alternatives, headings or labels; generated content is reviewed before publication and assessed in its final rendered form.
Education/exams cover equations, timed sections, autosave, accommodations, answers, review and submission; document genuine timing exceptions rather than assuming all exams qualify.
Healthcare tasks cover appointments, patient forms, results/charts, secure messages and remote consultations with accessible confidentiality and recovery.
Public-service/benefit/job applications cover eligibility, evidence uploads, signatures, save/resume, deadline messaging and accessible decision documents.
Finance covers balance/trend interpretation, transfers, payee verification, fees, transaction review and statement access; step-up security remains within the audited process.
Travel covers route search, date/time changes, passenger assistance, seat selection, disruption notices, check-in and accessible boarding documents.

Games/immersive experiences record remapping, sensory alternatives, captions, difficulty/timing choices, motion and safe flash handling; identify separate specialist scope rather than implying WCAG covers everything.
Each supported locale has correct language, translated accessible names, date/number formats and usable long labels; mixed-language content is identified appropriately.
Right-to-left and bidirectional content preserve meaningful reading/focus sequence, currency, identifiers and editing; visual mirroring does not corrupt semantics.
Third-party consent, payments, CAPTCHA, maps, chat, analytics UI and embedded documents are tested in the host context; record provider/version and escalation owner.
Network interruption, slow loading, duplicate submission and stale sessions produce accessible outcomes and recovery without silently losing completed work.
Feature flags, A/B variants and personalization receive relevant checks; a passing default variant does not cover inaccessible alternatives served to real users.
User support can accept accessibility reports and provide timely assistance; reporting forms, statements and contact channels are themselves usable.
Review contextual equivalents for informative, functional, decorative and complex visuals, and special cases.
Test alternatives for each standalone audio/video item; distinguish equivalent text from synchronized media.
Compare captions against speech and meaningful sounds in recorded synchronized media.
Check the applicable description or full media-alternative route; do not confuse this with AA audio description.
Inspect captions in live synchronized media, including speaker changes and meaningful audio.
Verify necessary visual information is available through audio description; a text transcript alone is insufficient.
If AAA is selected, assess sign-language interpretation for prerecorded audio in synchronized media.
Assess whether additional pauses/descriptions convey visual information when existing audio pauses are insufficient.
Evaluate an equivalent alternative covering prerecorded synchronized and video-only information.
Assess equivalent access to live audio-only information; separate this from live synchronized captions.
Inspect semantic structure and associations for headings, lists, forms, tables and visual groupings.
Read sequentially across responsive rearrangement, columns, content insertion and exports.
Review instructions depending only on shape, position, sound, size, orientation or color.
Rotate devices and inspect restrictions; establish whether a claimed orientation exception is essential.
Inspect standardized purposes for applicable user-information fields, including address and account forms.
Assess whether regions, controls and symbols expose purpose for personalization in markup-based content.
Check links, charts, validation and selection for an additional visual means of conveying meaning.
Test independent control of automatically playing audio over three seconds.
Measure normal/large text in actual states/backgrounds; record applicable exceptions and correct size units.
Resize to 200 percent and complete tasks without lost content/function; consider stated exceptions.
Identify avoidable images of text and document customizable or essential presentation exceptions.
Measure enhanced text thresholds: normally 7:1, qualifying large text 4.5:1; assess exceptions.
Assess prerecorded speech-focused audio against background-sound options, level difference and exceptions.
Evaluate user control of text presentation, line width, alignment, spacing and resizing under the exact criterion.
Assess stricter limits for images of text, preserving only the criterion's actual allowances.
Test 320 CSS pixel width or corresponding vertical-writing height; isolate essential two-dimensional content.
Measure visual identification of controls/states and meaningful graphics against adjacent colors, with exceptions.
Apply all required spacing overrides together and inspect lost content/function across widgets.
Test dismissibility, pointer travel into extra content and persistence under applicable conditions.
Complete all functionality by keyboard; distinguish genuinely path-dependent input from ordinary interaction.
Enter and leave components; verify any nonstandard exit instructions and modal completion/dismissal.
Evaluate keyboard operation without the A-level exception for underlying path-dependent functionality.
Test disable/remap/focus-only safeguards for character shortcuts and collisions with typing or dictation.
Trigger time limits and verify an allowed adjustment route or valid exception, including usable warnings.
Check applicable moving content and auto-updating information; assess controls and essential exceptions separately.
Assess timing in events/activities under the stricter criterion and its noninteractive/synchronized-media exceptions.
Check whether non-emergency interruptions can be postponed or suppressed.
Let a session expire and verify work continues without data loss after reauthentication.

Audit Code reduction, quality and architecture
Libraries, CLIs, plugins, and native code
AI, data pipelines, search, and automation

values: Record repository, commit, branch, uncommitted changes, build artifact, deployed version, environments, and audit date/timezone. Identify mismatches between source and deployment.
List entry points: UI routes, APIs, command lines, workers, schedules, webhooks, migrations, plugins, administrative tools, and externally configured triggers.
Name critical journeys and invariants such as one charge per purchase, one authoritative owner per record, or no cross-tenant reads; identify where each is enforced.
Capture data sensitivity, tenancy, traffic shape, latency/recovery targets, supported devices and clients, regions, team capacity, budget, and compatibility commitments.
Map components to owners, consumers, deployment units, stores, third parties, trust zones, and lifecycle status; include shared infrastructure and dormant features.
Separate an existing defect from a missing optional feature, subjective preference, speculative optimization, and an accepted product limitation.
State permitted inspection and execution, target environments, synthetic accounts/data, request bounds, and exclusions. A reusable audit does not authorize destructive or third-party tests.
Select guides and check IDs before calculating completeness; record why excluded checks do not apply and which unavailable evidence remains Not verified.
Trace representative critical paths across layers, including authorization, validation, persistence, asynchronous work, side effects, and response/error handling.
Sample by risk and variation: old/new code, sync/async, privileged/public, each tenant role, large/empty datasets, each deployment unit, and different supported client generations.
Expand inspection when a sampled problem suggests a shared generator, helper, schema, framework convention, or configuration; distinguish inspected population from estimated reach.
Record expected versus observed behavior, exact locations and revision, reproducer prerequisites, tools/settings, evidence time, and affected users or data.
Distinguish static inspection, local execution, staging behavior, production observation, and untested hypotheses; a passing build does not verify runtime tenant isolation or rollback.
Inspect scanner configuration, exclusions, supported file types, generated code, and reachable entry points before trusting tool results. Report tool failures and blind spots.
Keep evidence minimal and redacted, with reproducible references and an appropriate retention location; do not paste credentials, private payloads, or unrestricted production dumps into reports.
Confirm reported failures against current code and configuration; label historical findings and illustrative examples so they cannot be mistaken for observed defects.
Give each finding one root cause, primary owner, affected check IDs, consequence, reach, severity, confidence, exposure, and separately justified priority/blocker status.
Distinguish a reachable security/data failure from latent disabled code and ordinary maintenance friction; neither scanner severity nor file size alone establishes business severity.
Explain architectural concerns through a realistic change or failure scenario, such as adding a tenant or losing a provider; show which assumption fails and why.
Compare the smallest effective repair with consolidation, deletion, staged migration, or explicit acceptance; include cost, compatibility, and operational consequences.
Define acceptance checks that prove the intended behavior, directly affected regression paths, deployment/rollback dependencies, owner, and target date.
Record accepted risks with accountable person, reason, compensating controls, expiry, and revisit trigger. Keep acceptance separate from a Pass result.
Verify fixes against the changed revision and relevant deployed configuration; record actual execution results and remaining gaps, including checks that could not run.
Report selected, assessed, Pass, Fail, Not verified, and Not applicable counts with a clear denominator; do not turn completion percentage into an architecture quality score.
Inventory hidden folders, tooling, generated files, assets, scripts, examples, vendored code, session artifacts, runtime/dev dependencies, and externally invoked jobs alongside source modules.
For every removal candidate identify consumers across static imports, reflection, naming conventions, route discovery, plugins, code generation, schedules, deployment manifests, and external clients.
Distinguish unused code from rarely invoked recovery, support, migration, security, and disaster-response paths; verify the supported obligation before retiring them.
Review expired flags and experiments across all variants, configuration, telemetry, tests, and rollout rules; preserve emergency controls that still have an owner and operational purpose.
Find abandoned endpoints, alternate implementations, copied components, orphan translations/assets, unreachable handlers, disabled workflows, and scaffolding; verify dynamic usage before deletion.
Retire dependencies with their imports, configuration, lockfile entries, scripts, containers, documentation, and CI jobs using supported package tooling.
Separate reproducible outputs from source-of-truth inputs; retain required generated distributions, schema baselines, license notices, and recovery assets with a documented reason.
Check whether historical documentation or artifacts have support, retention, license, or evidence value before removal; consolidate authoritative instructions and remove stale duplicates.
Define deprecation notice, consumer migration, compatibility window, observability, and rollback for externally consumed APIs or packages; repository references cannot prove no outside users exist.
Report deleted, simplified, retained, and unresolved candidates with evidence and affected verification; count reduced cost or complexity without treating fewer lines as the primary goal.
Check that names express domain meaning, units, ownership, and side effects; avoid ambiguous booleans, magic values, and misleading helper names on critical paths.

Investigate long functions, deep branching, broad parameter lists, and oversized modules through actual comprehension or change failures; split cohesive responsibilities rather than enforcing arbitrary length limits.
Identify duplicated business decisions and independent copies that drift; consolidate only when they share semantics and lifecycle, not merely similar syntax.
Review wrappers, factories, inheritance, generic repositories, utility modules, and framework layers for a demonstrated boundary or invariant; simplify indirection that only forwards calls.
Trace hidden side effects in imports, constructors, property access, callbacks, and global initialization; make ordering and ownership visible to maintainers.
Check dependency direction and circular imports, including runtime and type-only differences; verify initialization behavior instead of relying only on a graph warning.
Inspect shared mutable state, global service locators, implicit context, and ambient tenant/session values for cross-request leakage and hard-to-isolate changes.
Make domain constraints explicit through suitable types, constructors, validation, and state transitions; avoid invalid combinations hidden in loosely structured dictionaries or flags.
Keep exceptions to local conventions justified and discoverable; distinguish harmless stylistic variation from ambiguity that causes defects or blocks maintenance.
Confirm comments explain reasons, contracts, and surprising behavior; remove misleading commented-out implementations and update examples that no longer match the code.
Check monorepo/package boundaries, dependency declarations, import paths, ownership, and independent release assumptions; detect accidental dependencies on another package's private files.
Ensure generated changes can be traced to inputs and generator versions; avoid hand fixes that will be overwritten or editing generated output without updating its source.
Review public exports and extension points for accidental commitments; keep internal implementation details out of supported API surfaces when consumers do not need them.
Trace high-churn or incident-prone modules to concrete change costs and ownership gaps; use history as a prioritization aid rather than evidence that every frequently edited file is defective.
Confirm project-specific lint, format, and type rules run on relevant files; investigate broad exclusions and suppression comments with no reason or expiry.
Check that small shared-code changes can be validated against actual consumers without requiring unrelated production deployments or undocumented manual edits.
Verify AI-generated code, copied patterns, suggested packages, and generated explanations against actual APIs, contracts, licenses, and local conventions; claimed execution requires tool evidence.
Apply the original session-test retention rules to every new test, fixture, snapshot, mock, and helper; retain distinct material assurance and remove orphaned support after justified retirement.

Validate runtime input at every external boundary: requests, configuration, database legacy records, events, files, plugins, third-party responses, and model output; static types do not validate arriving bytes.
Exercise absent, null, empty, zero, false, negative, oversized, malformed, duplicate, and unexpected fields; distinguish a missing value from an intentional empty update.
Check parse/canonicalize/validate order, repeated decoding, Unicode normalization, alternate separators, and case sensitivity where they affect identity, paths, signatures, or authorization.
Bound text length, collection size, nesting, decompression, regex work, uploads, and pagination before expensive processing; include streamed and chunked inputs.
Review implicit coercion, truthiness, unchecked casts, dynamic access, enum fallbacks, non-exhaustive switches, and unknown discriminators for silently accepted invalid states.
Check integer range, signedness, precision loss, NaN/infinity, division by zero, rounding direction, and accumulation; preserve identifiers beyond a language's safe numeric range.
Keep money, percentages, quantities, and units explicit; verify currency minor units, rounding allocation, refunds, discounts, and mixed-unit conversion against product rules.
Separate instants, durations, local dates, and schedules; exercise timezones, daylight-saving gaps/repeats, leap days, end-of-month rules, expiry boundaries, and clock skew.
Use monotonic elapsed-time measurement where required; avoid treating wall-clock changes, timestamp ordering, or local clock accuracy as proof of distributed order.
Exercise inclusive/exclusive range ends, pagination cursors, zero/one-element collections, sorting ties, unstable ordering, duplicate items, and off-by-one loops.
Name legal entity states, transitions, preconditions, and terminal behavior; reject impossible transitions even when callers bypass the normal UI.
Enforce critical rules at authoritative server/data boundaries; duplicated client validation may improve UX but must not be the only enforcement.
Derive actor, tenant, ownership, price, entitlement, and privileged fields from trusted context; reject mass assignment and caller-controlled scope changes.
Verify object/function/field permissions for read, write, bulk, export, background, and administrative paths, including stale sessions and permission changes during work.
Check lookup and decision behavior for missing, soft-deleted, archived, suspended, expired, or partially migrated records; default behavior must match the domain contract.
Exercise duplicate submissions, retry after uncertain success, stale forms, concurrent edits, and back/forward navigation; define intended conflict or idempotent behavior.
Check whether authorization or validation can become invalid between check and use; move enforcement into a transaction, conditional operation, or equivalent durable boundary where needed.
Separate successful execution from accepted, pending, queued, or partially completed outcomes; never report durable success before required effects are confirmed.
Verify fallback and default branches preserve business restrictions; missing configuration, provider errors, or unknown states must not silently grant access or mark payment complete.
Keep nondeterminism, random seeds, ordering assumptions, and environment-dependent behavior explicit where reproducibility or fair outcomes matter.
Check parameterized database access and context-appropriate output escaping; inspect dynamic query fragments, templates, shell commands, and expression execution separately.
Validate outbound destinations, redirects, DNS/IP resolution behavior, and file paths at the actual use point; include private-network access, symlinks, archives, and path traversal.
Check deserialization, user templates, imports, macros, unsafe reflection, and native bridges for unintended code execution or privileged object construction.
Review credential/token generation, comparison, storage, expiry, rotation, and revocation using supported security libraries; verify sensitive tokens and payloads cannot enter logs or client bundles.
Inspect session/cookie, CSRF, cross-origin, and browser/server trust assumptions for state-changing requests; exemptions need a demonstrated equivalent control.

Verify each executable extension or model-selected tool has the caller's intended authority, bounded inputs, and explicit execution context; untrusted content must not become instructions or trusted identifiers.
Preserve useful error causes and correlation without disclosing secrets or internals to callers; distinguish user, transient, permanent, and invariant failures.
Inspect swallowed exceptions, broad catches, ignored return codes, detached promises/tasks, and success-shaped fallbacks that hide failed side effects.
Ensure files, sockets, database sessions, subscriptions, native handles, temporary resources, and locks are released on success, failure, early return, timeout, and cancellation.
Verify partial initialization and partial writes leave a recoverable state; cleanup failure should not mask the original problem or erase needed recovery evidence.
Propagate cancellation and deadlines to owned work; distinguish cancellation of waiting from actual cancellation of a remote operation that may still commit.
Check sync/async boundary exceptions, callback reentrancy, iterator exhaustion, repeated cleanup, and resource reuse after disposal where the chosen runtime permits them.
Maintain a current context/container view showing entry points, components, stores, providers, deployment units, trust boundaries, and operators; verify it against code and deployed configuration.
Name quality requirements with a workload and measurable target where relevant: latency, throughput, availability, data freshness, recovery, portability, accessibility, and cost.
Review boundaries around business capabilities and change ownership; identify layers or services that must always change together despite claiming independence.
Keep domain decisions independent of incidental UI, transport, vendor SDK, and persistence details where that improves actual changeability; avoid layers that add only forwarding code.
Assign a source of truth and writer ownership for each entity and rule; investigate competing implementations across services, triggers, jobs, clients, and stored procedures.
Detect cycles, cross-service table access, shared mutable schemas, backdoor imports, and hidden synchronous dependencies that undermine stated module boundaries.
Examine public interfaces for cohesive responsibilities, stable semantics, explicit dependencies, bounded outputs, and accidental exposure of framework internals.
Validate tenancy assumptions in storage, identity, caches, workers, search, exports, admin paths, configuration, and observability; examine a realistic second-tenant scenario.
Trace authority across browser, API, worker, database, edge, and provider boundaries; privileged operations need an accountable enforcement point, including public endpoints.
Confirm independently deployed applications are independently configured and secured as intended, including shared libraries, runtime processes, credentials, and failure domains.
Justify monolith, modular monolith, services, serverless, edge, or batch topology using present constraints and credible growth; do not require distribution solely for future scale.
Follow critical-path network hops and synchronous fan-out; evaluate partial failure, cumulative latency, dependency availability, and a cheaper or simpler local alternative.
Identify process-local locks, sessions, caches, queues, filesystem state, and rate limits that fail under multiple replicas, cold starts, instance replacement, or long-lived workers.
Document consistency and partition behavior per operation; decide what can be stale, rejected, queued, read-only, or unavailable without violating invariants.
Bound fan-out, task creation, resource pools, queue growth, cardinality, payloads, and expensive computation; record expected load and saturation behavior.
Check noisy-neighbor isolation, tenant-level fairness, hot keys, hot partitions, and disproportionate work caused by a single account or request.
Include database, third-party, egress, storage, rebuild, observability, and on-call costs in architecture choices; average request cost alone can miss expensive idle or burst behavior.
Match redundancy and regional complexity to recovery and business requirements; identify shared failure points rather than assuming more replicas establish resilience.
Confirm team skills, staffing, ownership, debugging tools, incident capacity, and upgrade burden can support the chosen technologies and deployment count.
Record what happens when a provider, region, identity service, database, or control plane is unavailable; distinguish failover capability from unexecuted design intent.
Rehearse a plausible change such as a second tenant, pricing rule, provider replacement, or bulk import; identify brittle assumptions using actual touched modules and contracts.
Inventory supported clients, event consumers, persisted formats, plugins, and independently released services before changing a shared interface.
Plan expand/migrate/contract sequencing, mixed-version operation, backfill, verification, and retirement of old paths; state the authoritative source during each stage.
Separate code rollback from data recovery; identify irreversible writes, old-reader incompatibility, and the point after which rollback requires a forward repair.
Avoid dual writes without a reconciliation or atomicity strategy; define ownership and verification while old and new systems coexist.
Inspect vendor-specific identity, data formats, SQL, storage URLs, schedules, and runtime APIs; test the portability actually promised rather than requiring universal provider abstraction.
Prefer incremental replacement with measurable checkpoints when viable; justify rewrites with verified constraints, migration costs, parity requirements, and a retirement plan.
Preserve required historical compatibility and migration assets while removing obsolete design paths; document evidence that the final supported consumer has moved.
Record context, constraints, decision owner, status, date, alternatives, reasons, expected benefits, negative consequences, and implementation follow-up for material choices.
Compare alternatives on complexity, correctness, cost, scale, portability, team familiarity, security, reversibility, and operation using relevant evidence rather than a universal weighted score.
Record assumptions, uncertainty, validation experiments, success measures, and revisit triggers; distinguish an accepted tradeoff from an implementation defect.
Link decisions to implementation and superseding decisions; remove misleading diagrams or mark them historical when reality has changed.

Inventory application code, routes, components, jobs, schemas, assets, dependencies, scripts, tests, fixtures, configuration, CI workflows, generated outputs, and documentation. Include hidden/tooling folders and artifacts created during AI or development sessions; inspect references without copying secrets into reports.

For each candidate, record its path, current consumer or operational purpose, evidence, and a decision: delete, simplify/consolidate, retain with a concrete reason, or investigate. Prefer deletion when no current purpose remains; unresolved usage requires investigation before removal.

Remove unreachable code, unused exports/imports, abandoned features and flags, obsolete compatibility paths, duplicate business rules, redundant wrappers, and abstractions that add no useful boundary. Prefer a direct implementation where it preserves required behavior and clarity.

Remove unused runtime and development dependencies, obsolete scripts and configuration, redundant build/CI steps, and duplicated tooling. Update manifests, lockfiles, references, documentation, and workflows together using the project's supported tooling.

Remove unused assets, sample/demo content, scaffolding, placeholder pages, scratch files, debug helpers, temporary logs, generated reports, build outputs, and caches that have no continuing purpose. Keep reproducible generated artifacts out of version control unless the build/distribution process requires them; define appropriate ignore rules.

Delete obsolete or duplicated documentation, session notes, task plans, and audit artifacts from the maintained project when they have no ongoing value or retention requirement. Keep a concise authoritative setup and operations reference; store required release evidence in its intended location with bounded retention.

Confirm actual usage through entry points, runtime/dynamic imports, reflection, auto-discovery, plugins, scheduled jobs, deployment configuration, external API consumers, and supported clients. A static unused-code report or a zero-reference search alone does not establish safe deletion.

Account for supported upgrade paths, database migrations, user data, recovery assets, licenses, and required records. Repository cleanup does not authorize deleting production data or breaking supported clients; record any separately scoped retirement needed.

Review every session-created test, helper, fixture, snapshot, mock, browser recording, screenshot, and test-only dependency. Delete one-off reproduction checks after verification when they provide no continuing regression protection; delete duplicate, obsolete, implementation-mirroring, trivial, and low-value generated tests and their orphaned support files.

Retain the smallest useful set that protects critical user journeys, security/tenant boundaries, data integrity, payments, important external contracts, and meaningful fixed defects where applicable. Name the behavior or failure each retained check protects; consolidate overlapping checks without losing distinct necessary assurance.

Do not add tests for reversible, low-impact edits merely to accompany a change. Prefer existing checks and bounded manual verification when sufficient. Add a focused durable test only when an uncovered material risk justifies maintaining it; do not require a coverage percentage, test count, or per-session test quota.

Repair or replace a valuable flaky/failing check before retiring it, or document equivalent verification and the remaining gap. Never delete a check solely to make CI pass. Remove obsolete test runners, fixtures, snapshots, scripts, dependencies, and CI jobs when their final justified consumer is gone.

Establish relevant baseline results, remove coherent groups of unnecessary elements, and verify the affected build/startup, key flows, deployment tasks, and retained checks. Match verification to the removal risk; broaden or repeat it only for new changes, failures, or unresolved dependencies. Keep necessary temporary verification outside the maintained source and remove its disposable artifacts afterward.

Report deleted/simplified items with reasons, remaining uncertain candidates, justified retentions, and verification results. Include useful before/after counts or dependency/build changes when available; line-count reduction is evidence of scope, not a success target that overrides correctness. Do not report an authorized cleanup complete while known unnecessary items remain unexplained.
Identify entry points, domain logic, data access, external integrations, jobs, and UI boundaries. Keep trusted operations and credentials out of client modules.
Check duplicated rules, dead code, abandoned dependencies, stale feature flags, and unclear shared state. Confirm dynamic/runtime uses before deleting apparently unused code.
Validate external data at runtime, including configuration, API payloads, events, and AI output. Static types alone do not validate these boundaries.
Examine error handling, cancellation, timeouts, cleanup, and resource lifetimes. Failures should remain diagnosable without being swallowed or leaking internals.
Inspect concurrency assumptions, mutable global state, process-local caches/limiters, and multi-worker behavior. Identify assumptions that change when deployed on a persistent VPS.
Make business rules and migrations understandable. Prefer changes supported by an observed problem over speculative rewrites.
Verify package identity, provenance, maintenance, and necessity, including packages suggested by AI. Investigate typosquatting, unexpected install scripts, and abandoned libraries.
Commit appropriate lockfiles and use reproducible supported build/install workflows. Inventory production runtime, framework, OS, container, and transitive dependencies.

Scan the actual dependency/container stack using appropriate ecosystem tools. Assess affected versions, deployed reachability, and upstream fixes; do not equate a clean package audit with complete security.
Review base image sources, tags/digests, registry permissions, and rebuild/update practices. Check that dependencies and runtimes remain supported.
Scope CI and deployment credentials, isolate untrusted pull request builds, review workflow/action dependencies, and prevent secrets reaching build logs or artifacts.
Track licensing obligations with 11 and retain a useful dependency inventory or SBOM where project risk warrants it.
Confirm a clean checkout can install, configure, build, and run using documented placeholders and supported runtime versions.
Keep linting/type/build gates meaningful for the selected stack. Inspect bypasses, ignored errors, and checks that never run in CI.
Use tests at business boundaries and critical failure paths; avoid treating coverage percentage as a substitute for correctness. See 15.
Document local setup, architectural decisions that matter, operational dependencies, and ownership of shared code.
Verify separate projects remain independently secured and deployable where intended. A secure primary app does not automatically secure another app sharing its repository or VPS.

Review the schema as a whole: entity relationships, ownership, constraints, lifecycle, and tenant boundaries. Exercise a plausible second-tenant or product-rule change to identify brittle assumptions before adding isolated tables or fields.

Check modules with excessive responsibilities or size for concrete maintenance problems; split only where clearer boundaries justify the change. Record architectural decisions and reasons so future maintainers can assess tradeoffs.
Verify changes receive accountable human review, including AI-generated changes, and a documented branch/merge workflow prevents accidental overwrites and bypassed checks. Match review depth to risk.

Assign a dependency/framework update cadence and an urgent vulnerability response path; plan upgrades before support ends. A monthly routine review may be suitable, but the cadence belongs in project scope.
Have a maintainer follow the README from a clean checkout and record time and missing steps. Keep setup, system boundaries, and operational handover usable by someone other than the original author.
Map entities, relationships, owners, tenant keys, lifecycle, retention, and source-of-truth rules; include blobs, search indexes, caches, analytics, and provider-held state.
Enforce required uniqueness, referential integrity, nullability, checks, and tenant-scoped relationships at an appropriate authoritative boundary; application validation alone may race.
Check identifier stability, uniqueness, guessability implications, foreign-key scope, externally exposed IDs, and collisions across imports or merged systems.
Review normalization or deliberate denormalization against actual access/change patterns; define synchronization and repair for duplicated derived fields.
Trace transaction boundaries around multi-record invariants; exercise partial failure, commit uncertainty, rollback failure, and effects outside the database transaction.
Verify isolation level, lost-update protection, optimistic versions, conditional writes, and lock ordering for concurrent edits; do not infer serial behavior from a single-user run.
Check soft deletion, restoration, cascades, archived records, unique-key reuse, tenant deletion, and background cleanup against the full entity graph.
Verify erasure and retention propagate to derived stores where required, with explicit exceptions for necessary records; prevent deleted data from being resurrected by replay or restore.
Inspect query plans and representative cardinality for hot paths; confirm useful indexes and their write/storage cost instead of adding indexes without workload evidence.
Detect N+1 queries, repeated counts, unnecessary columns, cross-tenant scans, chatty transactions, and queries or result sets without bounds.
Verify stable pagination, cursor semantics, tie-breakers, changing datasets, deleted cursors, and maximum page sizes; avoid silently dropping or duplicating records under documented usage.
Bound transaction duration, pool size/waits, lock waits, batch size, and query time; inspect leaked connections and retries that multiply pool exhaustion.
Make replica lag, read-after-write behavior, write routing, and failover assumptions explicit; use authoritative reads where stale state breaks an invariant.
Check blob upload completion, metadata consistency, checksums where justified, orphan cleanup, authorized download, and expiration of temporary or signed access.
Verify database roles and application credentials match necessary operations; check that destructive maintenance and migration privileges are not ambient runtime defaults.
Test schema changes against representative data volumes and supported old/new binaries; account for locks, table rewrites, index builds, defaults, and operation-specific database behavior.
Sequence additive changes, compatible readers/writers, backfill, verification, and removal; keep migration history needed for supported installs and upgrades.
Make large backfills restartable, bounded, observable, and safe to resume; identify invalid legacy rows and reconciliation rather than silently discarding them.
Prevent concurrent migration runners and ambiguous migration state; verify startup behavior when schema is ahead, behind, or partially changed.
Distinguish reversible schema operations from irreversible data transformation; define backup/restore or forward-repair prerequisites and rehearse proportionately under module 09.
Validate imports/exports for schema versions, encoding, delimiters, units, timezones, duplicates, formula injection where applicable, partial failures, and authorization.
Check seed/bootstrap/reset scripts for idempotency, environment targeting, synthetic data, privilege, and protection from accidental destructive execution.
Verify request, response, and event schemas match actual behavior, including error bodies, status codes, nullable fields, ordering, and content types.
Define compatibility for added/removed fields, new enum variants, defaults, unknown fields, numeric representation, and older consumers; generated clients require runtime contract evidence too.
Keep HTTP or RPC semantics, retryability, idempotency keys, pagination, rate-limit responses, and timeout behavior explicit for callers.
Review bulk operations for per-item authorization, size bounds, atomic-versus-partial semantics, error attribution, and repeat submission behavior.
Verify webhook/event authenticity, replay controls, schema version, tenant routing, deduplication, and order assumptions; acknowledge only after the required durable acceptance step.
Document event identity, ordering scope, event time versus processing time, retention, poison messages, and safe replay; do not infer exactly-once end-to-end behavior from one broker feature.
Keep API specifications and examples current through the normal delivery workflow; identify unsupported endpoints and undocumented internal consumers before retirement.
Include tenant, user/permission scope, locale, feature/config version, and other response dimensions in cache keys as appropriate; check shared-cache exposure of personalized data.
Define TTL, invalidation, stale-read allowance, negative caching, and response to permission or entitlement changes; a cache must not become a second uncontrolled authority.
Bound memory, key cardinality, stampedes, hot keys, eviction effects, and cache-outage fallback load; verify the backing system can survive intended fallback behavior.
Verify search/index/materialized-view freshness, rebuild, versioning, tenant filters, and repair after missed updates; expose appropriate consistency expectations to consumers.
Test replay and rebuild for deterministic or explicitly versioned transformations, duplicate handling, deletion tombstones, and changing business rules.
Inventory concurrently accessed state, including globals, caches, sessions, files, counters, database rows, and external resources; identify the synchronization scope actually used.
Check read-modify-write operations, check-then-act sequences, lazy initialization, and duplicate startup across workers for races and lost updates.
Verify thread/process safety of SDK clients, pools, native libraries, and shared objects; include runtime/context restrictions and supported initialization patterns.
Inspect lock scope, ordering, reentrancy, lease expiry, deadlock, starvation, and work performed while holding a lock; avoid relying on process-local locks for cross-instance guarantees.
Protect against an expired lock holder continuing to write where required, using fencing or equivalent authoritative checks; successful lease acquisition alone does not prove exclusive completion.
Check stale callbacks, reordered responses, reentrant handlers, and concurrent state updates; ensure an older result cannot overwrite newer authoritative state.
Bound parallel tasks, fan-out, recursion, buffers, and pending futures; verify backpressure reaches producers and resource usage does not grow without a limit.
Verify cancellation and task ownership for child work, detached jobs, subscriptions, and request termination; ensure critical committed work has an appropriate durable owner.
Give remote calls finite deadlines and propagate a total operation budget; distinguish connection, response, stream-idle, and total timeouts where relevant.
Retry only appropriate failures with bounded attempts/time, backoff, jitter, and provider hints; prevent retries at multiple layers from multiplying requests unexpectedly.
Treat timeout/disconnect as uncertain outcome for remote writes; reconcile provider state or reuse durable idempotency rather than blindly creating a second effect.
Define idempotency key scope, persistence, payload mismatch behavior, expiry, concurrency handling, and response replay; ensure duplicate requests cannot both pass a pre-check.
Ensure deduplication retention covers the supported retry/replay horizon or document a bounded guarantee; account for retries after process or deployment replacement.
Coordinate state change and message publication with an outbox, transactional facility, or explicit reconciliation strategy where atomicity matters.
Define compensation and repair for multi-system workflows; compensation itself can fail, retry, or become invalid after intervening user actions.
Check fallback, circuit-breaker, and bulkhead behavior against business restrictions; ensure degraded paths do not grant authority, hide data loss, or overwhelm another dependency.
Verify durable enqueue, consumer acknowledgement, visibility/lease duration, crash windows, redelivery, and completion recording against the queue's actual semantics.
Exercise duplicate, delayed, missing, and out-of-order messages; define per-entity ordering and conflict resolution instead of assuming global FIFO.
Bound worker concurrency, queue retention, message size, consumer lag, retries, and dead-letter growth; identify overload rejection or shedding behavior.
Give poison-message quarantine, investigation, redrive, and disposal an owner; verify redrive respects authorization, schema versions, and idempotency.
Make long jobs checkpointable and restartable where required; avoid partial output appearing complete and define cleanup/reconciliation for abandoned attempts.
Check scheduled-work timezone, daylight-saving behavior, missed runs, overlapping runs, leader election, duplicate external schedulers, and behavior after extended downtime.
Revalidate actor/tenant permissions for delayed work where necessary; define what happens after account suspension, deletion, entitlement expiry, or credential rotation.
Ensure job payloads are version-compatible across rolling deployments; support or intentionally retire queued old work and observe resulting failures.
Separate startup, readiness, liveness, and dependency health semantics; avoid a liveness response that creates restart storms during a dependency outage.
Stop accepting work, drain bounded in-flight tasks, release leases, and close owned resources on shutdown; account for the platform's actual termination deadline.
Exercise cold starts, restarts during writes, network partitions, connection resets, disk/full quota, exhausted pools, and provider throttling in authorized bounded environments.
Confirm overload signals and degraded behavior are visible to operators and callers; include recovery behavior after backlog or dependency restoration.
Check that recovery, replay, or failover cannot create two active writers or duplicate side effects; state which system is authoritative during transition.
Verify stale DNS/connections, rotated credentials, time skew, and changed configuration do not require an undocumented manual restart or silently leave part of the fleet broken.
Inventory direct/transitive runtime and development packages, vendored code, binaries, containers, plugins, generators, actions, and downloaded build tools with their actual consumers.

Verify package identity, registry, publisher/provenance, repository, necessity, and maintenance; investigate typosquatting, dependency confusion, unexpected registry fallback, and fabricated AI suggestions.
Inspect install/build scripts, postinstall hooks, native extensions, and remote downloads for unexpected execution or network access; avoid exposing unrelated credentials during installation.
Use supported package tooling and appropriate committed lockfiles; confirm CI uses the intended frozen/locked install behavior rather than silently resolving a different graph.
