Review floating versions, Git references, mutable container tags, unverified binaries, and remote script execution; select pinning/integrity controls and update ownership appropriate to exposure.
Check runtime/framework/compiler/base-image support windows and upgrade paths against current primary documentation; record exact versions rather than assuming a named major version is supported.
Scan the actual lockfiles, runtime artifacts, OS packages, images, and relevant native components; distinguish scanner coverage gaps from absence of vulnerabilities.
Triage advisories by affected version/configuration, reachable paths, exploit preconditions, exposure, available fixes, and compensating controls; time-bound suppressions with an owner.
Remove unnecessary dependencies and duplicate libraries; evaluate replacement cost, API behavior, licenses, and security rather than selecting the smallest package count blindly.
Retain an appropriate component inventory or SBOM with artifact/version context where warranted; coordinate attribution and redistribution obligations with module 11.
Verify a clean checkout can install, configure, build, and start with documented supported tools and placeholder configuration; distinguish documented steps from a developer's cached environment.
Identify generated inputs, code generators, compiler options, environment-dependent constants, and build-time network requirements; ensure required inputs are versioned or reliably obtainable.

Check build determinism and traceability to the degree required by the project; record toolchain, lockfile, source revision, and artifact identity without claiming bit-for-bit reproducibility unless measured.
Verify path casing, line endings, executable permissions, locale/encoding, shell behavior, symlinks, filesystem layout, and supported CPU/OS differences that can break clean builds.
Inspect bundling, tree shaking, conditional exports, source maps, production/debug flags, and environment replacement for omitted required code or exposed secrets/internal source.
Check incremental/remote build caches for correct input keys, cross-branch or cross-tenant contamination, poisoning by untrusted builds, and behavior after cache invalidation.
Verify monorepo affected-build logic includes shared types, schemas, generated clients, config, and transitive dependents; ensure changed packages cannot evade necessary checks.

Ensure release packaging includes required runtime files, migrations, templates, assets, native libraries, notices, and compatible dependency versions; test the packaged output rather than only source mode.
Separate untrusted pull-request execution from privileged workflows; inspect fork triggers, checkout choices, reusable workflows, and contexts that can expose secrets or write tokens.
Scope CI tokens, cloud identities, registry access, signing, and deployment permissions to required actions/environments; prefer bounded credentials supported by the platform.
Review third-party actions, runners, images, caches, and downloaded tools as supply-chain dependencies; assess pinning, provenance, update, and isolation practices.

Confirm intended lint/type/build/security gates actually execute, fail the job on material errors, cover the right paths, and cannot be bypassed by ignored exit codes or misleading status aggregation.
Prevent secrets and private data in logs, environment dumps, test reports, source maps, caches, and uploaded artifacts; check retention and artifact access boundaries.
Identify the artifact built, reviewed, scanned, promoted, and deployed; detect rebuilding from mutable inputs between approval and deployment or swapping artifact tags.
Review branch/release permissions, required reviews, emergency bypasses, and auditability proportionately; verify an accountable path exists even when a small team combines roles.
Check concurrent releases, cancelled jobs, partial deployments, environment targeting, and rollback selection for stale artifacts or unintended overwrites.
Maintain a typed/validated configuration contract, safe defaults, documented required fields, and environment separation; fail clearly for invalid critical configuration.
Distinguish build-time from runtime variables, public from secret variables, and process-local from centrally refreshed config; verify actual precedence and deployed values without exposing secrets.

Check container build contexts, ignore rules, layers, image source, dependency stage boundaries, architecture, and runtime files; deletion in a later layer does not remove secrets from earlier layers.

Verify the packaged process handles signals, non-root/readonly constraints where intended, writable paths, working directory, health endpoints, and shutdown deadlines; use module 12 for deployed privilege evidence.
Confirm feature flags and remote config have ownership, safe behavior when unavailable, change visibility, and consistency expectations across replicas and clients.
Document ordinary update cadence, urgent vulnerability response, rollback/forward-repair constraints, and a responsible maintainer before dependencies become unsupported.
Check server/client module boundaries, hydration, serialized props, source maps, and environment injection for private data or server credentials reaching browser code.
Verify server rendering, static generation, edge caching, and streaming use the correct user/tenant context; shared output must not contain personalized state.
Exercise pending, empty, failed, stale, and partial states; prevent duplicate submissions and stale responses from replacing newer user intent.
Check component subscriptions, timers, observers, event handlers, retained DOM, and route changes for leaked resources or repeated side effects.
Verify optimistic updates reconcile server failure, conflict, permission loss, and refetch; do not allow client state to become authoritative for money or access.
Inspect service-worker lifecycle, cache versioning, logout/private-data cleanup, stale offline assets, and mixed frontend/backend releases.
Check navigation/deep links, back/forward behavior, form restoration, locale handling, bundle boundaries, and supported browser APIs against actual product requirements.
Keep UI state and domain rules separable where useful; coordinate semantic interaction, focus, loading/error announcements, and keyboard behavior with the accessibility audit.
Verify middleware order, proxy trust, authentication context, request-body consumption, exception boundaries, and request-scoped state isolation in the actual framework lifecycle.
Check cold start, execution-duration limits, ephemeral filesystem, freeze/resume, connection reuse, detached work, and local-state assumptions for serverless/edge targets.
For WebSocket/subscription/SSE paths, check authorization at connect and during lifetime, tenant routing, reconnect/resume, heartbeat, fan-out bounds, and slow-consumer handling.
Check GraphQL or flexible-query surfaces for field authorization, nested query cost, batching, pagination, error leakage, and data-loader cache scope where applicable.
Review multi-process/prefork workers, hot reload, singleton initialization, startup jobs, and context propagation for behavior that differs from single-process development mode.
Check application lifecycle, suspend/resume, process death, background restrictions, interrupted writes, and restart recovery on supported platforms.
Review local storage, secure credential facilities, log/crash exports, clipboard, notifications, and backup behavior for sensitive state and account/tenant switching.
Verify offline queues, conflict resolution, tombstones, identity changes, expired authority, and clock differences; define what happens to pending work after logout or account deletion.
Check deep links, IPC, custom protocols, embedded webviews, file associations, and desktop bridges for caller validation and unintended privileged actions.
Confirm update signatures/integrity where supported, old-client compatibility, data-format migration, rollback limits, permission changes, and interrupted installation behavior.
Exercise reconnect on unstable/metered networks, duplicate push delivery, permission denial, unavailable platform services, and device resource pressure without unbounded retries.
Libraries, CLIs, plugins, and native code
For public packages, verify exported API/types, packaging targets, semantic compatibility commitments, peer dependencies, documented examples, and consumers of the actual published artifact.
Libraries, CLIs, plugins, and native code
For CLI tools, check argument parsing, stdin/TTY behavior, exit codes, stdout versus stderr, signal handling, noninteractive operation, and stable machine-readable output where promised.
Libraries, CLIs, plugins, and native code
Make filesystem writes, overwrite/recursive operations, working-directory assumptions, shell quoting, symbolic links, and partial-output cleanup explicit for automation and local tools.
Libraries, CLIs, plugins, and native code
Check plugin discovery, version compatibility, permission boundaries, dependency conflicts, lifecycle cleanup, and behavior when an extension fails; dynamic usage affects deletion decisions.
Libraries, CLIs, plugins, and native code
For native/FFI code, examine ownership, lifetimes, bounds, alignment, integer conversion, unsafe blocks, ABI/layout compatibility, thread affinity, and error propagation across language boundaries.
Libraries, CLIs, plugins, and native code
Review sandboxing or process isolation for untrusted extensions where required; loading a plugin in-process generally exposes the host's ambient authority.
AI, data pipelines, search, and automation
Separate prompts, retrieval, deterministic domain rules, model calls, parsing, tool selection, execution authority, and persistence; validate outputs before they become code, queries, or actions.
AI, data pipelines, search, and automation
Version model/config/prompt/schema/embedding dependencies where reproducibility matters; define behavior after model retirement, response-format drift, or changed embedding dimensions.
AI, data pipelines, search, and automation
Scope retrieval, vector/search indexes, caches, conversation history, and generated exports to authorized tenants/users; ingestion filters alone cannot establish query-time isolation.
AI, data pipelines, search, and automation
Bound agent/tool loops, token budgets, provider retries, context growth, paid calls, and concurrent sessions; coordinate quality/evaluation and spend evidence with modules 07 and 08.
AI, data pipelines, search, and automation
For ETL/analytics, check event-time windows, late/duplicate records, schema drift, checkpoints, backfill/replay, aggregation units, and reconciliation against the source.
AI, data pipelines, search, and automation

Separate training/evaluation/serving artifacts where relevant; review data leakage, version lineage, rollout compatibility, and safe fallback without inventing model-quality guarantees from unit tests.
AI, data pipelines, search, and automation
For scheduled automation, inventory triggers outside the repository, identity/permissions, overlapping runs, idempotency, credential expiry, and an owned disable/recovery path.
Games, realtime simulation, embedded, and specialist products
For games/simulation, check frame/tick budgets, allocation spikes, asset lifetime, scene/state transitions, object pooling reset, save/load versioning, and deterministic replay where promised.
Games, realtime simulation, embedded, and specialist products
For multiplayer, verify authoritative state, client prediction/reconciliation, ordering, lag/disconnect/rejoin, abuse boundaries, and identity/entitlement checks outside client code.
Games, realtime simulation, embedded, and specialist products
For embedded/IoT, review watchdog behavior, bounded memory, real-time deadlines, power-loss-safe writes, firmware update integrity/recovery, and hardware/driver dependencies.
Games, realtime simulation, embedded, and specialist products
For financial/inventory/booking systems, trace conservation and exclusivity invariants, reconciliation, concurrent reservations, expiry, decimal precision, and compensating actions.
Games, realtime simulation, embedded, and specialist products
For large files/media/geospatial/scientific workloads, check streaming versus full buffering, coordinate systems/units, precision, malformed inputs, native codec limits, and bounded processing.
Games, realtime simulation, embedded, and specialist products
For regulated or safety-sensitive systems, identify applicable specialist assurance and accountable reviewers; this general library cannot establish compliance or replace hazard analysis.
Map critical invariants and failure modes to existing checks, bounded manual evidence, or an explicit gap; coverage percentages and test counts are not substitutes for this mapping.
Choose a focused unit, integration, contract, end-to-end, property, or manual check based on the boundary at risk; do not require every test category for every change.
Verify assertions observe meaningful outcomes and durable side effects, not only mocked calls or implementation structure; test data must make an incorrect implementation fail.
Inspect mocks/fakes for drift from provider, database, queue, clock, filesystem, and authorization semantics; use appropriate boundary evidence for material differences.
Include important negative and transition cases such as stale authority, duplicate submission, crash/retry windows, old schema/client versions, and cancellation after a side effect where applicable.
Verify checks run with production-relevant modes and packaged artifacts when those differ from development; an in-memory database may not exercise actual transaction or lock behavior.
Keep tests independent of order, ambient environment, current date, shared mutable accounts, and uncontrolled network state; control nondeterminism when it affects reproducibility.
Investigate flakiness and quarantines with an owner, gap statement, and expiry; never delete a valuable check solely to make CI pass.
Retain only distinct necessary regression/boundary assurance; remove one-off, obsolete, duplicate, trivial, or implementation-mirroring session checks and orphan fixtures/dependencies.
Confirm scripts and runners propagate failures, execute intended tests, and do not silently pass after zero tests, skipped suites, ignored exit codes, or stale result uploads.
Run focused verification for changes and directly affected flows; broaden or repeat only after relevant changes, failures, or unresolved dependencies rather than a per-session quota.
Record commands, revision/environment, actual results, skipped checks, limitations, and bounded manual steps; distinguish planned, simulated, and executed verification.
Trace a critical operation across request, job, database, and provider boundaries using appropriate correlation; avoid exposing credentials, private prompts, or unnecessary personal data.
Log actionable failures with cause and context, and distinguish expected rejection from internal failure; avoid swallowed errors, noisy duplicate logs, and success metrics emitted before commit.
Bound log/metric/trace volume and label cardinality, sampling, payload size, and retention; observability must not create an unbounded cost or resource path.
Measure hot-path latency distributions, workload shape, dataset size, concurrency, and resource use before proposing performance refactors; record the baseline and changed result.
Inspect algorithmic complexity, repeated serialization, allocations, memory retention, blocking event loops, excessive network calls, and unbounded computation where workload evidence warrants it.
Check resource budgets and performance under supported worst-case inputs, realistic data growth, cold/warm cache, and saturation; averages can hide tail failures and memory growth.
Ensure application signals can reveal failed invariants, stuck jobs, backlog, dependency degradation, and migration failures; coordinate operational alerts and ownership with module 10.
Verify debug/profiling endpoints, verbose modes, and diagnostics are appropriately controlled in deployed environments and that retained artifacts serve a continuing purpose.
Have a maintainer follow setup/build/run instructions from a clean checkout; record missing steps and unavailable prerequisites rather than relying on the original author's environment.
Document system boundaries, domain invariants, data authority, external dependencies, important decisions, and known limits in a concise maintained source of truth.
Assign ownership for shared modules, migrations, dependencies, releases, urgent fixes, scheduled jobs, and recovery; identify gaps when the original author is unavailable.
Match code review depth to risk and include AI-generated changes; verify an accountable reviewer can explain the behavior and evidence behind material changes.
Keep branch/merge/release practices understandable and proportionate, with a route for urgent repair and a record of exceptional bypasses; avoid accidental overwrites of concurrent work.
Link runbooks to architecture decisions, recovery dependencies, artifact versions, and known rollback limits; perform the specialist recovery checks before claiming recovery is proven.
Define debt items through actual cost, failure risk, owner, smallest useful remedy, and revisit trigger; avoid backlogs consisting only of preferences or indefinite rewrites.
Finish with verified findings, reduction outcomes, justified retentions, unresolved usage/evidence, accepted risks, and a sequenced remediation plan; do not imply a report alone fixes the project.

headings.text: Cost, quotas and abuse audit library
Audit Hidden recurring costs, quotas and abuse
Required discovery of recurring work and hidden spend
Eliminate unnecessary recurring work and charges
Verify that work and charges actually stop
Cost, quotas and abuse audit output

values: Record project, source/deployed revisions, environments, audit window and timezone, owners, authorized access, allowed test surfaces, spending ceiling and stop conditions. Identify production dependencies used by staging or local development.

Enumerate cloud organizations/accounts/projects, regions, hosting, VPSs, SaaS, payment methods and reseller arrangements. Include former providers, employee-managed accounts and services billed outside the main cloud invoice. Mark inaccessible accounts Not verified.

Trace costly user journeys from entry point through authorization, admission, reservation, queue, worker, provider, persistence and delivery. Include administrative actions, public demos, mobile/desktop clients, SDKs, imports, exports, webhooks and support tools.

Inventory shared infrastructure and ownership boundaries. Separate application spend from common databases, networks, observability, CI and account-level quotas. Identify who can change global settings and who receives bills.
Classify assets and features as active, disabled, retired, planned or unknown. Confirm disabled features cannot still be invoked through APIs, old clients, scheduler entries or retained credentials.

Inventory physical capacity as well as money: disk/inodes, memory, CPU/GPU, DB connections, queue depth, file descriptors, sockets, IPs, provider quotas and worker slots. A fixed-price server can still be exhausted.
Include local agents, unattended browser sessions, developer scripts, notebooks, evaluation runs, test credentials and externally hosted automations if they consume project funds or shared resources.

Record provider, service/SKU, billing unit, unit scale, currency, region, pricing source and retrieval date. Distinguish tokens from requests, characters from messages, decimal GB from GiB, and elapsed duration from rounded billable duration.

Document fixed fees, minimums, tiers, rounding, failed-request charging, ingress/egress, retrieval, storage, per-seat charges, taxes, discounts, credit expiry, commitments and overage rules. Verify the rules that materially affect this project's estimate.

Reconcile invoice/usage exports to resources, jobs and features over the same period. Explain unknown/unallocated spend, currency conversion, invoice lag and adjustments. A missing tag or zero dashboard value is not proof of no cost.

Establish cost attribution to environment, feature, tenant and outcome where feasible. Include unattributed shared costs explicitly and use a documented allocation driver; do not count the same charge in multiple totals.

Separate provider cost, customer price, product credits and capacity units. Document conversion, precision and rounding for each. A credit is not automatically one currency unit or one provider request.

Protect pricing and attribution configuration from untrusted inputs. Verify a client cannot select a privileged billing owner, free cost code, arbitrary provider credential or cheaper accounting class for expensive work.

Measure representative cost per successful outcome, including failed attempts, retries, validation, moderation, downstream calls, storage, delivery and attributable shared cost. Keep success criteria and denominator consistent.
Model ordinary, heavy legitimate, launch/burst, retry-storm and abusive usage. Include advertised maximum plan usage, slow consumers, long-lived sessions and inactive accounts retaining assets.

For every expensive path, identify a measured or conservative per-operation upper bound and the control enforcing it. Treat unbounded fan-out, duration or output as unknown exposure rather than inventing a finite estimate.

Estimate remaining financial exposure after a stop: accepted/in-flight work, backlog that cannot be cancelled, provider reporting delay, stop propagation, accrued usage and fixed commitments. Avoid double counting queued and in-flight operations.

Compare revenue excluding applicable pass-through taxes with variable costs, payment fees, expected refunds/fraud and support burden under the same scenario. Separate contribution margin from fully allocated profit.
Assess plan pooling, unlimited claims, free tier resets, annual/monthly mismatch and shared customer accounts. Record deliberate subsidies or loss leaders with an owner and bounded budget.
Estimate optimization payback after implementation effort, migration, reliability, support and rollback costs. Avoid adding infrastructure whose total burden exceeds credible savings.

Select test dimensions explicitly: identity/role/plan, tenant, credential, route/version, region/replica, sync/async, normal/failure state, billing/reset boundary and cache state. Inspect all materially distinct admission paths and expand samples after inconsistent results.

Use synthetic identities/data, low balances and controllable provider stubs first. Set request/concurrency/duration ceilings, cancellation and cleanup before execution. A test plan alone is Not verified runtime behavior.

For live provider checks, confirm allowed environment, destinations, maximum billable calls and budget. Avoid real recipient spam, bulk account creation, uncontrolled load and third-party abuse testing. Record which provider effects remain untested.

Attach expected/actual results, request/job/ledger/provider IDs, starting and ending counters, errors and elapsed time. Redact keys, personal data, payment details and sensitive payloads while preserving correlation.

Prioritize active material financial loss or capacity exhaustion for incident containment; treat reproducible unbounded public spending or a material quota race as potential release blockers. Set thresholds from project risk and available funds, not a universal amount.

Record workflow state separately from check status. Assign action, owner, dependency, acceptance test, effort, rollback and due/review date. Accepted risk needs an accountable decision and expiry; it does not turn a failed control into Pass.

Inspect system/user cron, timers, Windows Task Scheduler, hosting/Coolify schedules, application timers, queue repeaters, DB schedulers, CI schedules and external automation providers. Include synthetic checks, analytics exports and uptime monitors.

Cover production, staging, previews, old releases, disaster-recovery environments, personal sandboxes, all known regions/accounts and shared infrastructure. Reconcile discovered jobs against code and declared architecture.
Record each scheduler ID, executable/workflow revision, credentials, owner, consumer, business purpose, cadence/timezone, enabled state, last/next run, typical/max duration and downstream cost chain.

Check overlapping runs, per-replica registration, leader changes, deployment duplication, daylight-saving transitions, catch-up after downtime and scheduler misfire policies. Confirm intended behavior during clock changes and timezone edits.

Identify duplicate polling/sync loops, obsolete migrations, ownerless notifications, synthetic traffic generating real jobs and tasks still running after trial, tenant, feature or environment retirement.
Bound each job's runtime, work units, pagination, fan-out, concurrency, retry/backoff and backfill horizon. Include failed/no-op runs, empty scans and jobs that schedule their own successors.
Verify leases and overlap controls under slow runs, lost locks and restarts. A lease expiry must not silently authorize duplicate irreversible provider effects.
Reconcile scheduler status to execution logs, queue state and provider usage. An enabled job with no log access and a disabled job with residual queue work both need explicit evidence gaps.

Inventory VMs, containers, clusters, GPU instances, databases/replicas, object stores, volumes, snapshots, backups, image registries, public IPs, load balancers, gateways, DNS zones and paid network features.
Inspect stopped workloads for attached storage, reserved addresses, snapshots, replicas, licenses and commitments. Confirm which charges continue despite no application traffic.

Find abandoned previews, branch databases, development environments, stale deployment images and resources outside infrastructure-as-code state. Inspect failed/partial provisioning and deleted projects' residual assets.

Inventory SaaS seats, dormant members, paid add-ons, domains/certificates where charged, support plans, marketplace subscriptions and organization-wide licenses. Check whether removing a user actually releases a paid seat.
Record renewal/notice dates, contractual minimums, non-cancellable commitments, trial/credit expiry, auto-upgrades and top-ups. Distinguish avoidable usage from charges already committed.

Match resources and renewals to current owners and consumers. Search invoices/payment records for providers absent from current source and verify legitimate shared use before classifying them as waste.
Check tagging/ownership drift and environment TTL policies. Exemptions need an owner, reason and review date; a TTL must not delete essential recovery or customer data automatically.
Classify each candidate as retire, consolidate, reduce, retain with justification or investigate. Include baseline cost, expected savings range, risk, dependencies and decision owner.

For retained schedules, justify cadence against freshness requirements. Compare batch/event-driven processing, conditional requests, change detection, empty-work skipping and consolidation using total operating cost.
Right-size necessary resources using representative peaks, recovery requirements and measured headroom. Compare scale-to-zero or shutdown savings against startup latency and residual charges.

Remove obsolete schedules at their authoritative scheduler and update code, CI, infrastructure definitions and repeaters that could recreate them. Confirm old deployments and every replica are covered.
Drain or cancel queued/in-flight work under documented integrity rules. Define treatment of reserved credits, partial results, downstream cancellation and user communication.

Before deleting data/resources, check shared dependencies, retention obligations, legal holds, restore needs, export requirements and cancellation terms. Execute only within the actual authorized implementation scope.

After retirement, revoke obsolete credentials and triggers where appropriate, remove dangling integrations and update inventories/runbooks. Verify revocation does not stop a still-needed shared consumer.
Prevent recreation from rollback images, bootstrap scripts, deployment hooks, forgotten CI branches and disaster-recovery templates. Preserve a deliberate restoration path for necessary services.

Retain before/after scheduler configuration, queue counts, execution logs, resource state and provider effects. Observe the next trigger or use equivalent bounded verification of the scheduler without waiting for a long billing cycle.
Verify essential flows, backups and recovery behavior affected by the reduction. A successful deletion is not evidence that shared consumers remain healthy.
Separate immediate usage reduction, projected monthly savings and realized invoiced savings. Record reporting delay, workload changes, credits, fixed commitments and residual retention costs.

Assign an owner and date for delayed billing confirmation. Check for recreated resources, continuing renewals and cancellation acknowledgements. Do not close financial verification solely because source files disappeared.

Define the unit charged for every costly operation and the authoritative balance/usage store. Specify whether quota measures attempts, successful outcomes, input/output units, reserved capacity, retained bytes or a combination.

Document reservation, commit, adjustment, refund, expiry, reset and reconciliation transitions. Distinguish product-credit refunds from actual provider refunds; a failed customer outcome can still cost money.

State invariants: accepted liability stays within authorized balance plus explicit bounded overage; one logical debit/refund per defined operation; currency/credit precision is deterministic; customer balances and provider charges are reconciled separately.
Separate rolling rate limits, period usage, prepaid credits, storage quota, worker slots and monetary budgets. Exhaustion of any applicable limit must have defined admission and recovery behavior.

Record quota scopes and hierarchy: user, member, tenant, organization, project, credential, feature, provider and global account. Apply all required constraints atomically or through a documented conservative admission design.
Establish how balances are purchased, granted, expired, transferred and adjusted. Require server-authoritative amounts and scoped admin permissions; log manual grants, overrides and reversals.

Enforce current permissions and quota before paid effects on direct APIs, workers, retries, revisions, exports, imports, previews and administrative tools. Include legacy API versions and alternate transports.
Verify atomic admission near a balance boundary across simultaneous requests, replicas and regions. A separate read-then-debit or stale cache must not allow overspending.

Make multi-unit and batch operations reserve their full bounded liability or incrementally admit each unit. Check partial batches, per-item failures and pagination; one request must not conceal unlimited work.

For variable-cost work, reserve a conservative bounded maximum, meter bounded increments or reject when an upper bound cannot be enforced. Define handling when actual usage differs, without silently creating unlimited debt.

Test ledger/limiter store outages, timeouts, stale reads, failover and partitions. Paid work needs an explicit fail-closed or strictly bounded degraded allowance; monitor consumption of that allowance.
Prevent negative, zero, non-finite, oversized, fractional or overflowing input quantities from bypassing accounting. Use suitable precision and rounding consistently at admission and settlement.
Verify usage/budget writes cannot be performed by the client or by unauthorized tenant/admin roles. Check object ownership when a request supplies project, wallet, membership or credential IDs.
Verify quota enforcement and ledger state survive restart, restore and redeploy. Restoring a stale DB or rebuilding a counter must not restore already consumed credits without reconciliation.
Scope idempotency keys to principal, operation and request semantics. Same-key/same-payload retries converge; same-key/different-payload requests are rejected or handled by an explicit safe policy.
Bound key size, storage and retention. Retention must cover the actual retry/replay window, or a durable business identifier must prevent repeated financial effects after cache expiry.
Exercise duplicate HTTP requests, queue deliveries, provider callbacks and operator retries. Check logical operation, provider effect, output delivery and ledger settlement independently.

Test crashes before/after reservation, queue publication, provider acceptance, provider completion and local settlement. Ensure recovery neither loses accepted work nor blindly repeats irreversible spending.
Treat an external timeout as an ambiguous result when appropriate. Query/reconcile provider status or use provider idempotency; do not assume no charge or instantly refund and retry without a bound.
Expire stale reservations safely. Verify late workers cannot execute against released capacity without reauthorization, and that heartbeat/lease loss cannot cause both refund and continued paid work.

Define cancellation, disconnect and partial-success policy. Reconcile consumed units, residual output, late completion and refunds; a closed browser or failed stream is not proof that provider work stopped.
Prevent refund/cancellation loops from yielding repeated useful output without net quota consumption. Apply the disclosed policy fairly when the platform or provider failed.
Test trial expiry, failed/delinquent payment, cancellation, scheduled downgrade, upgrade and reactivation with direct costly operations. Do not rely solely on the UI or on timely callbacks.
Define when queued work inherits admission rights and when workers must recheck current rights. Test revocation or downgrade while work is queued/running and contain remaining liability.

Check calendar, subscription-anniversary and rolling resets; record timezone, period IDs, boundary inclusivity, leap-day behavior and clock authority. Concurrent reset/settlement must not double grant or lose usage.
Define whether rollover, promotional and purchased credits expire, their consumption order and caps. Test expiry during reservations and refunds into an expired bucket.

Test multiple memberships, tenant switching, team pooling, member removal and moving projects between organizations. Ensure balances cannot be borrowed from unrelated tenants or multiplied by adding seats/keys.

Test API key rotation, account deletion/recreation, email changes and region changes against period and trial history. Respect the project's privacy/retention rules while preventing unintended re-grants.
Replay delayed, duplicated and out-of-order financial events. Verify the authoritative payment state and effective time drive access and credit changes exactly as intended, with no duplicate grant.

Verify UI, API and support tools show consistent remaining/reserved/used units, reset time and reasons for denial. Indicate estimates or delayed metering honestly and avoid exposing other tenants' usage.

Reconcile admitted operations, reservations, commits, refunds and adjustments with worker state and provider records. Attribute unexplained discrepancies and duplicate charges rather than silently overwriting balances.

Protect ledger/audit retention and correction history. Use compensating adjustments where appropriate; restrict destructive edits and ensure debugging logs do not expose secrets or unnecessary payloads.

Execute the low-balance burst, duplicate, crash, ambiguous-outcome and reset scenarios in [07](07-EXECUTABLE-SCENARIOS-AND-EVIDENCE.md). Record accepted work and provider effects, including after the initial HTTP response.

Inventory public and authenticated costly routes, old versions, GraphQL operations, WebSockets, streaming endpoints, upload initiation/completion, webhooks and worker entry points. Map each to its actual admission control.
Combine sustained rate, burst, concurrency, duration, payload, result-size and spend limits according to resource demand. Requests/minute alone cannot bound a slow stream or expensive batch.

Select keys using authenticated identity/tenant and trustworthy network context. Verify which proxy sets forwarding headers, reject spoofed identity signals and cover direct-origin access where it is exposed.

Test limit sharing across replicas, regions, workers and restarts. Document whether the algorithm is fixed-window, sliding-window, token-bucket or another design, including any boundary burst allowance.

Check alternate route aliases, methods, content types, API versions, case/encoding variations and credential rotation for unintended separate limit buckets. Canonicalization must preserve authorization semantics.

Verify batch APIs, GraphQL aliases/nesting and multi-recipient actions are charged and limited by bounded underlying work. Cover complexity, pagination and response amplification as well as request count.
Bound open connections, streams, subscriptions and polling frequency. Release capacity after disconnect, timeout and worker death; cap reconnect/resubscribe storms and slow readers.

Apply cheap rejection before expensive parsing, database scans, cryptography, media conversion or provider calls where feasible. Bound decompression, parser nesting, regex work and malformed input processing.
Document limiter-state outages and edge/origin disagreement. Ensure degraded operation has a known bound and an alert rather than implicitly allowing unlimited costly work.

Return suitable denial responses and retry guidance without leaking cross-tenant balances. Use 429 for rate rejection where appropriate; if Retry-After is supplied, verify clients respect it and add bounded backoff/jitter.
Bound limiter key cardinality and expiry so rotating attacker-controlled values cannot exhaust the limiter store. Avoid logging one large event for every blocked request during an attack.
Model repeated signups, disposable identities, referral rings, self-referrals, trial resets and promotion stacking. Verify controls at the actual grant/consumption boundary, not only the signup form.
Check anonymous demos, guest accounts, invite flows and onboarding previews for material spending before verification. Define per-visitor, per-account and global free-use exposure.
Inspect coupon validation, redemption concurrency, campaign/recipient scope, expiry and combination rules. Reject client-controlled discounts, currency confusion and duplicate bonus grants.
Ensure referral rewards require the intended qualifying event and cannot be amplified by replayed callbacks, multiple memberships, refunds or immediate cancellations.

Apply risk-based verification and progressive allowances when justified. CAPTCHA, email verification and payment checks supplement server budgets; assess accessibility, privacy, false positives and dependency cost.

Distinguish abusive automation from intended API clients, accessibility tools, shared office/mobile IPs and high-value batch users. Provide a controlled appeal/review route and scoped exceptions with expiry.
Inspect internal/support override paths and compromised admin scenarios. Limit who can grant unrestricted credits, remove blocks or enable overage, and retain accountable audit records.
Bound login, signup, reset, verification-code, contact, invite, email/SMS and resend flows by account, destination, tenant and global provider budget. Avoid using real recipients in tests.

Check SMS/voice destination countries, premium/high-cost routes, message segmentation, repeated OTP sends and telephony fraud. Verify destination policies server-side and include provider-side restrictions where available.

Prevent email contact forms and notification templates from becoming arbitrary relays. Bound recipients, attachments, rendered output and webhook-triggered notification loops; monitor bounces/complaints and sender reputation.

Assess scraping, bulk export and data enumeration for resource amplification and commercial harm. Authorize datasets, bound result sets and pace expensive exports without relying on robots.txt as enforcement.
Check reservation, stock, appointment and game-economy flows for hoarding or artificial scarcity. Bound held capacity, release expiry safely and avoid rewarding repetitive cancel/rebook cycles.

Verify public media, download links, embedding and hotlink access policies. Where signed URLs are used, inspect authorization at issuance, expiry, cache behavior and bounded remaining exposure after revocation.

Treat leaked credentials and unintended open proxies as spending risks. Scope credentials and outbound integrations; prevent user-supplied URLs/models/destinations from turning a feature into an unrestricted paid relay.
Bound callback/replay processing and authenticate integrations before expensive work. Validly signed duplicate events can still cause amplification if deduplication or downstream budgets are missing.
Test noisy-neighbor behavior with synthetic tenants. Protect a legitimate tenant's worker slots, database connections and provider capacity when another reaches its allowance or behaves abusively.
Set priorities, fair queues or reserved capacity where the product needs them. Bound both work items and their weights; prevent one heavy job or high-priority producer from starving others.
Verify suspension/revocation reaches sessions, keys, workers, retries and queued work. Record residual liability from already issued links and remote work that cannot be cancelled.
Keep block evidence proportionate and privacy-conscious. Document reason, scope, operator, expiry/review and recovery, while preserving an appeal route appropriate to the product.
Execute bounded bypass, trial replay, multi-replica and fairness cases from [07](07-EXECUTABLE-SCENARIOS-AND-EVIDENCE.md). Record false positives alongside prevented work and cost.

Inventory inference, embeddings, reranking, moderation, OCR, transcription, speech, image/video generation, retrieval stores, hosted tools and evaluation pipelines. Include local GPU rental and resources retained between calls.
Enforce server-controlled allowed models, providers, quality, resolution, duration, variants and input/output limits. Reject client-supplied premium selections or credentials that bypass plan rules.

Bound total context, retrieved documents, conversation growth, attachments, intermediate results and generated output. Include provider-billed categories not visible in the final user response where applicable.
Bound agent turns, tool calls, recursion depth, parallel branches, wall time and total run budget across all children. A per-model-call limit cannot contain an unbounded autonomous loop.

Put costly tool execution behind policy and budget checks independent of generated text. Test untrusted documents/tool results attempting to increase workload, change models or trigger repeated paid actions using synthetic fixtures.
Reauthorize continuations, retries, revisions, regenerate buttons and resumed runs. Prevent splitting a long task into unlimited nominally free continuations.

Verify stream disconnect/cancellation propagation to provider and child tools. Meter actual consumed units, document uncancellable work and prevent automatic retry merely because the client saw no final answer.
Define fallback provider/model policy with maximum cost and allowed capabilities. Test outages and throttling; do not silently move to a more expensive or unapproved service.

Inspect prompt/result caches for tenant isolation, expiry, actual cache-hit billing and invalidation. Test cache misses/evictions and adversarial unique inputs so budget safety does not depend on optimistic hit rates.

Bound evaluation datasets, experiment sweeps, prompt tuning, benchmark retries and developer playgrounds. Attribute evaluation spending separately from production and prevent scheduled tests from multiplying across branches.
Bound queue depth/bytes, per-tenant backlog, oldest age, worker concurrency and accepted liability. Apply backpressure before admission when work cannot finish within the promised service or budget.
Limit retries at every layer: client, SDK, gateway, worker, workflow and provider. Calculate combined attempt multiplication and bound retry horizon with backoff/jitter.
Test poison messages, visibility/lease expiry, worker crashes, redrive and dead-letter replay. Prevent repeated permanent failures from consuming unlimited money or repeatedly notifying users.
Bound fan-out across workflows, map/reduce jobs, webhooks and callbacks. Detect self-triggering object updates or bidirectional sync loops; include downstream work in the parent budget.
Batch only where it lowers total cost without violating latency or isolation. Count per-item provider units and partial failures, and cap response expansion and intermediate persistence.

Compare webhooks/event-driven updates with polling costs and reliability needs. For retained polling, use bounded pagination, cursors/conditional fetches where supported, empty-work skipping and a justified cadence.

Enforce per-file, total stored bytes, object count, temporary storage and tenant quotas. Check multipart uploads, concurrent uploads, overwritten versions, chunked transfer and unknown content lengths.

Issue upload/download credentials only after authorization and bounded admission. Verify actual bytes/object metadata after upload; constrain expiry, object key, content size/type and allowed operations as the platform supports.

Inspect abandoned multipart parts, incomplete uploads, failed exports, thumbnails, transformed copies, object versions, delete markers and orphan records. Cleanup must cover provider state, not only application rows.
Bound archive extraction by expanded size, file count, nesting, CPU/time and disk. Bound image dimensions, video duration, conversion profiles and generated renditions before expensive processing.
Define lifecycle/retention for originals, derivatives, exports, logs and backups. Verify implementation respects active references, shared assets, legal holds and required recovery copies.

Test logical deletion against actual reclaimed capacity and charges. Include versioning, replication, soft-delete, early-deletion/minimum-storage fees and eventual reporting; deletion may incur cost or retain recoverable copies.

Model CDN/origin egress, cross-region/zone transfer, NAT/proxy charges, cache misses, range requests and repeated downloads. Enforce bandwidth/transfer budgets appropriate to public assets and authenticated exports.

Inspect cache-key cardinality, query-string variations, image-transform parameters and cache bypass headers for origin amplification. Preserve authorization and avoid private-content leakage when improving cache reuse.

Bound query time, scanned rows/bytes, joins, sort complexity, result size and pagination. Inspect expensive search/reporting paths, missing indexes and user-controlled query patterns with safe plans or bounded fixtures.
Cap connection pools and concurrent queries across all app/worker replicas. Test idle transactions, lock contention, reconnect storms and retries against database/provider limits.

Review replicas, point-in-time recovery, backup snapshots, indexes and change streams against business needs. Include retention growth and restore/retrieval cost without weakening required recoverability.

Inspect serverless duration/memory, autoscaling maximums, minimum instances, GPU allocation and startup behavior. Verify effective organization/service quotas and the cost/capacity tradeoff of scaling ceilings.
Bound CPU/memory/temp disk/processes and downstream calls per job or container. Check OOM/crash loops, auto-restarts, rescheduling and overprovisioned idle services.

Review public IPs, gateways, cross-region replication, load balancers, health checks and licensed agents. Confirm networking/security tooling costs are attributed and proportionate to the required protection.

Inventory CI minutes, runner sizes, concurrent builds, test matrices, scheduled pipelines, artifacts, caches, container storage and preview environments. Bound retention and ensure branch deletion/expiry removes dependent resources.

Prevent untrusted contributions from accessing paid secrets or unrestricted self-hosted runners. Check workflow triggers, permissions, dependency hooks and user-controlled build inputs for unintended paid execution.
Stop redundant superseded builds when safe; avoid duplicate push/PR/scheduled runs. Inspect flaky-test reruns, failed deployment loops and multi-environment migrations for cost multiplication.
Bound log/trace/metric ingestion, retention, high-cardinality labels, payload size, debug modes and sampling. Include error storms, user-controlled log text, dashboard queries and export traffic.
Verify cost/abuse monitoring cannot itself create uncontrolled spend through one paid alert, trace or external analysis call per rejected event. Preserve enough aggregated evidence for investigation.
Inspect test and staging services for real email/SMS sends, paid model calls, production webhooks, duplicate analytics and unbounded synthetic users. Use isolated credentials and explicit budgets.

Check security scanners, uptime checks, backup verification, analytics enrichment, maps/geocoding, search APIs and licensed datasets for execution/seat/retention charges and unnecessary duplicate subscriptions.

Record monetary and capacity budgets, periods, currencies, owners, thresholds and action levels for global account, environment, feature, tenant and provider. Define which essential functions retain a bounded emergency allowance.

Classify every provider control as notification, forecast, prepaid balance, contractual cap, quota, request rejection or automated action. Document actual coverage, delay and exceptions; do not call a notification a hard spending cap.
Verify effective provider settings and permissions in the deployed account. Include auto-top-up, overage, paid-plan upgrade, credit expiry, tier changes, shared organizations and delegated accounts.

Where provider controls are absent or delayed, enforce application admission budgets from a trustworthy current ledger or conservative reservations. Include all costly paths and reserve headroom for accepted work and reporting lag.

Identify the maximum residual exposure after each stop mechanism. Include already running jobs, remote uncancellable work, long-lived sessions, queued commitments, storage, renewals and non-cancellable contracts.

Restrict budget increases, limit bypasses and kill-switch changes to accountable roles. Record actor, reason, old/new value, expiry and restoration; prevent client input or generated content from changing them.
Verify budget behavior when metering, config, limiter or provider APIs fail. Choose an explicit fail-closed or bounded degraded policy and ensure recovery cannot replay unlimited accumulated work.

Provide a tested hierarchy of global, provider, feature, tenant and credential stops appropriate to the architecture. Operators must be able to contain one offending tenant without unnecessary wider outage.

Verify a stop blocks new HTTP/API admissions, scheduler triggers, enqueue operations, worker starts, retries, child tasks and alternate interfaces. Measure propagation across replicas/regions and config caches.
Define safe treatment of accepted work: complete bounded essential work, drain, pause or cancel. Reconcile reservations, partial output, customer messages and uncancellable provider charges.
Test expired workers, scheduled retries, delayed callbacks and queue redrive while the stop is active. No path may unintentionally resume spending because it bypasses interactive admission.
Avoid automatic expensive failover, top-ups or autoscaling that defeats containment. Document protected recovery/security services whose continuing spend is intentional.
Test stop persistence through restart, redeploy, rollback and regional failover. Maintain an accessible operator control path even if the primary application is overloaded.
Reopen gradually using a bounded canary, current balance checks and queue admission limits. Prevent a backlog/retry thundering herd and define when a stop re-engages.

Show honest exhausted-budget/suspended/degraded states. Preserve user work, avoid charging for unstarted operations, document refund policy and provide useful retry guidance without promising an unknown restoration time.
Measure total/categorical spend, cost per successful outcome, usage velocity, forecast, remaining budget and unattributed costs. Separate measured, estimated, delayed and invoiced values.
Monitor rejection rate, reservation age, unsettled ledger items, retry multiplication, queue age/depth, active jobs, storage/egress growth and unusual model/destination selection where applicable.
Detect cost without expected activity, activity without accounting, new providers/SKUs/regions and abrupt unit-price changes. Check credits masking persistent uneconomic usage.
Set actionable anomaly thresholds using baseline and exposure tolerance. Include absolute and rate-of-change signals so gradual growth and fast bursts are both visible.
Exercise alert delivery to an accountable person, acknowledgement/escalation and a usable runbook. Record timestamps and operational response delay, not merely a configured email address.

Keep metrics/log cardinality, retention and alert volume bounded during an attack. Record enough redacted correlation to investigate; do not expose tenant financial information through public metrics.

Assign incident lead, technical owner, billing liaison and communication responsibility appropriate to team size. Define materiality triggers for rapid action and an accessible emergency contact path.

Capture rate, cumulative exposure, affected accounts/tenants/features, active provider work, queue state and last-known-good configuration before evidence changes, provided collection does not delay urgent containment.
Contain at the narrowest effective admission/provider/scheduler boundary; revoke compromised credentials when appropriate. Verify actual downstream usage reduction and record residual costs.

Preserve redacted evidence and make an impact estimate with explicit unknowns. Distinguish platform cost, customer charges, service disruption, abuse attribution and suspected compromise; use security/privacy processes where relevant.
Reconcile ambiguous operations, customer credits/refunds and provider invoices. Provider billing disputes and credits are separate follow-up work; do not assume they will reverse losses.
Restore service only after root cause and bounds are verified. Record corrective controls, acceptance tests, owner, review date and what would trigger renewed containment.
Before launch or a pricing/plan change, verify worst-case permitted usage, effective budgets, exhaustion UX, concurrency accounting, alerts and stop/reopen paths on the release configuration.
During migration, reconcile old/new schedules, queues, ledgers, credentials, resource ownership and provider accounts. Test dual-running costs, cutover routing, idempotency and balance authority.

Verify rollback cannot resurrect retired jobs, reset consumed quota, restore old permissive limits or enable duplicate billing. Track unavoidable overlapping resources until the recovery window closes.

Define a proportionate review cadence for bills, subscriptions, ownerless resources, pricing changes, unused seats, savings confirmation and exception expiry. Reuse existing processes rather than adding unnecessary recurring jobs.

Record ready, conditionally ready, blocked or insufficient evidence for this scope. List material gaps, residual exposure, accepted risks and follow-up owners explicitly; an average pass percentage cannot override a verified blocker.
