values: Record product, release/build, environment, audit date/timezone, owner, intended decision, and evidence destinations; distinguish current production from designs and upcoming work.
Inventory active, hidden, flagged, deprecated, partial, and planned features; record actual audience eligibility and identify which promises apply to this release.
Map user, buyer, administrator, operator, beneficiary, and affected non-user roles; include users who are rejected, inactive, or leaving.
Define primary jobs, success outcomes, critical journeys, expected frequency, and the consequences of failure; include assisted and manual steps outside the app.
Record supported clients, devices, input methods, locales, markets, timezones, versions, account types, plans, quotas, and relevant data scale; leave unknowns explicit.
Inventory dependencies, external providers, integrations, background jobs, human approvals, contractual commitments, and responsible teams; name each source of truth.

Gather current requirements, designs, help, marketing, contracts, tickets, research, analytics definitions, and incidents; record contradictions instead of silently choosing the most convenient version.
Select applicable checks and specialist audit handoffs. Exclude unsupported capabilities with reasons; log evidence access limits and the decisions they prevent.
Link every assessed check to an environment, preconditions, input, method, expected result, observed result, date, and sanitized evidence; another reviewer can repeat the scenario.
Separate source inspection, prototype observation, staging execution, and production observation. A code path or screenshot alone does not prove the full production journey.
Verify persistent and downstream effects, not only a toast or HTTP success. Reconcile UI state with records, generated artifacts, deliveries, and accounting where applicable.

Separate confirmed defects, verification gaps, hypotheses, research insights, and opportunities. An out-of-scope feature request remains an opportunity unless a binding promise makes it a requirement.
Record verified sample and potentially affected population separately; explain selection, omissions, and the basis of any extrapolation.
Deduplicate common causes across journeys and audit modules; retain all affected check IDs and use one primary finding owner.
Store redacted evidence with stable relative references; avoid secrets and unnecessary participant/customer data, and set access and retention for sensitive material.
Assign severity, confidence, exposure, delivery priority, and launch-blocker decision separately; include user impact, workaround, owner, due date, and acceptance conditions.
Cover the representative success, meaningful rejection, interrupted action, and recovery for each critical journey; link selected scenarios to requirements and checks.
Test high-risk intersections such as revoked role during export, timeout after payment, offline edit followed by deletion, and plan downgrade during a queued job where applicable.
Add scenarios from historical incidents, support recurrence, architecture risks, and customer commitments; expand sampling when results conflict.
Reconcile check statuses and report selected, assessed, failed, not verified, and excluded counts; disclose partial scope and unresolved blockers.
State who experiences the problem, the triggering situation, frequency, severity, current workaround, and desired outcome; cite evidence rather than starting with a requested widget.
Separate symptoms from underlying causes; consider awareness, ability, motivation, policy, information, and process before assuming missing functionality.
Write functional, emotional, and social jobs where relevant; distinguish the buyer's objective from the end user's and from affected third parties.
Segment by need, context, maturity, workflow, constraints, and willingness/ability to adopt; identify whose needs differ or conflict.
Include non-customers, churned users, failed signups, accessibility needs, and low-connectivity contexts when relevant; do not infer the whole market from vocal power users.
Quantify or explicitly mark unknown the cost of the problem, population affected, frequency, and consequence of doing nothing; distinguish observed values from estimates.
Compare current substitutes including spreadsheets, manual services, competing products, and doing nothing; explain why switching would be worthwhile.
Validate the end-to-end ecosystem: upstream inputs, user handoffs, organizational approvals, downstream work, and the part the product can realistically improve.
Connect the opportunity to an agreed product/business outcome; state the causal mechanism and potential second-order effects or cannibalization.
Generate multiple distinct approaches before convergence, using the baseline skill's 5-7 approaches when useful; include process, policy, service, removal, and no-build options.
Challenge the direction using inversion, analogies, SCAMPER, first principles, or an opportunity-solution tree; record evidence separately from speculative ideas.
Compare alternatives on user value, feasibility, adoption burden, strategic fit, risk, ongoing operations, and reversibility; explain selected and rejected options.
Test whether the feature adds complexity, duplicates existing capability, weakens another journey, or requires users to change behavior without sufficient benefit.
Check positioning and differentiation against actual capabilities; avoid assuming competitor feature parity proves demand or that competitor marketing proves behavior.
Evaluate distribution and discovery: how eligible users encounter the feature, understand it, try it, and fit it into existing routines.
Identify whether sales promises, incentives, revenue targets, or a single large customer are distorting the target problem; document explicit strategic exceptions.
Estimate recurring provider, support, moderation, training, migration, and maintenance costs alongside build effort; name constraints that may make an otherwise appealing idea unviable.
Compare short-term relief with longer-term direction, including dependencies, options enabled/foreclosed, and likely responses from ecosystem partners.
List user, problem, solution, business, feasibility, and adoption assumptions; record confidence, evidence age, and what would falsify each material assumption.
Identify the assumption most likely to invalidate the investment; design the cheapest credible test before committing to broad implementation.
Distinguish stated preference, prototype interest, purchase intent, actual use, repeat value, and willingness to pay; do not treat them as equivalent signals.
Define the smallest complete outcome that can be learned from; an MVP must deliver its promised outcome or clearly disclose a prototype/concierge service.
Record proceed, revise, research, defer, or stop with rationale, accountable owner, evidence, open uncertainties, and a review trigger.
Define success, failure, and stop conditions before the pilot; include opportunity cost and the outcome that would justify removing or simplifying an existing feature.
Express the decision the study will inform, research questions, current assumptions, existing evidence, and what would change the decision.
Match method to uncertainty: contextual interviews for needs, task observation for usability, diaries for repeated use, surveys for measured attitudes, and experiments for causal comparisons.
Distinguish generative, evaluative, attitudinal, behavioral, qualitative, and quantitative evidence; avoid claiming prevalence from a small purposive interview sample.
Review prior research, support, sales, churn, analytics, and incidents before new recruitment; record contradictory and outdated evidence.
Define inclusion/exclusion criteria, segments, recruitment channel, incentives, and bias risks; distinguish buyers, admins, users, non-users, and assisted users.

Justify sample coverage against heterogeneous needs and the decision's risk. For estimates/experiments, plan uncertainty or power; for qualitative work, track recurring themes and unresolved segment gaps.
Include relevant assistive technology, language, device, connectivity, and domain expertise; make participation accessible and allow alternative participation modes.

Define informed participation, recording choice, withdrawal process, storage/access, redaction, and retention; use additional project-approved review where vulnerable populations or sensitive data are involved.
Identify real-world harms or consequences from study tasks; use synthetic accounts/data and safe prototypes when purchases, publication, messaging, or deletion are involved.
Pilot the screener, task instructions, survey, recording setup, and analysis approach; remove ambiguity before the main sessions.
Ask about specific recent behavior and real workarounds before showing concepts; avoid leading, hypothetical, and double-barreled questions.
Separate unaided behavior from prompted behavior. Record moderator assistance, prior exposure, task order, and prototype limitations.
Use realistic tasks framed as goals rather than UI instructions; define observable task completion, critical errors, abandonment, and recovery.
Observe comprehension, findability, expectation, confidence, and consequences alongside completion time; a fast incorrect result is not a successful task.
Include first use, repeat use, failed paths, workarounds, and handoffs where relevant; capture environmental interruptions and organizational constraints.
Keep warm-up/context, deep dive, concept reaction, and wrap-up distinct; do not contaminate problem discovery with an early feature pitch.
Capture accurate observations and participant wording with consent; distinguish verbatim quotes, paraphrases, observer interpretation, and model-generated synthesis.
Include disconfirming cases and evidence that challenges the favored solution; avoid selectively quoting enthusiastic participants.
Check survey wording, neutral response options, accessible formatting, skip logic, and an appropriate unknown/not-applicable choice.
Record invitation denominator, completion denominator, field dates, missing responses, duplicate responses, and recruitment bias; report weighted and unweighted bases where used.
Avoid generalizing opt-in customer responses to the total market without justification; disclose non-response, coverage, recall, and desirability bias.
Define scales consistently and avoid interpreting incomparable wording, cohorts, or time windows as trends; preserve the exact instrument version.
Link behavior measures to the relevant eligible population and observation period; protect privacy when joining session, research, and account data.
Preserve an observation-to-theme-to-insight-to-opportunity trail; use affinity mapping, journey mapping, or JTBD only when they help answer the question.
Report the number and relevant contexts of observations without implying statistical prevalence; separate severity of an observed failure from its unknown population frequency.
Review alternative explanations such as recruitment, moderator assistance, novelty, prototype fidelity, or device limitations; record confidence and disagreements.
Link recommendations to evidence and distinguish research-supported needs from speculative solutions; assign follow-up learning or delivery owners.
Share a redacted synthesis with limitations and decision implications; control access to recordings and highlight reels, and execute the agreed retention/deletion plan.
Check whether research changed a decision and whether later behavior confirmed the insight; schedule reassessment after material audience or workflow changes.
If using AI for transcription or synthesis, verify consent and approved handling, check summaries against source material, and never fabricate participants, quotes, or interview findings.
State the evidenced problem, target segments, triggering context, frequency, current workaround, and cost of leaving it unresolved.
Define measurable user and business outcomes; distinguish outputs such as shipping a wizard from outcomes such as successful first setup.
Document goals and explicit non-goals with rationale, supported markets/clients, first-release boundaries, and future considerations.
Record alternatives, selected direction, trade-offs, assumptions, supporting research, and decisions; keep unresolved questions visible with an owner and blocking status.
Write role-specific stories that connect capability to benefit; split large stories into independently verifiable outcomes without losing the complete journey.
Categorize requirements as Must/Should/Could/Future or explicitly define the project's scheme; challenge an unbounded must-have list.
Name contractual deadlines, external dependencies, design/engineering/data/support owners, and feasibility unknowns before making delivery commitments.
Assign stable requirement IDs and link each to stories, designs, implementation/tickets, scenarios, evidence, and the release containing the change.
Define preconditions, inputs, actions, state transitions, persisted output, visible feedback, and downstream consequences for the main success path.
Specify empty, invalid, denied, loading, delayed, partial, failed, canceled, expired, and interrupted states with actionable user feedback.
Define field validation, units, precision, formats, uniqueness, supported size/count limits, and authoritative rules; record why boundaries exist.
Specify role, ownership, tenant, plan, quota, and flag eligibility across UI and direct operations, including changes while work is in flight.
Specify retries, idempotency, conflict behavior, cancellation, undo, and recovery; distinguish timeout/unknown outcome from confirmed failure.
Define data lifecycle, visibility, sharing, archive/delete/restore behavior, exports, and effects on dependent records and external recipients.
Define timing semantics: user timezone, deadlines, recurrence, expiry, freshness, delayed delivery, and processing expectations.
Define imports, integration contracts, required input quality, partial failures, version compatibility, and which system owns each state.
Define accessibility, localization, supported client behavior, performance expectations under a stated workload, and relevant specialist review requirements.
Describe administrative/support actions, observability, user correction/appeal, operational ownership, and any manual work required to fulfill the promise.
Give each required behavior an independently observable acceptance condition; replace vague terms such as fast, intuitive, or seamless with project-specific evidence.
Include representative success, negative, boundary, interruption, and recovery scenarios; specify what must not happen, including duplicate charges or unintended publication.
Define metric numerator, denominator, eligible population, baseline, target or hypothesis, time window, data source, owner, and review date.
Pair desired metrics with harm/cost/quality guardrails; distinguish adoption from successful outcomes and correlation from causal impact.
Mark prototype behavior and mocked dependencies explicitly; do not accept a mock as evidence that a promised integration works.
Define rollout audience, migration needs, support/help changes, rollback or containment, post-launch observation, and stop conditions.
Review critical requirements with the relevant product, design, engineering, data, and operations owners; document disagreement and accepted risk.
Record approved scope changes with rationale and impact on capacity, date, dependencies, and acceptance; move deferred ideas into a separate opportunity backlog.
Reconcile implementation against the final approved behavior, including advertised/help/contractual promises; resolve stale designs and contradictory requirements.
Confirm each must-have has evidence or an explicit verification gap; a completed ticket or passing build alone does not prove the requirement.
Compare marketing, demos, screenshots, sales commitments, pricing, and help with the enabled release; identify materially false promises and unsupported limitations.
Test entry from homepage, campaign, invitation, shared item, bookmark, search result, notification, and deep link where supported; preserve intended destination through sign-in.
Verify guest exploration, signup, verification, sign-in, recovery, and returning sessions where present; no state traps the user without an explanation or recovery route.
Check defaults, examples, sample data, permissions, and prerequisite setup; separate demo content from the user's real records and provide a clear next action.
Complete first value with realistic synthetic input and no undocumented staff intervention; record time, assistance, errors, and the final persisted outcome.
Check skipped, dismissed, resumed, and repeated onboarding; returning users retain progress and are not forced through irrelevant steps.
Test invitations before and after account creation, duplicate/expired/revoked invites, wrong account, and existing organization membership.
Explain requested permissions and their timing; test denial, limited permission, revocation, and later recovery for device or integration access.
Verify names, information hierarchy, labels, icons, and status language match user expectations and remain consistent across surfaces.
Test navigation, back/forward, refresh, open in new tab, unsaved changes, and shared URLs; selected context and state behave as promised.
Check search, filter, sort, pagination, saved views, and no-results states using known records; counts and scope are clear and reset paths work.
Distinguish no data, no permission, loading, filtering to zero results, and fetch failure; do not show a misleading empty state for an error.
Verify forms preserve valid input after errors, identify the affected field, explain correction, and handle keyboard/autofill/paste as supported.
Check units, labels, totals, rounding, freshness, timestamps, and previews against the resulting action; users can understand what will change before committing.
Verify primary actions, disabled actions, and upgrade/permission barriers explain the cause and available remedy without promising access the user cannot obtain.
Check bulk selection across pagination/filters and explain selected count/scope; destructive or expensive bulk actions affect exactly the documented items.
Test create, edit, duplicate, save, preview, publish, archive, restore, and delete where supported; visible status agrees with underlying state.
Check action feedback distinguishes accepted, processing, completed, partially completed, failed, and unknown; completion is not claimed before the promised effect.
Verify keyboard navigation, focus after dialogs/errors/updates, screen-reader feedback, and accessible labels on critical tasks with relevant specialist review.
Check zoom/reflow, touch targets, orientation, small screens, virtual keyboard, contrast-dependent signals, motion preferences, and long translated strings in supported clients.
Test supported locales, right-to-left layout, pluralization, dates, numbers, currencies, names, addresses, and timezone selection without corrupting stored values.
Check slow networks, reduced bandwidth, long jobs, backgrounding, device sleep, interrupted sessions, and returning later; progress and recovery match the actual state.
Verify cross-device and cross-channel continuity where promised; local drafts, cloud saves, pending sync, and conflicts are distinguishable.
Test supported browser/device versions and embedded/in-app contexts where relevant; unsupported clients receive an accurate limitation or fallback.
Check long, complex, emotional, or high-stakes tasks for understandable instructions, review before submission, and correction routes.
Verify confirmations, receipts, status messages, and help links identify the right item, actor, time, and next step without disclosing unnecessary data.
Test channel preferences, per-workspace settings, quiet hours, digest rules, and opt-out; distinguish optional engagement messages from required service/security notices.
Check notification timing, deduplication, stale links, delayed/out-of-order messages, and actions already completed elsewhere; avoid contradictory state claims.
Verify reminders and recommendations reflect actual progress and eligibility; completed, canceled, or deleted work does not keep generating irrelevant prompts.
Evaluate repeat value and reactivation against the user's natural usage cycle; unnecessary daily engagement is not a universal success condition.
Check feedback/help/support paths in failed and blocked states; users can provide a safe diagnostic reference and receive a realistic response expectation.
Review upsells, defaults, scarcity claims, consent, cancellation, and destructive flows for misleading pressure, hidden costs, or obstructive steps.
Confirm documentation, product tours, release notes, and support scripts match current behavior, supported limits, and recovery paths.
Verify exit, export, cancellation, deletion, and return paths are understandable; clearly distinguish account deletion, data deletion, service cancellation, and sign-out.
Test absent, null, empty, whitespace-only, zero, negative, and default values where meaningful; validation distinguishes valid zero from missing input.
Test just below, exactly at, and just above supported length, count, size, precision, and duration limits; UI and server rules agree.
Check duplicate identifiers, case/whitespace normalization, canonical forms, and uniqueness within the correct scope; errors explain existing/conflicting records.
Test accents, apostrophes, emoji, combining characters, right-to-left text, multiline values, and long names through input, storage, search, display, and export.
Verify numeric units, decimal separators, rounding, currency precision, aggregate totals, and conversion rules against approved examples; do not assume all currencies use two decimals.
Check dates before/at/after boundaries, leap dates, month-end, year-end, DST, timezone changes, recurrence, expiration, and clock skew relevant to the product.
Verify schema changes, legacy records, unknown enum values, optional fields, and old clients; unsupported versions fail visibly without silently corrupting data.
Check zero, one, typical, and maximum supported datasets for functional correctness, counts, ordering, pagination, and processing feedback.
Test missing/deleted dependencies, orphaned references, moved items, and archived parents; actions follow a documented rule rather than creating inaccessible records.
Map allowed state transitions and explicitly reject invalid transitions, including actions attempted after completion, expiry, cancellation, archive, or deletion.
Test double clicks, retries, refresh, browser back, duplicate submissions, and replayed requests; documented idempotency rules prevent unintended duplicate effects.
Simulate timeout after a successful commit; users can discover the real outcome and safely retry without duplicate work or false failure claims.
Test two tabs/devices/editors changing the same record; conflict detection, merge, lock, or last-write behavior is explicit and does not silently lose promised work.
Check actions against stale views after another actor edits/deletes/transfers the item; the result preserves authoritative rules and explains conflicts.
Test revocation, logout, suspension, plan change, and quota exhaustion while a form, export, upload, or background job is already running.
Verify ordering, repeated events, delayed callbacks, and eventual consistency; older updates do not incorrectly reverse a later authoritative state.
Check bulk operations for all-or-nothing versus partial-result behavior, item-level errors, retry scope, and accurate totals after interrupted execution.
Verify cancel and undo at each meaningful stage; distinguish stopping future work, compensating a completed action, and recalling an external effect that cannot be reversed.
Test drafts, autosave, unsaved-change warnings, reconnect, and resume; identify which state is local, pending, committed, or recoverable.
Check queued, running, delayed, stuck, failed, canceled, and completed jobs; progress, timestamps, and user-facing expectations reflect actual state.
Verify bounded retry behavior, actionable terminal failure, reprocessing rules, and who can recover a stuck job; avoid endless silent retries.
Simulate dependency unavailability, slow response, authentication expiry, rate limit, malformed payload, and partial response; each has truthful feedback and a defined fallback.
Test a provider succeeds but local acknowledgement fails, and the reverse; reconcile state before repeating costly or irreversible external operations.
Verify freshness labels, stale caches, polling, refresh, and delayed propagation; stale data is not presented as a guaranteed current value.
Check user-visible latency and capacity limits against the scoped workload; use bounded authorized tests and record behavior at saturation.
Verify failed processing does not silently retain locks, reserve capacity forever, consume undocumented quota, or leave an item in an unrecoverable state.
Test supported import encodings, BOM, delimiters, quoted separators/newlines, headers, blank rows, malformed values, legacy versions, and duplicate rows.
Verify import preview/mapping, validation, partial success, error file, restart/retry, and rollback where promised; accepted/rejected totals reconcile.
Verify exports include the correct scope, fields, record count, timezone/units, encoding, and supported spreadsheet behavior; route formula-injection and access safety to security review.
Check generated files for empty/large results, naming, expiry, link access, interrupted download, repeated retrieval, and deletion after the declared retention window.
Test attachment/upload type, size, corrupt input, duplicate names, interruption/resume, scan/processing delay, and failed replacement; existing valid content is preserved as promised.
Verify ownership, lineage, versions, provenance, and last-updated metadata after copy, merge, import, restore, and transfer.
Check archive/delete/restore semantics, cascades, shared links, search indexes, cached views, scheduled work, exports, and notifications; document delayed cleanup and exceptions.
Verify deletion/restoration interactions with retained backups and external copies through the specialist data module; do not promise recall or immediate erasure where unsupported.
Reconcile data and user-visible state after migration, rollback, provider replacement, and legacy-to-new feature transitions using representative project records.
Retest known incidents and verify diagnostics let operators distinguish a failed action from delayed processing without exposing sensitive data.
Test signup, verification, login methods, recovery, email change, duplicate identity, and existing-account linking against the approved account rules.
Check invitation acceptance by the wrong signed-in account, expired/revoked invite, repeated acceptance, and pre-existing membership; do not silently join the wrong organization.
Verify organization switching, default workspace, direct links, recent items, notifications, and search use the intended context and make that context clear.
Test role creation/change/removal, ownership transfer, last-owner departure, suspended members, and service accounts where supported; preserve an authorized management route.
Check access and explanations for guests, viewers, editors, admins, owners, and support through both UI and direct operations with specialist authorization evidence.
Verify offboarding revokes access and handles assigned work, shared content, integrations, scheduled tasks, and ownership according to documented policy.
Test organization merge/split, account merge, domain change, and managed provisioning only if supported; document conflict and recovery behavior.
Check account suspension, recovery, deletion, re-registration, and restore; explain consequences for collaborators, billing, content, and retained records.
Verify private/shared/public scopes, inherited permissions, guest access, link expiry/revocation, and onward sharing; visibility labels match actual access.
Test simultaneous comments/edits, mentions, assignments, approvals, rejected changes, resolved discussions, and deleted targets where present.
Verify author attribution, version history, change notification, conflict recovery, and undo; users can understand whose change is current.
Check sharing/transferring an item with attachments, child records, external links, and integrations; dependent access follows the documented rule.
Verify approvals and delegation under absence, role revocation, self-approval restrictions, repeated requests, and skipped steps where the workflow requires them.
Reconcile pricing copy, available plans, checkout amounts, currency, billing interval, taxes/fees presentation, seat rules, and included allowances with scoped commercial policy.
Test trial eligibility, start/end, extension, conversion, cancellation, and re-entry; expiry behavior and retained work are explained before they occur.
Verify upgrade/downgrade timing, proration explanation, annual/monthly changes, pending changes, discounts, legacy plans, and grandfathered entitlements where supported.
Test successful, failed, canceled, abandoned, duplicated, and delayed checkout; redirect success alone does not prove payment or entitlement activation.
Verify pending/failed payment, grace period, recovery, retry, suspension, refund, dispute, and cancellation states through user-facing access and messages.
Check seat increases/decreases, invited-but-inactive members, removed members, minimum seats, and ownership transfer against the billable-seat definition.
Explain usage units, included amounts, reservations, overage, reset timezone, expiry, and pooling; UI counters reconcile with authoritative accounting.
Test zero/near/exact/over quota, simultaneous requests, retried work, partial failure, canceled work, and provider failure against the documented charging rule.
Verify downgrading below current usage or storage has an explicit outcome; retained data, blocked actions, grace periods, and restoration are understandable.
Test receipts, invoices, billing-contact changes, payment-method updates, cancellation confirmation, and renewal notices as applicable; dates and amounts agree across channels.
Check promotions, credits, gifts, refunds, and expiring balances where present; stacking, eligibility, redemption limits, and remaining value follow the scoped policy.
Verify exit and reactivation do not introduce unexpected renewal, duplicate subscription, lost promised access, or silent loss of recoverable data.
Test connect, permission selection, wrong external account, revoked/expired credential, reconnect, and disconnect; users can see the connected identity and sync scope.
Verify first sync, incremental sync, backfill, duplicate handling, conflict ownership, deletion propagation, lag, and repair for supported integration workflows.
Check webhook/email/delivery settings, endpoint validation, delivery failure, retry, replay, and disable; distinguish accepted requests from recipient delivery or action.
Verify authorized support/admin users can inspect account, payment, quota, and job state using appropriate tools and a diagnostic reference.
Test supported support actions such as retry, quota correction, refund request, reassign, or unlock; require scoped permissions, audit history, and clear irreversible-action feedback.
Check impersonation or assisted access if supported, including authorization, scope, visible attribution, expiry, and auditability through the security module.
Verify handoff between automated support and humans preserves context appropriately, provides a real escalation route, and does not fabricate resolution or response times.
Reconcile help, incident communication, service expectations, staff training, runbooks, and ownership with the actual release and support capacity.
Confirm support feedback can be linked to recurring product failures without turning every one-off request into a committed feature.
SaaS, enterprise, APIs, and developer tools
For SaaS, verify single-user and team activation, workspace setup, plan eligibility, trial expiry, seat/quota changes, and owner departure; test both individual and organization value.
SaaS, enterprise, APIs, and developer tools

For enterprise features, check purchased SSO/provisioning/admin policy, domain ownership, managed-account recovery, audit export, and rollout/migration; unsupported enterprise features remain opportunities.
SaaS, enterprise, APIs, and developer tools
For APIs/SDKs/CLI tools, complete the documented first successful call from a clean environment; verify examples, credentials, environments, errors, pagination, and supported versions.
SaaS, enterprise, APIs, and developer tools
For developer products, test sandbox-to-production transition, key rotation, rate-limit discovery, retries, idempotency, webhook replay, deprecation, and backwards compatibility as promised.
For commerce, test discovery, variants, stock, cart, address, shipping availability, discounts, checkout, and order confirmation using authoritative stock and price.
Check concurrent stock changes, price changes in cart, partial fulfillment, backorder, failed delivery, return, exchange, refund, and cancellation; totals and order state reconcile.
For digital goods, verify payment-to-access timing, license/seat rules, download limits, link expiry, refund effects, and re-download after device/account changes.
For marketplaces, test buyer, seller, operator, and affected third-party journeys; cover onboarding, listings, matching, trust signals, commission, and supply-demand constraints.
Verify disputes, fraud reports, seller suspension, payout delay/failure, partial refund, cancellation, and off-platform fulfillment boundaries; each side sees a consistent state.
For service/booking products, test availability, timezones, holds, concurrent booking, capacity, waiting lists, recurring bookings, rescheduling, no-show, and cancellation deadlines.
Verify provider absence, customer late arrival, location changes, DST transitions, confirmation/reminders, deposits, and partial service delivery against the promised policy.
For publishing/CMS tools, verify draft, review, preview, schedule, publish, unpublish, version restore, permissions, and syndication; previews and public content match the intended version.
For media products, test supported playback formats, resume, captions, quality changes, downloads/offline rights, geo/plan availability, and interrupted delivery.

For learning products, test enrollment, prerequisites, sequence, progress sync, retakes, grading, completion, certificates, and course updates; completion claims reflect the defined learning evidence.
For communities/UGC, test creation, editing, deletion, reporting, blocking/muting, moderation, appeals, and notification effects; deleted or restricted content follows the declared visibility policy.
Test moderation queues, repeated abuse, malicious reporting, moderator absence, evidence retention, and vulnerable-user protections within the scoped safety process.
For search/recommendation products, use known relevant, irrelevant, ambiguous, misspelled, multilingual, and no-result queries; evaluate relevance, freshness, permissions, and actionable fallback.
Check cold start, feedback correction, preference changes, filter interactions, repeated recommendations, sponsored content labeling, and unintended exclusion of relevant inventory.
Define the AI task, supported inputs, intended users, limitations, prohibited uses, human review needs, and what counts as a successful result beyond generating text.
Evaluate representative tasks, edge cases, language/segment variation, refusals, and adversarial inputs using a versioned evaluation set with human-reviewed criteria.
Test incorrect, fabricated, unsupported, stale, and overconfident output; verify correction, provenance/citations where promised, uncertainty communication, and safe fallback.
Test tool permission boundaries, preview/confirmation for consequential actions, duplicate execution, interrupted tool calls, cancellation, and human takeover through specialist security/AI review.
Check prompt-injection scenarios in user content and retrieved material through specialist review; product state and user messaging must reflect blocked or incomplete actions truthfully.
Verify model/provider changes, nondeterminism, context limits, long conversations, retrieval gaps, latency, cost ceilings, and degraded mode against the scoped quality contract.
Check memory/personalization visibility, correction, opt-out/deletion, data freshness, and cross-account boundaries; users understand what is retained and why.
For automated recommendations/decisions affecting people, verify explanation, contest/correction, escalation, human accountability, and segment-specific harms with qualified project reviewers.
Mobile, desktop, offline, and connected devices
For mobile/desktop apps, test installation, update, first launch, deep links, app permissions, backgrounding, crash recovery, logout, and supported OS versions.
Mobile, desktop, offline, and connected devices
Check app-store or platform purchase/restore flows, external versus in-app subscription state, notification opt-in, and device migration where supported.
Mobile, desktop, offline, and connected devices
For offline-first products, verify local changes, pending status, conflict resolution, reconnect, account switch, storage exhaustion, and remote deletion; no silent loss of promised work.
Mobile, desktop, offline, and connected devices
For hardware/IoT products, verify pairing, identity, connectivity loss, stale readings, calibration, firmware change, safe state, replacement, and ownership transfer as scoped.
Data, workflow, public services, and sensitive use
For dashboards/data products, reconcile source lineage, freshness, missing values, dimensions, filters, aggregates, exports, and access scope; distinguish zero, unknown, and unavailable.
Data, workflow, public services, and sensitive use
For automation/workflow tools, test triggers, schedules, conditions, branching, retries, loop prevention, approvals, execution history, pause/resume, and version changes during running work.
Data, workflow, public services, and sensitive use
For collaborative/design/document tools, verify large documents, embedded assets, real-time edits, version restore, offline merge, export fidelity, and cross-client rendering.
Data, workflow, public services, and sensitive use

For lead-generation/service sites, verify inquiry routing, form validation, spam handling, confirmation, appointment/contact fulfillment, and attribution; a submitted form alone does not prove receipt.
Data, workflow, public services, and sensitive use

For nonprofit/public-service products, test eligibility, assisted access, language, evidence submission, rejection/appeal, service continuity, and users without conventional account/payment credentials.
Data, workflow, public services, and sensitive use

For healthcare, financial, legal, children's, or other sensitive contexts, identify qualified reviewers, project-specific obligations, consent/guardian needs, accessibility, harm controls, escalation, and audit evidence; generic checklist completion does not establish compliance.
Data, workflow, public services, and sensitive use
For games or gamified products, verify progression, saves, rewards, purchases, fairness, account/device migration, multiplayer/social safety, reset seasons, and recovery where applicable.
Data, workflow, public services, and sensitive use
For internal tools, verify staff onboarding/offboarding, least-privilege workflow, manual fallback, data corrections, approval accountability, and the real productivity outcome.
Define primary user outcome, supporting business outcome, leading/lagging indicators, and guardrails; explain how each is expected to respond to the feature.
Define numerator, denominator, event semantics, unit of analysis, eligibility, period, timezone, and cohort; distinguish user, account, organization, session, and action metrics.
Record baseline, target or explicit hypothesis, confidence/limitations, metric owner, query/source, and decision date; do not substitute invented benchmarks.
Define activation as meaningful value rather than a click; distinguish eligible, exposed, tried, completed, repeated, and retained users.
Define retention/reactivation against the natural job frequency and cohort maturity; seasonal or infrequent use should not automatically be treated as churn.
Measure task success, time, error, abandonment, recovery, and support demand as relevant; exclude incomplete/canceled tasks transparently rather than hiding them.
Specify an event dictionary with stable names, trigger, source of truth, properties, version, and permitted data; collect only what the measurement needs.
Verify consent/opt-out and data handling through the privacy module; report coverage gaps rather than assuming untracked users behave identically.
Trace known synthetic actions from client through ingestion, storage, transformation, and reporting; check duplicates, missing/late events, retries, and event ordering.
Reconcile analytics with authoritative successful actions, revenue, usage, and deliveries; distinguish intended, accepted, completed, and failed events.
Check identity linking, account merges, organization membership, cross-device use, bot/internal traffic, and timezone boundaries for distorted counts.
Test reporting after schema/event changes, backfills, migrations, consent changes, and feature flags; annotate breaks in comparability.
Segment outcomes by relevant cohort, role, plan, device, locale, accessibility need, acquisition source, and maturity without exposing unnecessary personal data.
Check survivorship, selection, seasonality, small denominators, Simpson's paradox, and concurrent releases before attributing aggregate trends to a feature.
Separate correlation between feature use and retention from causal evidence; already successful users may be more likely to adopt the feature.
Report absolute counts, rates, uncertainty where estimable, observation period, missingness, and exclusions; unknown does not mean zero.
Pair satisfaction/NPS/feedback with observed behavior and respondent context; a higher score alone does not establish better task performance.
Review cost-to-serve, support, latency, quality, safety, accessibility, and business guardrails alongside adoption or revenue gains.
Write the hypothesis, mechanism, eligible audience, intervention, comparison, primary metric, guardrails, success/failure threshold, and resulting decision before exposure.
Choose a method suited to traffic, risk, and uncertainty: prototype, concierge pilot, staged rollout, randomized test, or qualified observational analysis.
For randomized tests, define assignment unit, exposure event, allocation, persistence, exclusion rules, and contamination/interference risks including shared organizations.

Plan baseline rate/variance, minimum meaningful effect, error criteria, sample/duration, and analysis approach; obtain competent statistical review where needed instead of using a fixed sample heuristic.
Check assignment/exposure instrumentation, sample-ratio mismatch, variant parity, novelty, carryover, and conflicting experiments before interpreting outcomes.
Predefine stopping and analysis rules; avoid repeated unplanned peeking, metric switching, or subgroup selection that manufactures a winning result.
Include natural usage cycles and outcome maturation; distinguish no detectable effect, inconclusive evidence, demonstrated equivalence under a defined margin, and harm.
Verify experiment eligibility cannot expose unsupported users to dangerous, misleading, or contractually incorrect behavior; use project-approved review for consequential changes.
Record cost, adverse events, qualitative feedback, and segment differences; explain trade-offs rather than declaring victory from one favorable metric.
Decide ship, iterate, stop, or gather evidence with owner, rationale, residual uncertainty, rollout/rollback plan, and post-launch review date.
Verify uplift persists after rollout and does not merely move failure to another funnel step; retire unused flags and obsolete event variants.
Close the loop from recurring support/research insight to a tested change and measured outcome; retain unsuccessful experiments to avoid repeating disproven assumptions.
Reconcile the release inventory with approved scope, acceptance evidence, current promises, deferred work, and known limitations; no active stub is presented as complete.
Verify critical end-to-end journeys in the intended environment with realistic synthetic data, applicable roles/plans, and representative failure/recovery paths.
Confirm each blocker is fixed and verified or explicitly accepted by the accountable owner with reason, expiry, compensating controls, and affected audience.
Record unresolved verification gaps and their decision impact; do not claim production readiness solely from source review or a passing build.
Define rollout cohort, eligibility, flag defaults, staged exposure, observation windows, owner, and stop/rollback triggers linked to measurable signals.
Verify flag combinations, disabled paths, entitlement interactions, and removal plans; turning off a UI flag does not reverse already-completed external effects.
Rehearse data/content/configuration migration, legacy compatibility, user-visible transition, and rollback/forward recovery in a disposable environment as appropriate.
Define what happens to queued jobs, edits in progress, open checkout, shared links, drafts, and old clients during deployment or rollback.
Prepare accurate launch copy, pricing/help updates, onboarding, release notes, training, and notices for changed or removed behavior.
Confirm support ownership, monitoring, escalation, staffing, provider capacity, manual fulfillment, and known-issue communication match launch scale.
Test production configuration and bounded smoke journeys after deployment; verify state and effects rather than assuming staging results transfer automatically.
Record release decision, build/configuration, date, decision-maker, evidence, residual risks, follow-up owners, and the next outcome review.
Review activation, task success, errors, support, costs, guardrails, and relevant segments against the agreed baseline after adequate observation.
Investigate adoption shortfalls as discovery, comprehension, eligibility, performance, trust, or value problems before adding more features.
Confirm promised fast-follow work is delivered or explicitly re-scoped; update help and commitments when direction changes.
Review low-use and high-maintenance features for merge, simplify, improve, reposition, or retire; consider infrequent but essential use and contractual commitments.
Revisit research and assumptions after audience shifts, pricing changes, provider/model changes, incidents, or unexpected usage patterns.
Track recurring product debt such as inconsistent rules, abandoned onboarding, stale permissions, temporary manual work, and unresolved edge cases with ownership.
Update scenario coverage from incidents and real support patterns; remove obsolete checks only with a documented scope or behavior change.
Check the roadmap balances urgent defects, foundational work, learning, and new opportunities against actual team capacity and dependencies.
Inventory active users, rare-but-critical users, contracts, integrations, saved links, automations, data, and dependents before retiring a capability.
Define replacement or manual alternatives, migration/export route, notice period, assistance, owner, and exceptions based on project commitments.
Verify deprecation notices reach affected users through suitable channels and accurately describe dates, timezone, impact, and required action.
Test export, migration, redirect/fallback, old-client behavior, queued work, and archived/shared content before cutover; confirm data reconciliation where needed.
Prevent new purchases or enrollment into a retiring capability unless terms are accurate; resolve prepaid value, credits, refunds, and renewals according to policy.
Verify cleanup of UI, flags, scheduled tasks, provider resources, documentation, analytics, support scripts, and retained data with accountable owners.
Monitor breakage, support demand, migrated outcomes, remaining dependents, and unintended cost after removal; retain an appropriate recovery/containment route.
Close the lifecycle decision with evidence, lessons, remaining obligations, and ownership; avoid declaring success while unresolved users or data are stranded.

Identify project, release owner, decision maker, technical responder and support contact. Record actual availability and backup coverage appropriate to team size rather than assuming a large launch team.
Record source commit, build/artifact identity, runtime/dependencies, deployed environment, schema/migration state and active configuration/flags. Identify anything still changing after verification.
Describe launch type: new product, beta, relaunch, feature activation, price/plan change, platform distribution or migration. State intended audience, regions, supported platforms and exclusions.
Define critical user outcomes, explicit non-goals and business invariants. Include revenue, identity, tenant isolation, data durability and costly work where present.

Record exposure plan: invite-only/public, initial cohort, ramp stages, traffic expectations, marketing timing and integrations consuming the release. Separate installed/deployed from enabled and publicly discoverable.
Inventory repositories, services, domains, accounts, workers, schedules, external providers, native clients and shared infrastructure involved. Mark unknown owners and inaccessible environments.

Identify data categories, migration volumes, retention/recovery obligations, user commitments and project-specific legal/commercial reviews. Link applicable specialist review instead of inventing jurisdiction-wide rules.
Select relevant audit modules and controls, with reasons for exclusions. Include inherited shared-host controls and independent per-application permissions and data boundaries.

Define project-relative blocker criteria before evaluating findings: unacceptable loss/exposure, broken essential outcome, material financial risk or inadequate recovery. Tie severity to impact and likelihood in the proposed exposure.
Distinguish mandatory pre-exposure prerequisites from monitored post-launch follow-up. A condition necessary for safety must be satisfied before the affected cohort receives the feature.
Define acceptable degraded modes, maintenance windows, support limitations and outage tolerance. Align promises, rollout gates, recovery targets and actual staffing.

Set measurable rollout success, pause and abort conditions using product outcomes, errors, latency, saturation, queue freshness, integrity and spend as applicable. Avoid universal thresholds unsupported by a baseline.

Confirm gate feasibility: who can obtain evidence, who can stop exposure, where authority lies and whether the deadline leaves time to respond. Record intentional scope reductions rather than silently skipping checks.
Define readiness for distinct cohorts/platforms if they differ. A web release passing does not establish native client, enterprise SSO, international market or migration readiness.
Separate availability of optional marketing/analytics enhancements from critical product/security controls. Missing an unnecessary tool must not become an automatic blocker.

For beta/internal/low-traffic releases, document which controls may be proportionately lighter and which risks remain material despite a small audience. A beta label does not establish authorization or data safety.

Map each essential outcome and invariant to specialist check IDs, existing test results, deployed config and selected rehearsal scenarios. Reuse sound evidence rather than automatically adding durable tests.
Define the role/tenant/plan/device/browser/locale/provider matrix needed for real users. Cover materially distinct implementations and risk boundaries; document sampling and untested population.
Set authorized environments, synthetic identities/data, external-effect restrictions, request/concurrency/duration/cost ceilings and cancellation/cleanup before live verification.

Capture expected outcomes independently from implementation, including allowed and denied operations and persisted/provider side effects. An HTTP response or an assistant's statement alone is not runtime proof.
Bind evidence to candidate revision, configuration, schema and platform. Explain staging/production differences, access limitations, flaky/skipped checks and verification freshness.

Define what invalidates prior evidence: relevant code/config changes, data migrations, dependency/provider changes or changed exposure. Rerun changed controls and affected flows; broaden only when risk or observed failures justify it.
Protect evidence using project access/retention rules. Redact credentials, personal/payment data and production payloads while preserving correlation; avoid copying live data unnecessarily.
Link findings by root cause, affected surface and owning module. Keep defects, verification gaps, improvement opportunities and business choices distinguishable, with acceptance tests and owners.

Record accepted risks with actual exposure, alternatives, compensating controls, accountable decision, expiry/review date and affected cohort. Acceptance does not change Fail to Pass or satisfy an external obligation.

Use insufficient evidence when critical assurance cannot be established, and blocked when verified conditions prevent the proposed launch. Do not average away a blocker with many low-risk passing checks.
Establish ownership and deadline for every unresolved item, conditional prerequisite and post-launch task. Record escalation if the owner is unavailable or a prerequisite misses its deadline.
Preserve the final decision, candidate manifest, evidence references and run-of-show together. Reassess after a material candidate/exposure change using the established project release process.
Execute each essential visitor/customer/admin journey end to end on the release candidate, including a clear entry point, primary action, result and recovery/support route.

Verify navigation, search, deep links, redirects, consequential outbound links and back/forward behavior. Check authenticated links opened anonymously and externally shared links opened in another session.
Test signup, verification, login, reset, session expiry and logout where offered. Account for link expiry, cross-device use, resend behavior and useful recovery without account enumeration.

Check onboarding, invitations, required permissions and first meaningful success with fresh synthetic accounts. Existing developer/admin state must not mask missing setup or inaccessible initial data.

Exercise forms with valid/invalid input, validation errors, duplicate submit, slow submit and failure after submission. Preserve safe user input and show actual completion rather than misleading success.

Verify loading, empty, partial, unavailable, denied, expired and error states. Provide actionable next steps, appropriate status codes and a useful 404 without returning a successful page for a missing resource.
Remove placeholder copy, broken assets, fabricated claims and obsolete contact/pricing details. Verify promises, screenshots, tutorials and plan comparisons match enabled features and actual limits.
Isolate or remove test/demo content and test privileges using an authorized data-safe method. Verify fixtures, seeded credentials and demo write paths cannot affect real tenants.
Check transactional copy, confirmations, receipts and timestamps against actual state. Distinguish accepted, queued, completed and failed work; do not promise an outcome before it exists.

Apply the project's accessibility target with keyboard and selected assistive-technology journeys. Verify focus order/visibility, labels, names, errors and status announcements; automated scans alone do not establish conformance.

Check contrast, zoom/reflow, text resize, meaningful alternatives, reduced motion and media captions where applicable. Ensure cookie dialogs, payment flows and support widgets do not block core access.
Test core actions on supported mobile/tablet/desktop layouts and input methods. Cover touch targets, virtual keyboards, orientation and browser chrome rather than only a responsive screenshot.
Use representative constrained devices and poor connectivity for loading, submitting and resuming. Check offline/interrupted behavior and prevent duplicate purchases/writes after reconnect.

Verify declared browser/OS/client support and meaningful old-client compatibility. Record unsupported combinations honestly instead of assuming every platform or the newest desktop browser is sufficient.

For supported locales, verify language, text expansion, right-to-left layout, currency, dates, timezone, decimal formats and encoding. Keep user-visible terms and support routes coherent with the enabled market.
Check authentication/payment challenges and abuse defenses for accessible alternatives and false positives. Include intended API clients and legitimate shared-IP users where relevant.

For public searchable content, verify production titles, descriptions, canonical hosts, sitemap, robots rules, indexing directives and redirects. Keep private/staging content access-controlled; robots.txt is not a security boundary.
Test representative HTTP status codes, redirect chains, removed URLs and old bookmarks. For relaunches, verify important old-to-new mappings rather than redirecting every missing URL to the homepage.
Verify social preview cards/images, favicon, branding and link appearance with actual public assets. Ensure previews reveal no private or placeholder information.

Measure key page/API performance on representative release infrastructure and user conditions. State test method, data size, percentile/window where meaningful and limits of synthetic versus real-user evidence.

Verify images, responsive sizing, fonts, script loading and lazy-loading behavior preserve essential content and interaction. Test cold caches and third-party widget failures as well as repeat visits.

Verify applicable privacy, terms, refund/cancellation, contact and consent disclosures are reachable and match actual data/product behavior. Obtain project-specific review for obligations rather than copying generic policy text as assurance.

Where consent is required, test accept, reject, withdrawal and preference persistence against actual tracking and third-party requests. Do not require a cookie banner when the scoped implementation does not need one.
Make pricing, trials, renewal, cancellation, usage limits and material AI/product limitations clear before commitment. Match claims to actual entitlement behavior and supported geography/platform.

For APIs/SDKs, verify published endpoints, version/auth instructions, examples, errors, quotas and a small real supported-client journey. Check that documentation points to the live supported version.
For native/desktop/mobile/game distribution, verify intended package, signing identity, version, supported hardware/OS, architecture, install permissions and trusted download/store destination.

Test fresh install, upgrade and uninstall or rollback behavior as applicable. Preserve user data/settings/save compatibility according to product promises; define recovery when downgrading cannot read new data.
Check store review/release state, staged distribution, region/age/content declarations, required platform permissions and release notes against current platform requirements where applicable.
Test native deep links, OAuth return paths, push permissions and links from email/store/browser in supported app states. Prevent wrong-environment callbacks and duplicate account/transaction effects.

For service workers/offline caches/installed web apps, test a returning user with an old client and cached assets. Avoid mixed-version failures and stale feature/authorization assumptions after deployment.

Verify platform-specific critical experiences, such as game saves, matchmaking, licensed assets, notifications or file associations, when they are part of the advertised release. Exclude them explicitly otherwise.

Align announcements, help pages, app/store listings and release notes with the actual cohort/flag schedule. Prepared content must not expose an unavailable feature or bypass an intentionally limited rollout.

Confirm organization-controlled ownership, billing, administrative recovery and primary/backup authorized access for registrar, DNS, hosting, source control, database, payment, email and backup providers.

Verify available MFA, scoped access, secure recovery and emergency operator access for consequential accounts. Remove obsolete/shared credentials where required without losing a working recovery route.

Resolve intended domains/subdomains and inspect A/AAAA/CNAME records, proxy/CDN routing and old hosts. Include IPv6 and direct-origin exposure where configured, not only the developer's cached resolver.

Verify valid TLS for every public name and callback endpoint, HTTPS redirects, certificate renewal operation and expiry notifications. Assess strict transport settings against actual subdomain readiness.

Review security headers and browser policies against the application: content policy, framing, content types and referrer behavior as relevant. Verify essential payment/OAuth/media flows still work under effective headers.
Record effective environment values, secret references, allowed hosts/origins, callback URLs and active flags. Separate test/live resources and ensure missing required configuration fails safely.

Protect staging, previews, administration and diagnostic surfaces with actual access controls. Check alternate domains, old deployments, source maps, backup files and exposed storage; indexing directives alone do not protect them.

Confirm production disables unsafe debug output, test bypasses, default accounts, placeholder secrets and public privileged diagnostics. Verify defaults in a clean deployment, not only an already configured server.

Check CDN/cache/proxy settings preserve authentication, private response isolation, client address trust and correct URL schemes. Test a logged-out/other-tenant request after a privileged response has been cached.

Execute essential allowed and denied operations with anonymous, ordinary, other-tenant, disabled and privileged synthetic users. Link response and persisted/external-effect evidence from the security module.
Verify session/cookie/token settings for production hosts, expiry, logout, revocation and CSRF protection where applicable. Test existing sessions across the planned release or domain change.

Test signup, verification, reset and invitation links for expiry, ownership and correct destination. Ensure tokens and unnecessary personal information do not leak through logs, referrers or error pages.

Confirm OAuth/SSO redirect registrations, tenant restrictions, state/nonce handling and role mapping for the live identity configuration. Include account linking and users without the expected domain/role.
Verify upload, import, rich text, URL-fetch and export paths apply specialist validation and authorization. Include storage access policies and server-side rejection before harmful or costly effects.
Confirm API/admin/worker entry points enforce the same material permissions as the UI. A hidden menu, unlisted URL or disabled button is not deployed authorization.

Review security-relevant changes against the final candidate through the project's existing process. Invalidate affected review evidence after relevant edits; do not treat tool installation as proof of review.

Inspect release source/history exposure, frontend bundles, container layers, CI artifacts, logs, diagnostic endpoints and committed configuration for privileged credentials. Record inspected surfaces and limits.
Revoke/rotate exposed credentials and verify downstream services use the new secret. Deleting the visible string does not invalidate an already exposed key or token.
Verify least-privilege provider/database/service credentials and environment separation. A staging leak must not grant unnecessary production payment, backup or administrative capabilities.
Link the candidate to its source and build inputs; verify the deployed artifact/digest and configured runtime. Avoid an untracked rebuild or mutable image tag changing what was reviewed.

Run applicable build, lint/type, dependency and container/runtime security checks for the actual stack. Record skipped checks, actionable results and effective deployed versions, not just a local lockfile.
Inspect pipeline permissions, protected release paths, untrusted contribution execution and access to paid/production secrets. Required gates must actually run for the chosen release mechanism.

Check build/install hooks, downloaded binaries, base images and third-party assets for appropriate provenance and licenses. Link specialist findings rather than introducing an unsupported universal certification gate.
Verify secrets/configuration can be restored or reissued through secure references without baking credentials into distributable artifacts. Test access using approved synthetic or scoped credentials.

Verify only intended ports/services are reachable, administrative interfaces are restricted and trusted proxy/firewall rules match the deployed topology. Include database/cache/debug ports on shared hosts.

Attach effective runtime/OS patch ownership and container privileges, mounts, resource limits and persistence evidence where relevant. A healthy local container does not establish host hardening or durable storage.

Confirm provider accounts are active, funded or contracted as required, out of unintended sandbox mode and provisioned in approved regions. Verify launch-critical quotas and any pending access approvals.

Review third-party scripts, widgets, analytics and support tools for required access, data flow and failure behavior. A vendor outage or blocked script must not prevent an essential unrelated action without a documented reason.
Ensure security findings and production evidence gaps have release consequences, accountable owners and acceptance conditions. Record which inherited infrastructure controls were verified and when.

Verify safe operator response to a compromised key/device/account: access revocation, alternate recovery, protected evidence and production continuity. Link a rehearsal or current verified runbook proportionate to the risk.
Verify the final schema, constraints, indexes and seeded reference data against the candidate. Separate required product data from unsafe test/admin fixtures.

Execute representative create/read/update/delete and export/import journeys for important entities, roles and tenants. Include relationships, active references and declared deletion/retention behavior.
Confirm duplicate submissions, retries and concurrent updates preserve material invariants. Validate persisted results and external effects, not only status codes or successful UI notifications.
Test interrupted writes, partial batches, process restart and dependency timeouts using bounded fixtures. State recovery/reconciliation behavior for work that was accepted but not completed.

Verify storage is durable across restart, redeploy, rescheduling and the selected hosting model. Include uploads, mounted volumes, generated files, encryption keys and metadata, not only database rows.

Attach retention, deletion, audit and privacy-review evidence for applicable data flows. Document production data left in logs, providers, replicas or backups and the intended access/lifecycle policy.

Reconcile real scheduler/worker/repeater ownership across environments and replicas. Record schedule/timezone, overlap, retries, dead-letter handling and freshness alerts for critical background work.
Check queue admission, backpressure, concurrency, backlog age and cancellation. Ensure restart or redrive does not duplicate irreversible effects or replay retired work.

Inventory live provider endpoints, credentials, scopes, callback registrations, schema/API versions and owners. Identify critical dependencies still waiting for approval, verification or production access.
Test callback/webhook authentication, duplicate delivery, replay, delay and out-of-order events. Invalid/duplicate events must not create unauthorized state, charges, grants or notifications.
Exercise provider timeout/outage/rate-limit behavior with controlled faults. Bound retries across SDK, gateway, worker and application layers and track ambiguous outcomes for reconciliation.

Verify live sender identity and applicable email authentication, reply/contact routes and delivery configuration. Use approved recipients or sandbox/stub evidence; distinguish accepted-by-provider from delivered/read.
Check message templates, links, expiry, locale/timezone, attachments and unsubscribe/preferences where applicable. Prevent real marketing or transactional sends from test/staging workflows.
Test external consumer/API compatibility for changed contracts, event schemas, pagination and authentication. Document deprecation, version transition and recovery for unsupported clients.
Verify production payment account, intended live products/prices/currency/tax configuration, keys, callback secrets and return URLs. Keep sandbox and live identifiers visibly distinct in evidence.

Attach sandbox lifecycle evidence for success, decline, additional authentication, duplicate submission, abandon/retry and ambiguous completion. Any live verification must be separately authorized and tightly bounded.
Verify refund/partial-refund, cancel/reactivate, delinquency, trial expiry and downgrade behavior against policy. Confirm provider, internal financial state, entitlement and effective time agree.
Replay delayed/duplicated/out-of-order financial callbacks and test direct protected operations. Client redirects or UI claims alone must not establish payment authority or grant access.
Verify receipts/invoices, renewal notices and support refund/cancellation tools as applicable. Ensure staff permissions and audit trails match actual support duties.

Confirm server-authoritative prices, plans and credit grants, including promotions and referrals. Test concurrent quota/credit admission and queued work across expiry or revocation using synthetic balances.

Record expected launch traffic, marketing bursts, data sizes, expensive operations, concurrent sessions and dependency demand. Identify uncertainty and available headroom rather than inventing a precise forecast.

Use bounded authorized capacity evidence on representative infrastructure where risk warrants it. Include cold starts, caches, connection pools, shared-host contention and the configured scaling ceiling.
Verify per-request duration/size, connection, upload, result and concurrency limits plus tenant/global controls. Include public demos, signup/reset, exports and legacy routes that bypass the UI.

Attach effective AI/messaging/storage/egress/compute budgets and application stop evidence. Distinguish provider alerts, quotas and actual spending rejection, including reporting lag and in-flight liabilities.
Check plan economics under allowed maximum usage, expiry of credits/discounts and a heavy legitimate user. Record deliberate subsidies, overage and exposure ownership.
Verify operators can suspend abuse, revoke keys/sessions and stop queued/retrying expensive work. Preserve legitimate shared-IP/API/accessibility access and record residual uncancellable effects.
Bound recurring jobs, orphan resources, preview environments and subscriptions. Ensure launch or migration does not leave duplicate paid work or forgotten old environments active.

Confirm database, disk/inodes, memory, CPU/GPU, sockets, queue storage and provider service quotas can support the defined exposure. Fixed-price infrastructure can fail from capacity exhaustion without a billing spike.

For AI features, attach evaluation evidence for advertised capabilities, material failure modes and unsupported behavior. Include representative task inputs and release-specific model/prompt/tool changes.
Verify tenant/data isolation and permissions for retrieval and tools, including synthetic untrusted-content attempts. Generated text must not itself authorize privileged actions or budget increases.

Bound agent turns, tool fan-out, total run cost/time, retries, continuations and model fallbacks. Test exhausted-budget and stream-disconnect behavior without assuming remote work automatically stops.
Check file/media processing, archive expansion, large import/export and batch workloads for bounded CPU/memory/disk/output. Preserve safe partial results and cleanup according to policy.
Define degraded behavior when a critical provider is unavailable or unaffordable. Preserve user work and honest status; do not silently send data to a new provider or charge for unstarted work.
Reconcile launch-critical findings from data reliability, integrations, payments, AI and cost modules into the candidate's release decision with owners and acceptance evidence.
Identify the exact artifact, configuration, secrets references, schema requirements and deployment entry point. Verify the artifact promoted to production is the candidate actually reviewed.
Record deploy owner, operator access, prerequisites, expected duration, change conflicts and a run-of-show with ordered steps and stop points. Use the existing project release mechanism.

Rehearse build/promotion/deploy on representative isolated infrastructure with the intended runtime, proxy, persistence and worker startup. Record deviations from production and unresolved portability assumptions.

Verify health/readiness/startup checks reflect appropriate dependencies and do not route traffic before useful service is available. Distinguish safe liveness from dependency failures that would cause restart loops.

Check graceful drain, connection/stream handling, long jobs and termination deadlines during update. Test interruption and retries according to actual service promises rather than assuming zero downtime.
Verify staged rollout/cohort/feature-flag targeting and server enforcement. Check anonymous, logged-in, old-client and alternate-route access, flag defaults, expiry and unauthorized flag changes.
Confirm cache invalidation, asset versioning and service-worker behavior do not mix incompatible frontend/backend versions. Test a returning session and stale CDN/browser assets.
Verify post-deploy smoke checks include essential user outcomes, authentication, write/read, background completion and applicable money/provider paths, with safe bounded effects.

Review schema migration order, transaction/lock behavior, expected runtime, free space and required permissions using a representative bounded rehearsal. Identify destructive/irreversible steps explicitly.
Test old/new application and worker versions against the schema during rolling deployment. Use compatible expansion/transition/contraction or a documented maintenance alternative.
Verify data backfills/conversions are bounded, resumable and reconcilable. Include partial failure, duplicates, invalid legacy records and concurrent new writes; record checkpoints and ownership.

Confirm message/event/API contracts remain compatible with queued old jobs, delayed callbacks and supported installed clients. A completed database migration does not establish external consumer compatibility.
Define migration authority and exactly which process can run each change. Prevent multiple deploy replicas or old/new environments from performing the same non-idempotent migration/job.
Verify downgrade/rollback compatibility with newly written data and changed provider state. Record a fail-forward path or maintenance recovery when a binary rollback would corrupt or lose valid work.

Inventory required recovery assets: databases, uploaded/generated files, persistent volumes, configuration, keys, identity dependencies and external-system references. State what cannot be reconstructed.
Define RPO and RTO from product needs and commitments. Compare measured backup age/coverage and recovery time with those targets; a nominal daily schedule is not proof of adequacy.

Verify backups actually complete, remain accessible after account/host failure and have appropriate encryption, access and retention. Include recovery key and vendor-account availability without exposing secrets.

Perform or attach a recent representative isolated restore and validate application-readable data, integrity, permissions and files. A successful backup log or checksum alone does not prove usable recovery.
Test the recovery access path independently of the failed application/host. Keep runbooks and required recovery references available outside the failure domain.

State restore consequences for accepted writes, payment effects, idempotency records, credits and external callbacks after the recovery point. Reconcile rather than replaying irreversible effects blindly.
Define objective pause/rollback/fail-forward triggers and who can invoke them. Record executable steps, known limitations, required data checkpoint and time to restoration.
Rehearse the chosen recovery using a synthetic candidate failure. Validate essential journeys and data/provider consistency after recovery; a script's zero exit code alone is insufficient.
For hosting/domain changes, verify source/destination dependencies, persistent storage, network/TLS, callbacks, identity redirects and provider allowlists before traffic moves.
Declare the authoritative writer and ownership of jobs/events/queues at each cutover step. Prevent split-brain, duplicate charges, duplicated notifications and writes to an abandoned database.

Rehearse initial copy, deltas/final sync, write freeze where needed, verification and traffic switch with measured duration. Compare records/files using suitable counts, checksums and domain-level validation.

Account for DNS caching, long-lived connections, CDN propagation and clients still reaching the old host. Define treatment of late writes/callbacks without assuming a record change moves all traffic instantly.
Record when rollback becomes unsafe because data or external effects diverge. Preserve a data-safe reconciliation/fail-forward plan; switching DNS back is not a complete recovery procedure.
Keep old infrastructure only for a justified recovery/retention window with owners and budgets. Disable duplicate processing and retire unused resources/credentials after evidence permits it.

Verify rollback/redeploy cannot resurrect retired jobs, permissive flags, consumed quotas or obsolete credentials. Test restored configuration and actual scheduler state, not just the current source tree.
Record evidence, measured durations, residual data/financial discrepancies and remaining manual steps from deployment and recovery rehearsals. Bind results to the final procedure and candidate.
Ensure material rehearsal failures are corrected or reflected in the release decision. Define focused retests after migration, recovery procedure or configuration changes.
