Hand over recoverable artifacts, configuration references, data checkpoints and owners. Verify the nominated backup operator can locate the procedure and obtain authorized access.

Verify external monitoring from outside the application's failure domain for an appropriate public/core path. A running process or always-green health endpoint is not sufficient evidence of useful service.
Capture meaningful browser/client/server/worker/integration errors with release, request/job/event correlation. Control sensitive payloads, log access, sampling and retention.
Measure critical outcome success, errors, representative latency, traffic and saturation. Define metric windows/denominators and distinguish client retries from unique outcomes.
Monitor queue depth/age, scheduled-task freshness, webhook backlog, backup age, certificate/domain expiry and provider dependency failures where applicable. A missing run may emit no exception.
Verify actionable capacity, unexpected spend, abuse and security signals. Distinguish delayed estimates from actual enforced limits and include monitoring's own cost/cardinality.
Exercise one controlled relevant failure through the real monitoring route. Record detection, delivery, recipient, acknowledgement/escalation and the operator action available.
Suppress duplicate/noisy alerts and retain detection for important failures during deploy/maintenance. A temporary silence needs an owner and expiry so launch does not remain unmonitored.
If analytics serves a defined product need, verify meaningful events, privacy/consent behavior and duplicate/test traffic filtering. Optional analytics is not a universal release prerequisite.
Name primary and backup responders with realistic availability, access and escalation. Schedule exposure/ramp stages when the required response capability actually exists.
Keep concise runbooks for outage, data loss, failed deploy, compromised account/key, provider outage, payment drift, backlog and uncontrolled spend where relevant.

Verify runbooks, credential-recovery references and incident communication remain accessible during host/application/account failure. Avoid placing the sole recovery instructions in the system being recovered.
Test a support contact route using synthetic content and confirm accountable receipt. Verify help links, expected response commitments and routing for billing, safety/security and account recovery.
Give staff sufficient scoped tooling for refunds, suspensions, data corrections, queue handling and customer recovery. Check authorization/auditing and avoid support privileges becoming a bypass.

Prepare troubleshooting/help material for known limitations, failed onboarding, quota exhaustion and supported platforms. Staff should know actual enabled features and conditions, not just marketing promises.

Define incident lead, technical response and customer communication duties. Link security/privacy/legal processes for notification assessment where applicable without inventing a universal notification deadline.
Verify customer/status communication channels as needed, including their access and independence from the failed service. Drafted announcements are not sent as part of an audit.

Complete a preflight for candidate/config/schema identity, owner availability, prerequisites, external provider health, backups and competing changes. Reassess if the environment has materially drifted.
Record the final decision through the established process with scope, evidence, blockers, risk acceptances and prerequisites. Do not treat an auditor's checklist completion as release authorization.
Use a stepwise run-of-show identifying actor, action, expected state/evidence, deadline and stop/recovery condition. Include activation, traffic routing, job ownership and post-deploy smoke.

At each ramp stage, compare actual outcomes with baseline/control and declared gates. Confirm enough representative traffic/time for the interpretation; low error count with no real usage is weak evidence.
Verify kill switches, scoped feature disablement, admission limits and recovery controls are available to the responder. Define user-facing behavior and treatment of queued/in-flight work.
Pause or recover when agreed triggers fire; record action time, affected cohort and external/data effects. Avoid continuing the ramp solely because an announcement or deadline exists.
Revalidate smoke journeys, provider callbacks, worker freshness, entitlement and important metrics after configuration/routing changes. Check the actual user-facing host and deployed artifact.
Coordinate publication, invitation and marketing timing with actual availability and support readiness. Verify old links and newly announced entry points once authorized exposure begins.
Define an observation window based on material usage and critical schedules: renewals, scheduled jobs, daily/weekly tasks or delayed events may need evidence after immediate smoke checks.

Assign delayed verification owners/dates for billing, renewals, long-running jobs, search processing, backups and propagation. Distinguish current deployed success from future confirmation still pending.
Review support feedback, false-positive abuse blocks, accessibility issues and cohort-specific failures during the ramp. Update scope and pause criteria when new material behavior appears.
Close temporary credentials, debug instrumentation, alert silences, test accounts and obsolete environments under authorized lifecycle rules. Preserve evidence and required recovery/retention copies.

Hand over service ownership, inventory, budgets, contracts/renewals, support, incident access and recovery artifacts. Confirm the backup operator can use the handoff without relying on one person's laptop or memory.
Deduplicate launch defects into the owning backlog with priority, acceptance tests, owner and due/review date. Track unresolved verification gaps and expiring risk acceptances explicitly.
Record launch outcome against the scoped goals, actual exposure, incidents and rollback/degraded operation. Separate technical release success from business adoption or later growth results.

Capture proportionate lessons and reusable procedure fixes after material incidents or surprising launch behavior. Define when evidence/gates need refresh for the next release rather than repeating every check automatically.

headings.text: Legal, licensing, and content IP audit library
Change, supply chain, and exceptional cases
Content, assets, ownership, and user contributions
Open content, quotations, brands, and databases
Commercial behavior, marketing, contracts, and platform terms
Email, SMS, calls, and audience acquisition
AI, specialist surfaces, and cross-border cases
Audit Legal licensing and content IP
Legal, licensing, and content IP audit — [product/release]

values: Identify applicable privacy, cookie, consumer, accessibility, marketing, platform, and sector-specific requirements. Do not assume that every project has the same obligations or that the operator's location is the only relevant jurisdiction.
Verify public identity/contact information and applicable privacy, terms, acceptable-use, refund/cancellation, and cookie notices. Compare their promises with actual processing and product behavior.

Identify personal data purposes, legal bases, recipients, retention, user rights, processors/subprocessors, processing agreements, and cross-border transfers where applicable. Coordinate implemented access/export/deletion with 01 and 09.

Inventory cookies and similar tracking. Determine which are essential and which require consent under applicable rules; verify blocked-before-consent behavior, withdrawal, and accessible controls. For Spanish rules, consult current AEPD guidance, including equal visibility of acceptance/rejection where applicable. [AEPD cookie guidance](https://www.aepd.es/preguntas-frecuentes/17-internet-y-redes-sociales/FAQ-1707-importancia-de-las-cookies-en-la-proteccion-de-datos)
Assess minors, sensitive data, profiling, automated decisions, and regulated activities if present. Identify where additional controls or specialist review are needed.

Determine whether children's privacy requirements apply from the intended audience, actual use/knowledge, countries, and data collected. For applicable COPPA flows, verify notices, verifiable parental consent, parental rights, minimization, and retention; test any age screen before collection. Do not add date-of-birth collection to every general-audience product or assume an age checkbox alone satisfies the requirements. [FTC COPPA guidance](https://www.ftc.gov/business-guidance/resources/complying-coppa-frequently-asked-questions)

Inventory browser requests to external font, asset, analytics, chat, and replay providers, including requests made before consent. Assess disclosed recipients, legal basis, and international transfers even when no cookie is set. Consider licensed self-hosted fonts to avoid unnecessary third-party requests; check the actual applicable rules rather than treating one court award as a universal tariff. [Bavarian authority's external-font guidance, scoped to public bodies](https://www.datenschutz-bayern.de/datenschutzreform2018/aki42.html)

Where session replay, heatmaps, keystroke capture, or chat recording exists, assess applicable privacy and communications-interception rules, including California CIPA where relevant. Record provider roles, purposes, notice/consent timing, sensitive routes, and permitted retention. Require qualified review of disputed applicability; neither a banner nor field masking alone establishes lawful recording. Use 01 for capture and consent verification.
Record incident-notification assessment, retention/deletion exceptions, and responsible decision makers. Check that support and analytics do not introduce undeclared processing.
Inventory licenses for source dependencies, SDKs, images, stock assets, fonts, icons, audio/music, video, datasets, models, and exported content.

Check rights for the exact use: web display, server processing, embedding in exports, redistribution, modification, resale, commercial use, and training where relevant. Attribution requirements vary by source and license.
Keep required notices and evidence of asset/license provenance. Verify that a purchased or downloadable asset actually permits the intended distribution.

Review current API and platform terms for storage/caching, resale, branding, generated output, prohibited uses, scraping, and rate limits. Record provider/version/date; do not generalize one vendor's terms to another.
Define rights and responsibilities for user uploads and generated output. Include complaint/takedown handling where relevant and avoid guaranteeing exclusive rights that cannot be established.

If relying on US DMCA section 512 safe harbor, assess eligibility for the actual service activities. Where required, verify a current registered designated agent and publicly accessible contact details, renewal ownership, notice/counter-notice handling, expeditious action, and a reasonably implemented repeat-infringer policy. Registration alone does not establish eligibility; record the other applicable conditions and legal review. [Copyright Office section 512 guidance](https://www.copyright.gov/512/), [designated-agent directory](https://www.copyright.gov/dmca-directory/)

For AI or synthetic media, assess applicable disclosure, personality/publicity rights, impersonation, deceptive advertising, and testimonial rules. Distinguish a presenter reading approved copy from claims of real customer experience; verify legal requirements for the actual audience and format.
Compare marketing claims, endorsements, affiliate/sponsor disclosures, price display, taxes, trial conversions, renewals, cancellation, and refunds against applicable obligations.
Verify transactional versus marketing email/message treatment, consent or other permission, opt-out/unsubscribe, suppression, and recordkeeping. Use 14 for delivery implementation.

Classify launch announcements and mixed promotional/account messages by their actual primary purpose. Where CAN-SPAM applies, verify truthful sender/subject information, advertising identification as required, a valid physical postal address, and an easy opt-out honored within the applicable period. An existing customer relationship does not by itself make a promotional email transactional; assess other applicable marketing rules separately. [FTC CAN-SPAM guide](https://www.ftc.gov/business-guidance/resources/can-spam-act-compliance-guide-business)

Determine applicable automatic-renewal rules for consumer subscriptions and trials, including California where relevant. Check clear pre-purchase renewal/price/frequency/cancellation disclosures, placement relative to consent, affirmative consent and evidence, acknowledgments, required reminders/change notices, and usable cancellation. Assign applicable timing and remedy questions to the responsible reviewer; do not assume every renewal creates an automatic refund. Use 13 for end-to-end verification. [California Attorney General renewal guidance](https://oag.ca.gov/node/608083)
Check contracts, domain/brand ownership, customer support obligations, and required records for the product's distribution model.

Determine whether SOC 2 assurance, healthcare rules such as HIPAA, payment-card requirements, or other sector/contractual controls actually apply. Record scope, accountable specialists, and required evidence; a checklist does not establish certification or compliance.

Where required, verify appropriate processor agreements or BAAs cover each relevant vendor and service, including AI providers. Confirm approved services, uses, and data flows before sending regulated data; do not infer applicability from the presence of any health-related record alone.
Verify promised data residency across primary storage, replicas, backups, logs, support access, subprocessors, and model/fallback routing. Record any exceptions and their contractual basis.

Trace access/export/deletion requests through related tables, files, logs, derived data, and vendors. Document justified retention exceptions and backup expiry; ensure restores do not silently reactivate data that must remain deleted.

Keep evidence-backed security questionnaire answers and required policy/audit records current. Match claims to the actual scope, independent assurance evidence, and known exceptions; use 01 for security testing, disclosure, access reviews, and read-audit controls.
Test the exact shipped artifact, deployment, policy version, provider plan and contractual entity; an approved demo or different plan is not equivalent evidence.
Check public preview, beta, free, trial and internal-only claims against actual external access/distribution and data collection.
Inspect white-label, reseller and client handover paths for notices, rights, data duties and allocation of responsibility beyond the primary brand.
Recheck rights and obligations when a previously private upload, repository, dashboard or export becomes public or shared externally.
Verify pending, revoked, expired, territory-limited and replaced permissions cannot silently remain approved in the release process.
Test vendor outages, fallback services and emergency migrations for undeclared data use, rights restrictions and contract/residency changes.
Review long-lived offline/device/downloaded releases for continuing notice, source-delivery, support and update obligations after hosted pages change.
Check account deletion, cancellation, subscription expiry and license termination as distinct events with their own data, payment and rights consequences.
Verify complaints, legal holds and preservation instructions do not silently conflict with ordinary deletion/cleanup jobs; assign and document the decision.
Review import, export, restore, duplicate submissions and failed background jobs for promises that are met in the UI but not across the completed process.
Verify marketing, customer contracts, policies and provider terms remain consistent after a feature, model, region or pricing change.
Separate unknown rights/applicability from confirmed noncompliance and enhancements; retain unresolved questions with an owner and required decision date.
Inventory direct/transitive dependencies, vendored files, copied snippets, generated scaffolding, plugins and submodules; reconcile manifests against build and shipped artifacts.
Inspect server, browser, mobile, desktop, extension, CLI, device and on-premises outputs separately; code served to a browser is part of the distribution analysis.
Include build tools and development dependencies when their code, runtime helpers, templates or bundled assets appear in outputs; a devDependency label is not decisive.
Record exact version/commit, origin, hash, copyright holder, license text and modifications; preserve evidence if an upstream repository disappears.
Treat missing, conflicting, placeholder or repository-only license metadata as unresolved; inspect file headers, package contents, exceptions and separate asset directories.
Distinguish public availability from a permission grant; code visible on a website or public repository is not automatically licensed for reuse.
Review pasted forum answers, tutorials, gists and AI-suggested snippets for source and applicable rights; attribution alone does not necessarily authorize reuse.
Record forks, patches, generated code and downstream modifications; upstream scanning results do not automatically cover local changes.
Preserve precise SPDX expressions, including OR, AND, WITH, version-only/later distinctions and custom LicenseRef texts; document the actual selected option.
Assess compatibility for the actual combination, linking, modification and conveyance; do not infer a legal conclusion solely from “permissive” or “copyleft” labels.
Examine dual/commercial licensing choices, eligibility, covered entity, payment, version and deployment rights; buying one seat does not establish all organizational rights.
Review source-available and restricted licenses for hosting, competing-service, production, user, revenue or field-of-use limits; “source available” does not mean OSI open source.
Assess time-delayed license changes against the exact release/date and grant; do not apply a future open license to an earlier restricted period without a basis.
Check license exceptions, linking permissions and separate notices rather than applying the base license in isolation.
Record applicable patent grants, retaliation/termination provisions, excluded trademark rights and other permissions needing review; a copyright license is not every right clearance.
Route ambiguous aggregation/derivative-work, plugin, IPC and static/dynamic-linking questions to a documented qualified decision rather than relying on process boundaries alone.
Retain required copyright, license and disclaimer text in the form required for the actual distribution; verify notices in archives/installers, not only the repository.
Review Apache-licensed material for applicable license, modification and NOTICE handling; do not assume every project has identical NOTICE content.
Include file-specific attribution, acknowledgments, advertising or documentation obligations where the actual license requires them; don't generalize modern BSD terms to every variant.
Check minification, tree shaking, compression and packaging do not strip required notices without an adequate compliant delivery mechanism.
Verify app-store packages, offline installations, container images, downloadable SDKs and generated exports carry their applicable notices after the final build.
Distinguish necessary legal notices from unnecessary disclosure of internal inventories, secrets or confidential components; publish what is required and retain internal evidence separately.
Confirm notice links work after domain changes, shutdown, offline use and long-lived device releases where the chosen compliance method requires them.
Verify localization and white-label/reseller packaging preserve required text and identify the responsible distributor.
Identify each GPL/LGPL/AGPL/MPL or other reciprocal component and the exact obligations triggered by modifications, combination, distribution or network interaction.
For relevant GPL distributions, assess corresponding-source scope, build/install materials, delivery method and exact-version correspondence using the controlling license.
Test source download/offer fulfillment as the actual recipient; inaccessible links, wrong versions and missing local patches remain gaps.

If relying on a written offer, verify allowed use of that route, recipients, duration, fulfillment ownership and preservation of source for the required period; do not assume a generic offer fits all versions.
For LGPL cases assess the actual linking/relinking mechanism, modifications, notices and applicable recipient rights; static versus dynamic linking is a fact, not a complete conclusion.
For MPL cases identify covered files, modifications and relevant source availability without assuming the entire application has the same obligation.
For modified AGPL-covered network software assess the exact remote-interaction source requirement; “we only run SaaS” is not a sufficient exclusion rationale.
Where applicable examine installation information and anti-circumvention/recipient-rights provisions; contracts or DRM must not negate rights granted by the relevant license.
Verify commercial SDK, engine, library and plugin rights for developer seats, build servers, contractors, revenue tiers, territories and redistribution.
Check evaluation, educational, personal-use, startup, nonprofit and free-tier restrictions against actual production/commercial use and current eligibility.
Inventory base images, operating-system packages, drivers, codecs, firmware, fonts and models shipped in containers/devices; an application SBOM alone may omit them.
Review codec, cryptography, patent-pool and media-format issues where relevant; an open-source implementation alone does not settle every patent or territory question.
Check hosted services, APIs and managed databases for customer access, embedding, white-label, resale, benchmarking and competing-product restrictions in applicable terms.
Review marketplace/app-store agreements, signing accounts and distribution rules alongside software licenses; resolve conflicting recipient restrictions before release.
Verify license keys, activation and offline rights are assigned to the right entity/environment and survive permitted disaster recovery or migration.
Check vendor end-of-term obligations: uninstall, cease use, remove redistributables, preserve permitted customer access and fulfill surviving obligations.
Change, supply chain, and exceptional cases
Detect license changes on dependency upgrades, forks, acquisitions and package-name substitutions; prior approval does not cover every future version.
Change, supply chain, and exceptional cases
Reconcile SBOM/scanner results with original texts and manual review; false matches, unknown binaries and custom licenses remain tracked.
Change, supply chain, and exceptional cases
Inspect examples, test fixtures, sample media, documentation and demonstration datasets included in a public repo or package for separate rights.
Change, supply chain, and exceptional cases
Review contributions, CLAs, DCO/sign-off practices and inbound/outbound rights; a sign-off or platform account is not automatically a complete IP assignment.
Change, supply chain, and exceptional cases
Confirm the organization has authority to publish its chosen outbound license, including employee, contractor and pre-existing third-party code.
Change, supply chain, and exceptional cases
For customer-specific builds, air-gapped deliveries and resellers verify artifact-specific notices/source access and identify who fulfills recipient requests.
Change, supply chain, and exceptional cases

If a rights defect is found, assess affected releases, recipients, potential cure/termination issues and replacement/source-delivery options with the accountable reviewer; do not assume deleting code cures historical distribution.
Change, supply chain, and exceptional cases
Rebuild the final artifact after remediation and verify notices, source correspondence and selected license route; a manifest edit alone does not prove release compliance.
Inventory copy, code, design, photos, illustrations, icons, video, music, voices, fonts, templates, documents, datasets and models, including hidden/demo/exported material.
Identify actual owners and each transfer/license in the chain; a seller, agency or uploader may not own every underlying right.
Review employee-created work against applicable law, employment terms, scope and pre-existing material; do not assume employment transfers all rights everywhere.
Verify freelancer, contractor, agency and subcontractor grants cover deliverables, source files, modification, territories, duration, media and intended redistribution.
Distinguish assignment from an exclusive/non-exclusive license and record retained rights, moral-rights treatment and execution requirements where relevant.
Review founder contributions, prior employers, acquisitions, joint development, grants and university/research obligations for gaps or conflicting rights.
Check commissioned work that contains stock assets, templates, licensed fonts or subcontracted material; the commissioned-work agreement may not convey those underlying rights.
Preserve invoices, permissions, releases, accepted terms, source versions and usage history; a receipt without the applicable grant is incomplete evidence.
Verify stock-photo/illustration licenses for commercial/editorial use, advertising, products for resale, audience/impression limits and sensitive contexts.
Check model/property releases where relevant; copyright permission and recognizable-person, trademark or location rights are distinct questions.
Review screenshots, product interfaces, maps, third-party logos and brand guidelines for the specific context; a press kit is not unrestricted permission.
Check icon packs, design-system assets, themes, templates and marketplace purchases for redistribution, extraction, client transfer and white-label restrictions.
Identify font rights separately for desktop use, web serving, mobile/app embedding, server rendering, PDF/e-book exports and redistribution.
Verify font licenses cover actual domains, traffic/seat limits, contractors, customer-generated documents and editable output where relevant.
Assess self-hosting, CDN delivery, subsetting, format conversion and embedding permissions; self-hosting can reduce a data flow but does not create font rights.
Inspect exported slides, PDFs, social cards, videos and printable merchandise for assets that were licensed only for display within the original app.
Separate music composition, recording, performance, synchronization and other relevant rights; permission for one layer may not cover the final video, stream or event.
Check music/sound libraries for platforms, advertising, client work, games, distribution, monetization and automated claim/Content ID restrictions.
Review voiceover, actor, presenter and performer agreements for territories, term, edits, paid advertising and synthetic reuse/voice cloning.
Distinguish an authorized scripted presenter from a claimed real customer; reviews and testimonials require separate substantiation and disclosure review.
Verify live-event/webinar recording, audience participation, transcripts, clips and later replay have the applicable permissions and notices.
Check recognizable people, names, likeness, voice, private information and impersonation for applicable publicity/personality, privacy and deceptive-use concerns.
Review translations, adaptations, dubbing, captioning and accessibility conversions for the relevant permission or applicable exception; do not assume every adaptation is unrestricted.
Ensure accessibility alternatives and asset replacements meet their own rights requirements while preserving equivalent content for users.
Open content, quotations, brands, and databases
Record the precise Creative Commons license/version/jurisdiction and source; apply attribution, adaptation, share-alike, noncommercial and no-derivatives terms to the actual use.
Open content, quotations, brands, and databases

Assess whether proposed edits/translations constitute restricted adaptations and whether planned commercial contexts fit the actual grant; escalate uncertainty rather than treating NC/ND as decorative labels.
Open content, quotations, brands, and databases
Verify attribution includes required information and modification indication in a suitable location; preserve links and notices in copies/exports when required.
Open content, quotations, brands, and databases
Check public-domain/CC0 assertions by work, territory, term and rights type; public-domain copyright status does not automatically settle privacy, trademark or contractual restrictions.
Open content, quotations, brands, and databases

Assess quotations, excerpts, thumbnails, parody, fair use/fair dealing and other exceptions against the actual jurisdiction, purpose and amount; no universal word count or attribution rule guarantees permission.
Open content, quotations, brands, and databases
Review product names, domains, logos, app names and trade dress for clearance, territory/class conflicts and misleading affiliation; domain registration is not trademark clearance.
Open content, quotations, brands, and databases
Check comparative claims, competitor marks, badges and compatibility statements for substantiation and appropriate presentation; avoid implying sponsorship or certification without evidence.
Open content, quotations, brands, and databases
Identify database, dataset, map and compilation rights separately from individual facts; inspect extraction/reuse terms, territorial rights and update obligations.
Terms request only the upload/content rights needed for the service and separately address publication, promotion, sublicensing, training and post-deletion survival where relevant.
Verify the user granting rights has capacity/authority and that shared workspace, employer and co-author scenarios are covered; a checkbox is not proof of ownership.
Review public/private defaults, embeds, sharing links, remixing, exports and cross-tenant reuse against actual user permissions and expectations.
Check removal/deletion implications for caches, public embeds, licensed derivatives and prior exports; explain operational limits without promising impossible recall.
Offer usable channels for copyright, trademark, privacy, impersonation and other complaints; route them correctly rather than treating every complaint as copyright.
If relying on US section 512 protection, review eligibility and conditions for the service activity, designated agent requirements, public contacts and renewal ownership where applicable.
Test notice intake, required information, validation, prompt handling, user notification and evidence retention using synthetic internal cases; registration alone does not establish safe harbor.

Review counter-notice, restoration, repeat-infringer and disputed-ownership handling against the applicable procedure; record legally confirmed response windows rather than inventing one global deadline.
For EU intermediary/platform activity, classify the service and applicable DSA duties, exemptions, notice/action, reasons and redress; do not copy DMCA procedure as a universal substitute.
Distinguish illegal-content handling from platform-policy enforcement; moderation and appeal notices explain the actual basis and applicable route.
Prevent complaint abuse, doxxing and unnecessary exposure of claimant/user information; verify authorized case access and evidence preservation.
Address reuploads, mirrors, thumbnails, search indexes and syndicated copies consistently after a confirmed action, while respecting scope and valid appeals.
Before publication, reconcile the final asset/version/crop/translation with its permission and attribution; approval of a draft does not cover substituted assets.
Track expiring, territory-limited, campaign-only and revocable grants; identify affected URLs, ads, binaries and exports when use must stop or change.
Check migration, acquisition, entity changes and client handover for transfer/sublicensing restrictions and the ability to deliver provenance records.
When a disputed asset is replaced, assess historical copies, complaints, contractual commitments and preservation duties; removal does not by itself resolve past use.
Inventory data collection through UI, APIs, devices, uploads, integrations, support, recruitment, billing, logs and inferred/derived information; inspect deployed traffic and settings.
Identify controller, joint-controller, processor, service-provider or other applicable roles by activity; a vendor's label does not alone settle the relationship.
Map each purpose to relevant categories, people, source, legal basis/permission, recipients, locations, retention and required transparency.
Separate account/service delivery, fraud prevention, analytics, personalization, marketing, advertising, research and AI training purposes; do not silently reuse one purpose's authorization.
Assess necessity and minimization field by field; remove unjustified required data and avoid collecting identity documents or birth dates by default.
Review sensitive/special-category, biometric, precise-location, financial, communications and inferred data under the applicable definitions and conditions.
Where consent is relied upon, verify freely given, informed, specific and demonstrable choice plus withdrawal under applicable rules; an audit log alone cannot cure an invalid choice.
Where another basis is relied upon, document its actual conditions and any required assessment; do not use “legitimate interest” or “contract” as an unexplained blanket label.
Privacy notices identify the responsible entity, purposes, recipients, retention information and rights/contact routes required for the actual context.
Collection-time notices appear before or when required, including indirect collection and unexpected sensitive uses; a buried general policy may be insufficient.
Compare “we do not sell/share/train,” retention, residency and encryption claims with vendors, toggles, logs, advertising and actual processing.
Cover employee/applicant, customer/end-user, visitor and uploaded-third-party information separately where processing differs.
Check translations, mobile/webview versions and authenticated routes for current consistent notices and usable access.
Version policy and permission changes, assess whether renewed notice/choice is required, and preserve applicable acceptance evidence without claiming every edit needs fresh consent.
Inventory cookies, pixels, local/session storage, device identifiers, fingerprinting, SDKs and server-side tracking; absence of cookies does not prove absence of tracking.
Classify each purpose and provider against the relevant exemption/permission rules; a vendor or CMP “essential” label is not sufficient evidence.
On a clean browser profile, inspect network/storage before any choice, after reject, after category selection and after accept; verify actual behavior, not banner configuration alone.
Test direct deep links, login, embedded media, payment pages, SPA transitions, delayed tags and third-party widgets for bypasses of the intended tracking controls.
Check acceptance/rejection presentation against applicable guidance; for Spain examine AEPD's same-time, same-level and same-visibility expectations in context.
Confirm granular choices, clear purposes, no unauthorized preselection and usable access to settings; assess coercive/cookie-wall designs against current applicable rules.
Withdraw or change choices and verify propagation to tags, vendors, server events and stored identifiers where required; refreshing only the banner state is insufficient.
Record consent evidence with scope/version/time and necessary identifiers, plus expiry/re-prompt rules justified by applicable authority and changed purposes.
Test browser privacy signals, global opt-out controls and sale/share/targeted-advertising opt-outs where applicable; verify backend action rather than a UI-only toggle.
Examine external fonts, assets, chat, maps, analytics and replay requests for data disclosures/transfers even without cookies; a single court award is not a universal tariff.
Assess session replay, heatmaps, keystrokes, call/chat recording and communications interception, including CIPA where relevant; field masking or a banner alone is not a legal conclusion.
Test sensitive routes, query strings, DOM content, shadow roots, attachments and pasted fields for recording leakage; coordinate security verification without collecting real sensitive content.
Match each processor/service provider and subprocessor to the actual service, entity, signed terms, purpose and permitted data categories.
Verify required DPA, BAA, joint-controller or other arrangements and instructions are executed and cover the service/features in use; a sales claim does not replace terms.
Trace international storage, access, support, backups, logs, telemetry, model routing and subprocessors; primary database region alone does not establish residency or transfer compliance.
Determine applicable transfer mechanism and supporting assessments/safeguards where required; distinguish legal entity, destination and data-access facts.
Review vendor training, product improvement, human review, retention, abuse monitoring and fallback use against customer promises and actual service settings.
Check new subprocessors, vendor acquisitions, region changes and plan changes for notice, objection, assessment or contractual action triggers.
Assess data-import providers, enrichment services and purchased audiences for source legitimacy, permitted uses and required indirect-collection notices.
Verify customer offboarding, provider termination and migration include export, deletion/return, evidence and justified surviving retention.
Provide usable intake for applicable access, correction, deletion, portability, objection, restriction and opt-out rights; don't assume every right applies identically everywhere.
Verify identity/authority proportionately, including authorized agents, parents and deceased/incapacitated-user cases as relevant; avoid unnecessary document collection.
Assign jurisdiction-specific response/extension periods and ownership; rehearse discovery, escalation and communication before any real request is due.
Trace access/export requests through tables, files, vendors, logs and derived profiles; protect other people's data and relevant confidential information.
Trace correction/deletion through active stores, search indexes, caches, attachments, analytics, vendors and derived artifacts where applicable.
Document lawful exceptions, dispute/litigation holds, financial records and necessary suppression evidence; deletion is neither “keep everything” nor “erase all records regardless of obligation.”
Inspect backup expiry and restores so deleted data is not silently reactivated; document restrictions and deletion replay where appropriate.
Assign retention by purpose/category and test actual expiry jobs, exports, failed jobs and orphaned data; a written schedule does not prove implementation.
Assess anonymization/pseudonymization claims against realistic reidentification and retained linkage; pseudonymized data is not automatically outside privacy scope.
Preserve sufficient request audit evidence while limiting sensitive content and access; test duplicate, disputed, failed and partially fulfilled requests.
Determine child-directed/mixed/general audience and actual knowledge using applicable rules and evidence; do not add intrusive age collection indiscriminately.
Where COPPA or local child-data rules apply, review required notices, verified parental consent, parental rights, minimization, sharing and retention for current requirements.
Test age/parental flows before relevant collection, including social login, SDK initialization, guest use and attempts to bypass the intended controls.
Evaluate child-oriented design, profiling/advertising restrictions and age-assurance proportionality by jurisdiction; an age checkbox alone does not establish compliance.
Identify profiling, automated eligibility/ranking/decisions and human-review claims; determine applicable information, contest, intervention or impact-assessment obligations.
Assess whether DPIA, risk assessment, DPO/representative or records-of-processing duties apply; record scope, decision and review triggers rather than requiring them universally.
Review employee monitoring, recordings, location and workplace AI for applicable privacy, labor and consultation obligations, including vendor secondary use.
Review health/wellness, biometrics and location use even when a named sector law does not apply; other privacy or consumer rules may remain relevant.
Define incident assessment ownership, relevant clocks, notification thresholds, recipients and evidence preservation according to applicable laws/contracts.
Rehearse a privacy incident with synthetic facts, including vendor notice, wrong-recipient exports and accidental public files; don't assume every event has the same notification rule.
Verify support, analytics, ticket attachments and debug logs do not introduce undeclared processing or defeat retention/deletion commitments.
Recheck legal/data-flow decisions after new features, purposes, vendors, countries, acquisitions and retention changes; update notices and operational controls together.
Verify legal operator, seller, contact and required registration/tax/business disclosures for the markets and channels actually used.
Distinguish terms of service, purchase terms, privacy notices, AUP and service-specific policies; ensure the correct entity and product appear in each.
Inspect acceptance placement, linked terms, timing and evidence by registration/checkout/upgrade flow; don't assume a footer link proves agreement.
Preserve the version accepted, user/organization authority, timestamp and relevant order details; test retrieval when a dispute concerns an older version.
Check order forms, negotiated amendments, DPAs, SLAs, marketplace terms and online terms for incorporation and precedence; don't assume the latest web page overrides signed terms.
Compare liability, warranty, indemnity, dispute, governing-law and unilateral-change provisions with actual obligations and enforceability review; template clauses are not universally valid.
Review minors' contracting capacity, parent/guardian authority and enterprise-admin authority where relevant, separately from privacy permission.
Check policy changes, notice, objection, termination and reacceptance where applicable; preserve historical versions without claiming every edit requires the same process.
Display applicable total-price, currency, tax, mandatory-fee and payment information at the required point; compare ads, plans, cart, confirmation and invoice.
State recurring price, billing interval, minimum term, commitment, trial length and conversion conditions clearly before the relevant consent or commitment.
Test free trials, introductory discounts, credits and usage-based charges for actual conversion/billing behavior matching the disclosed offer.
Determine applicable renewal laws and obtain required affirmative-consent evidence and acknowledgment; distinguish federal, state and local rules and current legal status.
Verify required renewal, trial-end and material-change notices have correct timing/content/channel for the applicable contract and market.
Complete cancellation through each signup channel and plan, including mobile stores and resellers; check barriers, retention offers, login loss and support failures.
Confirm cancellation stops or schedules billing/access as disclosed, communicates effective date and preserves proof; cancellation and refund are separate questions.
Test pause/reactivate, downgrade, annual/monthly change, proration, failed payment and reactivation against applicable terms and disclosure duties.
Review withdrawal/cooling-off rights, exceptions, digital-content/service consents and acknowledgment where relevant; do not apply one global “no refunds” rule.
Match refund, return, guarantee and chargeback handling to applicable rights and contractual promises; do not assume a disclaimer removes statutory remedies.
Reconcile seller/merchant-of-record, tax/invoice and refund responsibilities across payment providers, app stores and marketplaces; vendor handling does not eliminate all operator duties.
Check gift purchases, vouchers, credits, expiry, unclaimed balances and transferred subscriptions for applicable restrictions and clear user information.
Substantiate objective product, performance, savings, security, environmental and comparative claims before publication; preserve methodology, scope and expiry.
Check “free,” “unlimited,” “lifetime,” “anonymous,” “zero retention,” “certified,” “compliant” and “guaranteed” claims against actual limits and evidence.
Review testimonials, reviews and case studies for genuine experience, permission, accuracy, material connections and claims the advertiser can support.
Label affiliates, sponsorships, paid placements, employee reviews and gifted endorsements as required in each medium; placement and clarity matter as well as existence.
Test review collection/moderation for fake reviews, undisclosed incentives, misleading suppression and fabricated social proof; distinguish verified purchase from broader authenticity claims.
Inspect countdowns, scarcity, stock, discounts and reference prices for factual accuracy across refresh, locale and user variants.
Review AI avatars, synthetic voices and composite customers for required disclosure and deceptive-endorsement risks; a presenter is not necessarily a real user.
Check competitions, giveaways, referrals, loyalty schemes and influencer campaigns for local eligibility, terms, prize, tax and platform conditions before launch.
Email, SMS, calls, and audience acquisition
Classify transactional, marketing and mixed messages by actual content/purpose and applicable rules; an existing account does not make every announcement transactional.
Email, SMS, calls, and audience acquisition
Record lawful permission/consent or other valid route for each channel, audience, sender and territory; email and SMS permissions are not automatically interchangeable.
Email, SMS, calls, and audience acquisition
Where CAN-SPAM applies, verify sender/subject truthfulness, required advertising identification, valid postal address, usable opt-out and timely honoring under the current rule.
Email, SMS, calls, and audience acquisition
Where EU/UK or other local electronic-marketing rules apply, assess opt-in/soft-opt-in conditions, business-recipient distinctions and opt-out rather than importing US email assumptions.
Email, SMS, calls, and audience acquisition
For SMS, messaging apps, automated calls and prerecorded/synthetic voices assess applicable consent, identification, time-of-day, do-not-contact and revocation requirements.
Email, SMS, calls, and audience acquisition
Test unsubscribe/suppression through CRM, ESP, SMS provider, ad audiences, imported lists and agencies; reimports must not silently resubscribe excluded people.
Email, SMS, calls, and audience acquisition
Review purchased/enriched lists, scraped addresses, partner sharing and lead forms for provenance, notice, permission and vendor claims.
Email, SMS, calls, and audience acquisition
Preserve permission scope, wording, version, source, time and withdrawal evidence as needed, while limiting unnecessary personal data retention.
Review accepted API/platform terms for storage, caching, redistribution, derived products, training, scraping, branding, rate limits and prohibited uses; record service-specific variations.
Check API fallback, proxy, aggregator and reseller chains; permission from one intermediary does not automatically cover the underlying provider's conditions.
Compare app-store listing, in-app purchasing, external-payment links, subscription management and required policy/contact pages with current applicable platform rules.
Review marketplace seller/trader verification, listing information, unsafe/illegal goods handling and allocation of buyer remedies for the actual operator role.
Inspect data portability, account suspension, termination, migration and export restrictions before depending on provider continuity or promising customer exit rights.
Check account sharing, seat reassignment, subcontracting, white-label, client deliverables and agency/reseller rights against actual usage.
Map SLA, support hours, response/remedy, uptime, backup, recovery and deletion commitments to implemented operations and evidence.
Verify security questionnaires, badges and assurance claims match the audited entity, system, period and exceptions; SOC 2 is an attestation report, not a universal product certification.
Review indemnities, insurance, audit rights, breach-notification, data-residency and subcontractor commitments for conflicting duties or missing operational ownership.
Test contract renewal, price changes, service deprecation, customer notice and termination workflows using synthetic timelines; don't rely on a spreadsheet without an accountable action process.
Identify public-sector, procurement, accessibility, localization and recordkeeping requirements that arise from actual customers/contracts; cross-link the responsible specialist audit.
Review product shutdown, acquisition and migration for surviving customer rights, prepaid balances, data return, license/source commitments and notice obligations.
Inventory model weights, tokenizers, adapters, embeddings, training/fine-tuning/evaluation data and retrieval corpora separately; each can have different rights and restrictions.
Check the exact model/version/hosting route for commercial use, deployment, redistribution, use restrictions, attribution and downstream pass-through terms.
Verify rights for collection, copying, retrieval, training, fine-tuning and output reuse separately; lawful access or a display license does not automatically authorize every operation.
Review scraping, website/database terms, machine-readable reservations and applicable text/data-mining exceptions in context; robots.txt alone does not resolve copyright or contract questions.
Check employee/customer/user uploads for authority, confidentiality and personal data before provider submission, logging, evaluation or training.
Match vendor promises on ownership, training, retention, human review, indemnities and geography to the actual plan, endpoint, fallback model and settings.
Distinguish contractual output-use permission from statutory copyrightability, exclusivity, non-infringement and third-party rights; do not promise rights that cannot be established.

Review generated text/code/images/audio for source reproduction, recognizable characters, brands, personal likeness and sensitive content before publication; automated similarity checks are evidence aids, not clearance decisions.
Preserve relevant human authorship, selection/editing and provenance evidence for rights claims or registration where needed without assuming prompts alone establish authorship.
Inspect retrieval citations, snippets, cached copies and exports for license/attribution, update and removal constraints; citation does not itself authorize the reproduced content.
Check synthetic presenters, voice clones, deepfakes and impersonation for actual permissions, context, disclosure and misleading-use concerns.

Determine applicable AI-system role and risk/transparency duties by activity; verify current official text, amendments, transition provisions and dates instead of one generic “AI Act compliant” label.
Where required, test AI interaction notices, synthetic-content markings and disclosures in the actual displayed/downloaded format, including API and white-label outputs.
Check model changes, distillation, merges, quantization and fine-tuning for continuing license and data restrictions; a technical transformation does not automatically remove obligations.
Review provider termination, model withdrawal and deletion requests for retained prompts, datasets, embeddings, fine-tunes and artifacts; record technical limits and applicable duties honestly.
Keep documented human review/escalation for legal, medical, employment, credit or other consequential AI uses; a disclaimer alone does not settle sector or decision-making obligations.
For health services classify parties/data/activities under applicable health rules, including HIPAA where relevant; health-related content alone does not prove covered-entity status.
Where a BAA or other regulated-data agreement is needed, verify each actual service/feature/provider is covered before data submission, including AI, logs and support.
For payments/financial services identify merchant, processor, marketplace, custodian or advisory roles and applicable specialist review; using a payment gateway does not settle every duty.
For payment-card obligations determine actual data handling and contractual scope; an integration mode or questionnaire alone is not a universal PCI compliance conclusion.
For education/children evaluate student-record, school/vendor, parental, exam and accessibility duties from actual relationships and countries.
For employment/recruiting review candidate data, background checks, monitoring, automated selection, bias/discrimination and required notices or assessments.
For accessibility obligations identify applicable law/contract, covered service, standard/version, exemptions and statement/feedback requirements; cross-link actual accessibility test evidence.
For advertising in regulated sectors review prohibited claims, required qualifications/disclosures, approval and audience restrictions for the actual offer.
For games, virtual items, loot boxes, gambling-like features and age ratings obtain market-specific classification and platform decisions; monetization labels do not settle the issue.
For connected devices, digital products and downloadable software examine product-safety, security-update, vulnerability-disclosure, support-period and lifecycle requirements where applicable.
For public-sector/procurement customers identify accessibility, records, hosting, localization, audit and supplier-flow-down obligations in executed terms.
For SOC 2, ISO or other assurance commitments verify entity, service, scope, period, report/certificate status and permitted claims; distinguish attestation, certification and contractual controls.
Determine applicable export/sanctions/import restrictions from software, encryption, technology, destination, parties, users and activity; choose a documented specialist review when needed.
Assess region restrictions, reseller distribution and remote access against both license territory and applicable trade rules; a billing-country dropdown is not complete enforcement evidence.
Check local entity, tax/invoice, consumer, language and marketing requirements when adding countries; do not assume translated terms alone localize the service.
Review acquisitions, entity changes, restructuring and asset sales for assignment/change-of-control consent, IP title, user notice and data-transfer issues.
During investment/client due diligence reconcile claims of ownership and “all licenses cleared” with the actual inventory, exceptions and signed contributor grants.

Review patent-sensitive features, inventions, confidentiality and open-source patent clauses where risk justifies it; trademark searches and dependency scans do not provide patent freedom-to-operate clearance.
Maintain trade-secret/confidential-information controls for source, prompts, datasets, customer documents and partner roadmaps; publication or provider use can conflict with obligations.
Distinguish allegations, rights requests, contractual disputes, regulator inquiries and litigation holds; route to the right owner and avoid destructive evidence cleanup.
Test preservation instructions alongside retention/deletion schedules so holds are authorized, scoped, reviewable and released when appropriate.
For product shutdown or vendor exit plan surviving license offers, source delivery, customer exports, prepaid remedies, public notices and retained records.
Check translated agreements, multiple governing documents and territorial overrides for conflicts; record which language/version controls and obtain enforceability interpretation as needed.
Reassess specialist scope when features, roles, countries, audiences or provider chains change; record unresolved obligations before enabling the changed activity.
