Test access immediately before/at/after trial, period, grace, credit, invite, and manual-override expiry; missing callbacks do not indefinitely preserve access.
Verify entitlement-service/provider outage policy is explicit for reads, writes, and expensive work; fail-open/fail-closed choices match consequence and approved risk.
Check partial propagation, conflicting caches, unavailable primary database, and stale replica; user feedback reflects actual access state rather than silently inconsistent clients.
Test pre-signed downloads, shared links, streaming sessions, device/offline licenses, and persistent sockets for their documented revocation/expiry limits where supported.
Revalidate queued/in-flight work after role, subscription, quota, or ownership changes according to policy; cancellation/compensation handles work already externally committed.
Test invitation, assignment, reassignment, removal, inactive users, concurrent assignment, and seat reduction against supported seat/license rules.
Check last-owner departure, billing-admin replacement, account merge, organization transfer/split, and domain-managed membership only where supported.
Verify multiple workspaces/organizations do not accidentally share private paid allowances or evade user/account-scoped limits through switching.
For device/concurrent-use licenses, test activation, deactivation, device replacement/loss, offline period, clock change, and concurrent sessions within the supported policy.
Test upgrade grant with failed local write, delayed event, failed payment, and retry; reconcile paid-but-no-access and access-without-required-payment.
Test downgrade/expiry beyond current storage/seats/usage; preserve, restrict, migrate, or delete only according to documented policy with appropriate notices.
Verify partial refund, full refund, dispute, charge reversal, and dispute win affect only the intended products/periods/beneficiaries under policy.
Test reinstatement after payment recovery, dispute resolution, manual correction, and erroneous revocation; avoid granting another reset or bonus unless intended.
Check complimentary/support/test accounts and employee access have clear production eligibility, scope, cost controls, owner, expiry, and audit history.
Verify gift/transfer/resale/bundle/sponsored access where offered, including redemption/revocation and payer-versus-recipient refund consequences.
Reconcile entitlement state against authoritative current financial/contract state on a risk-appropriate schedule and after missed events/incidents.
Detect stale grants/revocations, dangling licenses, missing effective dates, and orphaned entitlement sources; repairs are scoped, idempotent, and auditable.
Provide authorized support an explanation of why access is allowed/denied and the relevant effective times without exposing unnecessary financial or other-tenant data.
Require authorization, reason, scope, expiry, and audit evidence for manual access overrides; later reconciliation follows explicit precedence rather than unpredictably undoing or extending them.
Verify restore/migration/rollback does not resurrect revoked rights, lose paid grants, forget manual overrides, or re-enable retired entitlements without reconciliation.
Ensure denied users get truthful next steps distinguishing permission, plan, payment, quota, and temporary state; an upsell is not shown when purchase cannot fix the denial.
Test end-to-end allowed/denied operations for every critical paid capability and meaningful transition, recording provider/internal/access state and actual persisted effects.
Monitor entitlement drift and support recurrence with accountable alerts, repair procedures, and focused verification; do not declare alignment merely because one dashboard is green.
Define billable unit, measurement source, precision, aggregation, rounding, period/timezone, minimums, included usage, overage, and attribution to payer/tenant/product.
Specify when work is reserved, consumed, billed, released, refunded, or corrected; distinguish requested, accepted, completed, partially successful, and failed work.
Define balance categories, currency/product units, purchased/promotional origin, expiry, refund eligibility, transferability, and consumption priority.
Record immutable or appropriately auditable ledger movements with operation identity, source, amount/unit, effective time, reason, actor, and reversal reference.
Verify displayed and available balance reconcile with grants, consumption, reservations, expiry, corrections, and reversals; a cached total is not the only evidence.
Use exact supported unit/money precision and boundary rules; prevent accidental fractional truncation, negative quantities, overflow, and currency/unit confusion.
Bind usage/balance operations to trusted customer/tenant ownership and permitted product; reject client-supplied price multipliers or another account's ledger IDs.
Define authoritative source and repair policy when provider metering, internal events, and completed work disagree; retain versioned definitions for past billing periods.
Test zero, near, exact, and above available balance/quota, including simultaneous requests across replicas; spending/reservation follows the approved overspend policy.
Check reservation timeout, worker crash, late worker, retry, cancel, and abandoned sessions; reserved value is neither leaked forever nor released while the committed effect is still possible.
Test failure before provider effect, timeout with unknown effect, partial success, and success followed by local write failure; reconcile before refunding or repeating work.
Verify repeated requests, duplicated usage events, webhook replay, and concurrent finalization apply one intended debit/grant/correction.
Check failed-request, retry, moderation/refusal, empty-output, canceled-job, and provider-error charging against the declared rule rather than an assumed universal free/fair policy.
Handle correction/refund after reservation expiry or account closure without creating duplicate value, untracked negative balance, or a new unrelated grant.
Test late/out-of-order usage and effective event time versus receipt time across reset, renewal, plan change, and invoice finalization boundaries.
Verify backlog processing rechecks current entitlement/budget when required and attributes usage to the intended period/policy instead of whichever price is current at retry.
Test included monthly/annual grants, rollover, caps, resets, carryover, and unused-value treatment as offered; period transition does not grant twice.
Check upgrade/downgrade/trial/cancellation effects on included balances, prior purchases, and pending reservations with approved examples.
Verify purchased top-up is granted only after the required authoritative payment state; failed/pending/duplicate purchases do not create spendable value incorrectly.
Test partial/full top-up refund and dispute after some value has been consumed; resulting balance/access and recoverable value follow explicit policy.
Check promotional/referral/support grants for eligibility, amount caps, redemption limits, expiry, attribution, and audit evidence.
Test expiry before/at/after cutoff, timezone changes, oldest/earliest-expiring consumption order, held reservations, and late adjustments where supported.
Verify automated top-up threshold, maximum amount/frequency, affirmative setup, duplicate prevention, failed charge, cancellation, and notification as applicable.
Check mixed purchased/promotional balances, multiple units, bundle limits, and restricted credits cannot be incorrectly exchanged for cash or an ineligible product.
Test transfer/gifting/sharing/pooling only where offered, including concurrent spend, revocation, membership changes, and correct payer attribution.
Verify billing-method update, restore, key rotation, account merge, and tenant switching do not reset spent usage or regenerate consumed promotional value.
Reconcile measured events to billable aggregates, invoice line quantities/rates, provider usage submissions, internal ledger, and finance exports.
Check duplicate provider meter submissions, corrections, delayed acceptance, rejection, and unknown outcome; external idempotency/retention limits are documented.
Test backdated correction after finalized invoice/payment, including approved credit note or next-period adjustment; historical totals are not silently rewritten without trace.
Expose customer-appropriate usage/balance history, units, freshness, reserved amounts, resets, and explanations; unknown or delayed usage is not shown as guaranteed zero.
Restrict support balance changes with reason, source, bounds, expiry/reversal where relevant, and independent review proportionate to value.
Detect ledger invariant violations, unexpected negative balances, missing releases, unexplained grants, stale meters, and invoice mismatches with an accountable repair route.
Reconcile balances and already completed external work after backup restore, migration, replay, and pricing-version changes; purchased value and prior debits are preserved.
Execute a complete synthetic purchase/grant/reserve/consume/fail/correct/expire/refund cycle for supported paths, recording ledger, invoice, provider, and access outcomes.
Define refund eligibility, amount basis, currency, time window, original payment/line, refundable balance, tax/fee treatment, owner, and entitlement consequence.
Separate customer-requested, support-issued, automatic, provider-initiated, partial, and full refunds; each uses an authorized supported workflow.
Verify another tenant/order/payment/customer ID, unauthorized support role, and client-supplied refund amount cannot create or redirect a refund.
Check cumulative partial refunds, simultaneous requests, and the final refundable amount; prevent unintended over-refund across provider and internal channels.
Test zero/negative/above-remaining amounts, currency mismatch, uncaptured authorization, pending method, and ineligible payment type with clear rejection/alternative handling.
Record refund reason, source order/payment/line, actor, approval where required, business identity, requested amount, and current result without unnecessary sensitive data.
Verify customer support cannot bypass refund limits or independently edit authoritative paid/refunded totals without traceable corrective movements.
Clarify whether refund cancels future renewals, removes access, restores credits/stock, or affects a beneficiary; perform only the intended related changes.
Test refund success, pending, failed, canceled/returned where supported, provider rejection, insufficient merchant funds, and delayed final result using approved fixtures.
Handle timeout after provider acceptance by lookup/reconciliation and stable idempotency; retry does not initiate a second refund.
Test crash before/after provider effect, internal ledger update, entitlement change, and response; all accepted work has a durable repair path.
Replay duplicate/concurrent/out-of-order refund events and operator requests; final refunded amount, balance, and access change only once per intended effect.
Verify a requested refund is not presented as completed before the required authoritative status; distinguish merchant action from customer bank posting where relevant.
Test full versus line/quantity/partial-period refunds against discounts, tax, shipping/fees, consumed credits, proration, and earlier adjustments using approved examples.
Check multiple payment attempts, split tender, installment/deferred methods, and multiple currencies only where supported; refund maps to the correct original transaction.
Verify receipt/credit-note/customer notice, invoice status, finance export, and provider totals reflect final state and effective time; failure notices remain actionable.
Check account deletion, payer-versus-beneficiary, removed member, and legacy/migrated order do not make a valid correction impossible or disclose another party's data.
Ensure refund reversal/failure restores any previously provisional internal change only according to explicit policy, not by blindly regranting access or duplicating value.
Define dispute/chargeback/inquiry, response deadline, accountable owner, evidence source, privacy controls, and escalation for supported payment methods.
Test dispute opened, updated, won, lost, withdrawn/reversed where supported, and delayed notice; provider/internal financial/access states remain distinguishable.
Verify provisional versus final funds movement, dispute fees, reserves, and settlement adjustments are represented in reconciliation rather than treated as ordinary sales/refunds.
Check dispute after partial/full refund, refund during dispute, duplicate dispute events, and later reversal; avoid returning the same value through two channels.
Test authorized access suspension, retention, and reinstatement under dispute policy; do not equate every inquiry or provisional state with final fraud/loss.
Verify evidence submission, deadline tracking, file access, correct case binding, and review accountability; automated tools do not fabricate documents or customer consent.
For bank returns/payment reversals, test delayed failure after provisional success, spent credits/fulfilled goods, negative balance policy, and customer remediation.
For canceled/expired authorizations, distinguish releasing a hold from refunding captured money; customer/internal descriptions match the actual operation.
Reconcile refunds, credit notes, ledger reversals, dispute adjustments, fees, and payouts to original payments/orders and approved reports.
Monitor pending/stuck refunds, approaching dispute deadlines, failed notifications, cumulative anomalies, and unresolved entitlement drift with tested alert receipt.
Provide customers/support a safe status/history with amount/currency, action date, current state, and next step without guaranteeing unsupported bank timing.
Reconcile restore/replay/migration against provider refund/dispute history before allowing another correction or reinstating access.
Verify risk controls for repeated refund/cancel/promotion loops proportionately, with legitimate correction and appeal paths and documented false-positive handling.
Execute complete sandbox refund/failure/dispute/reinstatement scenarios where supported and replay relevant events; retain final provider/internal/balance/access evidence.
Define quote/order/invoice/receipt/credit-note relationships, issuer, customer/payer, currency, period, due date, finalization, status transitions, and authoritative identifiers.
Verify applicable invoice fields, numbering, addresses, tax identifiers, purchase orders, language, delivery, and retention against reviewer-approved requirements.
Check draft, finalized, open, paid, partially paid, voided, uncollectible, credited, and overdue states only where supported; amount due and access consequences follow explicit policy.
Test invoice creation/finalization retries and concurrent billing jobs; one intended period/order is not invoiced twice.
Verify line descriptions, service periods, quantities, rates, discounts, proration, taxes, shipping/fees, credits, and final total against approved exact calculations.
Check customer address/tax/business identity changes before/after finalization; historic documents are corrected through the approved traceable workflow.
Test invoice download/portal/email access for correct payer/tenant/role, expired links, removed membership, and sensitive fields; direct references do not expose another customer's records.
Verify manual/out-of-band payment recording is authorized and evidence-backed; marking an invoice paid does not independently prove cash receipt.
Check partial payment, overpayment, underpayment, duplicate transfer, wrong reference, unallocated payment, and currency mismatch only where offered, with an accountable resolution route.
Test invoice terms/collections, due-date changes, write-offs, void/reissue, and credit notes under approved policy with auditability and appropriate access consequences.
Link each served market/product/customer category to approved tax/VAT responsibility, classification, configuration, exemption evidence, and reviewer/date under shared module 11.
Verify representative destination, evidence-of-location, business/consumer, valid/invalid/missing tax identity, and exemption flows as actually supported.
Check tax calculation across inclusive/exclusive price, discount, shipping/fees, proration, refunds, credits, and supported currency rounding using approved examples.
Test tax service unavailable, invalid address, conflicting evidence, rate/configuration change, and missing classification; documented policy prevents silent unintended collection.
Verify merchant-of-record, marketplace/platform, processor, and seller responsibilities are not confused in customer documents and internal reports.
Check effective-date changes and historical corrections preserve required evidence and do not silently recalculate previously finalized documents under today's settings.
Verify invoice/receipt/credit-note totals and required fields remain consistent in UI, PDF, email, exports, supported locales, and finance tools.
Define handling of required tax/customer records after account deletion and after retention/hold expiry with approved access controls rather than blanket immediate deletion or indefinite retention.
Define reconciliation sources, matching keys, period/cutoff/timezone, frequency, tolerances with rationale, owner, exceptions, and completion evidence.
Reconcile orders/invoices to payment attempts, authorizations/captures, refunds, credits, disputes, fees, provider balance movements, payouts, and settlement as applicable.
Distinguish gross sales, collected amounts, fees, adjustments, net payout, outstanding receivable, prepaid product value, and accounting classifications approved by finance.
Keep currencies separate and use approved conversion rates/date/source for consolidated reports; displayed revenue is not inferred by adding unlike currencies.
Test delayed settlement, payout failure/reversal, reserve/hold, bank mismatch, negative provider balance, and account restriction where supported.
Verify timing/cutoff for late usage, refunds, delayed callbacks, disputes, credits, annual prepayment, and month/year-end; reports disclose event versus settlement periods.
Detect missing/duplicated provider objects, orphan payments, paid-without-access, access-without-required-payment, refunded-but-available credits, and unresolved pending states.
Check exports cover intended scope, full pagination, stable IDs, exact amounts/units, timezone, status, lineage, duplicates, and version changes; spreadsheet safety goes to security review.
Verify import into finance/reporting tools is idempotent or has explicit duplicate controls, rejected-row handling, correction, and traceability to the original record.
Restrict financial exports, reconciliation edits, bank/payout destination changes, and manual journal/correction operations according to approved roles and review policy.
Confirm reconciliation repairs do not create additional charges/refunds/grants merely to force a report match; financial movements retain original and corrective history.
Maintain an exception register with amount/currency, age, scope, evidence, owner, deadline, proposed action, and independent review proportionate to risk.
Verify restored/migrated/backfilled data reconciles with external financial history before reopening billing, refunds, payouts, and entitlement updates.
Test missing/stale reconciliation and anomalous variance alerts through actual receipt and support/finance investigation without exposing sensitive customer data.
Retain approved evidence/report versions and acceptance of unresolved differences; unknown financial data is not silently represented as zero or as a closed balance.
Have qualified project finance/tax owners review applicable calculations, document configuration, reconciliation coverage, and outstanding policy questions before declaring those areas verified.
Name primary/backup owners and response expectations for billing, failed payment, entitlement drift, refunds, disputes, reconciliation, and provider/account outage.
Correlate provider request/event/object IDs with internal customer/order/ledger/entitlement records and release/configuration without logging secrets or unnecessary payment data.
Monitor callback age/failures, stale lifecycle work, duplicate-effect attempts, unknown payments, refund/dispute deadlines, ledger drift, and paid-access failures with tested alert receipt.
Provide scoped support views and authorized actions for status, repair, refund, cancellation, access correction, and payment recovery; avoid routine untracked database edits.
Require reason, actor, permissions, effective time, bounds, and audit evidence for manual financial/access changes; review high-impact operations proportionately.
Maintain runbooks for duplicate charge, paid-no-access, unexpected renewal, missed expiry, stuck refund, dispute, provider outage, leaked key, and reconciliation failure.
Verify scoped/global stops for new purchases, renewals where controllable, refunds, usage, grants, and replay; distinguish stopping local work from provider-side scheduled effects.
During provider outage, preserve pending work, explain unknown status, bound retries/cost, and avoid silently routing to another provider in a way that duplicates financial effects.
Reopen after containment only after checking external state, budgets, permissions, backlog, financial/access invariants, and rate-limited replay.
Test required billing/consent/renewal/trial/cancellation/recovery notices with correct recipient, locale, effective time, state, approved content, delivery-failure visibility, and retention.
Verify sandbox/live separation and cutover of keys, prices, customers, endpoints, signatures, event subscriptions, portals, schedules, and tax settings in the actual deployment.
Test SDK/API/event/schema/configuration upgrades and mixed-version deployment with representative historical objects, pending work, stale clients, and rollback limits.
Rehearse restore after provider actions continued beyond the database snapshot; reconcile charges, refunds, grants, spent credits, cancellations, and revoked rights before enabling work.
Check old/new deployments, schedulers, webhook handlers, providers, and store channels do not independently renew, refund, replay, or grant the same customer value.
For provider/account migration, inventory portable versus nonportable customer/payment/subscription/mandate/tax/consent data and obtain approved transfer/recollection procedures.
Verify migration preserves billing anchors, remaining paid time, balances, discounts, arrears, cancellation, invoice/refund lineage, and customer communication without duplicate charges.
Define rollback/forward recovery for irreversible charges, external cancellations, migrated mandates, and issued documents; a code rollback is not assumed to reverse money movement.
Retire old endpoints/keys/jobs/products/accounts only after delayed-event, refund/dispute, record retention, export, payout, and residual-billing obligations are addressed.
Confirm organization-controlled provider/bank/admin ownership, backup access, renewal/payment contacts, and lost-device/staff-departure recovery through shared modules 01 and 10.
Record go/hold/limited-rollout decision with verified critical lifecycles, unresolved gaps, accepted-risk expiry, accountable owner, and focused post-release observation.
For one-time digital goods, test payment-to-license/download, delivery failure, expiry/re-download, guest recovery, duplicate purchase, refund/revocation, and ownership transfer if offered.
For physical commerce, test stock/price changes, split fulfillment, shipping tax/fees, partial cancellation/return/refund, and reconciliation of payment versus actual fulfillment.
For bookings/services, test deposit, remaining balance, hold/authorization, no-show, reschedule, cancellation deadline/timezone, provider absence, and partial delivery against policy.
For usage-based/AI products, test delayed/corrected usage, reservation leaks, failed provider work, changing unit costs, hard budgets, expensive fallback, and invoice finalization boundaries.
For B2B/invoiced sales, test payer-versus-user, negotiated contracts, seats, purchase orders, payment terms, manual collection evidence, credit notes, and approved access/grace policy.

For app stores/platform billing, test purchase verification, account binding, restore purchase, renewals, platform refund/revocation, grace, cross-device access, and web/store overlap using current platform guidance.

For multiple providers, test routed attempt identity, unknown outcome, fallback, token/account mapping, subscription ownership, fees/currency, reconciliation, and provider-specific dispute/refund handling.

For marketplaces/connected accounts, verify seller onboarding/eligibility, platform-versus-seller charges, fees, transfers, payouts, refunds, reserves, negative balance, and responsible merchant under approved contracts.

For marketplace refunds/disputes, test transfer reversal, seller already paid/unavailable, partial platform fee return, cross-account scope, and recovery of unresolved liability without assuming funds are recoverable.
For wallets/stored value/gift cards, obtain qualified applicability review and test issuance, redemption, transfer, expiry, refund, lost access, and ledger reconciliation within the approved model.

For installments/deferred payment, test lender/provider acceptance, provisional fulfillment, partial payments, return/cancellation, late reversal, and customer/support ownership without assuming card behavior.
For donations/sponsorships, test one-time/recurring designation, restricted purpose, donor-versus-beneficiary, receipts, cancellation, refunds, and approved tax-claim wording.
For bundles/memberships/multiple products, test overlapping grants, mixed intervals, add-on dependencies, per-item refund, seat assignment, and cancellation that leaves other purchased rights intact.
For family/team/sponsored access, test payer departure, beneficiary removal, shared allowances, role changes, refunds, privacy boundaries, and continued/revoked access under policy.
For high-value/manual agreements, test approval, quote expiry, signed-term/version evidence, staged collection, provisioning, amendments, and finance/support handoff as scoped.
For multiple markets/currencies, test supported method combinations, settlement/FX display, localized terms, approved tax/documents, notice timing, and clear rejection of unsupported combinations.
For each chosen model, execute at least one supported success, meaningful rejection/failure, delayed/duplicate outcome, and correction/recovery with linked final-state evidence.
Separate transaction settlement from product fulfillment/access and from accounting classification; each material boundary has an accountable source of truth and reconciliation.
Add scenarios after incidents, policy/provider changes, new markets/payment methods, pricing/model changes, or significant scale; retain failed/near-miss lessons with owners.
Close accepted actions only after focused verification of financial, ledger, entitlement, effective-time, and notice results; preserve explicit remaining gaps and next review triggers.

headings.text: Reliability and data integrity audit library
Jobs, events, retries, schedules, and dependencies
Query completeness, storage, caches, time, and representation
Backups, restoration, failover, and disaster recovery
Migrations, deployments, repairs, and data lifecycle

values: Identify authoritative records, invariants, and multi-step writes. Use supported transactions/constraints, or an explicit recoverable workflow when one transaction cannot cover all systems.
Test simultaneous creates, edits, deletions, quota reservations, and job claims. Prevent lost updates, duplicate records, and operations against deleted or unauthorized resources.

Define idempotency keys and persistence lifetime for repeated API operations, jobs, and provider events. Verify that deduplication and business updates cannot leave an unprocessed event marked complete.
Check queue delivery guarantees, durable acknowledgment, retry bounds/backoff, dead-letter handling, and controlled replay. Jobs must survive the intended process/container restart behavior.
Recover expired leases, stuck states, orphaned files, missing objects, and partially completed external operations. Avoid cleanup that can delete valid active work.
Treat caches as rebuildable unless intentionally authoritative; document persistence and eviction assumptions for quota counters, sessions, and work coordination.

Double-click submit, retry after a timeout, and send equivalent concurrent create requests. Verify one intended order/booking/business record and one external side effect using persisted results, not only button state or HTTP status. Separate intentionally distinct submissions from retries of the same operation.

Seed more records than the configured API/page cap and traverse lists, search, exports, and background processing. Verify stable pagination, complete coverage, and no silent truncation or duplicated/skipped records. Supabase documents a default maximum of 1,000 returned rows; inspect the deployed setting and use pagination rather than assuming one response is complete. [Supabase fetch documentation](https://supabase.com/docs/reference/javascript/v1/select)

Measure frequent filters, joins, sorts, and tenant-scoped queries on realistic data volumes/distributions. Inspect query plans and relevant indexes, then verify latency against the project's target; a few dozen fixtures or an index on every column is not useful performance evidence.
Bound downstream calls and use retries only when safe. Handle partial success, ambiguous provider results, timeout, disconnect, rate limits, and dependency outages without retry storms.
Verify graceful shutdown, in-flight work handling, cancellation, and restart recovery. Reconcile work interrupted during deployment or host failure.
Check disk-full, resource exhaustion, storage unavailability, corrupt/invalid data, and stale configuration behavior. Errors should preserve useful state and remain observable.
Validate migration safety, compatibility between old/new application versions, and backup prerequisites. Code rollback and data rollback are different operations.
Define RPO and RTO for each important dataset and service. Choose backup frequency and point-in-time recovery to meet them; daily backups are only sufficient when the tolerated data loss permits it.

Inventory database data, uploads, objects, persistent volumes, configuration, encryption keys, and other non-rebuildable state. A VPS snapshot or control-plane backup alone may omit application state.

Keep protected off-site copies with appropriate encryption, retention, and access separation. Consider immutable/versioned copies where the risk warrants them; avoid a production credential able to erase every recovery copy.
Verify backup scheduling, freshness, completeness, and failure alerts. A successful job or existing file is not proof of recoverability.

Verify the actual provider plan's backup availability, retention, and restore access. If managed recovery does not meet RPO/RTO, schedule and monitor an independent export with protected off-site retention. For Supabase Free projects, follow the documented regular export guidance rather than assuming usable managed backups; database backups do not include Storage objects. [Supabase backup documentation](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/platform/backups)
Restore into an isolated fresh environment, inspect representative records/files, and run a representative application workflow. Measure actual loss window and restore time against RPO/RTO.
Verify encryption-key and credential recovery through a secure external store. Align backup access, expiry, and restored deleted data with the retention/deletion process.
Document recovery sequencing, data authority, and reconciliation of events that arrive while a service is unavailable. Test who can perform recovery if the normal operator is absent.

Distinguish instants, local dates, and recurring wall-clock schedules. Preserve the timezone needed for future scheduling and test daylight-saving gaps/repeated hours, timezone changes, and user-visible reminder times.

For PostgreSQL, store instants in `timestamptz` (or an equivalent instant-aware type in another database) and retain each user's IANA timezone separately for local reminders. An instant column does not preserve the user's original timezone; date-only values and future local schedules need their own appropriate representation.

Where accidental-deletion recovery is promised, test soft delete or equivalent recovery, related records, uniqueness, retention expiry, and authorized restoration. Recovered data must preserve tenant boundaries and applicable deletion commitments.

Rehearse forward migrations and the supported rollback or fail-forward path on representative data. Measure table-lock duration and concurrent traffic impact; use staged/backward-compatible changes where required by availability targets.

Record a reversal/recovery plan for every schema migration. For reversible changes, keep reverse SQL or the migration tool's equivalent and run both directions on an isolated, sanitized production-shaped copy. For destructive/irreversible changes, document lost information and rehearse restore or fail-forward recovery; invented reverse SQL cannot recover dropped data. Record integrity checks and the old/new application's compatibility after recovery.
Verify distributed scheduled jobs have coordinated ownership or equivalent deduplication so adding a replica does not duplicate business effects. Test daylight-saving changes and missed-run recovery.

Maintain a disaster recovery plan covering dependency order, regional outage, and absence of the normal operator. Rehearse at the agreed risk-based interval (for example annually) and after material changes; add another region only when recovery/availability commitments require it.
Verify correctness through client, API, database, queue, provider and generated artifact; a successful intermediate step does not establish completed business work.
Repeat key cases across replicas, workers, old/new versions, tenants, roles and plan limits rather than assuming one process represents the deployed topology.
Exercise the difference between graceful stop, hard process kill, host loss and persistent-volume loss in the permitted isolated scope; record which guarantees each test supports.
Inspect ambiguous results after timeout/cancel/disconnect; delayed work or callbacks must not silently override a valid newer outcome.
Test recovery when cache, replica, index or checkpoint is ahead of or behind restored authority; incompatible copies must not be treated as truth.
Verify negative/failure responses leave explicit recoverable state; failure must not mean “nothing happened” when a side effect already completed.
Reconcile old, delayed and replayed operations after cancellation, deletion, migration and restore using current lifecycle/authorization rules.
Check observability reflects durable outcomes, invariant violations, backlog age and missing recovery coverage rather than only process uptime or successful HTTP responses.
Validate recovery without the original operator, original host or undocumented local files; required access and instructions must exist outside the failed component.
Check concurrent recovery/cleanup/reconciliation cannot duplicate effects or destroy valid slow work; repairs follow the same correctness rules as normal operations.
Record workload, fault boundaries, measured outcomes and limitations; do not turn unexecuted recovery code or a mocked outage into a claim of proven disaster recovery.
Reassess targets and evidence after changing providers, plans, persistence, topology, data volume, schema, keys or important background work.
Identify authority for each business fact and reconcile conflicting database, provider, cache and client copies; define who wins during recovery.
Express uniqueness, referential, balance, capacity, ownership and state-transition conditions with exact scope and permitted intermediate states.
Enforce applicable invariants at the authoritative boundary; application prechecks alone must not admit a concurrent violation.
Review null, missing, empty, soft-deleted and case-folded values against intended uniqueness and relationship rules using actual database semantics.
Check composite tenant/parent relationships so cross-tenant identifiers cannot create valid-looking but incorrectly owned records.
Validate cascade, restrict, set-null and manual cleanup behavior through deletion and rollback; optional references must not become unintended orphans.
Inspect direct SQL, imports, admin tools, jobs and repair scripts for bypasses of invariants enforced only in one API path.
Verify generated identifiers, sequence gaps, external IDs and natural keys are interpreted correctly; do not use gap-free sequence assumptions as an integrity oracle without a requirement.
Identify the exact atomic boundary of multi-record writes and whether all operations actually share the intended connection/session/transaction.
Inject failures after each significant write and verify rollback or documented recoverable intermediate state, including exceptions swallowed by helpers.
Test read-check-write races under the configured isolation level rather than assuming a transaction automatically prevents oversell or duplicate creation.
Exercise nonrepeatable reads, changing result sets and write-skew risks where the operation depends on multiple reads or rows.
Test serialization failures and deadlocks; retry the correct whole unit with bounded attempts and without repeating an unprotected external effect.
Verify failed transactions are correctly rolled back/reset before pooled connections are reused; subsequent requests do not inherit broken or stale session state.
Review nested transaction/savepoint behavior in the actual driver/ORM, including partial error recovery and callbacks executed before durable commit.
Set and test relevant lock/statement/transaction deadlines; request timeout must not leave unbounded work or indefinite locks unnoticed.
Check long transactions, idle-in-transaction sessions and large batches for contention, retained history and recovery impact at realistic volume.
Inspect whether DDL, external calls, sequence operations or nontransactional tables have different rollback semantics from ordinary row updates.
Run simultaneous equivalent creates behind a controlled barrier and verify the number of committed records and side effects, not just returned statuses.
Race independent intentional creates with retries of one operation; deduplication must not merge legitimately distinct user actions.
Race updates from stale clients; prevent unintended lost updates through a suitable conflict/atomic-update strategy and explain conflicts to callers.
Race update/delete, restore/delete and child-create/parent-delete; verify the chosen lifecycle and ownership rules.
Test increments/decrements, balances, counters and inventory under contention; read-modify-write must not lose or manufacture value.
Race quota check/reservation/commit/release, including expiry and failure, and verify no double allocation or permanently leaked reservation.
Race uniqueness checks across tabs, replicas, API versions and background jobs; inspect final state after all attempts settle.
Verify optimistic concurrency tokens/version checks cover all mutable fields and channels; blind upserts must not undo newer edits.
Test collaborative/offline merge policies where present; conflicts, tombstones and stale synchronization do not silently resurrect deleted data.
Verify bulk actions and partially failed batches have explicit all-or-nothing or per-item outcomes that can be retried safely.
Verify job/leader/resource claims are atomic and ownership is scoped correctly; a read followed by an unguarded write is not an exclusive claim.
Test lease expiry while the old holder is paused; a resumed stale holder must not corrupt state after another worker takes ownership.
Where stale owners can write, verify fencing/version checks or an equivalent authority-side rejection rather than relying only on a lock's expiry.
Verify renewal, release and cancellation compare ownership tokens; an expired worker must not release another worker's new lock.
Test clock assumptions, process pauses, network delays and lock-store restart for ownership algorithms; record the actual guarantee boundary.
Review lock order and contention across resources; deadlock recovery does not leave partial allocations or retry indefinitely.
Test multiple replicas during scheduled/maintenance work and leader handover; exclusive ownership survives deployment and interrupted renewal as designed.
Verify stale/stuck-state repair distinguishes active slow work from abandoned work and does not steal or delete valid processing prematurely.
Define permitted read staleness and read-your-writes behavior; replica reads after a successful update do not falsely report failure or invite duplicate work.
Test replica lag, unavailable replicas and fallback routing against correctness as well as latency; critical decisions do not silently use stale authority.
Record replication/write acknowledgment settings and determine what acknowledged work can be lost under the agreed failover scenario.
In an isolated exercise, verify promotion/failover behavior and reconcile divergent or ambiguous writes before normal service resumes.
Test old-primary fencing and clients with stale routing; topology changes must not allow unsupported concurrent authoritative writers.
Verify connection pools, proxies and long-lived clients reconnect to the correct role after failover; read-only/role errors are handled explicitly.
Where multi-region/multi-writer operation exists, test conflicts and convergence under partition/reconnection; document availability versus consistency choices per operation.
Reconcile CDC/search/cache consumers after source failover or history discontinuity; checkpoints must not silently skip or reapply incompatible changes.
Record actual fsync/journal/WAL/write-concern settings and storage persistence; distinguish process crash survival from host/power/volume loss.
Verify a success response follows the required durable boundary; acknowledgments issued before persistence are explicitly part of the loss model.
Interrupt the connection after commit but before response and verify safe lookup/retry of the unknown outcome.
Check database/file writes on ephemeral containers, temporary directories and unmounted volumes; restart/redeploy must not discard intended persistent state.
Test disk-full, write rejection and resource exhaustion in a bounded disposable environment; failed writes do not masquerade as committed success.
Validate audit/history records and financial corrections remain traceable and consistent with business changes; auxiliary logging failure follows an explicit policy.
Verify reads after restart using independent connections and consistency checks rather than an in-memory cache or old ORM identity map.
Check invariants after fault recovery and reconciliation, including related records, provider effects and derived state; one correct main row does not prove the whole operation correct.
Define the logical operation identity, key scope, tenant binding, request fingerprint and retention period; transport event IDs and business operation IDs may serve different purposes.
Retry the same key and request sequentially and concurrently; verify one intended persisted result and allowed external effects.
Reuse a key with a different payload, tenant or operation and verify explicit rejection or documented semantics rather than silent result substitution.
Test timeout after provider success but before local persistence; resolve the ambiguous result through provider lookup/idempotency/reconciliation rather than blind duplication.
Test timeout after local commit but before response; retried callers can retrieve a stable outcome without executing again.
Verify deduplication recording and business-state changes are atomic or recoverably coordinated; an event marked done before work commits must not be lost.
Check pending/failed idempotency records recover after crashes; permanent “in progress” states do not block legitimate completion indefinitely.
Align deduplication expiry with actual provider retries, queue retention, offline clients and manual replay; expired keys must not unexpectedly duplicate old effects.
Test distinct events describing the same business transition and repeated business actions with different transport IDs; define the correct semantic deduplication boundary.
Keep idempotency results durable across restarts, replicas and topology changes; a per-process map or evictable cache must not be assumed sufficient.
Document actual broker delivery, retention, visibility, ordering and acknowledgment semantics for the configured queue/plan.
Crash a consumer before and after business commit and before and after acknowledgment; verify redelivery cannot lose or duplicate the intended effect.
Test producer interruption around send/acknowledgment; ambiguous publication is deduplicated or reconciled downstream.
Where a database update requires event publication, inspect outbox or another recoverable coordination method; publish failure must not strand committed state silently.
Test outbox insertion, publishing, marking and cleanup boundaries; publisher retries and concurrent publishers preserve required effects.
Check consumer inbox/checkpoint recording is coupled correctly to business processing; persisted offsets alone do not prove a business update succeeded.
Verify visibility/lease settings fit actual processing, renewal and worst-case pauses; overlapping consumers remain safe if a message becomes visible early.
Test message ordering assumptions per key/partition and across queues; reorder events intentionally and verify version/state-transition handling.
Check broker restart, disconnect, rebalance and partition reassignment; unfinished work and checkpoints recover without unsupported guarantees.
Verify queue retention/expiry and backlog age cannot silently remove important work before processing or recovery; alert against business deadlines.
Classify transient, permanent and ambiguous errors; retry only safe operations with an explicit bounded policy.
Apply a total retry/deadline budget across client, proxy, SDK, worker and provider layers; nested retries must not amplify work without bound.
Check exponential or otherwise suitable backoff, jitter and provider retry guidance; synchronized workers do not repeatedly overload a recovering dependency.
Test poison messages, invalid schema, oversized payloads and unavailable referenced records; one bad item does not permanently block unrelated work.
Verify maximum attempts/age and dead-letter disposition are visible, retained and actionable; silently dropping failed jobs is not successful completion.
Replay dead letters in a controlled sample with ownership, rate, duplicate safeguards and reconciliation; replay-all must not repeat destructive external effects.
Check replay after code/schema/configuration changes; old messages still decode or have an explicit conversion/quarantine path.
Verify operators can identify and recover unknown/stuck operations without clearing deduplication records or mass-resetting valid state blindly.
Keep event correlation, attempt history and outcome evidence through retries while limiting sensitive payload retention.
Test late success after timeout/cancellation and callbacks after local failure; terminal-state handling must not overwrite a newer valid decision.
Bound connection, read, overall request and processing time where appropriate; a single slow dependency cannot hold resources indefinitely.
Test unavailable, slow, malformed, partial and rate-limited provider responses; distinguish response parsing failure from a known business rejection.
Verify cancellation and client disconnect behavior; stopping the caller does not automatically prove external work stopped.
Inspect circuit-breaker/open/recovery behavior where used; half-open probes and retries do not create a recovery surge.
Isolate pools, concurrency and queues where necessary so a failing optional dependency does not exhaust resources for essential work.
Test fallback services for correctness, compatible data/identifiers and duplicate effects; a fallback must not execute a second charge after an unknown primary outcome.
Verify degradation communicates pending/unavailable state and preserves retry/recovery evidence instead of falsely confirming completion.
Test provider credential rotation, certificate/DNS changes, stale endpoints and revoked access as recoverable configuration failures.
Bound backlog drain and replay after outages; resource use, external quotas and live requests remain within agreed limits.
Verify dependency recovery triggers reconciliation of pending/unknown work, not merely a green health check.
Inventory app schedulers, host cron, provider schedules, database jobs and external automation; record owner, purpose and actual execution source.
Run multiple replicas and deployment overlap to verify scheduled business effects have coordinated ownership or equivalent deduplication.
Test missed-run behavior after downtime: skip, catch-up, coalesce or bounded replay matches the business requirement and does not create a storm.
Test overlapping long-running schedules, lease expiry and late prior runs; old work cannot overwrite or duplicate a newer period's result.
Test daylight-saving gaps/repeated hours, timezone changes and local-time recurrence; record how each logical scheduled occurrence is identified.
Verify schedule edits, cancellation and pause take effect for already queued work as intended; stale jobs do not ignore current authorization/state.
Check business-period keys and cutoffs around month/year boundaries, leap days and locale-independent dates.
Verify scheduler state, last-run markers and deduplication survive the intended restart/restore path; restoring old checkpoints must not blindly rerun historical effects.
On graceful shutdown stop new claims, handle in-flight work and release/expire ownership correctly within actual platform termination deadlines.
Hard-kill a worker at representative boundaries in isolation; process-local promises/timers must not be the only record of important work.
Review cross-system workflows for explicit compensation, retry or manual reconciliation when one transaction cannot cover all participants.
Test compensation success, failure and repeated execution; undo must not exceed the original effect or erase evidence of a completed external action.
Verify reconciliation jobs compare authoritative states, identify drift and repair safely with limits, checkpoints and audit evidence.
Race reconciliation/cleanup with normal work and late callbacks; recovery does not delete a valid upload, release a live reservation or reapply an old result.
Define a maximum age for pending/unknown/stuck business states and actionable escalation; permanent limbo is not an acceptable retry strategy.
Validate end-to-end outcomes after restart/replay using independent persisted records, provider receipts and invariant checks; broker metrics alone are insufficient.
Seed above API/server/export page caps and traverse all pages; compare expected IDs and totals, not just nonempty responses.
Use deterministic ordering with adequate tie-breaking; equal timestamps/names must not cause skipped or repeated records.
Insert/update/delete records during traversal and verify the documented snapshot/live-list semantics, including acceptable duplicates or changes if explicitly designed.
Check keyset/offset/cursor boundaries, empty final pages, one-record pages, invalid/expired cursors and changed filters.
Validate tenant, role, soft-delete and status filters on every page, count, export and background batch; a complete result must also be correctly scoped.
Verify joins, one-to-many expansion, deduplication and aggregation don't silently drop parents or inflate totals.
Test null, missing, empty, zero and boundary values in filters/sorts; UI counts and server queries use compatible meaning.
Inspect realistic plans and indexes for frequent filters/joins/sorts; include skew, hot tenants, long history and cold-cache behavior where relevant.
Verify statement/client timeouts, partial responses and failed later pages produce explicit incomplete outcomes rather than successful truncation.
Test bulk processing over more than one chunk with crash/resume; checkpoints do not skip uncommitted items or repeat unsafe effects.
Compare list/search/export totals against a known oracle and declared snapshot; independent differences are investigated, not dismissed as pagination.
Verify provider response caps and deployed project settings; source examples or SDK defaults are not evidence that one response covers all records.
Validate import schema, encoding, required fields, type conversion and row-level errors before committing unintended data.
Test duplicate files/rows, interrupted imports and resumed batches; distinguish repeated uploads from intentionally new revisions.
Define atomic versus partial import semantics and provide recoverable per-row/batch outcomes; invalid rows do not silently disappear.
Check large/streamed exports for complete content, finalization, failure reporting and consistent authorization while running.
Avoid exposing unfinished exports as complete files; checksums/counts/manifests or equivalent verification match the actual delivered artifact.
Verify reports/materialized views/warehouse pipelines maintain declared freshness and recover from missed, repeated and out-of-order changes.
Test CDC snapshot-to-stream handoff, checkpoint recovery and schema evolution where present; no silent gap or double counting at the boundary.
Ensure reconciliation/repair can rebuild derived aggregates and distinguish historical corrections from new business activity.
Map object metadata to actual files, versions and ownership; detect missing objects, orphan metadata and unreferenced uploads safely.
Test upload initiation, partial transfer, completion, metadata commit and response interruption; users are not shown a completed record for an unusable object.
Verify multipart/chunked uploads can resume/cancel and abandoned parts expire safely; cleanup does not remove active uploads.
Check object naming, collision and overwrite/version rules under simultaneous uploads and retries; content must not be assigned to the wrong record.
Validate size, hash/content integrity and format as required after transfer/copy/restore; object existence or HTTP 200 alone does not establish correctness.
Test copy/move/delete and database updates as a cross-system workflow; partial success has reconciliation rather than dangling references.
Inspect object-store consistency and lifecycle/versioning rules for the configured provider; do not generalize one platform's read/list guarantees.
Verify generated thumbnails, renditions, attachments and exports are either backed up or reproducible from retained source/version/tooling.
Check signed-link expiry, storage class/archive retrieval and restored permissions against promised user access and recovery time.
Verify local volumes, mount paths, ownership and permissions survive redeploy/host recovery; writing to an unmounted directory must not silently create a different state store.
Exercise bounded storage exhaustion/unavailability and invalid content; errors preserve recoverable state and expose a usable retry/reconciliation path.
Confirm retention/object lifecycle does not delete files still referenced by active, held or restored records; cleanup uses authority and appropriate safety windows.
Classify each cache as rebuildable or intentionally authoritative; identify quotas, coordination, sessions and reservations that carry more than performance value.
Test restart, eviction, expiry and cold rebuild under the configured persistence policy; important state is not lost under an undocumented cache assumption.
Verify cache keys include the necessary tenant, role, locale, version and query scope; stale/mis-scoped data must not be returned as another user's truth.
Race invalidation with writes/read-through fills; late stale fills must not indefinitely replace newer state.
Check TTL, negative caching and failure caching against permitted staleness; a transient missing record must not remain invisible beyond the target.
Test cache outage and stampede/rebuild behavior; fallback does not overload authority or bypass correctness checks.
Verify search/vector indexes handle updates, deletes, schema/model changes and failed indexing with bounded lag and reconciliation.
Rebuild indexes from authoritative data without silent omissions, wrong versions or cross-tenant mixing; record checkpoints and completeness checks.
Test stale index hits pointing to deleted/unauthorized records and missing fresh hits; final access and business decisions use the appropriate authority.
Coordinate index/cache rebuild after backup restore so future/stale derived entries do not resurrect invalid or deleted data.
Distinguish instants, local dates, durations, timezone-aware recurrences and business periods; use representations fitting each meaning.
Preserve IANA timezone identity where future wall-clock schedules depend on it; an instant or fixed UTC offset alone does not encode the future local rule.
Test daylight-saving skipped/repeated times, timezone edits, travel and changed timezone rules; define how ambiguous/nonexistent times are resolved.
Check UTC/local conversion, offset-bearing API input and serialization round trips across database, worker, browser and export.
Use an appropriate monotonic elapsed-time source for durations where required; wall-clock adjustments must not corrupt timeout/lease assumptions.
Test clock skew and time synchronization loss within a bounded environment; ordering, expiry and deduplication do not depend on impossible clock precision.
Check month/year transitions, leap day, end-of-month recurrence and inclusive/exclusive time ranges; date-only values do not shift with user timezone.
Preserve intended precision for money, quantities, identifiers and timestamps across API/DB/export; binary floating-point or unsafe integer conversion must not silently change business values.
Define rounding, currency/unit conversion, overflow and negative-value rules; totals and corrections use consistent policies.
Test Unicode normalization, collation, case sensitivity, long strings and encoding boundaries against uniqueness, search and round-trip requirements.
Distinguish absent/null/empty/default values across JSON, forms, CSV and schema evolution; a partial update must not inadvertently erase fields.
Validate checksums/signatures or equivalent integrity markers over a defined canonical representation when used; harmless serialization differences must not create false corruption results.
Check compressed/encrypted/archived data has recoverable keys, format/version metadata and valid integrity checks before discarding originals.
Compare representative end-to-end round trips after import, export, migration and restore for IDs, values, relationships, timezone meaning and file content.
Inventory every non-rebuildable state store, including database, uploads, volumes, user files, broker state, external receipts and required configuration.
Record RPO/RTO by important dataset/service and the agreed timing boundaries; include detection, access, provisioning, verification and reconciliation as specified.
Identify dependencies between records, files, encryption keys, identities, schema, application versions and queue offsets that must form a usable recovery set.
Distinguish host/process loss, accidental deletion, corruption, malicious deletion, credential loss, provider/region outage and operator absence; coverage for one does not imply all.
Verify selected provider plan, enabled features, retention, export/restore permissions and actual available recovery points; sales documentation alone is insufficient.
Confirm snapshot/control-plane coverage explicitly includes application state or is supplemented; rebuilding a server does not recreate absent uploads or keys.
Identify rebuildable caches/indexes and measure reconstruction time at realistic volume; “rebuildable” does not guarantee the RTO.
Record vendor-owned/nonexportable state and alternatives for obtaining it after outage or account loss; expose limitations in recovery promises.
Verify scheduling, last successful completion and latest recoverable data point; job start time and backup-file modification time are not necessarily the recovery point.
Check consistency of online backups, transactions and multi-volume/object snapshots using supported mechanisms; arbitrary file copying may not yield recoverable state.
Verify full/incremental/log chains are complete and retained together; one missing segment or base backup must be detected before recovery is needed.
Test PITR to a chosen safe point around a known change and record archive continuity, timeline and recovery boundary where supported.
Verify object files and database references have compatible recovery coverage; metadata backups alone may omit the actual uploaded objects.
Check backup inclusion/exclusion filters, new tables/buckets/volumes and large/rare objects; a legacy job may omit newly introduced state.
Verify supported backup tooling/version, compression/encryption and readable manifests/checksums; file size alone is not a completeness check.
Test interrupted/failed backups, overlapping jobs, unavailable destinations and exhausted quotas; incomplete copies must not replace the last usable recovery set.
Verify freshness, failure and chain-gap alerts reach an accountable operator with time to act before RPO coverage is exceeded.
Assess backup load and retention/storage growth against production capacity; backup success must not create recurring availability failures.
Keep recovery copies outside the production failure domain with access separation appropriate to the threat model; production credentials should not erase every copy.
Verify immutability/versioning/delete protection where required, including actual retention configuration and privileged bypass paths.
Check backup encryption, key versions and independently recoverable access; keys lost with the primary host must not make protected copies unusable.
Rehearse loss of the usual operator/device/account through approved recovery access and a second trained operator without exposing secrets in the runbook.
Verify backup retention and expiry satisfy recovery needs and applicable deletion/hold policies; “keep forever” and “delete immediately everywhere” are not interchangeable defaults.
Check old restore tools, credentials, extension binaries and configuration are retained or obtainable for supported historical recovery points.
Verify backup evidence and restricted data remain protected during test restores, downloads, transfers and temporary-environment cleanup.
Simulate source/account compromise in a tabletop or permitted isolated exercise; confirm protected recovery access and copies remain available.
Restore a representative recovery set into a clean environment rather than overwriting the only working production copy.
Block outbound payments, emails, webhooks, scheduled jobs and production writes before starting restored services; restored credentials/configuration must not escape isolation.
Recover schema, roles, extensions, ownership and required configuration as well as rows; the application must be able to use the restored data securely.
Validate representative records, counts, invariants, relationships and file hashes against the selected recovery point; a database starting successfully is insufficient.
Run a representative end-to-end application workflow, including authentication, file access and a controlled write where appropriate, to establish usability.
Measure actual recovered data boundary and loss window against RPO; include gaps between the newest file, database, log and external-state recovery points.
Measure elapsed recovery to the agreed usable-service boundary against RTO, including setup, access, restore, validation and required reconciliation.
Test missing/corrupt backup elements and older recovery points so fallback choices and resulting loss are understood.
Verify deletion tombstones, revocations and access changes occurring after the restored point are reapplied or otherwise handled before exposure.
Reconcile post-recovery provider events and operations already performed externally; old queue/idempotency state must not repeat charges or lose valid outcomes.
Rebuild caches/search/derived data from the chosen authority and verify no newer incompatible entries remain from the pre-restore system.
Record restore blockers, actual operator steps, evidence, required fixes and next exercise triggers; a failed drill stays a failure until retested.
Document service startup/recovery dependency order, including secrets, identity, storage, database, broker, workers, network and application.
Verify standby capacity, quotas, images, dependencies and access can support the promised recovery workload; a nominal standby may be empty or unusable.
Test old-writer fencing, routing and reconnect behavior during failover; the failed site must not keep accepting unsupported authoritative writes.
For regional/provider recovery, account for DNS, certificates, identity, endpoints, object locations and externally allowlisted callbacks, not only database promotion.
Define queue/event handling while unavailable: buffer, reject, persist or backfill with an explicit loss/expiry model and customer-visible status.
Drain recovery backlog at a controlled rate; live traffic, quotas and critical invariants remain protected during catch-up.
Plan failback/return to the normal site, including source of truth, divergent writes, synchronization, write freeze and validation; reversing DNS alone is not sufficient.
Keep decision authority, escalation, customer-status coordination and alternate-operator instructions available outside the failed system.
Rehearse at the agreed risk-based interval and after material changes; tabletop planning and a full restore exercise are recorded as different evidence.
After the exercise, verify isolation cleanup, temporary credentials, cost/resources, production noninterference and updates to runbooks/targets before closing it.
Inventory schema, data, index, extension, collation, storage-format and provider-semantic changes, not only files in the migration directory.
Record prerequisites, irreversible effects, expected duration, owner, stop conditions and reversal/recovery route for each material change.
Verify the old application works with the expanded schema and new application handles pre-backfill data during rolling deployment.
Check mixed-version workers, APIs, scheduled jobs and event payloads; deployment overlap must not write incompatible records or messages.
Use staged expand/backfill/switch/contract or another justified compatibility strategy where availability targets require it; destructive contraction waits for actual consumer retirement.
Verify feature flags and disabled paths do not still write/read retired structures through old replicas, admin tools or delayed jobs.
Check database/driver/extension upgrades and restore-tool compatibility using actual versions; supported SQL syntax alone does not settle behavior changes.
Document code rollback separately from schema reversal, data restoration and provider compensation; each path has its own acceptance evidence.
Rehearse with production-shaped size, skew, history, tenant distribution and edge values; tiny fixtures do not measure locking or completion time.
Measure lock acquisition/duration, blocked traffic and transaction impact; long waits and deadlocks have bounded stop/recovery behavior.
Verify migration ownership/locking prevents duplicate concurrent execution across replicas, deployment jobs and operators.
Interrupt migration/backfill before and after checkpoints; rerun/resume must not skip or duplicate transformations.
Inspect actual DDL/transaction behavior, online index options and failure cleanup for the selected engine; don't assume every migration can roll back atomically.
Verify batch size, throttling, checkpoints and retry bounds keep foreground traffic, storage and replica lag within agreed limits.
Test concurrent old/new writes during backfill; copied data and late changes converge without overwriting newer values.
Compare row/object counts, key coverage, relationships, value totals and semantic samples before/after; equal counts alone do not prove a correct transformation.
Validate new constraints against legacy data before relying on them; invalid/conflicting records have an explicit repair or quarantine path.
Check required indexes/constraints are valid and active after interrupted creation; a named object may exist without being usable as intended.
Account for storage/log/archive growth, temporary space and replica/network load caused by changes; failure from capacity exhaustion is planned for.
Record migration ledger/version only at the intended completion boundary; “applied” must not hide an incomplete backfill or failed postcondition.
Define source of truth before, during and after cutover; prevent accidental independent writers on both old and new stores.
If dual writing, test one-side failure, retries, reordering and reconciliation; two successful API calls are not atomicity evidence.
Verify snapshot/copy plus CDC/event handoff has no untracked gap and a documented catch-up position before reads/writes switch.
Rehearse final synchronization/write-freeze or equivalent boundary and measure the actual service interruption.
Verify old connections, DNS caches, worker pools, webhooks and delayed jobs route to the intended authority after cutover.
Reconcile provider IDs, identity/account mappings, object URLs, timestamps and sequences so new writes do not collide with imported records.
Rehearse reverse migration where genuinely reversible and inspect old/new application compatibility afterward; reverse syntax is not proof of restored meaning.
For irreversible changes identify lost information and execute the planned restore/fail-forward exercise; a fabricated down migration cannot recover dropped data.
Check rollback after new production-format writes: preserve/reconcile those writes or explicitly document the loss/compensation boundary.
Retain recovery points and compatibility routes until agreed validation completes; old-state cleanup must not prematurely remove the only fallback.
Test failed deployment/startup and interrupted shutdown with the new schema; rollback must not repeatedly trigger unsafe migration side effects.
Verify a fresh install and an upgrade from supported prior versions produce compatible complete state; a working long-lived database can hide missing initialization steps.
Define hard delete, soft delete, archive and cancellation distinctly, including related records, search, files, external providers and retention rules.
Test soft-deleted uniqueness, filters, references and concurrent restore/new-create; recovery does not create duplicate active identities or records.
Verify authorized restoration preserves tenant/ownership/access boundaries and does not revive expired permissions or revoked shares.
Check retention jobs use correct scope, timestamps, timezone and exclusions; dry-run samples/limits prevent broad unintended deletion.
Race cleanup with active uploads/jobs, late callbacks, restore and updates; age alone is not proof that a record/object is safe to remove.
Coordinate deletion tombstones and exceptions through backup restore, reimports, synchronization and replay; deleted data must not silently reappear.
Assess legal/operational holds with the responsible owner; holds are scoped, auditable and eventually released rather than silently disabling all retention.
Repair corrupted/inconsistent records with an explicit source of truth, bounded selection, preconditions and validation; scripts must not overwrite intervening valid changes.
Verify repair/backfill/cleanup tools support safe restart and duplicate invocation, with per-item outcomes or transactional guarantees suited to the work.
Preserve immutable business history where required; corrective entries and reconciliation are distinguishable from undocumented mutation.
Compare current invariants and service/freshness targets after rollout, including delayed jobs and derived data, before declaring completion.
Document residual quarantined records, manual interventions and uncertain outcomes with owners; successful majority processing must not hide untracked exceptions.
Verify new backups and an appropriate restore path work with the changed schema/format/keys; old recovery evidence may no longer apply.
Retire old stores, credentials, jobs and routes only after verification and retention decisions; abandoned writers can reintroduce divergence later.
Update inventory, runbooks, on-call ownership, recovery sequence and evidence references for the final deployed architecture.
For shutdown, acquisition or provider exit preserve required exports, history, recovery access and deletion obligations; closing a service does not automatically finish its data lifecycle.

headings.text: Audit library review and proposed changes
Sixth reference image: legal risks, 15 October 2026
Code and test reduction emphasis, 17 October 2026
Hidden recurring costs and scheduled-work reduction, 17 October 2026
Additional identity, browser and lifecycle boundaries

values: Record project, audit date/timezone, source/deployed revision, artifact/runtime, environments, configuration/flags, owners and current release/exposure. Identify disabled, legacy and planned features separately.
Enumerate public/private domains, APIs, server actions, WebSockets, mobile/desktop clients, databases, object stores, search indexes, queues, schedulers and administrative surfaces.

Inventory cloud/provider accounts, regions, identity systems, shared infrastructure, previews, old deployments and externally configured integrations. Mark inaccessible surfaces Not verified rather than assuming absence.

Classify sensitive business assets and personal data, including credentials, tokens, financial records, private content, location, identifiers, communications, embeddings and derived profiles where present.

Map actors and capabilities: anonymous visitor, user, member, owner, other tenant, support/admin, integration, worker, CI and provider. Include compromised low-privilege accounts and accidental operator misuse.
Identify authoritative sources for identity, role, ownership, tenant, price/entitlement and consent. Label untrusted identifiers, headers, claims, files, generated text and provider events.
Describe trust boundaries and data flows between browser/client, edge, service, worker, database, vendor and administrator. Include sync and async paths plus import/export and recovery flows.

Record per-asset owner, allowed operations, confidentiality/integrity/availability expectations, retention and recovery dependencies. Identify shared credentials and administrators with unusually broad reach.
Define intended public access explicitly for assets, database views/RPCs, storage and frontend keys. A public key's name does not establish either harmlessness or privileged access.
Model account takeover, cross-tenant access, privilege escalation, data exfiltration, injection, SSRF, insecure files, supply-chain compromise and harmful resource use relevant to the architecture.
Model accidental leaks through logs, analytics/session replay, support tickets, screenshots, CI artifacts, source maps, AI chats/tool artifacts and copied development datasets.
Consider automation/business misuse, stolen keys, malicious insiders, third-party compromise, old clients and long-delayed jobs/events. Link financial/capacity exposure to module 08.
Identify critical invariants such as no cross-tenant reads/writes, no client-assigned privileges, no unsigned event authority and no secret exposure to untrusted clients.

Document architectural defenses and limits: authorization point, service/DB roles, isolation, encryption/key control, egress controls, storage permissions and auditability. Avoid relying on one defense without testing its bypass roles.

Identify privacy purposes, sensitive populations/use cases, contractual commitments and relevant jurisdictions for accountable review. Determine whether additional privacy/security assessment is needed without inventing universal legal thresholds.

Record intentional exceptions and compensating controls, including public previews, support impersonation, shared services, offline clients and legacy integrations. Assign owner, scope, expiry and review trigger.

Record authorized systems/accounts, environments, techniques, data access, external effects and testing limits. Use synthetic identities and owned fixtures; follow existing authorization rather than requesting redundant permission.

Set request/concurrency/duration/cost and file-size ceilings, cancellation/cleanup and operator stop conditions. Avoid real metadata services, unsolicited messages, unrestricted scanning and destructive production tests.
Create at least two distinct synthetic users/tenants and the relevant service/admin roles for boundary tests. Use the same effective application roles and network paths as the deployed design.
Derive expected allowance/denial from product policy independently of current implementation. Pair denied operations with intended allowed operations so rejecting everything cannot pass.
Record direct sanitized requests, actual responses and resulting DB/storage/job/provider effects. A success response can hide a denied write, and an error can occur after an unauthorized side effect.

Distinguish source inspection, config review, local/staging execution and production evidence. Record untested scope, inaccessible providers, realistic sample sizes and relevant environment differences.

Select materially distinct routes, roles, tenants, policies, authentication methods, clients and failure states. Expand coverage after inconsistencies; do not infer every path from one passing endpoint.

Reuse meaningful tests and tools. Where material regression tests are needed, follow module 15's isolated test-sensitivity method; retain the smallest useful set, not a test mirroring every checklist sentence.

Protect audit evidence with redaction, restricted access and proportionate retention. Store correlation without live secrets, unnecessary personal records or portable exploit material against real targets.
Distinguish verified defect, opportunity and verification gap; group shared root causes while recording all affected surfaces. Link existing specialist findings instead of duplicating them.

Prioritize according to demonstrated access, data sensitivity, affected population, financial/availability impact, exploit prerequisites and confidence. A dependency severity score or missing header alone does not define business priority.
