Review backup transport, storage access, retention, privacy, and access logging; avoid placing public backups, dumps, or temporary restore files behind a web route.
Verify schedules, timezone, overlap, duration, timeouts, skipped jobs, database/container downtime, and resource competition under actual deployment conditions.
Monitor creation, completeness, remote upload, freshness, remote availability, and failure/warning outcomes independently; local success does not establish an off-site copy exists.
Inspect size/content anomalies, exclusions, command exit codes, compression/encryption failures, partial files, and backup jobs that appear successful after doing no work.
Define retention across local and remote stores, versioning/lifecycle, failed residues, and deletion permissions; ensure no policy removes the last useful recovery generation unexpectedly.
Verify storage/disk/inode/egress costs and capacity for backup growth, download, decompression, restore, and temporary copies; recovery may need more space than the archive size.
Test failure/alert reception through an authorized bounded method and confirm an off-host recipient/owner responds; an enabled notification toggle is not delivered evidence.
Rehearse on an isolated fresh host or equivalent clean environment using actual documented tools, versions, keys, backups, and available credentials rather than cached source-server state.
Prevent restored jobs, webhooks, mail, payments, and external writes from running against production during rehearsal; isolate identities, endpoints, and recipients as well as networks.
Document restore order and prerequisites for accounts, network/firewalls, OS/runtime, control plane, keys, volumes, databases, apps, proxy, DNS, monitoring, and jobs.
Verify restored secrets can be used through safe functional checks, not secret printing; check decryption, credentials, image/source access, and remote-server identity after replacement.
Validate row/entity relationships, business invariants, uploaded files, permissions/tenants, application behavior, and version compatibility; row counts or a running dashboard alone are insufficient.
Measure actual restore and verification times, last recoverable committed state, external dependencies, and gaps against RPO/RTO; do not substitute schedule frequency for achieved RPO.
Reconcile data and external effects after restore, including queue replay, payment state, mail/webhook delivery, deleted accounts, and events newer than the recovered snapshot.
Establish one intended writer and scheduler/consumer owner before restoring service; prevent old/new hosts from concurrently performing consequential work.
Verify post-recovery DNS/TLS/routing, origin restrictions, alerts, new backups, and ordinary deployment operation; retain old evidence/assets until their recovery purpose ends.
Record rehearsal results, artifact/key references, actual versions, isolated cleanup, failures, owners, and next triggers without embedding recovery secrets in the report.
Distinguish DNS/delegation failure, upstream network saturation, host outage, storage exhaustion, proxy/TLS failure, application failure, and suspected compromise using layer-specific evidence.
Maintain an off-host incident sequence with authority, provider contacts, safe restrictions, legitimate-traffic checks, sanitized evidence preservation, and communication dependencies.
For suspected compromise, plan controlled isolation and clean provisioning from trusted inputs; do not assume restoring the latest system snapshot removes persistence or compromised keys.

Scope credential rotation to hosting, registrar, DNS, control plane, SSH, source/registry, app providers, database, and backups as affected; perform rotation from a trusted system with consumer sequencing.
Assess backup contamination and select a defensible recovery point; preserve necessary incident evidence separately and validate repaired data/financial consequences.
Complete post-incident review, permanent fixes, risk/ownership updates, and focused rechecks; report unknown compromise scope or unverified restore as an unresolved gap.
Monitor external DNS, TLS, HTTP/application journeys, control-plane access, host health, and dependency health separately; a running container or ping response is not product availability.
Check CPU/steal, memory/OOM, swap, disk bytes/inodes, I/O, bandwidth, connection tracking, file descriptors, queue age, and relevant provider quotas against actual failure risks.
Keep monitoring and alert reception sufficiently independent of the VPS, hosted DNS/mail, and critical identity dependencies to detect their failure.
Verify alert delivery, thresholds, recovery notices, ownership, and escalation with bounded evidence; avoid noisy alerts that are never acted upon.
Maintain useful correlation/time synchronization across edge, proxy, host, containers, jobs, and provider logs without recording unnecessary secrets or private payloads.
Bound log/metric/trace retention, label cardinality, disk use, access, and export costs; logging must not become the cause of storage exhaustion or a privacy leak.
Detect drift in firewall attachment, listeners, DNS, routes, memberships, credentials, images, volumes, and backup status against an owned configuration source.
Assign routine patch/reboot, certificate/credential renewal, capacity, backup/restore, domain/billing, and incident responsibilities; cadence should reflect actual risk.
Record current/desired configuration, affected hosts/apps, scope, prerequisites, owner, maintenance window, success metrics, and stop/rollback triggers before consequential changes.
Establish a verified alternate admin/rescue path and known-good configuration before changing SSH, routing, VPN, provider firewall, or host network policy.
Sequence add/validate/restrict/remove where appropriate so the new path is proven before the old one is retired; avoid combining unrelated access changes that obscure recovery.
Validate configuration syntax/version compatibility and persistent versus runtime state using supported methods before reload/restart; do not deploy unreviewed generic hardening commands.
Include Docker/Coolify/proxy updates, OS/kernel reboots, and dependency changes in the recovery plan; code/image rollback may not reverse data/config migrations.
Recheck administrative, web, database, webhook, streaming, backup, DNS, certificate, and monitoring paths affected by the change, including legitimate denied/allowed outcomes.
Remove temporary broad rules, test hostnames, tokens, preview containers, debug listeners, and bypasses after their purpose ends; verify cleanup without deleting required evidence/recovery assets.
Record actual result, changed version/config, rollback/forward repair if used, residual risk, and handover; planned success is not a verified completed change.
Identify single points in host, control plane, proxy, DNS authority, identity, registry, backups, region, and human ownership; compare with agreed availability/recovery requirements.
Distinguish a multi-host management dashboard from a tested highly available application/control plane; document which components actually fail over.
For multiple replicas/hosts, verify shared sessions/uploads, database authority, queue/cron ownership, cache/limit scope, health routing, and consistent configuration.
For failover, validate IP/DNS movement, certificate identity, provider policy attachment, private routing, replication lag, stale readers, and prevention of split writers.
Ensure spare/replacement capacity and recovery transfer time match the target; theoretical failover without deployable resources or usable credentials is a gap.
For remote/build servers, test intended behavior during controller loss, SSH failure, registry outage, failed builds, and reconnection without assuming running apps require a healthy dashboard.
For shared multi-project VPSs, check cross-project network/volume/secret access, resource fairness, build/backup contention, and the maximum acceptable host-wide blast radius.
For preview/staging environments, isolate data/credentials/recipients and public access, label owners/expiry, and remove orphaned resources and DNS safely.
For external/managed databases, verify private/TLS routing, egress addresses/allowlists, pools, region latency, credentials, backups, and provider outage behavior.
For local SQLite/file-backed stores, check actual persistent path, concurrent writer limits, permissions, backup consistency, and behavior on redeploy/recreation.
For object/NFS/shared storage, verify mounts, identity, encryption, permissions, locking/consistency semantics, outage behavior, backup, and deletion/recovery expectations.
For game/voice/VPN/mail/DNS workloads, audit non-HTTP ports, protocols, clients, upstream protection, and provider restrictions without assuming the web proxy secures them.
For tunnels/private-only origins, review connector/device enrollment, credentials, access policy, routing, resolution, recovery, and whether a direct public bypass still exists.
For IPv6-only, NAT-constrained, or mixed-architecture hosts, verify package/image/provider compatibility, outbound dependencies, published services, and real client reachability.
For high-volume transfers, streaming, or AI workloads, check proxy buffering/timeouts, temporary storage, egress, concurrency, worker lifetime, and expensive-feature shutdown.
For sensitive or regulated workloads, record applicable data location/access/retention requirements and accountable specialists; this general infrastructure checklist cannot establish compliance.
Before provider/IP/DNS moves, map source/destination authority, records, secrets, certificates, allowlists, callbacks, jobs, data, and rollback constraints; use module 17 for the full cutover.
Preserve supported old paths during cache/consumer transition while preventing duplicate writers/jobs; reversing DNS alone is not data-safe rollback.
Retire old instances, IPs, volumes, snapshots, DNS, tokens, tunnels, deployments, and paid services only after dependency, retention, recovery, and observation requirements are satisfied.
Have another maintainer follow the operating/recovery instructions and document gaps; finish with owned findings, verified controls, unresolved evidence, and explicit review triggers.

Protect hosting, registrar, DNS, source control, registry, and backup accounts with available MFA, controlled ownership, scoped tokens, and externally stored recovery methods. Verify domain/service renewal and payment-failure notifications.

Use individual SSH keys and a documented administrative path. Validate key access and the provider console/rescue recovery path before disabling password or root login, changing ports, or narrowing firewall rules.
Separate routine operator accounts from automation credentials. If Coolify needs elevated access, document the actual sudo/Docker powers; a non-root account with broad elevation is still privileged.
Restrict SSH to necessary administrator/VPN and Coolify-controller sources, including a separate controller if used. Avoid assuming the user's home IP is the only legitimate SSH source.
Review stale users, keys, access logs, and suspicious authentication. Optional intrusion-blocking tools complement key access and perimeter controls; they do not replace upstream mitigation.

Configure the actual provider perimeter and host/container filtering together. Contabo's documented firewall blocks inbound traffic unless allowed and does not restrict outbound traffic; verify attachment to the correct instance and effective address-family coverage. [Contabo firewall](https://help.contabo.com/en/support/solutions/articles/103000390430-firewall-what-is-it-and-how-does-it-protect-my-vps-vds-)

Inventory listeners and Docker-published ports against approved services. Ordinary UFW rules may not filter Docker-published ports because Docker routes this traffic before UFW's normal chains. Use the provider perimeter or an appropriately supported Docker-aware policy and verify externally. Do not disable Docker's firewall integration blindly. [Docker firewall behavior](https://docs.docker.com/engine/network/packet-filtering-firewalls/)
Identify the deployed iptables/nftables backend and maintain compatible rules. Do not assume a rule intended for one backend or forwarding chain works on another.
Verify IPv4 and IPv6 independently, including AAAA records, public interfaces, container exposure, and any private/VPN route. Do not accidentally create an unfiltered IPv6 bypass.
Keep databases, Redis/caches, internal APIs, Docker API/socket, debug ports, and metrics endpoints private unless a justified integration explicitly requires protected access.

Do not open inbound TCP/UDP 53 merely because the apps use DNS. Outbound DNS resolution and serving DNS are different. If deliberately hosting DNS, separately verify authoritative/resolver role, restricted recursion, and flood/amplification defenses.

Preserve required outbound resolution, time sync, updates, certificate flows, provider APIs, and backup uploads. Where outbound restrictions are used, test them and account for dynamic provider endpoints.

Treat Coolify as a privileged control plane. Protect its dashboard with HTTPS, verified authentication/MFA capabilities, limited membership, and an appropriate VPN/private-access or identity-gateway boundary. Closing direct ports alone does not restrict the dashboard domain. [Coolify security model](https://coolify.io/docs/core/security-model)

Verify necessary machine webhooks and automation still function through any administrative access gateway. Authenticate endpoints; avoid globally bypassing dashboard protection to make callbacks work.
Scope Git/registry/deployment tokens and stored SSH keys; review user invitations, administrative sessions, API tokens, deploy hooks, and audit records.
Separate production/staging, credentials, volumes, and container networks. Check whether apps can reach another project's database or files; do not rely on project labels alone for isolation.

Avoid privileged app containers, unnecessary capabilities, host namespace use, Docker socket mounts, and broad host mounts. Apply non-root execution, resource limits, and filesystem restrictions where compatible. Isolate higher-risk workloads on separate hosts when shared-host risk is unacceptable.
Budget CPU, memory, disk, inodes, logs, build cache, I/O, database pools, and worker concurrency per project. Rehearse a deploy/build while other apps are serving traffic.
Keep OS, Docker, proxy, Coolify, and images patched. Plan security update/reboot windows and verify restart policies, health checks, graceful shutdown, and service recovery.
Inventory A/AAAA/CNAME/MX/TXT/CAA records, nameservers, TTLs, credentials, wildcard records, and stale/dangling references. Record ownership and change/expiry monitoring.

Enable and validate DNSSEC where supported; ensure the registrar DS record matches the authoritative provider. Rehearse DNS provider changes to avoid stale delegation breaking resolution. [DNSSEC activation](https://developers.cloudflare.com/registrar/get-started/enable-dnssec/)

If using an edge proxy, confirm the intended web records are actually proxied and audit DNS-only records, mail services, and historical IP exposure. Test a known origin IP with the real Host/SNI; it should not bypass the intended edge restrictions.

Choose an origin design: allowlisted trusted ingress with suitable origin authentication, or an outbound tunnel where appropriate. Account for health checks, callbacks, certificate renewal, range updates, and IPv6. Shared proxy IP ranges alone do not prove that a request belongs to your specific site/account. [Origin protection options](https://developers.cloudflare.com/fundamentals/security/protect-your-origin-server/)

Encrypt and authenticate edge-to-origin traffic. For Cloudflare use a correctly configured Full (strict) equivalent with a valid trusted origin certificate; verify renewal and certificate compatibility with any direct access. [Cloudflare Full strict TLS](https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/origin-configuration/ssl-modes/full-strict/)

Reject unintended Host values/default routes and secure proxy forwarding. Trust client-IP/protocol headers only from verified proxy hops and prevent spoofed headers affecting limits, logs, redirects, or secure cookies.
Validate HTTPS redirects, renewal automation, WebSockets, SSE/AI streaming, upload limits, and sensible route-specific timeouts. Apply HSTS only after validating its hostname/subdomain scope.

Select WAF/rate/bot controls based on actual plan capabilities and observed traffic. Combine edge controls with server-side per-user/tenant limits, global budgets, and bounded expensive jobs under 08.
Test that rules do not break login, APIs, signed webhooks, search indexing, uploads, or accessibility. Use documented verification exceptions instead of blanket challenges on machine clients.
Prevent slow/oversized requests and connection exhaustion with bounded request bodies, connections, and appropriate timeouts. Keep streaming/long jobs on explicitly supported paths.

Monitor edge versus origin requests, errors, latency, bandwidth, connection counts, CPU/RAM, disk, queue age, authentication failures, and billing signals. Place uptime/alert reception outside this VPS.
Define controlled abuse suspension, emergency rate tightening, and expensive-feature shutdown. Operators need a safe rollback for false positives.

Back up Coolify configuration/state independently from app databases, uploads, volumes, and other persistent data. Preserve the instance APP_KEY securely outside the server; a database backup cannot recover encrypted stored secrets without the key. Never print it into audit logs. [Coolify instance backup](https://coolify.io/docs/core/backup-and-recovery/instance-backup)

Verify engine-specific application backup/restore support, off-site destinations, freshness, retention, encryption, and alerts. Coolify backup support differs by database type; use native procedures where needed. [Database backups](https://coolify.io/docs/databases/backups), [database restoration](https://coolify.io/docs/databases/restore)

Rehearse restoring onto an isolated fresh host or equivalent environment. Restore control plane, keys, networks, apps, databases, files, and jobs in a documented order; measure RPO/RTO and inspect real application behavior.

Prepare an incident sequence: identify network/DNS/web/application symptoms, contact the relevant upstream provider, apply proportionate restrictions, preserve sanitized evidence, suspend expensive work, and assess compromise. A compromised host may require clean rebuild and credential rotation rather than an in-place restart.

During mitigation check legitimate traffic and shared-project effects; after recovery review the cause, data/financial consequences, and remaining controls. Keep the runbook and contacts available off-host.

checks.heading: Manual testing
checks.text: **Keyboard navigation:** Tab through entire page, use Enter/Space to activate

checks.heading: Manual testing
checks.text: **Screen reader:** Test with VoiceOver (Mac), NVDA (Windows), or TalkBack (Android)

checks.heading: Manual testing
checks.text: **Zoom:** Content usable at 200% zoom

checks.heading: Manual testing
checks.text: **High contrast:** Test with Windows High Contrast Mode

checks.heading: Manual testing
checks.text: **Reduced motion:** Test with `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`

checks.heading: Manual testing
checks.text: **Focus order:** Logical and follows visual order

checks.heading: Manual testing
checks.text: **Target size:** Interactive elements meet 24×24px minimum

checks.heading: Structure and reading sequence
checks.text: CORE-001 — Titles identify page topic/purpose and distinguish similar pages, errors and meaningful client-side route changes.

checks.heading: Structure and reading sequence
checks.text: CORE-002 — Headings convey hierarchy and topic; visual headings expose semantics. Investigate skipped levels in context rather than treating every skip as an automatic failure.

checks.heading: Structure and reading sequence
checks.text: CORE-003 — Main content, navigation, header/footer and complementary regions are understandable in the accessibility tree; repeated region types have distinguishing labels where needed.

checks.heading: Structure and reading sequence
checks.text: CORE-004 — DOM and screen-reader order preserve meaning when flex/grid, columns, cards or responsive layouts rearrange the display.

checks.heading: Structure and reading sequence
checks.text: CORE-005 — Lists, quotations, definitions, control groups and tables expose relationships; spacing alone does not carry essential structure.

checks.heading: Structure and reading sequence
checks.text: CORE-006 — Default language and substantive language changes are identifiable programmatically; consider exceptions for names and technical terms.

checks.heading: Structure and reading sequence
checks.text: CORE-007 — Instructions such as “press the green button on the right” also identify the control without depending solely on sensory characteristics.

checks.heading: Structure and reading sequence
checks.text: CORE-008 — Meaningful pseudo-element text, icons and badges are available appropriately; decorative content does not create repetitive speech.

checks.heading: Structure and reading sequence
checks.text: CORE-009 — Hidden, collapsed, off-canvas and inert content is not misleadingly exposed or keyboard reachable; visible essential content is not hidden from AT.

checks.heading: Structure and reading sequence
checks.text: CORE-010 — Duplicate IDs and invalid relationships are investigated for actual label, state or interaction failures. Removed criterion 4.1.1 is not a WCAG 2.2 requirement.

checks.heading: Keyboard, focus, and navigation
checks.text: CORE-011 — Complete critical tasks without a pointer, including correction, cancellation and recovery controls.

checks.heading: Keyboard, focus, and navigation
checks.text: CORE-012 — Tab/Shift+Tab order preserves meaning and operability; visual rearrangement and positive tabindex do not cause disorienting jumps.

checks.heading: Keyboard, focus, and navigation
checks.text: CORE-013 — Native/custom controls activate with expected keys without duplicate submission; Space does not scroll during button activation.

checks.heading: Keyboard, focus, and navigation
checks.text: CORE-014 — Focus is visible on every interactive element in supported themes/states, including icons, inline links, embeds and shadow DOM.

checks.heading: Keyboard, focus, and navigation
checks.text: CORE-015 — Sticky bars, banners and overlays do not entirely obscure focused components at AA. Partial obscuring is an additional usability/AAA concern.

checks.heading: Keyboard, focus, and navigation
checks.text: CORE-016 — Users can leave components using a keyboard; nonstandard exit instructions are discoverable. Modal containment has a usable completion or dismissal path.

checks.heading: Keyboard, focus, and navigation
checks.text: CORE-017 — A mechanism bypasses repeated blocks. If using a skip link, verify focus visibility, destination and where subsequent keyboard navigation continues.

checks.heading: Keyboard, focus, and navigation
checks.text: CORE-018 — Focus remains meaningful after deletion, filtering, sorting, pagination, row insertion, banner dismissal and replacement of a focused element.

checks.heading: Keyboard, focus, and navigation
checks.text: CORE-019 — Dialogs, route changes and view transitions have deliberate contextual focus behavior; background updates do not repeatedly steal focus.

checks.heading: Keyboard, focus, and navigation
checks.text: CORE-020 — Single-character shortcuts can be disabled/remapped or only activate when the relevant component has focus; speech input does not trigger unwanted commands.

checks.heading: Keyboard, focus, and navigation
checks.text: CORE-021 — Link purpose is clear from text and permitted programmatic context. Repeated “read more” links are checked in context; standalone clarity is enhanced guidance.

checks.heading: Keyboard, focus, and navigation
checks.text: CORE-022 — Multiple ways to find pages in a set exist where required; document process-step/result exceptions. Repeated navigation and help remain predictably ordered.

checks.heading: Keyboard, focus, and navigation
checks.text: CORE-023 — Focus does not unexpectedly navigate, submit or open a context; input changes do not cause unannounced context changes.

checks.heading: Keyboard, focus, and navigation
checks.text: CORE-024 — Back/forward, deep links and in-page anchors preserve understandable position/state; restored focus does not land behind an overlay.

checks.heading: Pointer, touch, voice, and motion input
checks.text: CORE-025 — Visible label wording occurs within accessible names so voice users can target controls; hidden overrides do not replace the wording.

checks.heading: Pointer, touch, voice, and motion input
checks.text: CORE-026 — Multipoint/path-based gestures have a single-pointer operation without a path-based gesture unless essential; examine custom pinch and drawn gestures.

checks.heading: Pointer, touch, voice, and motion input
checks.text: CORE-027 — Dragging has a click/tap alternative without dragging unless an exception applies. A keyboard-only alternative alone does not satisfy this requirement.

checks.heading: Pointer, touch, voice, and motion input
checks.text: CORE-028 — Pointer actions permit cancellation, reversal or safe release under the applicable criterion; test down, move away, release and accidental activation.

checks.heading: Pointer, touch, voice, and motion input
checks.text: CORE-029 — Hit areas meet 24 by 24 CSS pixels or a valid 2.5.8 exception: spacing, equivalent, inline, user-agent control or essential presentation. Measure actual targets.

checks.heading: Pointer, touch, voice, and motion input
checks.text: CORE-030 — Dense toolbars, pagination, pins, calendar cells and adjacent destructive buttons remain usable by touch; consider 44 by 44 targets as an enhanced goal with its own exceptions.

checks.heading: Pointer, touch, voice, and motion input
checks.text: CORE-031 — Shaking, tilting or motion-actuated functions have UI alternatives and can be disabled unless an exception applies.

checks.heading: Pointer, touch, voice, and motion input
checks.text: CORE-032 — Hover-only, long-press, swipe-to-delete and context-menu actions have usable keyboard/touch alternatives where needed.

checks.heading: Contrast, zoom, and adaptation
checks.text: CORE-033 — Normal text meets 4.5:1; qualifying large text meets 3:1. Large means at least 18 pt (24 CSS px), or 14 pt bold (about 18.67 CSS px), not 18/14 CSS px.

checks.heading: Contrast, zoom, and adaptation
checks.text: CORE-034 — Measure text on actual backgrounds including gradients, photographs, overlays, opacity, placeholders and selection; document applicable exceptions.

checks.heading: Contrast, zoom, and adaptation
checks.text: CORE-035 — Visual information needed to identify controls/states and meaningful graphics meets applicable 3:1 non-text contrast against adjacent colors; borders are not mandatory on every control.

checks.heading: Contrast, zoom, and adaptation
checks.text: CORE-036 — Color is not the only visual cue for errors, selection, availability, links, required fields, chart series or change direction.

checks.heading: Contrast, zoom, and adaptation
checks.text: CORE-037 — Text remains usable at 200% resize without loss of content/function; understand the criterion's caption/image-of-text exceptions.

checks.heading: Contrast, zoom, and adaptation
checks.text: CORE-038 — Content reflows at 320 CSS pixel viewport width without loss or two-dimensional scrolling except qualifying two-dimensional content; test 256 CSS pixel height for vertical writing.

checks.heading: Contrast, zoom, and adaptation
checks.text: CORE-039 — High zoom leaves menus, dialogs, tables, tooltips, sticky UI and error summaries reachable; fixed-height containers do not trap essential content.

checks.heading: Contrast, zoom, and adaptation
checks.text: CORE-040 — Simultaneously override line height to 1.5 times font size, paragraph spacing to 2 times, letter spacing to 0.12 em and word spacing to 0.16 em without loss. Consider script-specific exceptions.

checks.heading: Contrast, zoom, and adaptation
checks.text: CORE-041 — Portrait/landscape both work unless orientation is essential; design preference is not an essential restriction.

checks.heading: Contrast, zoom, and adaptation
checks.text: CORE-042 — Forced colors and user contrast settings preserve names, selection, focus and meaningful icons. Classify usability findings separately when no specific criterion fails.

checks.heading: Contrast, zoom, and adaptation
checks.text: CORE-043 — Font changes, minimum font settings and long translations do not hide essential content; text stays selectable where the task needs it.

checks.heading: Contrast, zoom, and adaptation
checks.text: CORE-044 — Real text replaces images of text where possible; document customizable/essential exceptions, such as logotypes.

checks.heading: Contrast, zoom, and adaptation
checks.text: CORE-045 — Hover/focus content is dismissible, hoverable and persistent under 1.4.13 conditions/exceptions; test magnification and moving into the popup.

checks.heading: Alternatives and complex information
checks.text: CORE-046 — Informative images have equivalent contextual alternatives, without filenames or needless repetition of surrounding text.

checks.heading: Alternatives and complex information
checks.text: CORE-047 — Decorative images are ignored appropriately; functional image alternatives identify action/destination rather than appearance alone.

checks.heading: Alternatives and complex information
checks.text: CORE-048 — Linked image/text combinations have useful non-repetitive names; icon-only controls and social links expose localized names.

checks.heading: Alternatives and complex information
checks.text: CORE-049 — SVG, canvas, background images, emoji and icon fonts convey meaningful information through accessible text or equivalent interfaces; test actual AT exposure.

checks.heading: Alternatives and complex information
checks.text: CORE-050 — Charts, maps, diagrams, scientific notation and infographics expose task-relevant values/relationships through structured descriptions, tables or equivalent controls.

checks.heading: Alternatives and complex information
checks.text: CORE-051 — CAPTCHA identifies its purpose and provides alternatives required by 1.1.1; assess authentication separately under 3.3.8. An audio fallback alone does not prove the process accessible.

checks.heading: Alternatives and complex information
checks.text: CORE-052 — Alternatives stay correct after localization, responsive-image swaps, CMS edits, user uploads and image failures.

checks.heading: Forms, authentication, and recovery
checks.text: CORE-053 — Fields have meaningful accessible names and visible labels or adequate instructions where required; investigate disappearing placeholder-only context.

checks.heading: Forms, authentication, and recovery
checks.text: CORE-054 — Group labels, legends, hints, units, formats, limits and required states are available at entry and associated programmatically where appropriate.

checks.heading: Forms, authentication, and recovery
checks.text: CORE-055 — Applicable personal-data fields identify input purpose through standardized tokens; input type alone does not replace autocomplete purpose.

checks.heading: Forms, authentication, and recovery
checks.text: CORE-056 — Password managers, autofill, paste, dictation and correction work; segmented codes assist whole-code entry and expose meaningful order/labels.

checks.heading: Forms, authentication, and recovery
checks.text: CORE-057 — Login, MFA, recovery, step-up and identity challenges meet accessible-authentication conditions; examine cognitive tests, assistance and alternatives explicitly.

checks.heading: Forms, authentication, and recovery
checks.text: CORE-058 — Errors identify field/problem in text, expose invalid state appropriately and suggest known corrections unless security/purpose would be compromised.

checks.heading: Forms, authentication, and recovery
checks.text: CORE-059 — Submit errors become discoverable through a suitable summary, focus strategy or announcement, without duplicate speech or lost data.

checks.heading: Forms, authentication, and recovery
checks.text: CORE-060 — Async validation handles pending/success/failure and stale responses; users are not repeatedly interrupted before finishing input.

checks.heading: Forms, authentication, and recovery
checks.text: CORE-061 — Correcting an error preserves unrelated valid inputs; hidden conditional fields do not create unreachable validation blockers.

checks.heading: Forms, authentication, and recovery
checks.text: CORE-062 — Data already entered/provided in the same process is auto-populated or selectable where 3.3.7 applies; document essential, security and no-longer-valid exceptions.

checks.heading: Forms, authentication, and recovery
checks.text: CORE-063 — Legal/financial submissions, stored-user-data changes/deletions and test responses meet applicable reversible, checked or confirmed error-prevention conditions.

checks.heading: Forms, authentication, and recovery
checks.text: CORE-064 — Review pages/receipts expose confirmation details; correction links return to usable fields and preserve other steps.

checks.heading: Forms, authentication, and recovery
checks.text: CORE-065 — Disabled/read-only fields and unavailable actions expose understandable states and discoverable reasons; required completion is not hidden behind an unnamed disabled button.

checks.heading: Forms, authentication, and recovery
checks.text: CORE-066 — Upload supports keyboard selection, constraints, progress, cancellation, failure, replacement and removal; drag-and-drop is not the sole path.

checks.heading: Media, timing, flashing, and movement
checks.text: CORE-067 — Prerecorded audio-only has an equivalent transcript; prerecorded video-only has an equivalent time-based or text alternative as applicable.

checks.heading: Media, timing, flashing, and movement
checks.text: CORE-068 — Prerecorded synchronized media has accurate synchronized captions covering speech and meaningful non-speech audio, unless the specific media-alternative exception applies.

checks.heading: Media, timing, flashing, and movement
checks.text: CORE-069 — Essential visual information in prerecorded synchronized media has audio description at AA; a transcript alone does not replace 1.2.5. Evaluate the distinct A-level alternative under 1.2.3.

checks.heading: Media, timing, flashing, and movement
checks.text: CORE-070 — Live synchronized media has live captions at AA; assess usability of accuracy, delay, speaker changes and essential events.

checks.heading: Media, timing, flashing, and movement
checks.text: CORE-071 — Alternatives are discoverable, synchronized where needed, localized as applicable and equivalent to the currently published version.

checks.heading: Media, timing, flashing, and movement
checks.text: CORE-072 — Player controls, tracks, volume, speed, fullscreen and picture-in-picture work with supported inputs/AT; controls do not hide captions.

checks.heading: Media, timing, flashing, and movement
checks.text: CORE-073 — Automatically playing audio lasting over three seconds has required pause/stop or independently adjustable volume.

checks.heading: Media, timing, flashing, and movement
checks.text: CORE-074 — Moving/blinking/scrolling content starting automatically, lasting over five seconds and presented alongside content can be paused/stopped/hidden unless essential; assess auto-updating information separately.

checks.heading: Media, timing, flashing, and movement
checks.text: CORE-075 — Time limits can be turned off, adjusted or extended under 2.2.1 or a documented exception applies; warnings and extension actions are reachable in time.

checks.heading: Media, timing, flashing, and movement
checks.text: CORE-076 — Flashing meets the three-flashes-or-below-threshold criterion; do not expose testers to suspected dangerous flashing merely to gather evidence.

checks.heading: Media, timing, flashing, and movement
checks.text: CORE-077 — Reduced motion suppresses unnecessary parallax, zoom and smooth scrolling as enhanced guidance; map interaction animation to AAA 2.3.3 where applicable.

checks.heading: Media, timing, flashing, and movement
checks.text: CORE-078 — Disabling animation does not leave hidden content or never-completing transitions; movement can also be controlled where A/AA requires it.

checks.heading: Dynamic interfaces and robust exposure
checks.text: CORE-079 — Custom controls expose name, role, state/value; expanded, checked, selected, pressed and busy changes reach AT.

checks.heading: Dynamic interfaces and robust exposure
checks.text: CORE-080 — ARIA references resolve after hydration, repetition and rerendering; ARIA does not contradict native semantics or visible wording.

checks.heading: Dynamic interfaces and robust exposure
checks.text: CORE-081 — Status messages such as counts, saved changes, progress and outcomes are available programmatically without focus where 4.1.3 applies.

checks.heading: Dynamic interfaces and robust exposure
checks.text: CORE-082 — Live regions announce meaningful updates once at suitable urgency; clocks, tokens, typing and progress increments do not flood speech.

checks.heading: Dynamic interfaces and robust exposure
checks.text: CORE-083 — SPA routes update title, context and focus appropriately; back/forward and loading/error paths work with virtual navigation.

checks.heading: Dynamic interfaces and robust exposure
checks.text: CORE-084 — Lazy loading, virtualization and infinite scroll permit discovery of task-relevant content and access beyond the list, including the footer.

checks.heading: Dynamic interfaces and robust exposure
checks.text: CORE-085 — Skeleton, empty, offline and server-error states explain outcome and next action; busy states do not freeze navigation indefinitely.

checks.heading: Dynamic interfaces and robust exposure
checks.text: CORE-086 — Shadow DOM, portals, iframes and embeds preserve relationships, reading order, focus transitions and return behavior across boundaries.

checks.heading: Dynamic interfaces and robust exposure
checks.text: CORE-087 — Delayed widgets, ad refresh and personalization do not unexpectedly reorder tasks or replace focused controls.

checks.heading: Dynamic interfaces and robust exposure
checks.text: CORE-088 — Repeated controls/help use consistent identification/order where required; icons with different functions are distinguishable.

checks.heading: Cognitive usability and completion
checks.text: CORE-089 — Instructions explain prerequisites, steps, units and consequences before commitment; complex wording and abbreviations receive useful explanations as enhanced checks.

checks.heading: Cognitive usability and completion
checks.text: CORE-090 — Multi-step tasks show understandable progress, permit correction, preserve work through reasonable interruptions and explain unrecoverable loss.

checks.heading: Cognitive usability and completion
checks.text: CORE-091 — Alerts, upsells and chat invitations do not repeatedly interrupt reading or obscure correction controls; distinguish usability advice from criterion failures.

checks.heading: Cognitive usability and completion
checks.text: CORE-092 — Accessible support/reporting is discoverable; reporting a barrier does not require completing the inaccessible process.

checks.heading: Navigation, links, and disclosure
checks.text: CMP-001 — Ordinary site navigation uses links and disclosure buttons appropriately; a visual “menu” is not automatically an ARIA application menu requiring desktop-style keys.

checks.heading: Navigation, links, and disclosure
checks.text: CMP-002 — Mobile drawers have a named opener, exposed expanded state, logical focus entry/exit and a reachable close control; collapsed links are not tabbable off screen.

checks.heading: Navigation, links, and disclosure
checks.text: CMP-003 — Nested/mega navigation works by keyboard, pointer and touch; users can open subnavigation without being forced to follow its parent link.

checks.heading: Navigation, links, and disclosure
checks.text: CMP-004 — Current page, breadcrumbs and in-page location are understandable without relying on color; repeated navigation regions can be distinguished.

checks.heading: Navigation, links, and disclosure
checks.text: CMP-005 — Accordions expose button headings and expanded state; opening a section preserves focus, and collapsed contents do not receive focus. Test independent/multiple-open variants.

checks.heading: Navigation, links, and disclosure
checks.text: CMP-006 — Pagination identifies current page and meaningful previous/next actions; switching pages communicates new results and preserves a sensible reading/focus position.

checks.heading: Navigation, links, and disclosure
checks.text: CMP-007 — “Load more” reports appended content and permits users to reach it without traversing the entire preceding list again; loading failures leave retry usable.

checks.heading: Navigation, links, and disclosure
checks.text: CMP-008 — Context/action menus expose their trigger, menu items, enabled/disabled states and expected keyboard exit; focus returns meaningfully after selection or dismissal.

checks.heading: Dialogs, popovers, and overlays
checks.text: CMP-009 — A modal has an accessible name, suitable dialog semantics and initial focus that makes its purpose/content available; lengthy content is not read as one unusable description.

checks.heading: Dialogs, popovers, and overlays
checks.text: CMP-010 — Modal focus stays in the active dialog, background interaction is unavailable as intended, and keyboard/screen-reader users can complete or dismiss it. Test actual modality rather than assuming every dialog element is modal.

checks.heading: Dialogs, popovers, and overlays
checks.text: CMP-011 — Closing a dialog returns focus to its opener or a logical successor when the opener no longer exists; background scroll and reading position recover.

checks.heading: Dialogs, popovers, and overlays
checks.text: CMP-012 — Nested dialogs, confirmations and provider overlays do not create competing focus loops, invisible active dialogs or accidental closure of both layers.

checks.heading: Dialogs, popovers, and overlays
checks.text: CMP-013 — Short viewports, high zoom and virtual keyboards allow dialog content and actions to scroll into view; sticky action rows do not cover fields.

checks.heading: Dialogs, popovers, and overlays
checks.text: CMP-014 — Nonmodal popovers do not trap focus as if modal; dismissal and return behavior match the chosen pattern, with no invisible focusable leftovers.

checks.heading: Dialogs, popovers, and overlays
checks.text: CMP-015 — Tooltips supplement rather than replace a control's accessible name; they open on focus as appropriate and satisfy hover/focus-content conditions.

checks.heading: Dialogs, popovers, and overlays
checks.text: CMP-016 — Toasts communicate relevant status without stealing focus; essential recovery actions remain available long enough or in a persistent location.

checks.heading: Choice, tabs, and composite widgets
checks.text: CMP-017 — Checkboxes expose checked/unchecked/mixed state; clicking a label works; mixed-state parent behavior matches actual child selection.

checks.heading: Choice, tabs, and composite widgets
checks.text: CMP-018 — Radio groups have a group name and understandable selected option; arrow navigation and focus entry follow the chosen native/custom pattern.

checks.heading: Choice, tabs, and composite widgets
checks.text: CMP-019 — Switches and toggle buttons expose current state and keep stable names where appropriate; state changes are not conveyed by color alone.

checks.heading: Choice, tabs, and composite widgets
checks.text: CMP-020 — Tabs expose tablist, tabs and associated panels; selection, focus, orientation and roving tabindex match the pattern; panel content remains reachable.

checks.heading: Choice, tabs, and composite widgets
checks.text: CMP-021 — Automatic tab activation is usable without disruptive latency; manual activation supports expected activation keys. Removing/reordering tabs leaves a meaningful active tab.

checks.heading: Choice, tabs, and composite widgets
checks.text: CMP-022 — Listboxes expose selected/focused options distinctly; single/multiselect keyboard behavior, labeling and selection updates are usable.

checks.heading: Choice, tabs, and composite widgets
checks.text: CMP-023 — Comboboxes expose name, value and expanded state; popup navigation, selection, cancellation and editable-text keys do not conflict.

checks.heading: Choice, tabs, and composite widgets
checks.text: CMP-024 — Autocomplete announces useful results/loading/no-results without excess speech; typed text is not silently overwritten, and manual entry remains usable where intended.

checks.heading: Choice, tabs, and composite widgets
checks.text: CMP-025 — Multi-select chips have named remove actions, predictable focus after removal and understandable selection count; Backspace does not unexpectedly erase unrelated content.

checks.heading: Choice, tabs, and composite widgets
checks.text: CMP-026 — Tree views expose hierarchy, expanded state and selection; parent/child traversal and lazy-loaded nodes work; hidden descendants do not remain reachable.

checks.heading: Choice, tabs, and composite widgets
checks.text: CMP-027 — Toolbars have an intelligible name and navigation model; roving focus does not make controls undiscoverable or interfere with text/slider keys.

checks.heading: Date, numeric, search, and input controls
checks.text: CMP-028 — Date pickers provide usable typed entry where appropriate, clear localized format instructions, calendar navigation and announced month/year changes.

checks.heading: Date, numeric, search, and input controls
checks.text: CMP-029 — Calendar grids identify full dates, today, selection and unavailable dates without color alone; month/year crossing and focus return work.

checks.heading: Date, numeric, search, and input controls
checks.text: CMP-030 — Date ranges, timezones, daylight-saving boundaries and invalid end-before-start states have understandable feedback and correction.

checks.heading: Date, numeric, search, and input controls
checks.text: CMP-031 — Sliders expose name, current value, limits and useful value text; keyboard and non-drag single-pointer adjustment work, including touch screen-reader use.

checks.heading: Date, numeric, search, and input controls
checks.text: CMP-032 — Dual-thumb sliders identify each endpoint; thumbs remain distinguishable, values do not cross unexpectedly, and zoom does not hide their values.

checks.heading: Date, numeric, search, and input controls
checks.text: CMP-033 — Spinbuttons and quantity controls support direct entry or suitable alternatives, boundaries, invalid values and announced value changes without duplicate submissions.

checks.heading: Date, numeric, search, and input controls
checks.text: CMP-034 — Search supports submission, clearing, suggestion dismissal and no-results recovery; clear buttons are named and do not unexpectedly clear unrelated filters.

checks.heading: Date, numeric, search, and input controls
checks.text: CMP-035 — Password reveal exposes its action/state, preserves value/focus and does not break autofill; strength guidance is available without color or repeated intrusive announcements.

checks.heading: Date, numeric, search, and input controls
checks.text: CMP-036 — Rich-text editors expose editing area and formatting states; toolbar operation returns to the editing context and does not trap keyboard users in the editor.

checks.heading: Date, numeric, search, and input controls
checks.text: CMP-037 — Formatting, mentions, emoji, slash commands and link dialogs are available without inaccessible popups; authoring tools allow headings, lists and alternatives for published content.

checks.heading: Date, numeric, search, and input controls
checks.text: CMP-038 — Code editors expose a usable editing/reading mode, instructions for leaving Tab indentation mode, diagnostics and accessible equivalent interactions when needed.

checks.heading: Tables, grids, charts, and spatial interfaces
checks.text: CMP-039 — Data tables expose headers and associations for simple, row-header, multilevel and irregular layouts; captions/context explain their purpose.

checks.heading: Tables, grids, charts, and spatial interfaces
checks.text: CMP-040 — Sorting controls identify the column and current sort; sorting leaves focus stable and communicates the new state.

checks.heading: Tables, grids, charts, and spatial interfaces
checks.text: CMP-041 — Responsive tables/cards preserve header/value relationships and reading sequence; horizontal scrolling of a qualifying table does not force the whole page to scroll both ways.

checks.heading: Tables, grids, charts, and spatial interfaces
checks.text: CMP-042 — Interactive grids implement a deliberate cell/row navigation model; entering/exiting edit mode, selecting rows and operating cell controls are possible without a pointer.

checks.heading: Tables, grids, charts, and spatial interfaces
checks.text: CMP-043 — Virtualized grids expose row/column information accurately where supported; offscreen data can be reached and read; row recycling does not move focus to a different record silently.

checks.heading: Tables, grids, charts, and spatial interfaces
checks.text: CMP-044 — Bulk selection reports scope, including “all matching” versus “this page”; destructive bulk actions offer applicable checking/confirmation/reversal and retain meaningful focus.

checks.heading: Tables, grids, charts, and spatial interfaces
checks.text: CMP-045 — Charts provide a concise summary and equivalent task-relevant data/relationships; axes, units, legends, filters and series are understandable without color alone.

checks.heading: Tables, grids, charts, and spatial interfaces
checks.text: CMP-046 — Interactive chart tooltips and data points work through supported non-pointer paths without thousands of unusable Tab stops; chart filters also update accessible equivalents.

checks.heading: Tables, grids, charts, and spatial interfaces
checks.text: CMP-047 — Maps have task-equivalent address/search/list or other interfaces where possible; markers, zoom and directions are named and operable without drag-only panning.

checks.heading: Tables, grids, charts, and spatial interfaces
checks.text: CMP-048 — Diagram editors, whiteboards and canvas tools expose meaningful objects, selections and editing alternatives; distinguish genuinely essential path-dependent actions from ordinary controls.

checks.heading: Tables, grids, charts, and spatial interfaces
checks.text: CMP-049 — Math and scientific notation remain understandable with the selected AT and output formats; do not assume a screenshot, raw markup or alt text alone supports the required task.

checks.heading: Reordering, carousels, and feedback
checks.text: CMP-050 — Sortable lists and kanban cards support non-drag click/tap movement as well as keyboard access; item/destination/order changes are communicated.

checks.heading: Reordering, carousels, and feedback
checks.text: CMP-051 — Reordering an item preserves focus on that item or a useful control; undo and first/last positions work without impossible moves.

checks.heading: Reordering, carousels, and feedback
checks.text: CMP-052 — Carousels have named controls and understandable slide position; automatic rotation can be controlled where required and hidden slides do not contain stray focus stops.

checks.heading: Reordering, carousels, and feedback
checks.text: CMP-053 — Carousel changes preserve reading/focus appropriately; announcing every auto-rotating slide does not overwhelm speech.

checks.heading: Reordering, carousels, and feedback
checks.text: CMP-054 — Progress bars expose meaningful name/value where determinate; indeterminate activity is distinguishable from completed or failed work.

checks.heading: Reordering, carousels, and feedback
checks.text: CMP-055 — Skeletons are not repeated as fake content in AT; loading completion and failure leave the actual content and retry discoverable.

checks.heading: Reordering, carousels, and feedback
checks.text: CMP-056 — Alerts and error summaries have appropriate urgency and linking; focus and live-region strategies do not announce the same long message repeatedly.

checks.heading: Reordering, carousels, and feedback
checks.text: CMP-057 — Rating/review controls expose the scale, each option and selected value; hover preview is not the only way to determine the rating.

checks.heading: Reordering, carousels, and feedback
checks.text: CMP-058 — Steppers/wizards expose current/completed/available steps; returning to edit and moving forward preserves values and a sensible focus destination.

checks.heading: Embedded and less common controls
checks.text: CMP-059 — File drop zones expose a real selection mechanism; progress, per-file errors, previews and remove/cancel actions remain usable for large batches.

checks.heading: Embedded and less common controls
checks.text: CMP-060 — Color pickers expose usable named values or equivalent entry, selected state and non-drag adjustment; color alone does not identify saved swatches.

checks.heading: Embedded and less common controls
checks.text: CMP-061 — Audio recording and camera capture expose permission, start/stop, elapsed state, review, retry and alternate upload paths appropriate to the task.

checks.heading: Embedded and less common controls
checks.text: CMP-062 — Resizable panes have non-drag alternatives where required and do not hide critical controls at minimum size; splitters expose usable orientation/value if interactive.

checks.heading: Embedded and less common controls
checks.text: CMP-063 — Iframes have meaningful titles and usable content; focus can enter/exit provider controls without trapping, disappearing or skipping required fields.

checks.heading: Embedded and less common controls
checks.text: CMP-064 — Consent preference panels expose categories, states, links and save outcomes; all offered choices are operable and dismissal does not leave a blocked page.

checks.heading: Embedded and less common controls
checks.text: CMP-065 — Starred/saved items, reaction controls and counters distinguish action from current state and announce changes without replacing their accessible name unpredictably.

checks.heading: Embedded and less common controls
checks.text: CMP-066 — Notifications lists distinguish read/unread, provide meaningful timestamps and preserve position when items arrive or are dismissed.

checks.heading: Embedded and less common controls
checks.text: CMP-067 — Download/export controls identify relevant format/context and communicate queued, ready, expired and failed states; accessible data is not lost in the exported artifact.

checks.heading: Embedded and less common controls
checks.text: CMP-068 — Web components retain labels and focus indicators across shadow boundaries; slot changes, hydration and component upgrades do not break interaction.

checks.heading: Accounts and identity
checks.text: JRN-001 — Registration works from invitation/entry through validation, consent, verification and first login; activation email content and expired-link recovery are accessible.

checks.heading: Accounts and identity
checks.text: JRN-002 — Login works with password managers and paste; show-password, remember-me and alternative sign-in choices remain understandable and operable.

checks.heading: Accounts and identity
checks.text: JRN-003 — MFA handles paste/autofill, whole-code input, expiry, resend, alternative factor and unavailable-device recovery without unnecessary cognitive barriers.

checks.heading: Accounts and identity
checks.text: JRN-004 — Passkeys, SSO and cross-device redirects preserve context and provide usable failure/cancel/retry paths; record OS/provider boundaries explicitly.

checks.heading: Accounts and identity
checks.text: JRN-005 — Password reset and account recovery work without remembering inaccessible prior data or relying on a single sensory challenge.

checks.heading: Accounts and identity
checks.text: JRN-006 — Session warnings are announced and reachable; extension follows the selected criterion and documented exceptions. Reauthentication does not silently destroy work; separately assess AAA preservation.

checks.heading: Accounts and identity
checks.text: JRN-007 — Profile changes, email changes, logout, account export and deletion have usable verification and outcomes; destructive changes meet applicable error prevention.

checks.heading: Accounts and identity
checks.text: JRN-008 — Identity/document/biometric checks include a usable route for relevant impairments; examine camera alignment, movement, audio prompts and manual-review alternatives.

checks.heading: Commerce, payments, and booking
checks.text: JRN-009 — Users can discover products through search/navigation and operate filters, sorting, comparison and no-results recovery without pointer-only actions.

checks.heading: Commerce, payments, and booking
checks.text: JRN-010 — Variants, swatches, availability, price changes, subscription intervals and size guides are understandable without color or images alone.

checks.heading: Commerce, payments, and booking
checks.text: JRN-011 — Add-to-cart announces item/quantity outcome and supports continue-shopping or checkout without unexpected focus loss.

checks.heading: Commerce, payments, and booking
checks.text: JRN-012 — Cart quantity edits, removal, undo, coupons, errors and total changes are accessible; out-of-stock changes do not strand the user.

checks.heading: Commerce, payments, and booking
checks.text: JRN-013 — Guest/account checkout, saved addresses, address lookup/manual entry and billing/shipping reuse preserve information and expose errors.

checks.heading: Commerce, payments, and booking
checks.text: JRN-014 — Shipping options, fees, taxes, delivery dates and recurring terms are available before commitment and after changes.

checks.heading: Commerce, payments, and booking
checks.text: JRN-015 — Payment fields, provider iframes, wallet redirects and step-up challenges work through success, decline, timeout and cancellation. Use sandbox/test transactions where available.

checks.heading: Commerce, payments, and booking
checks.text: JRN-016 — Order review permits checking/correction under applicable error prevention; confirmation, receipt and order history are readable and accessible.

checks.heading: Commerce, payments, and booking
checks.text: JRN-017 — Refund, cancellation, subscription pause and returns are as testable as purchase; inaccessible support is not the only recovery route.

checks.heading: Commerce, payments, and booking
checks.text: JRN-018 — Booking calendars, availability grids, seat/room choices and timezones have equivalent nonvisual/non-drag operations; held-slot expiry is announced and recoverable.

checks.heading: Search, content, and communication
checks.text: JRN-019 — Search supports query entry, suggestions, count, results, pagination and no-results actions; updated counts do not steal focus or overwhelm speech.

checks.heading: Search, content, and communication
checks.text: JRN-020 — Articles/documentation expose meaningful heading structure, anchors, code snippets, footnotes, glossary and copy controls across narrow layouts.

checks.heading: Search, content, and communication
checks.text: JRN-021 — Paywalls, newsletter overlays, age gates, ads and consent do not create traps or hide required reading/close controls at zoom.

checks.heading: Search, content, and communication
checks.text: JRN-022 — Comments, reviews and user-generated media have accessible input, moderation feedback, reporting and authoring guidance for alternatives/captions.

checks.heading: Search, content, and communication
checks.text: JRN-023 — Chat/support permits opening, composing, sending, reviewing history, attachments, closing and returning to the host task; incoming messages do not continuously interrupt.

checks.heading: Search, content, and communication
checks.text: JRN-024 — Audio/video calls expose join, mute, captions, participant status, chat and device errors; assess accessible alternatives for essential communication tasks.

checks.heading: Search, content, and communication
checks.text: JRN-025 — Email and transactional messages have logical order, meaningful links, readable contrast and alternatives; critical actions do not depend on image loading.

checks.heading: Search, content, and communication
checks.text: JRN-026 — Notification settings, language choices, unsubscribe and support escalation work with keyboard, screen reader and mobile touch.

checks.heading: SaaS, administration, and data-heavy tasks
checks.text: JRN-027 — Onboarding/tutorials are skippable or otherwise usable, preserve context and do not require a visual spotlight or drag gesture to proceed.

checks.heading: SaaS, administration, and data-heavy tasks
checks.text: JRN-028 — Dashboards expose current metrics, time ranges, trends and equivalent data; refreshed data and filters keep summaries/tables synchronized.

checks.heading: SaaS, administration, and data-heavy tasks
checks.text: JRN-029 — Create/edit/delete records, inline editing, selection and bulk actions work across empty, large, filtered and permission-limited datasets.

checks.heading: SaaS, administration, and data-heavy tasks
checks.text: JRN-030 — Long forms/autosave communicate pending, saved, conflict and failed states; recovery does not require finding an invisible transient toast.

checks.heading: SaaS, administration, and data-heavy tasks
checks.text: JRN-031 — Import workflows expose column matching, row errors, progress, cancel/retry and accessible result reports; invalid files do not erase configuration.

checks.heading: SaaS, administration, and data-heavy tasks
checks.text: JRN-032 — Collaboration communicates edits, mentions, presence and conflicts without excessive announcements; focus does not follow other users' cursors.

checks.heading: SaaS, administration, and data-heavy tasks
checks.text: JRN-033 — Role/permission differences do not produce unnamed disabled controls, unreachable actions or silent authorization failures.

checks.heading: SaaS, administration, and data-heavy tasks
checks.text: JRN-034 — Settings changes, theme previews and personalization remain usable before and after saving; resetting settings can recover from a broken configuration.

checks.heading: SaaS, administration, and data-heavy tasks
checks.text: JRN-035 — Data exports, print views and generated reports preserve labels, reading order and data equivalence rather than flattening essential information into images.

checks.heading: Mobile web, native apps, and kiosks
checks.text: JRN-036 — Mobile screen-reader exploration/swiping reaches every required element; touch activation does not depend on inaccessible hover or custom gestures.

checks.heading: Mobile web, native apps, and kiosks
checks.text: JRN-037 — Virtual keyboards, safe-area insets, bottom sheets and browser chrome do not cover active inputs, errors or primary actions; scrolling reveals them.

checks.heading: Mobile web, native apps, and kiosks
checks.text: JRN-038 — Orientation changes and responsive breakpoints preserve entered data, current step, reading order and focused content.

checks.heading: Mobile web, native apps, and kiosks
checks.text: JRN-039 — Voice control can select visible controls by label; switch access has a practical scanning order and a usable route through composite controls.

checks.heading: Mobile web, native apps, and kiosks
checks.text: JRN-040 — Native app scope includes platform text scaling, AT semantics/actions, external keyboard, reduced motion, contrast and permission dialogs; commission platform-specific verification.

checks.heading: Mobile web, native apps, and kiosks
checks.text: JRN-041 — Webviews preserve semantics and focus across native/web boundaries; app links, external authentication and return-to-app failures have usable recovery.

checks.heading: Mobile web, native apps, and kiosks
checks.text: JRN-042 — Kiosk/hardware scope records physical reach, tactile/audio output, privacy, timeouts, payment hardware and accessible assistance; a web-only pass cannot settle these requirements.

checks.heading: Documents and downloadable artifacts
checks.text: JRN-043 — Inventory PDFs, office files, slide decks, spreadsheets, certificates, tickets, invoices and attachments required by a task; identify authoring and export owners.

checks.heading: Documents and downloadable artifacts
checks.text: JRN-044 — PDFs have correct tags, language, title, reading order, headings, lists, links, alternatives and table associations; verify with AT, not only a checker.

checks.heading: Documents and downloadable artifacts
checks.text: JRN-045 — Scanned documents receive accurate recognition and structure as needed; OCR alone does not prove usable headings, order, tables or form fields.

checks.heading: Documents and downloadable artifacts
checks.text: JRN-046 — Fillable documents expose names, instructions, logical tab order, error handling and signatures; submitting, saving and reopening preserve usability.

checks.heading: Documents and downloadable artifacts
checks.text: JRN-047 — Office files use meaningful styles, slide order, alt text, table structure and labels; spreadsheet meaning does not depend on color, merged cells or unexplained coordinates alone.

checks.heading: Documents and downloadable artifacts
checks.text: JRN-048 — Accessible HTML or other alternatives are equivalent, current and discoverable before an inaccessible download; record when additional PDF/UA or document standards are in scope.

checks.heading: Documents and downloadable artifacts
checks.text: JRN-049 — Generate and inspect artifacts from realistic long, localized and missing-data records; a manually repaired sample does not prove the export generator is fixed.

checks.heading: AI and conversational interfaces
checks.text: JRN-050 — Prompt input, attachment, send, stop, retry, edit and regenerate are named and operable; submitting does not erase the only accessible copy of the prompt.

checks.heading: AI and conversational interfaces
checks.text: JRN-051 — Streaming responses have a readable final structure and useful completion/error feedback; token-by-token announcements do not overwhelm speech.

checks.heading: AI and conversational interfaces
checks.text: JRN-052 — Auto-scroll respects users reading earlier content; history, references and newly generated controls remain discoverable without forced focus jumps.

checks.heading: AI and conversational interfaces
checks.text: JRN-053 — Generated tables, code, citations, math and images expose usable structure/alternatives; copy and export preserve task-relevant meaning.

checks.heading: AI and conversational interfaces
checks.text: JRN-054 — Generated choices, tool approvals, refusals, rate limits and connection failures expose clear outcomes and recovery without color or hidden affordances alone.

checks.heading: AI and conversational interfaces
checks.text: JRN-055 — Speech input/output has usable text alternatives and controls as applicable; microphone permissions, playback, interruption and errors are understandable.

checks.heading: AI and conversational interfaces
checks.text: JRN-056 — Model outputs do not silently overwrite user-provided alternatives, headings or labels; generated content is reviewed before publication and assessed in its final rendered form.

checks.heading: Specialist and high-impact services
checks.text: JRN-057 — Education/exams cover equations, timed sections, autosave, accommodations, answers, review and submission; document genuine timing exceptions rather than assuming all exams qualify.

checks.heading: Specialist and high-impact services
checks.text: JRN-058 — Healthcare tasks cover appointments, patient forms, results/charts, secure messages and remote consultations with accessible confidentiality and recovery.

checks.heading: Specialist and high-impact services
checks.text: JRN-059 — Public-service/benefit/job applications cover eligibility, evidence uploads, signatures, save/resume, deadline messaging and accessible decision documents.

checks.heading: Specialist and high-impact services
checks.text: JRN-060 — Finance covers balance/trend interpretation, transfers, payee verification, fees, transaction review and statement access; step-up security remains within the audited process.

checks.heading: Specialist and high-impact services
checks.text: JRN-061 — Travel covers route search, date/time changes, passenger assistance, seat selection, disruption notices, check-in and accessible boarding documents.

checks.heading: Specialist and high-impact services
checks.text: JRN-062 — Games/immersive experiences record remapping, sensory alternatives, captions, difficulty/timing choices, motion and safe flash handling; identify separate specialist scope rather than implying WCAG covers everything.

checks.heading: Localization, providers, and resilience
checks.text: JRN-063 — Each supported locale has correct language, translated accessible names, date/number formats and usable long labels; mixed-language content is identified appropriately.

checks.heading: Localization, providers, and resilience
checks.text: JRN-064 — Right-to-left and bidirectional content preserve meaningful reading/focus sequence, currency, identifiers and editing; visual mirroring does not corrupt semantics.

checks.heading: Localization, providers, and resilience
checks.text: JRN-065 — Third-party consent, payments, CAPTCHA, maps, chat, analytics UI and embedded documents are tested in the host context; record provider/version and escalation owner.

checks.heading: Localization, providers, and resilience
checks.text: JRN-066 — Network interruption, slow loading, duplicate submission and stale sessions produce accessible outcomes and recovery without silently losing completed work.

checks.heading: Localization, providers, and resilience
checks.text: JRN-067 — Feature flags, A/B variants and personalization receive relevant checks; a passing default variant does not cover inaccessible alternatives served to real users.

checks.heading: Localization, providers, and resilience
checks.text: JRN-068 — User support can accept accessibility reports and provide timely assistance; reporting forms, statements and contact channels are themselves usable.

checks.heading: Remediation and acceptance
checks.text: Original failing task succeeds using [configuration/input].

checks.heading: Remediation and acceptance
checks.text: Relevant semantics/state/focus/feedback satisfy [specific conditions].

checks.heading: Remediation and acceptance
checks.text: Relevant error/narrow/theme/localized/sibling cases checked: [ ].

checks.heading: Remediation and acceptance
checks.text: Complete affected process and relevant regressions checked: [ ].

checks.heading: System boundaries and accountability
checks.text: **GOV-01 — Feature inventory.** Compare source routes, feature flags, provider dashboards, scheduled jobs, integrations, and deployed user journeys.

checks.heading: System boundaries and accountability
checks.text: **GOV-02 — Task contract.** Ask the product owner for supported tasks, prohibited uses, success criteria, and non-AI alternatives; run representative journeys.

checks.heading: System boundaries and accountability
checks.text: **GOV-03 — Trust and data-flow map.** Follow one request through preprocessing, models, retrieval, tools, output rendering, telemetry, and downstream consumers.

checks.heading: System boundaries and accountability
checks.text: **GOV-04 — Affected people and harm.** Review credible misuse, error consequences, scale, vulnerable audiences, and indirect effects with domain owners.

checks.heading: System boundaries and accountability
checks.text: **GOV-05 — Responsibility and competence.** Trace who can approve data use, model changes, consequential actions, incidents, and risk acceptance.

checks.heading: System boundaries and accountability
checks.text: **GOV-06 — Applicable obligations.** Inventory markets, user groups, sector, contractual commitments, and provider terms; obtain competent review where needed.

checks.heading: System boundaries and accountability
checks.text: **GOV-07 — Third-party capabilities.** Inspect embedded assistants, browser extensions, SaaS AI switches, and vendor subprocessors relevant to the feature.

checks.heading: Data permissions and lifecycle
checks.text: **GOV-08 — Approved inputs.** Compare permitted classifications with real prompts, uploads, OCR, retrieval, embeddings, and tool results using synthetic records.

checks.heading: Data permissions and lifecycle
checks.text: **GOV-09 — Minimization and redaction.** Seed synthetic identifiers and secrets in structured fields, free text, attachments, metadata, and nested tool responses.

checks.heading: Data permissions and lifecycle
checks.text: **GOV-10 — Provider data settings.** Inspect actual account, project, endpoint, region, training-use, retention, and subprocessor settings against the approved data flow.

checks.heading: Data permissions and lifecycle
checks.text: **GOV-11 — Retention and deletion.** Delete a synthetic subject and track source records, histories, files, vectors, caches, feedback, exports, and recoverable backups.

checks.heading: Data permissions and lifecycle
checks.text: **GOV-12 — Permissions after revocation.** Revoke access, remove group membership, disable an account, and replay a previously valid conversation or document reference.

checks.heading: Data permissions and lifecycle
checks.text: **GOV-13 — Sensitive inferences.** Test requests to infer sensitive traits or private facts from incomplete evidence and ordinary metadata.

checks.heading: Data permissions and lifecycle
checks.text: **GOV-14 — Feedback and training reuse.** Trace thumbs-up feedback, support exports, human labels, and accepted outputs into analytics, evaluation, and training stores.

checks.heading: Data permissions and lifecycle
checks.text: **GOV-15 — Residency and fallback.** Exercise primary failure and inspect traffic, logs, temporary files, and alternate provider routes.

checks.heading: Data permissions and lifecycle
checks.text: **GOV-16 — Diagnostic access.** Review support impersonation, prompt inspection, administrator queries, and export permissions.

checks.heading: Human control and user expectations
checks.text: **GOV-17 — AI disclosure and limits.** Inspect onboarding, generated artifacts, consequential screens, and sales claims in supported languages.

checks.heading: Human control and user expectations
checks.text: **GOV-18 — Human review effectiveness.** Have a reviewer handle realistic errors with source evidence, uncertainty, workload, and a deadline.

checks.heading: Human control and user expectations
checks.text: **GOV-19 — Appeal and correction.** Submit a harmful or incorrect output through the actual reporting, correction, and appeal workflow.

checks.heading: Human control and user expectations
checks.text: **GOV-20 — Risk acceptance.** Inspect unresolved controls and compare exceptions with current exposure, compensating controls, and release conditions.

checks.heading: Human control and user expectations
checks.text: **GOV-21 — Decommissioning.** Retire a synthetic feature and inspect routing, jobs, API keys, indexes, stored content, and user exports.

checks.heading: Prompt injection and information boundaries
checks.text: **SEC-01 — Direct instruction attacks.** Try role spoofing, claimed administrator authority, instruction replacement, and requests for forbidden actions through the real API and UI.

checks.heading: Prompt injection and information boundaries
checks.text: **SEC-02 — Indirect instruction attacks.** Place harmless canary instructions in retrieved pages, uploads, emails, issue text, repository comments, and tool results.

checks.heading: Prompt injection and information boundaries
checks.text: **SEC-03 — Multimodal instruction attacks.** Embed synthetic instructions in image text, PDF layers, OCR, audio transcription, subtitles, and metadata where supported.

checks.heading: Prompt injection and information boundaries
checks.text: **SEC-04 — Encoded and fragmented attacks.** Try Unicode variants, supported languages, encoded content, split messages, and long-context placement.

checks.heading: Prompt injection and information boundaries
checks.text: **SEC-05 — Multi-turn escalation.** Build a benign conversation, introduce a hostile document, request compaction, then resume or branch the session.

checks.heading: Prompt injection and information boundaries
checks.text: **SEC-06 — Exfiltration through output channels.** Request canary disclosure in links, remote image URLs, citations, logs, generated filenames, or tool arguments.

checks.heading: Prompt injection and information boundaries
checks.text: **SEC-07 — Prompt and configuration exposure.** Ask for hidden prompts, credentials, internal routes, and operational context; inspect actual secret placement.

checks.heading: Prompt injection and information boundaries
checks.text: **SEC-08 — Safety control failure.** Force a classifier timeout, parser error, moderation outage, or unsupported language in an isolated environment.

checks.heading: Tool authorization and execution
checks.text: **SEC-09 — Identity propagation.** Forge user, tenant, role, conversation, and resource identifiers in model-generated tool arguments.

checks.heading: Tool authorization and execution
checks.text: **SEC-10 — Least privilege.** Inspect credentials and attempt actions outside the tool's required resource and operation scope.

checks.heading: Tool authorization and execution
checks.text: **SEC-11 — Argument validation.** Submit unknown fields, type confusion, nested objects, oversized values, invalid currency, and forbidden destinations.

checks.heading: Tool authorization and execution
checks.text: **SEC-12 — Command and query boundaries.** Request path traversal, shell metacharacters, destructive SQL, unsafe code imports, and unrestricted filesystem access in a sandbox.

checks.heading: Tool authorization and execution
checks.text: **SEC-13 — URL and network access.** Use local stub targets to exercise private-address URLs, alternate schemes, redirects, DNS changes, and unexpected egress.

checks.heading: Tool authorization and execution
checks.text: **SEC-14 — Approval binding.** Approve one synthetic action, then alter recipient, amount, target, attachment, or material consequences before execution.

checks.heading: Tool authorization and execution
checks.text: **SEC-15 — Authorization freshness.** Queue or pause a job, revoke access or change the target state, then resume it.

checks.heading: Tool authorization and execution
checks.text: **SEC-16 — Idempotent actions.** Simulate timeout after a successful write and retry the same tool call or workflow.

checks.heading: Tool authorization and execution
