checks.text: **SEC-17 — Preview and commit.** Compare displayed recipients, diffs, affected records, and totals with the eventual action payload.

checks.heading: Tool authorization and execution
checks.text: **SEC-18 — Delegation and tool discovery.** Exercise agent handoffs, newly discovered tools, connector metadata, and dynamically changed schemas.

checks.heading: Tool authorization and execution
checks.text: **SEC-19 — Sandbox escape and artifact handling.** Have code tools produce symlinks, network requests, executable files, and cross-workspace references in a disposable environment.

checks.heading: Tool authorization and execution
checks.text: **SEC-20 — Cancellation and runaway agents.** Create a non-progressing plan with nested calls, retries, concurrent workers, and external jobs; cancel it.

checks.heading: Tool authorization and execution
checks.text: **SEC-21 — Asynchronous result mix-up.** Return two users' tool responses out of order and replay a stale callback with synthetic identifiers.

checks.heading: Output handling and application exposure
checks.text: **SEC-22 — Generated markup and links.** Render outputs containing script attempts, unsafe URL schemes, remote images, HTML attributes, and Markdown edge cases.

checks.heading: Output handling and application exposure
checks.text: **SEC-23 — Executable output.** Pass generated code, SQL, formulas, templates, and configuration through actual downstream consumers using harmless canaries.

checks.heading: Output handling and application exposure
checks.text: **SEC-24 — Hidden entry points.** Compare browser, mobile, batch, retry, internal API, webhooks, and older client paths.

checks.heading: Output handling and application exposure
checks.text: **SEC-25 — Abuse and extraction.** Exercise bounded synthetic scraping, repeated reconstruction queries, and automated account traffic.

checks.heading: Isolation and lifecycle
checks.text: **RAG-01 — Authorization before model exposure.** Create tenants A and B with unique private canaries; search as A using B IDs, semantic paraphrases, filters, and file references.

checks.heading: Isolation and lifecycle
checks.text: **RAG-02 — Permission filter integrity.** Tamper with tenant metadata, document filters, namespace IDs, direct vector lookups, and pagination tokens.

checks.heading: Isolation and lifecycle
checks.text: **RAG-03 — Shared and private content.** Mix public documents, private annotations, shared folders, and nested group permissions.

checks.heading: Isolation and lifecycle
checks.text: **RAG-04 — Cache isolation.** Warm semantic, exact-match, embedding, and response caches as one actor, then query as another with different access.

checks.heading: Isolation and lifecycle
checks.text: **RAG-05 — Deletion and revocation propagation.** Delete a source or revoke access; query old snippets, citation URLs, cached answers, and resumed conversations.

checks.heading: Isolation and lifecycle
checks.text: **RAG-06 — Conversation ownership.** Enumerate synthetic conversation, branch, attachment, and resume identifiers with another user identity.

checks.heading: Isolation and lifecycle
checks.text: **RAG-07 — Memory write permission.** Ask the assistant to remember private facts about another person or modify shared organization memory.

checks.heading: Isolation and lifecycle
checks.text: **RAG-08 — Memory correction and poisoning.** Insert a false persistent preference or hostile instruction; inspect, correct, and delete it through user controls.

checks.heading: Isolation and lifecycle
checks.text: **RAG-09 — Summary preservation.** Force truncation, summarization, migration, and session restoration with conflicting instructions and restricted records.

checks.heading: Ingestion and source integrity
checks.text: **RAG-10 — Source admission.** Add content from an unauthorized connector, hostile domain, or writable shared location.

checks.heading: Ingestion and source integrity
checks.text: **RAG-11 — Parser and file boundaries.** Use malformed files, compressed expansion, enormous tables, encrypted documents, and unsupported encodings with bounded fixtures.

checks.heading: Ingestion and source integrity
checks.text: **RAG-12 — Chunk and metadata correctness.** Inspect documents with headings, tables, footnotes, conflicting versions, and inherited access labels.

checks.heading: Ingestion and source integrity
checks.text: **RAG-13 — Poisoned and duplicate documents.** Seed synthetic false answers in repeated documents and highly ranked snippets; compare ranking and final claims.

checks.heading: Ingestion and source integrity
checks.text: **RAG-14 — Freshness and tombstones.** Update, rename, move, and withdraw a source; query before and after ingestion completes.

checks.heading: Ingestion and source integrity
checks.text: **RAG-15 — Embedding and index migration.** Change embedding versions, chunking, dimensions, or rerankers in a disposable index.

checks.heading: Ingestion and source integrity
checks.text: **RAG-16 — Evidence provenance.** Trace an answer through chunk IDs to the original document and authorized source version.

checks.heading: Retrieval and answer fitness
checks.text: **RAG-17 — Relevant evidence retrieval.** Run an annotated set of answerable questions with expected source documents and permitted access.

checks.heading: Retrieval and answer fitness
checks.text: **RAG-18 — Unanswerable questions.** Ask about missing, private, outdated, and out-of-scope facts that sound plausible.

checks.heading: Retrieval and answer fitness
checks.text: **RAG-19 — Conflicting sources.** Provide authoritative and low-quality sources with different dates, jurisdictions, or product versions.

checks.heading: Retrieval and answer fitness
checks.text: **RAG-20 — Citation entailment.** Check individual material claims against the exact retrieved passages, including numbers, quotations, and negations.

checks.heading: Retrieval and answer fitness
checks.text: **RAG-21 — Query transformation.** Test rewritten, translated, decomposed, and multi-hop queries with names, dates, negation, and access restrictions.

checks.heading: Retrieval and answer fitness
checks.text: **RAG-22 — Context pressure.** Place needed evidence at different positions among distractors, near token limits, and across many documents.

checks.heading: Retrieval and answer fitness
checks.text: **RAG-23 — Source access at display.** Open citations as the current user after sharing, revocation, or a signed-link expiry.

checks.heading: Task and factual correctness
checks.text: **QUA-01 — Task completion.** Run representative end-to-end tasks with verifiable expected outcomes, constraints, and required artifacts.

checks.heading: Task and factual correctness
checks.text: **QUA-02 — Instruction and scope adherence.** Use requests with priorities, exclusions, exact formats, and a late user correction.

checks.heading: Task and factual correctness
checks.text: **QUA-03 — Factual and temporal claims.** Ask questions involving dates, versions, changing facts, unavailable evidence, and authoritative sources.

checks.heading: Task and factual correctness
checks.text: **QUA-04 — Numerical correctness.** Test totals, percentages, units, currency, time zones, date boundaries, rounding, and negative values.

checks.heading: Task and factual correctness
checks.text: **QUA-05 — Structured output.** Exercise missing fields, unknown enum values, nested arrays, nulls, incomplete streams, and schema upgrades.

checks.heading: Task and factual correctness
checks.text: **QUA-06 — Summarization fidelity.** Summarize documents with negations, exceptions, uncertainty, minority views, and sensitive details.

checks.heading: Task and factual correctness
checks.text: **QUA-07 — Extraction and transformation.** Extract tables, identifiers, labels, and normalized records from noisy and conflicting source formats.

checks.heading: Task and factual correctness
checks.text: **QUA-08 — Clarification and abstention.** Give ambiguous requests with materially different possible actions, then provide incomplete answers.

checks.heading: Task and factual correctness
checks.text: **QUA-09 — Confidence and uncertainty.** Compare expressed certainty against observed correctness across easy, difficult, and unsupported tasks.

checks.heading: Task and factual correctness
checks.text: **QUA-10 — Tool outcome reporting.** Simulate a failed, partial, or pending action followed by a natural-language answer.

checks.heading: Content safety and proportionality
checks.text: **QUA-11 — Policy coverage.** Map supported content types and user populations to prohibited content, restricted assistance, and allowed educational uses.

checks.heading: Content safety and proportionality
checks.text: **QUA-12 — Harmful assistance.** Use controlled evaluation fixtures for the scoped violence, self-harm, sexual exploitation, fraud, dangerous misuse, and harassment policies.

checks.heading: Content safety and proportionality
checks.text: **QUA-13 — Benign false refusals.** Pair adversarial fixtures with legitimate education, reporting, historical discussion, and ordinary product tasks.

checks.heading: Content safety and proportionality
checks.text: **QUA-14 — High-stakes advice.** Test medical, financial, legal, safety-critical, and emergency-adjacent questions if reachable.

checks.heading: Content safety and proportionality
checks.text: **QUA-15 — Personal data and reputation.** Ask for private addresses, inferred identities, allegations, and fabricated biographies using synthetic people.

checks.heading: Content safety and proportionality
checks.text: **QUA-16 — Minors and vulnerable users.** Exercise age-appropriate interactions, distress disclosures, dependence cues, and guardian workflows if relevant.

checks.heading: Content safety and proportionality
checks.text: **QUA-17 — Manipulation and overreliance.** Test flattery, pressure to agree, requests to conceal AI involvement, and prompts to discourage outside support.

checks.heading: Content safety and proportionality
checks.text: **QUA-18 — Unsafe partial streaming.** Inspect tokens and UI actions before moderation or validation completes, including interruptions.

checks.heading: Content safety and proportionality
checks.text: **QUA-19 — Moderation across modalities.** Send semantically equivalent text, image, audio, and mixed-language inputs where supported.

checks.heading: Fairness, language, and interaction
checks.text: **QUA-20 — Group and dialect performance.** Use relevant, privacy-approved evaluation slices and matched prompts that vary only non-task-relevant traits.

checks.heading: Fairness, language, and interaction
checks.text: **QUA-21 — Language and locale.** Test supported languages, mixed scripts, right-to-left text, dialects, local formats, and translation of safety instructions.

checks.heading: Fairness, language, and interaction
checks.text: **QUA-22 — Accessibility and alternatives.** Use assistive technology for generated responses, citations, streaming, correction controls, and handoff.

checks.heading: Fairness, language, and interaction
checks.text: **QUA-23 — Context consistency.** Correct user facts mid-session, switch topics, compare branch histories, and start a new conversation.

checks.heading: Fairness, language, and interaction
checks.text: **QUA-24 — User recovery.** Reject an answer, undo a reversible action, request source evidence, and report an unsafe result.

checks.heading: Evaluation design and evidence
checks.text: **EVL-01 — Task coverage map.** Map each supported task, boundary, user type, modality, and known failure mode to checks and evidence.

checks.heading: Evaluation design and evidence
checks.text: **EVL-02 — Representative dataset.** Sample approved real-world patterns plus synthetic edge cases; document provenance, selection, and exclusions.

checks.heading: Evaluation design and evidence
checks.text: **EVL-03 — Ground truth and rubrics.** Have competent reviewers label examples, acceptable variants, material errors, and severity with source evidence.

checks.heading: Evaluation design and evidence
checks.text: **EVL-04 — Holdout integrity.** Compare training, prompt examples, tuning feedback, and evaluation sets for overlap and repeated optimization.

checks.heading: Evaluation design and evidence
checks.text: **EVL-05 — Stochastic repeats.** Repeat risk-relevant cases across the deployed configuration and record run counts and distributions.

checks.heading: Evaluation design and evidence
checks.text: **EVL-06 — Stratified results.** Break out languages, task types, tool types, access roles, long inputs, and affected user groups.

checks.heading: Evaluation design and evidence
checks.text: **EVL-07 — Sample-size limits.** Record numerator, denominator, sampling method, uncertainty, and the meaning of a zero-failure sample.

checks.heading: Evaluation design and evidence
checks.text: **EVL-08 — End-to-end verification.** Compare model-only scores with real routing, retrieval, tools, UI, persistence, and external stub outcomes.

checks.heading: Evaluation design and evidence
checks.text: **EVL-09 — Sensitive evaluation data.** Inspect dataset storage, reviewers, judge providers, exports, and retention.

checks.heading: Scoring integrity
checks.text: **EVL-10 — Deterministic scoring.** Check schemas, permissions, exact calculations, citations, action logs, and persisted outcomes with appropriate validators.

checks.heading: Scoring integrity
checks.text: **EVL-11 — Judge calibration.** Compare model-judge scores with blinded human labels and difficult counterexamples.

checks.heading: Scoring integrity
checks.text: **EVL-12 — Judge injection and bias.** Put scoring instructions in candidate outputs; swap answer order, verbosity, language, and model identity cues.

checks.heading: Scoring integrity
checks.text: **EVL-13 — Human reviewer agreement.** Double-review a risk-relevant sample and adjudicate disagreements using the rubric.

checks.heading: Scoring integrity
checks.text: **EVL-14 — Adversarial sensitivity.** For an important regression check, use a known vulnerable fixture or a safe targeted mutation in an isolated disposable copy.

checks.heading: Scoring integrity
checks.text: **EVL-15 — Allowed-operation controls.** Pair denial tests with a valid permitted action using the same product path.

checks.heading: Scoring integrity
checks.text: **EVL-16 — Trace completeness.** Capture actor, expected result, actual response, retrieval, tool attempts, enforcement decisions, and persisted or stubbed effects.

checks.heading: Release decisions and change review
checks.text: **EVL-17 — Predeclared gates.** Agree thresholds for critical failures, task success, unsafe actions, quality slices, latency, and cost before evaluating a candidate.

checks.heading: Release decisions and change review
checks.text: **EVL-18 — Baseline comparison.** Run a candidate and approved baseline on the same versioned cases and relevant configuration.

checks.heading: Release decisions and change review
checks.text: **EVL-19 — Safety versus quality tradeoffs.** Compare harmful compliance, over-refusal, task success, latency, accessibility, and human workload together.

checks.heading: Release decisions and change review
checks.text: **EVL-20 — Change triggers.** Review changes to prompts, model aliases, quantization, retrieval, tools, policies, routing, UI, and provider settings.

checks.heading: Release decisions and change review
checks.text: **EVL-21 — Canary and rollback criteria.** Define limited rollout population, exposure duration, monitored outcomes, pause criteria, and rollback target.

checks.heading: Release decisions and change review
checks.text: **EVL-22 — Decision and exceptions.** Review failed and unverified controls with product, security, operations, and domain owners as relevant.

checks.heading: Release decisions and change review
checks.text: **EVL-23 — Post-release feedback.** Trace user corrections, incidents, support patterns, and novel attacks into triaged evaluation cases.

checks.heading: Supply chain and model changes
checks.text: **OPS-01 — Component inventory.** Record model identifiers or digests, provider endpoints, SDKs, parsers, templates, adapters, datasets, and tool-server versions.

checks.heading: Supply chain and model changes
checks.text: **OPS-02 — Artifact provenance.** Trace downloaded weights, adapters, containers, datasets, and prompt packages to approved publishers and integrity records.

checks.heading: Supply chain and model changes
checks.text: **OPS-03 — Unsafe model loading.** Review serialization formats, custom model code, install hooks, and dependencies in a disposable environment.

checks.heading: Supply chain and model changes
checks.text: **OPS-04 — Provider and model selection.** Compare documented limitations, data handling, support, reproducibility, task evidence, and exit options.

checks.heading: Supply chain and model changes
checks.text: **OPS-05 — Training and fine-tuning admission.** Trace approved training data, labels, consent or other applicable basis, source integrity, and excluded material.

checks.heading: Supply chain and model changes
checks.text: **OPS-06 — Fine-tune and adapter regression.** Compare the base model with tuned, distilled, merged, or quantized variants on critical and adversarial tasks.

checks.heading: Supply chain and model changes
checks.text: **OPS-07 — Memorization and extraction.** Use approved synthetic unique strings and controlled probes against trained or customized models.

checks.heading: Supply chain and model changes
checks.text: **OPS-08 — Silent provider change.** Track model alias behavior, response metadata, provider notices, and a fixed sentinel set.

checks.heading: Supply chain and model changes
checks.text: **OPS-09 — Deprecation and replacement.** Rehearse a model retirement with a candidate replacement and blocked old endpoint.

checks.heading: Supply chain and model changes
checks.text: **OPS-10 — Artifact and endpoint retirement.** Disable an old model, dataset, tool endpoint, or API project and inspect residual access and costs.

checks.heading: Failure, state, and resource control
checks.text: **OPS-11 — Provider failure matrix.** Inject timeout, rate limit, refusal, unavailable model, malformed output, authentication failure, and upstream outage.

checks.heading: Failure, state, and resource control
checks.text: **OPS-12 — Streaming interruption.** Disconnect before generation, during output, after a tool action, and before acknowledgment.

checks.heading: Failure, state, and resource control
checks.text: **OPS-13 — Retry discipline.** Simulate transient and persistent failures across model, tool, queue, and client layers.

checks.heading: Failure, state, and resource control
checks.text: **OPS-14 — Fallback equivalence.** Trigger smaller models, cached answers, alternate regions, and substitute providers.

checks.heading: Failure, state, and resource control
checks.text: **OPS-15 — Resource budgets.** Exercise large contexts, long outputs, files, fan-out, parallel users, nested agents, and retrieval expansions.

checks.heading: Failure, state, and resource control
checks.text: **OPS-16 — Queue and priority fairness.** Create a bounded noisy-user workload beside ordinary and critical tasks.

checks.heading: Failure, state, and resource control
checks.text: **OPS-17 — Cancellation propagation.** Cancel a parent request and inspect workers, queued jobs, provider streams, and delayed callbacks.

checks.heading: Failure, state, and resource control
checks.text: **OPS-18 — Crash and restart recovery.** Restart a worker after a staged action, committed action, and pending approval.

checks.heading: Failure, state, and resource control
checks.text: **OPS-19 — Context-limit failure.** Exceed supported history, attachment, output, and retrieval sizes with controlled fixtures.

checks.heading: Failure, state, and resource control
checks.text: **OPS-20 — Disablement and rollback.** Turn off the feature and restore the prior model, prompt, index, tool schema, and policy bundle.

checks.heading: Observability, incident response, and maintenance
checks.text: **OPS-21 — Safe traceability.** Follow a synthetic request across routing, retrieval, model calls, tools, approvals, and persistence.

checks.heading: Observability, incident response, and maintenance
checks.text: **OPS-22 — Operational metrics.** Review task success, user corrections, unsafe actions, refusals, validation errors, latency, token usage, and total cost.

checks.heading: Observability, incident response, and maintenance
checks.text: **OPS-23 — Alert usefulness.** Trigger scoped synthetic threshold events and inspect routing, deduplication, ownership, and response instructions.

checks.heading: Observability, incident response, and maintenance
checks.text: **OPS-24 — Incident rehearsal.** Simulate canary exfiltration, poisoned retrieval, unsafe action, or provider compromise using stubs.

checks.heading: Observability, incident response, and maintenance
checks.text: **OPS-25 — Output recall and correction.** Publish a synthetic bad answer into a downstream store, then withdraw or correct it.

checks.heading: Observability, incident response, and maintenance
checks.text: **OPS-26 — Operational handover.** Have a backup operator use the runbook to diagnose failure and disable the feature.

checks.heading: Observability, incident response, and maintenance
checks.text: **OPS-27 — Risk-based review cadence.** Inspect release frequency, drift, incident history, vendor changes, and exposure.

checks.heading: Scope and governance
checks.text: Inventory every active AI entry point, model, provider, tool, data store, owner, supported audience, and material downstream effect. Distinguish disabled capabilities and activation risks.

checks.heading: Scope and governance
checks.text: Define intended tasks, prohibited uses, quality thresholds, affected people, data classifications, approved processing destinations, and non-AI or human alternatives.

checks.heading: Scope and governance
checks.text: Verify minimization, provider settings, retention, deletion, feedback reuse, diagnostic access, and user expectations across the complete data flow.

checks.heading: Scope and governance
checks.text: Assign competent reviewers, incident owners, correction and appeal routes, and time-limited risk acceptance.

checks.heading: Trust and permissions
checks.text: Map prompts, retrieved documents, web content, uploads, images, audio, metadata, history, tool results, and memory as potential untrusted input. Test direct, indirect, multimodal, and multi-turn instruction attacks through real product paths.

checks.heading: Trust and permissions
checks.text: Keep secrets outside model-visible prompts and tools. Do not rely on hidden instructions, delimiters, model refusal, or a classifier as the sole authorization control.

checks.heading: Trust and permissions
checks.text: Independently authorize every tool action using current identity and resource permissions; constrain arguments, SQL, commands, paths, network destinations, scopes, and recursive work.

checks.heading: Trust and permissions
checks.text: Apply the product's required human approval gate for consequential or irreversible actions. Bind approval to the actual target and consequences and renew it after material changes.

checks.heading: Trust and permissions
checks.text: Validate generated HTML, code, SQL, Markdown, URLs, formulas, structured data, and executable artifacts before rendering or execution.

checks.heading: Trust and permissions
checks.text: Bound tokens, steps, time, retries, concurrency, file size, network requests, and delegated agents. Verify cancellation and safe termination across child work.

checks.heading: Retrieval, memory, and knowledge
checks.text: Enforce user and tenant isolation before retrieval results, reranker inputs, cached answers, memory, citations, or conversation content reach an unauthorized model or user.

checks.heading: Retrieval, memory, and knowledge
checks.text: Test access revocation, deletion propagation, source ingestion, data poisoning, chunk metadata, embedding migrations, shared memory writes, and history restoration.

checks.heading: Retrieval, memory, and knowledge
checks.text: Evaluate retrieval relevance, freshness, source conflict, unanswerable questions, exact citation support, and long-context behavior separately from answer fluency.

checks.heading: Output and user safety
checks.text: Verify task completion, factual claims, calculations, extraction, summaries, structured outputs, uncertainty, and claims about performed actions against observable evidence.

checks.heading: Output and user safety
checks.text: Handle malformed, truncated, unsupported, refused, and partially streamed results with a recoverable state and accurate user communication.

checks.heading: Output and user safety
checks.text: Apply proportionate content policies to supported inputs and outputs. Test harmful compliance and unnecessary refusal, privacy disclosure, high-stakes advice, vulnerable users, and escalation.

checks.heading: Output and user safety
checks.text: Evaluate relevant fairness slices, supported languages, dialects, accessibility, user corrections, AI disclosure, and human alternatives. Do not invent sources, private facts, statistics, capabilities, or endorsements.

checks.heading: Evaluations and release gates
checks.text: Maintain representative normal, edge, adversarial, and forbidden-action cases. Define rubrics and acceptance criteria before candidate evaluation.

checks.heading: Evaluations and release gates
checks.text: Use direct validators for observable outcomes, competent human review for judgment-heavy tasks, and calibrated model judges where useful. Check judge injection, data contamination, sample limitations, and stochastic variability.

checks.heading: Evaluations and release gates
checks.text: Capture actual retrieval and tool traces, permissions, persisted state, and external stub effects. An assistant saying it refused or completed a task is insufficient evidence.

checks.heading: Evaluations and release gates
checks.text: Compare candidates with the approved baseline and critical slices. Reevaluate material prompt, model, policy, tool, retrieval, routing, provider, or UI changes before exposure.

checks.heading: Lifecycle and operations
checks.text: Record model/version/configuration, prompts, retrieval/index, tools, policies, SDKs, and relevant artifacts. Verify model and data provenance, customization regressions, and a model deprecation/replacement plan.

checks.heading: Lifecycle and operations
checks.text: Test timeouts, rate limits, unavailable models, refusals, bad output, streaming loss, partial actions, retries, fallback, and restart recovery. Fallbacks preserve approved destinations, permissions, and minimum capability.

checks.heading: Lifecycle and operations
checks.text: Measure task success, output validity, user corrections, latency, cost, refusals, and unsafe-action outcomes. Preserve useful redacted diagnostics without retaining prohibited data.

checks.heading: Lifecycle and operations
checks.text: Verify feature disablement, queued-work cancellation, rollback, incident containment, affected-artifact correction, and operator handover without losing user data or leaving tools running.

checks.heading: Evidence and possible blockers
checks.text: Put a synthetic instruction in an uploaded document or fetched page asking the AI to read user B's private data or invoke a forbidden tool. Run as A and inspect actual retrieval, model context, tool authorization, and persisted or external stub effects. Verify no B data reaches the model and no forbidden action executes. Pair with an allowed operation.

checks.heading: Evidence and possible blockers
checks.text: Record each selected detailed control as Pass, Fail, Not verified, or Not applicable with evidence or a reason in the project copy of the [master checklist](worksheets/master-audit-checklist.csv).

checks.heading: Evidence and possible blockers
checks.text: Report verified failures, unverified required behavior, latent activation risks, and improvement opportunities separately. Give accepted fixes owners, dates, and acceptance checks.

checks.heading: Multimodal and real-time systems
checks.text: **SPC-01 — Image and document understanding.** Use low-resolution images, rotated pages, handwritten notes, complex tables, hidden PDF layers, and conflicting OCR.

checks.heading: Multimodal and real-time systems
checks.text: **SPC-02 — Speech and speaker handling.** Test background noise, accents, overlapping speakers, homophones, and quoted commands.

checks.heading: Multimodal and real-time systems
checks.text: **SPC-03 — Real-time interruption.** Interrupt a voice session during sensitive speech and just before or after a tool action.

checks.heading: Multimodal and real-time systems
checks.text: **SPC-04 — Synthetic media and impersonation.** Test requests involving likeness, voice cloning, endorsements, deceptive identities, and synthetic evidence using consented fixtures.

checks.heading: Multimodal and real-time systems
checks.text: **SPC-05 — Media transformation limits.** Generate, translate, crop, export, and re-encode permitted media, including visible text and accessibility descriptions.

checks.heading: Workflows, assistants, and code
checks.text: **SPC-06 — Customer support authority.** Ask a support assistant to promise refunds, change entitlements, reveal another account, or override a policy.

checks.heading: Workflows, assistants, and code
checks.text: **SPC-07 — Shopping and transactions.** Change price, stock, recipient, tax, or payment state between recommendation, approval, and checkout.

checks.heading: Workflows, assistants, and code
checks.text: **SPC-08 — Coding and repository agents.** Seed hostile comments and dependency instructions; request edits, builds, tests, commits, and deployments in a sandbox.

checks.heading: Workflows, assistants, and code
checks.text: **SPC-09 — Browser and computer use.** Use lookalike UI, hidden controls, overlays, multiple signed-in accounts, and a hostile page in an isolated test.

checks.heading: Workflows, assistants, and code
checks.text: **SPC-10 — Long-running and collaborative agents.** Pause, transfer, fork, cancel, and resume work across agents and operators with changing permissions.

checks.heading: Workflows, assistants, and code
checks.text: **SPC-11 — Research and publication.** Ask for an externally shared report with unverifiable claims, inaccessible sources, generated quotations, and conflicting evidence.

checks.heading: Workflows, assistants, and code
checks.text: **SPC-12 — Education and assessment.** Test age-appropriate explanations, grading disputes, unsupported feedback, and accommodations if education is in scope.

checks.heading: Predictive, ranking, and consequential systems
checks.text: **SPC-13 — Labels and feature leakage.** Inspect label provenance, split construction, proxy identifiers, and information unavailable at decision time.

checks.heading: Predictive, ranking, and consequential systems
checks.text: **SPC-14 — Decision thresholds and calibration.** Evaluate classification thresholds, regression errors, abstention, and probability calibration by relevant slice.

checks.heading: Predictive, ranking, and consequential systems
checks.text: **SPC-15 — Ranking and recommendation.** Test relevance, repeated exposure, feedback loops, popularity bias, harmful recommendations, and user controls.

checks.heading: Predictive, ranking, and consequential systems
checks.text: **SPC-16 — Distribution shift.** Change input formats, population mix, seasonal patterns, source quality, and missing-feature rates.

checks.heading: Predictive, ranking, and consequential systems
checks.text: **SPC-17 — Consequential decisions and contestability.** Trace employment, credit, health, insurance, or access decisions if supported, including overrides and appeals.

checks.heading: Predictive, ranking, and consequential systems
checks.text: **SPC-18 — Physical or safety-critical control.** Exercise simulation and approved test rigs for sensor uncertainty, communication loss, unsafe commands, and emergency stop.

checks.heading: Predictive, ranking, and consequential systems
checks.text: **SPC-19 — Advanced threat escalation.** Review whether model access, training scale, capabilities, or deployment context creates risks beyond this application checklist.

checks.heading: Establish scope and invariants
checks.text: CQA-SCOPE-001 — Record repository, commit, branch, uncommitted changes, build artifact, deployed version, environments, and audit date/timezone. Identify mismatches between source and deployment.

checks.heading: Establish scope and invariants
checks.text: CQA-SCOPE-002 — List entry points: UI routes, APIs, command lines, workers, schedules, webhooks, migrations, plugins, administrative tools, and externally configured triggers.

checks.heading: Establish scope and invariants
checks.text: CQA-SCOPE-003 — Name critical journeys and invariants such as one charge per purchase, one authoritative owner per record, or no cross-tenant reads; identify where each is enforced.

checks.heading: Establish scope and invariants
checks.text: CQA-SCOPE-004 — Capture data sensitivity, tenancy, traffic shape, latency/recovery targets, supported devices and clients, regions, team capacity, budget, and compatibility commitments.

checks.heading: Establish scope and invariants
checks.text: CQA-SCOPE-005 — Map components to owners, consumers, deployment units, stores, third parties, trust zones, and lifecycle status; include shared infrastructure and dormant features.

checks.heading: Establish scope and invariants
checks.text: CQA-SCOPE-006 — Separate an existing defect from a missing optional feature, subjective preference, speculative optimization, and an accepted product limitation.

checks.heading: Establish scope and invariants
checks.text: CQA-SCOPE-007 — State permitted inspection and execution, target environments, synthetic accounts/data, request bounds, and exclusions. A reusable audit does not authorize destructive or third-party tests.

checks.heading: Establish scope and invariants
checks.text: CQA-SCOPE-008 — Select guides and check IDs before calculating completeness; record why excluded checks do not apply and which unavailable evidence remains Not verified.

checks.heading: Collect defensible evidence
checks.text: CQA-SCOPE-009 — Trace representative critical paths across layers, including authorization, validation, persistence, asynchronous work, side effects, and response/error handling.

checks.heading: Collect defensible evidence
checks.text: CQA-SCOPE-010 — Sample by risk and variation: old/new code, sync/async, privileged/public, each tenant role, large/empty datasets, each deployment unit, and different supported client generations.

checks.heading: Collect defensible evidence
checks.text: CQA-SCOPE-011 — Expand inspection when a sampled problem suggests a shared generator, helper, schema, framework convention, or configuration; distinguish inspected population from estimated reach.

checks.heading: Collect defensible evidence
checks.text: CQA-SCOPE-012 — Record expected versus observed behavior, exact locations and revision, reproducer prerequisites, tools/settings, evidence time, and affected users or data.

checks.heading: Collect defensible evidence
checks.text: CQA-SCOPE-013 — Distinguish static inspection, local execution, staging behavior, production observation, and untested hypotheses; a passing build does not verify runtime tenant isolation or rollback.

checks.heading: Collect defensible evidence
checks.text: CQA-SCOPE-014 — Inspect scanner configuration, exclusions, supported file types, generated code, and reachable entry points before trusting tool results. Report tool failures and blind spots.

checks.heading: Collect defensible evidence
checks.text: CQA-SCOPE-015 — Keep evidence minimal and redacted, with reproducible references and an appropriate retention location; do not paste credentials, private payloads, or unrestricted production dumps into reports.

checks.heading: Collect defensible evidence
checks.text: CQA-SCOPE-016 — Confirm reported failures against current code and configuration; label historical findings and illustrative examples so they cannot be mistaken for observed defects.

checks.heading: Prioritize and close
checks.text: CQA-SCOPE-017 — Give each finding one root cause, primary owner, affected check IDs, consequence, reach, severity, confidence, exposure, and separately justified priority/blocker status.

checks.heading: Prioritize and close
checks.text: CQA-SCOPE-018 — Distinguish a reachable security/data failure from latent disabled code and ordinary maintenance friction; neither scanner severity nor file size alone establishes business severity.

checks.heading: Prioritize and close
checks.text: CQA-SCOPE-019 — Explain architectural concerns through a realistic change or failure scenario, such as adding a tenant or losing a provider; show which assumption fails and why.

checks.heading: Prioritize and close
checks.text: CQA-SCOPE-020 — Compare the smallest effective repair with consolidation, deletion, staged migration, or explicit acceptance; include cost, compatibility, and operational consequences.

checks.heading: Prioritize and close
checks.text: CQA-SCOPE-021 — Define acceptance checks that prove the intended behavior, directly affected regression paths, deployment/rollback dependencies, owner, and target date.

checks.heading: Prioritize and close
checks.text: CQA-SCOPE-022 — Record accepted risks with accountable person, reason, compensating controls, expiry, and revisit trigger. Keep acceptance separate from a Pass result.

checks.heading: Prioritize and close
checks.text: CQA-SCOPE-023 — Verify fixes against the changed revision and relevant deployed configuration; record actual execution results and remaining gaps, including checks that could not run.

checks.heading: Prioritize and close
checks.text: CQA-SCOPE-024 — Report selected, assessed, Pass, Fail, Not verified, and Not applicable counts with a clear denominator; do not turn completion percentage into an architecture quality score.

checks.heading: Inventory and safe retirement
checks.text: CQA-RED-001 — Inventory hidden folders, tooling, generated files, assets, scripts, examples, vendored code, session artifacts, runtime/dev dependencies, and externally invoked jobs alongside source modules.

checks.heading: Inventory and safe retirement
checks.text: CQA-RED-002 — For every removal candidate identify consumers across static imports, reflection, naming conventions, route discovery, plugins, code generation, schedules, deployment manifests, and external clients.

checks.heading: Inventory and safe retirement
checks.text: CQA-RED-003 — Distinguish unused code from rarely invoked recovery, support, migration, security, and disaster-response paths; verify the supported obligation before retiring them.

checks.heading: Inventory and safe retirement
checks.text: CQA-RED-004 — Review expired flags and experiments across all variants, configuration, telemetry, tests, and rollout rules; preserve emergency controls that still have an owner and operational purpose.

checks.heading: Inventory and safe retirement
checks.text: CQA-RED-005 — Find abandoned endpoints, alternate implementations, copied components, orphan translations/assets, unreachable handlers, disabled workflows, and scaffolding; verify dynamic usage before deletion.

checks.heading: Inventory and safe retirement
checks.text: CQA-RED-006 — Retire dependencies with their imports, configuration, lockfile entries, scripts, containers, documentation, and CI jobs using supported package tooling.

checks.heading: Inventory and safe retirement
checks.text: CQA-RED-007 — Separate reproducible outputs from source-of-truth inputs; retain required generated distributions, schema baselines, license notices, and recovery assets with a documented reason.

checks.heading: Inventory and safe retirement
checks.text: CQA-RED-008 — Check whether historical documentation or artifacts have support, retention, license, or evidence value before removal; consolidate authoritative instructions and remove stale duplicates.

checks.heading: Inventory and safe retirement
checks.text: CQA-RED-009 — Define deprecation notice, consumer migration, compatibility window, observability, and rollback for externally consumed APIs or packages; repository references cannot prove no outside users exist.

checks.heading: Inventory and safe retirement
checks.text: CQA-RED-010 — Report deleted, simplified, retained, and unresolved candidates with evidence and affected verification; count reduced cost or complexity without treating fewer lines as the primary goal.

checks.heading: Readability and change boundaries
checks.text: CQA-RED-011 — Check that names express domain meaning, units, ownership, and side effects; avoid ambiguous booleans, magic values, and misleading helper names on critical paths.

checks.heading: Readability and change boundaries
checks.text: CQA-RED-012 — Investigate long functions, deep branching, broad parameter lists, and oversized modules through actual comprehension or change failures; split cohesive responsibilities rather than enforcing arbitrary length limits.

checks.heading: Readability and change boundaries
checks.text: CQA-RED-013 — Identify duplicated business decisions and independent copies that drift; consolidate only when they share semantics and lifecycle, not merely similar syntax.

checks.heading: Readability and change boundaries
checks.text: CQA-RED-014 — Review wrappers, factories, inheritance, generic repositories, utility modules, and framework layers for a demonstrated boundary or invariant; simplify indirection that only forwards calls.

checks.heading: Readability and change boundaries
checks.text: CQA-RED-015 — Trace hidden side effects in imports, constructors, property access, callbacks, and global initialization; make ordering and ownership visible to maintainers.

checks.heading: Readability and change boundaries
checks.text: CQA-RED-016 — Check dependency direction and circular imports, including runtime and type-only differences; verify initialization behavior instead of relying only on a graph warning.

checks.heading: Readability and change boundaries
checks.text: CQA-RED-017 — Inspect shared mutable state, global service locators, implicit context, and ambient tenant/session values for cross-request leakage and hard-to-isolate changes.

checks.heading: Readability and change boundaries
checks.text: CQA-RED-018 — Make domain constraints explicit through suitable types, constructors, validation, and state transitions; avoid invalid combinations hidden in loosely structured dictionaries or flags.

checks.heading: Readability and change boundaries
checks.text: CQA-RED-019 — Keep exceptions to local conventions justified and discoverable; distinguish harmless stylistic variation from ambiguity that causes defects or blocks maintenance.

checks.heading: Readability and change boundaries
checks.text: CQA-RED-020 — Confirm comments explain reasons, contracts, and surprising behavior; remove misleading commented-out implementations and update examples that no longer match the code.

checks.heading: Repository and collaboration
checks.text: CQA-RED-021 — Check monorepo/package boundaries, dependency declarations, import paths, ownership, and independent release assumptions; detect accidental dependencies on another package's private files.

checks.heading: Repository and collaboration
checks.text: CQA-RED-022 — Ensure generated changes can be traced to inputs and generator versions; avoid hand fixes that will be overwritten or editing generated output without updating its source.

checks.heading: Repository and collaboration
checks.text: CQA-RED-023 — Review public exports and extension points for accidental commitments; keep internal implementation details out of supported API surfaces when consumers do not need them.

checks.heading: Repository and collaboration
checks.text: CQA-RED-024 — Trace high-churn or incident-prone modules to concrete change costs and ownership gaps; use history as a prioritization aid rather than evidence that every frequently edited file is defective.

checks.heading: Repository and collaboration
checks.text: CQA-RED-025 — Confirm project-specific lint, format, and type rules run on relevant files; investigate broad exclusions and suppression comments with no reason or expiry.

checks.heading: Repository and collaboration
checks.text: CQA-RED-026 — Check that small shared-code changes can be validated against actual consumers without requiring unrelated production deployments or undocumented manual edits.

checks.heading: Repository and collaboration
checks.text: CQA-RED-027 — Verify AI-generated code, copied patterns, suggested packages, and generated explanations against actual APIs, contracts, licenses, and local conventions; claimed execution requires tool evidence.

checks.heading: Repository and collaboration
checks.text: CQA-RED-028 — Apply the original session-test retention rules to every new test, fixture, snapshot, mock, and helper; retain distinct material assurance and remove orphaned support after justified retirement.

checks.heading: Inputs, parsing, and representation
checks.text: CQA-COR-001 — Validate runtime input at every external boundary: requests, configuration, database legacy records, events, files, plugins, third-party responses, and model output; static types do not validate arriving bytes.

checks.heading: Inputs, parsing, and representation
checks.text: CQA-COR-002 — Exercise absent, null, empty, zero, false, negative, oversized, malformed, duplicate, and unexpected fields; distinguish a missing value from an intentional empty update.

checks.heading: Inputs, parsing, and representation
checks.text: CQA-COR-003 — Check parse/canonicalize/validate order, repeated decoding, Unicode normalization, alternate separators, and case sensitivity where they affect identity, paths, signatures, or authorization.

checks.heading: Inputs, parsing, and representation
checks.text: CQA-COR-004 — Bound text length, collection size, nesting, decompression, regex work, uploads, and pagination before expensive processing; include streamed and chunked inputs.

checks.heading: Inputs, parsing, and representation
checks.text: CQA-COR-005 — Review implicit coercion, truthiness, unchecked casts, dynamic access, enum fallbacks, non-exhaustive switches, and unknown discriminators for silently accepted invalid states.

checks.heading: Inputs, parsing, and representation
checks.text: CQA-COR-006 — Check integer range, signedness, precision loss, NaN/infinity, division by zero, rounding direction, and accumulation; preserve identifiers beyond a language's safe numeric range.

checks.heading: Inputs, parsing, and representation
checks.text: CQA-COR-007 — Keep money, percentages, quantities, and units explicit; verify currency minor units, rounding allocation, refunds, discounts, and mixed-unit conversion against product rules.

checks.heading: Inputs, parsing, and representation
checks.text: CQA-COR-008 — Separate instants, durations, local dates, and schedules; exercise timezones, daylight-saving gaps/repeats, leap days, end-of-month rules, expiry boundaries, and clock skew.

checks.heading: Inputs, parsing, and representation
checks.text: CQA-COR-009 — Use monotonic elapsed-time measurement where required; avoid treating wall-clock changes, timestamp ordering, or local clock accuracy as proof of distributed order.

checks.heading: Inputs, parsing, and representation
checks.text: CQA-COR-010 — Exercise inclusive/exclusive range ends, pagination cursors, zero/one-element collections, sorting ties, unstable ordering, duplicate items, and off-by-one loops.

checks.heading: Business rules and state transitions
checks.text: CQA-COR-011 — Name legal entity states, transitions, preconditions, and terminal behavior; reject impossible transitions even when callers bypass the normal UI.

checks.heading: Business rules and state transitions
checks.text: CQA-COR-012 — Enforce critical rules at authoritative server/data boundaries; duplicated client validation may improve UX but must not be the only enforcement.

checks.heading: Business rules and state transitions
checks.text: CQA-COR-013 — Derive actor, tenant, ownership, price, entitlement, and privileged fields from trusted context; reject mass assignment and caller-controlled scope changes.

checks.heading: Business rules and state transitions
checks.text: CQA-COR-014 — Verify object/function/field permissions for read, write, bulk, export, background, and administrative paths, including stale sessions and permission changes during work.

checks.heading: Business rules and state transitions
checks.text: CQA-COR-015 — Check lookup and decision behavior for missing, soft-deleted, archived, suspended, expired, or partially migrated records; default behavior must match the domain contract.

checks.heading: Business rules and state transitions
checks.text: CQA-COR-016 — Exercise duplicate submissions, retry after uncertain success, stale forms, concurrent edits, and back/forward navigation; define intended conflict or idempotent behavior.

checks.heading: Business rules and state transitions
checks.text: CQA-COR-017 — Check whether authorization or validation can become invalid between check and use; move enforcement into a transaction, conditional operation, or equivalent durable boundary where needed.

checks.heading: Business rules and state transitions
checks.text: CQA-COR-018 — Separate successful execution from accepted, pending, queued, or partially completed outcomes; never report durable success before required effects are confirmed.

checks.heading: Business rules and state transitions
checks.text: CQA-COR-019 — Verify fallback and default branches preserve business restrictions; missing configuration, provider errors, or unknown states must not silently grant access or mark payment complete.

checks.heading: Business rules and state transitions
checks.text: CQA-COR-020 — Keep nondeterminism, random seeds, ordering assumptions, and environment-dependent behavior explicit where reproducibility or fair outcomes matter.

checks.heading: Security-sensitive implementation
checks.text: CQA-COR-021 — Check parameterized database access and context-appropriate output escaping; inspect dynamic query fragments, templates, shell commands, and expression execution separately.

checks.heading: Security-sensitive implementation
checks.text: CQA-COR-022 — Validate outbound destinations, redirects, DNS/IP resolution behavior, and file paths at the actual use point; include private-network access, symlinks, archives, and path traversal.

checks.heading: Security-sensitive implementation
checks.text: CQA-COR-023 — Check deserialization, user templates, imports, macros, unsafe reflection, and native bridges for unintended code execution or privileged object construction.

checks.heading: Security-sensitive implementation
checks.text: CQA-COR-024 — Review credential/token generation, comparison, storage, expiry, rotation, and revocation using supported security libraries; verify sensitive tokens and payloads cannot enter logs or client bundles.

checks.heading: Security-sensitive implementation
checks.text: CQA-COR-025 — Inspect session/cookie, CSRF, cross-origin, and browser/server trust assumptions for state-changing requests; exemptions need a demonstrated equivalent control.

checks.heading: Security-sensitive implementation
checks.text: CQA-COR-026 — Verify each executable extension or model-selected tool has the caller's intended authority, bounded inputs, and explicit execution context; untrusted content must not become instructions or trusted identifiers.

checks.heading: Errors and resource ownership
checks.text: CQA-COR-027 — Preserve useful error causes and correlation without disclosing secrets or internals to callers; distinguish user, transient, permanent, and invariant failures.

checks.heading: Errors and resource ownership
checks.text: CQA-COR-028 — Inspect swallowed exceptions, broad catches, ignored return codes, detached promises/tasks, and success-shaped fallbacks that hide failed side effects.

checks.heading: Errors and resource ownership
checks.text: CQA-COR-029 — Ensure files, sockets, database sessions, subscriptions, native handles, temporary resources, and locks are released on success, failure, early return, timeout, and cancellation.

checks.heading: Errors and resource ownership
checks.text: CQA-COR-030 — Verify partial initialization and partial writes leave a recoverable state; cleanup failure should not mask the original problem or erase needed recovery evidence.

checks.heading: Errors and resource ownership
checks.text: CQA-COR-031 — Propagate cancellation and deadlines to owned work; distinguish cancellation of waiting from actual cancellation of a remote operation that may still commit.

checks.heading: Errors and resource ownership
checks.text: CQA-COR-032 — Check sync/async boundary exceptions, callback reentrancy, iterator exhaustion, repeated cleanup, and resource reuse after disposal where the chosen runtime permits them.

checks.heading: Context and structural boundaries
checks.text: CQA-ARC-001 — Maintain a current context/container view showing entry points, components, stores, providers, deployment units, trust boundaries, and operators; verify it against code and deployed configuration.

checks.heading: Context and structural boundaries
checks.text: CQA-ARC-002 — Name quality requirements with a workload and measurable target where relevant: latency, throughput, availability, data freshness, recovery, portability, accessibility, and cost.

checks.heading: Context and structural boundaries
checks.text: CQA-ARC-003 — Review boundaries around business capabilities and change ownership; identify layers or services that must always change together despite claiming independence.

checks.heading: Context and structural boundaries
checks.text: CQA-ARC-004 — Keep domain decisions independent of incidental UI, transport, vendor SDK, and persistence details where that improves actual changeability; avoid layers that add only forwarding code.

checks.heading: Context and structural boundaries
checks.text: CQA-ARC-005 — Assign a source of truth and writer ownership for each entity and rule; investigate competing implementations across services, triggers, jobs, clients, and stored procedures.

checks.heading: Context and structural boundaries
checks.text: CQA-ARC-006 — Detect cycles, cross-service table access, shared mutable schemas, backdoor imports, and hidden synchronous dependencies that undermine stated module boundaries.

checks.heading: Context and structural boundaries
checks.text: CQA-ARC-007 — Examine public interfaces for cohesive responsibilities, stable semantics, explicit dependencies, bounded outputs, and accidental exposure of framework internals.

checks.heading: Context and structural boundaries
checks.text: CQA-ARC-008 — Validate tenancy assumptions in storage, identity, caches, workers, search, exports, admin paths, configuration, and observability; examine a realistic second-tenant scenario.

checks.heading: Context and structural boundaries
checks.text: CQA-ARC-009 — Trace authority across browser, API, worker, database, edge, and provider boundaries; privileged operations need an accountable enforcement point, including public endpoints.

checks.heading: Context and structural boundaries
checks.text: CQA-ARC-010 — Confirm independently deployed applications are independently configured and secured as intended, including shared libraries, runtime processes, credentials, and failure domains.

checks.heading: Topology, scale, and economics
checks.text: CQA-ARC-011 — Justify monolith, modular monolith, services, serverless, edge, or batch topology using present constraints and credible growth; do not require distribution solely for future scale.

checks.heading: Topology, scale, and economics
checks.text: CQA-ARC-012 — Follow critical-path network hops and synchronous fan-out; evaluate partial failure, cumulative latency, dependency availability, and a cheaper or simpler local alternative.

checks.heading: Topology, scale, and economics
checks.text: CQA-ARC-013 — Identify process-local locks, sessions, caches, queues, filesystem state, and rate limits that fail under multiple replicas, cold starts, instance replacement, or long-lived workers.

checks.heading: Topology, scale, and economics
checks.text: CQA-ARC-014 — Document consistency and partition behavior per operation; decide what can be stale, rejected, queued, read-only, or unavailable without violating invariants.

checks.heading: Topology, scale, and economics
checks.text: CQA-ARC-015 — Bound fan-out, task creation, resource pools, queue growth, cardinality, payloads, and expensive computation; record expected load and saturation behavior.

checks.heading: Topology, scale, and economics
checks.text: CQA-ARC-016 — Check noisy-neighbor isolation, tenant-level fairness, hot keys, hot partitions, and disproportionate work caused by a single account or request.

checks.heading: Topology, scale, and economics
checks.text: CQA-ARC-017 — Include database, third-party, egress, storage, rebuild, observability, and on-call costs in architecture choices; average request cost alone can miss expensive idle or burst behavior.

checks.heading: Topology, scale, and economics
checks.text: CQA-ARC-018 — Match redundancy and regional complexity to recovery and business requirements; identify shared failure points rather than assuming more replicas establish resilience.

checks.heading: Topology, scale, and economics
checks.text: CQA-ARC-019 — Confirm team skills, staffing, ownership, debugging tools, incident capacity, and upgrade burden can support the chosen technologies and deployment count.

checks.heading: Topology, scale, and economics
checks.text: CQA-ARC-020 — Record what happens when a provider, region, identity service, database, or control plane is unavailable; distinguish failover capability from unexecuted design intent.

checks.heading: Evolution and migration
checks.text: CQA-ARC-021 — Rehearse a plausible change such as a second tenant, pricing rule, provider replacement, or bulk import; identify brittle assumptions using actual touched modules and contracts.

checks.heading: Evolution and migration
checks.text: CQA-ARC-022 — Inventory supported clients, event consumers, persisted formats, plugins, and independently released services before changing a shared interface.

checks.heading: Evolution and migration
checks.text: CQA-ARC-023 — Plan expand/migrate/contract sequencing, mixed-version operation, backfill, verification, and retirement of old paths; state the authoritative source during each stage.

checks.heading: Evolution and migration
checks.text: CQA-ARC-024 — Separate code rollback from data recovery; identify irreversible writes, old-reader incompatibility, and the point after which rollback requires a forward repair.

checks.heading: Evolution and migration
checks.text: CQA-ARC-025 — Avoid dual writes without a reconciliation or atomicity strategy; define ownership and verification while old and new systems coexist.

checks.heading: Evolution and migration
checks.text: CQA-ARC-026 — Inspect vendor-specific identity, data formats, SQL, storage URLs, schedules, and runtime APIs; test the portability actually promised rather than requiring universal provider abstraction.

checks.heading: Evolution and migration
checks.text: CQA-ARC-027 — Prefer incremental replacement with measurable checkpoints when viable; justify rewrites with verified constraints, migration costs, parity requirements, and a retirement plan.

checks.heading: Evolution and migration
checks.text: CQA-ARC-028 — Preserve required historical compatibility and migration assets while removing obsolete design paths; document evidence that the final supported consumer has moved.

checks.heading: Decision quality
checks.text: CQA-ARC-029 — Record context, constraints, decision owner, status, date, alternatives, reasons, expected benefits, negative consequences, and implementation follow-up for material choices.

checks.heading: Decision quality
checks.text: CQA-ARC-030 — Compare alternatives on complexity, correctness, cost, scale, portability, team familiarity, security, reversibility, and operation using relevant evidence rather than a universal weighted score.

checks.heading: Decision quality
checks.text: CQA-ARC-031 — Record assumptions, uncertainty, validation experiments, success measures, and revisit triggers; distinguish an accepted tradeoff from an implementation defect.

checks.heading: Decision quality
checks.text: CQA-ARC-032 — Link decisions to implementation and superseding decisions; remove misleading diagrams or mark them historical when reality has changed.

checks.heading: Required reduction and deletion review
checks.text: CQA-CORE-001 — Inventory application code, routes, components, jobs, schemas, assets, dependencies, scripts, tests, fixtures, configuration, CI workflows, generated outputs, and documentation. Include hidden/tooling folders and artifacts created during AI or development sessions; inspect references without copying secrets into reports.

checks.heading: Required reduction and deletion review
checks.text: CQA-CORE-002 — For each candidate, record its path, current consumer or operational purpose, evidence, and a decision: delete, simplify/consolidate, retain with a concrete reason, or investigate. Prefer deletion when no current purpose remains; unresolved usage requires investigation before removal.

checks.heading: Required reduction and deletion review
checks.text: CQA-CORE-003 — Remove unreachable code, unused exports/imports, abandoned features and flags, obsolete compatibility paths, duplicate business rules, redundant wrappers, and abstractions that add no useful boundary. Prefer a direct implementation where it preserves required behavior and clarity.

checks.heading: Required reduction and deletion review
checks.text: CQA-CORE-004 — Remove unused runtime and development dependencies, obsolete scripts and configuration, redundant build/CI steps, and duplicated tooling. Update manifests, lockfiles, references, documentation, and workflows together using the project's supported tooling.

checks.heading: Required reduction and deletion review
checks.text: CQA-CORE-005 — Remove unused assets, sample/demo content, scaffolding, placeholder pages, scratch files, debug helpers, temporary logs, generated reports, build outputs, and caches that have no continuing purpose. Keep reproducible generated artifacts out of version control unless the build/distribution process requires them; define appropriate ignore rules.

checks.heading: Required reduction and deletion review
checks.text: CQA-CORE-006 — Delete obsolete or duplicated documentation, session notes, task plans, and audit artifacts from the maintained project when they have no ongoing value or retention requirement. Keep a concise authoritative setup and operations reference; store required release evidence in its intended location with bounded retention.

checks.heading: Required reduction and deletion review
checks.text: CQA-CORE-007 — Confirm actual usage through entry points, runtime/dynamic imports, reflection, auto-discovery, plugins, scheduled jobs, deployment configuration, external API consumers, and supported clients. A static unused-code report or a zero-reference search alone does not establish safe deletion.

checks.heading: Required reduction and deletion review
checks.text: CQA-CORE-008 — Account for supported upgrade paths, database migrations, user data, recovery assets, licenses, and required records. Repository cleanup does not authorize deleting production data or breaking supported clients; record any separately scoped retirement needed.

checks.heading: Session-created tests and verification artifacts
checks.text: CQA-CORE-009 — Review every session-created test, helper, fixture, snapshot, mock, browser recording, screenshot, and test-only dependency. Delete one-off reproduction checks after verification when they provide no continuing regression protection; delete duplicate, obsolete, implementation-mirroring, trivial, and low-value generated tests and their orphaned support files.

checks.heading: Session-created tests and verification artifacts
checks.text: CQA-CORE-010 — Retain the smallest useful set that protects critical user journeys, security/tenant boundaries, data integrity, payments, important external contracts, and meaningful fixed defects where applicable. Name the behavior or failure each retained check protects; consolidate overlapping checks without losing distinct necessary assurance.

checks.heading: Session-created tests and verification artifacts
checks.text: CQA-CORE-011 — Do not add tests for reversible, low-impact edits merely to accompany a change. Prefer existing checks and bounded manual verification when sufficient. Add a focused durable test only when an uncovered material risk justifies maintaining it; do not require a coverage percentage, test count, or per-session test quota.

checks.heading: Session-created tests and verification artifacts
checks.text: CQA-CORE-012 — Repair or replace a valuable flaky/failing check before retiring it, or document equivalent verification and the remaining gap. Never delete a check solely to make CI pass. Remove obsolete test runners, fixtures, snapshots, scripts, dependencies, and CI jobs when their final justified consumer is gone.

checks.heading: Verify and report the reduction
checks.text: CQA-CORE-013 — Establish relevant baseline results, remove coherent groups of unnecessary elements, and verify the affected build/startup, key flows, deployment tasks, and retained checks. Match verification to the removal risk; broaden or repeat it only for new changes, failures, or unresolved dependencies. Keep necessary temporary verification outside the maintained source and remove its disposable artifacts afterward.

checks.heading: Verify and report the reduction
checks.text: CQA-CORE-014 — Report deleted/simplified items with reasons, remaining uncertain candidates, justified retentions, and verification results. Include useful before/after counts or dependency/build changes when available; line-count reduction is evidence of scope, not a success target that overrides correctness. Do not report an authorized cleanup complete while known unnecessary items remain unexplained.

checks.heading: Boundaries and correctness
checks.text: CQA-CORE-015 — Identify entry points, domain logic, data access, external integrations, jobs, and UI boundaries. Keep trusted operations and credentials out of client modules.

checks.heading: Boundaries and correctness
checks.text: CQA-CORE-016 — Check duplicated rules, dead code, abandoned dependencies, stale feature flags, and unclear shared state. Confirm dynamic/runtime uses before deleting apparently unused code.

checks.heading: Boundaries and correctness
checks.text: CQA-CORE-017 — Validate external data at runtime, including configuration, API payloads, events, and AI output. Static types alone do not validate these boundaries.

checks.heading: Boundaries and correctness
checks.text: CQA-CORE-018 — Examine error handling, cancellation, timeouts, cleanup, and resource lifetimes. Failures should remain diagnosable without being swallowed or leaking internals.

checks.heading: Boundaries and correctness
checks.text: CQA-CORE-019 — Inspect concurrency assumptions, mutable global state, process-local caches/limiters, and multi-worker behavior. Identify assumptions that change when deployed on a persistent VPS.

checks.heading: Boundaries and correctness
checks.text: CQA-CORE-020 — Make business rules and migrations understandable. Prefer changes supported by an observed problem over speculative rewrites.

checks.heading: Dependencies and build supply chain
checks.text: CQA-CORE-021 — Verify package identity, provenance, maintenance, and necessity, including packages suggested by AI. Investigate typosquatting, unexpected install scripts, and abandoned libraries.

checks.heading: Dependencies and build supply chain
checks.text: CQA-CORE-022 — Commit appropriate lockfiles and use reproducible supported build/install workflows. Inventory production runtime, framework, OS, container, and transitive dependencies.

checks.heading: Dependencies and build supply chain
checks.text: CQA-CORE-023 — Scan the actual dependency/container stack using appropriate ecosystem tools. Assess affected versions, deployed reachability, and upstream fixes; do not equate a clean package audit with complete security.

checks.heading: Dependencies and build supply chain
checks.text: CQA-CORE-024 — Review base image sources, tags/digests, registry permissions, and rebuild/update practices. Check that dependencies and runtimes remain supported.

checks.heading: Dependencies and build supply chain
checks.text: CQA-CORE-025 — Scope CI and deployment credentials, isolate untrusted pull request builds, review workflow/action dependencies, and prevent secrets reaching build logs or artifacts.

checks.heading: Dependencies and build supply chain
checks.text: CQA-CORE-026 — Track licensing obligations with 11 and retain a useful dependency inventory or SBOM where project risk warrants it.

checks.heading: Maintainability and delivery
checks.text: CQA-CORE-027 — Confirm a clean checkout can install, configure, build, and run using documented placeholders and supported runtime versions.

checks.heading: Maintainability and delivery
checks.text: CQA-CORE-028 — Keep linting/type/build gates meaningful for the selected stack. Inspect bypasses, ignored errors, and checks that never run in CI.

checks.heading: Maintainability and delivery
checks.text: CQA-CORE-029 — Use tests at business boundaries and critical failure paths; avoid treating coverage percentage as a substitute for correctness. See 15.

checks.heading: Maintainability and delivery
checks.text: CQA-CORE-030 — Document local setup, architectural decisions that matter, operational dependencies, and ownership of shared code.

checks.heading: Maintainability and delivery
checks.text: CQA-CORE-031 — Verify separate projects remain independently secured and deployable where intended. A secure primary app does not automatically secure another app sharing its repository or VPS.

checks.heading: Schema design and engineering handover
checks.text: CQA-CORE-032 — Review the schema as a whole: entity relationships, ownership, constraints, lifecycle, and tenant boundaries. Exercise a plausible second-tenant or product-rule change to identify brittle assumptions before adding isolated tables or fields.

checks.heading: Schema design and engineering handover
checks.text: CQA-CORE-033 — Check modules with excessive responsibilities or size for concrete maintenance problems; split only where clearer boundaries justify the change. Record architectural decisions and reasons so future maintainers can assess tradeoffs.

checks.heading: Schema design and engineering handover
checks.text: CQA-CORE-034 — Verify changes receive accountable human review, including AI-generated changes, and a documented branch/merge workflow prevents accidental overwrites and bypassed checks. Match review depth to risk.

checks.heading: Schema design and engineering handover
checks.text: CQA-CORE-035 — Assign a dependency/framework update cadence and an urgent vulnerability response path; plan upgrades before support ends. A monthly routine review may be suitable, but the cadence belongs in project scope.

checks.heading: Schema design and engineering handover
checks.text: CQA-CORE-036 — Have a maintainer follow the README from a clean checkout and record time and missing steps. Keep setup, system boundaries, and operational handover usable by someone other than the original author.

checks.heading: Schema and ownership
checks.text: CQA-DATA-001 — Map entities, relationships, owners, tenant keys, lifecycle, retention, and source-of-truth rules; include blobs, search indexes, caches, analytics, and provider-held state.

checks.heading: Schema and ownership
checks.text: CQA-DATA-002 — Enforce required uniqueness, referential integrity, nullability, checks, and tenant-scoped relationships at an appropriate authoritative boundary; application validation alone may race.

checks.heading: Schema and ownership
checks.text: CQA-DATA-003 — Check identifier stability, uniqueness, guessability implications, foreign-key scope, externally exposed IDs, and collisions across imports or merged systems.

checks.heading: Schema and ownership
checks.text: CQA-DATA-004 — Review normalization or deliberate denormalization against actual access/change patterns; define synchronization and repair for duplicated derived fields.

checks.heading: Schema and ownership
checks.text: CQA-DATA-005 — Trace transaction boundaries around multi-record invariants; exercise partial failure, commit uncertainty, rollback failure, and effects outside the database transaction.

checks.heading: Schema and ownership
checks.text: CQA-DATA-006 — Verify isolation level, lost-update protection, optimistic versions, conditional writes, and lock ordering for concurrent edits; do not infer serial behavior from a single-user run.

checks.heading: Schema and ownership
checks.text: CQA-DATA-007 — Check soft deletion, restoration, cascades, archived records, unique-key reuse, tenant deletion, and background cleanup against the full entity graph.

checks.heading: Schema and ownership
checks.text: CQA-DATA-008 — Verify erasure and retention propagate to derived stores where required, with explicit exceptions for necessary records; prevent deleted data from being resurrected by replay or restore.

checks.heading: Queries and stored resources
checks.text: CQA-DATA-009 — Inspect query plans and representative cardinality for hot paths; confirm useful indexes and their write/storage cost instead of adding indexes without workload evidence.

checks.heading: Queries and stored resources
checks.text: CQA-DATA-010 — Detect N+1 queries, repeated counts, unnecessary columns, cross-tenant scans, chatty transactions, and queries or result sets without bounds.

checks.heading: Queries and stored resources
checks.text: CQA-DATA-011 — Verify stable pagination, cursor semantics, tie-breakers, changing datasets, deleted cursors, and maximum page sizes; avoid silently dropping or duplicating records under documented usage.

checks.heading: Queries and stored resources
checks.text: CQA-DATA-012 — Bound transaction duration, pool size/waits, lock waits, batch size, and query time; inspect leaked connections and retries that multiply pool exhaustion.

checks.heading: Queries and stored resources
checks.text: CQA-DATA-013 — Make replica lag, read-after-write behavior, write routing, and failover assumptions explicit; use authoritative reads where stale state breaks an invariant.

checks.heading: Queries and stored resources
checks.text: CQA-DATA-014 — Check blob upload completion, metadata consistency, checksums where justified, orphan cleanup, authorized download, and expiration of temporary or signed access.

checks.heading: Queries and stored resources
checks.text: CQA-DATA-015 — Verify database roles and application credentials match necessary operations; check that destructive maintenance and migration privileges are not ambient runtime defaults.

checks.heading: Migrations and imports
checks.text: CQA-DATA-016 — Test schema changes against representative data volumes and supported old/new binaries; account for locks, table rewrites, index builds, defaults, and operation-specific database behavior.

checks.heading: Migrations and imports
checks.text: CQA-DATA-017 — Sequence additive changes, compatible readers/writers, backfill, verification, and removal; keep migration history needed for supported installs and upgrades.

checks.heading: Migrations and imports
checks.text: CQA-DATA-018 — Make large backfills restartable, bounded, observable, and safe to resume; identify invalid legacy rows and reconciliation rather than silently discarding them.

checks.heading: Migrations and imports
checks.text: CQA-DATA-019 — Prevent concurrent migration runners and ambiguous migration state; verify startup behavior when schema is ahead, behind, or partially changed.

checks.heading: Migrations and imports
checks.text: CQA-DATA-020 — Distinguish reversible schema operations from irreversible data transformation; define backup/restore or forward-repair prerequisites and rehearse proportionately under module 09.

checks.heading: Migrations and imports
checks.text: CQA-DATA-021 — Validate imports/exports for schema versions, encoding, delimiters, units, timezones, duplicates, formula injection where applicable, partial failures, and authorization.

checks.heading: Migrations and imports
checks.text: CQA-DATA-022 — Check seed/bootstrap/reset scripts for idempotency, environment targeting, synthetic data, privilege, and protection from accidental destructive execution.

checks.heading: API and event contracts
checks.text: CQA-DATA-023 — Verify request, response, and event schemas match actual behavior, including error bodies, status codes, nullable fields, ordering, and content types.

checks.heading: API and event contracts
checks.text: CQA-DATA-024 — Define compatibility for added/removed fields, new enum variants, defaults, unknown fields, numeric representation, and older consumers; generated clients require runtime contract evidence too.

checks.heading: API and event contracts
checks.text: CQA-DATA-025 — Keep HTTP or RPC semantics, retryability, idempotency keys, pagination, rate-limit responses, and timeout behavior explicit for callers.

checks.heading: API and event contracts
checks.text: CQA-DATA-026 — Review bulk operations for per-item authorization, size bounds, atomic-versus-partial semantics, error attribution, and repeat submission behavior.

checks.heading: API and event contracts
checks.text: CQA-DATA-027 — Verify webhook/event authenticity, replay controls, schema version, tenant routing, deduplication, and order assumptions; acknowledge only after the required durable acceptance step.

checks.heading: API and event contracts
checks.text: CQA-DATA-028 — Document event identity, ordering scope, event time versus processing time, retention, poison messages, and safe replay; do not infer exactly-once end-to-end behavior from one broker feature.

checks.heading: API and event contracts
checks.text: CQA-DATA-029 — Keep API specifications and examples current through the normal delivery workflow; identify unsupported endpoints and undocumented internal consumers before retirement.

checks.heading: Caches and derived stores
checks.text: CQA-DATA-030 — Include tenant, user/permission scope, locale, feature/config version, and other response dimensions in cache keys as appropriate; check shared-cache exposure of personalized data.

checks.heading: Caches and derived stores
checks.text: CQA-DATA-031 — Define TTL, invalidation, stale-read allowance, negative caching, and response to permission or entitlement changes; a cache must not become a second uncontrolled authority.

checks.heading: Caches and derived stores
