checks.text: CQA-DATA-032 — Bound memory, key cardinality, stampedes, hot keys, eviction effects, and cache-outage fallback load; verify the backing system can survive intended fallback behavior.

checks.heading: Caches and derived stores
checks.text: CQA-DATA-033 — Verify search/index/materialized-view freshness, rebuild, versioning, tenant filters, and repair after missed updates; expose appropriate consistency expectations to consumers.

checks.heading: Caches and derived stores
checks.text: CQA-DATA-034 — Test replay and rebuild for deterministic or explicitly versioned transformations, duplicate handling, deletion tombstones, and changing business rules.

checks.heading: Shared state and execution order
checks.text: CQA-ASYNC-001 — Inventory concurrently accessed state, including globals, caches, sessions, files, counters, database rows, and external resources; identify the synchronization scope actually used.

checks.heading: Shared state and execution order
checks.text: CQA-ASYNC-002 — Check read-modify-write operations, check-then-act sequences, lazy initialization, and duplicate startup across workers for races and lost updates.

checks.heading: Shared state and execution order
checks.text: CQA-ASYNC-003 — Verify thread/process safety of SDK clients, pools, native libraries, and shared objects; include runtime/context restrictions and supported initialization patterns.

checks.heading: Shared state and execution order
checks.text: CQA-ASYNC-004 — Inspect lock scope, ordering, reentrancy, lease expiry, deadlock, starvation, and work performed while holding a lock; avoid relying on process-local locks for cross-instance guarantees.

checks.heading: Shared state and execution order
checks.text: CQA-ASYNC-005 — Protect against an expired lock holder continuing to write where required, using fencing or equivalent authoritative checks; successful lease acquisition alone does not prove exclusive completion.

checks.heading: Shared state and execution order
checks.text: CQA-ASYNC-006 — Check stale callbacks, reordered responses, reentrant handlers, and concurrent state updates; ensure an older result cannot overwrite newer authoritative state.

checks.heading: Shared state and execution order
checks.text: CQA-ASYNC-007 — Bound parallel tasks, fan-out, recursion, buffers, and pending futures; verify backpressure reaches producers and resource usage does not grow without a limit.

checks.heading: Shared state and execution order
checks.text: CQA-ASYNC-008 — Verify cancellation and task ownership for child work, detached jobs, subscriptions, and request termination; ensure critical committed work has an appropriate durable owner.

checks.heading: Retry and side-effect semantics
checks.text: CQA-ASYNC-009 — Give remote calls finite deadlines and propagate a total operation budget; distinguish connection, response, stream-idle, and total timeouts where relevant.

checks.heading: Retry and side-effect semantics
checks.text: CQA-ASYNC-010 — Retry only appropriate failures with bounded attempts/time, backoff, jitter, and provider hints; prevent retries at multiple layers from multiplying requests unexpectedly.

checks.heading: Retry and side-effect semantics
checks.text: CQA-ASYNC-011 — Treat timeout/disconnect as uncertain outcome for remote writes; reconcile provider state or reuse durable idempotency rather than blindly creating a second effect.

checks.heading: Retry and side-effect semantics
checks.text: CQA-ASYNC-012 — Define idempotency key scope, persistence, payload mismatch behavior, expiry, concurrency handling, and response replay; ensure duplicate requests cannot both pass a pre-check.

checks.heading: Retry and side-effect semantics
checks.text: CQA-ASYNC-013 — Ensure deduplication retention covers the supported retry/replay horizon or document a bounded guarantee; account for retries after process or deployment replacement.

checks.heading: Retry and side-effect semantics
checks.text: CQA-ASYNC-014 — Coordinate state change and message publication with an outbox, transactional facility, or explicit reconciliation strategy where atomicity matters.

checks.heading: Retry and side-effect semantics
checks.text: CQA-ASYNC-015 — Define compensation and repair for multi-system workflows; compensation itself can fail, retry, or become invalid after intervening user actions.

checks.heading: Retry and side-effect semantics
checks.text: CQA-ASYNC-016 — Check fallback, circuit-breaker, and bulkhead behavior against business restrictions; ensure degraded paths do not grant authority, hide data loss, or overwhelm another dependency.

checks.heading: Workers, queues, and schedules
checks.text: CQA-ASYNC-017 — Verify durable enqueue, consumer acknowledgement, visibility/lease duration, crash windows, redelivery, and completion recording against the queue's actual semantics.

checks.heading: Workers, queues, and schedules
checks.text: CQA-ASYNC-018 — Exercise duplicate, delayed, missing, and out-of-order messages; define per-entity ordering and conflict resolution instead of assuming global FIFO.

checks.heading: Workers, queues, and schedules
checks.text: CQA-ASYNC-019 — Bound worker concurrency, queue retention, message size, consumer lag, retries, and dead-letter growth; identify overload rejection or shedding behavior.

checks.heading: Workers, queues, and schedules
checks.text: CQA-ASYNC-020 — Give poison-message quarantine, investigation, redrive, and disposal an owner; verify redrive respects authorization, schema versions, and idempotency.

checks.heading: Workers, queues, and schedules
checks.text: CQA-ASYNC-021 — Make long jobs checkpointable and restartable where required; avoid partial output appearing complete and define cleanup/reconciliation for abandoned attempts.

checks.heading: Workers, queues, and schedules
checks.text: CQA-ASYNC-022 — Check scheduled-work timezone, daylight-saving behavior, missed runs, overlapping runs, leader election, duplicate external schedulers, and behavior after extended downtime.

checks.heading: Workers, queues, and schedules
checks.text: CQA-ASYNC-023 — Revalidate actor/tenant permissions for delayed work where necessary; define what happens after account suspension, deletion, entitlement expiry, or credential rotation.

checks.heading: Workers, queues, and schedules
checks.text: CQA-ASYNC-024 — Ensure job payloads are version-compatible across rolling deployments; support or intentionally retire queued old work and observe resulting failures.

checks.heading: Lifecycle and failure containment
checks.text: CQA-ASYNC-025 — Separate startup, readiness, liveness, and dependency health semantics; avoid a liveness response that creates restart storms during a dependency outage.

checks.heading: Lifecycle and failure containment
checks.text: CQA-ASYNC-026 — Stop accepting work, drain bounded in-flight tasks, release leases, and close owned resources on shutdown; account for the platform's actual termination deadline.

checks.heading: Lifecycle and failure containment
checks.text: CQA-ASYNC-027 — Exercise cold starts, restarts during writes, network partitions, connection resets, disk/full quota, exhausted pools, and provider throttling in authorized bounded environments.

checks.heading: Lifecycle and failure containment
checks.text: CQA-ASYNC-028 — Confirm overload signals and degraded behavior are visible to operators and callers; include recovery behavior after backlog or dependency restoration.

checks.heading: Lifecycle and failure containment
checks.text: CQA-ASYNC-029 — Check that recovery, replay, or failover cannot create two active writers or duplicate side effects; state which system is authoritative during transition.

checks.heading: Lifecycle and failure containment
checks.text: CQA-ASYNC-030 — Verify stale DNS/connections, rotated credentials, time skew, and changed configuration do not require an undocumented manual restart or silently leave part of the fleet broken.

checks.heading: Dependency identity and lifecycle
checks.text: CQA-BUILD-001 — Inventory direct/transitive runtime and development packages, vendored code, binaries, containers, plugins, generators, actions, and downloaded build tools with their actual consumers.

checks.heading: Dependency identity and lifecycle
checks.text: CQA-BUILD-002 — Verify package identity, registry, publisher/provenance, repository, necessity, and maintenance; investigate typosquatting, dependency confusion, unexpected registry fallback, and fabricated AI suggestions.

checks.heading: Dependency identity and lifecycle
checks.text: CQA-BUILD-003 — Inspect install/build scripts, postinstall hooks, native extensions, and remote downloads for unexpected execution or network access; avoid exposing unrelated credentials during installation.

checks.heading: Dependency identity and lifecycle
checks.text: CQA-BUILD-004 — Use supported package tooling and appropriate committed lockfiles; confirm CI uses the intended frozen/locked install behavior rather than silently resolving a different graph.

checks.heading: Dependency identity and lifecycle
checks.text: CQA-BUILD-005 — Review floating versions, Git references, mutable container tags, unverified binaries, and remote script execution; select pinning/integrity controls and update ownership appropriate to exposure.

checks.heading: Dependency identity and lifecycle
checks.text: CQA-BUILD-006 — Check runtime/framework/compiler/base-image support windows and upgrade paths against current primary documentation; record exact versions rather than assuming a named major version is supported.

checks.heading: Dependency identity and lifecycle
checks.text: CQA-BUILD-007 — Scan the actual lockfiles, runtime artifacts, OS packages, images, and relevant native components; distinguish scanner coverage gaps from absence of vulnerabilities.

checks.heading: Dependency identity and lifecycle
checks.text: CQA-BUILD-008 — Triage advisories by affected version/configuration, reachable paths, exploit preconditions, exposure, available fixes, and compensating controls; time-bound suppressions with an owner.

checks.heading: Dependency identity and lifecycle
checks.text: CQA-BUILD-009 — Remove unnecessary dependencies and duplicate libraries; evaluate replacement cost, API behavior, licenses, and security rather than selecting the smallest package count blindly.

checks.heading: Dependency identity and lifecycle
checks.text: CQA-BUILD-010 — Retain an appropriate component inventory or SBOM with artifact/version context where warranted; coordinate attribution and redistribution obligations with module 11.

checks.heading: Build correctness and reproducibility
checks.text: CQA-BUILD-011 — Verify a clean checkout can install, configure, build, and start with documented supported tools and placeholder configuration; distinguish documented steps from a developer's cached environment.

checks.heading: Build correctness and reproducibility
checks.text: CQA-BUILD-012 — Identify generated inputs, code generators, compiler options, environment-dependent constants, and build-time network requirements; ensure required inputs are versioned or reliably obtainable.

checks.heading: Build correctness and reproducibility
checks.text: CQA-BUILD-013 — Check build determinism and traceability to the degree required by the project; record toolchain, lockfile, source revision, and artifact identity without claiming bit-for-bit reproducibility unless measured.

checks.heading: Build correctness and reproducibility
checks.text: CQA-BUILD-014 — Verify path casing, line endings, executable permissions, locale/encoding, shell behavior, symlinks, filesystem layout, and supported CPU/OS differences that can break clean builds.

checks.heading: Build correctness and reproducibility
checks.text: CQA-BUILD-015 — Inspect bundling, tree shaking, conditional exports, source maps, production/debug flags, and environment replacement for omitted required code or exposed secrets/internal source.

checks.heading: Build correctness and reproducibility
checks.text: CQA-BUILD-016 — Check incremental/remote build caches for correct input keys, cross-branch or cross-tenant contamination, poisoning by untrusted builds, and behavior after cache invalidation.

checks.heading: Build correctness and reproducibility
checks.text: CQA-BUILD-017 — Verify monorepo affected-build logic includes shared types, schemas, generated clients, config, and transitive dependents; ensure changed packages cannot evade necessary checks.

checks.heading: Build correctness and reproducibility
checks.text: CQA-BUILD-018 — Ensure release packaging includes required runtime files, migrations, templates, assets, native libraries, notices, and compatible dependency versions; test the packaged output rather than only source mode.

checks.heading: CI trust and artifact integrity
checks.text: CQA-BUILD-019 — Separate untrusted pull-request execution from privileged workflows; inspect fork triggers, checkout choices, reusable workflows, and contexts that can expose secrets or write tokens.

checks.heading: CI trust and artifact integrity
checks.text: CQA-BUILD-020 — Scope CI tokens, cloud identities, registry access, signing, and deployment permissions to required actions/environments; prefer bounded credentials supported by the platform.

checks.heading: CI trust and artifact integrity
checks.text: CQA-BUILD-021 — Review third-party actions, runners, images, caches, and downloaded tools as supply-chain dependencies; assess pinning, provenance, update, and isolation practices.

checks.heading: CI trust and artifact integrity
checks.text: CQA-BUILD-022 — Confirm intended lint/type/build/security gates actually execute, fail the job on material errors, cover the right paths, and cannot be bypassed by ignored exit codes or misleading status aggregation.

checks.heading: CI trust and artifact integrity
checks.text: CQA-BUILD-023 — Prevent secrets and private data in logs, environment dumps, test reports, source maps, caches, and uploaded artifacts; check retention and artifact access boundaries.

checks.heading: CI trust and artifact integrity
checks.text: CQA-BUILD-024 — Identify the artifact built, reviewed, scanned, promoted, and deployed; detect rebuilding from mutable inputs between approval and deployment or swapping artifact tags.

checks.heading: CI trust and artifact integrity
checks.text: CQA-BUILD-025 — Review branch/release permissions, required reviews, emergency bypasses, and auditability proportionately; verify an accountable path exists even when a small team combines roles.

checks.heading: CI trust and artifact integrity
checks.text: CQA-BUILD-026 — Check concurrent releases, cancelled jobs, partial deployments, environment targeting, and rollback selection for stale artifacts or unintended overwrites.

checks.heading: Configuration and runtime packaging
checks.text: CQA-BUILD-027 — Maintain a typed/validated configuration contract, safe defaults, documented required fields, and environment separation; fail clearly for invalid critical configuration.

checks.heading: Configuration and runtime packaging
checks.text: CQA-BUILD-028 — Distinguish build-time from runtime variables, public from secret variables, and process-local from centrally refreshed config; verify actual precedence and deployed values without exposing secrets.

checks.heading: Configuration and runtime packaging
checks.text: CQA-BUILD-029 — Check container build contexts, ignore rules, layers, image source, dependency stage boundaries, architecture, and runtime files; deletion in a later layer does not remove secrets from earlier layers.

checks.heading: Configuration and runtime packaging
checks.text: CQA-BUILD-030 — Verify the packaged process handles signals, non-root/readonly constraints where intended, writable paths, working directory, health endpoints, and shutdown deadlines; use module 12 for deployed privilege evidence.

checks.heading: Configuration and runtime packaging
checks.text: CQA-BUILD-031 — Confirm feature flags and remote config have ownership, safe behavior when unavailable, change visibility, and consistency expectations across replicas and clients.

checks.heading: Configuration and runtime packaging
checks.text: CQA-BUILD-032 — Document ordinary update cadence, urgent vulnerability response, rollback/forward-repair constraints, and a responsible maintainer before dependencies become unsupported.

checks.heading: Browser UI and full-stack web
checks.text: CQA-PROFILE-001 — Check server/client module boundaries, hydration, serialized props, source maps, and environment injection for private data or server credentials reaching browser code.

checks.heading: Browser UI and full-stack web
checks.text: CQA-PROFILE-002 — Verify server rendering, static generation, edge caching, and streaming use the correct user/tenant context; shared output must not contain personalized state.

checks.heading: Browser UI and full-stack web
checks.text: CQA-PROFILE-003 — Exercise pending, empty, failed, stale, and partial states; prevent duplicate submissions and stale responses from replacing newer user intent.

checks.heading: Browser UI and full-stack web
checks.text: CQA-PROFILE-004 — Check component subscriptions, timers, observers, event handlers, retained DOM, and route changes for leaked resources or repeated side effects.

checks.heading: Browser UI and full-stack web
checks.text: CQA-PROFILE-005 — Verify optimistic updates reconcile server failure, conflict, permission loss, and refetch; do not allow client state to become authoritative for money or access.

checks.heading: Browser UI and full-stack web
checks.text: CQA-PROFILE-006 — Inspect service-worker lifecycle, cache versioning, logout/private-data cleanup, stale offline assets, and mixed frontend/backend releases.

checks.heading: Browser UI and full-stack web
checks.text: CQA-PROFILE-007 — Check navigation/deep links, back/forward behavior, form restoration, locale handling, bundle boundaries, and supported browser APIs against actual product requirements.

checks.heading: Browser UI and full-stack web
checks.text: CQA-PROFILE-008 — Keep UI state and domain rules separable where useful; coordinate semantic interaction, focus, loading/error announcements, and keyboard behavior with the accessibility audit.

checks.heading: Backend, serverless, edge, and realtime
checks.text: CQA-PROFILE-009 — Verify middleware order, proxy trust, authentication context, request-body consumption, exception boundaries, and request-scoped state isolation in the actual framework lifecycle.

checks.heading: Backend, serverless, edge, and realtime
checks.text: CQA-PROFILE-010 — Check cold start, execution-duration limits, ephemeral filesystem, freeze/resume, connection reuse, detached work, and local-state assumptions for serverless/edge targets.

checks.heading: Backend, serverless, edge, and realtime
checks.text: CQA-PROFILE-011 — For WebSocket/subscription/SSE paths, check authorization at connect and during lifetime, tenant routing, reconnect/resume, heartbeat, fan-out bounds, and slow-consumer handling.

checks.heading: Backend, serverless, edge, and realtime
checks.text: CQA-PROFILE-012 — Check GraphQL or flexible-query surfaces for field authorization, nested query cost, batching, pagination, error leakage, and data-loader cache scope where applicable.

checks.heading: Backend, serverless, edge, and realtime
checks.text: CQA-PROFILE-013 — Review multi-process/prefork workers, hot reload, singleton initialization, startup jobs, and context propagation for behavior that differs from single-process development mode.

checks.heading: Mobile, desktop, and offline-first
checks.text: CQA-PROFILE-014 — Check application lifecycle, suspend/resume, process death, background restrictions, interrupted writes, and restart recovery on supported platforms.

checks.heading: Mobile, desktop, and offline-first
checks.text: CQA-PROFILE-015 — Review local storage, secure credential facilities, log/crash exports, clipboard, notifications, and backup behavior for sensitive state and account/tenant switching.

checks.heading: Mobile, desktop, and offline-first
checks.text: CQA-PROFILE-016 — Verify offline queues, conflict resolution, tombstones, identity changes, expired authority, and clock differences; define what happens to pending work after logout or account deletion.

checks.heading: Mobile, desktop, and offline-first
checks.text: CQA-PROFILE-017 — Check deep links, IPC, custom protocols, embedded webviews, file associations, and desktop bridges for caller validation and unintended privileged actions.

checks.heading: Mobile, desktop, and offline-first
checks.text: CQA-PROFILE-018 — Confirm update signatures/integrity where supported, old-client compatibility, data-format migration, rollback limits, permission changes, and interrupted installation behavior.

checks.heading: Mobile, desktop, and offline-first
checks.text: CQA-PROFILE-019 — Exercise reconnect on unstable/metered networks, duplicate push delivery, permission denial, unavailable platform services, and device resource pressure without unbounded retries.

checks.heading: Libraries, CLIs, plugins, and native code
checks.text: CQA-PROFILE-020 — For public packages, verify exported API/types, packaging targets, semantic compatibility commitments, peer dependencies, documented examples, and consumers of the actual published artifact.

checks.heading: Libraries, CLIs, plugins, and native code
checks.text: CQA-PROFILE-021 — For CLI tools, check argument parsing, stdin/TTY behavior, exit codes, stdout versus stderr, signal handling, noninteractive operation, and stable machine-readable output where promised.

checks.heading: Libraries, CLIs, plugins, and native code
checks.text: CQA-PROFILE-022 — Make filesystem writes, overwrite/recursive operations, working-directory assumptions, shell quoting, symbolic links, and partial-output cleanup explicit for automation and local tools.

checks.heading: Libraries, CLIs, plugins, and native code
checks.text: CQA-PROFILE-023 — Check plugin discovery, version compatibility, permission boundaries, dependency conflicts, lifecycle cleanup, and behavior when an extension fails; dynamic usage affects deletion decisions.

checks.heading: Libraries, CLIs, plugins, and native code
checks.text: CQA-PROFILE-024 — For native/FFI code, examine ownership, lifetimes, bounds, alignment, integer conversion, unsafe blocks, ABI/layout compatibility, thread affinity, and error propagation across language boundaries.

checks.heading: Libraries, CLIs, plugins, and native code
checks.text: CQA-PROFILE-025 — Review sandboxing or process isolation for untrusted extensions where required; loading a plugin in-process generally exposes the host's ambient authority.

checks.heading: AI, data pipelines, search, and automation
checks.text: CQA-PROFILE-026 — Separate prompts, retrieval, deterministic domain rules, model calls, parsing, tool selection, execution authority, and persistence; validate outputs before they become code, queries, or actions.

checks.heading: AI, data pipelines, search, and automation
checks.text: CQA-PROFILE-027 — Version model/config/prompt/schema/embedding dependencies where reproducibility matters; define behavior after model retirement, response-format drift, or changed embedding dimensions.

checks.heading: AI, data pipelines, search, and automation
checks.text: CQA-PROFILE-028 — Scope retrieval, vector/search indexes, caches, conversation history, and generated exports to authorized tenants/users; ingestion filters alone cannot establish query-time isolation.

checks.heading: AI, data pipelines, search, and automation
checks.text: CQA-PROFILE-029 — Bound agent/tool loops, token budgets, provider retries, context growth, paid calls, and concurrent sessions; coordinate quality/evaluation and spend evidence with modules 07 and 08.

checks.heading: AI, data pipelines, search, and automation
checks.text: CQA-PROFILE-030 — For ETL/analytics, check event-time windows, late/duplicate records, schema drift, checkpoints, backfill/replay, aggregation units, and reconciliation against the source.

checks.heading: AI, data pipelines, search, and automation
checks.text: CQA-PROFILE-031 — Separate training/evaluation/serving artifacts where relevant; review data leakage, version lineage, rollout compatibility, and safe fallback without inventing model-quality guarantees from unit tests.

checks.heading: AI, data pipelines, search, and automation
checks.text: CQA-PROFILE-032 — For scheduled automation, inventory triggers outside the repository, identity/permissions, overlapping runs, idempotency, credential expiry, and an owned disable/recovery path.

checks.heading: Games, realtime simulation, embedded, and specialist products
checks.text: CQA-PROFILE-033 — For games/simulation, check frame/tick budgets, allocation spikes, asset lifetime, scene/state transitions, object pooling reset, save/load versioning, and deterministic replay where promised.

checks.heading: Games, realtime simulation, embedded, and specialist products
checks.text: CQA-PROFILE-034 — For multiplayer, verify authoritative state, client prediction/reconciliation, ordering, lag/disconnect/rejoin, abuse boundaries, and identity/entitlement checks outside client code.

checks.heading: Games, realtime simulation, embedded, and specialist products
checks.text: CQA-PROFILE-035 — For embedded/IoT, review watchdog behavior, bounded memory, real-time deadlines, power-loss-safe writes, firmware update integrity/recovery, and hardware/driver dependencies.

checks.heading: Games, realtime simulation, embedded, and specialist products
checks.text: CQA-PROFILE-036 — For financial/inventory/booking systems, trace conservation and exclusivity invariants, reconciliation, concurrent reservations, expiry, decimal precision, and compensating actions.

checks.heading: Games, realtime simulation, embedded, and specialist products
checks.text: CQA-PROFILE-037 — For large files/media/geospatial/scientific workloads, check streaming versus full buffering, coordinate systems/units, precision, malformed inputs, native codec limits, and bounded processing.

checks.heading: Games, realtime simulation, embedded, and specialist products
checks.text: CQA-PROFILE-038 — For regulated or safety-sensitive systems, identify applicable specialist assurance and accountable reviewers; this general library cannot establish compliance or replace hazard analysis.

checks.heading: Meaningful verification
checks.text: CQA-QA-001 — Map critical invariants and failure modes to existing checks, bounded manual evidence, or an explicit gap; coverage percentages and test counts are not substitutes for this mapping.

checks.heading: Meaningful verification
checks.text: CQA-QA-002 — Choose a focused unit, integration, contract, end-to-end, property, or manual check based on the boundary at risk; do not require every test category for every change.

checks.heading: Meaningful verification
checks.text: CQA-QA-003 — Verify assertions observe meaningful outcomes and durable side effects, not only mocked calls or implementation structure; test data must make an incorrect implementation fail.

checks.heading: Meaningful verification
checks.text: CQA-QA-004 — Inspect mocks/fakes for drift from provider, database, queue, clock, filesystem, and authorization semantics; use appropriate boundary evidence for material differences.

checks.heading: Meaningful verification
checks.text: CQA-QA-005 — Include important negative and transition cases such as stale authority, duplicate submission, crash/retry windows, old schema/client versions, and cancellation after a side effect where applicable.

checks.heading: Meaningful verification
checks.text: CQA-QA-006 — Verify checks run with production-relevant modes and packaged artifacts when those differ from development; an in-memory database may not exercise actual transaction or lock behavior.

checks.heading: Meaningful verification
checks.text: CQA-QA-007 — Keep tests independent of order, ambient environment, current date, shared mutable accounts, and uncontrolled network state; control nondeterminism when it affects reproducibility.

checks.heading: Meaningful verification
checks.text: CQA-QA-008 — Investigate flakiness and quarantines with an owner, gap statement, and expiry; never delete a valuable check solely to make CI pass.

checks.heading: Meaningful verification
checks.text: CQA-QA-009 — Retain only distinct necessary regression/boundary assurance; remove one-off, obsolete, duplicate, trivial, or implementation-mirroring session checks and orphan fixtures/dependencies.

checks.heading: Meaningful verification
checks.text: CQA-QA-010 — Confirm scripts and runners propagate failures, execute intended tests, and do not silently pass after zero tests, skipped suites, ignored exit codes, or stale result uploads.

checks.heading: Meaningful verification
checks.text: CQA-QA-011 — Run focused verification for changes and directly affected flows; broaden or repeat only after relevant changes, failures, or unresolved dependencies rather than a per-session quota.

checks.heading: Meaningful verification
checks.text: CQA-QA-012 — Record commands, revision/environment, actual results, skipped checks, limitations, and bounded manual steps; distinguish planned, simulated, and executed verification.

checks.heading: Diagnosis and measured efficiency
checks.text: CQA-QA-013 — Trace a critical operation across request, job, database, and provider boundaries using appropriate correlation; avoid exposing credentials, private prompts, or unnecessary personal data.

checks.heading: Diagnosis and measured efficiency
checks.text: CQA-QA-014 — Log actionable failures with cause and context, and distinguish expected rejection from internal failure; avoid swallowed errors, noisy duplicate logs, and success metrics emitted before commit.

checks.heading: Diagnosis and measured efficiency
checks.text: CQA-QA-015 — Bound log/metric/trace volume and label cardinality, sampling, payload size, and retention; observability must not create an unbounded cost or resource path.

checks.heading: Diagnosis and measured efficiency
checks.text: CQA-QA-016 — Measure hot-path latency distributions, workload shape, dataset size, concurrency, and resource use before proposing performance refactors; record the baseline and changed result.

checks.heading: Diagnosis and measured efficiency
checks.text: CQA-QA-017 — Inspect algorithmic complexity, repeated serialization, allocations, memory retention, blocking event loops, excessive network calls, and unbounded computation where workload evidence warrants it.

checks.heading: Diagnosis and measured efficiency
checks.text: CQA-QA-018 — Check resource budgets and performance under supported worst-case inputs, realistic data growth, cold/warm cache, and saturation; averages can hide tail failures and memory growth.

checks.heading: Diagnosis and measured efficiency
checks.text: CQA-QA-019 — Ensure application signals can reveal failed invariants, stuck jobs, backlog, dependency degradation, and migration failures; coordinate operational alerts and ownership with module 10.

checks.heading: Diagnosis and measured efficiency
checks.text: CQA-QA-020 — Verify debug/profiling endpoints, verbose modes, and diagnostics are appropriately controlled in deployed environments and that retained artifacts serve a continuing purpose.

checks.heading: Ownership and maintainers
checks.text: CQA-QA-021 — Have a maintainer follow setup/build/run instructions from a clean checkout; record missing steps and unavailable prerequisites rather than relying on the original author's environment.

checks.heading: Ownership and maintainers
checks.text: CQA-QA-022 — Document system boundaries, domain invariants, data authority, external dependencies, important decisions, and known limits in a concise maintained source of truth.

checks.heading: Ownership and maintainers
checks.text: CQA-QA-023 — Assign ownership for shared modules, migrations, dependencies, releases, urgent fixes, scheduled jobs, and recovery; identify gaps when the original author is unavailable.

checks.heading: Ownership and maintainers
checks.text: CQA-QA-024 — Match code review depth to risk and include AI-generated changes; verify an accountable reviewer can explain the behavior and evidence behind material changes.

checks.heading: Ownership and maintainers
checks.text: CQA-QA-025 — Keep branch/merge/release practices understandable and proportionate, with a route for urgent repair and a record of exceptional bypasses; avoid accidental overwrites of concurrent work.

checks.heading: Ownership and maintainers
checks.text: CQA-QA-026 — Link runbooks to architecture decisions, recovery dependencies, artifact versions, and known rollback limits; perform the specialist recovery checks before claiming recovery is proven.

checks.heading: Ownership and maintainers
checks.text: CQA-QA-027 — Define debt items through actual cost, failure risk, owner, smallest useful remedy, and revisit trigger; avoid backlogs consisting only of preferences or indefinite rewrites.

checks.heading: Ownership and maintainers
checks.text: CQA-QA-028 — Finish with verified findings, reduction outcomes, justified retentions, unresolved usage/evidence, accepted risks, and a sequenced remediation plan; do not imply a report alone fixes the project.

checks.heading: Establish the complete boundary
checks.text: **CQA-01-01** Record project, source/deployed revisions, environments, audit window and timezone, owners, authorized access, allowed test surfaces, spending ceiling and stop conditions. Identify production dependencies used by staging or local development.

checks.heading: Establish the complete boundary
checks.text: **CQA-01-02** Enumerate cloud organizations/accounts/projects, regions, hosting, VPSs, SaaS, payment methods and reseller arrangements. Include former providers, employee-managed accounts and services billed outside the main cloud invoice. Mark inaccessible accounts Not verified.

checks.heading: Establish the complete boundary
checks.text: **CQA-01-03** Trace costly user journeys from entry point through authorization, admission, reservation, queue, worker, provider, persistence and delivery. Include administrative actions, public demos, mobile/desktop clients, SDKs, imports, exports, webhooks and support tools.

checks.heading: Establish the complete boundary
checks.text: **CQA-01-04** Inventory shared infrastructure and ownership boundaries. Separate application spend from common databases, networks, observability, CI and account-level quotas. Identify who can change global settings and who receives bills.

checks.heading: Establish the complete boundary
checks.text: **CQA-01-05** Classify assets and features as active, disabled, retired, planned or unknown. Confirm disabled features cannot still be invoked through APIs, old clients, scheduler entries or retained credentials.

checks.heading: Establish the complete boundary
checks.text: **CQA-01-06** Inventory physical capacity as well as money: disk/inodes, memory, CPU/GPU, DB connections, queue depth, file descriptors, sockets, IPs, provider quotas and worker slots. A fixed-price server can still be exhausted.

checks.heading: Establish the complete boundary
checks.text: **CQA-01-07** Include local agents, unattended browser sessions, developer scripts, notebooks, evaluation runs, test credentials and externally hosted automations if they consume project funds or shared resources.

checks.heading: Billing units and attribution
checks.text: **CQA-01-08** Record provider, service/SKU, billing unit, unit scale, currency, region, pricing source and retrieval date. Distinguish tokens from requests, characters from messages, decimal GB from GiB, and elapsed duration from rounded billable duration.

checks.heading: Billing units and attribution
checks.text: **CQA-01-09** Document fixed fees, minimums, tiers, rounding, failed-request charging, ingress/egress, retrieval, storage, per-seat charges, taxes, discounts, credit expiry, commitments and overage rules. Verify the rules that materially affect this project's estimate.

checks.heading: Billing units and attribution
checks.text: **CQA-01-10** Reconcile invoice/usage exports to resources, jobs and features over the same period. Explain unknown/unallocated spend, currency conversion, invoice lag and adjustments. A missing tag or zero dashboard value is not proof of no cost.

checks.heading: Billing units and attribution
checks.text: **CQA-01-11** Establish cost attribution to environment, feature, tenant and outcome where feasible. Include unattributed shared costs explicitly and use a documented allocation driver; do not count the same charge in multiple totals.

checks.heading: Billing units and attribution
checks.text: **CQA-01-12** Separate provider cost, customer price, product credits and capacity units. Document conversion, precision and rounding for each. A credit is not automatically one currency unit or one provider request.

checks.heading: Billing units and attribution
checks.text: **CQA-01-13** Protect pricing and attribution configuration from untrusted inputs. Verify a client cannot select a privileged billing owner, free cost code, arbitrary provider credential or cheaper accounting class for expensive work.

checks.heading: Economics and exposure
checks.text: **CQA-01-14** Measure representative cost per successful outcome, including failed attempts, retries, validation, moderation, downstream calls, storage, delivery and attributable shared cost. Keep success criteria and denominator consistent.

checks.heading: Economics and exposure
checks.text: **CQA-01-15** Model ordinary, heavy legitimate, launch/burst, retry-storm and abusive usage. Include advertised maximum plan usage, slow consumers, long-lived sessions and inactive accounts retaining assets.

checks.heading: Economics and exposure
checks.text: **CQA-01-16** For every expensive path, identify a measured or conservative per-operation upper bound and the control enforcing it. Treat unbounded fan-out, duration or output as unknown exposure rather than inventing a finite estimate.

checks.heading: Economics and exposure
checks.text: **CQA-01-17** Estimate remaining financial exposure after a stop: accepted/in-flight work, backlog that cannot be cancelled, provider reporting delay, stop propagation, accrued usage and fixed commitments. Avoid double counting queued and in-flight operations.

checks.heading: Economics and exposure
checks.text: **CQA-01-18** Compare revenue excluding applicable pass-through taxes with variable costs, payment fees, expected refunds/fraud and support burden under the same scenario. Separate contribution margin from fully allocated profit.

checks.heading: Economics and exposure
checks.text: **CQA-01-19** Assess plan pooling, unlimited claims, free tier resets, annual/monthly mismatch and shared customer accounts. Record deliberate subsidies or loss leaders with an owner and bounded budget.

checks.heading: Economics and exposure
checks.text: **CQA-01-20** Estimate optimization payback after implementation effort, migration, reliability, support and rollback costs. Avoid adding infrastructure whose total burden exceeds credible savings.

checks.heading: Verification and prioritization
checks.text: **CQA-01-21** Select test dimensions explicitly: identity/role/plan, tenant, credential, route/version, region/replica, sync/async, normal/failure state, billing/reset boundary and cache state. Inspect all materially distinct admission paths and expand samples after inconsistent results.

checks.heading: Verification and prioritization
checks.text: **CQA-01-22** Use synthetic identities/data, low balances and controllable provider stubs first. Set request/concurrency/duration ceilings, cancellation and cleanup before execution. A test plan alone is Not verified runtime behavior.

checks.heading: Verification and prioritization
checks.text: **CQA-01-23** For live provider checks, confirm allowed environment, destinations, maximum billable calls and budget. Avoid real recipient spam, bulk account creation, uncontrolled load and third-party abuse testing. Record which provider effects remain untested.

checks.heading: Verification and prioritization
checks.text: **CQA-01-24** Attach expected/actual results, request/job/ledger/provider IDs, starting and ending counters, errors and elapsed time. Redact keys, personal data, payment details and sensitive payloads while preserving correlation.

checks.heading: Verification and prioritization
checks.text: **CQA-01-25** Prioritize active material financial loss or capacity exhaustion for incident containment; treat reproducible unbounded public spending or a material quota race as potential release blockers. Set thresholds from project risk and available funds, not a universal amount.

checks.heading: Verification and prioritization
checks.text: **CQA-01-26** Record workflow state separately from check status. Assign action, owner, dependency, acceptance test, effort, rollback and due/review date. Accepted risk needs an accountable decision and expiry; it does not turn a failed control into Pass.

checks.heading: Discover authoritative schedules
checks.text: **CQA-02-01** Inspect system/user cron, timers, Windows Task Scheduler, hosting/Coolify schedules, application timers, queue repeaters, DB schedulers, CI schedules and external automation providers. Include synthetic checks, analytics exports and uptime monitors.

checks.heading: Discover authoritative schedules
checks.text: **CQA-02-02** Cover production, staging, previews, old releases, disaster-recovery environments, personal sandboxes, all known regions/accounts and shared infrastructure. Reconcile discovered jobs against code and declared architecture.

checks.heading: Discover authoritative schedules
checks.text: **CQA-02-03** Record each scheduler ID, executable/workflow revision, credentials, owner, consumer, business purpose, cadence/timezone, enabled state, last/next run, typical/max duration and downstream cost chain.

checks.heading: Discover authoritative schedules
checks.text: **CQA-02-04** Check overlapping runs, per-replica registration, leader changes, deployment duplication, daylight-saving transitions, catch-up after downtime and scheduler misfire policies. Confirm intended behavior during clock changes and timezone edits.

checks.heading: Discover authoritative schedules
checks.text: **CQA-02-05** Identify duplicate polling/sync loops, obsolete migrations, ownerless notifications, synthetic traffic generating real jobs and tasks still running after trial, tenant, feature or environment retirement.

checks.heading: Discover authoritative schedules
checks.text: **CQA-02-06** Bound each job's runtime, work units, pagination, fan-out, concurrency, retry/backoff and backfill horizon. Include failed/no-op runs, empty scans and jobs that schedule their own successors.

checks.heading: Discover authoritative schedules
checks.text: **CQA-02-07** Verify leases and overlap controls under slow runs, lost locks and restarts. A lease expiry must not silently authorize duplicate irreversible provider effects.

checks.heading: Discover authoritative schedules
checks.text: **CQA-02-08** Reconcile scheduler status to execution logs, queue state and provider usage. An enabled job with no log access and a disabled job with residual queue work both need explicit evidence gaps.

checks.heading: Resources, subscriptions and commitments
checks.text: **CQA-02-09** Inventory VMs, containers, clusters, GPU instances, databases/replicas, object stores, volumes, snapshots, backups, image registries, public IPs, load balancers, gateways, DNS zones and paid network features.

checks.heading: Resources, subscriptions and commitments
checks.text: **CQA-02-10** Inspect stopped workloads for attached storage, reserved addresses, snapshots, replicas, licenses and commitments. Confirm which charges continue despite no application traffic.

checks.heading: Resources, subscriptions and commitments
checks.text: **CQA-02-11** Find abandoned previews, branch databases, development environments, stale deployment images and resources outside infrastructure-as-code state. Inspect failed/partial provisioning and deleted projects' residual assets.

checks.heading: Resources, subscriptions and commitments
checks.text: **CQA-02-12** Inventory SaaS seats, dormant members, paid add-ons, domains/certificates where charged, support plans, marketplace subscriptions and organization-wide licenses. Check whether removing a user actually releases a paid seat.

checks.heading: Resources, subscriptions and commitments
checks.text: **CQA-02-13** Record renewal/notice dates, contractual minimums, non-cancellable commitments, trial/credit expiry, auto-upgrades and top-ups. Distinguish avoidable usage from charges already committed.

checks.heading: Resources, subscriptions and commitments
checks.text: **CQA-02-14** Match resources and renewals to current owners and consumers. Search invoices/payment records for providers absent from current source and verify legitimate shared use before classifying them as waste.

checks.heading: Resources, subscriptions and commitments
checks.text: **CQA-02-15** Check tagging/ownership drift and environment TTL policies. Exemptions need an owner, reason and review date; a TTL must not delete essential recovery or customer data automatically.

checks.heading: Reduce or retire work
checks.text: **CQA-02-16** Classify each candidate as retire, consolidate, reduce, retain with justification or investigate. Include baseline cost, expected savings range, risk, dependencies and decision owner.

checks.heading: Reduce or retire work
checks.text: **CQA-02-17** For retained schedules, justify cadence against freshness requirements. Compare batch/event-driven processing, conditional requests, change detection, empty-work skipping and consolidation using total operating cost.

checks.heading: Reduce or retire work
checks.text: **CQA-02-18** Right-size necessary resources using representative peaks, recovery requirements and measured headroom. Compare scale-to-zero or shutdown savings against startup latency and residual charges.

checks.heading: Reduce or retire work
checks.text: **CQA-02-19** Remove obsolete schedules at their authoritative scheduler and update code, CI, infrastructure definitions and repeaters that could recreate them. Confirm old deployments and every replica are covered.

checks.heading: Reduce or retire work
checks.text: **CQA-02-20** Drain or cancel queued/in-flight work under documented integrity rules. Define treatment of reserved credits, partial results, downstream cancellation and user communication.

checks.heading: Reduce or retire work
checks.text: **CQA-02-21** Before deleting data/resources, check shared dependencies, retention obligations, legal holds, restore needs, export requirements and cancellation terms. Execute only within the actual authorized implementation scope.

checks.heading: Reduce or retire work
checks.text: **CQA-02-22** After retirement, revoke obsolete credentials and triggers where appropriate, remove dangling integrations and update inventories/runbooks. Verify revocation does not stop a still-needed shared consumer.

checks.heading: Reduce or retire work
checks.text: **CQA-02-23** Prevent recreation from rollback images, bootstrap scripts, deployment hooks, forgotten CI branches and disaster-recovery templates. Preserve a deliberate restoration path for necessary services.

checks.heading: Prove the result
checks.text: **CQA-02-24** Retain before/after scheduler configuration, queue counts, execution logs, resource state and provider effects. Observe the next trigger or use equivalent bounded verification of the scheduler without waiting for a long billing cycle.

checks.heading: Prove the result
checks.text: **CQA-02-25** Verify essential flows, backups and recovery behavior affected by the reduction. A successful deletion is not evidence that shared consumers remain healthy.

checks.heading: Prove the result
checks.text: **CQA-02-26** Separate immediate usage reduction, projected monthly savings and realized invoiced savings. Record reporting delay, workload changes, credits, fixed commitments and residual retention costs.

checks.heading: Prove the result
checks.text: **CQA-02-27** Assign an owner and date for delayed billing confirmation. Check for recreated resources, continuing renewals and cancellation acknowledgements. Do not close financial verification solely because source files disappeared.

checks.heading: Define the accounting contract
checks.text: **CQA-03-01** Define the unit charged for every costly operation and the authoritative balance/usage store. Specify whether quota measures attempts, successful outcomes, input/output units, reserved capacity, retained bytes or a combination.

checks.heading: Define the accounting contract
checks.text: **CQA-03-02** Document reservation, commit, adjustment, refund, expiry, reset and reconciliation transitions. Distinguish product-credit refunds from actual provider refunds; a failed customer outcome can still cost money.

checks.heading: Define the accounting contract
checks.text: **CQA-03-03** State invariants: accepted liability stays within authorized balance plus explicit bounded overage; one logical debit/refund per defined operation; currency/credit precision is deterministic; customer balances and provider charges are reconciled separately.

checks.heading: Define the accounting contract
checks.text: **CQA-03-04** Separate rolling rate limits, period usage, prepaid credits, storage quota, worker slots and monetary budgets. Exhaustion of any applicable limit must have defined admission and recovery behavior.

checks.heading: Define the accounting contract
checks.text: **CQA-03-05** Record quota scopes and hierarchy: user, member, tenant, organization, project, credential, feature, provider and global account. Apply all required constraints atomically or through a documented conservative admission design.

checks.heading: Define the accounting contract
checks.text: **CQA-03-06** Establish how balances are purchased, granted, expired, transferred and adjusted. Require server-authoritative amounts and scoped admin permissions; log manual grants, overrides and reversals.

checks.heading: Server enforcement and concurrency
checks.text: **CQA-03-07** Enforce current permissions and quota before paid effects on direct APIs, workers, retries, revisions, exports, imports, previews and administrative tools. Include legacy API versions and alternate transports.

checks.heading: Server enforcement and concurrency
checks.text: **CQA-03-08** Verify atomic admission near a balance boundary across simultaneous requests, replicas and regions. A separate read-then-debit or stale cache must not allow overspending.

checks.heading: Server enforcement and concurrency
checks.text: **CQA-03-09** Make multi-unit and batch operations reserve their full bounded liability or incrementally admit each unit. Check partial batches, per-item failures and pagination; one request must not conceal unlimited work.

checks.heading: Server enforcement and concurrency
checks.text: **CQA-03-10** For variable-cost work, reserve a conservative bounded maximum, meter bounded increments or reject when an upper bound cannot be enforced. Define handling when actual usage differs, without silently creating unlimited debt.

checks.heading: Server enforcement and concurrency
checks.text: **CQA-03-11** Test ledger/limiter store outages, timeouts, stale reads, failover and partitions. Paid work needs an explicit fail-closed or strictly bounded degraded allowance; monitor consumption of that allowance.

checks.heading: Server enforcement and concurrency
checks.text: **CQA-03-12** Prevent negative, zero, non-finite, oversized, fractional or overflowing input quantities from bypassing accounting. Use suitable precision and rounding consistently at admission and settlement.

checks.heading: Server enforcement and concurrency
checks.text: **CQA-03-13** Verify usage/budget writes cannot be performed by the client or by unauthorized tenant/admin roles. Check object ownership when a request supplies project, wallet, membership or credential IDs.

checks.heading: Server enforcement and concurrency
checks.text: **CQA-03-14** Verify quota enforcement and ledger state survive restart, restore and redeploy. Restoring a stale DB or rebuilding a counter must not restore already consumed credits without reconciliation.

checks.heading: Idempotency and ambiguous outcomes
checks.text: **CQA-03-15** Scope idempotency keys to principal, operation and request semantics. Same-key/same-payload retries converge; same-key/different-payload requests are rejected or handled by an explicit safe policy.

checks.heading: Idempotency and ambiguous outcomes
checks.text: **CQA-03-16** Bound key size, storage and retention. Retention must cover the actual retry/replay window, or a durable business identifier must prevent repeated financial effects after cache expiry.

checks.heading: Idempotency and ambiguous outcomes
checks.text: **CQA-03-17** Exercise duplicate HTTP requests, queue deliveries, provider callbacks and operator retries. Check logical operation, provider effect, output delivery and ledger settlement independently.

checks.heading: Idempotency and ambiguous outcomes
checks.text: **CQA-03-18** Test crashes before/after reservation, queue publication, provider acceptance, provider completion and local settlement. Ensure recovery neither loses accepted work nor blindly repeats irreversible spending.

checks.heading: Idempotency and ambiguous outcomes
checks.text: **CQA-03-19** Treat an external timeout as an ambiguous result when appropriate. Query/reconcile provider status or use provider idempotency; do not assume no charge or instantly refund and retry without a bound.

checks.heading: Idempotency and ambiguous outcomes
checks.text: **CQA-03-20** Expire stale reservations safely. Verify late workers cannot execute against released capacity without reauthorization, and that heartbeat/lease loss cannot cause both refund and continued paid work.

checks.heading: Idempotency and ambiguous outcomes
checks.text: **CQA-03-21** Define cancellation, disconnect and partial-success policy. Reconcile consumed units, residual output, late completion and refunds; a closed browser or failed stream is not proof that provider work stopped.

checks.heading: Idempotency and ambiguous outcomes
checks.text: **CQA-03-22** Prevent refund/cancellation loops from yielding repeated useful output without net quota consumption. Apply the disclosed policy fairly when the platform or provider failed.

checks.heading: Plan and period boundaries
checks.text: **CQA-03-23** Test trial expiry, failed/delinquent payment, cancellation, scheduled downgrade, upgrade and reactivation with direct costly operations. Do not rely solely on the UI or on timely callbacks.

checks.heading: Plan and period boundaries
checks.text: **CQA-03-24** Define when queued work inherits admission rights and when workers must recheck current rights. Test revocation or downgrade while work is queued/running and contain remaining liability.

checks.heading: Plan and period boundaries
checks.text: **CQA-03-25** Check calendar, subscription-anniversary and rolling resets; record timezone, period IDs, boundary inclusivity, leap-day behavior and clock authority. Concurrent reset/settlement must not double grant or lose usage.

checks.heading: Plan and period boundaries
checks.text: **CQA-03-26** Define whether rollover, promotional and purchased credits expire, their consumption order and caps. Test expiry during reservations and refunds into an expired bucket.

checks.heading: Plan and period boundaries
checks.text: **CQA-03-27** Test multiple memberships, tenant switching, team pooling, member removal and moving projects between organizations. Ensure balances cannot be borrowed from unrelated tenants or multiplied by adding seats/keys.

checks.heading: Plan and period boundaries
checks.text: **CQA-03-28** Test API key rotation, account deletion/recreation, email changes and region changes against period and trial history. Respect the project's privacy/retention rules while preventing unintended re-grants.

checks.heading: Plan and period boundaries
checks.text: **CQA-03-29** Replay delayed, duplicated and out-of-order financial events. Verify the authoritative payment state and effective time drive access and credit changes exactly as intended, with no duplicate grant.

checks.heading: Plan and period boundaries
checks.text: **CQA-03-30** Verify UI, API and support tools show consistent remaining/reserved/used units, reset time and reasons for denial. Indicate estimates or delayed metering honestly and avoid exposing other tenants' usage.

checks.heading: Reconciliation and evidence
checks.text: **CQA-03-31** Reconcile admitted operations, reservations, commits, refunds and adjustments with worker state and provider records. Attribute unexplained discrepancies and duplicate charges rather than silently overwriting balances.

checks.heading: Reconciliation and evidence
checks.text: **CQA-03-32** Protect ledger/audit retention and correction history. Use compensating adjustments where appropriate; restrict destructive edits and ensure debugging logs do not expose secrets or unnecessary payloads.

checks.heading: Reconciliation and evidence
checks.text: **CQA-03-33** Execute the low-balance burst, duplicate, crash, ambiguous-outcome and reset scenarios in [07](07-EXECUTABLE-SCENARIOS-AND-EVIDENCE.md). Record accepted work and provider effects, including after the initial HTTP response.

checks.heading: Admission and distributed limits
checks.text: **CQA-04-01** Inventory public and authenticated costly routes, old versions, GraphQL operations, WebSockets, streaming endpoints, upload initiation/completion, webhooks and worker entry points. Map each to its actual admission control.

checks.heading: Admission and distributed limits
checks.text: **CQA-04-02** Combine sustained rate, burst, concurrency, duration, payload, result-size and spend limits according to resource demand. Requests/minute alone cannot bound a slow stream or expensive batch.

checks.heading: Admission and distributed limits
checks.text: **CQA-04-03** Select keys using authenticated identity/tenant and trustworthy network context. Verify which proxy sets forwarding headers, reject spoofed identity signals and cover direct-origin access where it is exposed.

checks.heading: Admission and distributed limits
checks.text: **CQA-04-04** Test limit sharing across replicas, regions, workers and restarts. Document whether the algorithm is fixed-window, sliding-window, token-bucket or another design, including any boundary burst allowance.

checks.heading: Admission and distributed limits
checks.text: **CQA-04-05** Check alternate route aliases, methods, content types, API versions, case/encoding variations and credential rotation for unintended separate limit buckets. Canonicalization must preserve authorization semantics.

checks.heading: Admission and distributed limits
checks.text: **CQA-04-06** Verify batch APIs, GraphQL aliases/nesting and multi-recipient actions are charged and limited by bounded underlying work. Cover complexity, pagination and response amplification as well as request count.

checks.heading: Admission and distributed limits
checks.text: **CQA-04-07** Bound open connections, streams, subscriptions and polling frequency. Release capacity after disconnect, timeout and worker death; cap reconnect/resubscribe storms and slow readers.

checks.heading: Admission and distributed limits
checks.text: **CQA-04-08** Apply cheap rejection before expensive parsing, database scans, cryptography, media conversion or provider calls where feasible. Bound decompression, parser nesting, regex work and malformed input processing.

checks.heading: Admission and distributed limits
checks.text: **CQA-04-09** Document limiter-state outages and edge/origin disagreement. Ensure degraded operation has a known bound and an alert rather than implicitly allowing unlimited costly work.

checks.heading: Admission and distributed limits
checks.text: **CQA-04-10** Return suitable denial responses and retry guidance without leaking cross-tenant balances. Use 429 for rate rejection where appropriate; if Retry-After is supplied, verify clients respect it and add bounded backoff/jitter.

checks.heading: Admission and distributed limits
checks.text: **CQA-04-11** Bound limiter key cardinality and expiry so rotating attacker-controlled values cannot exhaust the limiter store. Avoid logging one large event for every blocked request during an attack.

checks.heading: Account, trial and promotion abuse
checks.text: **CQA-04-12** Model repeated signups, disposable identities, referral rings, self-referrals, trial resets and promotion stacking. Verify controls at the actual grant/consumption boundary, not only the signup form.

checks.heading: Account, trial and promotion abuse
checks.text: **CQA-04-13** Check anonymous demos, guest accounts, invite flows and onboarding previews for material spending before verification. Define per-visitor, per-account and global free-use exposure.

checks.heading: Account, trial and promotion abuse
checks.text: **CQA-04-14** Inspect coupon validation, redemption concurrency, campaign/recipient scope, expiry and combination rules. Reject client-controlled discounts, currency confusion and duplicate bonus grants.

checks.heading: Account, trial and promotion abuse
checks.text: **CQA-04-15** Ensure referral rewards require the intended qualifying event and cannot be amplified by replayed callbacks, multiple memberships, refunds or immediate cancellations.

checks.heading: Account, trial and promotion abuse
checks.text: **CQA-04-16** Apply risk-based verification and progressive allowances when justified. CAPTCHA, email verification and payment checks supplement server budgets; assess accessibility, privacy, false positives and dependency cost.

checks.heading: Account, trial and promotion abuse
checks.text: **CQA-04-17** Distinguish abusive automation from intended API clients, accessibility tools, shared office/mobile IPs and high-value batch users. Provide a controlled appeal/review route and scoped exceptions with expiry.

checks.heading: Account, trial and promotion abuse
checks.text: **CQA-04-18** Inspect internal/support override paths and compromised admin scenarios. Limit who can grant unrestricted credits, remove blocks or enable overage, and retain accountable audit records.

checks.heading: Messaging, scraping and business flows
checks.text: **CQA-04-19** Bound login, signup, reset, verification-code, contact, invite, email/SMS and resend flows by account, destination, tenant and global provider budget. Avoid using real recipients in tests.

checks.heading: Messaging, scraping and business flows
checks.text: **CQA-04-20** Check SMS/voice destination countries, premium/high-cost routes, message segmentation, repeated OTP sends and telephony fraud. Verify destination policies server-side and include provider-side restrictions where available.

checks.heading: Messaging, scraping and business flows
checks.text: **CQA-04-21** Prevent email contact forms and notification templates from becoming arbitrary relays. Bound recipients, attachments, rendered output and webhook-triggered notification loops; monitor bounces/complaints and sender reputation.

checks.heading: Messaging, scraping and business flows
checks.text: **CQA-04-22** Assess scraping, bulk export and data enumeration for resource amplification and commercial harm. Authorize datasets, bound result sets and pace expensive exports without relying on robots.txt as enforcement.

checks.heading: Messaging, scraping and business flows
checks.text: **CQA-04-23** Check reservation, stock, appointment and game-economy flows for hoarding or artificial scarcity. Bound held capacity, release expiry safely and avoid rewarding repetitive cancel/rebook cycles.

checks.heading: Messaging, scraping and business flows
checks.text: **CQA-04-24** Verify public media, download links, embedding and hotlink access policies. Where signed URLs are used, inspect authorization at issuance, expiry, cache behavior and bounded remaining exposure after revocation.

checks.heading: Messaging, scraping and business flows
checks.text: **CQA-04-25** Treat leaked credentials and unintended open proxies as spending risks. Scope credentials and outbound integrations; prevent user-supplied URLs/models/destinations from turning a feature into an unrestricted paid relay.

checks.heading: Messaging, scraping and business flows
checks.text: **CQA-04-26** Bound callback/replay processing and authenticate integrations before expensive work. Validly signed duplicate events can still cause amplification if deduplication or downstream budgets are missing.

checks.heading: Fairness and response
checks.text: **CQA-04-27** Test noisy-neighbor behavior with synthetic tenants. Protect a legitimate tenant's worker slots, database connections and provider capacity when another reaches its allowance or behaves abusively.

checks.heading: Fairness and response
checks.text: **CQA-04-28** Set priorities, fair queues or reserved capacity where the product needs them. Bound both work items and their weights; prevent one heavy job or high-priority producer from starving others.

checks.heading: Fairness and response
checks.text: **CQA-04-29** Verify suspension/revocation reaches sessions, keys, workers, retries and queued work. Record residual liability from already issued links and remote work that cannot be cancelled.

checks.heading: Fairness and response
checks.text: **CQA-04-30** Keep block evidence proportionate and privacy-conscious. Document reason, scope, operator, expiry/review and recovery, while preserving an appeal route appropriate to the product.

checks.heading: Fairness and response
checks.text: **CQA-04-31** Execute bounded bypass, trial replay, multi-replica and fairness cases from [07](07-EXECUTABLE-SCENARIOS-AND-EVIDENCE.md). Record false positives alongside prevented work and cost.

checks.heading: AI, generation and autonomous work
checks.text: **CQA-05-01** Inventory inference, embeddings, reranking, moderation, OCR, transcription, speech, image/video generation, retrieval stores, hosted tools and evaluation pipelines. Include local GPU rental and resources retained between calls.

checks.heading: AI, generation and autonomous work
checks.text: **CQA-05-02** Enforce server-controlled allowed models, providers, quality, resolution, duration, variants and input/output limits. Reject client-supplied premium selections or credentials that bypass plan rules.

checks.heading: AI, generation and autonomous work
checks.text: **CQA-05-03** Bound total context, retrieved documents, conversation growth, attachments, intermediate results and generated output. Include provider-billed categories not visible in the final user response where applicable.

checks.heading: AI, generation and autonomous work
checks.text: **CQA-05-04** Bound agent turns, tool calls, recursion depth, parallel branches, wall time and total run budget across all children. A per-model-call limit cannot contain an unbounded autonomous loop.

checks.heading: AI, generation and autonomous work
checks.text: **CQA-05-05** Put costly tool execution behind policy and budget checks independent of generated text. Test untrusted documents/tool results attempting to increase workload, change models or trigger repeated paid actions using synthetic fixtures.

checks.heading: AI, generation and autonomous work
checks.text: **CQA-05-06** Reauthorize continuations, retries, revisions, regenerate buttons and resumed runs. Prevent splitting a long task into unlimited nominally free continuations.

checks.heading: AI, generation and autonomous work
checks.text: **CQA-05-07** Verify stream disconnect/cancellation propagation to provider and child tools. Meter actual consumed units, document uncancellable work and prevent automatic retry merely because the client saw no final answer.

checks.heading: AI, generation and autonomous work
checks.text: **CQA-05-08** Define fallback provider/model policy with maximum cost and allowed capabilities. Test outages and throttling; do not silently move to a more expensive or unapproved service.

checks.heading: AI, generation and autonomous work
checks.text: **CQA-05-09** Inspect prompt/result caches for tenant isolation, expiry, actual cache-hit billing and invalidation. Test cache misses/evictions and adversarial unique inputs so budget safety does not depend on optimistic hit rates.

checks.heading: AI, generation and autonomous work
checks.text: **CQA-05-10** Bound evaluation datasets, experiment sweeps, prompt tuning, benchmark retries and developer playgrounds. Attribute evaluation spending separately from production and prevent scheduled tests from multiplying across branches.

checks.heading: Queues and integration chains
checks.text: **CQA-05-11** Bound queue depth/bytes, per-tenant backlog, oldest age, worker concurrency and accepted liability. Apply backpressure before admission when work cannot finish within the promised service or budget.

checks.heading: Queues and integration chains
checks.text: **CQA-05-12** Limit retries at every layer: client, SDK, gateway, worker, workflow and provider. Calculate combined attempt multiplication and bound retry horizon with backoff/jitter.

checks.heading: Queues and integration chains
checks.text: **CQA-05-13** Test poison messages, visibility/lease expiry, worker crashes, redrive and dead-letter replay. Prevent repeated permanent failures from consuming unlimited money or repeatedly notifying users.

checks.heading: Queues and integration chains
checks.text: **CQA-05-14** Bound fan-out across workflows, map/reduce jobs, webhooks and callbacks. Detect self-triggering object updates or bidirectional sync loops; include downstream work in the parent budget.

checks.heading: Queues and integration chains
checks.text: **CQA-05-15** Batch only where it lowers total cost without violating latency or isolation. Count per-item provider units and partial failures, and cap response expansion and intermediate persistence.

checks.heading: Queues and integration chains
checks.text: **CQA-05-16** Compare webhooks/event-driven updates with polling costs and reliability needs. For retained polling, use bounded pagination, cursors/conditional fetches where supported, empty-work skipping and a justified cadence.

checks.heading: Storage, transfers and media
checks.text: **CQA-05-17** Enforce per-file, total stored bytes, object count, temporary storage and tenant quotas. Check multipart uploads, concurrent uploads, overwritten versions, chunked transfer and unknown content lengths.

checks.heading: Storage, transfers and media
checks.text: **CQA-05-18** Issue upload/download credentials only after authorization and bounded admission. Verify actual bytes/object metadata after upload; constrain expiry, object key, content size/type and allowed operations as the platform supports.

checks.heading: Storage, transfers and media
checks.text: **CQA-05-19** Inspect abandoned multipart parts, incomplete uploads, failed exports, thumbnails, transformed copies, object versions, delete markers and orphan records. Cleanup must cover provider state, not only application rows.

checks.heading: Storage, transfers and media
checks.text: **CQA-05-20** Bound archive extraction by expanded size, file count, nesting, CPU/time and disk. Bound image dimensions, video duration, conversion profiles and generated renditions before expensive processing.

checks.heading: Storage, transfers and media
checks.text: **CQA-05-21** Define lifecycle/retention for originals, derivatives, exports, logs and backups. Verify implementation respects active references, shared assets, legal holds and required recovery copies.

checks.heading: Storage, transfers and media
checks.text: **CQA-05-22** Test logical deletion against actual reclaimed capacity and charges. Include versioning, replication, soft-delete, early-deletion/minimum-storage fees and eventual reporting; deletion may incur cost or retain recoverable copies.

checks.heading: Storage, transfers and media
checks.text: **CQA-05-23** Model CDN/origin egress, cross-region/zone transfer, NAT/proxy charges, cache misses, range requests and repeated downloads. Enforce bandwidth/transfer budgets appropriate to public assets and authenticated exports.

checks.heading: Storage, transfers and media
checks.text: **CQA-05-24** Inspect cache-key cardinality, query-string variations, image-transform parameters and cache bypass headers for origin amplification. Preserve authorization and avoid private-content leakage when improving cache reuse.

checks.heading: Database, compute and infrastructure
checks.text: **CQA-05-25** Bound query time, scanned rows/bytes, joins, sort complexity, result size and pagination. Inspect expensive search/reporting paths, missing indexes and user-controlled query patterns with safe plans or bounded fixtures.

checks.heading: Database, compute and infrastructure
checks.text: **CQA-05-26** Cap connection pools and concurrent queries across all app/worker replicas. Test idle transactions, lock contention, reconnect storms and retries against database/provider limits.

checks.heading: Database, compute and infrastructure
checks.text: **CQA-05-27** Review replicas, point-in-time recovery, backup snapshots, indexes and change streams against business needs. Include retention growth and restore/retrieval cost without weakening required recoverability.

checks.heading: Database, compute and infrastructure
checks.text: **CQA-05-28** Inspect serverless duration/memory, autoscaling maximums, minimum instances, GPU allocation and startup behavior. Verify effective organization/service quotas and the cost/capacity tradeoff of scaling ceilings.

checks.heading: Database, compute and infrastructure
checks.text: **CQA-05-29** Bound CPU/memory/temp disk/processes and downstream calls per job or container. Check OOM/crash loops, auto-restarts, rescheduling and overprovisioned idle services.

checks.heading: Database, compute and infrastructure
checks.text: **CQA-05-30** Review public IPs, gateways, cross-region replication, load balancers, health checks and licensed agents. Confirm networking/security tooling costs are attributed and proportionate to the required protection.

checks.heading: CI, development and observability
checks.text: **CQA-05-31** Inventory CI minutes, runner sizes, concurrent builds, test matrices, scheduled pipelines, artifacts, caches, container storage and preview environments. Bound retention and ensure branch deletion/expiry removes dependent resources.

checks.heading: CI, development and observability
checks.text: **CQA-05-32** Prevent untrusted contributions from accessing paid secrets or unrestricted self-hosted runners. Check workflow triggers, permissions, dependency hooks and user-controlled build inputs for unintended paid execution.

checks.heading: CI, development and observability
checks.text: **CQA-05-33** Stop redundant superseded builds when safe; avoid duplicate push/PR/scheduled runs. Inspect flaky-test reruns, failed deployment loops and multi-environment migrations for cost multiplication.

checks.heading: CI, development and observability
checks.text: **CQA-05-34** Bound log/trace/metric ingestion, retention, high-cardinality labels, payload size, debug modes and sampling. Include error storms, user-controlled log text, dashboard queries and export traffic.

checks.heading: CI, development and observability
checks.text: **CQA-05-35** Verify cost/abuse monitoring cannot itself create uncontrolled spend through one paid alert, trace or external analysis call per rejected event. Preserve enough aggregated evidence for investigation.

checks.heading: CI, development and observability
checks.text: **CQA-05-36** Inspect test and staging services for real email/SMS sends, paid model calls, production webhooks, duplicate analytics and unbounded synthetic users. Use isolated credentials and explicit budgets.

checks.heading: CI, development and observability
checks.text: **CQA-05-37** Check security scanners, uptime checks, backup verification, analytics enrichment, maps/geocoding, search APIs and licensed datasets for execution/seat/retention charges and unnecessary duplicate subscriptions.

checks.heading: Budget architecture
checks.text: **CQA-06-01** Record monetary and capacity budgets, periods, currencies, owners, thresholds and action levels for global account, environment, feature, tenant and provider. Define which essential functions retain a bounded emergency allowance.

checks.heading: Budget architecture
checks.text: **CQA-06-02** Classify every provider control as notification, forecast, prepaid balance, contractual cap, quota, request rejection or automated action. Document actual coverage, delay and exceptions; do not call a notification a hard spending cap.

checks.heading: Budget architecture
checks.text: **CQA-06-03** Verify effective provider settings and permissions in the deployed account. Include auto-top-up, overage, paid-plan upgrade, credit expiry, tier changes, shared organizations and delegated accounts.

checks.heading: Budget architecture
checks.text: **CQA-06-04** Where provider controls are absent or delayed, enforce application admission budgets from a trustworthy current ledger or conservative reservations. Include all costly paths and reserve headroom for accepted work and reporting lag.

checks.heading: Budget architecture
checks.text: **CQA-06-05** Identify the maximum residual exposure after each stop mechanism. Include already running jobs, remote uncancellable work, long-lived sessions, queued commitments, storage, renewals and non-cancellable contracts.

checks.heading: Budget architecture
checks.text: **CQA-06-06** Restrict budget increases, limit bypasses and kill-switch changes to accountable roles. Record actor, reason, old/new value, expiry and restoration; prevent client input or generated content from changing them.

checks.heading: Budget architecture
checks.text: **CQA-06-07** Verify budget behavior when metering, config, limiter or provider APIs fail. Choose an explicit fail-closed or bounded degraded policy and ensure recovery cannot replay unlimited accumulated work.

checks.heading: Stop and recovery mechanisms
checks.text: **CQA-06-08** Provide a tested hierarchy of global, provider, feature, tenant and credential stops appropriate to the architecture. Operators must be able to contain one offending tenant without unnecessary wider outage.

checks.heading: Stop and recovery mechanisms
checks.text: **CQA-06-09** Verify a stop blocks new HTTP/API admissions, scheduler triggers, enqueue operations, worker starts, retries, child tasks and alternate interfaces. Measure propagation across replicas/regions and config caches.

checks.heading: Stop and recovery mechanisms
checks.text: **CQA-06-10** Define safe treatment of accepted work: complete bounded essential work, drain, pause or cancel. Reconcile reservations, partial output, customer messages and uncancellable provider charges.

checks.heading: Stop and recovery mechanisms
checks.text: **CQA-06-11** Test expired workers, scheduled retries, delayed callbacks and queue redrive while the stop is active. No path may unintentionally resume spending because it bypasses interactive admission.
