checks.heading: Stop and recovery mechanisms
checks.text: **CQA-06-12** Avoid automatic expensive failover, top-ups or autoscaling that defeats containment. Document protected recovery/security services whose continuing spend is intentional.

checks.heading: Stop and recovery mechanisms
checks.text: **CQA-06-13** Test stop persistence through restart, redeploy, rollback and regional failover. Maintain an accessible operator control path even if the primary application is overloaded.

checks.heading: Stop and recovery mechanisms
checks.text: **CQA-06-14** Reopen gradually using a bounded canary, current balance checks and queue admission limits. Prevent a backlog/retry thundering herd and define when a stop re-engages.

checks.heading: Stop and recovery mechanisms
checks.text: **CQA-06-15** Show honest exhausted-budget/suspended/degraded states. Preserve user work, avoid charging for unstarted operations, document refund policy and provide useful retry guidance without promising an unknown restoration time.

checks.heading: Signals and accountability
checks.text: **CQA-06-16** Measure total/categorical spend, cost per successful outcome, usage velocity, forecast, remaining budget and unattributed costs. Separate measured, estimated, delayed and invoiced values.

checks.heading: Signals and accountability
checks.text: **CQA-06-17** Monitor rejection rate, reservation age, unsettled ledger items, retry multiplication, queue age/depth, active jobs, storage/egress growth and unusual model/destination selection where applicable.

checks.heading: Signals and accountability
checks.text: **CQA-06-18** Detect cost without expected activity, activity without accounting, new providers/SKUs/regions and abrupt unit-price changes. Check credits masking persistent uneconomic usage.

checks.heading: Signals and accountability
checks.text: **CQA-06-19** Set actionable anomaly thresholds using baseline and exposure tolerance. Include absolute and rate-of-change signals so gradual growth and fast bursts are both visible.

checks.heading: Signals and accountability
checks.text: **CQA-06-20** Exercise alert delivery to an accountable person, acknowledgement/escalation and a usable runbook. Record timestamps and operational response delay, not merely a configured email address.

checks.heading: Signals and accountability
checks.text: **CQA-06-21** Keep metrics/log cardinality, retention and alert volume bounded during an attack. Record enough redacted correlation to investigate; do not expose tenant financial information through public metrics.

checks.heading: Incident procedure
checks.text: **CQA-06-22** Assign incident lead, technical owner, billing liaison and communication responsibility appropriate to team size. Define materiality triggers for rapid action and an accessible emergency contact path.

checks.heading: Incident procedure
checks.text: **CQA-06-23** Capture rate, cumulative exposure, affected accounts/tenants/features, active provider work, queue state and last-known-good configuration before evidence changes, provided collection does not delay urgent containment.

checks.heading: Incident procedure
checks.text: **CQA-06-24** Contain at the narrowest effective admission/provider/scheduler boundary; revoke compromised credentials when appropriate. Verify actual downstream usage reduction and record residual costs.

checks.heading: Incident procedure
checks.text: **CQA-06-25** Preserve redacted evidence and make an impact estimate with explicit unknowns. Distinguish platform cost, customer charges, service disruption, abuse attribution and suspected compromise; use security/privacy processes where relevant.

checks.heading: Incident procedure
checks.text: **CQA-06-26** Reconcile ambiguous operations, customer credits/refunds and provider invoices. Provider billing disputes and credits are separate follow-up work; do not assume they will reverse losses.

checks.heading: Incident procedure
checks.text: **CQA-06-27** Restore service only after root cause and bounds are verified. Record corrective controls, acceptance tests, owner, review date and what would trigger renewed containment.

checks.heading: Release, migration and operating review
checks.text: **CQA-06-28** Before launch or a pricing/plan change, verify worst-case permitted usage, effective budgets, exhaustion UX, concurrency accounting, alerts and stop/reopen paths on the release configuration.

checks.heading: Release, migration and operating review
checks.text: **CQA-06-29** During migration, reconcile old/new schedules, queues, ledgers, credentials, resource ownership and provider accounts. Test dual-running costs, cutover routing, idempotency and balance authority.

checks.heading: Release, migration and operating review
checks.text: **CQA-06-30** Verify rollback cannot resurrect retired jobs, reset consumed quota, restore old permissive limits or enable duplicate billing. Track unavoidable overlapping resources until the recovery window closes.

checks.heading: Release, migration and operating review
checks.text: **CQA-06-31** Define a proportionate review cadence for bills, subscriptions, ownerless resources, pricing changes, unused seats, savings confirmation and exception expiry. Reuse existing processes rather than adding unnecessary recurring jobs.

checks.heading: Release, migration and operating review
checks.text: **CQA-06-32** Record ready, conditionally ready, blocked or insufficient evidence for this scope. List material gaps, residual exposure, accepted risks and follow-up owners explicitly; an average pass percentage cannot override a verified blocker.

checks.heading: Required discovery of recurring work and hidden spend
checks.text: Inventory cron entries, system/user timers, Windows Task Scheduler tasks where applicable, hosting/Coolify schedules, CI scheduled workflows, cloud/serverless/database schedulers, queue repeaters, application timers, external SaaS automations, and synthetic monitors. Include production, staging, previews, old deployments, and shared infrastructure across known accounts and regions. Mark inaccessible accounts or scheduler state Not verified.

checks.heading: Required discovery of recurring work and hidden spend
checks.text: For each job, record its scheduler/resource ID, environment, owner, current purpose and consumer, trigger/cadence/timezone, execution duration, last/next run, replicas, overlap policy, retry/backfill behavior, and downstream API/AI/compute/storage/egress usage. Identify ownerless jobs and jobs that continue after a feature, tenant, trial, or environment is retired.

checks.heading: Required discovery of recurring work and hidden spend
checks.text: Reconcile provider resource inventories, subscriptions, invoices, usage exports, and payment records with the declared services and job inventory. Include resources created manually or in previous sessions and providers no longer referenced by current code. Use an explicit billing window and sanitized evidence; missing billing access is a verification gap, not proof of zero spend.

checks.heading: Required discovery of recurring work and hidden spend
checks.text: Separate fixed commitments from usage-based charges. Estimate recurring cost from run frequency, duration, replicas, retries, downstream calls, retained storage, and actual billing units; include no-op/failed runs and applicable minimum charges. Attribute shared costs without double counting and distinguish measured cost from assumptions, credits, and introductory discounts.

checks.heading: Required discovery of recurring work and hidden spend
checks.text: Find duplicate schedules, obsolete health/sync/polling loops, empty-work scans, never-ending retries, overlapping runs, unbounded catch-up, fan-out, and jobs recreated by every replica or deployment. Check whether migration left both old and new environments active. Trace the complete chain of triggered work rather than pricing only the initial job.

checks.heading: Required discovery of recurring work and hidden spend
checks.text: Inventory idle or orphaned VMs, databases, workers, volumes, snapshots, object versions, public IPs, load balancers, previews, registries, paid integrations, and auto-renewing subscriptions/domains. Check log/trace/analytics ingestion, retention, backups, egress, and scheduled CI usage for avoidable recurring charges. A stopped workload may still retain billable resources.

checks.heading: Eliminate unnecessary recurring work and charges
checks.text: Classify each candidate as retire, consolidate, reduce frequency/size/retention, retain with a concrete reason, or investigate. Prioritize actual avoidable spend and uncontrolled exposure; include the action, owner, dependencies, expected savings, and uncertainty in the report.

checks.heading: Eliminate unnecessary recurring work and charges
checks.text: Retire obsolete schedules at their authoritative scheduler and remove unused code/configuration, CI entries, repeaters, and infrastructure definitions that could recreate them. Account for already queued, retrying, and in-flight work; use an appropriate drain/cancel strategy that preserves data integrity. Verify all applicable replicas and old environments stop issuing work.

checks.heading: Eliminate unnecessary recurring work and charges
checks.text: Remove unnecessary paid resources and cancel obsolete service renewals within authorized scope, checking shared consumers, data/recovery needs, cancellation terms, and residual charges first. Pausing a cron, stopping a container, deleting a repository, or revoking a key does not establish that billing has ended.

checks.heading: Eliminate unnecessary recurring work and charges
checks.text: For necessary work, justify its cadence against freshness and business requirements. Where it reduces total complexity and cost, use existing event/webhook mechanisms, batch work, skip empty/unchanged work, reduce payloads and retention, or scale idle capacity down. Do not add a queue, scheduler, service, or paid plan merely to claim optimization; compare total cost and operational burden.

checks.heading: Eliminate unnecessary recurring work and charges
checks.text: Bound executions by runtime, concurrency, batch size, retries/backoff, catch-up window, and spend. Prevent unintended overlap and duplicate effects, and define what happens at a limit or provider outage. Verify that a kill switch also covers schedulers, queue consumers, retries, and downstream work; a disabled UI alone is insufficient.

checks.heading: Eliminate unnecessary recurring work and charges
checks.text: Set an accountable cost owner, actionable spending alerts, and enforceable limits where available for retained work. Review auto-renewal dates, trial/credit expiry, overage settings, and automatic upgrades/top-ups. Include monitoring's own ingestion and execution cost; use an existing low-cost review mechanism rather than creating unnecessary recurring jobs.

checks.heading: Verify that work and charges actually stop
checks.text: Establish pre-change run/usage/spend evidence, verify scheduler and resource state after changes, and observe through the next expected trigger or equivalent bounded scheduler verification. Confirm no queued/recreated work or downstream calls remain. Exercise affected essential flows and recovery checks in proportion to the change; do not delete production data to prove a saving.

checks.heading: Verify that work and charges actually stop
checks.text: Confirm usage and billing changes after the provider's reporting delay and relevant billing period. Separate immediate usage reduction, projected monthly savings, realized savings, fixed commitments, and remaining storage/renewal charges. Record pending confirmation as Not verified, with an owner and follow-up point; do not claim savings from source deletion alone. Provide a compact before/after table: job/resource, purpose, measured or estimated cost, decision, action, retained dependencies, and verification status.

checks.heading: Metering and entitlements
checks.text: Enforce plan limits and permissions on the server for every costly path, including demo, revise, retry, export, upload, image/video generation, email, and SMS paths.

checks.heading: Metering and entitlements
checks.text: Specify when usage is reserved, committed, refunded, and reset. Use atomic accounting or equivalent concurrency protection; test simultaneous requests near the quota boundary.

checks.heading: Metering and entitlements
checks.text: After free usage is exhausted, call each costly API directly to verify denial despite bypassed UI controls. With a small synthetic balance, issue a bounded concurrent burst (for example 20 requests in an isolated environment) and reconcile accepted work, reservations, debits, refunds, and provider effects. Successful work must stay within the authorized balance under the documented accounting rules.

checks.heading: Metering and entitlements
checks.text: Verify retry and duplicate-delivery accounting. Use provider idempotency where supported and reconciliation where an external operation has an ambiguous result; do not promise that every remote charge can be undone.

checks.heading: Metering and entitlements
checks.text: Check reset timezone, billing-period changes, trials, downgrades, multiple memberships, and canceled or delinquent accounts. Display the same rules in the UI; see 13 for authoritative payment state.

checks.heading: Metering and entitlements
checks.text: Scope cost attribution and quotas to user, tenant, project, credential, and global account where appropriate. Shared keys must not let one project exhaust every project's budget.

checks.heading: Traffic and concurrency
checks.text: Apply suitable rate, concurrency, request-size, duration, pagination, token, and upload limits. Cover login, signup, password reset, verification codes, contact forms, and expensive unauthenticated operations.

checks.heading: Traffic and concurrency
checks.text: Combine identity/tenant controls with trustworthy network signals. Distributed attackers and shared-IP legitimate users make an IP-only limiter insufficient.

checks.heading: Traffic and concurrency
checks.text: Verify that limits remain effective across app processes, replicas, workers, restarts, and the edge/origin boundary. Specify behavior when the limiter store is unavailable.

checks.heading: Traffic and concurrency
checks.text: Bound job queues, worker concurrency, leases, retry counts, and poison messages. Expired workers should release reservations without enabling duplicate work.

checks.heading: Traffic and concurrency
checks.text: Add risk-based signup/form abuse defenses where needed. Email verification, delayed free credits, and CAPTCHA may help, but are neither universal requirements nor substitutes for server limits; preserve accessibility.

checks.heading: Traffic and concurrency
checks.text: Give operators a controlled way to suspend abusive accounts, revoke keys/sessions, stop queued work, and disable costly features. Record actions and recovery procedures.

checks.heading: Spend containment and economics
checks.text: Inventory variable-cost AI, storage, egress, compute, messaging, and third-party services. Estimate representative cost per successful outcome and worst-case retry/concurrency exposure.

checks.heading: Spend containment and economics
checks.text: Configure provider hard limits where available and confirm their actual enforcement and reporting delay. Distinguish notification thresholds, prepaid balance, contractual limits, and automatic request rejection.

checks.heading: Spend containment and economics
checks.text: Enforce application budgets and a global kill switch independently where provider controls are absent or delayed. Include in-flight requests, distributed workers, and recovery behavior.

checks.heading: Spend containment and economics
checks.text: Alert on unusual total spend, cost per user, burst volume, repeated failures, and traffic/egress spikes. Verify a notification reaches an accountable person.

checks.heading: Spend containment and economics
checks.text: Model whether plans remain viable at their advertised limits, including payment fees, storage retention, customer support, and abusive but formally permitted usage.

checks.heading: Spend containment and economics
checks.text: Test the exhausted-budget path: preserve user work, explain unavailability honestly, and stop uncontrolled retries without silently switching to a more expensive provider.

checks.heading: Spend containment and economics
checks.text: Enforce storage lifecycle rules for temporary uploads, abandoned exports, object versions, and expired artifacts. Verify cleanup preserves active work, contractual retention, and recovery copies; measure reclaimed capacity and ongoing storage cost.

checks.heading: Additional workload and business boundaries
checks.text: Bound aggregate AI/agent run costs across turns, tools, retries, parallel children and continuations. Enforce permitted model/quality/output choices on the server; test disconnects and costlier fallback behavior.

checks.heading: Additional workload and business boundaries
checks.text: Test reservation expiry, late workers, crashes around provider effects, ambiguous timeouts and refunds after partial success. Unknown remote outcomes require reconciliation rather than assumptions of no charge.

checks.heading: Additional workload and business boundaries
checks.text: Verify quotas persist across reset, restart, restore, key rotation, tenant switching and membership changes. Include queued work when rights expire or are revoked.

checks.heading: Additional workload and business boundaries
checks.text: Assess repeated trials, promotion stacking, referral replay and refund/cancellation loops using bounded synthetic fixtures. Protect legitimate shared-IP/API/accessibility users and record false positives.

checks.heading: Additional workload and business boundaries
checks.text: Check email/SMS/voice destination costs, resend limits, recipient fan-out and notification loops, including a global provider budget. Use stubs or approved sandboxes for recipient tests.

checks.heading: Additional workload and business boundaries
checks.text: Bound storage bytes and object count, multipart/temporary uploads, archive expansion, media transformations, downloads, cache-miss amplification and cross-region egress. Verify logical deletion against retained provider objects.

checks.heading: Additional workload and business boundaries
checks.text: Bound database query work/connections, compute autoscaling, CI/build triggers, previews, artifacts, log/trace ingestion and metric cardinality. Include fixed-price shared infrastructure capacity as well as monetary charges.

checks.heading: Additional workload and business boundaries
checks.text: Verify global/scoped stops cover every entry point and survive restart, rollback and migration. Reopening must recheck budgets and avoid a backlog/retry storm.

checks.heading: Additional workload and business boundaries
checks.text: Reconcile billed units and currency with product credits and successful outcomes. Model maximum advertised usage, expired discounts, residual commitments and unallocated shared cost explicitly.

checks.heading: Scope and inventory
checks.text: FP-SCP-001: Record product, release/build, environment, audit date/timezone, owner, intended decision, and evidence destinations; distinguish current production from designs and upcoming work.

checks.heading: Scope and inventory
checks.text: FP-SCP-002: Inventory active, hidden, flagged, deprecated, partial, and planned features; record actual audience eligibility and identify which promises apply to this release.

checks.heading: Scope and inventory
checks.text: FP-SCP-003: Map user, buyer, administrator, operator, beneficiary, and affected non-user roles; include users who are rejected, inactive, or leaving.

checks.heading: Scope and inventory
checks.text: FP-SCP-004: Define primary jobs, success outcomes, critical journeys, expected frequency, and the consequences of failure; include assisted and manual steps outside the app.

checks.heading: Scope and inventory
checks.text: FP-SCP-005: Record supported clients, devices, input methods, locales, markets, timezones, versions, account types, plans, quotas, and relevant data scale; leave unknowns explicit.

checks.heading: Scope and inventory
checks.text: FP-SCP-006: Inventory dependencies, external providers, integrations, background jobs, human approvals, contractual commitments, and responsible teams; name each source of truth.

checks.heading: Scope and inventory
checks.text: FP-SCP-007: Gather current requirements, designs, help, marketing, contracts, tickets, research, analytics definitions, and incidents; record contradictions instead of silently choosing the most convenient version.

checks.heading: Scope and inventory
checks.text: FP-SCP-008: Select applicable checks and specialist audit handoffs. Exclude unsupported capabilities with reasons; log evidence access limits and the decisions they prevent.

checks.heading: Evidence and classification
checks.text: FP-SCP-009: Link every assessed check to an environment, preconditions, input, method, expected result, observed result, date, and sanitized evidence; another reviewer can repeat the scenario.

checks.heading: Evidence and classification
checks.text: FP-SCP-010: Separate source inspection, prototype observation, staging execution, and production observation. A code path or screenshot alone does not prove the full production journey.

checks.heading: Evidence and classification
checks.text: FP-SCP-011: Verify persistent and downstream effects, not only a toast or HTTP success. Reconcile UI state with records, generated artifacts, deliveries, and accounting where applicable.

checks.heading: Evidence and classification
checks.text: FP-SCP-012: Separate confirmed defects, verification gaps, hypotheses, research insights, and opportunities. An out-of-scope feature request remains an opportunity unless a binding promise makes it a requirement.

checks.heading: Evidence and classification
checks.text: FP-SCP-013: Record verified sample and potentially affected population separately; explain selection, omissions, and the basis of any extrapolation.

checks.heading: Evidence and classification
checks.text: FP-SCP-014: Deduplicate common causes across journeys and audit modules; retain all affected check IDs and use one primary finding owner.

checks.heading: Evidence and classification
checks.text: FP-SCP-015: Store redacted evidence with stable relative references; avoid secrets and unnecessary participant/customer data, and set access and retention for sensitive material.

checks.heading: Evidence and classification
checks.text: FP-SCP-016: Assign severity, confidence, exposure, delivery priority, and launch-blocker decision separately; include user impact, workaround, owner, due date, and acceptance conditions.

checks.heading: Scenario selection matrix
checks.text: FP-SCP-017: Cover the representative success, meaningful rejection, interrupted action, and recovery for each critical journey; link selected scenarios to requirements and checks.

checks.heading: Scenario selection matrix
checks.text: FP-SCP-018: Test high-risk intersections such as revoked role during export, timeout after payment, offline edit followed by deletion, and plan downgrade during a queued job where applicable.

checks.heading: Scenario selection matrix
checks.text: FP-SCP-019: Add scenarios from historical incidents, support recurrence, architecture risks, and customer commitments; expand sampling when results conflict.

checks.heading: Scenario selection matrix
checks.text: FP-SCP-020: Reconcile check statuses and report selected, assessed, failed, not verified, and excluded counts; disclose partial scope and unresolved blockers.

checks.heading: Problem and audience
checks.text: FP-DIS-001: State who experiences the problem, the triggering situation, frequency, severity, current workaround, and desired outcome; cite evidence rather than starting with a requested widget.

checks.heading: Problem and audience
checks.text: FP-DIS-002: Separate symptoms from underlying causes; consider awareness, ability, motivation, policy, information, and process before assuming missing functionality.

checks.heading: Problem and audience
checks.text: FP-DIS-003: Write functional, emotional, and social jobs where relevant; distinguish the buyer's objective from the end user's and from affected third parties.

checks.heading: Problem and audience
checks.text: FP-DIS-004: Segment by need, context, maturity, workflow, constraints, and willingness/ability to adopt; identify whose needs differ or conflict.

checks.heading: Problem and audience
checks.text: FP-DIS-005: Include non-customers, churned users, failed signups, accessibility needs, and low-connectivity contexts when relevant; do not infer the whole market from vocal power users.

checks.heading: Problem and audience
checks.text: FP-DIS-006: Quantify or explicitly mark unknown the cost of the problem, population affected, frequency, and consequence of doing nothing; distinguish observed values from estimates.

checks.heading: Problem and audience
checks.text: FP-DIS-007: Compare current substitutes including spreadsheets, manual services, competing products, and doing nothing; explain why switching would be worthwhile.

checks.heading: Problem and audience
checks.text: FP-DIS-008: Validate the end-to-end ecosystem: upstream inputs, user handoffs, organizational approvals, downstream work, and the part the product can realistically improve.

checks.heading: Strategy and alternatives
checks.text: FP-DIS-009: Connect the opportunity to an agreed product/business outcome; state the causal mechanism and potential second-order effects or cannibalization.

checks.heading: Strategy and alternatives
checks.text: FP-DIS-010: Generate multiple distinct approaches before convergence, using the baseline skill's 5-7 approaches when useful; include process, policy, service, removal, and no-build options.

checks.heading: Strategy and alternatives
checks.text: FP-DIS-011: Challenge the direction using inversion, analogies, SCAMPER, first principles, or an opportunity-solution tree; record evidence separately from speculative ideas.

checks.heading: Strategy and alternatives
checks.text: FP-DIS-012: Compare alternatives on user value, feasibility, adoption burden, strategic fit, risk, ongoing operations, and reversibility; explain selected and rejected options.

checks.heading: Strategy and alternatives
checks.text: FP-DIS-013: Test whether the feature adds complexity, duplicates existing capability, weakens another journey, or requires users to change behavior without sufficient benefit.

checks.heading: Strategy and alternatives
checks.text: FP-DIS-014: Check positioning and differentiation against actual capabilities; avoid assuming competitor feature parity proves demand or that competitor marketing proves behavior.

checks.heading: Strategy and alternatives
checks.text: FP-DIS-015: Evaluate distribution and discovery: how eligible users encounter the feature, understand it, try it, and fit it into existing routines.

checks.heading: Strategy and alternatives
checks.text: FP-DIS-016: Identify whether sales promises, incentives, revenue targets, or a single large customer are distorting the target problem; document explicit strategic exceptions.

checks.heading: Strategy and alternatives
checks.text: FP-DIS-017: Estimate recurring provider, support, moderation, training, migration, and maintenance costs alongside build effort; name constraints that may make an otherwise appealing idea unviable.

checks.heading: Strategy and alternatives
checks.text: FP-DIS-018: Compare short-term relief with longer-term direction, including dependencies, options enabled/foreclosed, and likely responses from ecosystem partners.

checks.heading: Assumptions and decisions
checks.text: FP-DIS-019: List user, problem, solution, business, feasibility, and adoption assumptions; record confidence, evidence age, and what would falsify each material assumption.

checks.heading: Assumptions and decisions
checks.text: FP-DIS-020: Identify the assumption most likely to invalidate the investment; design the cheapest credible test before committing to broad implementation.

checks.heading: Assumptions and decisions
checks.text: FP-DIS-021: Distinguish stated preference, prototype interest, purchase intent, actual use, repeat value, and willingness to pay; do not treat them as equivalent signals.

checks.heading: Assumptions and decisions
checks.text: FP-DIS-022: Define the smallest complete outcome that can be learned from; an MVP must deliver its promised outcome or clearly disclose a prototype/concierge service.

checks.heading: Assumptions and decisions
checks.text: FP-DIS-023: Record proceed, revise, research, defer, or stop with rationale, accountable owner, evidence, open uncertainties, and a review trigger.

checks.heading: Assumptions and decisions
checks.text: FP-DIS-024: Define success, failure, and stop conditions before the pilot; include opportunity cost and the outcome that would justify removing or simplifying an existing feature.

checks.heading: Research question and method
checks.text: FP-RES-001: Express the decision the study will inform, research questions, current assumptions, existing evidence, and what would change the decision.

checks.heading: Research question and method
checks.text: FP-RES-002: Match method to uncertainty: contextual interviews for needs, task observation for usability, diaries for repeated use, surveys for measured attitudes, and experiments for causal comparisons.

checks.heading: Research question and method
checks.text: FP-RES-003: Distinguish generative, evaluative, attitudinal, behavioral, qualitative, and quantitative evidence; avoid claiming prevalence from a small purposive interview sample.

checks.heading: Research question and method
checks.text: FP-RES-004: Review prior research, support, sales, churn, analytics, and incidents before new recruitment; record contradictory and outdated evidence.

checks.heading: Research question and method
checks.text: FP-RES-005: Define inclusion/exclusion criteria, segments, recruitment channel, incentives, and bias risks; distinguish buyers, admins, users, non-users, and assisted users.

checks.heading: Research question and method
checks.text: FP-RES-006: Justify sample coverage against heterogeneous needs and the decision's risk. For estimates/experiments, plan uncertainty or power; for qualitative work, track recurring themes and unresolved segment gaps.

checks.heading: Research question and method
checks.text: FP-RES-007: Include relevant assistive technology, language, device, connectivity, and domain expertise; make participation accessible and allow alternative participation modes.

checks.heading: Research question and method
checks.text: FP-RES-008: Define informed participation, recording choice, withdrawal process, storage/access, redaction, and retention; use additional project-approved review where vulnerable populations or sensitive data are involved.

checks.heading: Research question and method
checks.text: FP-RES-009: Identify real-world harms or consequences from study tasks; use synthetic accounts/data and safe prototypes when purchases, publication, messaging, or deletion are involved.

checks.heading: Guides, interviews, and observation
checks.text: FP-RES-010: Pilot the screener, task instructions, survey, recording setup, and analysis approach; remove ambiguity before the main sessions.

checks.heading: Guides, interviews, and observation
checks.text: FP-RES-011: Ask about specific recent behavior and real workarounds before showing concepts; avoid leading, hypothetical, and double-barreled questions.

checks.heading: Guides, interviews, and observation
checks.text: FP-RES-012: Separate unaided behavior from prompted behavior. Record moderator assistance, prior exposure, task order, and prototype limitations.

checks.heading: Guides, interviews, and observation
checks.text: FP-RES-013: Use realistic tasks framed as goals rather than UI instructions; define observable task completion, critical errors, abandonment, and recovery.

checks.heading: Guides, interviews, and observation
checks.text: FP-RES-014: Observe comprehension, findability, expectation, confidence, and consequences alongside completion time; a fast incorrect result is not a successful task.

checks.heading: Guides, interviews, and observation
checks.text: FP-RES-015: Include first use, repeat use, failed paths, workarounds, and handoffs where relevant; capture environmental interruptions and organizational constraints.

checks.heading: Guides, interviews, and observation
checks.text: FP-RES-016: Keep warm-up/context, deep dive, concept reaction, and wrap-up distinct; do not contaminate problem discovery with an early feature pitch.

checks.heading: Guides, interviews, and observation
checks.text: FP-RES-017: Capture accurate observations and participant wording with consent; distinguish verbatim quotes, paraphrases, observer interpretation, and model-generated synthesis.

checks.heading: Guides, interviews, and observation
checks.text: FP-RES-018: Include disconfirming cases and evidence that challenges the favored solution; avoid selectively quoting enthusiastic participants.

checks.heading: Surveys and quantitative evidence
checks.text: FP-RES-019: Check survey wording, neutral response options, accessible formatting, skip logic, and an appropriate unknown/not-applicable choice.

checks.heading: Surveys and quantitative evidence
checks.text: FP-RES-020: Record invitation denominator, completion denominator, field dates, missing responses, duplicate responses, and recruitment bias; report weighted and unweighted bases where used.

checks.heading: Surveys and quantitative evidence
checks.text: FP-RES-021: Avoid generalizing opt-in customer responses to the total market without justification; disclose non-response, coverage, recall, and desirability bias.

checks.heading: Surveys and quantitative evidence
checks.text: FP-RES-022: Define scales consistently and avoid interpreting incomparable wording, cohorts, or time windows as trends; preserve the exact instrument version.

checks.heading: Surveys and quantitative evidence
checks.text: FP-RES-023: Link behavior measures to the relevant eligible population and observation period; protect privacy when joining session, research, and account data.

checks.heading: Synthesis and action
checks.text: FP-RES-024: Preserve an observation-to-theme-to-insight-to-opportunity trail; use affinity mapping, journey mapping, or JTBD only when they help answer the question.

checks.heading: Synthesis and action
checks.text: FP-RES-025: Report the number and relevant contexts of observations without implying statistical prevalence; separate severity of an observed failure from its unknown population frequency.

checks.heading: Synthesis and action
checks.text: FP-RES-026: Review alternative explanations such as recruitment, moderator assistance, novelty, prototype fidelity, or device limitations; record confidence and disagreements.

checks.heading: Synthesis and action
checks.text: FP-RES-027: Link recommendations to evidence and distinguish research-supported needs from speculative solutions; assign follow-up learning or delivery owners.

checks.heading: Synthesis and action
checks.text: FP-RES-028: Share a redacted synthesis with limitations and decision implications; control access to recordings and highlight reels, and execute the agreed retention/deletion plan.

checks.heading: Synthesis and action
checks.text: FP-RES-029: Check whether research changed a decision and whether later behavior confirmed the insight; schedule reassessment after material audience or workflow changes.

checks.heading: Synthesis and action
checks.text: FP-RES-030: If using AI for transcription or synthesis, verify consent and approved handling, check summaries against source material, and never fabricate participants, quotes, or interview findings.

checks.heading: Release completeness
checks.text: List active features and their acceptance criteria. Distinguish complete behavior, stubs, partially implemented flows, disabled work, and future opportunities.

checks.heading: Release completeness
checks.text: Complete the core journey end to end with realistic synthetic data. Verify resulting records, files, notifications, and user feedback rather than stopping when a button responds.

checks.heading: Release completeness
checks.text: Assess onboarding, defaults, discovery, first successful outcome, and help/recovery routes. Check first-time and returning users separately.

checks.heading: Release completeness
checks.text: Check navigation, deep links, bookmarks, search, exports/imports, and account lifecycle where present. No active action should lead to an unexplained dead end.

checks.heading: Release completeness
checks.text: Verify advertised capabilities, pricing, data freshness, and supported formats match the release. Remove misleading live UI for unavailable features.

checks.heading: Rules and edge cases
checks.text: Check empty and large datasets, invalid or duplicated input, long names, timezone boundaries, locale formatting, and representative user roles.

checks.heading: Rules and edge cases
checks.text: Verify role and plan behavior through direct server operations as well as UI states. Users should receive a clear explanation for unavailable actions.

checks.heading: Rules and edge cases
checks.text: For metered products, check remaining usage, reset times, retries, partial success, and failed-request accounting against the documented rules. Use 08 for enforcement and economics.

checks.heading: Rules and edge cases
checks.text: For billing products, verify plan selection, checkout, trial, downgrade, cancellation, and failed-payment journeys. Use 13 for payment state and entitlement correctness.

checks.heading: Rules and edge cases
checks.text: Test slow networks, provider failure, repeated clicks, refresh during processing, simultaneous edits, and returning after an interrupted session.

checks.heading: Rules and edge cases
checks.text: Verify saved state, undo or recovery where intended, and consistent behavior across pages, clients, and channels.

checks.heading: Product learning
checks.text: Define success metrics for the primary outcomes and instrument only necessary events. Confirm metrics are meaningful and respect consent/data minimization requirements.

checks.heading: Product learning
checks.text: Identify feedback/support paths and a way to prioritize recurrent user failures. Separate usability improvements from unrequested feature expansion.

checks.heading: Product learning
checks.text: Check notification preferences and truthful transactional messages. A completed action and a sent email may have different success states.

checks.heading: Data exchange and support workflows
checks.text: Test exports for complete, correctly scoped records and usable spreadsheet formats. Test supported CSV imports with declared encodings, delimiters, quoted fields, legacy files, malformed rows, and duplicates; report partial failures without silent data loss. Use 01 for access and spreadsheet formula-injection checks where exports can contain untrusted cells.

checks.heading: Data exchange and support workflows
checks.text: Test apostrophes, accents, emoji, and right-to-left text across entry, storage, search, display, and export. Verify translations and locale formatting for the supported markets rather than assuming every field accepts the same character set.

checks.heading: Data exchange and support workflows
checks.text: Verify available admin/support tools let authorized staff investigate account and job state and resolve supported issues without routine direct database edits. Apply least privilege and audit trails under 01; missing tools outside the agreed scope are opportunities.

checks.heading: Data exchange and support workflows
checks.text: Verify optional notification preferences actually suppress the relevant channels without suppressing required account/security notices. Check that customer-facing release notes and help reflect changed behavior.

checks.heading: Problem, outcomes, and boundaries
checks.text: FP-SPC-001: State the evidenced problem, target segments, triggering context, frequency, current workaround, and cost of leaving it unresolved.

checks.heading: Problem, outcomes, and boundaries
checks.text: FP-SPC-002: Define measurable user and business outcomes; distinguish outputs such as shipping a wizard from outcomes such as successful first setup.

checks.heading: Problem, outcomes, and boundaries
checks.text: FP-SPC-003: Document goals and explicit non-goals with rationale, supported markets/clients, first-release boundaries, and future considerations.

checks.heading: Problem, outcomes, and boundaries
checks.text: FP-SPC-004: Record alternatives, selected direction, trade-offs, assumptions, supporting research, and decisions; keep unresolved questions visible with an owner and blocking status.

checks.heading: Problem, outcomes, and boundaries
checks.text: FP-SPC-005: Write role-specific stories that connect capability to benefit; split large stories into independently verifiable outcomes without losing the complete journey.

checks.heading: Problem, outcomes, and boundaries
checks.text: FP-SPC-006: Categorize requirements as Must/Should/Could/Future or explicitly define the project's scheme; challenge an unbounded must-have list.

checks.heading: Problem, outcomes, and boundaries
checks.text: FP-SPC-007: Name contractual deadlines, external dependencies, design/engineering/data/support owners, and feasibility unknowns before making delivery commitments.

checks.heading: Behavior contract
checks.text: FP-SPC-008: Assign stable requirement IDs and link each to stories, designs, implementation/tickets, scenarios, evidence, and the release containing the change.

checks.heading: Behavior contract
checks.text: FP-SPC-009: Define preconditions, inputs, actions, state transitions, persisted output, visible feedback, and downstream consequences for the main success path.

checks.heading: Behavior contract
checks.text: FP-SPC-010: Specify empty, invalid, denied, loading, delayed, partial, failed, canceled, expired, and interrupted states with actionable user feedback.

checks.heading: Behavior contract
checks.text: FP-SPC-011: Define field validation, units, precision, formats, uniqueness, supported size/count limits, and authoritative rules; record why boundaries exist.

checks.heading: Behavior contract
checks.text: FP-SPC-012: Specify role, ownership, tenant, plan, quota, and flag eligibility across UI and direct operations, including changes while work is in flight.

checks.heading: Behavior contract
checks.text: FP-SPC-013: Specify retries, idempotency, conflict behavior, cancellation, undo, and recovery; distinguish timeout/unknown outcome from confirmed failure.

checks.heading: Behavior contract
checks.text: FP-SPC-014: Define data lifecycle, visibility, sharing, archive/delete/restore behavior, exports, and effects on dependent records and external recipients.

checks.heading: Behavior contract
checks.text: FP-SPC-015: Define timing semantics: user timezone, deadlines, recurrence, expiry, freshness, delayed delivery, and processing expectations.

checks.heading: Behavior contract
checks.text: FP-SPC-016: Define imports, integration contracts, required input quality, partial failures, version compatibility, and which system owns each state.

checks.heading: Behavior contract
checks.text: FP-SPC-017: Define accessibility, localization, supported client behavior, performance expectations under a stated workload, and relevant specialist review requirements.

checks.heading: Behavior contract
checks.text: FP-SPC-018: Describe administrative/support actions, observability, user correction/appeal, operational ownership, and any manual work required to fulfill the promise.

checks.heading: Acceptance and measurement
checks.text: FP-SPC-019: Give each required behavior an independently observable acceptance condition; replace vague terms such as fast, intuitive, or seamless with project-specific evidence.

checks.heading: Acceptance and measurement
checks.text: FP-SPC-020: Include representative success, negative, boundary, interruption, and recovery scenarios; specify what must not happen, including duplicate charges or unintended publication.

checks.heading: Acceptance and measurement
checks.text: FP-SPC-021: Define metric numerator, denominator, eligible population, baseline, target or hypothesis, time window, data source, owner, and review date.

checks.heading: Acceptance and measurement
checks.text: FP-SPC-022: Pair desired metrics with harm/cost/quality guardrails; distinguish adoption from successful outcomes and correlation from causal impact.

checks.heading: Acceptance and measurement
checks.text: FP-SPC-023: Mark prototype behavior and mocked dependencies explicitly; do not accept a mock as evidence that a promised integration works.

checks.heading: Acceptance and measurement
checks.text: FP-SPC-024: Define rollout audience, migration needs, support/help changes, rollback or containment, post-launch observation, and stop conditions.

checks.heading: Acceptance and measurement
checks.text: FP-SPC-025: Review critical requirements with the relevant product, design, engineering, data, and operations owners; document disagreement and accepted risk.

checks.heading: Acceptance and measurement
checks.text: FP-SPC-026: Record approved scope changes with rationale and impact on capacity, date, dependencies, and acceptance; move deferred ideas into a separate opportunity backlog.

checks.heading: Acceptance and measurement
checks.text: FP-SPC-027: Reconcile implementation against the final approved behavior, including advertised/help/contractual promises; resolve stale designs and contradictory requirements.

checks.heading: Acceptance and measurement
checks.text: FP-SPC-028: Confirm each must-have has evidence or an explicit verification gap; a completed ticket or passing build alone does not prove the requirement.

checks.heading: Entry, onboarding, and first value
checks.text: FP-JRN-001: Compare marketing, demos, screenshots, sales commitments, pricing, and help with the enabled release; identify materially false promises and unsupported limitations.

checks.heading: Entry, onboarding, and first value
checks.text: FP-JRN-002: Test entry from homepage, campaign, invitation, shared item, bookmark, search result, notification, and deep link where supported; preserve intended destination through sign-in.

checks.heading: Entry, onboarding, and first value
checks.text: FP-JRN-003: Verify guest exploration, signup, verification, sign-in, recovery, and returning sessions where present; no state traps the user without an explanation or recovery route.

checks.heading: Entry, onboarding, and first value
checks.text: FP-JRN-004: Check defaults, examples, sample data, permissions, and prerequisite setup; separate demo content from the user's real records and provide a clear next action.

checks.heading: Entry, onboarding, and first value
checks.text: FP-JRN-005: Complete first value with realistic synthetic input and no undocumented staff intervention; record time, assistance, errors, and the final persisted outcome.

checks.heading: Entry, onboarding, and first value
checks.text: FP-JRN-006: Check skipped, dismissed, resumed, and repeated onboarding; returning users retain progress and are not forced through irrelevant steps.

checks.heading: Entry, onboarding, and first value
checks.text: FP-JRN-007: Test invitations before and after account creation, duplicate/expired/revoked invites, wrong account, and existing organization membership.

checks.heading: Entry, onboarding, and first value
checks.text: FP-JRN-008: Explain requested permissions and their timing; test denial, limited permission, revocation, and later recovery for device or integration access.

checks.heading: Navigation, comprehension, and action
checks.text: FP-JRN-009: Verify names, information hierarchy, labels, icons, and status language match user expectations and remain consistent across surfaces.

checks.heading: Navigation, comprehension, and action
checks.text: FP-JRN-010: Test navigation, back/forward, refresh, open in new tab, unsaved changes, and shared URLs; selected context and state behave as promised.

checks.heading: Navigation, comprehension, and action
checks.text: FP-JRN-011: Check search, filter, sort, pagination, saved views, and no-results states using known records; counts and scope are clear and reset paths work.

checks.heading: Navigation, comprehension, and action
checks.text: FP-JRN-012: Distinguish no data, no permission, loading, filtering to zero results, and fetch failure; do not show a misleading empty state for an error.

checks.heading: Navigation, comprehension, and action
checks.text: FP-JRN-013: Verify forms preserve valid input after errors, identify the affected field, explain correction, and handle keyboard/autofill/paste as supported.

checks.heading: Navigation, comprehension, and action
checks.text: FP-JRN-014: Check units, labels, totals, rounding, freshness, timestamps, and previews against the resulting action; users can understand what will change before committing.

checks.heading: Navigation, comprehension, and action
checks.text: FP-JRN-015: Verify primary actions, disabled actions, and upgrade/permission barriers explain the cause and available remedy without promising access the user cannot obtain.

checks.heading: Navigation, comprehension, and action
checks.text: FP-JRN-016: Check bulk selection across pagination/filters and explain selected count/scope; destructive or expensive bulk actions affect exactly the documented items.

checks.heading: Navigation, comprehension, and action
checks.text: FP-JRN-017: Test create, edit, duplicate, save, preview, publish, archive, restore, and delete where supported; visible status agrees with underlying state.

checks.heading: Navigation, comprehension, and action
checks.text: FP-JRN-018: Check action feedback distinguishes accepted, processing, completed, partially completed, failed, and unknown; completion is not claimed before the promised effect.

checks.heading: Continuity, accessibility, and localization
checks.text: FP-JRN-019: Verify keyboard navigation, focus after dialogs/errors/updates, screen-reader feedback, and accessible labels on critical tasks with relevant specialist review.

checks.heading: Continuity, accessibility, and localization
checks.text: FP-JRN-020: Check zoom/reflow, touch targets, orientation, small screens, virtual keyboard, contrast-dependent signals, motion preferences, and long translated strings in supported clients.

checks.heading: Continuity, accessibility, and localization
checks.text: FP-JRN-021: Test supported locales, right-to-left layout, pluralization, dates, numbers, currencies, names, addresses, and timezone selection without corrupting stored values.

checks.heading: Continuity, accessibility, and localization
checks.text: FP-JRN-022: Check slow networks, reduced bandwidth, long jobs, backgrounding, device sleep, interrupted sessions, and returning later; progress and recovery match the actual state.

checks.heading: Continuity, accessibility, and localization
checks.text: FP-JRN-023: Verify cross-device and cross-channel continuity where promised; local drafts, cloud saves, pending sync, and conflicts are distinguishable.

checks.heading: Continuity, accessibility, and localization
checks.text: FP-JRN-024: Test supported browser/device versions and embedded/in-app contexts where relevant; unsupported clients receive an accurate limitation or fallback.

checks.heading: Continuity, accessibility, and localization
checks.text: FP-JRN-025: Check long, complex, emotional, or high-stakes tasks for understandable instructions, review before submission, and correction routes.

checks.heading: Communication, trust, and retention
checks.text: FP-JRN-026: Verify confirmations, receipts, status messages, and help links identify the right item, actor, time, and next step without disclosing unnecessary data.

checks.heading: Communication, trust, and retention
checks.text: FP-JRN-027: Test channel preferences, per-workspace settings, quiet hours, digest rules, and opt-out; distinguish optional engagement messages from required service/security notices.

checks.heading: Communication, trust, and retention
checks.text: FP-JRN-028: Check notification timing, deduplication, stale links, delayed/out-of-order messages, and actions already completed elsewhere; avoid contradictory state claims.

checks.heading: Communication, trust, and retention
checks.text: FP-JRN-029: Verify reminders and recommendations reflect actual progress and eligibility; completed, canceled, or deleted work does not keep generating irrelevant prompts.

checks.heading: Communication, trust, and retention
checks.text: FP-JRN-030: Evaluate repeat value and reactivation against the user's natural usage cycle; unnecessary daily engagement is not a universal success condition.

checks.heading: Communication, trust, and retention
checks.text: FP-JRN-031: Check feedback/help/support paths in failed and blocked states; users can provide a safe diagnostic reference and receive a realistic response expectation.

checks.heading: Communication, trust, and retention
checks.text: FP-JRN-032: Review upsells, defaults, scarcity claims, consent, cancellation, and destructive flows for misleading pressure, hidden costs, or obstructive steps.

checks.heading: Communication, trust, and retention
checks.text: FP-JRN-033: Confirm documentation, product tours, release notes, and support scripts match current behavior, supported limits, and recovery paths.

checks.heading: Communication, trust, and retention
checks.text: FP-JRN-034: Verify exit, export, cancellation, deletion, and return paths are understandable; clearly distinguish account deletion, data deletion, service cancellation, and sign-out.

checks.heading: Inputs and data boundaries
checks.text: FP-RUL-001: Test absent, null, empty, whitespace-only, zero, negative, and default values where meaningful; validation distinguishes valid zero from missing input.

checks.heading: Inputs and data boundaries
checks.text: FP-RUL-002: Test just below, exactly at, and just above supported length, count, size, precision, and duration limits; UI and server rules agree.

checks.heading: Inputs and data boundaries
checks.text: FP-RUL-003: Check duplicate identifiers, case/whitespace normalization, canonical forms, and uniqueness within the correct scope; errors explain existing/conflicting records.

checks.heading: Inputs and data boundaries
checks.text: FP-RUL-004: Test accents, apostrophes, emoji, combining characters, right-to-left text, multiline values, and long names through input, storage, search, display, and export.

checks.heading: Inputs and data boundaries
checks.text: FP-RUL-005: Verify numeric units, decimal separators, rounding, currency precision, aggregate totals, and conversion rules against approved examples; do not assume all currencies use two decimals.

checks.heading: Inputs and data boundaries
checks.text: FP-RUL-006: Check dates before/at/after boundaries, leap dates, month-end, year-end, DST, timezone changes, recurrence, expiration, and clock skew relevant to the product.

checks.heading: Inputs and data boundaries
checks.text: FP-RUL-007: Verify schema changes, legacy records, unknown enum values, optional fields, and old clients; unsupported versions fail visibly without silently corrupting data.

checks.heading: Inputs and data boundaries
checks.text: FP-RUL-008: Check zero, one, typical, and maximum supported datasets for functional correctness, counts, ordering, pagination, and processing feedback.

checks.heading: Inputs and data boundaries
checks.text: FP-RUL-009: Test missing/deleted dependencies, orphaned references, moved items, and archived parents; actions follow a documented rule rather than creating inaccessible records.

checks.heading: State and concurrency
checks.text: FP-RUL-010: Map allowed state transitions and explicitly reject invalid transitions, including actions attempted after completion, expiry, cancellation, archive, or deletion.

checks.heading: State and concurrency
checks.text: FP-RUL-011: Test double clicks, retries, refresh, browser back, duplicate submissions, and replayed requests; documented idempotency rules prevent unintended duplicate effects.

checks.heading: State and concurrency
checks.text: FP-RUL-012: Simulate timeout after a successful commit; users can discover the real outcome and safely retry without duplicate work or false failure claims.

checks.heading: State and concurrency
checks.text: FP-RUL-013: Test two tabs/devices/editors changing the same record; conflict detection, merge, lock, or last-write behavior is explicit and does not silently lose promised work.

checks.heading: State and concurrency
checks.text: FP-RUL-014: Check actions against stale views after another actor edits/deletes/transfers the item; the result preserves authoritative rules and explains conflicts.

checks.heading: State and concurrency
checks.text: FP-RUL-015: Test revocation, logout, suspension, plan change, and quota exhaustion while a form, export, upload, or background job is already running.

checks.heading: State and concurrency
checks.text: FP-RUL-016: Verify ordering, repeated events, delayed callbacks, and eventual consistency; older updates do not incorrectly reverse a later authoritative state.

checks.heading: State and concurrency
checks.text: FP-RUL-017: Check bulk operations for all-or-nothing versus partial-result behavior, item-level errors, retry scope, and accurate totals after interrupted execution.

checks.heading: State and concurrency
checks.text: FP-RUL-018: Verify cancel and undo at each meaningful stage; distinguish stopping future work, compensating a completed action, and recalling an external effect that cannot be reversed.

checks.heading: State and concurrency
checks.text: FP-RUL-019: Test drafts, autosave, unsaved-change warnings, reconnect, and resume; identify which state is local, pending, committed, or recoverable.

checks.heading: Asynchronous work and dependencies
checks.text: FP-RUL-020: Check queued, running, delayed, stuck, failed, canceled, and completed jobs; progress, timestamps, and user-facing expectations reflect actual state.

checks.heading: Asynchronous work and dependencies
checks.text: FP-RUL-021: Verify bounded retry behavior, actionable terminal failure, reprocessing rules, and who can recover a stuck job; avoid endless silent retries.

checks.heading: Asynchronous work and dependencies
checks.text: FP-RUL-022: Simulate dependency unavailability, slow response, authentication expiry, rate limit, malformed payload, and partial response; each has truthful feedback and a defined fallback.

checks.heading: Asynchronous work and dependencies
checks.text: FP-RUL-023: Test a provider succeeds but local acknowledgement fails, and the reverse; reconcile state before repeating costly or irreversible external operations.

checks.heading: Asynchronous work and dependencies
checks.text: FP-RUL-024: Verify freshness labels, stale caches, polling, refresh, and delayed propagation; stale data is not presented as a guaranteed current value.

checks.heading: Asynchronous work and dependencies
checks.text: FP-RUL-025: Check user-visible latency and capacity limits against the scoped workload; use bounded authorized tests and record behavior at saturation.

checks.heading: Asynchronous work and dependencies
checks.text: FP-RUL-026: Verify failed processing does not silently retain locks, reserve capacity forever, consume undocumented quota, or leave an item in an unrecoverable state.

checks.heading: Import, export, and lifecycle
checks.text: FP-RUL-027: Test supported import encodings, BOM, delimiters, quoted separators/newlines, headers, blank rows, malformed values, legacy versions, and duplicate rows.

checks.heading: Import, export, and lifecycle
checks.text: FP-RUL-028: Verify import preview/mapping, validation, partial success, error file, restart/retry, and rollback where promised; accepted/rejected totals reconcile.

checks.heading: Import, export, and lifecycle
checks.text: FP-RUL-029: Verify exports include the correct scope, fields, record count, timezone/units, encoding, and supported spreadsheet behavior; route formula-injection and access safety to security review.

checks.heading: Import, export, and lifecycle
checks.text: FP-RUL-030: Check generated files for empty/large results, naming, expiry, link access, interrupted download, repeated retrieval, and deletion after the declared retention window.

checks.heading: Import, export, and lifecycle
checks.text: FP-RUL-031: Test attachment/upload type, size, corrupt input, duplicate names, interruption/resume, scan/processing delay, and failed replacement; existing valid content is preserved as promised.

checks.heading: Import, export, and lifecycle
checks.text: FP-RUL-032: Verify ownership, lineage, versions, provenance, and last-updated metadata after copy, merge, import, restore, and transfer.

checks.heading: Import, export, and lifecycle
checks.text: FP-RUL-033: Check archive/delete/restore semantics, cascades, shared links, search indexes, cached views, scheduled work, exports, and notifications; document delayed cleanup and exceptions.

checks.heading: Import, export, and lifecycle
checks.text: FP-RUL-034: Verify deletion/restoration interactions with retained backups and external copies through the specialist data module; do not promise recall or immediate erasure where unsupported.

checks.heading: Import, export, and lifecycle
checks.text: FP-RUL-035: Reconcile data and user-visible state after migration, rollback, provider replacement, and legacy-to-new feature transitions using representative project records.

checks.heading: Import, export, and lifecycle
checks.text: FP-RUL-036: Retest known incidents and verify diagnostics let operators distinguish a failed action from delayed processing without exposing sensitive data.

checks.heading: Identity and organization lifecycle
checks.text: FP-OPS-001: Test signup, verification, login methods, recovery, email change, duplicate identity, and existing-account linking against the approved account rules.

checks.heading: Identity and organization lifecycle
checks.text: FP-OPS-002: Check invitation acceptance by the wrong signed-in account, expired/revoked invite, repeated acceptance, and pre-existing membership; do not silently join the wrong organization.

checks.heading: Identity and organization lifecycle
checks.text: FP-OPS-003: Verify organization switching, default workspace, direct links, recent items, notifications, and search use the intended context and make that context clear.

checks.heading: Identity and organization lifecycle
checks.text: FP-OPS-004: Test role creation/change/removal, ownership transfer, last-owner departure, suspended members, and service accounts where supported; preserve an authorized management route.

checks.heading: Identity and organization lifecycle
checks.text: FP-OPS-005: Check access and explanations for guests, viewers, editors, admins, owners, and support through both UI and direct operations with specialist authorization evidence.

checks.heading: Identity and organization lifecycle
checks.text: FP-OPS-006: Verify offboarding revokes access and handles assigned work, shared content, integrations, scheduled tasks, and ownership according to documented policy.

checks.heading: Identity and organization lifecycle
checks.text: FP-OPS-007: Test organization merge/split, account merge, domain change, and managed provisioning only if supported; document conflict and recovery behavior.

checks.heading: Identity and organization lifecycle
checks.text: FP-OPS-008: Check account suspension, recovery, deletion, re-registration, and restore; explain consequences for collaborators, billing, content, and retained records.

checks.heading: Collaboration and sharing
checks.text: FP-OPS-009: Verify private/shared/public scopes, inherited permissions, guest access, link expiry/revocation, and onward sharing; visibility labels match actual access.

checks.heading: Collaboration and sharing
checks.text: FP-OPS-010: Test simultaneous comments/edits, mentions, assignments, approvals, rejected changes, resolved discussions, and deleted targets where present.

checks.heading: Collaboration and sharing
checks.text: FP-OPS-011: Verify author attribution, version history, change notification, conflict recovery, and undo; users can understand whose change is current.

checks.heading: Collaboration and sharing
checks.text: FP-OPS-012: Check sharing/transferring an item with attachments, child records, external links, and integrations; dependent access follows the documented rule.

checks.heading: Collaboration and sharing
checks.text: FP-OPS-013: Verify approvals and delegation under absence, role revocation, self-approval restrictions, repeated requests, and skipped steps where the workflow requires them.

checks.heading: Plans, usage, and purchases
checks.text: FP-OPS-014: Reconcile pricing copy, available plans, checkout amounts, currency, billing interval, taxes/fees presentation, seat rules, and included allowances with scoped commercial policy.

checks.heading: Plans, usage, and purchases
checks.text: FP-OPS-015: Test trial eligibility, start/end, extension, conversion, cancellation, and re-entry; expiry behavior and retained work are explained before they occur.

checks.heading: Plans, usage, and purchases
checks.text: FP-OPS-016: Verify upgrade/downgrade timing, proration explanation, annual/monthly changes, pending changes, discounts, legacy plans, and grandfathered entitlements where supported.

checks.heading: Plans, usage, and purchases
checks.text: FP-OPS-017: Test successful, failed, canceled, abandoned, duplicated, and delayed checkout; redirect success alone does not prove payment or entitlement activation.

checks.heading: Plans, usage, and purchases
checks.text: FP-OPS-018: Verify pending/failed payment, grace period, recovery, retry, suspension, refund, dispute, and cancellation states through user-facing access and messages.

checks.heading: Plans, usage, and purchases
checks.text: FP-OPS-019: Check seat increases/decreases, invited-but-inactive members, removed members, minimum seats, and ownership transfer against the billable-seat definition.

checks.heading: Plans, usage, and purchases
checks.text: FP-OPS-020: Explain usage units, included amounts, reservations, overage, reset timezone, expiry, and pooling; UI counters reconcile with authoritative accounting.

checks.heading: Plans, usage, and purchases
checks.text: FP-OPS-021: Test zero/near/exact/over quota, simultaneous requests, retried work, partial failure, canceled work, and provider failure against the documented charging rule.

checks.heading: Plans, usage, and purchases
checks.text: FP-OPS-022: Verify downgrading below current usage or storage has an explicit outcome; retained data, blocked actions, grace periods, and restoration are understandable.

checks.heading: Plans, usage, and purchases
checks.text: FP-OPS-023: Test receipts, invoices, billing-contact changes, payment-method updates, cancellation confirmation, and renewal notices as applicable; dates and amounts agree across channels.

checks.heading: Plans, usage, and purchases
checks.text: FP-OPS-024: Check promotions, credits, gifts, refunds, and expiring balances where present; stacking, eligibility, redemption limits, and remaining value follow the scoped policy.

checks.heading: Plans, usage, and purchases
checks.text: FP-OPS-025: Verify exit and reactivation do not introduce unexpected renewal, duplicate subscription, lost promised access, or silent loss of recoverable data.

checks.heading: Integrations and operations
checks.text: FP-OPS-026: Test connect, permission selection, wrong external account, revoked/expired credential, reconnect, and disconnect; users can see the connected identity and sync scope.

checks.heading: Integrations and operations
checks.text: FP-OPS-027: Verify first sync, incremental sync, backfill, duplicate handling, conflict ownership, deletion propagation, lag, and repair for supported integration workflows.

checks.heading: Integrations and operations
checks.text: FP-OPS-028: Check webhook/email/delivery settings, endpoint validation, delivery failure, retry, replay, and disable; distinguish accepted requests from recipient delivery or action.

checks.heading: Integrations and operations
checks.text: FP-OPS-029: Verify authorized support/admin users can inspect account, payment, quota, and job state using appropriate tools and a diagnostic reference.

checks.heading: Integrations and operations
checks.text: FP-OPS-030: Test supported support actions such as retry, quota correction, refund request, reassign, or unlock; require scoped permissions, audit history, and clear irreversible-action feedback.

checks.heading: Integrations and operations
checks.text: FP-OPS-031: Check impersonation or assisted access if supported, including authorization, scope, visible attribution, expiry, and auditability through the security module.

checks.heading: Integrations and operations
checks.text: FP-OPS-032: Verify handoff between automated support and humans preserves context appropriately, provides a real escalation route, and does not fabricate resolution or response times.

checks.heading: Integrations and operations
checks.text: FP-OPS-033: Reconcile help, incident communication, service expectations, staff training, runbooks, and ownership with the actual release and support capacity.

checks.heading: Integrations and operations
checks.text: FP-OPS-034: Confirm support feedback can be linked to recurring product failures without turning every one-off request into a committed feature.

checks.heading: SaaS, enterprise, APIs, and developer tools
checks.text: FP-MOD-001: For SaaS, verify single-user and team activation, workspace setup, plan eligibility, trial expiry, seat/quota changes, and owner departure; test both individual and organization value.

checks.heading: SaaS, enterprise, APIs, and developer tools
checks.text: FP-MOD-002: For enterprise features, check purchased SSO/provisioning/admin policy, domain ownership, managed-account recovery, audit export, and rollout/migration; unsupported enterprise features remain opportunities.

checks.heading: SaaS, enterprise, APIs, and developer tools
checks.text: FP-MOD-003: For APIs/SDKs/CLI tools, complete the documented first successful call from a clean environment; verify examples, credentials, environments, errors, pagination, and supported versions.

checks.heading: SaaS, enterprise, APIs, and developer tools
checks.text: FP-MOD-004: For developer products, test sandbox-to-production transition, key rotation, rate-limit discovery, retries, idempotency, webhook replay, deprecation, and backwards compatibility as promised.

checks.heading: Commerce, marketplaces, and transactional services
checks.text: FP-MOD-005: For commerce, test discovery, variants, stock, cart, address, shipping availability, discounts, checkout, and order confirmation using authoritative stock and price.

checks.heading: Commerce, marketplaces, and transactional services
checks.text: FP-MOD-006: Check concurrent stock changes, price changes in cart, partial fulfillment, backorder, failed delivery, return, exchange, refund, and cancellation; totals and order state reconcile.

checks.heading: Commerce, marketplaces, and transactional services
checks.text: FP-MOD-007: For digital goods, verify payment-to-access timing, license/seat rules, download limits, link expiry, refund effects, and re-download after device/account changes.

checks.heading: Commerce, marketplaces, and transactional services
checks.text: FP-MOD-008: For marketplaces, test buyer, seller, operator, and affected third-party journeys; cover onboarding, listings, matching, trust signals, commission, and supply-demand constraints.

checks.heading: Commerce, marketplaces, and transactional services
checks.text: FP-MOD-009: Verify disputes, fraud reports, seller suspension, payout delay/failure, partial refund, cancellation, and off-platform fulfillment boundaries; each side sees a consistent state.

checks.heading: Commerce, marketplaces, and transactional services
checks.text: FP-MOD-010: For service/booking products, test availability, timezones, holds, concurrent booking, capacity, waiting lists, recurring bookings, rescheduling, no-show, and cancellation deadlines.

checks.heading: Commerce, marketplaces, and transactional services
checks.text: FP-MOD-011: Verify provider absence, customer late arrival, location changes, DST transitions, confirmation/reminders, deposits, and partial service delivery against the promised policy.

checks.heading: Content, learning, community, and discovery
checks.text: FP-MOD-012: For publishing/CMS tools, verify draft, review, preview, schedule, publish, unpublish, version restore, permissions, and syndication; previews and public content match the intended version.

checks.heading: Content, learning, community, and discovery
checks.text: FP-MOD-013: For media products, test supported playback formats, resume, captions, quality changes, downloads/offline rights, geo/plan availability, and interrupted delivery.

checks.heading: Content, learning, community, and discovery
checks.text: FP-MOD-014: For learning products, test enrollment, prerequisites, sequence, progress sync, retakes, grading, completion, certificates, and course updates; completion claims reflect the defined learning evidence.

checks.heading: Content, learning, community, and discovery
checks.text: FP-MOD-015: For communities/UGC, test creation, editing, deletion, reporting, blocking/muting, moderation, appeals, and notification effects; deleted or restricted content follows the declared visibility policy.

checks.heading: Content, learning, community, and discovery
checks.text: FP-MOD-016: Test moderation queues, repeated abuse, malicious reporting, moderator absence, evidence retention, and vulnerable-user protections within the scoped safety process.

checks.heading: Content, learning, community, and discovery
checks.text: FP-MOD-017: For search/recommendation products, use known relevant, irrelevant, ambiguous, misspelled, multilingual, and no-result queries; evaluate relevance, freshness, permissions, and actionable fallback.

checks.heading: Content, learning, community, and discovery
checks.text: FP-MOD-018: Check cold start, feedback correction, preference changes, filter interactions, repeated recommendations, sponsored content labeling, and unintended exclusion of relevant inventory.

checks.heading: AI and automated decision products
checks.text: FP-MOD-019: Define the AI task, supported inputs, intended users, limitations, prohibited uses, human review needs, and what counts as a successful result beyond generating text.

checks.heading: AI and automated decision products
checks.text: FP-MOD-020: Evaluate representative tasks, edge cases, language/segment variation, refusals, and adversarial inputs using a versioned evaluation set with human-reviewed criteria.

checks.heading: AI and automated decision products
checks.text: FP-MOD-021: Test incorrect, fabricated, unsupported, stale, and overconfident output; verify correction, provenance/citations where promised, uncertainty communication, and safe fallback.

checks.heading: AI and automated decision products
checks.text: FP-MOD-022: Test tool permission boundaries, preview/confirmation for consequential actions, duplicate execution, interrupted tool calls, cancellation, and human takeover through specialist security/AI review.

checks.heading: AI and automated decision products
checks.text: FP-MOD-023: Check prompt-injection scenarios in user content and retrieved material through specialist review; product state and user messaging must reflect blocked or incomplete actions truthfully.

checks.heading: AI and automated decision products
checks.text: FP-MOD-024: Verify model/provider changes, nondeterminism, context limits, long conversations, retrieval gaps, latency, cost ceilings, and degraded mode against the scoped quality contract.

checks.heading: AI and automated decision products
checks.text: FP-MOD-025: Check memory/personalization visibility, correction, opt-out/deletion, data freshness, and cross-account boundaries; users understand what is retained and why.

checks.heading: AI and automated decision products
checks.text: FP-MOD-026: For automated recommendations/decisions affecting people, verify explanation, contest/correction, escalation, human accountability, and segment-specific harms with qualified project reviewers.

checks.heading: Mobile, desktop, offline, and connected devices
checks.text: FP-MOD-027: For mobile/desktop apps, test installation, update, first launch, deep links, app permissions, backgrounding, crash recovery, logout, and supported OS versions.

checks.heading: Mobile, desktop, offline, and connected devices
checks.text: FP-MOD-028: Check app-store or platform purchase/restore flows, external versus in-app subscription state, notification opt-in, and device migration where supported.

checks.heading: Mobile, desktop, offline, and connected devices
checks.text: FP-MOD-029: For offline-first products, verify local changes, pending status, conflict resolution, reconnect, account switch, storage exhaustion, and remote deletion; no silent loss of promised work.

checks.heading: Mobile, desktop, offline, and connected devices
checks.text: FP-MOD-030: For hardware/IoT products, verify pairing, identity, connectivity loss, stale readings, calibration, firmware change, safe state, replacement, and ownership transfer as scoped.

checks.heading: Data, workflow, public services, and sensitive use
checks.text: FP-MOD-031: For dashboards/data products, reconcile source lineage, freshness, missing values, dimensions, filters, aggregates, exports, and access scope; distinguish zero, unknown, and unavailable.

checks.heading: Data, workflow, public services, and sensitive use
checks.text: FP-MOD-032: For automation/workflow tools, test triggers, schedules, conditions, branching, retries, loop prevention, approvals, execution history, pause/resume, and version changes during running work.

checks.heading: Data, workflow, public services, and sensitive use
checks.text: FP-MOD-033: For collaborative/design/document tools, verify large documents, embedded assets, real-time edits, version restore, offline merge, export fidelity, and cross-client rendering.

checks.heading: Data, workflow, public services, and sensitive use
checks.text: FP-MOD-034: For lead-generation/service sites, verify inquiry routing, form validation, spam handling, confirmation, appointment/contact fulfillment, and attribution; a submitted form alone does not prove receipt.

checks.heading: Data, workflow, public services, and sensitive use
checks.text: FP-MOD-035: For nonprofit/public-service products, test eligibility, assisted access, language, evidence submission, rejection/appeal, service continuity, and users without conventional account/payment credentials.

checks.heading: Data, workflow, public services, and sensitive use
