checks.text: FP-MOD-036: For healthcare, financial, legal, children's, or other sensitive contexts, identify qualified reviewers, project-specific obligations, consent/guardian needs, accessibility, harm controls, escalation, and audit evidence; generic checklist completion does not establish compliance.

checks.heading: Data, workflow, public services, and sensitive use
checks.text: FP-MOD-037: For games or gamified products, verify progression, saves, rewards, purchases, fairness, account/device migration, multiplayer/social safety, reset seasons, and recovery where applicable.

checks.heading: Data, workflow, public services, and sensitive use
checks.text: FP-MOD-038: For internal tools, verify staff onboarding/offboarding, least-privilege workflow, manual fallback, data corrections, approval accountability, and the real productivity outcome.

checks.heading: Outcome and instrumentation
checks.text: FP-MEA-001: Define primary user outcome, supporting business outcome, leading/lagging indicators, and guardrails; explain how each is expected to respond to the feature.

checks.heading: Outcome and instrumentation
checks.text: FP-MEA-002: Define numerator, denominator, event semantics, unit of analysis, eligibility, period, timezone, and cohort; distinguish user, account, organization, session, and action metrics.

checks.heading: Outcome and instrumentation
checks.text: FP-MEA-003: Record baseline, target or explicit hypothesis, confidence/limitations, metric owner, query/source, and decision date; do not substitute invented benchmarks.

checks.heading: Outcome and instrumentation
checks.text: FP-MEA-004: Define activation as meaningful value rather than a click; distinguish eligible, exposed, tried, completed, repeated, and retained users.

checks.heading: Outcome and instrumentation
checks.text: FP-MEA-005: Define retention/reactivation against the natural job frequency and cohort maturity; seasonal or infrequent use should not automatically be treated as churn.

checks.heading: Outcome and instrumentation
checks.text: FP-MEA-006: Measure task success, time, error, abandonment, recovery, and support demand as relevant; exclude incomplete/canceled tasks transparently rather than hiding them.

checks.heading: Outcome and instrumentation
checks.text: FP-MEA-007: Specify an event dictionary with stable names, trigger, source of truth, properties, version, and permitted data; collect only what the measurement needs.

checks.heading: Outcome and instrumentation
checks.text: FP-MEA-008: Verify consent/opt-out and data handling through the privacy module; report coverage gaps rather than assuming untracked users behave identically.

checks.heading: Outcome and instrumentation
checks.text: FP-MEA-009: Trace known synthetic actions from client through ingestion, storage, transformation, and reporting; check duplicates, missing/late events, retries, and event ordering.

checks.heading: Outcome and instrumentation
checks.text: FP-MEA-010: Reconcile analytics with authoritative successful actions, revenue, usage, and deliveries; distinguish intended, accepted, completed, and failed events.

checks.heading: Outcome and instrumentation
checks.text: FP-MEA-011: Check identity linking, account merges, organization membership, cross-device use, bot/internal traffic, and timezone boundaries for distorted counts.

checks.heading: Outcome and instrumentation
checks.text: FP-MEA-012: Test reporting after schema/event changes, backfills, migrations, consent changes, and feature flags; annotate breaks in comparability.

checks.heading: Analysis quality
checks.text: FP-MEA-013: Segment outcomes by relevant cohort, role, plan, device, locale, accessibility need, acquisition source, and maturity without exposing unnecessary personal data.

checks.heading: Analysis quality
checks.text: FP-MEA-014: Check survivorship, selection, seasonality, small denominators, Simpson's paradox, and concurrent releases before attributing aggregate trends to a feature.

checks.heading: Analysis quality
checks.text: FP-MEA-015: Separate correlation between feature use and retention from causal evidence; already successful users may be more likely to adopt the feature.

checks.heading: Analysis quality
checks.text: FP-MEA-016: Report absolute counts, rates, uncertainty where estimable, observation period, missingness, and exclusions; unknown does not mean zero.

checks.heading: Analysis quality
checks.text: FP-MEA-017: Pair satisfaction/NPS/feedback with observed behavior and respondent context; a higher score alone does not establish better task performance.

checks.heading: Analysis quality
checks.text: FP-MEA-018: Review cost-to-serve, support, latency, quality, safety, accessibility, and business guardrails alongside adoption or revenue gains.

checks.heading: Experiment design and interpretation
checks.text: FP-MEA-019: Write the hypothesis, mechanism, eligible audience, intervention, comparison, primary metric, guardrails, success/failure threshold, and resulting decision before exposure.

checks.heading: Experiment design and interpretation
checks.text: FP-MEA-020: Choose a method suited to traffic, risk, and uncertainty: prototype, concierge pilot, staged rollout, randomized test, or qualified observational analysis.

checks.heading: Experiment design and interpretation
checks.text: FP-MEA-021: For randomized tests, define assignment unit, exposure event, allocation, persistence, exclusion rules, and contamination/interference risks including shared organizations.

checks.heading: Experiment design and interpretation
checks.text: FP-MEA-022: Plan baseline rate/variance, minimum meaningful effect, error criteria, sample/duration, and analysis approach; obtain competent statistical review where needed instead of using a fixed sample heuristic.

checks.heading: Experiment design and interpretation
checks.text: FP-MEA-023: Check assignment/exposure instrumentation, sample-ratio mismatch, variant parity, novelty, carryover, and conflicting experiments before interpreting outcomes.

checks.heading: Experiment design and interpretation
checks.text: FP-MEA-024: Predefine stopping and analysis rules; avoid repeated unplanned peeking, metric switching, or subgroup selection that manufactures a winning result.

checks.heading: Experiment design and interpretation
checks.text: FP-MEA-025: Include natural usage cycles and outcome maturation; distinguish no detectable effect, inconclusive evidence, demonstrated equivalence under a defined margin, and harm.

checks.heading: Experiment design and interpretation
checks.text: FP-MEA-026: Verify experiment eligibility cannot expose unsupported users to dangerous, misleading, or contractually incorrect behavior; use project-approved review for consequential changes.

checks.heading: Experiment design and interpretation
checks.text: FP-MEA-027: Record cost, adverse events, qualitative feedback, and segment differences; explain trade-offs rather than declaring victory from one favorable metric.

checks.heading: Experiment design and interpretation
checks.text: FP-MEA-028: Decide ship, iterate, stop, or gather evidence with owner, rationale, residual uncertainty, rollout/rollback plan, and post-launch review date.

checks.heading: Experiment design and interpretation
checks.text: FP-MEA-029: Verify uplift persists after rollout and does not merely move failure to another funnel step; retire unused flags and obsolete event variants.

checks.heading: Experiment design and interpretation
checks.text: FP-MEA-030: Close the loop from recurring support/research insight to a tested change and measured outcome; retain unsuccessful experiments to avoid repeating disproven assumptions.

checks.heading: Release and rollout
checks.text: FP-LIF-001: Reconcile the release inventory with approved scope, acceptance evidence, current promises, deferred work, and known limitations; no active stub is presented as complete.

checks.heading: Release and rollout
checks.text: FP-LIF-002: Verify critical end-to-end journeys in the intended environment with realistic synthetic data, applicable roles/plans, and representative failure/recovery paths.

checks.heading: Release and rollout
checks.text: FP-LIF-003: Confirm each blocker is fixed and verified or explicitly accepted by the accountable owner with reason, expiry, compensating controls, and affected audience.

checks.heading: Release and rollout
checks.text: FP-LIF-004: Record unresolved verification gaps and their decision impact; do not claim production readiness solely from source review or a passing build.

checks.heading: Release and rollout
checks.text: FP-LIF-005: Define rollout cohort, eligibility, flag defaults, staged exposure, observation windows, owner, and stop/rollback triggers linked to measurable signals.

checks.heading: Release and rollout
checks.text: FP-LIF-006: Verify flag combinations, disabled paths, entitlement interactions, and removal plans; turning off a UI flag does not reverse already-completed external effects.

checks.heading: Release and rollout
checks.text: FP-LIF-007: Rehearse data/content/configuration migration, legacy compatibility, user-visible transition, and rollback/forward recovery in a disposable environment as appropriate.

checks.heading: Release and rollout
checks.text: FP-LIF-008: Define what happens to queued jobs, edits in progress, open checkout, shared links, drafts, and old clients during deployment or rollback.

checks.heading: Release and rollout
checks.text: FP-LIF-009: Prepare accurate launch copy, pricing/help updates, onboarding, release notes, training, and notices for changed or removed behavior.

checks.heading: Release and rollout
checks.text: FP-LIF-010: Confirm support ownership, monitoring, escalation, staffing, provider capacity, manual fulfillment, and known-issue communication match launch scale.

checks.heading: Release and rollout
checks.text: FP-LIF-011: Test production configuration and bounded smoke journeys after deployment; verify state and effects rather than assuming staging results transfer automatically.

checks.heading: Release and rollout
checks.text: FP-LIF-012: Record release decision, build/configuration, date, decision-maker, evidence, residual risks, follow-up owners, and the next outcome review.

checks.heading: Post-launch and portfolio health
checks.text: FP-LIF-013: Review activation, task success, errors, support, costs, guardrails, and relevant segments against the agreed baseline after adequate observation.

checks.heading: Post-launch and portfolio health
checks.text: FP-LIF-014: Investigate adoption shortfalls as discovery, comprehension, eligibility, performance, trust, or value problems before adding more features.

checks.heading: Post-launch and portfolio health
checks.text: FP-LIF-015: Confirm promised fast-follow work is delivered or explicitly re-scoped; update help and commitments when direction changes.

checks.heading: Post-launch and portfolio health
checks.text: FP-LIF-016: Review low-use and high-maintenance features for merge, simplify, improve, reposition, or retire; consider infrequent but essential use and contractual commitments.

checks.heading: Post-launch and portfolio health
checks.text: FP-LIF-017: Revisit research and assumptions after audience shifts, pricing changes, provider/model changes, incidents, or unexpected usage patterns.

checks.heading: Post-launch and portfolio health
checks.text: FP-LIF-018: Track recurring product debt such as inconsistent rules, abandoned onboarding, stale permissions, temporary manual work, and unresolved edge cases with ownership.

checks.heading: Post-launch and portfolio health
checks.text: FP-LIF-019: Update scenario coverage from incidents and real support patterns; remove obsolete checks only with a documented scope or behavior change.

checks.heading: Post-launch and portfolio health
checks.text: FP-LIF-020: Check the roadmap balances urgent defects, foundational work, learning, and new opportunities against actual team capacity and dependencies.

checks.heading: Deprecation, replacement, and exit
checks.text: FP-LIF-021: Inventory active users, rare-but-critical users, contracts, integrations, saved links, automations, data, and dependents before retiring a capability.

checks.heading: Deprecation, replacement, and exit
checks.text: FP-LIF-022: Define replacement or manual alternatives, migration/export route, notice period, assistance, owner, and exceptions based on project commitments.

checks.heading: Deprecation, replacement, and exit
checks.text: FP-LIF-023: Verify deprecation notices reach affected users through suitable channels and accurately describe dates, timezone, impact, and required action.

checks.heading: Deprecation, replacement, and exit
checks.text: FP-LIF-024: Test export, migration, redirect/fallback, old-client behavior, queued work, and archived/shared content before cutover; confirm data reconciliation where needed.

checks.heading: Deprecation, replacement, and exit
checks.text: FP-LIF-025: Prevent new purchases or enrollment into a retiring capability unless terms are accurate; resolve prepaid value, credits, refunds, and renewals according to policy.

checks.heading: Deprecation, replacement, and exit
checks.text: FP-LIF-026: Verify cleanup of UI, flags, scheduled tasks, provider resources, documentation, analytics, support scripts, and retained data with accountable owners.

checks.heading: Deprecation, replacement, and exit
checks.text: FP-LIF-027: Monitor breakage, support demand, migrated outcomes, remaining dependents, and unintended cost after removal; retain an appropriate recovery/containment route.

checks.heading: Deprecation, replacement, and exit
checks.text: FP-LIF-028: Close the lifecycle decision with evidence, lessons, remaining obligations, and ownership; avoid declaring success while unresolved users or data are stranded.

checks.heading: Acceptance Criteria
checks.text: Admin can enter SSO provider URL in organization settings

checks.heading: Acceptance Criteria
checks.text: Team members see "Log in with SSO" button on login page

checks.heading: Acceptance Criteria
checks.text: SSO login creates a new account if one does not exist

checks.heading: Acceptance Criteria
checks.text: SSO login links to existing account if email matches

checks.heading: Acceptance Criteria
checks.text: Failed SSO attempts show a clear error message

checks.heading: Scope and service decisions
checks.text: **SCP-01 — Migration objective.** Agree the problem, destination options, constraints, and measurable success with the project owner.

checks.heading: Scope and service decisions
checks.text: **SCP-02 — Source and destination inventory.** Compare repositories, provider dashboards, billing, DNS, deployment configuration, and actual traffic.

checks.heading: Scope and service decisions
checks.text: **SCP-03 — Move or retain decision.** Review each database, storage bucket, queue, identity provider, analytics service, and email integration separately.

checks.heading: Scope and service decisions
checks.text: **SCP-04 — Shared infrastructure inheritance.** Map shared host, proxy, backup, network, and control-plane controls to each application.

checks.heading: Scope and service decisions
checks.text: **SCP-05 — Dependency graph and order.** Trace startup, runtime, deployment, recovery, and external event dependencies.

checks.heading: Scope and service decisions
checks.text: **SCP-06 — Actual production baseline.** Capture versions, core journeys, traffic patterns, error rates, latency, data volumes, and job backlog before changing anything.

checks.heading: Scope and service decisions
checks.text: **SCP-07 — Exposure and sensitive data.** Identify users, tenants, regulated or confidential data, regions, and supported access paths.

checks.heading: Scope and service decisions
checks.text: **SCP-08 — Access and account ownership.** Inspect registrar, DNS, hosting, registry, backup, source-control, and vendor administrator access.

checks.heading: Scope and service decisions
checks.text: **SCP-09 — Time and recovery targets.** Agree maintenance tolerance, acceptable data-loss window, recovery time, observation period, and decision deadlines.

checks.heading: Scope and service decisions
checks.text: **SCP-10 — Change scope control.** Compare planned runtime, schema, framework, domain, identity, and provider changes.

checks.heading: Platform discovery and economic constraints
checks.text: **SCP-11 — Platform feature discovery.** Inspect edge functions, image services, cron dashboards, deploy hooks, managed add-ons, caches, and hidden scheduled work.

checks.heading: Platform discovery and economic constraints
checks.text: **SCP-12 — Provider limits and support.** Check actual account quotas, region availability, networking, backup limits, maintenance rules, and support contacts.

checks.heading: Platform discovery and economic constraints
checks.text: **SCP-13 — Network and data transfer cost.** Estimate trial transfers and steady-state traffic between application, database, storage, users, and backup destinations.

checks.heading: Platform discovery and economic constraints
checks.text: **SCP-14 — Operational cost and responsibility.** Compare managed service costs with operator time, patching, monitoring, recovery, and incident coverage.

checks.heading: Platform discovery and economic constraints
checks.text: **SCP-15 — Contract and exit constraints.** Review data export rights, termination notice, licenses, account transfer, domain ownership, and retention obligations.

checks.heading: Platform discovery and economic constraints
checks.text: **SCP-16 — Hybrid network design.** Measure paths between migrated components and services intentionally left managed.

checks.heading: Future portability
checks.text: **SCP-17 — Rebuildable configuration.** Attempt to reconstruct a disposable environment from approved manifests and documented external settings.

checks.heading: Future portability
checks.text: **SCP-18 — Export completeness.** Inventory export formats for records, files, identities, permissions, audit history, and application metadata.

checks.heading: Future portability
checks.text: **SCP-19 — Credential and key ownership.** Identify encryption keys, signing keys, service accounts, and provider-owned key dependencies.

checks.heading: Future portability
checks.text: **SCP-20 — Domain and URL control.** Trace canonical domains, embedded asset URLs, redirects, signed links, and provider subdomains.

checks.heading: Future portability
checks.text: **SCP-21 — Independent recovery.** Have a backup operator locate artifacts and rebuild outside the source deployment account in a disposable environment.

checks.heading: Future portability
checks.text: **SCP-22 — Decision and exclusions.** Review unresolved dependencies, unavailable evidence, and conditional future capabilities.

checks.heading: Build and configuration parity
checks.text: **RUN-01 — Runtime and architecture compatibility.** Build on the actual target OS and CPU architecture with required runtime, native modules, binaries, and system libraries.

checks.heading: Build and configuration parity
checks.text: **RUN-02 — Reproducible production artifact.** Build the recorded source revision with lockfiles and approved tool versions; capture the image digest or artifact identifier.

checks.heading: Build and configuration parity
checks.text: **RUN-03 — Build-time versus runtime variables.** Change public and private configuration across build and startup, inspecting generated bundles and server behavior.

checks.heading: Build and configuration parity
checks.text: **RUN-04 — Framework adapter and execution model.** Exercise serverless, edge, static export, SSR, API routes, and platform adapters actually used.

checks.heading: Build and configuration parity
checks.text: **RUN-05 — Environment completeness.** Compare required variables, defaults, multiline secrets, URLs, locale, time zone, and production mode across environments.

checks.heading: Build and configuration parity
checks.text: **RUN-06 — Registry and deployment access.** Pull the approved private artifact using destination and recovery identities, including token expiry and registry outage rehearsal.

checks.heading: Build and configuration parity
checks.text: **RUN-07 — Build isolation and resource pressure.** Run a bounded build beside representative application and backup workload.

checks.heading: Build and configuration parity
checks.text: **RUN-08 — Generated and static assets.** Compare asset manifests, public paths, image transforms, localization files, fonts, and source-map exposure.

checks.heading: Process and deployment behavior
checks.text: **RUN-09 — Listen address and startup.** Start the production artifact through the destination deployment mechanism and inspect bind address, port, command, and working directory.

checks.heading: Process and deployment behavior
checks.text: **RUN-10 — Readiness and liveness.** Delay a required dependency and simulate an unhealthy process while observing proxy and restart behavior.

checks.heading: Process and deployment behavior
checks.text: **RUN-11 — Graceful termination.** Stop or redeploy a process during an in-flight request, upload, and worker task.

checks.heading: Process and deployment behavior
checks.text: **RUN-12 — Restart and boot ordering.** Reboot a disposable destination and restart the control plane, network, application, and required services.

checks.heading: Process and deployment behavior
checks.text: **RUN-13 — Filesystem assumptions.** Create uploads and temporary files, redeploy, reschedule, and inspect persistent mounts.

checks.heading: Process and deployment behavior
checks.text: **RUN-14 — UID GID and filesystem policy.** Exercise reads, writes, executable bits, symlinks, and ownership under the actual container identity.

checks.heading: Process and deployment behavior
checks.text: **RUN-15 — Multiple replicas and local state.** Send alternating requests to replicas while updating sessions, cache entries, files, and coordination locks.

checks.heading: Process and deployment behavior
checks.text: **RUN-16 — Rolling deployment compatibility.** Run old and new application versions together against the planned schema, cache, and message formats.

checks.heading: Process and deployment behavior
checks.text: **RUN-17 — Coolify configuration and persistence.** When used, inspect deployed resources, mounts, networks, health checks, deployment hooks, and protected recovery references for the instance encryption key and required SSH keys.

checks.heading: Capacity and infrastructure handoff
checks.text: **RUN-18 — Connection pool sizing.** Measure per-process and per-replica database and provider connections during startup, peak work, and deployment overlap.

checks.heading: Capacity and infrastructure handoff
checks.text: **RUN-19 — Destination capacity.** Run bounded representative concurrency with builds, backups, workers, and other applications on the shared server.

checks.heading: Capacity and infrastructure handoff
checks.text: **RUN-20 — Disk pressure and cleanup.** Fill a disposable quota using logs, temporary files, image layers, and failed build artifacts.

checks.heading: Capacity and infrastructure handoff
checks.text: **RUN-21 — Resource limits and neighbor effects.** Throttle or restart a synthetic neighboring workload and observe the application.

checks.heading: Capacity and infrastructure handoff
checks.text: **RUN-22 — Application exposure.** Inspect public ports, debug endpoints, administration routes, raw origin access, and temporary domains.

checks.heading: Capacity and infrastructure handoff
checks.text: **RUN-23 — Destination backup ownership.** Compare host snapshots, control-plane backups, application volumes, databases, keys, and external configuration.

checks.heading: Capacity and infrastructure handoff
checks.text: **RUN-24 — Operator deploy and rollback.** Have a backup operator deploy a known artifact and restore the previous compatible version in a disposable environment.

checks.heading: Compatibility and recoverable transfer
checks.text: **DAT-01 — Database feature inventory.** Inspect engine versions, extensions, functions, triggers, views, partitions, jobs, roles, and special data types.

checks.heading: Compatibility and recoverable transfer
checks.text: **DAT-02 — Encoding collation and time semantics.** Compare character encoding, collation, locale, case sensitivity, time zones, and timestamp behavior with representative records.

checks.heading: Compatibility and recoverable transfer
checks.text: **DAT-03 — Migration method compatibility.** Check the selected engine/version documentation and execute the intended migration method on a representative disposable copy.

checks.heading: Compatibility and recoverable transfer
checks.text: **DAT-04 — Consistent snapshot.** Create a backup while synthetic related records change and restore it in isolation.

checks.heading: Compatibility and recoverable transfer
checks.text: **DAT-05 — Pre-change backup and recovery.** Restore the planned backup using destination access and encryption keys before destructive schema or data changes.

checks.heading: Compatibility and recoverable transfer
checks.text: **DAT-06 — Migration credentials and transport.** Inspect export/import identities, temporary files, transfer encryption, logs, and access expiry.

checks.heading: Compatibility and recoverable transfer
checks.text: **DAT-07 — Object and file inventory.** List required uploads, bucket objects, filesystem trees, versions, metadata, permissions, and database references.

checks.heading: Compatibility and recoverable transfer
checks.text: **DAT-08 — File semantics and object compatibility.** Test content types, cache metadata, key case, URL encoding, multipart uploads, range reads, ACLs, and signed URLs on the chosen store.

checks.heading: Compatibility and recoverable transfer
checks.text: **DAT-09 — Transfer verification.** Compare appropriate checksums, manifests, sizes, object counts, and application reads with a documented sampling or full-check strategy.

checks.heading: Synchronization and authority
checks.text: **DAT-10 — Authority state model.** Write down the authoritative database and file store before, during, and after every cutover phase.

checks.heading: Synchronization and authority
checks.text: **DAT-11 — Write freeze completeness.** Rehearse a freeze across HTTP, mobile APIs, admin tools, workers, cron, direct integrations, and database clients.

checks.heading: Synchronization and authority
checks.text: **DAT-12 — Replication lag and checkpoint.** Observe replication progress, failures, source retention, and the final synchronization position under representative writes.

checks.heading: Synchronization and authority
checks.text: **DAT-13 — Replication exclusions.** Compare schema DDL, sequence state, large objects, roles, and engine-specific features with the actual replication mechanism.

checks.heading: Synchronization and authority
checks.text: **DAT-14 — Change capture deletion handling.** Create, update, delete, and reorder related records during the transfer, including transaction boundaries.

checks.heading: Synchronization and authority
checks.text: **DAT-15 — Cross-store consistency.** Change a record and its associated file during copy and final synchronization.

checks.heading: Synchronization and authority
checks.text: **DAT-16 — Sequence and identity readiness.** Insert new destination records after importing explicit identifiers and synchronizing sequence or auto-increment state.

checks.heading: Synchronization and authority
checks.text: **DAT-17 — Schema transition and rollback compatibility.** Test old and new application versions across planned additive, backfill, and destructive schema phases.

checks.heading: Synchronization and authority
checks.text: **DAT-18 — Read-after-write and replica routing.** Write through one path and read through application replicas, retained services, caches, and background jobs.

checks.heading: Validation and protection
checks.text: **DAT-19 — Business invariant validation.** Compare balances, entitlements, ownership, foreign-key relationships, totals, and representative transformations.

checks.heading: Validation and protection
checks.text: **DAT-20 — Tenant and permission preservation.** Use synthetic users and tenants to read migrated records, object links, and export endpoints.

checks.heading: Validation and protection
checks.text: **DAT-21 — Encryption key availability.** Restore encrypted fields and files using approved destination and recovery identities.

checks.heading: Validation and protection
checks.text: **DAT-22 — Search and derived stores.** Rebuild or transfer search indexes, vector stores, materialized views, and derived caches from authoritative data.

checks.heading: Validation and protection
checks.text: **DAT-23 — Partial transfer and retry.** Interrupt import and file copy, then restart or resume using recorded checkpoints.

checks.heading: Validation and protection
checks.text: **DAT-24 — Data validation audit trail.** Record source and destination versions, counts, hashes where appropriate, sample derivation, checkpoints, and discrepancies.

checks.heading: Validation and protection
checks.text: **DAT-25 — Destination recovery after promotion.** Back up destination data after synthetic new writes and restore into an isolated environment.

checks.heading: DNS and certificates
checks.text: **NET-01 — Complete zone inventory.** Export and compare A, AAAA, CNAME, MX, TXT, CAA, SRV, wildcard, delegated subdomain, and verification records where present.

checks.heading: DNS and certificates
checks.text: **NET-02 — TTL preparation and cache limits.** Inspect prior and new record TTLs, negative caching, resolver behavior, and the time allowed before cutover.

checks.heading: DNS and certificates
checks.text: **NET-03 — IPv4 and IPv6 consistency.** Test public resolution and service reachability separately over both supported address families.

checks.heading: DNS and certificates
checks.text: **NET-04 — Registrar delegation and DNSSEC.** If changing DNS authority, rehearse nameserver, DS, signing, and delegated-zone changes with provider guidance.

checks.heading: DNS and certificates
checks.text: **NET-05 — Apex wildcard and split DNS.** Check root-domain aliasing, wildcard exceptions, internal DNS, service discovery, and custom tenant domains.

checks.heading: DNS and certificates
checks.text: **NET-06 — Certificate issuance readiness.** Issue test or production certificates through the approved challenge path without disabling normal trust verification.

checks.heading: DNS and certificates
checks.text: **NET-07 — Certificate renewal and trust.** Exercise the supported renewal check and inspect edge-to-origin trust, chain, expiry alerts, and private key ownership.

checks.heading: DNS and certificates
checks.text: **NET-08 — HSTS and redirect continuity.** Test HTTP, HTTPS, alternate hostnames, redirect chains, and browsers with existing HSTS state.

checks.heading: Proxy and protocol correctness
checks.text: **NET-09 — Origin proof and routing.** Send traceable requests through controlled pre-cutover routing and final public paths; correlate destination logs.

checks.heading: Proxy and protocol correctness
checks.text: **NET-10 — Trusted proxy and forwarded headers.** Send forged forwarding headers through public and internal paths and inspect scheme, host, client IP, and redirects.

checks.heading: Proxy and protocol correctness
checks.text: **NET-11 — Access restrictions and WAF parity.** Compare CDN rules, origin restrictions, rate limits, bot controls, and direct-IP paths.

checks.heading: Proxy and protocol correctness
checks.text: **NET-12 — WebSocket continuity.** Open authenticated sockets through the actual proxy and exercise idle periods, reconnects, deployment, and session expiry.

checks.heading: Proxy and protocol correctness
checks.text: **NET-13 — SSE and AI streaming.** Inspect incremental delivery, buffering, compression, heartbeat, cancellation, and disconnect behavior through the final edge.

checks.heading: Proxy and protocol correctness
checks.text: **NET-14 — Uploads downloads and long requests.** Transfer bounded representative files and long-running requests through all proxy layers.

checks.heading: Proxy and protocol correctness
checks.text: **NET-15 — Caching and private responses.** Exercise authenticated pages, tenant data, query strings, cache keys, purge, and stale assets across old/new origins.

checks.heading: Proxy and protocol correctness
checks.text: **NET-16 — Routing paths and canonical behavior.** Compare deep links, API prefixes, rewrites, trailing slashes, localized paths, robots directives, and public canonical URLs.

checks.heading: Identity and external reachability
checks.text: **NET-17 — Cookies and session continuity.** Test existing and new sessions across domain, proxy, signing-key, and SameSite/Secure configuration changes.

checks.heading: Identity and external reachability
checks.text: **NET-18 — OAuth OIDC and SAML.** Run login, callback, logout, state/nonce, issuer, audience, and clock-skew checks using synthetic accounts.

checks.heading: Identity and external reachability
checks.text: **NET-19 — Cross-origin and request integrity.** Test allowed and denied origins, preflight, CSRF protection, host validation, and browser storage assumptions.

checks.heading: Identity and external reachability
checks.text: **NET-20 — External IP allowlists.** Verify database, identity, payment, API, SMTP, and partner allowlists from actual destination egress paths.

checks.heading: Identity and external reachability
checks.text: **NET-21 — Outbound connectivity and DNS.** Test destination resolution, TLS, IPv6 preferences, network restrictions, NAT behavior, and proxy variables.

checks.heading: Identity and external reachability
checks.text: **NET-22 — Email DNS and delivery.** When mail-related infrastructure changes, test sender authentication, reply handling, bounce routing, and provider domain checks.

checks.heading: Identity and external reachability
checks.text: **NET-23 — Temporary environment protection.** Attempt unauthorized reads and writes against staging domains, preview URLs, raw origins, and certificates exposed in public logs.

checks.heading: Identity and external reachability
checks.text: **NET-24 — Legacy clients and old origin.** Route a controlled client to the old origin after the switch and exercise a long-lived session.

checks.heading: Background work and state
checks.text: **JOB-01 — Complete job inventory.** Compare application code with provider cron dashboards, OS schedules, queue consumers, database jobs, and external automation.

checks.heading: Background work and state
checks.text: **JOB-02 — Scheduler ownership.** Run old and new stacks together with synthetic scheduled work and inspect the effective activation mechanism.

checks.heading: Background work and state
checks.text: **JOB-03 — Worker lifecycle.** Start, stop, redeploy, and crash destination workers while observing readiness and queue consumption.

checks.heading: Background work and state
checks.text: **JOB-04 — Time zone and missed schedules.** Exercise UTC/local schedules, daylight-saving boundaries, clock skew, downtime, and catch-up behavior.

checks.heading: Background work and state
checks.text: **JOB-05 — Queue migration and in-flight tasks.** Pause producers, drain or transfer queued work, interrupt active tasks, and resume from a documented checkpoint.

checks.heading: Background work and state
checks.text: **JOB-06 — Message and worker version compatibility.** Feed old and new message formats to the versions present during deployment overlap.

checks.heading: Background work and state
checks.text: **JOB-07 — Idempotency and distributed coordination.** Replay a task across old and new workers and expire a coordination lease during execution.

checks.heading: Background work and state
checks.text: **JOB-08 — Retry and dead-letter recovery.** Inject transient and permanent failures, then inspect retry schedules, attempt caps, and dead-letter handling.

checks.heading: Background work and state
checks.text: **JOB-09 — Backlog and concurrency limits.** Generate a bounded migration backlog and resume consumers beside normal traffic.

checks.heading: External event correctness
checks.text: **JOB-10 — Webhook endpoint continuity.** Send signed synthetic callbacks before, during, and after endpoint changes, including events reaching the old address.

checks.heading: External event correctness
checks.text: **JOB-11 — Signature verification and raw body.** Send valid, tampered, re-encoded, and wrong-environment callbacks through the destination proxy.

checks.heading: External event correctness
checks.text: **JOB-12 — Duplicate and unordered events.** Deliver the same event to both stacks and deliver related events out of order.

checks.heading: External event correctness
checks.text: **JOB-13 — Acknowledgment and persistence.** Fail a worker after durable event receipt, before effect completion, and after completion but before acknowledgment.

checks.heading: External event correctness
checks.text: **JOB-14 — Webhook secret rotation.** Overlap and then retire synthetic signing secrets and endpoint registrations under the provider-supported procedure.

checks.heading: External event correctness
checks.text: **JOB-15 — Payments and entitlements.** Use test-mode payment lifecycles, refunds, subscription renewals, and entitlement updates across cutover.

checks.heading: External event correctness
checks.text: **JOB-16 — Email and notification containment.** Exercise staging alerts, queued notifications, scheduled digests, and retry delivery through recipient sinks.

checks.heading: External event correctness
checks.text: **JOB-17 — Outbound integration identity.** Check tokens, callback domains, IP allowlists, mTLS certificates, scopes, and environment identifiers from the destination.

checks.heading: External event correctness
checks.text: **JOB-18 — Rate limits and provider recovery.** Replay a bounded backlog that reaches external throttling or quota limits.

checks.heading: Specialized services and handoff
checks.text: **JOB-19 — Realtime subscriptions and reconnects.** Move synthetic pub/sub, presence, and event subscriptions while clients reconnect to both origins.

checks.heading: Specialized services and handoff
checks.text: **JOB-20 — Caches and session stores.** Change cache namespaces, serialization versions, eviction behavior, and retained connection paths.

checks.heading: Specialized services and handoff
checks.text: **JOB-21 — Search analytics and monitoring sinks.** Compare ingesters, indexers, analytics events, error reporting, and synthetic user events across both stacks.

checks.heading: Specialized services and handoff
checks.text: **JOB-22 — AI and long-running provider jobs.** If used, migrate streams, callback jobs, model credentials, retrieval stores, and provider region routes.

checks.heading: Specialized services and handoff
checks.text: **JOB-23 — Ownership handoff record.** Record last old worker activity, pending tasks, checkpoint, new activation time, and reconciliation results.

checks.heading: Rehearsal design
checks.text: **VAL-01 — Representative isolated environment.** Build the planned topology with synthetic or properly protected representative data and isolated credentials, queues, and recipients.

checks.heading: Rehearsal design
checks.text: **VAL-02 — Production difference register.** Compare data volume, provider plans, network path, domains, workers, resource contention, and identity configuration.

checks.heading: Rehearsal design
checks.text: **VAL-03 — Approved verification scope.** Record allowed environments, actions, identities, transfer volumes, resource budgets, and prohibited effects.

checks.heading: Rehearsal design
checks.text: **VAL-04 — Versioned migration bundle.** Capture source revision, image digests, schema steps, manifests, secrets references, DNS plan, and transfer tooling.

checks.heading: Rehearsal design
checks.text: **VAL-05 — Timed end-to-end rehearsal.** Execute preparation, backup, transfer, final sync, traffic switch, validation, and recovery with actual elapsed times.

checks.heading: Rehearsal design
checks.text: **VAL-06 — Recovery independence.** Rehearse recovery with the source provider or normal operator assumed unavailable.

checks.heading: Rehearsal design
checks.text: **VAL-07 — Safe failure injection.** Interrupt controlled network paths, transfer tasks, workers, and storage availability in a disposable environment.

checks.heading: Rehearsal design
checks.text: **VAL-08 — Validation sensitivity.** For a critical invariant, use a known bad fixture or safe disposable-copy mutation such as a missing object or wrong tenant mapping.

checks.heading: Evidence-driven validation
checks.text: **VAL-09 — Core journey matrix.** Map sign-in, read/write, uploads, search, purchase, notifications, administration, and relevant specialist paths to checks.

checks.heading: Evidence-driven validation
checks.text: **VAL-10 — Negative permission checks.** Attempt forbidden tenant reads, invalid callbacks, private file access, and unauthorized administrative operations using synthetic actors.

checks.heading: Evidence-driven validation
checks.text: **VAL-11 — Data verification plan.** Define full or sampled comparisons, source checkpoints, invariants, transformation tolerances, and discrepancy handling before copying.

checks.heading: Evidence-driven validation
checks.text: **VAL-12 — Performance and contention baseline.** Compare bounded representative workloads on source and destination including retained service latency and shared-host tasks.

checks.heading: Evidence-driven validation
checks.text: **VAL-13 — External reachability checks.** Use permitted outside-client checks for final DNS, trusted TLS, login callbacks, webhooks, and uploads.

checks.heading: Evidence-driven validation
checks.text: **VAL-14 — Observability readiness.** Trigger synthetic availability, error, backlog, backup, certificate, and capacity events before switching traffic.

checks.heading: Evidence-driven validation
checks.text: **VAL-15 — Evidence reproducibility.** Capture actor, prerequisites, sanitized requests, expected and actual effects, versions, timestamps, and artifact references.

checks.heading: Evidence-driven validation
checks.text: **VAL-16 — Contradictions and existing failures.** Compare source baseline, destination results, and conflicting evidence before assigning root cause.

checks.heading: Go no-go and handoff
checks.text: **VAL-17 — Predeclared acceptance gates.** Agree thresholds for core failures, data discrepancy, loss window, recovery duration, latency, backlog, and unauthorized effects.

checks.heading: Go no-go and handoff
checks.text: **VAL-18 — Readiness ownership.** Review access, backup proof, authority transitions, integration registration, rollback resources, and observation staffing.

checks.heading: Go no-go and handoff
checks.text: **VAL-19 — Rollback and fail-forward gates.** Define the point before new writes, the point after new writes, and any schema-related no-return boundary.

checks.heading: Go no-go and handoff
checks.text: **VAL-20 — Change freeze and drift.** Compare the approved bundle with source, destination, DNS, vendor settings, and last-minute configuration edits.

checks.heading: Go no-go and handoff
checks.text: **VAL-21 — Communications and escalation readiness.** Prepare maintenance status text, support instructions, incident contacts, and decision checkpoints.

checks.heading: Go no-go and handoff
checks.text: **VAL-22 — Risk acceptance and gaps.** Review failed and unverified critical controls, exclusions, mitigations, and expiry with accountable owners.

checks.heading: Go no-go and handoff
checks.text: **VAL-23 — Final migration decision.** Consolidate results and dependencies into ready, ready subject to recorded conditions, blocked, or insufficient evidence.

checks.heading: Preparation and controlled promotion
checks.text: **CUT-01 — Window and prerequisites.** Confirm change authority, current source state, backups, destination capacity, provider status, operators, and rollback access at the window start.

checks.heading: Preparation and controlled promotion
checks.text: **CUT-02 — Checkpointed execution.** Walk each runbook step with prerequisites, operator, timestamp, evidence, acceptance, and recovery action.

checks.heading: Preparation and controlled promotion
checks.text: **CUT-03 — Final writer fence.** Activate the planned source write suspension or verified single-writer routing across every entry point.

checks.heading: Preparation and controlled promotion
checks.text: **CUT-04 — Final synchronization proof.** Capture the final transaction or replication checkpoint and reconcile database, objects, and pending work.

checks.heading: Preparation and controlled promotion
checks.text: **CUT-05 — Destination promotion.** Enable the designated database, file store, workers, and event handlers in the planned dependency order.

checks.heading: Preparation and controlled promotion
checks.text: **CUT-06 — Traffic switch with mixed clients.** Apply the approved DNS or edge route change while controlled clients continue reaching old and new origins.

checks.heading: Preparation and controlled promotion
checks.text: **CUT-07 — Immediate smoke and origin check.** Run the core journey set, traceable writes, external reachability, and destination-log correlation.

checks.heading: Preparation and controlled promotion
checks.text: **CUT-08 — Background and financial reconciliation.** Compare source/destination task ledgers, provider events, queue depth, notifications, and financial state.

checks.heading: Rollback and fail-forward safety
checks.text: **CUT-09 — Rollback before destination writes.** Rehearse switching back before new destination mutations using the declared authority and event state.

checks.heading: Rollback and fail-forward safety
checks.text: **CUT-10 — Rollback after destination writes.** Create synthetic new destination records and files, then rehearse reverse synchronization or another reconciliation strategy.

checks.heading: Rollback and fail-forward safety
checks.text: **CUT-11 — Schema and application compatibility.** Attempt the planned application rollback against the actual post-migration schema and message versions.

checks.heading: Rollback and fail-forward safety
checks.text: **CUT-12 — No-return decision boundary.** Identify destructive transformations, unavailable reverse replication, retired keys, and other irreversible steps.

checks.heading: Rollback and fail-forward safety
checks.text: **CUT-13 — Fail-forward rehearsal.** Use a destination defect where reverting would lose accepted data and apply the planned repair or restore path.

checks.heading: Rollback and fail-forward safety
checks.text: **CUT-14 — Old origin behavior during recovery.** Exercise cached DNS, long-lived connections, retrying mobile clients, and delayed callbacks while recovering.

checks.heading: Rollback and fail-forward safety
checks.text: **CUT-15 — Recovery completion evidence.** Verify core tasks, invariant checks, job ownership, destination selection, and monitoring after rollback or repair.

checks.heading: Observation and responsible retirement
checks.text: **CUT-16 — Observation window coverage.** Monitor actual traffic cycles, scheduled work, certificate/backup operation, and retained integrations over the agreed period.

checks.heading: Observation and responsible retirement
checks.text: **CUT-17 — Destination backups and restore.** Verify scheduled destination backups and a post-promotion isolated restore of representative new state.

checks.heading: Observation and responsible retirement
checks.text: **CUT-18 — Stale traffic and dependency audit.** Inspect old origin logs, DNS, callbacks, scheduled tasks, embedded URLs, and external integrations before shutting down.

checks.heading: Observation and responsible retirement
checks.text: **CUT-19 — Retirement eligibility.** Review stability, reconciled writes, retention rules, rollback expiry, exported artifacts, and accountable approval.

checks.heading: Observation and responsible retirement
checks.text: **CUT-20 — Old worker and webhook shutdown.** Disable retired schedules, workers, event registrations, deployments, and source write identities in a controlled sequence.

checks.heading: Observation and responsible retirement
checks.text: **CUT-21 — Credential and access cleanup.** Rotate or revoke migration identities, temporary firewall rules, signed links, vendor tokens, and obsolete account access.

checks.heading: Observation and responsible retirement
checks.text: **CUT-22 — DNS and dangling resource cleanup.** Inspect stale CNAMEs, preview domains, delegated zones, abandoned buckets, certificates, and reclaimable service names.

checks.heading: Observation and responsible retirement
checks.text: **CUT-23 — Data disposal and retained archives.** Apply approved retention, encryption, access, deletion, and expiry to source volumes, exports, logs, snapshots, and keys.

checks.heading: Observation and responsible retirement
checks.text: **CUT-24 — Billing and subscription verification.** Compare post-retirement provider inventory and invoices with retained-service decisions and cancellation records.

checks.heading: Observation and responsible retirement
checks.text: **CUT-25 — Operational and portability handover.** Have the receiving operator use updated diagrams, manifests, secrets references, recovery instructions, and owner contacts.

checks.heading: Observation and responsible retirement
checks.text: **CUT-26 — Closure and future review.** Reconcile findings, exceptions, cost deltas, recovery targets, and lessons into the project report.

checks.heading: Platform dependency inventory
checks.text: Inventory actual production entry points, runtimes, build versions, CPU architecture, adapters, environment injection, secrets, domains, proxy behavior, and generated assets. Reproduce the production artifact on the destination.

checks.heading: Platform dependency inventory
checks.text: Find platform-specific queues, cron, image optimization, serverless functions, edge middleware, filesystem assumptions, analytics, caches, storage, and deployment hooks, including externally configured services. Name each replacement or retained integration.

checks.heading: Platform dependency inventory
checks.text: Record move/retain/replace/retire decisions, owners, dependencies, approved data destinations, access, time constraints, and total transition and operating costs.

checks.heading: Platform dependency inventory
checks.text: Verify durable workers and scheduling, timezone and daylight-saving behavior, ownership, retries, concurrency, missed runs, and redeploy behavior.

checks.heading: Platform dependency inventory
checks.text: Test persistent uploads, temporary storage cleanup, volume placement, UID/GID, capacity, backups, and lifecycle behavior. Container-local files are not assumed to persist across recreation.

checks.heading: Platform dependency inventory
checks.text: Evaluate database pools, process counts, replica overlap, transactions, session/cache state, and worker coordination under the actual destination topology.

checks.heading: Platform dependency inventory
checks.text: Verify listen address/port, startup, readiness, graceful shutdown, headers, redirects, WebSockets, SSE/AI streaming, buffering, upload limits, and timeouts through the actual edge/proxy.

checks.heading: Platform dependency inventory
checks.text: Measure retained-provider latency, connection limits, and shared-host CPU/RAM/disk/I/O pressure including builds and backups. Persistent hosting does not eliminate startup, contention, or capacity risk.

checks.heading: Destination validation
checks.text: Isolate staging credentials, databases, queues, recipients, payment mode, and outbound side effects. Use synthetic data or an approved protected representative copy.

checks.heading: Destination validation
checks.text: Validate destination routing through controlled DNS/Host paths or staging domains with normal TLS verification. Protect temporary endpoints from unauthorized access and accidental indexing; noindex is not an access control.

checks.heading: Destination validation
checks.text: Check OAuth/OIDC/SAML, callbacks, webhook signatures and raw-body handling, CORS, CSRF, signed URLs, cookie/session behavior, email DNS, and destination egress allowlists.

checks.heading: Destination validation
checks.text: Verify database schema, engine versions, extensions, collation, encoding, permissions, encryption keys, file/object semantics, and required transformations. Row counts alone do not establish correctness.

checks.heading: Destination validation
checks.text: Rehearse isolated migration and recovery with measured transfer, validation, restore, and total elapsed times. Record material production differences and recovery objectives.

checks.heading: Destination validation
checks.text: Verify important checks detect known bad fixtures safely, pair denial checks with allowed operations, and capture actual persisted or stubbed effects.

checks.heading: Cutover and data authority
checks.text: Define the source of truth in every phase. Choose a complete writer freeze, verified replication, or another tested synchronization mechanism; prevent unplanned independent old/new writes.

checks.heading: Cutover and data authority
checks.text: Back up before destructive changes and prove restore access. Validate final database/file state, business invariants, permissions, replication exclusions, sequence state, final synchronization checkpoint, and any permitted loss window.

checks.heading: Cutover and data authority
checks.text: Use deliberate schema phases. An older image may be incompatible with the new schema, message formats, or cache state; code rollback does not revert data.

checks.heading: Cutover and data authority
checks.text: Establish one intended owner for schedules, queue consumption, callbacks, and consequential effects. Drain or transfer pending work, deduplicate events, and reconcile arrivals during the window.

checks.heading: Cutover and data authority
checks.text: Prepare DNS changes early where useful and account for existing caches and clients reaching the old origin. Preserve required records, IPv6 behavior, delegation, and DNSSEC trust.

checks.heading: Cutover and data authority
checks.text: Validate certificate issuance and renewal through final firewall/edge paths. Coordinate secrets, registration, and endpoint changes without losing valid callbacks.

checks.heading: Cutover and data authority
checks.text: Predeclare measurable go/no-go and recovery triggers for journey failure, elevated errors/latency, payment drift, backlog, data discrepancy, or lost recovery margin. Name decision owners and observation coverage.

checks.heading: Rollback and retirement
checks.text: Keep a known working source release and required recovery assets through the agreed observation period. Document rollback before destination writes, after destination writes, and after any no-return boundary.

checks.heading: Rollback and retirement
checks.text: Preserve and reconcile new destination records, files, queued work, and external effects before resuming source writes. Reverting DNS alone can lose accepted data or create split authority.

checks.heading: Rollback and retirement
checks.text: Rehearse fail-forward or restore/reconciliation where schema or data changes make ordinary rollback unsafe. State downtime, loss assumptions, and user impact.

checks.heading: Rollback and retirement
checks.text: Verify actual serving origin, external reachability, journeys, permissions, payments, email, jobs, monitoring, alerts, file access, and post-promotion backups and restore.

checks.heading: Rollback and retirement
checks.text: Confirm stability across relevant traffic and scheduled-work cycles. Retire old jobs, handlers, endpoints, credentials, storage, and billing only after dependencies, retention, reconciliation, and recovery needs are satisfied.

checks.heading: Rollback and retirement
checks.text: Remove stale DNS and reclaimable resource references, temporary access, and abandoned deployment hooks. Verify retained costs are intentional and hand over a repeatable deploy/recover/exit procedure.

checks.heading: Scope and account ownership
checks.text: **IDN-01 — Integration inventory.** Compare source routes, environment configuration, provider dashboards, billing, connector catalogs, and scheduled work.

checks.heading: Scope and account ownership
checks.text: **IDN-02 — Provider contract record.** Record API/event versions, required capabilities, scopes, quotas, billable units, data destinations, and failure semantics.

checks.heading: Scope and account ownership
checks.text: **IDN-03 — Data minimization.** Trace synthetic private fields through API requests, callback payloads, messages, telemetry, support exports, and fallback routes.

checks.heading: Scope and account ownership
checks.text: **IDN-04 — Environment and account separation.** Exercise development, staging, production, sandbox, and provider subaccount identifiers through real routes.

checks.heading: Scope and account ownership
checks.text: **IDN-05 — Operational account ownership.** Inspect provider organization ownership, administrator roles, service identities, billing access, and backup operator access.

checks.heading: Scope and account ownership
checks.text: **IDN-06 — Consent and connection authority.** Attempt installation, scope expansion, reconnection, and organization-wide changes with different user roles.

checks.heading: Scope and account ownership
checks.text: **IDN-07 — Retention and disconnection policy.** Trace deletion requests and disconnect actions through tokens, imported records, caches, provider copies, and audit records.

checks.heading: Credential protection and freshness
checks.text: **IDN-08 — Credential placement.** Inspect frontend bundles, logs, traces, crash reports, URLs, configuration exports, and build artifacts using synthetic secret canaries.

checks.heading: Credential protection and freshness
checks.text: **IDN-09 — Least privilege and resource scope.** Try reads/writes outside the credential's required action, tenant, account, and resource scope.

checks.heading: Credential protection and freshness
checks.text: **IDN-10 — Rotation and revocation.** Rotate and revoke synthetic keys while requests, caches, workers, and pending jobs exist.

checks.heading: Credential protection and freshness
checks.text: **IDN-11 — Expired and invalid credentials.** Exercise expired tokens, wrong issuer/account credentials, malformed secrets, and denied scopes.

checks.heading: Credential protection and freshness
checks.text: **IDN-12 — Refresh concurrency.** Expire a connection and trigger concurrent refresh attempts with rotation or single-use refresh tokens where supported.

checks.heading: Credential protection and freshness
checks.text: **IDN-13 — Compromised credential containment.** Rehearse a leaked synthetic integration credential using the operator runbook.

checks.heading: OAuth and identity binding
checks.text: **IDN-14 — Authorization flow selection.** Review the actual grant type, client type, platform, and provider security requirements against current official guidance.

checks.heading: OAuth and identity binding
checks.text: **IDN-15 — Redirect and return target validation.** Attempt unexpected redirect URIs, alternate schemes, encoded variants, and malicious post-login return targets.

checks.heading: OAuth and identity binding
checks.text: **IDN-16 — Authorization transaction binding.** Start flows as users A and B, swap callback transaction data, replay a completed flow, and change browser session.

checks.heading: OAuth and identity binding
checks.text: **IDN-17 — Code interception and exchange.** Exercise the selected code flow's PKCE or other applicable protections and attempt code substitution in an isolated test.

checks.heading: OAuth and identity binding
checks.text: **IDN-18 — Provider and token identity.** Try responses from the wrong issuer, app client, audience, environment, or provider account.

checks.heading: OAuth and identity binding
checks.text: **IDN-19 — Unsafe account linking.** Use synthetic accounts with the same display email, changed email, unverified email, and an existing different identity.

checks.heading: OAuth and identity binding
checks.text: **IDN-20 — OIDC validation when used.** Exercise expired identity tokens, wrong audience/issuer, unsupported algorithms, nonce rules where applicable, and provider key rotation.

checks.heading: OAuth and identity binding
checks.text: **IDN-21 — Connection tenant isolation.** Substitute connection IDs, organization IDs, cached tokens, and job ownership across synthetic tenants.

checks.heading: OAuth and identity binding
checks.text: **IDN-22 — Reconnect unlink and removal.** Reconnect a different provider account, revoke at the provider, unlink locally, and remove the installing user.

checks.heading: OAuth and identity binding
checks.text: **IDN-23 — Permission and account changes.** Reduce scopes, change provider team membership, suspend an account, and resume pending work.

checks.heading: Request and response correctness
checks.text: **API-01 — Request schema and business rules.** Submit missing, unknown, nested, oversized, null, and incorrectly typed values through the actual integration route.

checks.heading: Request and response correctness
checks.text: **API-02 — Response validation and drift.** Return missing fields, unknown enum values, unexpected types, extra fields, empty bodies, and inconsistent success envelopes.

checks.heading: Request and response correctness
checks.text: **API-03 — Encoding and numeric semantics.** Test Unicode, escaped identifiers, time zones, timestamps, decimal amounts, large integer IDs, and unit conversions.

checks.heading: Request and response correctness
checks.text: **API-04 — Pagination and completeness.** Use empty pages, repeated cursors, changing datasets, expiring continuation tokens, and multiple result pages.

checks.heading: Request and response correctness
checks.text: **API-05 — Partial and batch results.** Return mixed per-item success/failure, partial pages, and accepted asynchronous operations.

checks.heading: Request and response correctness
checks.text: **API-06 — Response and parser limits.** Exercise bounded large/compressed responses, unsupported media types, deeply nested data, and malformed encodings.

checks.heading: Request and response correctness
checks.text: **API-07 — Untrusted provider content.** Render remote text, URLs, filenames, error messages, and imported metadata using harmless injection fixtures.

checks.heading: Request and response correctness
checks.text: **API-08 — Attachment and remote file access.** Where supported, request files using authorized object IDs and approved fetch destinations with bounded sizes.

checks.heading: Distributed operation safety
checks.text: **API-09 — Timeout and deadline propagation.** Delay connect, TLS, response headers, body chunks, and asynchronous completion using a stub.

checks.heading: Distributed operation safety
checks.text: **API-10 — Retry classification.** Return authentication errors, validation failures, rate limits, transient failures, and unknown results.

checks.heading: Distributed operation safety
checks.text: **API-11 — Ambiguous remote success.** Commit a synthetic remote write then drop the response before the client receives it.

checks.heading: Distributed operation safety
checks.text: **API-12 — Idempotency scope and fingerprints.** Repeat the same operation concurrently and reuse its idempotency key with different tenant or payload.

checks.heading: Distributed operation safety
checks.text: **API-13 — Local and remote consistency.** Fail between local intent persistence, remote commit, and local confirmation.

checks.heading: Distributed operation safety
checks.text: **API-14 — Cancellation and asynchronous jobs.** Cancel before sending, after remote acceptance, and while a job callback is pending.

checks.heading: Distributed operation safety
checks.text: **API-15 — Bulkheads and provider outage.** Make one integration slow or unavailable beside unrelated user journeys.

checks.heading: Distributed operation safety
checks.text: **API-16 — Rate fairness and burst handling.** Send bounded concurrent work from multiple tenants and receive provider throttling.

checks.heading: Distributed operation safety
checks.text: **API-17 — Upstream version lifecycle.** Compare pinned API versions and SDK behavior with actual provider notices and a proposed contract upgrade.

checks.heading: Customer-facing APIs
checks.text: **API-18 — Published API contract.** Compare documentation, supported versions, examples, errors, async states, and compatibility promises with deployed behavior.

checks.heading: Customer-facing APIs
checks.text: **API-19 — API key creation and display.** Create keys under authorized and unauthorized roles and inspect initial display, later views, storage, and logs.

checks.heading: Customer-facing APIs
checks.text: **API-20 — Object and tenant authorization.** Request other tenants' object IDs, list filters, exports, nested resources, and bulk operations using synthetic keys.

checks.heading: Customer-facing APIs
checks.text: **API-21 — Customer key rotation and revocation.** Rotate and revoke a key with active requests, cached credentials, and queued work.

checks.heading: Customer-facing APIs
checks.text: **API-22 — Rate limits and service errors.** Exercise bounded bursts, quota exhaustion, invalid requests, and maintenance through the public API.

checks.heading: Customer-facing APIs
checks.text: **API-23 — Sandbox and test path.** Use promised sandbox or equivalent supported testing with separate resources and synthetic operations.

checks.heading: Customer-facing APIs
checks.text: **API-24 — Client compatibility and deprecation.** Run representative existing client contracts against candidate schema and version changes.

checks.heading: Customer-facing APIs
checks.text: **API-25 — GraphQL RPC and bulk variants.** Where offered, compare authorization, complexity limits, pagination, and errors across alternate API protocols.

checks.heading: Authenticity and resource binding
checks.text: **INB-01 — Endpoint and source inventory.** List every callback route, provider account, event subscription, expected environment, and processing owner.

checks.heading: Authenticity and resource binding
checks.text: **INB-02 — Provider-supported authentication.** Send valid, missing, wrong-key, and tampered callback authentication through the deployed route.

checks.heading: Authenticity and resource binding
checks.text: **INB-03 — Exact payload verification.** Send valid fixtures with whitespace, encoding, compression, and raw-body differences through the actual middleware/proxy.

checks.heading: Authenticity and resource binding
checks.text: **INB-04 — Key and algorithm control.** Try unknown key identifiers, unsupported algorithms, wrong secrets, and overlapping rotation windows.

checks.heading: Authenticity and resource binding
checks.text: **INB-05 — Freshness and replay contract.** Deliver repeated and delayed signed fixtures with valid and invalid provider timestamps where supported.

checks.heading: Authenticity and resource binding
checks.text: **INB-06 — Source account and environment.** Send a correctly authenticated event for the wrong provider account, subaccount, application, or production/test environment.

checks.heading: Authenticity and resource binding
checks.text: **INB-07 — Tenant and resource binding.** Alter routing hints and object references using synthetic tenants while preserving other plausible event fields.

checks.heading: Authenticity and resource binding
checks.text: **INB-08 — Schema and event admission.** Send unknown types/versions, absent identifiers, unexpected fields, malformed bodies, and oversized or compressed payloads.

checks.heading: Durable and correct processing
checks.text: **INB-09 — Durable acceptance and acknowledgment.** Crash between receipt, durable storage, acknowledgment, and worker scheduling.

checks.heading: Durable and correct processing
checks.text: **INB-10 — Duplicate delivery concurrency.** Deliver the same valid event concurrently through multiple workers and application replicas.

checks.heading: Durable and correct processing
checks.text: **INB-11 — Ordering and stale transitions.** Deliver related events in reverse order, delay an older event, and repeat a terminal transition.

checks.heading: Durable and correct processing
checks.text: **INB-12 — Event snapshot versus current truth.** Send stale snapshot and sparse/thin-event fixtures where the provider supports them.

checks.heading: Durable and correct processing
checks.text: **INB-13 — Missing events and reconciliation.** Omit a synthetic callback then run the documented polling, listing, or reconciliation mechanism.

checks.heading: Durable and correct processing
checks.text: **INB-14 — Partial processing recovery.** Fail after one local state change or one external effect but before the whole workflow completes.

checks.heading: Durable and correct processing
checks.text: **INB-15 — Transaction and outbox boundary.** Exercise failure between committing business state and enqueueing downstream work where both are required.

checks.heading: Durable and correct processing
checks.text: **INB-16 — Acknowledgment code semantics.** Return controlled transient, permanent, malformed, and unsupported-event outcomes and observe the sender contract.

checks.heading: Durable and correct processing
checks.text: **INB-17 — Backlog and poison messages.** Place an unprocessable valid event among ordinary events and simulate provider retry bursts.

checks.heading: Replay, evolution, and network paths
checks.text: **INB-18 — Authorized replay.** Attempt replay as different operator roles and tenants and replay completed consequential events.

checks.heading: Replay, evolution, and network paths
checks.text: **INB-19 — Event retention and privacy.** Inspect stored raw payloads, parsed records, error details, operator views, and deletion handling.

checks.heading: Replay, evolution, and network paths
checks.text: **INB-20 — Schema and handler rollout.** Run old/new handlers and stored events across supported version changes and rollback.

checks.heading: Replay, evolution, and network paths
checks.text: **INB-21 — Edge and gateway routing.** Send signed fixtures through actual CDN/WAF/admin gateways and direct legacy routes.

checks.heading: Replay, evolution, and network paths
checks.text: **INB-22 — Endpoint and secret migration.** Register old/new test handlers and transition secrets while duplicate and delayed events arrive.

checks.heading: Replay, evolution, and network paths
checks.text: **INB-23 — Clock and verification dependency failure.** Skew a disposable clock or fail key lookup/verification dependencies under controlled limits.

checks.heading: Replay, evolution, and network paths
checks.text: **INB-24 — Operator event visibility.** Inspect received, accepted, processing, failed, completed, and reconciled event records.

checks.heading: Subscription and destination authority
checks.text: **OUT-01 — Subscription management.** Create, edit, inspect, disable, and delete endpoints under multiple synthetic users and tenants.

checks.heading: Subscription and destination authority
checks.text: **OUT-02 — Destination ownership or opt-in.** Register a controlled third-party-like fixture and exercise verification or enrollment rules appropriate to the product.

checks.heading: Subscription and destination authority
checks.text: **OUT-03 — URL parsing and protocol policy.** Submit credentials in URLs, unsupported schemes, alternate encodings, unexpected ports, and malformed hosts.

checks.heading: Subscription and destination authority
checks.text: **OUT-04 — Network destination restriction.** Use controlled loopback/private/link-local-like fixtures and relevant IPv4/IPv6 forms in an isolated test network.

checks.heading: Subscription and destination authority
checks.text: **OUT-05 — DNS changes and redirects.** Resolve or redirect a permitted test hostname to a forbidden test target between registration and delivery.

checks.heading: Subscription and destination authority
checks.text: **OUT-06 — Secret and payload forwarding.** Redirect a controlled destination to another host and inspect auth headers, signing secrets, payload, and logs.

checks.heading: Subscription and destination authority
checks.text: **OUT-07 — Endpoint rebinding and tenant changes.** Change endpoint ownership, tenant membership, or destination configuration while deliveries are queued.

checks.heading: Payload contract and secure delivery
checks.text: **OUT-08 — Minimal authorized event payload.** Emit events containing private fields, related-object references, and multiple tenant records using synthetic data.

checks.heading: Payload contract and secure delivery
checks.text: **OUT-09 — Event identity and version.** Compare event IDs, type, schema version, creation time, and object identity across retries and consumers.

checks.heading: Payload contract and secure delivery
checks.text: **OUT-10 — Signing and receiver verification.** Deliver a fixture and tampered variants to a reference receiver using the documented signature contract.

checks.heading: Payload contract and secure delivery
checks.text: **OUT-11 — Secret rotation and revocation.** Rotate delivery secrets and revoke a subscription while attempts are in flight.

checks.heading: Payload contract and secure delivery
checks.text: **OUT-12 — TLS and connection validation.** Use expired, wrong-host, and untrusted certificates plus an approved trusted endpoint.

checks.heading: Payload contract and secure delivery
checks.text: **OUT-13 — Payload stability across retry.** Change source data and endpoint settings between delivery attempts.

checks.heading: Payload contract and secure delivery
checks.text: **OUT-14 — Untrusted receiver responses.** Return script-like error bodies, enormous data, slow chunks, redirects, and unexpected content types.

checks.heading: Delivery state and customer recovery
checks.text: **OUT-15 — Durable event creation.** Crash between a committed product change, event creation, and queue insertion.

checks.heading: Delivery state and customer recovery
checks.text: **OUT-16 — Retry scheduling and final failure.** Return timeouts, rate limits, transient/server errors, permanent rejection, and success from a receiver stub.

checks.heading: Delivery state and customer recovery
checks.text: **OUT-17 — Ambiguous delivery outcome.** Accept an event at the receiver and drop acknowledgment before the sender sees it.

checks.heading: Delivery state and customer recovery
checks.text: **OUT-18 — Per-endpoint fairness.** Run one slow/failing endpoint beside ordinary customers under bounded concurrency.

checks.heading: Delivery state and customer recovery
checks.text: **OUT-19 — Disable delete and cancellation.** Disable a subscription with queued/retrying events and then attempt reactivation or deletion.

checks.heading: Delivery state and customer recovery
checks.text: **OUT-20 — Delivery history and redaction.** Inspect attempt time, result, status codes, failure classification, event ID, and authorized payload views.

checks.heading: Delivery state and customer recovery
checks.text: **OUT-21 — Authorized manual replay.** Replay a synthetic completed or failed event as allowed and denied roles after endpoint and permission changes.

checks.heading: Delivery state and customer recovery
checks.text: **OUT-22 — Customer documentation and test events.** Use published signing examples, sample payloads, sandbox endpoints, and safe test-event controls.

checks.heading: Sender identity and mail infrastructure
checks.text: **EML-01 — Sender and domain inventory.** List transactional, security, marketing, support, and employee senders across providers and subdomains.

checks.heading: Sender identity and mail infrastructure
checks.text: **EML-02 — SPF configuration.** Inspect actual SPF records and all legitimate sending services against current provider/receiver guidance.

checks.heading: Sender identity and mail infrastructure
checks.text: **EML-03 — DKIM signing and rotation.** Inspect signatures on representative messages, selector DNS, key ownership, and a controlled rotation.

checks.heading: Sender identity and mail infrastructure
checks.text: **EML-04 — DMARC alignment and rollout.** Compare visible From identity with observed SPF/DKIM alignment and legitimate sender reports before policy changes.

checks.heading: Sender identity and mail infrastructure
checks.text: **EML-05 — Transport and DNS continuity.** When operating relevant infrastructure, check required MX/PTR/forward DNS, trusted TLS, outbound restrictions, and domain verification.

checks.heading: Sender identity and mail infrastructure
checks.text: **EML-06 — Sending-stream isolation.** Inspect credentials, queues, domains/subdomains, quotas, and incident controls across marketing and essential transactional mail.

checks.heading: Sender identity and mail infrastructure
checks.text: **EML-07 — Bounce and reply routing.** Send to controlled success, temporary failure, permanent failure, and reply fixtures.

checks.heading: Sender identity and mail infrastructure
checks.text: **EML-08 — Provider failover equivalence.** Trigger an approved mail-provider failure using stubs and inspect alternate domains, signing, payload, suppression, and account routing.

checks.heading: Delivery lifecycle and reputation
checks.text: **EML-09 — Recipient address handling.** Exercise internationalized addresses where supported, whitespace, case/alias rules, invalid syntax, and address changes.

checks.heading: Delivery lifecycle and reputation
checks.text: **EML-10 — Queue send and provider acknowledgment.** Trace a synthetic message from business intent to queue record, API request, provider ID, and delivery status.

checks.heading: Delivery lifecycle and reputation
checks.text: **EML-11 — Send timeout and deduplication.** Accept a synthetic send at a provider stub then drop its acknowledgment and retry the workflow.

checks.heading: Delivery lifecycle and reputation
checks.text: **EML-12 — Delivery status authentication.** Send valid, tampered, duplicated, and wrong-tenant delivery/bounce/complaint callbacks.

checks.heading: Delivery lifecycle and reputation
checks.text: **EML-13 — Temporary and permanent failures.** Simulate deferrals, full mailbox, invalid recipient, blocked sender, expiration, and provider outage.

checks.heading: Delivery lifecycle and reputation
checks.text: **EML-14 — Complaint and reputation response.** Trigger synthetic complaint and sender-health signals in permitted test paths.

checks.heading: Delivery lifecycle and reputation
checks.text: **EML-15 — Volume ramp and receiver requirements.** Check projected and actual message volumes, campaign spikes, provider quotas, and current mailbox-provider requirements.

checks.heading: Delivery lifecycle and reputation
