checks.text: **EML-16 — Status limits and human receipt.** Compare provider states, controlled mailbox observations, link scanner activity, and tracking signals.

checks.heading: Message rendering and inbound email
checks.text: **EML-17 — Template data and header injection.** Render synthetic user text, URLs, newlines, Unicode, HTML-like strings, and address fields.

checks.heading: Message rendering and inbound email
checks.text: **EML-18 — Recipient confidentiality.** Render individual, CC/BCC, group, tenant, and bulk sends using controlled addresses.

checks.heading: Message rendering and inbound email
checks.text: **EML-19 — Client rendering and accessibility.** Open actual transactional and marketing templates in supported desktop/mobile clients and with accessibility tools.

checks.heading: Message rendering and inbound email
checks.text: **EML-20 — Action URL and localization correctness.** Render locale variants, final production domains, expired links, tracking redirects, and long action URLs.

checks.heading: Message rendering and inbound email
checks.text: **EML-21 — Remote resources and content privacy.** Inspect images, pixels, embedded assets, tracked links, and attachment downloads in private/security messages.

checks.heading: Message rendering and inbound email
checks.text: **EML-22 — Inbound sender and thread trust.** If receiving email, forge From/Reply-To, conversation identifiers, quoted history, and forwarded content using synthetic fixtures.

checks.heading: Message rendering and inbound email
checks.text: **EML-23 — Inbound attachments and parsing.** If receiving email, send malformed MIME, nested archives, oversized attachments, dangerous file types, and remote-reference fixtures within safe limits.

checks.heading: Message rendering and inbound email
checks.text: **EML-24 — Inbound loops and automation.** Create controlled auto-reply, bounce, forwarding, and webhook-to-email loops.

checks.heading: Permission and suppression lifecycle
checks.text: **MSG-01 — Message classification.** Compare triggers, content, recipient expectations, and provider stream configuration for marketing, transactional, security, and mixed messages.

checks.heading: Permission and suppression lifecycle
checks.text: **MSG-02 — Permission provenance.** Trace opt-in source, scope, channel, organization, wording/version, timestamp, and any withdrawal using approved synthetic records.

checks.heading: Permission and suppression lifecycle
checks.text: **MSG-03 — Sender identification and opt-out content.** Inspect rendered campaign and launch templates against jurisdiction/contract requirements determined under module 11.

checks.heading: Permission and suppression lifecycle
checks.text: **MSG-04 — Unsubscribe user journey.** Exercise opt-out from an actual rendered message on supported devices, including logged-out and expired-session states.

checks.heading: Permission and suppression lifecycle
checks.text: **MSG-05 — One-click unsubscribe contract.** Where required or supported, exercise the intended header-based unsubscribe request separately from visible footer links and ordinary link fetching.

checks.heading: Permission and suppression lifecycle
checks.text: **MSG-06 — Cross-system suppression propagation.** Unsubscribe a synthetic recipient across provider lists, CRM sync, scheduled campaigns, imports, and retry queues.

checks.heading: Permission and suppression lifecycle
checks.text: **MSG-07 — Resubscribe and import races.** Replay old opt-in events, run stale list imports, merge records, and explicitly resubscribe after withdrawal.

checks.heading: Permission and suppression lifecycle
checks.text: **MSG-08 — Bounce and complaint suppression.** Apply synthetic hard bounce, transient failure, complaint, and recovery signals.

checks.heading: Permission and suppression lifecycle
checks.text: **MSG-09 — Essential-message distinction.** Opt out of marketing and trigger required account-security or transactional flows through recipient sinks.

checks.heading: Permission and suppression lifecycle
checks.text: **MSG-10 — Preference privacy and link lifetime.** Open old preference links as different users and enumerate synthetic recipient identifiers.

checks.heading: Verification reset and recipient abuse
checks.text: **MSG-11 — Verification and recovery token binding.** Swap synthetic tokens across users, purposes, environments, and changed recipient addresses.

checks.heading: Verification reset and recipient abuse
checks.text: **MSG-12 — Expiry single use and concurrency.** Use expired links and race two redemption requests through the real state-changing path.

checks.heading: Verification reset and recipient abuse
checks.text: **MSG-13 — Scanner and preview safety.** Fetch security/action links with a simulated mail scanner before the user completes the intended action.

checks.heading: Verification reset and recipient abuse
checks.text: **MSG-14 — Recovery URL and secret leakage.** Manipulate Host/return parameters and inspect tracking redirects, logs, analytics, referrers, and URL previews.

checks.heading: Verification reset and recipient abuse
checks.text: **MSG-15 — Account enumeration and rate abuse.** Submit existing/nonexistent synthetic recipients and repeated send/verify attempts from multiple bounded identities.

checks.heading: Verification reset and recipient abuse
checks.text: **MSG-16 — Open relay and recipient control.** Use contact, demo, invite, share, signup, and resend endpoints with arbitrary recipients and injected template content.

checks.heading: Verification reset and recipient abuse
checks.text: **MSG-17 — Invitation and address-change safety.** Forward invitations, change email/phone mid-flow, revoke membership, and redeem stale invitations.

checks.heading: Verification reset and recipient abuse
checks.text: **MSG-18 — Recovery delivery failure.** Block provider delivery and exhaust the primary recovery channel using controlled fixtures.

checks.heading: SMS chat push and channel changes
checks.text: **MSG-19 — SMS and voice destination validation.** Where used, test supported country/number formats, restricted destinations, sender identity, and billable segments with a provider stub.

checks.heading: SMS chat push and channel changes
checks.text: **MSG-20 — Channel permission and stop signals.** Exercise supported SMS/chat opt-out keywords, block/unblock, push preferences, and provider preference callbacks.

checks.heading: SMS chat push and channel changes
checks.text: **MSG-21 — Phone identity changes.** Use synthetic recycled-number, changed-number, shared-device, and SIM-change risk scenarios relevant to the product.

checks.heading: SMS chat push and channel changes
checks.text: **MSG-22 — Push and device token isolation.** If push exists, sign out, switch users, rotate/reuse device tokens, revoke permission, and inspect notification previews.

checks.heading: SMS chat push and channel changes
checks.text: **MSG-23 — Chat bot and interactive actions.** If chat integrations exist, forge workspace/channel IDs and replay button commands or modal submissions.

checks.heading: SMS chat push and channel changes
checks.text: **MSG-24 — Multichannel fallback and deduplication.** Fail the preferred channel then recover it while fallback attempts and preference changes are pending.

checks.heading: Representative and safe verification
checks.text: **OPS-01 — Coverage and acceptance plan.** Map supported operations, accounts, roles, tenants, events, message categories, channels, and known failure modes to acceptance checks.

checks.heading: Representative and safe verification
checks.text: **OPS-02 — Contract fixtures and provenance.** Build approved synthetic provider responses, signed callbacks, messages, and reference client fixtures tied to actual versions.

checks.heading: Representative and safe verification
checks.text: **OPS-03 — Stubs sandbox and live differences.** Compare mocked behavior with official test mode and permitted deployed observations, recording account, network, and rate differences.

checks.heading: Representative and safe verification
checks.text: **OPS-04 — Isolation and side-effect containment.** Inspect test credentials, provider accounts, recipient sinks, queue names, endpoints, budgets, and teardown.

checks.heading: Representative and safe verification
checks.text: **OPS-05 — Allowed and denied operations.** Pair invalid signatures, cross-tenant IDs, revoked keys, and forbidden destinations with valid permitted operations.

checks.heading: Representative and safe verification
checks.text: **OPS-06 — Sensitivity of critical checks.** Use known bad fixtures or safe targeted mutations in an isolated disposable copy for important validators.

checks.heading: Representative and safe verification
checks.text: **OPS-07 — Failure matrix and crash points.** Exercise timeouts, outages, throttling, malformed data, duplicated/reordered/missing events, credential failure, and worker interruption.

checks.heading: Representative and safe verification
checks.text: **OPS-08 — End-to-end outcome evidence.** Trace business intent through provider request/event, durable state, queue, external stub effect, and user-visible result.

checks.heading: Operations and incident response
checks.text: **OPS-09 — Safe trace correlation.** Follow one synthetic operation across requests, retries, queue, callbacks, provider message/event IDs, and local persistence.

checks.heading: Operations and incident response
checks.text: **OPS-10 — Outcome and health metrics.** Review accepted/completed/failed work, backlog age, retries, delivery failures, reconnects, suppression lag, and provider quotas.

checks.heading: Operations and incident response
checks.text: **OPS-11 — Cost and abuse visibility.** Trigger bounded synthetic abnormal send volume, expensive routes, callback amplification, and retry growth.

checks.heading: Operations and incident response
checks.text: **OPS-12 — Actionable alert routing.** Generate a scoped outage, essential-mail failure, invalid-callback spike, and backlog threshold event.

checks.heading: Operations and incident response
checks.text: **OPS-13 — Operator permissions and redaction.** Inspect support views, payload exports, resend/replay controls, credential management, and customer history.

checks.heading: Operations and incident response
checks.text: **OPS-14 — Incident containment rehearsal.** Simulate a compromised key, webhook abuse, misdirected message, or provider outage using controlled fixtures.

checks.heading: Operations and incident response
checks.text: **OPS-15 — Recovery and reconciliation runbook.** Have a backup operator recover stuck events, ambiguous sends, failed refreshes, and missed state transitions.

checks.heading: Operations and incident response
checks.text: **OPS-16 — Retention deletion and backup restoration.** Delete synthetic subjects and restore permitted backups in isolation while inspecting event/message histories and suppression records.

checks.heading: Changes release and retirement
checks.text: **OPS-17 — Version and configuration record.** Capture deployed SDK, API/event versions, schemas, templates, DNS, retry policy, routes, signing keys references, and flags.

checks.heading: Changes release and retirement
checks.text: **OPS-18 — Compatibility and release gates.** Compare current and candidate contracts, templates, scopes, and policy on critical normal/adversarial slices.

checks.heading: Changes release and retirement
checks.text: **OPS-19 — Provider deprecation and scope change.** Track actual provider notices, mandatory upgrades, feature retirement, pricing/limit changes, and permission expansion.

checks.heading: Changes release and retirement
checks.text: **OPS-20 — Endpoint provider and domain migration.** Rehearse changing routes, senders, secrets, providers, or accounts with delayed callbacks, queued sends, and old clients.

checks.heading: Changes release and retirement
checks.text: **OPS-21 — Disablement and rollback.** Disable an integration and roll back handler/template/configuration versions with pending work.

checks.heading: Changes release and retirement
checks.text: **OPS-22 — Retirement and cleanup.** Retire a connector and inspect subscriptions, credentials, endpoints, external jobs, exports, queues, DNS, and provider billing.

checks.heading: Changes release and retirement
checks.text: **OPS-23 — Risk decision and handover.** Review confirmed failures, gaps, dormant capabilities, accepted exceptions, ownership, and next review triggers.

checks.heading: API and account contracts
checks.text: Inventory provider purpose, account/environment owner, API/event versions, scopes, quotas, billable units, data destinations/retention, external jobs, failure semantics, and disablement.

checks.heading: API and account contracts
checks.text: Validate request/response schemas and business rules, bounded sizes, encoding/numeric semantics, pagination completeness, partial/batch results, and asynchronous outcomes. Handle unsupported fields and contract drift deliberately.

checks.heading: API and account contracts
checks.text: Protect least-privileged credentials per project/environment; test expiry, revocation, rotation, concurrent refresh, reconnect, unlink, account removal, and unnecessary token/data deletion.

checks.heading: API and account contracts
checks.text: Bind OAuth flows and token use to the actual initiating user/tenant/provider account. Validate registered redirects, transaction binding, code-flow protections, identity/token context, and applicable OIDC requirements. Avoid unsafe email-based account linking.

checks.heading: API and account contracts
checks.text: Distinguish reversible local changes from ambiguous remote effects. Test timeout-after-commit, supported idempotency, durable intent, reconciliation, bounded retries/backoff, cancellation, and partial recovery.

checks.heading: API and account contracts
checks.text: Isolate provider failures and enforce global/per-tenant concurrency, request, retry, and cost budgets. Track external errors, latency, quotas, permission changes, and deprecations.

checks.heading: Webhook delivery
checks.text: Authenticate incoming callbacks using the actual provider-supported mechanism over the required payload bytes/metadata. A secret-looking URL or IP filter alone is not sufficient.

checks.heading: Webhook delivery
checks.text: Validate event/schema version, source account/environment, timestamp/replay controls where supported, payload size, tenant/resource ownership, and current operation permission before changing state.

checks.heading: Webhook delivery
checks.text: Test duplicate, concurrent, delayed, missing, malformed, and out-of-order events. Use durable processing identity, explicit state transitions, safe replay, and reconciliation for missed work.

checks.heading: Webhook delivery
checks.text: Acknowledge accepted critical work only with an appropriate durable recovery path. Verify response-code semantics, crash points, partial processing, queue/outbox boundaries, bounded work, and observable completion/failure.

checks.heading: Webhook delivery
checks.text: For outbound callbacks, authorize subscriptions and payload fields; document identity/version semantics and signing, protect delivery secrets, validate TLS, bound retries/responses, and constrain destinations against SSRF across DNS changes and redirects.

checks.heading: Webhook delivery
checks.text: Provide authorized delivery history, redacted failure details, safe test events, and bounded audited replay. A receiver can accept before an acknowledgment is lost, so consumers need documented duplicate handling.

checks.heading: Webhook delivery
checks.text: Test real edge/WAF/gateway routing without bypassing authentication. Migrate endpoints/secrets deliberately, account for delayed events, and prevent old/new handlers from applying the same effect twice.

checks.heading: Email and messaging
checks.text: Inventory legitimate sender streams and verify actual SPF, DKIM, DMARC alignment, provider domain checks, and relevant DNS/transport behavior. Stage policy changes using legitimate sender evidence and current applicable receiver requirements.

checks.heading: Email and messaging
checks.text: Separate transactional, security, and marketing purposes. Verify required permission, unsubscribe/suppression, bounce/complaint processing, and retention/policy obligations under shared 11.

checks.heading: Email and messaging
checks.text: Inspect rendered campaign/launch templates for required sender identity, postal/address information and clear opt-out. Exercise applicable no-login/no-fee opt-out, header-based one-click where relevant, link validity, and propagation across CRM/provider lists/imports/queued sends within the applicable deadline.

checks.heading: Email and messaging
checks.text: Prevent stale imports or retries from undoing suppression. Keep required transactional/security behavior distinct and prevent marketing from bypassing recipient preferences.

checks.heading: Email and messaging
checks.text: Prevent contact/demo/signup/invite/resend endpoints from becoming arbitrary email or SMS relays. Bound recipients, template variables, verification attempts, bulk volume, expensive routes, and billable work.

checks.heading: Email and messaging
checks.text: Bind verification/reset/invitation links to the correct recipient, environment and purpose with expiry and appropriate atomic single-use behavior. Test scanner/preview fetches, address changes, malicious host/return parameters, and token leakage through logs/tracking/referrers.

checks.heading: Email and messaging
checks.text: Test actual client rendering, accessible responsive content, plain-text/useful alternatives, final action links, localization, recipient confidentiality, and safe handling of user template variables.

checks.heading: Email and messaging
checks.text: Verify representative controlled delivery, expired actions, bounce/failure, provider outage/fallback, duplicate-send prevention, and essential recovery alternatives. Queuing/provider acceptance does not prove user receipt or inbox placement.

checks.heading: Email and messaging
checks.text: If receiving email, treat sender headers, thread IDs, quoted content, MIME and attachments as untrusted; enforce access, bounded parsing, and loop protection.

checks.heading: Email and messaging
checks.text: For SMS/voice/chat/push where present, test current recipient/device/workspace identity, provider callbacks, channel preferences, stop signals, phone changes, interactive action replay, sensitive previews, and approved fallback.

checks.heading: Customer-facing API lifecycle
checks.text: Publish accurate supported versions, schemas, async states, errors, deprecation notice and migration paths. Test representative existing clients and detect unexpected upstream contract changes.

checks.heading: Customer-facing API lifecycle
checks.text: Verify customer keys can be created, scoped, protected, rotated and revoked with current tenant/resource authorization across active requests, caches, jobs, exports and bulk operations.

checks.heading: Customer-facing API lifecycle
checks.text: Rate-limit requests to protect shared capacity while supporting legitimate bursts and providing actionable recovery guidance.

checks.heading: Customer-facing API lifecycle
checks.text: Supply a promised isolated sandbox or equivalent supported test path with synthetic data, separate credentials, and no unintended production charges, messages or state changes.

checks.heading: Customer-facing API lifecycle
checks.text: Expose scoped outbound-webhook history with attempt times, results, redaction, bounded retries and authorized replay. Documentation and sample signing/test payloads must match actual behavior.

checks.heading: Operations and verification
checks.text: Use representative valid/invalid fixtures, paired allowed/denied operations, safe sensitivity checks, and crash/failure evidence through real product paths. Record sandbox/production differences and missing access.

checks.heading: Operations and verification
checks.text: Trace provider request/message/event IDs through durable business outcomes without logging secrets or unnecessary message content. Measure backlog age, failures, retries, suppressed sends, quotas and spend.

checks.heading: Operations and verification
checks.text: Exercise actionable alerts, scoped support views, incident containment, backup-operator recovery, disablement, compatible rollback, deprecation migration and retirement of old credentials/jobs/endpoints/billing.

checks.heading: Define the proposed release
checks.text: **LR-01-01** Identify project, release owner, decision maker, technical responder and support contact. Record actual availability and backup coverage appropriate to team size rather than assuming a large launch team.

checks.heading: Define the proposed release
checks.text: **LR-01-02** Record source commit, build/artifact identity, runtime/dependencies, deployed environment, schema/migration state and active configuration/flags. Identify anything still changing after verification.

checks.heading: Define the proposed release
checks.text: **LR-01-03** Describe launch type: new product, beta, relaunch, feature activation, price/plan change, platform distribution or migration. State intended audience, regions, supported platforms and exclusions.

checks.heading: Define the proposed release
checks.text: **LR-01-04** Define critical user outcomes, explicit non-goals and business invariants. Include revenue, identity, tenant isolation, data durability and costly work where present.

checks.heading: Define the proposed release
checks.text: **LR-01-05** Record exposure plan: invite-only/public, initial cohort, ramp stages, traffic expectations, marketing timing and integrations consuming the release. Separate installed/deployed from enabled and publicly discoverable.

checks.heading: Define the proposed release
checks.text: **LR-01-06** Inventory repositories, services, domains, accounts, workers, schedules, external providers, native clients and shared infrastructure involved. Mark unknown owners and inaccessible environments.

checks.heading: Define the proposed release
checks.text: **LR-01-07** Identify data categories, migration volumes, retention/recovery obligations, user commitments and project-specific legal/commercial reviews. Link applicable specialist review instead of inventing jurisdiction-wide rules.

checks.heading: Define the proposed release
checks.text: **LR-01-08** Select relevant audit modules and controls, with reasons for exclusions. Include inherited shared-host controls and independent per-application permissions and data boundaries.

checks.heading: Set meaningful release gates
checks.text: **LR-01-09** Define project-relative blocker criteria before evaluating findings: unacceptable loss/exposure, broken essential outcome, material financial risk or inadequate recovery. Tie severity to impact and likelihood in the proposed exposure.

checks.heading: Set meaningful release gates
checks.text: **LR-01-10** Distinguish mandatory pre-exposure prerequisites from monitored post-launch follow-up. A condition necessary for safety must be satisfied before the affected cohort receives the feature.

checks.heading: Set meaningful release gates
checks.text: **LR-01-11** Define acceptable degraded modes, maintenance windows, support limitations and outage tolerance. Align promises, rollout gates, recovery targets and actual staffing.

checks.heading: Set meaningful release gates
checks.text: **LR-01-12** Set measurable rollout success, pause and abort conditions using product outcomes, errors, latency, saturation, queue freshness, integrity and spend as applicable. Avoid universal thresholds unsupported by a baseline.

checks.heading: Set meaningful release gates
checks.text: **LR-01-13** Confirm gate feasibility: who can obtain evidence, who can stop exposure, where authority lies and whether the deadline leaves time to respond. Record intentional scope reductions rather than silently skipping checks.

checks.heading: Set meaningful release gates
checks.text: **LR-01-14** Define readiness for distinct cohorts/platforms if they differ. A web release passing does not establish native client, enterprise SSO, international market or migration readiness.

checks.heading: Set meaningful release gates
checks.text: **LR-01-15** Separate availability of optional marketing/analytics enhancements from critical product/security controls. Missing an unnecessary tool must not become an automatic blocker.

checks.heading: Set meaningful release gates
checks.text: **LR-01-16** For beta/internal/low-traffic releases, document which controls may be proportionately lighter and which risks remain material despite a small audience. A beta label does not establish authorization or data safety.

checks.heading: Evidence and test selection
checks.text: **LR-01-17** Map each essential outcome and invariant to specialist check IDs, existing test results, deployed config and selected rehearsal scenarios. Reuse sound evidence rather than automatically adding durable tests.

checks.heading: Evidence and test selection
checks.text: **LR-01-18** Define the role/tenant/plan/device/browser/locale/provider matrix needed for real users. Cover materially distinct implementations and risk boundaries; document sampling and untested population.

checks.heading: Evidence and test selection
checks.text: **LR-01-19** Set authorized environments, synthetic identities/data, external-effect restrictions, request/concurrency/duration/cost ceilings and cancellation/cleanup before live verification.

checks.heading: Evidence and test selection
checks.text: **LR-01-20** Capture expected outcomes independently from implementation, including allowed and denied operations and persisted/provider side effects. An HTTP response or an assistant's statement alone is not runtime proof.

checks.heading: Evidence and test selection
checks.text: **LR-01-21** Bind evidence to candidate revision, configuration, schema and platform. Explain staging/production differences, access limitations, flaky/skipped checks and verification freshness.

checks.heading: Evidence and test selection
checks.text: **LR-01-22** Define what invalidates prior evidence: relevant code/config changes, data migrations, dependency/provider changes or changed exposure. Rerun changed controls and affected flows; broaden only when risk or observed failures justify it.

checks.heading: Evidence and test selection
checks.text: **LR-01-23** Protect evidence using project access/retention rules. Redact credentials, personal/payment data and production payloads while preserving correlation; avoid copying live data unnecessarily.

checks.heading: Evidence and test selection
checks.text: **LR-01-24** Link findings by root cause, affected surface and owning module. Keep defects, verification gaps, improvement opportunities and business choices distinguishable, with acceptance tests and owners.

checks.heading: Decision integrity
checks.text: **LR-01-25** Record accepted risks with actual exposure, alternatives, compensating controls, accountable decision, expiry/review date and affected cohort. Acceptance does not change Fail to Pass or satisfy an external obligation.

checks.heading: Decision integrity
checks.text: **LR-01-26** Use insufficient evidence when critical assurance cannot be established, and blocked when verified conditions prevent the proposed launch. Do not average away a blocker with many low-risk passing checks.

checks.heading: Decision integrity
checks.text: **LR-01-27** Establish ownership and deadline for every unresolved item, conditional prerequisite and post-launch task. Record escalation if the owner is unavailable or a prerequisite misses its deadline.

checks.heading: Decision integrity
checks.text: **LR-01-28** Preserve the final decision, candidate manifest, evidence references and run-of-show together. Reassess after a material candidate/exposure change using the established project release process.

checks.heading: Critical outcomes and content
checks.text: **LR-02-01** Execute each essential visitor/customer/admin journey end to end on the release candidate, including a clear entry point, primary action, result and recovery/support route.

checks.heading: Critical outcomes and content
checks.text: **LR-02-02** Verify navigation, search, deep links, redirects, consequential outbound links and back/forward behavior. Check authenticated links opened anonymously and externally shared links opened in another session.

checks.heading: Critical outcomes and content
checks.text: **LR-02-03** Test signup, verification, login, reset, session expiry and logout where offered. Account for link expiry, cross-device use, resend behavior and useful recovery without account enumeration.

checks.heading: Critical outcomes and content
checks.text: **LR-02-04** Check onboarding, invitations, required permissions and first meaningful success with fresh synthetic accounts. Existing developer/admin state must not mask missing setup or inaccessible initial data.

checks.heading: Critical outcomes and content
checks.text: **LR-02-05** Exercise forms with valid/invalid input, validation errors, duplicate submit, slow submit and failure after submission. Preserve safe user input and show actual completion rather than misleading success.

checks.heading: Critical outcomes and content
checks.text: **LR-02-06** Verify loading, empty, partial, unavailable, denied, expired and error states. Provide actionable next steps, appropriate status codes and a useful 404 without returning a successful page for a missing resource.

checks.heading: Critical outcomes and content
checks.text: **LR-02-07** Remove placeholder copy, broken assets, fabricated claims and obsolete contact/pricing details. Verify promises, screenshots, tutorials and plan comparisons match enabled features and actual limits.

checks.heading: Critical outcomes and content
checks.text: **LR-02-08** Isolate or remove test/demo content and test privileges using an authorized data-safe method. Verify fixtures, seeded credentials and demo write paths cannot affect real tenants.

checks.heading: Critical outcomes and content
checks.text: **LR-02-09** Check transactional copy, confirmations, receipts and timestamps against actual state. Distinguish accepted, queued, completed and failed work; do not promise an outcome before it exists.

checks.heading: Accessibility, devices and localization
checks.text: **LR-02-10** Apply the project's accessibility target with keyboard and selected assistive-technology journeys. Verify focus order/visibility, labels, names, errors and status announcements; automated scans alone do not establish conformance.

checks.heading: Accessibility, devices and localization
checks.text: **LR-02-11** Check contrast, zoom/reflow, text resize, meaningful alternatives, reduced motion and media captions where applicable. Ensure cookie dialogs, payment flows and support widgets do not block core access.

checks.heading: Accessibility, devices and localization
checks.text: **LR-02-12** Test core actions on supported mobile/tablet/desktop layouts and input methods. Cover touch targets, virtual keyboards, orientation and browser chrome rather than only a responsive screenshot.

checks.heading: Accessibility, devices and localization
checks.text: **LR-02-13** Use representative constrained devices and poor connectivity for loading, submitting and resuming. Check offline/interrupted behavior and prevent duplicate purchases/writes after reconnect.

checks.heading: Accessibility, devices and localization
checks.text: **LR-02-14** Verify declared browser/OS/client support and meaningful old-client compatibility. Record unsupported combinations honestly instead of assuming every platform or the newest desktop browser is sufficient.

checks.heading: Accessibility, devices and localization
checks.text: **LR-02-15** For supported locales, verify language, text expansion, right-to-left layout, currency, dates, timezone, decimal formats and encoding. Keep user-visible terms and support routes coherent with the enabled market.

checks.heading: Accessibility, devices and localization
checks.text: **LR-02-16** Check authentication/payment challenges and abuse defenses for accessible alternatives and false positives. Include intended API clients and legitimate shared-IP users where relevant.

checks.heading: Discovery, delivery and trust
checks.text: **LR-02-17** For public searchable content, verify production titles, descriptions, canonical hosts, sitemap, robots rules, indexing directives and redirects. Keep private/staging content access-controlled; robots.txt is not a security boundary.

checks.heading: Discovery, delivery and trust
checks.text: **LR-02-18** Test representative HTTP status codes, redirect chains, removed URLs and old bookmarks. For relaunches, verify important old-to-new mappings rather than redirecting every missing URL to the homepage.

checks.heading: Discovery, delivery and trust
checks.text: **LR-02-19** Verify social preview cards/images, favicon, branding and link appearance with actual public assets. Ensure previews reveal no private or placeholder information.

checks.heading: Discovery, delivery and trust
checks.text: **LR-02-20** Measure key page/API performance on representative release infrastructure and user conditions. State test method, data size, percentile/window where meaningful and limits of synthetic versus real-user evidence.

checks.heading: Discovery, delivery and trust
checks.text: **LR-02-21** Verify images, responsive sizing, fonts, script loading and lazy-loading behavior preserve essential content and interaction. Test cold caches and third-party widget failures as well as repeat visits.

checks.heading: Discovery, delivery and trust
checks.text: **LR-02-22** Verify applicable privacy, terms, refund/cancellation, contact and consent disclosures are reachable and match actual data/product behavior. Obtain project-specific review for obligations rather than copying generic policy text as assurance.

checks.heading: Discovery, delivery and trust
checks.text: **LR-02-23** Where consent is required, test accept, reject, withdrawal and preference persistence against actual tracking and third-party requests. Do not require a cookie banner when the scoped implementation does not need one.

checks.heading: Discovery, delivery and trust
checks.text: **LR-02-24** Make pricing, trials, renewal, cancellation, usage limits and material AI/product limitations clear before commitment. Match claims to actual entitlement behavior and supported geography/platform.

checks.heading: API, native and platform delivery
checks.text: **LR-02-25** For APIs/SDKs, verify published endpoints, version/auth instructions, examples, errors, quotas and a small real supported-client journey. Check that documentation points to the live supported version.

checks.heading: API, native and platform delivery
checks.text: **LR-02-26** For native/desktop/mobile/game distribution, verify intended package, signing identity, version, supported hardware/OS, architecture, install permissions and trusted download/store destination.

checks.heading: API, native and platform delivery
checks.text: **LR-02-27** Test fresh install, upgrade and uninstall or rollback behavior as applicable. Preserve user data/settings/save compatibility according to product promises; define recovery when downgrading cannot read new data.

checks.heading: API, native and platform delivery
checks.text: **LR-02-28** Check store review/release state, staged distribution, region/age/content declarations, required platform permissions and release notes against current platform requirements where applicable.

checks.heading: API, native and platform delivery
checks.text: **LR-02-29** Test native deep links, OAuth return paths, push permissions and links from email/store/browser in supported app states. Prevent wrong-environment callbacks and duplicate account/transaction effects.

checks.heading: API, native and platform delivery
checks.text: **LR-02-30** For service workers/offline caches/installed web apps, test a returning user with an old client and cached assets. Avoid mixed-version failures and stale feature/authorization assumptions after deployment.

checks.heading: API, native and platform delivery
checks.text: **LR-02-31** Verify platform-specific critical experiences, such as game saves, matchmaking, licensed assets, notifications or file associations, when they are part of the advertised release. Exclude them explicitly otherwise.

checks.heading: API, native and platform delivery
checks.text: **LR-02-32** Align announcements, help pages, app/store listings and release notes with the actual cohort/flag schedule. Prepared content must not expose an unavailable feature or bypass an intentionally limited rollout.

checks.heading: Accounts, domains and environment
checks.text: **LR-03-01** Confirm organization-controlled ownership, billing, administrative recovery and primary/backup authorized access for registrar, DNS, hosting, source control, database, payment, email and backup providers.

checks.heading: Accounts, domains and environment
checks.text: **LR-03-02** Verify available MFA, scoped access, secure recovery and emergency operator access for consequential accounts. Remove obsolete/shared credentials where required without losing a working recovery route.

checks.heading: Accounts, domains and environment
checks.text: **LR-03-03** Resolve intended domains/subdomains and inspect A/AAAA/CNAME records, proxy/CDN routing and old hosts. Include IPv6 and direct-origin exposure where configured, not only the developer's cached resolver.

checks.heading: Accounts, domains and environment
checks.text: **LR-03-04** Verify valid TLS for every public name and callback endpoint, HTTPS redirects, certificate renewal operation and expiry notifications. Assess strict transport settings against actual subdomain readiness.

checks.heading: Accounts, domains and environment
checks.text: **LR-03-05** Review security headers and browser policies against the application: content policy, framing, content types and referrer behavior as relevant. Verify essential payment/OAuth/media flows still work under effective headers.

checks.heading: Accounts, domains and environment
checks.text: **LR-03-06** Record effective environment values, secret references, allowed hosts/origins, callback URLs and active flags. Separate test/live resources and ensure missing required configuration fails safely.

checks.heading: Accounts, domains and environment
checks.text: **LR-03-07** Protect staging, previews, administration and diagnostic surfaces with actual access controls. Check alternate domains, old deployments, source maps, backup files and exposed storage; indexing directives alone do not protect them.

checks.heading: Accounts, domains and environment
checks.text: **LR-03-08** Confirm production disables unsafe debug output, test bypasses, default accounts, placeholder secrets and public privileged diagnostics. Verify defaults in a clean deployment, not only an already configured server.

checks.heading: Accounts, domains and environment
checks.text: **LR-03-09** Check CDN/cache/proxy settings preserve authentication, private response isolation, client address trust and correct URL schemes. Test a logged-out/other-tenant request after a privileged response has been cached.

checks.heading: Identity, authorization and untrusted inputs
checks.text: **LR-03-10** Execute essential allowed and denied operations with anonymous, ordinary, other-tenant, disabled and privileged synthetic users. Link response and persisted/external-effect evidence from the security module.

checks.heading: Identity, authorization and untrusted inputs
checks.text: **LR-03-11** Verify session/cookie/token settings for production hosts, expiry, logout, revocation and CSRF protection where applicable. Test existing sessions across the planned release or domain change.

checks.heading: Identity, authorization and untrusted inputs
checks.text: **LR-03-12** Test signup, verification, reset and invitation links for expiry, ownership and correct destination. Ensure tokens and unnecessary personal information do not leak through logs, referrers or error pages.

checks.heading: Identity, authorization and untrusted inputs
checks.text: **LR-03-13** Confirm OAuth/SSO redirect registrations, tenant restrictions, state/nonce handling and role mapping for the live identity configuration. Include account linking and users without the expected domain/role.

checks.heading: Identity, authorization and untrusted inputs
checks.text: **LR-03-14** Verify upload, import, rich text, URL-fetch and export paths apply specialist validation and authorization. Include storage access policies and server-side rejection before harmful or costly effects.

checks.heading: Identity, authorization and untrusted inputs
checks.text: **LR-03-15** Confirm API/admin/worker entry points enforce the same material permissions as the UI. A hidden menu, unlisted URL or disabled button is not deployed authorization.

checks.heading: Identity, authorization and untrusted inputs
checks.text: **LR-03-16** Review security-relevant changes against the final candidate through the project's existing process. Invalidate affected review evidence after relevant edits; do not treat tool installation as proof of review.

checks.heading: Secrets and build provenance
checks.text: **LR-03-17** Inspect release source/history exposure, frontend bundles, container layers, CI artifacts, logs, diagnostic endpoints and committed configuration for privileged credentials. Record inspected surfaces and limits.

checks.heading: Secrets and build provenance
checks.text: **LR-03-18** Revoke/rotate exposed credentials and verify downstream services use the new secret. Deleting the visible string does not invalidate an already exposed key or token.

checks.heading: Secrets and build provenance
checks.text: **LR-03-19** Verify least-privilege provider/database/service credentials and environment separation. A staging leak must not grant unnecessary production payment, backup or administrative capabilities.

checks.heading: Secrets and build provenance
checks.text: **LR-03-20** Link the candidate to its source and build inputs; verify the deployed artifact/digest and configured runtime. Avoid an untracked rebuild or mutable image tag changing what was reviewed.

checks.heading: Secrets and build provenance
checks.text: **LR-03-21** Run applicable build, lint/type, dependency and container/runtime security checks for the actual stack. Record skipped checks, actionable results and effective deployed versions, not just a local lockfile.

checks.heading: Secrets and build provenance
checks.text: **LR-03-22** Inspect pipeline permissions, protected release paths, untrusted contribution execution and access to paid/production secrets. Required gates must actually run for the chosen release mechanism.

checks.heading: Secrets and build provenance
checks.text: **LR-03-23** Check build/install hooks, downloaded binaries, base images and third-party assets for appropriate provenance and licenses. Link specialist findings rather than introducing an unsupported universal certification gate.

checks.heading: Secrets and build provenance
checks.text: **LR-03-24** Verify secrets/configuration can be restored or reissued through secure references without baking credentials into distributable artifacts. Test access using approved synthetic or scoped credentials.

checks.heading: Network, runtime and vendor exposure
checks.text: **LR-03-25** Verify only intended ports/services are reachable, administrative interfaces are restricted and trusted proxy/firewall rules match the deployed topology. Include database/cache/debug ports on shared hosts.

checks.heading: Network, runtime and vendor exposure
checks.text: **LR-03-26** Attach effective runtime/OS patch ownership and container privileges, mounts, resource limits and persistence evidence where relevant. A healthy local container does not establish host hardening or durable storage.

checks.heading: Network, runtime and vendor exposure
checks.text: **LR-03-27** Confirm provider accounts are active, funded or contracted as required, out of unintended sandbox mode and provisioned in approved regions. Verify launch-critical quotas and any pending access approvals.

checks.heading: Network, runtime and vendor exposure
checks.text: **LR-03-28** Review third-party scripts, widgets, analytics and support tools for required access, data flow and failure behavior. A vendor outage or blocked script must not prevent an essential unrelated action without a documented reason.

checks.heading: Network, runtime and vendor exposure
checks.text: **LR-03-29** Ensure security findings and production evidence gaps have release consequences, accountable owners and acceptance conditions. Record which inherited infrastructure controls were verified and when.

checks.heading: Network, runtime and vendor exposure
checks.text: **LR-03-30** Verify safe operator response to a compromised key/device/account: access revocation, alternate recovery, protected evidence and production continuity. Link a rehearsal or current verified runbook proportionate to the risk.

checks.heading: Data and durable work
checks.text: **LR-04-01** Verify the final schema, constraints, indexes and seeded reference data against the candidate. Separate required product data from unsafe test/admin fixtures.

checks.heading: Data and durable work
checks.text: **LR-04-02** Execute representative create/read/update/delete and export/import journeys for important entities, roles and tenants. Include relationships, active references and declared deletion/retention behavior.

checks.heading: Data and durable work
checks.text: **LR-04-03** Confirm duplicate submissions, retries and concurrent updates preserve material invariants. Validate persisted results and external effects, not only status codes or successful UI notifications.

checks.heading: Data and durable work
checks.text: **LR-04-04** Test interrupted writes, partial batches, process restart and dependency timeouts using bounded fixtures. State recovery/reconciliation behavior for work that was accepted but not completed.

checks.heading: Data and durable work
checks.text: **LR-04-05** Verify storage is durable across restart, redeploy, rescheduling and the selected hosting model. Include uploads, mounted volumes, generated files, encryption keys and metadata, not only database rows.

checks.heading: Data and durable work
checks.text: **LR-04-06** Attach retention, deletion, audit and privacy-review evidence for applicable data flows. Document production data left in logs, providers, replicas or backups and the intended access/lifecycle policy.

checks.heading: Data and durable work
checks.text: **LR-04-07** Reconcile real scheduler/worker/repeater ownership across environments and replicas. Record schedule/timezone, overlap, retries, dead-letter handling and freshness alerts for critical background work.

checks.heading: Data and durable work
checks.text: **LR-04-08** Check queue admission, backpressure, concurrency, backlog age and cancellation. Ensure restart or redrive does not duplicate irreversible effects or replay retired work.

checks.heading: Integrations and messages
checks.text: **LR-04-09** Inventory live provider endpoints, credentials, scopes, callback registrations, schema/API versions and owners. Identify critical dependencies still waiting for approval, verification or production access.

checks.heading: Integrations and messages
checks.text: **LR-04-10** Test callback/webhook authentication, duplicate delivery, replay, delay and out-of-order events. Invalid/duplicate events must not create unauthorized state, charges, grants or notifications.

checks.heading: Integrations and messages
checks.text: **LR-04-11** Exercise provider timeout/outage/rate-limit behavior with controlled faults. Bound retries across SDK, gateway, worker and application layers and track ambiguous outcomes for reconciliation.

checks.heading: Integrations and messages
checks.text: **LR-04-12** Verify live sender identity and applicable email authentication, reply/contact routes and delivery configuration. Use approved recipients or sandbox/stub evidence; distinguish accepted-by-provider from delivered/read.

checks.heading: Integrations and messages
checks.text: **LR-04-13** Check message templates, links, expiry, locale/timezone, attachments and unsubscribe/preferences where applicable. Prevent real marketing or transactional sends from test/staging workflows.

checks.heading: Integrations and messages
checks.text: **LR-04-14** Test external consumer/API compatibility for changed contracts, event schemas, pagination and authentication. Document deprecation, version transition and recovery for unsupported clients.

checks.heading: Payments, subscriptions and entitlements
checks.text: **LR-04-15** Verify production payment account, intended live products/prices/currency/tax configuration, keys, callback secrets and return URLs. Keep sandbox and live identifiers visibly distinct in evidence.

checks.heading: Payments, subscriptions and entitlements
checks.text: **LR-04-16** Attach sandbox lifecycle evidence for success, decline, additional authentication, duplicate submission, abandon/retry and ambiguous completion. Any live verification must be separately authorized and tightly bounded.

checks.heading: Payments, subscriptions and entitlements
checks.text: **LR-04-17** Verify refund/partial-refund, cancel/reactivate, delinquency, trial expiry and downgrade behavior against policy. Confirm provider, internal financial state, entitlement and effective time agree.

checks.heading: Payments, subscriptions and entitlements
checks.text: **LR-04-18** Replay delayed/duplicated/out-of-order financial callbacks and test direct protected operations. Client redirects or UI claims alone must not establish payment authority or grant access.

checks.heading: Payments, subscriptions and entitlements
checks.text: **LR-04-19** Verify receipts/invoices, renewal notices and support refund/cancellation tools as applicable. Ensure staff permissions and audit trails match actual support duties.

checks.heading: Payments, subscriptions and entitlements
checks.text: **LR-04-20** Confirm server-authoritative prices, plans and credit grants, including promotions and referrals. Test concurrent quota/credit admission and queued work across expiry or revocation using synthetic balances.

checks.heading: Capacity, costs and abuse
checks.text: **LR-04-21** Record expected launch traffic, marketing bursts, data sizes, expensive operations, concurrent sessions and dependency demand. Identify uncertainty and available headroom rather than inventing a precise forecast.

checks.heading: Capacity, costs and abuse
checks.text: **LR-04-22** Use bounded authorized capacity evidence on representative infrastructure where risk warrants it. Include cold starts, caches, connection pools, shared-host contention and the configured scaling ceiling.

checks.heading: Capacity, costs and abuse
checks.text: **LR-04-23** Verify per-request duration/size, connection, upload, result and concurrency limits plus tenant/global controls. Include public demos, signup/reset, exports and legacy routes that bypass the UI.

checks.heading: Capacity, costs and abuse
checks.text: **LR-04-24** Attach effective AI/messaging/storage/egress/compute budgets and application stop evidence. Distinguish provider alerts, quotas and actual spending rejection, including reporting lag and in-flight liabilities.

checks.heading: Capacity, costs and abuse
checks.text: **LR-04-25** Check plan economics under allowed maximum usage, expiry of credits/discounts and a heavy legitimate user. Record deliberate subsidies, overage and exposure ownership.

checks.heading: Capacity, costs and abuse
checks.text: **LR-04-26** Verify operators can suspend abuse, revoke keys/sessions and stop queued/retrying expensive work. Preserve legitimate shared-IP/API/accessibility access and record residual uncancellable effects.

checks.heading: Capacity, costs and abuse
checks.text: **LR-04-27** Bound recurring jobs, orphan resources, preview environments and subscriptions. Ensure launch or migration does not leave duplicate paid work or forgotten old environments active.

checks.heading: Capacity, costs and abuse
checks.text: **LR-04-28** Confirm database, disk/inodes, memory, CPU/GPU, sockets, queue storage and provider service quotas can support the defined exposure. Fixed-price infrastructure can fail from capacity exhaustion without a billing spike.

checks.heading: AI and high-impact workload gates
checks.text: **LR-04-29** For AI features, attach evaluation evidence for advertised capabilities, material failure modes and unsupported behavior. Include representative task inputs and release-specific model/prompt/tool changes.

checks.heading: AI and high-impact workload gates
checks.text: **LR-04-30** Verify tenant/data isolation and permissions for retrieval and tools, including synthetic untrusted-content attempts. Generated text must not itself authorize privileged actions or budget increases.

checks.heading: AI and high-impact workload gates
checks.text: **LR-04-31** Bound agent turns, tool fan-out, total run cost/time, retries, continuations and model fallbacks. Test exhausted-budget and stream-disconnect behavior without assuming remote work automatically stops.

checks.heading: AI and high-impact workload gates
checks.text: **LR-04-32** Check file/media processing, archive expansion, large import/export and batch workloads for bounded CPU/memory/disk/output. Preserve safe partial results and cleanup according to policy.

checks.heading: AI and high-impact workload gates
checks.text: **LR-04-33** Define degraded behavior when a critical provider is unavailable or unaffordable. Preserve user work and honest status; do not silently send data to a new provider or charge for unstarted work.

checks.heading: AI and high-impact workload gates
checks.text: **LR-04-34** Reconcile launch-critical findings from data reliability, integrations, payments, AI and cost modules into the candidate's release decision with owners and acceptance evidence.

checks.heading: Candidate and deployment procedure
checks.text: **LR-05-01** Identify the exact artifact, configuration, secrets references, schema requirements and deployment entry point. Verify the artifact promoted to production is the candidate actually reviewed.

checks.heading: Candidate and deployment procedure
checks.text: **LR-05-02** Record deploy owner, operator access, prerequisites, expected duration, change conflicts and a run-of-show with ordered steps and stop points. Use the existing project release mechanism.

checks.heading: Candidate and deployment procedure
checks.text: **LR-05-03** Rehearse build/promotion/deploy on representative isolated infrastructure with the intended runtime, proxy, persistence and worker startup. Record deviations from production and unresolved portability assumptions.

checks.heading: Candidate and deployment procedure
checks.text: **LR-05-04** Verify health/readiness/startup checks reflect appropriate dependencies and do not route traffic before useful service is available. Distinguish safe liveness from dependency failures that would cause restart loops.

checks.heading: Candidate and deployment procedure
checks.text: **LR-05-05** Check graceful drain, connection/stream handling, long jobs and termination deadlines during update. Test interruption and retries according to actual service promises rather than assuming zero downtime.

checks.heading: Candidate and deployment procedure
checks.text: **LR-05-06** Verify staged rollout/cohort/feature-flag targeting and server enforcement. Check anonymous, logged-in, old-client and alternate-route access, flag defaults, expiry and unauthorized flag changes.

checks.heading: Candidate and deployment procedure
checks.text: **LR-05-07** Confirm cache invalidation, asset versioning and service-worker behavior do not mix incompatible frontend/backend versions. Test a returning session and stale CDN/browser assets.

checks.heading: Candidate and deployment procedure
checks.text: **LR-05-08** Verify post-deploy smoke checks include essential user outcomes, authentication, write/read, background completion and applicable money/provider paths, with safe bounded effects.

checks.heading: Schema and contract compatibility
checks.text: **LR-05-09** Review schema migration order, transaction/lock behavior, expected runtime, free space and required permissions using a representative bounded rehearsal. Identify destructive/irreversible steps explicitly.

checks.heading: Schema and contract compatibility
checks.text: **LR-05-10** Test old/new application and worker versions against the schema during rolling deployment. Use compatible expansion/transition/contraction or a documented maintenance alternative.

checks.heading: Schema and contract compatibility
checks.text: **LR-05-11** Verify data backfills/conversions are bounded, resumable and reconcilable. Include partial failure, duplicates, invalid legacy records and concurrent new writes; record checkpoints and ownership.

checks.heading: Schema and contract compatibility
checks.text: **LR-05-12** Confirm message/event/API contracts remain compatible with queued old jobs, delayed callbacks and supported installed clients. A completed database migration does not establish external consumer compatibility.

checks.heading: Schema and contract compatibility
checks.text: **LR-05-13** Define migration authority and exactly which process can run each change. Prevent multiple deploy replicas or old/new environments from performing the same non-idempotent migration/job.

checks.heading: Schema and contract compatibility
checks.text: **LR-05-14** Verify downgrade/rollback compatibility with newly written data and changed provider state. Record a fail-forward path or maintenance recovery when a binary rollback would corrupt or lose valid work.

checks.heading: Backup and restore evidence
checks.text: **LR-05-15** Inventory required recovery assets: databases, uploaded/generated files, persistent volumes, configuration, keys, identity dependencies and external-system references. State what cannot be reconstructed.

checks.heading: Backup and restore evidence
checks.text: **LR-05-16** Define RPO and RTO from product needs and commitments. Compare measured backup age/coverage and recovery time with those targets; a nominal daily schedule is not proof of adequacy.

checks.heading: Backup and restore evidence
checks.text: **LR-05-17** Verify backups actually complete, remain accessible after account/host failure and have appropriate encryption, access and retention. Include recovery key and vendor-account availability without exposing secrets.

checks.heading: Backup and restore evidence
checks.text: **LR-05-18** Perform or attach a recent representative isolated restore and validate application-readable data, integrity, permissions and files. A successful backup log or checksum alone does not prove usable recovery.

checks.heading: Backup and restore evidence
checks.text: **LR-05-19** Test the recovery access path independently of the failed application/host. Keep runbooks and required recovery references available outside the failure domain.

checks.heading: Backup and restore evidence
checks.text: **LR-05-20** State restore consequences for accepted writes, payment effects, idempotency records, credits and external callbacks after the recovery point. Reconcile rather than replaying irreversible effects blindly.

checks.heading: Rollback, fail-forward and infrastructure migration
checks.text: **LR-05-21** Define objective pause/rollback/fail-forward triggers and who can invoke them. Record executable steps, known limitations, required data checkpoint and time to restoration.

checks.heading: Rollback, fail-forward and infrastructure migration
checks.text: **LR-05-22** Rehearse the chosen recovery using a synthetic candidate failure. Validate essential journeys and data/provider consistency after recovery; a script's zero exit code alone is insufficient.

checks.heading: Rollback, fail-forward and infrastructure migration
checks.text: **LR-05-23** For hosting/domain changes, verify source/destination dependencies, persistent storage, network/TLS, callbacks, identity redirects and provider allowlists before traffic moves.

checks.heading: Rollback, fail-forward and infrastructure migration
checks.text: **LR-05-24** Declare the authoritative writer and ownership of jobs/events/queues at each cutover step. Prevent split-brain, duplicate charges, duplicated notifications and writes to an abandoned database.

checks.heading: Rollback, fail-forward and infrastructure migration
checks.text: **LR-05-25** Rehearse initial copy, deltas/final sync, write freeze where needed, verification and traffic switch with measured duration. Compare records/files using suitable counts, checksums and domain-level validation.

checks.heading: Rollback, fail-forward and infrastructure migration
checks.text: **LR-05-26** Account for DNS caching, long-lived connections, CDN propagation and clients still reaching the old host. Define treatment of late writes/callbacks without assuming a record change moves all traffic instantly.

checks.heading: Rollback, fail-forward and infrastructure migration
checks.text: **LR-05-27** Record when rollback becomes unsafe because data or external effects diverge. Preserve a data-safe reconciliation/fail-forward plan; switching DNS back is not a complete recovery procedure.

checks.heading: Rollback, fail-forward and infrastructure migration
checks.text: **LR-05-28** Keep old infrastructure only for a justified recovery/retention window with owners and budgets. Disable duplicate processing and retire unused resources/credentials after evidence permits it.

checks.heading: Recovery closure
checks.text: **LR-05-29** Verify rollback/redeploy cannot resurrect retired jobs, permissive flags, consumed quotas or obsolete credentials. Test restored configuration and actual scheduler state, not just the current source tree.

checks.heading: Recovery closure
checks.text: **LR-05-30** Record evidence, measured durations, residual data/financial discrepancies and remaining manual steps from deployment and recovery rehearsals. Bind results to the final procedure and candidate.

checks.heading: Recovery closure
checks.text: **LR-05-31** Ensure material rehearsal failures are corrected or reflected in the release decision. Define focused retests after migration, recovery procedure or configuration changes.

checks.heading: Recovery closure
checks.text: **LR-05-32** Hand over recoverable artifacts, configuration references, data checkpoints and owners. Verify the nominated backup operator can locate the procedure and obtain authorized access.

checks.heading: Observe useful service
checks.text: **LR-06-01** Verify external monitoring from outside the application's failure domain for an appropriate public/core path. A running process or always-green health endpoint is not sufficient evidence of useful service.

checks.heading: Observe useful service
checks.text: **LR-06-02** Capture meaningful browser/client/server/worker/integration errors with release, request/job/event correlation. Control sensitive payloads, log access, sampling and retention.

checks.heading: Observe useful service
checks.text: **LR-06-03** Measure critical outcome success, errors, representative latency, traffic and saturation. Define metric windows/denominators and distinguish client retries from unique outcomes.

checks.heading: Observe useful service
checks.text: **LR-06-04** Monitor queue depth/age, scheduled-task freshness, webhook backlog, backup age, certificate/domain expiry and provider dependency failures where applicable. A missing run may emit no exception.

checks.heading: Observe useful service
checks.text: **LR-06-05** Verify actionable capacity, unexpected spend, abuse and security signals. Distinguish delayed estimates from actual enforced limits and include monitoring's own cost/cardinality.

checks.heading: Observe useful service
checks.text: **LR-06-06** Exercise one controlled relevant failure through the real monitoring route. Record detection, delivery, recipient, acknowledgement/escalation and the operator action available.

checks.heading: Observe useful service
checks.text: **LR-06-07** Suppress duplicate/noisy alerts and retain detection for important failures during deploy/maintenance. A temporary silence needs an owner and expiry so launch does not remain unmonitored.

checks.heading: Observe useful service
checks.text: **LR-06-08** If analytics serves a defined product need, verify meaningful events, privacy/consent behavior and duplicate/test traffic filtering. Optional analytics is not a universal release prerequisite.

checks.heading: Operator and support readiness
checks.text: **LR-06-09** Name primary and backup responders with realistic availability, access and escalation. Schedule exposure/ramp stages when the required response capability actually exists.

checks.heading: Operator and support readiness
checks.text: **LR-06-10** Keep concise runbooks for outage, data loss, failed deploy, compromised account/key, provider outage, payment drift, backlog and uncontrolled spend where relevant.

checks.heading: Operator and support readiness
checks.text: **LR-06-11** Verify runbooks, credential-recovery references and incident communication remain accessible during host/application/account failure. Avoid placing the sole recovery instructions in the system being recovered.

checks.heading: Operator and support readiness
checks.text: **LR-06-12** Test a support contact route using synthetic content and confirm accountable receipt. Verify help links, expected response commitments and routing for billing, safety/security and account recovery.

checks.heading: Operator and support readiness
checks.text: **LR-06-13** Give staff sufficient scoped tooling for refunds, suspensions, data corrections, queue handling and customer recovery. Check authorization/auditing and avoid support privileges becoming a bypass.

checks.heading: Operator and support readiness
checks.text: **LR-06-14** Prepare troubleshooting/help material for known limitations, failed onboarding, quota exhaustion and supported platforms. Staff should know actual enabled features and conditions, not just marketing promises.

checks.heading: Operator and support readiness
checks.text: **LR-06-15** Define incident lead, technical response and customer communication duties. Link security/privacy/legal processes for notification assessment where applicable without inventing a universal notification deadline.

checks.heading: Operator and support readiness
checks.text: **LR-06-16** Verify customer/status communication channels as needed, including their access and independence from the failed service. Drafted announcements are not sent as part of an audit.

checks.heading: Run the launch
checks.text: **LR-06-17** Complete a preflight for candidate/config/schema identity, owner availability, prerequisites, external provider health, backups and competing changes. Reassess if the environment has materially drifted.

checks.heading: Run the launch
checks.text: **LR-06-18** Record the final decision through the established process with scope, evidence, blockers, risk acceptances and prerequisites. Do not treat an auditor's checklist completion as release authorization.

checks.heading: Run the launch
checks.text: **LR-06-19** Use a stepwise run-of-show identifying actor, action, expected state/evidence, deadline and stop/recovery condition. Include activation, traffic routing, job ownership and post-deploy smoke.

checks.heading: Run the launch
checks.text: **LR-06-20** At each ramp stage, compare actual outcomes with baseline/control and declared gates. Confirm enough representative traffic/time for the interpretation; low error count with no real usage is weak evidence.

checks.heading: Run the launch
checks.text: **LR-06-21** Verify kill switches, scoped feature disablement, admission limits and recovery controls are available to the responder. Define user-facing behavior and treatment of queued/in-flight work.

checks.heading: Run the launch
checks.text: **LR-06-22** Pause or recover when agreed triggers fire; record action time, affected cohort and external/data effects. Avoid continuing the ramp solely because an announcement or deadline exists.

checks.heading: Run the launch
checks.text: **LR-06-23** Revalidate smoke journeys, provider callbacks, worker freshness, entitlement and important metrics after configuration/routing changes. Check the actual user-facing host and deployed artifact.

checks.heading: Run the launch
checks.text: **LR-06-24** Coordinate publication, invitation and marketing timing with actual availability and support readiness. Verify old links and newly announced entry points once authorized exposure begins.

checks.heading: Observation and handoff
checks.text: **LR-06-25** Define an observation window based on material usage and critical schedules: renewals, scheduled jobs, daily/weekly tasks or delayed events may need evidence after immediate smoke checks.

checks.heading: Observation and handoff
checks.text: **LR-06-26** Assign delayed verification owners/dates for billing, renewals, long-running jobs, search processing, backups and propagation. Distinguish current deployed success from future confirmation still pending.

checks.heading: Observation and handoff
checks.text: **LR-06-27** Review support feedback, false-positive abuse blocks, accessibility issues and cohort-specific failures during the ramp. Update scope and pause criteria when new material behavior appears.

checks.heading: Observation and handoff
checks.text: **LR-06-28** Close temporary credentials, debug instrumentation, alert silences, test accounts and obsolete environments under authorized lifecycle rules. Preserve evidence and required recovery/retention copies.

checks.heading: Observation and handoff
checks.text: **LR-06-29** Hand over service ownership, inventory, budgets, contracts/renewals, support, incident access and recovery artifacts. Confirm the backup operator can use the handoff without relying on one person's laptop or memory.

checks.heading: Observation and handoff
checks.text: **LR-06-30** Deduplicate launch defects into the owning backlog with priority, acceptance tests, owner and due/review date. Track unresolved verification gaps and expiring risk acceptances explicitly.

checks.heading: Observation and handoff
checks.text: **LR-06-31** Record launch outcome against the scoped goals, actual exposure, incidents and rollback/degraded operation. Separate technical release success from business adoption or later growth results.

checks.heading: Observation and handoff
checks.text: **LR-06-32** Capture proportionate lessons and reusable procedure fixes after material incidents or surprising launch behavior. Define when evidence/gates need refresh for the next release rather than repeating every check automatically.

checks.heading: Public experience
checks.text: Verify the primary journey and a clear principal CTA for each important page. Check onboarding, forms, feedback, mobile layouts, loading/error/empty states, and a useful custom 404 with the correct response status.

checks.heading: Public experience
checks.text: Fix broken navigation and consequential links, placeholder copy, false claims, and outdated contact/support details. Remove or isolate test accounts and test content without deleting valid customer data.

checks.heading: Public experience
checks.text: Confirm applicable privacy, terms, cookie, refund/cancellation, and contact information are accessible and accurate. A cookie banner is needed only when applicable; its behavior must reflect real tracking.

checks.heading: Public experience
checks.text: Verify accessible labels/alt text, contrast, keyboard operation, and core assistive-technology journeys under 03.

checks.heading: Public experience
checks.text: For public searchable content check titles/descriptions, social preview image/cards, favicon, canonical URLs, sitemap, robots.txt, redirects, and intended indexing. Keep staging/private data protected.

checks.heading: Public experience
checks.text: Verify optimized image delivery, appropriate lazy loading, font behavior, and measured page/API performance under 06, including constrained mobile use.

checks.heading: Production configuration and money
checks.text: Confirm production domains, DNS, TLS, renewal notifications, HTTPS redirects, and appropriate security headers. For VPS hosting, attach verified 12 evidence.

checks.heading: Production configuration and money
checks.text: Confirm no privileged secret is exposed in source/history, frontend assets, logs, or images; required exposed credentials have been revoked/rotated.

checks.heading: Production configuration and money
checks.text: Disable unsafe debug behavior, test bypasses, placeholder secrets, and publicly reachable diagnostics. Identify the deployed version and active feature flags.

checks.heading: Production configuration and money
checks.text: Review dependency/runtime security for the actual deployed stack, not only a local package lockfile scan.

checks.heading: Production configuration and money
checks.text: Protect important vendor dashboards and accounts with available MFA and secure recovery methods, including payment, hosting, DNS/registrar, database, source control, and backups.

checks.heading: Production configuration and money
checks.text: If accepting payments, verify live keys, live products/prices, live endpoint signature secrets, receipt/invoice behavior, and the tested refund/cancel/failed-payment/expiry paths under 13.

checks.heading: Production configuration and money
checks.text: Confirm authentication/form spam limits, upload limits, AI/messaging budgets, plan quotas, and an operational way to suspend abuse. Verify spending alerts versus actual stop mechanisms under 08.

checks.heading: Operation and release decision
checks.text: Enable privacy-appropriate analytics for necessary success metrics; validate event delivery and consent gating where applicable. Analytics is optional when it does not support a defined product need.

checks.heading: Operation and release decision
checks.text: Verify external uptime and error monitoring, job-failure/freshness alerts, spend/capacity alerts, accountable recipients, and controlled alert receipt.

checks.heading: Operation and release decision
checks.text: Attach backup inventory and a recent representative restore, including files/volumes and required recovery keys. Backup frequency must meet the project's RPO; daily is a possible baseline, not proof of adequacy.

checks.heading: Operation and release decision
checks.text: Confirm release/deploy ownership, smoke checks, rollback limits, support route, incident contacts, and a runbook available during a VPS outage.

checks.heading: Operation and release decision
checks.text: For a migration attach data-authority, callback/job ownership, DNS/certificate, and rollback evidence from 17. Avoid launching while old and new systems both process the same non-idempotent work.

checks.heading: Operation and release decision
checks.text: Record open findings, unknown critical controls, accepted risks, owners, and dates. Obtain the project's release decision through its established process after evidence is complete.

checks.heading: Additional release boundaries
checks.text: Bind the decision to source, immutable artifact/build, configuration/flags, schema, audience and exposure stage. Refresh affected evidence when relevant inputs change.

checks.heading: Additional release boundaries
checks.text: Verify fresh users, denied roles/tenants, expired sessions, locale/device variations, old clients and cached assets according to supported scope. Include eventual persisted/provider effects in important failure checks.

checks.heading: Additional release boundaries
checks.text: For APIs/native apps/games, verify applicable client contracts, package/signing/version, store/release state, install/upgrade behavior and data/save compatibility.

checks.heading: Additional release boundaries
checks.text: Attach duplicate/retry/out-of-order/timeout evidence for callbacks, jobs, payments and credits. Confirm only intended environments own critical writers, schedules and irreversible effects.

checks.heading: Additional release boundaries
checks.text: Rehearse mixed-version schema deployment, resumable backfill and graceful drain where relevant. State irreversible changes and when fail-forward is safer than binary/DNS rollback.

checks.heading: Additional release boundaries
checks.text: Verify actual usable restore, measured RPO/RTO and data/provider reconciliation after recovery. Include files, keys and access dependencies outside the application's failure domain.

checks.heading: Additional release boundaries
checks.text: Set project-specific ramp/pause/abort conditions, representative observation windows and an available responder. Low traffic or a green health endpoint alone does not establish successful user outcomes.

checks.heading: Additional release boundaries
checks.text: Exercise scoped stop/reopen controls and support/alert receipt. Track delayed schedules, billing, propagation, renewal and other post-launch confirmations with owners/dates.

checks.heading: Additional release boundaries
checks.text: Record prerequisite conditions separately from post-launch follow-up; do not expose an affected cohort before a required condition is satisfied. Accepted risk retains its underlying check status.

checks.heading: Inventory and provenance
checks.text: SW-001 — Inventory direct/transitive dependencies, vendored files, copied snippets, generated scaffolding, plugins and submodules; reconcile manifests against build and shipped artifacts.

checks.heading: Inventory and provenance
checks.text: SW-002 — Inspect server, browser, mobile, desktop, extension, CLI, device and on-premises outputs separately; code served to a browser is part of the distribution analysis.

checks.heading: Inventory and provenance
checks.text: SW-003 — Include build tools and development dependencies when their code, runtime helpers, templates or bundled assets appear in outputs; a devDependency label is not decisive.

checks.heading: Inventory and provenance
checks.text: SW-004 — Record exact version/commit, origin, hash, copyright holder, license text and modifications; preserve evidence if an upstream repository disappears.

checks.heading: Inventory and provenance
checks.text: SW-005 — Treat missing, conflicting, placeholder or repository-only license metadata as unresolved; inspect file headers, package contents, exceptions and separate asset directories.

checks.heading: Inventory and provenance
checks.text: SW-006 — Distinguish public availability from a permission grant; code visible on a website or public repository is not automatically licensed for reuse.

checks.heading: Inventory and provenance
checks.text: SW-007 — Review pasted forum answers, tutorials, gists and AI-suggested snippets for source and applicable rights; attribution alone does not necessarily authorize reuse.

checks.heading: Inventory and provenance
