checks.text: SW-008 — Record forks, patches, generated code and downstream modifications; upstream scanning results do not automatically cover local changes.

checks.heading: License interpretation and compatibility
checks.text: SW-009 — Preserve precise SPDX expressions, including OR, AND, WITH, version-only/later distinctions and custom LicenseRef texts; document the actual selected option.

checks.heading: License interpretation and compatibility
checks.text: SW-010 — Assess compatibility for the actual combination, linking, modification and conveyance; do not infer a legal conclusion solely from “permissive” or “copyleft” labels.

checks.heading: License interpretation and compatibility
checks.text: SW-011 — Examine dual/commercial licensing choices, eligibility, covered entity, payment, version and deployment rights; buying one seat does not establish all organizational rights.

checks.heading: License interpretation and compatibility
checks.text: SW-012 — Review source-available and restricted licenses for hosting, competing-service, production, user, revenue or field-of-use limits; “source available” does not mean OSI open source.

checks.heading: License interpretation and compatibility
checks.text: SW-013 — Assess time-delayed license changes against the exact release/date and grant; do not apply a future open license to an earlier restricted period without a basis.

checks.heading: License interpretation and compatibility
checks.text: SW-014 — Check license exceptions, linking permissions and separate notices rather than applying the base license in isolation.

checks.heading: License interpretation and compatibility
checks.text: SW-015 — Record applicable patent grants, retaliation/termination provisions, excluded trademark rights and other permissions needing review; a copyright license is not every right clearance.

checks.heading: License interpretation and compatibility
checks.text: SW-016 — Route ambiguous aggregation/derivative-work, plugin, IPC and static/dynamic-linking questions to a documented qualified decision rather than relying on process boundaries alone.

checks.heading: Notices and release artifacts
checks.text: SW-017 — Retain required copyright, license and disclaimer text in the form required for the actual distribution; verify notices in archives/installers, not only the repository.

checks.heading: Notices and release artifacts
checks.text: SW-018 — Review Apache-licensed material for applicable license, modification and NOTICE handling; do not assume every project has identical NOTICE content.

checks.heading: Notices and release artifacts
checks.text: SW-019 — Include file-specific attribution, acknowledgments, advertising or documentation obligations where the actual license requires them; don't generalize modern BSD terms to every variant.

checks.heading: Notices and release artifacts
checks.text: SW-020 — Check minification, tree shaking, compression and packaging do not strip required notices without an adequate compliant delivery mechanism.

checks.heading: Notices and release artifacts
checks.text: SW-021 — Verify app-store packages, offline installations, container images, downloadable SDKs and generated exports carry their applicable notices after the final build.

checks.heading: Notices and release artifacts
checks.text: SW-022 — Distinguish necessary legal notices from unnecessary disclosure of internal inventories, secrets or confidential components; publish what is required and retain internal evidence separately.

checks.heading: Notices and release artifacts
checks.text: SW-023 — Confirm notice links work after domain changes, shutdown, offline use and long-lived device releases where the chosen compliance method requires them.

checks.heading: Notices and release artifacts
checks.text: SW-024 — Verify localization and white-label/reseller packaging preserve required text and identify the responsible distributor.

checks.heading: Copyleft and source obligations
checks.text: SW-025 — Identify each GPL/LGPL/AGPL/MPL or other reciprocal component and the exact obligations triggered by modifications, combination, distribution or network interaction.

checks.heading: Copyleft and source obligations
checks.text: SW-026 — For relevant GPL distributions, assess corresponding-source scope, build/install materials, delivery method and exact-version correspondence using the controlling license.

checks.heading: Copyleft and source obligations
checks.text: SW-027 — Test source download/offer fulfillment as the actual recipient; inaccessible links, wrong versions and missing local patches remain gaps.

checks.heading: Copyleft and source obligations
checks.text: SW-028 — If relying on a written offer, verify allowed use of that route, recipients, duration, fulfillment ownership and preservation of source for the required period; do not assume a generic offer fits all versions.

checks.heading: Copyleft and source obligations
checks.text: SW-029 — For LGPL cases assess the actual linking/relinking mechanism, modifications, notices and applicable recipient rights; static versus dynamic linking is a fact, not a complete conclusion.

checks.heading: Copyleft and source obligations
checks.text: SW-030 — For MPL cases identify covered files, modifications and relevant source availability without assuming the entire application has the same obligation.

checks.heading: Copyleft and source obligations
checks.text: SW-031 — For modified AGPL-covered network software assess the exact remote-interaction source requirement; “we only run SaaS” is not a sufficient exclusion rationale.

checks.heading: Copyleft and source obligations
checks.text: SW-032 — Where applicable examine installation information and anti-circumvention/recipient-rights provisions; contracts or DRM must not negate rights granted by the relevant license.

checks.heading: Commercial software, platforms, and infrastructure
checks.text: SW-033 — Verify commercial SDK, engine, library and plugin rights for developer seats, build servers, contractors, revenue tiers, territories and redistribution.

checks.heading: Commercial software, platforms, and infrastructure
checks.text: SW-034 — Check evaluation, educational, personal-use, startup, nonprofit and free-tier restrictions against actual production/commercial use and current eligibility.

checks.heading: Commercial software, platforms, and infrastructure
checks.text: SW-035 — Inventory base images, operating-system packages, drivers, codecs, firmware, fonts and models shipped in containers/devices; an application SBOM alone may omit them.

checks.heading: Commercial software, platforms, and infrastructure
checks.text: SW-036 — Review codec, cryptography, patent-pool and media-format issues where relevant; an open-source implementation alone does not settle every patent or territory question.

checks.heading: Commercial software, platforms, and infrastructure
checks.text: SW-037 — Check hosted services, APIs and managed databases for customer access, embedding, white-label, resale, benchmarking and competing-product restrictions in applicable terms.

checks.heading: Commercial software, platforms, and infrastructure
checks.text: SW-038 — Review marketplace/app-store agreements, signing accounts and distribution rules alongside software licenses; resolve conflicting recipient restrictions before release.

checks.heading: Commercial software, platforms, and infrastructure
checks.text: SW-039 — Verify license keys, activation and offline rights are assigned to the right entity/environment and survive permitted disaster recovery or migration.

checks.heading: Commercial software, platforms, and infrastructure
checks.text: SW-040 — Check vendor end-of-term obligations: uninstall, cease use, remove redistributables, preserve permitted customer access and fulfill surviving obligations.

checks.heading: Change, supply chain, and exceptional cases
checks.text: SW-041 — Detect license changes on dependency upgrades, forks, acquisitions and package-name substitutions; prior approval does not cover every future version.

checks.heading: Change, supply chain, and exceptional cases
checks.text: SW-042 — Reconcile SBOM/scanner results with original texts and manual review; false matches, unknown binaries and custom licenses remain tracked.

checks.heading: Change, supply chain, and exceptional cases
checks.text: SW-043 — Inspect examples, test fixtures, sample media, documentation and demonstration datasets included in a public repo or package for separate rights.

checks.heading: Change, supply chain, and exceptional cases
checks.text: SW-044 — Review contributions, CLAs, DCO/sign-off practices and inbound/outbound rights; a sign-off or platform account is not automatically a complete IP assignment.

checks.heading: Change, supply chain, and exceptional cases
checks.text: SW-045 — Confirm the organization has authority to publish its chosen outbound license, including employee, contractor and pre-existing third-party code.

checks.heading: Change, supply chain, and exceptional cases
checks.text: SW-046 — For customer-specific builds, air-gapped deliveries and resellers verify artifact-specific notices/source access and identify who fulfills recipient requests.

checks.heading: Change, supply chain, and exceptional cases
checks.text: SW-047 — If a rights defect is found, assess affected releases, recipients, potential cure/termination issues and replacement/source-delivery options with the accountable reviewer; do not assume deleting code cures historical distribution.

checks.heading: Change, supply chain, and exceptional cases
checks.text: SW-048 — Rebuild the final artifact after remediation and verify notices, source correspondence and selected license route; a manifest edit alone does not prove release compliance.

checks.heading: Ownership and chain of title
checks.text: IP-001 — Inventory copy, code, design, photos, illustrations, icons, video, music, voices, fonts, templates, documents, datasets and models, including hidden/demo/exported material.

checks.heading: Ownership and chain of title
checks.text: IP-002 — Identify actual owners and each transfer/license in the chain; a seller, agency or uploader may not own every underlying right.

checks.heading: Ownership and chain of title
checks.text: IP-003 — Review employee-created work against applicable law, employment terms, scope and pre-existing material; do not assume employment transfers all rights everywhere.

checks.heading: Ownership and chain of title
checks.text: IP-004 — Verify freelancer, contractor, agency and subcontractor grants cover deliverables, source files, modification, territories, duration, media and intended redistribution.

checks.heading: Ownership and chain of title
checks.text: IP-005 — Distinguish assignment from an exclusive/non-exclusive license and record retained rights, moral-rights treatment and execution requirements where relevant.

checks.heading: Ownership and chain of title
checks.text: IP-006 — Review founder contributions, prior employers, acquisitions, joint development, grants and university/research obligations for gaps or conflicting rights.

checks.heading: Ownership and chain of title
checks.text: IP-007 — Check commissioned work that contains stock assets, templates, licensed fonts or subcontracted material; the commissioned-work agreement may not convey those underlying rights.

checks.heading: Ownership and chain of title
checks.text: IP-008 — Preserve invoices, permissions, releases, accepted terms, source versions and usage history; a receipt without the applicable grant is incomplete evidence.

checks.heading: Images, design, fonts, and templates
checks.text: IP-009 — Verify stock-photo/illustration licenses for commercial/editorial use, advertising, products for resale, audience/impression limits and sensitive contexts.

checks.heading: Images, design, fonts, and templates
checks.text: IP-010 — Check model/property releases where relevant; copyright permission and recognizable-person, trademark or location rights are distinct questions.

checks.heading: Images, design, fonts, and templates
checks.text: IP-011 — Review screenshots, product interfaces, maps, third-party logos and brand guidelines for the specific context; a press kit is not unrestricted permission.

checks.heading: Images, design, fonts, and templates
checks.text: IP-012 — Check icon packs, design-system assets, themes, templates and marketplace purchases for redistribution, extraction, client transfer and white-label restrictions.

checks.heading: Images, design, fonts, and templates
checks.text: IP-013 — Identify font rights separately for desktop use, web serving, mobile/app embedding, server rendering, PDF/e-book exports and redistribution.

checks.heading: Images, design, fonts, and templates
checks.text: IP-014 — Verify font licenses cover actual domains, traffic/seat limits, contractors, customer-generated documents and editable output where relevant.

checks.heading: Images, design, fonts, and templates
checks.text: IP-015 — Assess self-hosting, CDN delivery, subsetting, format conversion and embedding permissions; self-hosting can reduce a data flow but does not create font rights.

checks.heading: Images, design, fonts, and templates
checks.text: IP-016 — Inspect exported slides, PDFs, social cards, videos and printable merchandise for assets that were licensed only for display within the original app.

checks.heading: Audio, video, performance, and personality
checks.text: IP-017 — Separate music composition, recording, performance, synchronization and other relevant rights; permission for one layer may not cover the final video, stream or event.

checks.heading: Audio, video, performance, and personality
checks.text: IP-018 — Check music/sound libraries for platforms, advertising, client work, games, distribution, monetization and automated claim/Content ID restrictions.

checks.heading: Audio, video, performance, and personality
checks.text: IP-019 — Review voiceover, actor, presenter and performer agreements for territories, term, edits, paid advertising and synthetic reuse/voice cloning.

checks.heading: Audio, video, performance, and personality
checks.text: IP-020 — Distinguish an authorized scripted presenter from a claimed real customer; reviews and testimonials require separate substantiation and disclosure review.

checks.heading: Audio, video, performance, and personality
checks.text: IP-021 — Verify live-event/webinar recording, audience participation, transcripts, clips and later replay have the applicable permissions and notices.

checks.heading: Audio, video, performance, and personality
checks.text: IP-022 — Check recognizable people, names, likeness, voice, private information and impersonation for applicable publicity/personality, privacy and deceptive-use concerns.

checks.heading: Audio, video, performance, and personality
checks.text: IP-023 — Review translations, adaptations, dubbing, captioning and accessibility conversions for the relevant permission or applicable exception; do not assume every adaptation is unrestricted.

checks.heading: Audio, video, performance, and personality
checks.text: IP-024 — Ensure accessibility alternatives and asset replacements meet their own rights requirements while preserving equivalent content for users.

checks.heading: Open content, quotations, brands, and databases
checks.text: IP-025 — Record the precise Creative Commons license/version/jurisdiction and source; apply attribution, adaptation, share-alike, noncommercial and no-derivatives terms to the actual use.

checks.heading: Open content, quotations, brands, and databases
checks.text: IP-026 — Assess whether proposed edits/translations constitute restricted adaptations and whether planned commercial contexts fit the actual grant; escalate uncertainty rather than treating NC/ND as decorative labels.

checks.heading: Open content, quotations, brands, and databases
checks.text: IP-027 — Verify attribution includes required information and modification indication in a suitable location; preserve links and notices in copies/exports when required.

checks.heading: Open content, quotations, brands, and databases
checks.text: IP-028 — Check public-domain/CC0 assertions by work, territory, term and rights type; public-domain copyright status does not automatically settle privacy, trademark or contractual restrictions.

checks.heading: Open content, quotations, brands, and databases
checks.text: IP-029 — Assess quotations, excerpts, thumbnails, parody, fair use/fair dealing and other exceptions against the actual jurisdiction, purpose and amount; no universal word count or attribution rule guarantees permission.

checks.heading: Open content, quotations, brands, and databases
checks.text: IP-030 — Review product names, domains, logos, app names and trade dress for clearance, territory/class conflicts and misleading affiliation; domain registration is not trademark clearance.

checks.heading: Open content, quotations, brands, and databases
checks.text: IP-031 — Check comparative claims, competitor marks, badges and compatibility statements for substantiation and appropriate presentation; avoid implying sponsorship or certification without evidence.

checks.heading: Open content, quotations, brands, and databases
checks.text: IP-032 — Identify database, dataset, map and compilation rights separately from individual facts; inspect extraction/reuse terms, territorial rights and update obligations.

checks.heading: User uploads, community, and moderation
checks.text: IP-033 — Terms request only the upload/content rights needed for the service and separately address publication, promotion, sublicensing, training and post-deletion survival where relevant.

checks.heading: User uploads, community, and moderation
checks.text: IP-034 — Verify the user granting rights has capacity/authority and that shared workspace, employer and co-author scenarios are covered; a checkbox is not proof of ownership.

checks.heading: User uploads, community, and moderation
checks.text: IP-035 — Review public/private defaults, embeds, sharing links, remixing, exports and cross-tenant reuse against actual user permissions and expectations.

checks.heading: User uploads, community, and moderation
checks.text: IP-036 — Check removal/deletion implications for caches, public embeds, licensed derivatives and prior exports; explain operational limits without promising impossible recall.

checks.heading: User uploads, community, and moderation
checks.text: IP-037 — Offer usable channels for copyright, trademark, privacy, impersonation and other complaints; route them correctly rather than treating every complaint as copyright.

checks.heading: User uploads, community, and moderation
checks.text: IP-038 — If relying on US section 512 protection, review eligibility and conditions for the service activity, designated agent requirements, public contacts and renewal ownership where applicable.

checks.heading: User uploads, community, and moderation
checks.text: IP-039 — Test notice intake, required information, validation, prompt handling, user notification and evidence retention using synthetic internal cases; registration alone does not establish safe harbor.

checks.heading: User uploads, community, and moderation
checks.text: IP-040 — Review counter-notice, restoration, repeat-infringer and disputed-ownership handling against the applicable procedure; record legally confirmed response windows rather than inventing one global deadline.

checks.heading: User uploads, community, and moderation
checks.text: IP-041 — For EU intermediary/platform activity, classify the service and applicable DSA duties, exemptions, notice/action, reasons and redress; do not copy DMCA procedure as a universal substitute.

checks.heading: User uploads, community, and moderation
checks.text: IP-042 — Distinguish illegal-content handling from platform-policy enforcement; moderation and appeal notices explain the actual basis and applicable route.

checks.heading: User uploads, community, and moderation
checks.text: IP-043 — Prevent complaint abuse, doxxing and unnecessary exposure of claimant/user information; verify authorized case access and evidence preservation.

checks.heading: User uploads, community, and moderation
checks.text: IP-044 — Address reuploads, mirrors, thumbnails, search indexes and syndicated copies consistently after a confirmed action, while respecting scope and valid appeals.

checks.heading: Publication and lifecycle verification
checks.text: IP-045 — Before publication, reconcile the final asset/version/crop/translation with its permission and attribution; approval of a draft does not cover substituted assets.

checks.heading: Publication and lifecycle verification
checks.text: IP-046 — Track expiring, territory-limited, campaign-only and revocable grants; identify affected URLs, ads, binaries and exports when use must stop or change.

checks.heading: Publication and lifecycle verification
checks.text: IP-047 — Check migration, acquisition, entity changes and client handover for transfer/sublicensing restrictions and the ability to deliver provenance records.

checks.heading: Publication and lifecycle verification
checks.text: IP-048 — When a disputed asset is replaced, assess historical copies, complaints, contractual commitments and preservation duties; removal does not by itself resolve past use.

checks.heading: Data map and accountable processing
checks.text: PRIV-001 — Inventory data collection through UI, APIs, devices, uploads, integrations, support, recruitment, billing, logs and inferred/derived information; inspect deployed traffic and settings.

checks.heading: Data map and accountable processing
checks.text: PRIV-002 — Identify controller, joint-controller, processor, service-provider or other applicable roles by activity; a vendor's label does not alone settle the relationship.

checks.heading: Data map and accountable processing
checks.text: PRIV-003 — Map each purpose to relevant categories, people, source, legal basis/permission, recipients, locations, retention and required transparency.

checks.heading: Data map and accountable processing
checks.text: PRIV-004 — Separate account/service delivery, fraud prevention, analytics, personalization, marketing, advertising, research and AI training purposes; do not silently reuse one purpose's authorization.

checks.heading: Data map and accountable processing
checks.text: PRIV-005 — Assess necessity and minimization field by field; remove unjustified required data and avoid collecting identity documents or birth dates by default.

checks.heading: Data map and accountable processing
checks.text: PRIV-006 — Review sensitive/special-category, biometric, precise-location, financial, communications and inferred data under the applicable definitions and conditions.

checks.heading: Data map and accountable processing
checks.text: PRIV-007 — Where consent is relied upon, verify freely given, informed, specific and demonstrable choice plus withdrawal under applicable rules; an audit log alone cannot cure an invalid choice.

checks.heading: Data map and accountable processing
checks.text: PRIV-008 — Where another basis is relied upon, document its actual conditions and any required assessment; do not use “legitimate interest” or “contract” as an unexplained blanket label.

checks.heading: Notices and policy-to-product consistency
checks.text: PRIV-009 — Privacy notices identify the responsible entity, purposes, recipients, retention information and rights/contact routes required for the actual context.

checks.heading: Notices and policy-to-product consistency
checks.text: PRIV-010 — Collection-time notices appear before or when required, including indirect collection and unexpected sensitive uses; a buried general policy may be insufficient.

checks.heading: Notices and policy-to-product consistency
checks.text: PRIV-011 — Compare “we do not sell/share/train,” retention, residency and encryption claims with vendors, toggles, logs, advertising and actual processing.

checks.heading: Notices and policy-to-product consistency
checks.text: PRIV-012 — Cover employee/applicant, customer/end-user, visitor and uploaded-third-party information separately where processing differs.

checks.heading: Notices and policy-to-product consistency
checks.text: PRIV-013 — Check translations, mobile/webview versions and authenticated routes for current consistent notices and usable access.

checks.heading: Notices and policy-to-product consistency
checks.text: PRIV-014 — Version policy and permission changes, assess whether renewed notice/choice is required, and preserve applicable acceptance evidence without claiming every edit needs fresh consent.

checks.heading: Cookies and similar tracking
checks.text: PRIV-015 — Inventory cookies, pixels, local/session storage, device identifiers, fingerprinting, SDKs and server-side tracking; absence of cookies does not prove absence of tracking.

checks.heading: Cookies and similar tracking
checks.text: PRIV-016 — Classify each purpose and provider against the relevant exemption/permission rules; a vendor or CMP “essential” label is not sufficient evidence.

checks.heading: Cookies and similar tracking
checks.text: PRIV-017 — On a clean browser profile, inspect network/storage before any choice, after reject, after category selection and after accept; verify actual behavior, not banner configuration alone.

checks.heading: Cookies and similar tracking
checks.text: PRIV-018 — Test direct deep links, login, embedded media, payment pages, SPA transitions, delayed tags and third-party widgets for bypasses of the intended tracking controls.

checks.heading: Cookies and similar tracking
checks.text: PRIV-019 — Check acceptance/rejection presentation against applicable guidance; for Spain examine AEPD's same-time, same-level and same-visibility expectations in context.

checks.heading: Cookies and similar tracking
checks.text: PRIV-020 — Confirm granular choices, clear purposes, no unauthorized preselection and usable access to settings; assess coercive/cookie-wall designs against current applicable rules.

checks.heading: Cookies and similar tracking
checks.text: PRIV-021 — Withdraw or change choices and verify propagation to tags, vendors, server events and stored identifiers where required; refreshing only the banner state is insufficient.

checks.heading: Cookies and similar tracking
checks.text: PRIV-022 — Record consent evidence with scope/version/time and necessary identifiers, plus expiry/re-prompt rules justified by applicable authority and changed purposes.

checks.heading: Cookies and similar tracking
checks.text: PRIV-023 — Test browser privacy signals, global opt-out controls and sale/share/targeted-advertising opt-outs where applicable; verify backend action rather than a UI-only toggle.

checks.heading: Cookies and similar tracking
checks.text: PRIV-024 — Examine external fonts, assets, chat, maps, analytics and replay requests for data disclosures/transfers even without cookies; a single court award is not a universal tariff.

checks.heading: Cookies and similar tracking
checks.text: PRIV-025 — Assess session replay, heatmaps, keystrokes, call/chat recording and communications interception, including CIPA where relevant; field masking or a banner alone is not a legal conclusion.

checks.heading: Cookies and similar tracking
checks.text: PRIV-026 — Test sensitive routes, query strings, DOM content, shadow roots, attachments and pasted fields for recording leakage; coordinate security verification without collecting real sensitive content.

checks.heading: Vendors, transfers, and residency
checks.text: PRIV-027 — Match each processor/service provider and subprocessor to the actual service, entity, signed terms, purpose and permitted data categories.

checks.heading: Vendors, transfers, and residency
checks.text: PRIV-028 — Verify required DPA, BAA, joint-controller or other arrangements and instructions are executed and cover the service/features in use; a sales claim does not replace terms.

checks.heading: Vendors, transfers, and residency
checks.text: PRIV-029 — Trace international storage, access, support, backups, logs, telemetry, model routing and subprocessors; primary database region alone does not establish residency or transfer compliance.

checks.heading: Vendors, transfers, and residency
checks.text: PRIV-030 — Determine applicable transfer mechanism and supporting assessments/safeguards where required; distinguish legal entity, destination and data-access facts.

checks.heading: Vendors, transfers, and residency
checks.text: PRIV-031 — Review vendor training, product improvement, human review, retention, abuse monitoring and fallback use against customer promises and actual service settings.

checks.heading: Vendors, transfers, and residency
checks.text: PRIV-032 — Check new subprocessors, vendor acquisitions, region changes and plan changes for notice, objection, assessment or contractual action triggers.

checks.heading: Vendors, transfers, and residency
checks.text: PRIV-033 — Assess data-import providers, enrichment services and purchased audiences for source legitimacy, permitted uses and required indirect-collection notices.

checks.heading: Vendors, transfers, and residency
checks.text: PRIV-034 — Verify customer offboarding, provider termination and migration include export, deletion/return, evidence and justified surviving retention.

checks.heading: Rights requests and retention
checks.text: PRIV-035 — Provide usable intake for applicable access, correction, deletion, portability, objection, restriction and opt-out rights; don't assume every right applies identically everywhere.

checks.heading: Rights requests and retention
checks.text: PRIV-036 — Verify identity/authority proportionately, including authorized agents, parents and deceased/incapacitated-user cases as relevant; avoid unnecessary document collection.

checks.heading: Rights requests and retention
checks.text: PRIV-037 — Assign jurisdiction-specific response/extension periods and ownership; rehearse discovery, escalation and communication before any real request is due.

checks.heading: Rights requests and retention
checks.text: PRIV-038 — Trace access/export requests through tables, files, vendors, logs and derived profiles; protect other people's data and relevant confidential information.

checks.heading: Rights requests and retention
checks.text: PRIV-039 — Trace correction/deletion through active stores, search indexes, caches, attachments, analytics, vendors and derived artifacts where applicable.

checks.heading: Rights requests and retention
checks.text: PRIV-040 — Document lawful exceptions, dispute/litigation holds, financial records and necessary suppression evidence; deletion is neither “keep everything” nor “erase all records regardless of obligation.”

checks.heading: Rights requests and retention
checks.text: PRIV-041 — Inspect backup expiry and restores so deleted data is not silently reactivated; document restrictions and deletion replay where appropriate.

checks.heading: Rights requests and retention
checks.text: PRIV-042 — Assign retention by purpose/category and test actual expiry jobs, exports, failed jobs and orphaned data; a written schedule does not prove implementation.

checks.heading: Rights requests and retention
checks.text: PRIV-043 — Assess anonymization/pseudonymization claims against realistic reidentification and retained linkage; pseudonymized data is not automatically outside privacy scope.

checks.heading: Rights requests and retention
checks.text: PRIV-044 — Preserve sufficient request audit evidence while limiting sensitive content and access; test duplicate, disputed, failed and partially fulfilled requests.

checks.heading: Children, profiling, and high-risk processing
checks.text: PRIV-045 — Determine child-directed/mixed/general audience and actual knowledge using applicable rules and evidence; do not add intrusive age collection indiscriminately.

checks.heading: Children, profiling, and high-risk processing
checks.text: PRIV-046 — Where COPPA or local child-data rules apply, review required notices, verified parental consent, parental rights, minimization, sharing and retention for current requirements.

checks.heading: Children, profiling, and high-risk processing
checks.text: PRIV-047 — Test age/parental flows before relevant collection, including social login, SDK initialization, guest use and attempts to bypass the intended controls.

checks.heading: Children, profiling, and high-risk processing
checks.text: PRIV-048 — Evaluate child-oriented design, profiling/advertising restrictions and age-assurance proportionality by jurisdiction; an age checkbox alone does not establish compliance.

checks.heading: Children, profiling, and high-risk processing
checks.text: PRIV-049 — Identify profiling, automated eligibility/ranking/decisions and human-review claims; determine applicable information, contest, intervention or impact-assessment obligations.

checks.heading: Children, profiling, and high-risk processing
checks.text: PRIV-050 — Assess whether DPIA, risk assessment, DPO/representative or records-of-processing duties apply; record scope, decision and review triggers rather than requiring them universally.

checks.heading: Children, profiling, and high-risk processing
checks.text: PRIV-051 — Review employee monitoring, recordings, location and workplace AI for applicable privacy, labor and consultation obligations, including vendor secondary use.

checks.heading: Children, profiling, and high-risk processing
checks.text: PRIV-052 — Review health/wellness, biometrics and location use even when a named sector law does not apply; other privacy or consumer rules may remain relevant.

checks.heading: Incidents and operational evidence
checks.text: PRIV-053 — Define incident assessment ownership, relevant clocks, notification thresholds, recipients and evidence preservation according to applicable laws/contracts.

checks.heading: Incidents and operational evidence
checks.text: PRIV-054 — Rehearse a privacy incident with synthetic facts, including vendor notice, wrong-recipient exports and accidental public files; don't assume every event has the same notification rule.

checks.heading: Incidents and operational evidence
checks.text: PRIV-055 — Verify support, analytics, ticket attachments and debug logs do not introduce undeclared processing or defeat retention/deletion commitments.

checks.heading: Incidents and operational evidence
checks.text: PRIV-056 — Recheck legal/data-flow decisions after new features, purposes, vendors, countries, acquisitions and retention changes; update notices and operational controls together.

checks.heading: Identity, contracting, and public policies
checks.text: COM-001 — Verify legal operator, seller, contact and required registration/tax/business disclosures for the markets and channels actually used.

checks.heading: Identity, contracting, and public policies
checks.text: COM-002 — Distinguish terms of service, purchase terms, privacy notices, AUP and service-specific policies; ensure the correct entity and product appear in each.

checks.heading: Identity, contracting, and public policies
checks.text: COM-003 — Inspect acceptance placement, linked terms, timing and evidence by registration/checkout/upgrade flow; don't assume a footer link proves agreement.

checks.heading: Identity, contracting, and public policies
checks.text: COM-004 — Preserve the version accepted, user/organization authority, timestamp and relevant order details; test retrieval when a dispute concerns an older version.

checks.heading: Identity, contracting, and public policies
checks.text: COM-005 — Check order forms, negotiated amendments, DPAs, SLAs, marketplace terms and online terms for incorporation and precedence; don't assume the latest web page overrides signed terms.

checks.heading: Identity, contracting, and public policies
checks.text: COM-006 — Compare liability, warranty, indemnity, dispute, governing-law and unilateral-change provisions with actual obligations and enforceability review; template clauses are not universally valid.

checks.heading: Identity, contracting, and public policies
checks.text: COM-007 — Review minors' contracting capacity, parent/guardian authority and enterprise-admin authority where relevant, separately from privacy permission.

checks.heading: Identity, contracting, and public policies
checks.text: COM-008 — Check policy changes, notice, objection, termination and reacceptance where applicable; preserve historical versions without claiming every edit requires the same process.

checks.heading: Pricing, subscriptions, and refunds
checks.text: COM-009 — Display applicable total-price, currency, tax, mandatory-fee and payment information at the required point; compare ads, plans, cart, confirmation and invoice.

checks.heading: Pricing, subscriptions, and refunds
checks.text: COM-010 — State recurring price, billing interval, minimum term, commitment, trial length and conversion conditions clearly before the relevant consent or commitment.

checks.heading: Pricing, subscriptions, and refunds
checks.text: COM-011 — Test free trials, introductory discounts, credits and usage-based charges for actual conversion/billing behavior matching the disclosed offer.

checks.heading: Pricing, subscriptions, and refunds
checks.text: COM-012 — Determine applicable renewal laws and obtain required affirmative-consent evidence and acknowledgment; distinguish federal, state and local rules and current legal status.

checks.heading: Pricing, subscriptions, and refunds
checks.text: COM-013 — Verify required renewal, trial-end and material-change notices have correct timing/content/channel for the applicable contract and market.

checks.heading: Pricing, subscriptions, and refunds
checks.text: COM-014 — Complete cancellation through each signup channel and plan, including mobile stores and resellers; check barriers, retention offers, login loss and support failures.

checks.heading: Pricing, subscriptions, and refunds
checks.text: COM-015 — Confirm cancellation stops or schedules billing/access as disclosed, communicates effective date and preserves proof; cancellation and refund are separate questions.

checks.heading: Pricing, subscriptions, and refunds
checks.text: COM-016 — Test pause/reactivate, downgrade, annual/monthly change, proration, failed payment and reactivation against applicable terms and disclosure duties.

checks.heading: Pricing, subscriptions, and refunds
checks.text: COM-017 — Review withdrawal/cooling-off rights, exceptions, digital-content/service consents and acknowledgment where relevant; do not apply one global “no refunds” rule.

checks.heading: Pricing, subscriptions, and refunds
checks.text: COM-018 — Match refund, return, guarantee and chargeback handling to applicable rights and contractual promises; do not assume a disclaimer removes statutory remedies.

checks.heading: Pricing, subscriptions, and refunds
checks.text: COM-019 — Reconcile seller/merchant-of-record, tax/invoice and refund responsibilities across payment providers, app stores and marketplaces; vendor handling does not eliminate all operator duties.

checks.heading: Pricing, subscriptions, and refunds
checks.text: COM-020 — Check gift purchases, vouchers, credits, expiry, unclaimed balances and transferred subscriptions for applicable restrictions and clear user information.

checks.heading: Claims, endorsements, and promotion
checks.text: COM-021 — Substantiate objective product, performance, savings, security, environmental and comparative claims before publication; preserve methodology, scope and expiry.

checks.heading: Claims, endorsements, and promotion
checks.text: COM-022 — Check “free,” “unlimited,” “lifetime,” “anonymous,” “zero retention,” “certified,” “compliant” and “guaranteed” claims against actual limits and evidence.

checks.heading: Claims, endorsements, and promotion
checks.text: COM-023 — Review testimonials, reviews and case studies for genuine experience, permission, accuracy, material connections and claims the advertiser can support.

checks.heading: Claims, endorsements, and promotion
checks.text: COM-024 — Label affiliates, sponsorships, paid placements, employee reviews and gifted endorsements as required in each medium; placement and clarity matter as well as existence.

checks.heading: Claims, endorsements, and promotion
checks.text: COM-025 — Test review collection/moderation for fake reviews, undisclosed incentives, misleading suppression and fabricated social proof; distinguish verified purchase from broader authenticity claims.

checks.heading: Claims, endorsements, and promotion
checks.text: COM-026 — Inspect countdowns, scarcity, stock, discounts and reference prices for factual accuracy across refresh, locale and user variants.

checks.heading: Claims, endorsements, and promotion
checks.text: COM-027 — Review AI avatars, synthetic voices and composite customers for required disclosure and deceptive-endorsement risks; a presenter is not necessarily a real user.

checks.heading: Claims, endorsements, and promotion
checks.text: COM-028 — Check competitions, giveaways, referrals, loyalty schemes and influencer campaigns for local eligibility, terms, prize, tax and platform conditions before launch.

checks.heading: Email, SMS, calls, and audience acquisition
checks.text: COM-029 — Classify transactional, marketing and mixed messages by actual content/purpose and applicable rules; an existing account does not make every announcement transactional.

checks.heading: Email, SMS, calls, and audience acquisition
checks.text: COM-030 — Record lawful permission/consent or other valid route for each channel, audience, sender and territory; email and SMS permissions are not automatically interchangeable.

checks.heading: Email, SMS, calls, and audience acquisition
checks.text: COM-031 — Where CAN-SPAM applies, verify sender/subject truthfulness, required advertising identification, valid postal address, usable opt-out and timely honoring under the current rule.

checks.heading: Email, SMS, calls, and audience acquisition
checks.text: COM-032 — Where EU/UK or other local electronic-marketing rules apply, assess opt-in/soft-opt-in conditions, business-recipient distinctions and opt-out rather than importing US email assumptions.

checks.heading: Email, SMS, calls, and audience acquisition
checks.text: COM-033 — For SMS, messaging apps, automated calls and prerecorded/synthetic voices assess applicable consent, identification, time-of-day, do-not-contact and revocation requirements.

checks.heading: Email, SMS, calls, and audience acquisition
checks.text: COM-034 — Test unsubscribe/suppression through CRM, ESP, SMS provider, ad audiences, imported lists and agencies; reimports must not silently resubscribe excluded people.

checks.heading: Email, SMS, calls, and audience acquisition
checks.text: COM-035 — Review purchased/enriched lists, scraped addresses, partner sharing and lead forms for provenance, notice, permission and vendor claims.

checks.heading: Email, SMS, calls, and audience acquisition
checks.text: COM-036 — Preserve permission scope, wording, version, source, time and withdrawal evidence as needed, while limiting unnecessary personal data retention.

checks.heading: APIs, marketplaces, and providers
checks.text: COM-037 — Review accepted API/platform terms for storage, caching, redistribution, derived products, training, scraping, branding, rate limits and prohibited uses; record service-specific variations.

checks.heading: APIs, marketplaces, and providers
checks.text: COM-038 — Check API fallback, proxy, aggregator and reseller chains; permission from one intermediary does not automatically cover the underlying provider's conditions.

checks.heading: APIs, marketplaces, and providers
checks.text: COM-039 — Compare app-store listing, in-app purchasing, external-payment links, subscription management and required policy/contact pages with current applicable platform rules.

checks.heading: APIs, marketplaces, and providers
checks.text: COM-040 — Review marketplace seller/trader verification, listing information, unsafe/illegal goods handling and allocation of buyer remedies for the actual operator role.

checks.heading: APIs, marketplaces, and providers
checks.text: COM-041 — Inspect data portability, account suspension, termination, migration and export restrictions before depending on provider continuity or promising customer exit rights.

checks.heading: APIs, marketplaces, and providers
checks.text: COM-042 — Check account sharing, seat reassignment, subcontracting, white-label, client deliverables and agency/reseller rights against actual usage.

checks.heading: Enterprise contracts and operational promises
checks.text: COM-043 — Map SLA, support hours, response/remedy, uptime, backup, recovery and deletion commitments to implemented operations and evidence.

checks.heading: Enterprise contracts and operational promises
checks.text: COM-044 — Verify security questionnaires, badges and assurance claims match the audited entity, system, period and exceptions; SOC 2 is an attestation report, not a universal product certification.

checks.heading: Enterprise contracts and operational promises
checks.text: COM-045 — Review indemnities, insurance, audit rights, breach-notification, data-residency and subcontractor commitments for conflicting duties or missing operational ownership.

checks.heading: Enterprise contracts and operational promises
checks.text: COM-046 — Test contract renewal, price changes, service deprecation, customer notice and termination workflows using synthetic timelines; don't rely on a spreadsheet without an accountable action process.

checks.heading: Enterprise contracts and operational promises
checks.text: COM-047 — Identify public-sector, procurement, accessibility, localization and recordkeeping requirements that arise from actual customers/contracts; cross-link the responsible specialist audit.

checks.heading: Enterprise contracts and operational promises
checks.text: COM-048 — Review product shutdown, acquisition and migration for surviving customer rights, prepaid balances, data return, license/source commitments and notice obligations.

checks.heading: Models, data, and generated output
checks.text: AI-001 — Inventory model weights, tokenizers, adapters, embeddings, training/fine-tuning/evaluation data and retrieval corpora separately; each can have different rights and restrictions.

checks.heading: Models, data, and generated output
checks.text: AI-002 — Check the exact model/version/hosting route for commercial use, deployment, redistribution, use restrictions, attribution and downstream pass-through terms.

checks.heading: Models, data, and generated output
checks.text: AI-003 — Verify rights for collection, copying, retrieval, training, fine-tuning and output reuse separately; lawful access or a display license does not automatically authorize every operation.

checks.heading: Models, data, and generated output
checks.text: AI-004 — Review scraping, website/database terms, machine-readable reservations and applicable text/data-mining exceptions in context; robots.txt alone does not resolve copyright or contract questions.

checks.heading: Models, data, and generated output
checks.text: AI-005 — Check employee/customer/user uploads for authority, confidentiality and personal data before provider submission, logging, evaluation or training.

checks.heading: Models, data, and generated output
checks.text: AI-006 — Match vendor promises on ownership, training, retention, human review, indemnities and geography to the actual plan, endpoint, fallback model and settings.

checks.heading: Models, data, and generated output
checks.text: AI-007 — Distinguish contractual output-use permission from statutory copyrightability, exclusivity, non-infringement and third-party rights; do not promise rights that cannot be established.

checks.heading: Models, data, and generated output
checks.text: AI-008 — Review generated text/code/images/audio for source reproduction, recognizable characters, brands, personal likeness and sensitive content before publication; automated similarity checks are evidence aids, not clearance decisions.

checks.heading: Models, data, and generated output
checks.text: AI-009 — Preserve relevant human authorship, selection/editing and provenance evidence for rights claims or registration where needed without assuming prompts alone establish authorship.

checks.heading: Models, data, and generated output
checks.text: AI-010 — Inspect retrieval citations, snippets, cached copies and exports for license/attribution, update and removal constraints; citation does not itself authorize the reproduced content.

checks.heading: Models, data, and generated output
checks.text: AI-011 — Check synthetic presenters, voice clones, deepfakes and impersonation for actual permissions, context, disclosure and misleading-use concerns.

checks.heading: Models, data, and generated output
checks.text: AI-012 — Determine applicable AI-system role and risk/transparency duties by activity; verify current official text, amendments, transition provisions and dates instead of one generic “AI Act compliant” label.

checks.heading: Models, data, and generated output
checks.text: AI-013 — Where required, test AI interaction notices, synthetic-content markings and disclosures in the actual displayed/downloaded format, including API and white-label outputs.

checks.heading: Models, data, and generated output
checks.text: AI-014 — Check model changes, distillation, merges, quantization and fine-tuning for continuing license and data restrictions; a technical transformation does not automatically remove obligations.

checks.heading: Models, data, and generated output
checks.text: AI-015 — Review provider termination, model withdrawal and deletion requests for retained prompts, datasets, embeddings, fine-tunes and artifacts; record technical limits and applicable duties honestly.

checks.heading: Models, data, and generated output
checks.text: AI-016 — Keep documented human review/escalation for legal, medical, employment, credit or other consequential AI uses; a disclaimer alone does not settle sector or decision-making obligations.

checks.heading: Regulated services and assurance
checks.text: SPEC-001 — For health services classify parties/data/activities under applicable health rules, including HIPAA where relevant; health-related content alone does not prove covered-entity status.

checks.heading: Regulated services and assurance
checks.text: SPEC-002 — Where a BAA or other regulated-data agreement is needed, verify each actual service/feature/provider is covered before data submission, including AI, logs and support.

checks.heading: Regulated services and assurance
checks.text: SPEC-003 — For payments/financial services identify merchant, processor, marketplace, custodian or advisory roles and applicable specialist review; using a payment gateway does not settle every duty.

checks.heading: Regulated services and assurance
checks.text: SPEC-004 — For payment-card obligations determine actual data handling and contractual scope; an integration mode or questionnaire alone is not a universal PCI compliance conclusion.

checks.heading: Regulated services and assurance
checks.text: SPEC-005 — For education/children evaluate student-record, school/vendor, parental, exam and accessibility duties from actual relationships and countries.

checks.heading: Regulated services and assurance
checks.text: SPEC-006 — For employment/recruiting review candidate data, background checks, monitoring, automated selection, bias/discrimination and required notices or assessments.

checks.heading: Regulated services and assurance
checks.text: SPEC-007 — For accessibility obligations identify applicable law/contract, covered service, standard/version, exemptions and statement/feedback requirements; cross-link actual accessibility test evidence.

checks.heading: Regulated services and assurance
checks.text: SPEC-008 — For advertising in regulated sectors review prohibited claims, required qualifications/disclosures, approval and audience restrictions for the actual offer.

checks.heading: Regulated services and assurance
checks.text: SPEC-009 — For games, virtual items, loot boxes, gambling-like features and age ratings obtain market-specific classification and platform decisions; monetization labels do not settle the issue.

checks.heading: Regulated services and assurance
checks.text: SPEC-010 — For connected devices, digital products and downloadable software examine product-safety, security-update, vulnerability-disclosure, support-period and lifecycle requirements where applicable.

checks.heading: Regulated services and assurance
checks.text: SPEC-011 — For public-sector/procurement customers identify accessibility, records, hosting, localization, audit and supplier-flow-down obligations in executed terms.

checks.heading: Regulated services and assurance
checks.text: SPEC-012 — For SOC 2, ISO or other assurance commitments verify entity, service, scope, period, report/certificate status and permitted claims; distinguish attestation, certification and contractual controls.

checks.heading: Cross-border, business change, and disputes
checks.text: SPEC-013 — Determine applicable export/sanctions/import restrictions from software, encryption, technology, destination, parties, users and activity; choose a documented specialist review when needed.

checks.heading: Cross-border, business change, and disputes
checks.text: SPEC-014 — Assess region restrictions, reseller distribution and remote access against both license territory and applicable trade rules; a billing-country dropdown is not complete enforcement evidence.

checks.heading: Cross-border, business change, and disputes
checks.text: SPEC-015 — Check local entity, tax/invoice, consumer, language and marketing requirements when adding countries; do not assume translated terms alone localize the service.

checks.heading: Cross-border, business change, and disputes
checks.text: SPEC-016 — Review acquisitions, entity changes, restructuring and asset sales for assignment/change-of-control consent, IP title, user notice and data-transfer issues.

checks.heading: Cross-border, business change, and disputes
checks.text: SPEC-017 — During investment/client due diligence reconcile claims of ownership and “all licenses cleared” with the actual inventory, exceptions and signed contributor grants.

checks.heading: Cross-border, business change, and disputes
checks.text: SPEC-018 — Review patent-sensitive features, inventions, confidentiality and open-source patent clauses where risk justifies it; trademark searches and dependency scans do not provide patent freedom-to-operate clearance.

checks.heading: Cross-border, business change, and disputes
checks.text: SPEC-019 — Maintain trade-secret/confidential-information controls for source, prompts, datasets, customer documents and partner roadmaps; publication or provider use can conflict with obligations.

checks.heading: Cross-border, business change, and disputes
checks.text: SPEC-020 — Distinguish allegations, rights requests, contractual disputes, regulator inquiries and litigation holds; route to the right owner and avoid destructive evidence cleanup.

checks.heading: Cross-border, business change, and disputes
checks.text: SPEC-021 — Test preservation instructions alongside retention/deletion schedules so holds are authorized, scoped, reviewable and released when appropriate.

checks.heading: Cross-border, business change, and disputes
checks.text: SPEC-022 — For product shutdown or vendor exit plan surviving license offers, source delivery, customer exports, prepaid remedies, public notices and retained records.

checks.heading: Cross-border, business change, and disputes
checks.text: SPEC-023 — Check translated agreements, multiple governing documents and territorial overrides for conflicts; record which language/version controls and obtain enforceability interpretation as needed.

checks.heading: Cross-border, business change, and disputes
checks.text: SPEC-024 — Reassess specialist scope when features, roles, countries, audiences or provider chains change; record unresolved obligations before enabling the changed activity.

checks.heading: Policies and personal data
checks.text: LEG-001 — Identify applicable privacy, cookie, consumer, accessibility, marketing, platform, and sector-specific requirements. Do not assume that every project has the same obligations or that the operator's location is the only relevant jurisdiction.

checks.heading: Policies and personal data
checks.text: LEG-002 — Verify public identity/contact information and applicable privacy, terms, acceptable-use, refund/cancellation, and cookie notices. Compare their promises with actual processing and product behavior.

checks.heading: Policies and personal data
checks.text: LEG-003 — Identify personal data purposes, legal bases, recipients, retention, user rights, processors/subprocessors, processing agreements, and cross-border transfers where applicable. Coordinate implemented access/export/deletion with 01 and 09.

checks.heading: Policies and personal data
checks.text: LEG-004 — Inventory cookies and similar tracking. Determine which are essential and which require consent under applicable rules; verify blocked-before-consent behavior, withdrawal, and accessible controls. For Spanish rules, consult current AEPD guidance, including equal visibility of acceptance/rejection where applicable. [AEPD cookie guidance](https://www.aepd.es/preguntas-frecuentes/17-internet-y-redes-sociales/FAQ-1707-importancia-de-las-cookies-en-la-proteccion-de-datos)

checks.heading: Policies and personal data
checks.text: LEG-005 — Assess minors, sensitive data, profiling, automated decisions, and regulated activities if present. Identify where additional controls or specialist review are needed.

checks.heading: Policies and personal data
checks.text: LEG-006 — Determine whether children's privacy requirements apply from the intended audience, actual use/knowledge, countries, and data collected. For applicable COPPA flows, verify notices, verifiable parental consent, parental rights, minimization, and retention; test any age screen before collection. Do not add date-of-birth collection to every general-audience product or assume an age checkbox alone satisfies the requirements. [FTC COPPA guidance](https://www.ftc.gov/business-guidance/resources/complying-coppa-frequently-asked-questions)

checks.heading: Policies and personal data
checks.text: LEG-007 — Inventory browser requests to external font, asset, analytics, chat, and replay providers, including requests made before consent. Assess disclosed recipients, legal basis, and international transfers even when no cookie is set. Consider licensed self-hosted fonts to avoid unnecessary third-party requests; check the actual applicable rules rather than treating one court award as a universal tariff. [Bavarian authority's external-font guidance, scoped to public bodies](https://www.datenschutz-bayern.de/datenschutzreform2018/aki42.html)

checks.heading: Policies and personal data
checks.text: LEG-008 — Where session replay, heatmaps, keystroke capture, or chat recording exists, assess applicable privacy and communications-interception rules, including California CIPA where relevant. Record provider roles, purposes, notice/consent timing, sensitive routes, and permitted retention. Require qualified review of disputed applicability; neither a banner nor field masking alone establishes lawful recording. Use 01 for capture and consent verification.

checks.heading: Policies and personal data
checks.text: LEG-009 — Record incident-notification assessment, retention/deletion exceptions, and responsible decision makers. Check that support and analytics do not introduce undeclared processing.

checks.heading: Intellectual property and provider terms
checks.text: LEG-010 — Inventory licenses for source dependencies, SDKs, images, stock assets, fonts, icons, audio/music, video, datasets, models, and exported content.

checks.heading: Intellectual property and provider terms
checks.text: LEG-011 — Check rights for the exact use: web display, server processing, embedding in exports, redistribution, modification, resale, commercial use, and training where relevant. Attribution requirements vary by source and license.

checks.heading: Intellectual property and provider terms
checks.text: LEG-012 — Keep required notices and evidence of asset/license provenance. Verify that a purchased or downloadable asset actually permits the intended distribution.

checks.heading: Intellectual property and provider terms
checks.text: LEG-013 — Review current API and platform terms for storage/caching, resale, branding, generated output, prohibited uses, scraping, and rate limits. Record provider/version/date; do not generalize one vendor's terms to another.

checks.heading: Intellectual property and provider terms
checks.text: LEG-014 — Define rights and responsibilities for user uploads and generated output. Include complaint/takedown handling where relevant and avoid guaranteeing exclusive rights that cannot be established.

checks.heading: Intellectual property and provider terms
checks.text: LEG-015 — If relying on US DMCA section 512 safe harbor, assess eligibility for the actual service activities. Where required, verify a current registered designated agent and publicly accessible contact details, renewal ownership, notice/counter-notice handling, expeditious action, and a reasonably implemented repeat-infringer policy. Registration alone does not establish eligibility; record the other applicable conditions and legal review. [Copyright Office section 512 guidance](https://www.copyright.gov/512/), [designated-agent directory](https://www.copyright.gov/dmca-directory/)

checks.heading: Intellectual property and provider terms
checks.text: LEG-016 — For AI or synthetic media, assess applicable disclosure, personality/publicity rights, impersonation, deceptive advertising, and testimonial rules. Distinguish a presenter reading approved copy from claims of real customer experience; verify legal requirements for the actual audience and format.

checks.heading: Commercial behavior
checks.text: LEG-017 — Compare marketing claims, endorsements, affiliate/sponsor disclosures, price display, taxes, trial conversions, renewals, cancellation, and refunds against applicable obligations.

checks.heading: Commercial behavior
checks.text: LEG-018 — Verify transactional versus marketing email/message treatment, consent or other permission, opt-out/unsubscribe, suppression, and recordkeeping. Use 14 for delivery implementation.

checks.heading: Commercial behavior
checks.text: LEG-019 — Classify launch announcements and mixed promotional/account messages by their actual primary purpose. Where CAN-SPAM applies, verify truthful sender/subject information, advertising identification as required, a valid physical postal address, and an easy opt-out honored within the applicable period. An existing customer relationship does not by itself make a promotional email transactional; assess other applicable marketing rules separately. [FTC CAN-SPAM guide](https://www.ftc.gov/business-guidance/resources/can-spam-act-compliance-guide-business)

checks.heading: Commercial behavior
checks.text: LEG-020 — Determine applicable automatic-renewal rules for consumer subscriptions and trials, including California where relevant. Check clear pre-purchase renewal/price/frequency/cancellation disclosures, placement relative to consent, affirmative consent and evidence, acknowledgments, required reminders/change notices, and usable cancellation. Assign applicable timing and remedy questions to the responsible reviewer; do not assume every renewal creates an automatic refund. Use 13 for end-to-end verification. [California Attorney General renewal guidance](https://oag.ca.gov/node/608083)

checks.heading: Commercial behavior
checks.text: LEG-021 — Check contracts, domain/brand ownership, customer support obligations, and required records for the product's distribution model.

checks.heading: Enterprise assurance and regulated data
checks.text: LEG-022 — Determine whether SOC 2 assurance, healthcare rules such as HIPAA, payment-card requirements, or other sector/contractual controls actually apply. Record scope, accountable specialists, and required evidence; a checklist does not establish certification or compliance.

checks.heading: Enterprise assurance and regulated data
checks.text: LEG-023 — Where required, verify appropriate processor agreements or BAAs cover each relevant vendor and service, including AI providers. Confirm approved services, uses, and data flows before sending regulated data; do not infer applicability from the presence of any health-related record alone.

checks.heading: Enterprise assurance and regulated data
checks.text: LEG-024 — Verify promised data residency across primary storage, replicas, backups, logs, support access, subprocessors, and model/fallback routing. Record any exceptions and their contractual basis.

checks.heading: Enterprise assurance and regulated data
checks.text: LEG-025 — Trace access/export/deletion requests through related tables, files, logs, derived data, and vendors. Document justified retention exceptions and backup expiry; ensure restores do not silently reactivate data that must remain deleted.

checks.heading: Enterprise assurance and regulated data
checks.text: LEG-026 — Keep evidence-backed security questionnaire answers and required policy/audit records current. Match claims to the actual scope, independent assurance evidence, and known exceptions; use 01 for security testing, disclosure, access reviews, and read-audit controls.

checks.heading: Boundary, failure, and recovery cases
checks.text: LEG-X01 — Test the exact shipped artifact, deployment, policy version, provider plan and contractual entity; an approved demo or different plan is not equivalent evidence.

checks.heading: Boundary, failure, and recovery cases
checks.text: LEG-X02 — Check public preview, beta, free, trial and internal-only claims against actual external access/distribution and data collection.

checks.heading: Boundary, failure, and recovery cases
checks.text: LEG-X03 — Inspect white-label, reseller and client handover paths for notices, rights, data duties and allocation of responsibility beyond the primary brand.

checks.heading: Boundary, failure, and recovery cases
checks.text: LEG-X04 — Recheck rights and obligations when a previously private upload, repository, dashboard or export becomes public or shared externally.

checks.heading: Boundary, failure, and recovery cases
checks.text: LEG-X05 — Verify pending, revoked, expired, territory-limited and replaced permissions cannot silently remain approved in the release process.

checks.heading: Boundary, failure, and recovery cases
checks.text: LEG-X06 — Test vendor outages, fallback services and emergency migrations for undeclared data use, rights restrictions and contract/residency changes.

checks.heading: Boundary, failure, and recovery cases
checks.text: LEG-X07 — Review long-lived offline/device/downloaded releases for continuing notice, source-delivery, support and update obligations after hosted pages change.

checks.heading: Boundary, failure, and recovery cases
checks.text: LEG-X08 — Check account deletion, cancellation, subscription expiry and license termination as distinct events with their own data, payment and rights consequences.

checks.heading: Boundary, failure, and recovery cases
checks.text: LEG-X09 — Verify complaints, legal holds and preservation instructions do not silently conflict with ordinary deletion/cleanup jobs; assign and document the decision.

checks.heading: Boundary, failure, and recovery cases
checks.text: LEG-X10 — Review import, export, restore, duplicate submissions and failed background jobs for promises that are met in the UI but not across the completed process.

checks.heading: Boundary, failure, and recovery cases
checks.text: LEG-X11 — Verify marketing, customer contracts, policies and provider terms remain consistent after a feature, model, region or pricing change.

checks.heading: Boundary, failure, and recovery cases
checks.text: LEG-X12 — Separate unknown rights/applicability from confirmed noncompliance and enhancements; retain unresolved questions with an owner and required decision date.

checks.heading: Remediation and decision
checks.text: [Specific final artifact or behavior matches the documented obligation/right.]

checks.heading: Remediation and decision
checks.text: [Original failing state plus relevant related releases/variants checked.]

checks.heading: Remediation and decision
checks.text: [Required evidence, notice, fulfillment or decision is retained.]

checks.heading: Service and dependency inventory
checks.text: OO-SCP-001: Record project, deployed release/image, environment, audit period/timezone, accountable owner, decision needed, and evidence root; distinguish intended configuration from deployed state.

checks.heading: Service and dependency inventory
checks.text: OO-SCP-002: Inventory public and private entry points, clients, services, workers, queues, databases, caches, object stores, schedulers, integrations, and manual fulfillment steps.

checks.heading: Service and dependency inventory
checks.text: OO-SCP-003: Map critical user journeys to supporting components, dependencies, data authorities, and failure consequences; distinguish process health from useful service delivery.

checks.heading: Service and dependency inventory
checks.text: OO-SCP-004: Record supported regions, tenants, plans, clients, peak periods, data scale, availability promises, and operating hours; do not assume round-the-clock staffing or multi-region architecture.

checks.heading: Service and dependency inventory
checks.text: OO-SCP-005: Name primary and backup owners for each critical service, dependency, resource, alert, runbook, provider account, and operational decision.

checks.heading: Service and dependency inventory
checks.text: OO-SCP-006: Map shared-host, shared-database, shared-account, shared-region, shared-network, and shared-identity dependencies; identify failures that can affect several applications together.

checks.heading: Service and dependency inventory
checks.text: OO-SCP-007: Inventory monitoring collectors, pipelines, storage, dashboards, paging, status communication, identity, and their own dependencies; identify common failure domains with the application.

checks.heading: Service and dependency inventory
checks.text: OO-SCP-008: Reconcile repository declarations with hosting control planes, system schedulers, containers, external automations, queue repeaters, provider consoles, and billing evidence where access permits.

checks.heading: Service and dependency inventory
checks.text: OO-SCP-009: Record undeclared, ownerless, abandoned, duplicate, and retired resources or jobs; link recurring-work and spend reconciliation to shared module 08.

checks.heading: Service and dependency inventory
checks.text: OO-SCP-010: Record which services inherit verified shared infrastructure controls and which still need application-specific monitoring, permissions, and recovery evidence.

checks.heading: Assessment and evidence
checks.text: OO-SCP-011: Select applicable checks and specialist handoffs; exclude unsupported platforms/capabilities with reasons and name the evidence gaps caused by unavailable access.

checks.heading: Assessment and evidence
checks.text: OO-SCP-012: Record each scenario's build/configuration, environment, timestamp/timezone, actor, input, expected result, observed result, method/tool/settings, and sanitized evidence.

checks.heading: Assessment and evidence
checks.text: OO-SCP-013: Separate source/configuration review, staging execution, production observation, and provider reports; do not claim one proves another environment's behavior.

checks.heading: Assessment and evidence
checks.text: OO-SCP-014: Trace a representative successful action and a controlled failure from user outcome through telemetry, alert receipt, operator diagnosis, and recovery where applicable.

checks.heading: Assessment and evidence
checks.text: OO-SCP-015: Record verified sample separately from estimated affected population; explain sampling across services, tenants, regions, deployments, and failure modes.

checks.heading: Assessment and evidence
checks.text: OO-SCP-016: Distinguish confirmed defects, verification gaps, accepted risks, and opportunities; a missing enterprise-scale tool is not automatically a defect if a simpler workflow meets the requirement.

checks.heading: Assessment and evidence
checks.text: OO-SCP-017: Deduplicate root causes across operational and specialist audit modules; retain related check IDs and identify one primary owner.

checks.heading: Assessment and evidence
checks.text: OO-SCP-018: Assess severity, current exposure, confidence, delivery priority, and launch-blocker status separately using realistic impact and documented workarounds.

checks.heading: Assessment and evidence
checks.text: OO-SCP-019: Keep redacted evidence and operational documents accessible outside the service's failure domain, with approved access, retention, and recovery arrangements.

checks.heading: Assessment and evidence
checks.text: OO-SCP-020: Reconcile selected check statuses and report coverage, exclusions, unresolved gaps, owners, and acceptance/recheck conditions.

checks.heading: Safe verification and scenario selection
checks.text: OO-SCP-021: Bound any authorized live verification by target, request rate, duration, cost, impact, cleanup, and stop conditions; use synthetic data and disposable environments for destructive rehearsals.

checks.heading: Safe verification and scenario selection
checks.text: OO-SCP-022: Select scenarios across outage, partial degradation, silent omission, delayed work, wrong results, monitoring loss, and recovery; do not limit testing to thrown exceptions.

checks.heading: Safe verification and scenario selection
checks.text: OO-SCP-023: Cover relevant intersections such as provider outage during deployment, monitoring outage during an incident, expired operator access during recovery, and backlog replay after restoration.

checks.heading: Safe verification and scenario selection
checks.text: OO-SCP-024: Add incidents, near misses, support recurrence, migrations, and known architecture risks to project-specific coverage; expand sampling after inconsistent results.

checks.heading: Service indicators and objectives
checks.text: OO-SLO-001: Define the critical outcomes users rely on, affected audiences, natural usage cycles, and consequences of late, missing, or incorrect results.

checks.heading: Service indicators and objectives
checks.text: OO-SLO-002: Specify each service indicator's numerator, denominator, unit, eligible population, source, aggregation, timezone, and observation window.

checks.heading: Service indicators and objectives
checks.text: OO-SLO-003: Distinguish request availability, latency, correctness, durability, freshness, and end-to-end completion; a successful HTTP response alone does not establish all of them.

checks.heading: Service indicators and objectives
checks.text: OO-SLO-004: Record objective target, rationale, owner, review interval, and contractual relationship; distinguish internal objectives from external service commitments.

checks.heading: Service indicators and objectives
checks.text: OO-SLO-005: Define which requests or jobs are good, bad, excluded, or unknown; justify treatment of client errors, timeouts, canceled work, dependency failure, and planned maintenance.

checks.heading: Service indicators and objectives
checks.text: OO-SLO-006: Check low-traffic, no-traffic, bursty, seasonal, and batch services use meaningful windows and denominators rather than misleading percentages.

checks.heading: Service indicators and objectives
checks.text: OO-SLO-007: Measure relevant tenant, plan, region, endpoint, and client segments without letting a healthy high-volume segment hide a critical smaller outage.

checks.heading: Service indicators and objectives
checks.text: OO-SLO-008: Choose collection and aggregation that reflect real user experience; record gaps from sampling, client blocking, retries, caches, and internal traffic.

checks.heading: Service indicators and objectives
checks.text: OO-SLO-009: Verify indicator data against known successful, failed, slow, and partially completed synthetic actions with authoritative outcomes.

checks.heading: Service indicators and objectives
checks.text: OO-SLO-010: Define objective policy for missing telemetry and delayed ingestion; unknown periods are not silently counted as healthy.

checks.heading: Service indicators and objectives
checks.text: OO-SLO-011: Where using error budgets, define allowed bad outcomes, window, consumption calculation, owner, and responses to rapid or sustained consumption.

checks.heading: Service indicators and objectives
checks.text: OO-SLO-012: Verify objective breaches influence release, capacity, reliability, or investigation decisions; avoid collecting objectives with no accountable action.

checks.heading: Health checks and external probes
checks.text: OO-SLO-013: Distinguish liveness, readiness, startup, dependency health, and user-facing synthetic checks; document what each establishes and what it omits.

checks.heading: Health checks and external probes
checks.text: OO-SLO-014: Verify a process that is running but unable to serve useful work is detected by an appropriate readiness or user-facing check.

checks.heading: Health checks and external probes
checks.text: OO-SLO-015: Ensure health checks have suitable timeouts, frequency, thresholds, and hysteresis; they do not create restart loops or overload a failing dependency.

checks.heading: Health checks and external probes
checks.text: OO-SLO-016: Check whether dependency failures should remove an instance, mark partial degradation, or preserve a fallback; avoid one dependency outage unnecessarily removing all capacity.

checks.heading: Health checks and external probes
checks.text: OO-SLO-017: Run appropriate external monitoring outside the application's failure domain; record network, DNS, TLS, identity, and provider dependencies of the probe.

checks.heading: Health checks and external probes
checks.text: OO-SLO-018: Verify probes exercise the intended host, route, region, authentication state, and useful response rather than only a cached landing page or redirect.

checks.heading: Health checks and external probes
checks.text: OO-SLO-019: Test expected content/state, not only status codes; maintenance pages, login redirects, and empty success responses do not pass a useful-service check by accident.

checks.heading: Health checks and external probes
checks.text: OO-SLO-020: Use synthetic credentials/data with scoped permissions, cleanup, rotation, and cost bounds; probes do not create real purchases or contact unintended recipients.

checks.heading: Health checks and external probes
checks.text: OO-SLO-021: Cover relevant geographic/client entry points and distinguish regional network failures from global service outage using independent evidence where practical.

checks.heading: Health checks and external probes
