checks.text: OO-SLO-022: Verify health endpoints reveal no unnecessary secrets/topology, stay inexpensive, and have controls suited to their public/private exposure through specialist security review.

checks.heading: Silent failures and freshness
checks.text: OO-SLO-023: Define expected completion/freshness for critical scheduled jobs, reports, syncs, backups, notifications, and materialized data; missing execution triggers detection without an exception.

checks.heading: Silent failures and freshness
checks.text: OO-SLO-024: Check last-started, last-successful, completion deadline, runtime, overlap, and missed schedule separately; starting is not proof of useful completion.

checks.heading: Silent failures and freshness
checks.text: OO-SLO-025: Test disabled scheduler, stalled worker, missed trigger, success with zero useful output, and wrong-environment execution using controlled fixtures.

checks.heading: Silent failures and freshness
checks.text: OO-SLO-026: Account for business calendars, DST, local time, approved pauses, and planned infrequent execution without suppressing genuine stale-work failures.

checks.heading: Silent failures and freshness
checks.text: OO-SLO-027: Verify successful completion reflects validated output or reconciliation, not merely a process exit or heartbeat emitted before work finishes.

checks.heading: Silent failures and freshness
checks.text: OO-SLO-028: Monitor backup age and last verified restore separately; operational freshness does not prove the backup can restore correct data.

checks.heading: Silent failures and freshness
checks.text: OO-SLO-029: Check customer-visible freshness/status labels reflect actual data age and partial outages; degraded service is communicated truthfully.

checks.heading: Silent failures and freshness
checks.text: OO-SLO-030: Review objectives after architecture, audience, workload, dependency, or promise changes; retain the definition/version needed to interpret historical results.

checks.heading: Instrumentation and correlation
checks.text: OO-TEL-001: Capture meaningful client, API, server, worker, scheduler, integration, and administrative failures; verify controlled examples reach the actual monitoring backend.

checks.heading: Instrumentation and correlation
checks.text: OO-TEL-002: Use structured records with timestamp/timezone, service, environment, release, operation, stage, outcome, severity, duration, and appropriate correlation identifiers.

checks.heading: Instrumentation and correlation
checks.text: OO-TEL-003: Trace a user action across ingress, application, queued work, provider calls, persistence, and callback where relevant; asynchronous boundaries retain safe correlation.

checks.heading: Instrumentation and correlation
checks.text: OO-TEL-004: Distinguish original operation, retry, batch, item, request, job, and external event identities so duplicate effects and replay can be diagnosed.

checks.heading: Instrumentation and correlation
checks.text: OO-TEL-005: Record successful critical transitions as well as failures when needed for reconciliation; do not infer success merely from the absence of exceptions.

checks.heading: Instrumentation and correlation
checks.text: OO-TEL-006: Check caught exceptions, rejected promises/tasks, background crashes, startup failures, and shutdown failures are visible with useful context.

checks.heading: Instrumentation and correlation
checks.text: OO-TEL-007: Preserve actionable error classification and causal chain without repeatedly logging the same stack at every boundary; grouping distinguishes materially different failures.

checks.heading: Instrumentation and correlation
checks.text: OO-TEL-008: Verify source maps/debug symbols and release mapping where used, with access controls; production errors resolve to the actual deployed version.

checks.heading: Instrumentation and correlation
checks.text: OO-TEL-009: Check timestamps, clock synchronization, duration measurement, ingestion time, and out-of-order events; diagnose clock skew rather than presenting a false sequence.

checks.heading: Instrumentation and correlation
checks.text: OO-TEL-010: Verify instrumentation does not silently omit failed paths, pre-auth failures, cold starts, streaming errors, or work completed after the client disconnects.

checks.heading: Tracing and error diagnosis
checks.text: OO-TEL-011: Where tracing is needed, inspect meaningful spans for request, dependency, database, queue wait, and processing; separate waiting from execution time.

checks.heading: Tracing and error diagnosis
checks.text: OO-TEL-012: Propagate trace context across supported boundaries with documented trust rules; untrusted incoming correlation data does not enable spoofed authority or uncontrolled storage.

checks.heading: Tracing and error diagnosis
checks.text: OO-TEL-013: Document sampling strategy, loss, and limitations; rare/slow/failed requests needed for diagnosis remain discoverable by tracing or another adequate evidence source.

checks.heading: Tracing and error diagnosis
checks.text: OO-TEL-014: Check traces, metrics, and logs link to the same service/environment/release and time interval; unrelated events are not joined merely because identifiers collide.

checks.heading: Tracing and error diagnosis
checks.text: OO-TEL-015: Verify trace/error instrumentation captures final outcome for partial responses, canceled streams, retries, and provider timeout after a possible remote success.

checks.heading: Tracing and error diagnosis
checks.text: OO-TEL-016: Check profiling or deep diagnostics, if used, have bounded duration, overhead, access, and retention; avoid enabling costly capture indefinitely.

checks.heading: Tracing and error diagnosis
checks.text: OO-TEL-017: Give users/support a safe diagnostic reference that can locate the relevant event without revealing credentials or internal details.

checks.heading: Privacy, access, and retention
checks.text: OO-TEL-018: Inspect actual payloads for secrets, tokens, cookies, credentials, payment details, sensitive prompts, and unnecessary personal data; verify redaction before export where required.

checks.heading: Privacy, access, and retention
checks.text: OO-TEL-019: Check URLs/query strings, headers, stack locals, attachments, screenshots, session replay, and provider error bodies as potential sensitive-data paths.

checks.heading: Privacy, access, and retention
checks.text: OO-TEL-020: Restrict access by role/environment/tenant as needed; privileged telemetry queries, exports, and configuration changes have appropriate accountability.

checks.heading: Privacy, access, and retention
checks.text: OO-TEL-021: Define retention, deletion, archival, legal hold where applicable, and provider destinations by signal/data class; verify actual policies rather than relying only on documentation.

checks.heading: Privacy, access, and retention
checks.text: OO-TEL-022: Verify telemetry transport/storage credentials, rotation, encryption requirements, regional handling, and third-party processing through the security/privacy and legal modules.

checks.heading: Privacy, access, and retention
checks.text: OO-TEL-023: Bound untrusted values, escape log content appropriately, and prevent multiline/control-character input from obscuring event attribution or operational interpretation.

checks.heading: Privacy, access, and retention
checks.text: OO-TEL-024: Check temporary debug logging has an owner, expiry, approved data scope, and rollback; it does not persist unnoticed after an incident.

checks.heading: Pipeline reliability and economics
checks.text: OO-TEL-025: Inventory agents/collectors/exporters, buffers, transforms, sampling, indexes, storage tiers, dashboards, and alert queries; name ownership at each stage.

checks.heading: Pipeline reliability and economics
checks.text: OO-TEL-026: Monitor telemetry ingestion delay, dropped/rejected records, queue/buffer saturation, exporter errors, and backend query availability independently of application errors.

checks.heading: Pipeline reliability and economics
checks.text: OO-TEL-027: Test telemetry backend outage or blocked egress in a safe environment; application behavior, bounded buffers, disk use, and backpressure follow the intended policy.

checks.heading: Pipeline reliability and economics
checks.text: OO-TEL-028: Verify restart/reconnect behavior, duplicate delivery, buffer loss, and late events; disclose gaps rather than reconstructing invented continuity.

checks.heading: Pipeline reliability and economics
checks.text: OO-TEL-029: Bound log volume, record size, trace volume, metric dimensions, retention, indexing, and export costs; identify noisy loops and unexpected cardinality growth.

checks.heading: Pipeline reliability and economics
checks.text: OO-TEL-030: Check rotation and quotas prevent log files or telemetry buffers exhausting application disk/inodes; diagnostic evidence remains obtainable under pressure.

checks.heading: Pipeline reliability and economics
checks.text: OO-TEL-031: Verify collectors do not unintentionally duplicate ingestion across replicas, agents, environments, or overlapping integrations.

checks.heading: Pipeline reliability and economics
checks.text: OO-TEL-032: Confirm telemetry failure is detectable through an independent route proportionate to risk; a silent broken monitor does not report itself healthy.

checks.heading: Pipeline reliability and economics
checks.text: OO-TEL-033: Test a known diagnostic question against retained data and actual query permissions; chosen retention/sampling permits the required investigation window.

checks.heading: Pipeline reliability and economics
checks.text: OO-TEL-034: Record instrumentation overhead and cost at representative workload where material; operational visibility does not consume uncontrolled service capacity.

checks.heading: Metrics and dashboard correctness
checks.text: OO-MET-001: Define traffic, error, latency, completion, freshness, and saturation metrics relevant to each critical service; record unit, source, owner, labels, aggregation, and window.

checks.heading: Metrics and dashboard correctness
checks.text: OO-MET-002: Distinguish event time from scrape/ingestion time, absent data from zero, and failed collection from healthy inactivity.

checks.heading: Metrics and dashboard correctness
checks.text: OO-MET-003: Verify counters, rates, gauges, histograms, resets, units, and aggregation against known synthetic activity; restarts do not create misleading negative or inflated rates.

checks.heading: Metrics and dashboard correctness
checks.text: OO-MET-004: Show appropriate latency distribution and slow-tail behavior, sample count, and workload context; do not hide tail failures behind a global average.

checks.heading: Metrics and dashboard correctness
checks.text: OO-MET-005: Check histogram boundaries/resolution suit operational thresholds and actual workload; record approximation and aggregation limits.

checks.heading: Metrics and dashboard correctness
checks.text: OO-MET-006: Verify dashboards filter the correct environment, region, service, deployment, tenant class, and period; staging noise does not contaminate production conclusions.

checks.heading: Metrics and dashboard correctness
checks.text: OO-MET-007: Link dashboards to objective definitions, alert rules, relevant logs/traces, runbooks, and owner; annotations identify deployments, incidents, maintenance, and data gaps.

checks.heading: Metrics and dashboard correctness
checks.text: OO-MET-008: Test no-data, partial-data, delayed-data, timezone, daylight-saving, and access-denied states; displays do not imply valid health from an empty panel.

checks.heading: Metrics and dashboard correctness
checks.text: OO-MET-009: Check aggregation does not hide minority tenant/region failures, error bursts, or capacity imbalance; drill-down is available without exposing unnecessary customer data.

checks.heading: Metrics and dashboard correctness
checks.text: OO-MET-010: Verify dashboard/query versions, permissions, backups or reproducible definitions, and a usable fallback during the primary dashboard's outage.

checks.heading: Compute, storage, and shared infrastructure
checks.text: OO-MET-011: For self-hosted services, monitor CPU saturation/throttling, memory pressure, process/container restarts, and out-of-memory termination; identify the affected workload.

checks.heading: Compute, storage, and shared infrastructure
checks.text: OO-MET-012: Monitor disk space, inodes, I/O latency, filesystem errors, mount availability, and relevant storage quotas; capacity alerts leave realistic remediation time.

checks.heading: Compute, storage, and shared infrastructure
checks.text: OO-MET-013: Check network reachability, connection errors, bandwidth, egress, DNS/TLS failures, and load-balancer behavior where operated by the team.

checks.heading: Compute, storage, and shared infrastructure
checks.text: OO-MET-014: Measure database connection pool use/wait, slow queries, lock contention, replication lag, storage growth, and resource ceilings relevant to the deployed engine.

checks.heading: Compute, storage, and shared infrastructure
checks.text: OO-MET-015: Monitor queue depth and oldest age, arrival/completion rates, in-flight work, retries, dead letters, and consumer availability; depth alone does not establish latency or health.

checks.heading: Compute, storage, and shared infrastructure
checks.text: OO-MET-016: Check cache availability, hit/miss behavior, evictions, memory, stale data, and dependency load on cache loss; a high hit rate does not prove correct data.

checks.heading: Compute, storage, and shared infrastructure
checks.text: OO-MET-017: Track object count/bytes, versions, temporary uploads/exports, lifecycle cleanup, retrieval/egress, and provider quotas where material.

checks.heading: Compute, storage, and shared infrastructure
checks.text: OO-MET-018: Identify shared-host noisy neighbors and per-application resource attribution; a healthy host average does not hide one saturated workload.

checks.heading: Compute, storage, and shared infrastructure
checks.text: OO-MET-019: Monitor platform-specific ceilings such as file descriptors, process/thread count, port exhaustion, connection caps, and build/runtime limits where they can constrain service.

checks.heading: Compute, storage, and shared infrastructure
checks.text: OO-MET-020: Track capacity lost to backups, maintenance, deployments, scans, compaction, or batch jobs; routine work does not unexpectedly starve critical traffic.

checks.heading: Capacity planning and spend
checks.text: OO-MET-021: Record current typical/peak workload, forecast basis, headroom, bottleneck, and capacity owner; estimates identify uncertainty and expected growth rather than inventing demand.

checks.heading: Capacity planning and spend
checks.text: OO-MET-022: Verify autoscaling bounds, triggers, warm-up, scale-down, minimum capacity, and dependency constraints where used; scaling does not simply move the bottleneck or cost spike.

checks.heading: Capacity planning and spend
checks.text: OO-MET-023: Test approved overload/degraded-mode behavior with bounded workloads; admission control, queues, timeouts, and recovery protect useful service.

checks.heading: Capacity planning and spend
checks.text: OO-MET-024: Check capacity and cost after failover or loss of one component where redundancy is promised; document reduced capacity and the scope actually rehearsed.

checks.heading: Capacity planning and spend
checks.text: OO-MET-025: Reconcile resource usage and billed units with provider reports and cost-module inventories; missing billing access remains a gap, not proof of zero spend.

checks.heading: Capacity planning and spend
checks.text: OO-MET-026: Track relevant total spend, spend velocity, unit cost per useful outcome, unusual egress, repeated failed work, and unallocated shared cost.

checks.heading: Capacity planning and spend
checks.text: OO-MET-027: Monitor telemetry/cardinality, CI/build, previews, external automation, retained backups, abandoned resources, and idle-but-billable services as applicable.

checks.heading: Capacity planning and spend
checks.text: OO-MET-028: Define budget/capacity alert delay, recipient, decision, and containment route; distinguish advisory warnings from hard enforcement through shared module 08.

checks.heading: Capacity planning and spend
checks.text: OO-MET-029: Verify alerts anticipate contractual limits, certificate/domain renewal, license expiry, prepaid depletion, and storage exhaustion when these can interrupt service.

checks.heading: Capacity planning and spend
checks.text: OO-MET-030: Review forecasts and dashboards after launches, migrations, pricing changes, incidents, and major data growth; remove obsolete panels without losing necessary coverage.

checks.heading: Alert definition and actionability
checks.text: OO-ALT-001: Inventory alert rules with service, failure mode, source/query, threshold/window, severity, recipient, owner, runbook, and required action.

checks.heading: Alert definition and actionability
checks.text: OO-ALT-002: Map critical outcomes, silent missing work, resource exhaustion, dependency failures, spend, and relevant security changes to an appropriate detection/response route.

checks.heading: Alert definition and actionability
checks.text: OO-ALT-003: Separate urgent pages, working-hours tickets, informational notices, and trend reviews based on action urgency and impact rather than raw log level.

checks.heading: Alert definition and actionability
checks.text: OO-ALT-004: Set thresholds from objectives, workload, failure consequence, and remediation time; avoid importing arbitrary universal values.

checks.heading: Alert definition and actionability
checks.text: OO-ALT-005: Check both rapid severe deterioration and sustained smaller failure where material; objective/budget-based alerts have explicit windows, denominators, and action policy.

checks.heading: Alert definition and actionability
checks.text: OO-ALT-006: Define no-data, missing series, delayed ingestion, scrape failure, and telemetry outage behavior; absence of data does not silently clear a real incident.

checks.heading: Alert definition and actionability
checks.text: OO-ALT-007: Verify low-traffic denominators, expected idle periods, batch schedules, business calendars, and cold start do not generate misleading alerts or conceal failures.

checks.heading: Alert definition and actionability
checks.text: OO-ALT-008: Include environment, service, scope, start time, impact, safe diagnostic links, release context, and next action in the alert without leaking secrets or unnecessary customer data.

checks.heading: Alert definition and actionability
checks.text: OO-ALT-009: Verify alert queries and dashboards agree on scope/window/units; a responder can reproduce the condition from accessible evidence.

checks.heading: Alert definition and actionability
checks.text: OO-ALT-010: Test threshold crossing, sustained failure, recovery, and relapse using bounded synthetic fixtures; retain timestamps through detection and receipt.

checks.heading: Delivery and coverage
checks.text: OO-ALT-011: Route alerts to a current accountable person or staffed channel; former staff, personal-only accounts, and unmonitored inboxes are not the sole route for essential incidents.

checks.heading: Delivery and coverage
checks.text: OO-ALT-012: Define coverage hours, primary/backup, acknowledgement target, escalation path, and out-of-hours limitation; promises match actual availability.

checks.heading: Delivery and coverage
checks.text: OO-ALT-013: Test real receipt through the configured production alerting route using an explicitly labeled harmless test; vendor preview/configuration validation alone is insufficient.

checks.heading: Delivery and coverage
checks.text: OO-ALT-014: Test absent acknowledgement, unreachable primary, expired contact, invalid token, and notification-provider failure with approved scenarios; fallback reaches someone who can act.

checks.heading: Delivery and coverage
checks.text: OO-ALT-015: Verify mobile/email/paging settings, quiet modes, device changes, channel membership, and platform permissions do not defeat promised urgent delivery.

checks.heading: Delivery and coverage
checks.text: OO-ALT-016: Check acknowledgement, assignment, escalation, resolution, and handoff semantics; acknowledging a page does not automatically mean the incident is mitigated.

checks.heading: Delivery and coverage
checks.text: OO-ALT-017: Record end-to-end detection, routing, receipt, acknowledgement, and action times separately; do not report a single ambiguous response metric.

checks.heading: Delivery and coverage
checks.text: OO-ALT-018: Keep emergency contacts, provider escalation, and runbooks accessible if the app, main network, identity provider, or primary collaboration tool fails.

checks.heading: Delivery and coverage
checks.text: OO-ALT-019: Verify an independent route detects failure of the alerting pipeline proportionately to risk, including dead-man checks where appropriate.

checks.heading: Noise, grouping, and suppression
checks.text: OO-ALT-020: Group related symptom alerts while preserving affected services/tenants and useful context; deduplication does not merge unrelated incidents.

checks.heading: Noise, grouping, and suppression
checks.text: OO-ALT-021: Use inhibition/dependency rules carefully so a parent outage reduces noise without suppressing independent security, data-loss, or recovery failures.

checks.heading: Noise, grouping, and suppression
checks.text: OO-ALT-022: Check flapping, short spikes, repeated retries, and alert storms; persistence/hysteresis and rate limits reduce noise without delaying urgent detection beyond the agreed window.

checks.heading: Noise, grouping, and suppression
checks.text: OO-ALT-023: Define maintenance/silence scope, owner, reason, start/end, and automatic expiry; deployment maintenance does not mute unrelated services indefinitely.

checks.heading: Noise, grouping, and suppression
checks.text: OO-ALT-024: Verify alerts recover only after the real condition resolves; missing telemetry, manual closure, and a restarted collector do not fabricate recovery.

checks.heading: Noise, grouping, and suppression
checks.text: OO-ALT-025: Review alert volume, actionable proportion, duplicate pages, missed incidents, time to action, and responder workload using actual patterns.

checks.heading: Noise, grouping, and suppression
checks.text: OO-ALT-026: Remove or retune obsolete rules and identify missing ones after incidents; disabling a noisy alert includes an alternate detection route or documented risk acceptance.

checks.heading: Response sustainability
checks.text: OO-ALT-027: Provide responders the permissions, tools, context, and training needed for the expected action; a page to someone unable to access the system is not effective coverage.

checks.heading: Response sustainability
checks.text: OO-ALT-028: Test rotation/handoff, leave, illness, owner departure, and one-person-team fallback; record realistic external help or accepted coverage gaps.

checks.heading: Response sustainability
checks.text: OO-ALT-029: Check escalation avoids dependence on the same failed account, provider, network, or device wherever practical.

checks.heading: Response sustainability
checks.text: OO-ALT-030: Review coverage and contact accuracy after staffing, vendor, identity, application, and phone/device changes; retain evidence of the latest delivery rehearsal.

checks.heading: Build and deployment identity
checks.text: OO-REL-001: Identify deployed source revision, artifact/image digest, runtime, migration state, feature flags, and critical configuration without exposing secrets.

checks.heading: Build and deployment identity
checks.text: OO-REL-002: Trace the running artifact to its build and release record; distinguish a rebuild of a source revision from promotion of the exact same artifact.

checks.heading: Build and deployment identity
checks.text: OO-REL-003: Document build, verification, approval where required, deploy, smoke check, observation, and recovery steps with accountable operators.

checks.heading: Build and deployment identity
checks.text: OO-REL-004: Separate staging/test/live credentials, resource names, provider accounts, endpoints, and data; verify deployed configuration points to the intended environment.

checks.heading: Build and deployment identity
checks.text: OO-REL-005: Check failed builds, unavailable registries, partial uploads, missing artifacts, and expired deployment credentials produce visible failure rather than a false successful release.

checks.heading: Build and deployment identity
checks.text: OO-REL-006: Verify release metadata links telemetry and customer-visible failures to the actual instance/version during mixed-version deployments.

checks.heading: Build and deployment identity
checks.text: OO-REL-007: Ensure necessary deployment definitions and known-good artifacts remain recoverable with appropriate access if the primary workstation or build service is unavailable.

checks.heading: Configuration and secrets
checks.text: OO-REL-008: Inventory required environment/configuration values, source, owner, defaults, reload/restart needs, and validation; missing critical values fail safely and visibly.

checks.heading: Configuration and secrets
checks.text: OO-REL-009: Record intentional environment differences and detect meaningful drift between versioned declarations and deployed settings.

checks.heading: Configuration and secrets
checks.text: OO-REL-010: Verify secret rotation, expiry, revocation, overlapping validity where needed, distribution, restart behavior, and application recovery through specialist security review.

checks.heading: Configuration and secrets
checks.text: OO-REL-011: Prevent logs, build output, health pages, diagnostics, and release records exposing secrets; reference secret versions/identities rather than values.

checks.heading: Configuration and secrets
checks.text: OO-REL-012: Check configuration changes receive proportionate validation, change attribution, rollback/containment, and telemetry annotations like code changes.

checks.heading: Configuration and secrets
checks.text: OO-REL-013: Test feature-flag defaults, eligibility, stale clients, conflicting combinations, control-plane outage, and removal/expiry; disabled UI alone does not stop backend work.

checks.heading: Configuration and secrets
checks.text: OO-REL-014: Verify emergency controls and safe fallbacks do not silently enable an unintended provider, debug mode, public access, or unlimited spending.

checks.heading: Deploying under real conditions
checks.text: OO-REL-015: Test startup/readiness, warm-up, dependency initialization, startup migration, and insufficient-capacity behavior; instances receive traffic only according to the intended health policy.

checks.heading: Deploying under real conditions
checks.text: OO-REL-016: Verify draining and graceful shutdown for requests, streams, workers, locks, leases, and in-flight jobs; termination behavior is observable and documented.

checks.heading: Deploying under real conditions
checks.text: OO-REL-017: Test old/new application versions with relevant schema, message, API, and cache formats during rollout and rollback.

checks.heading: Deploying under real conditions
checks.text: OO-REL-018: Rehearse data migrations with representative scale, runtime, locks, failure midway, restart/resume, and irreversible steps in a disposable environment.

checks.heading: Deploying under real conditions
checks.text: OO-REL-019: Verify migrations and schedulers execute with the intended coordination across replicas; deployment does not create duplicate jobs or competing destructive changes.

checks.heading: Deploying under real conditions
checks.text: OO-REL-020: Check canary, rolling, blue/green, or simple replacement behavior only where used; traffic selection, observation, and abort conditions match the chosen strategy.

checks.heading: Deploying under real conditions
checks.text: OO-REL-021: Test partial rollout, unhealthy new instance, old instance remaining active, and deployment cancellation; the operator can identify and reconcile actual state.

checks.heading: Deploying under real conditions
checks.text: OO-REL-022: Verify static assets, CDN caches, client bundles, service workers, and API versions remain compatible or present an explicit supported refresh path.

checks.heading: Deploying under real conditions
checks.text: OO-REL-023: Check simultaneous deployments, operator retries, locked pipelines, and emergency changes; competing actions do not leave an unknown release/configuration state.

checks.heading: Deploying under real conditions
checks.text: OO-REL-024: Verify scheduled jobs, repeaters, external automations, and old environments are not duplicated by cutover; check actual deployed scheduling sources.

checks.heading: Deploying under real conditions
checks.text: OO-REL-025: Verify supported low/no-downtime claims under representative traffic, including database and worker transitions; document what was not rehearsed.

checks.heading: Recovery and maintenance
checks.text: OO-REL-026: Recover a known-good release using the actual operator route in a safe rehearsal; record access, artifact/configuration availability, steps, duration, and smoke results.

checks.heading: Recovery and maintenance
checks.text: OO-REL-027: Identify rollback limits for schema/data changes, external messages, charges, deleted records, and irreversible side effects; define forward recovery or compensation where needed.

checks.heading: Recovery and maintenance
checks.text: OO-REL-028: Define automatic/manual rollback triggers and decision authority; telemetry delay or missing metrics does not falsely certify a canary healthy.

checks.heading: Recovery and maintenance
checks.text: OO-REL-029: Run bounded post-deploy checks for useful user journeys, background work, data state, critical integrations, errors, and alerting; observe long enough for relevant delayed effects.

checks.heading: Recovery and maintenance
checks.text: OO-REL-030: Assign OS/runtime/dependency/platform patch ownership, supported-version tracking, update validation, failed-update detection, and required restart/reboot handling.

checks.heading: Recovery and maintenance
checks.text: OO-REL-031: Rehearse certificate, runtime, database, operating-system, and provider upgrades proportionately, including compatibility, backups, rollback limits, and operator availability.

checks.heading: Recovery and maintenance
checks.text: OO-REL-032: Track emergency/manual changes back into versioned automation or documented configuration; later reconciliation does not silently undo an essential mitigation.

checks.heading: Recovery and maintenance
checks.text: OO-REL-033: Retire old deployments, previews, temporary flags, credentials, jobs, and billable resources only after dependency checks; verify they stay retired after redeployment/reconciliation.

checks.heading: Recovery and maintenance
checks.text: OO-REL-034: Close the change record with actual version, times, outcome, incidents, residual risks, and follow-up owners rather than only the pipeline's success state.

checks.heading: Preparedness and triage
checks.text: OO-INC-001: Define incident criteria and impact-based severity examples for outages, degradation, data integrity, security/privacy, failed money flows, abuse, and unexpected spend.

checks.heading: Preparedness and triage
checks.text: OO-INC-002: Identify declaration, incident lead, technical responders, communications, provider escalation, and decision authority; include backup and small-team coverage.

checks.heading: Preparedness and triage
checks.text: OO-INC-003: Maintain accessible runbooks for the critical failure modes in scope, including outage, backlog, disk full, provider failure, credential compromise, restore, payment drift, and spend spike.

checks.heading: Preparedness and triage
checks.text: OO-INC-004: Each runbook includes symptoms, impact checks, prerequisites/access, safe diagnostic steps, mitigation, stop conditions, recovery validation, escalation, and owner/review date.

checks.heading: Preparedness and triage
checks.text: OO-INC-005: Distinguish read-only diagnosis from actions that delete, replay, charge, restart, fail over, or expose data; include appropriate authorization and bounded execution.

checks.heading: Preparedness and triage
checks.text: OO-INC-006: Verify emergency documentation, contacts, credentials/recovery methods, and communication routes remain available during app/host/network/identity outage.

checks.heading: Preparedness and triage
checks.text: OO-INC-007: Triage using user impact, blast radius, time of onset, recent changes, evidence confidence, and ongoing harm; avoid assuming the first correlated deployment is the cause.

checks.heading: Preparedness and triage
checks.text: OO-INC-008: Separate confirmed facts, hypotheses, unknowns, and actions in a timestamped timeline; preserve relevant redacted evidence before destructive recovery steps.

checks.heading: Preparedness and triage
checks.text: OO-INC-009: Establish a working incident channel and decision log with access suited to the sensitivity and outage scenario; do not rely solely on the failing application.

checks.heading: Containment and recovery control
checks.text: OO-INC-010: Test scoped/global feature, account, traffic, integration, worker, and cost stop controls where needed; controls cover all relevant entry points and replicas.

checks.heading: Containment and recovery control
checks.text: OO-INC-011: Verify kill switches persist or revert according to an explicit policy across restart, rollback, failover, and configuration reconciliation; operators can confirm the actual state.

checks.heading: Containment and recovery control
checks.text: OO-INC-012: Check containment preserves recoverable user work and essential security/admin access while limiting harm; user messages reflect the temporary limitation.

checks.heading: Containment and recovery control
checks.text: OO-INC-013: Validate restart, scale, drain, rollback, failover, replay, and restore actions against dependencies and data invariants through the relevant specialist audits.

checks.heading: Containment and recovery control
checks.text: OO-INC-014: Prevent competing responders from making conflicting changes; record operator, time, reason, target, result, and reversal/compensation route for material actions.

checks.heading: Containment and recovery control
checks.text: OO-INC-015: Define when to stop investigation and mitigate ongoing harm, and when evidence preservation or irreversible consequences require specialist involvement.

checks.heading: Containment and recovery control
checks.text: OO-INC-016: For security/privacy incidents, use the security response and legal assessment path, including jurisdiction-specific notification review by accountable qualified people.

checks.heading: Containment and recovery control
checks.text: OO-INC-017: For financial/usage drift, reconcile authoritative state before replaying payments, refunds, provider work, or entitlement updates; route correctness to modules 08 and 13.

checks.heading: Containment and recovery control
checks.text: OO-INC-018: Verify controlled reopening after containment checks budgets, permissions, dependency health, backlog, and retry storms rather than simply re-enabling everything.

checks.heading: Customer and stakeholder communication
checks.text: OO-INC-019: Assign communication owner, audience, channel, update cadence, approval needs, and fallback; expectations fit impact and actual staffing.

checks.heading: Customer and stakeholder communication
checks.text: OO-INC-020: Keep an appropriate incident/status route reachable outside the application's failure domain; test update access during relevant identity/hosting failures.

checks.heading: Customer and stakeholder communication
checks.text: OO-INC-021: Communicate confirmed scope, symptoms, workarounds, current action, and next update time; estimates and unresolved causes are identified as uncertain.

checks.heading: Customer and stakeholder communication
checks.text: OO-INC-022: Avoid disclosing credentials, exploit details, unnecessary personal data, or unverified attribution in status pages, support scripts, and internal broad channels.

checks.heading: Customer and stakeholder communication
checks.text: OO-INC-023: Align customer support, sales/account teams, provider tickets, and public status so users receive consistent information without claiming recovery before validation.

checks.heading: Customer and stakeholder communication
checks.text: OO-INC-024: Distinguish service restored, backlog cleared, data reconciled, financial corrections complete, and incident closed; report residual effects honestly.

checks.heading: Review and continuous learning
checks.text: OO-INC-025: Define impact, detection, acknowledgement, mitigation, restoration, reconciliation, and closure times separately with timezone and evidence.

checks.heading: Review and continuous learning
checks.text: OO-INC-026: Review contributing conditions, safeguards that worked/failed, alternate explanations, and organizational constraints without reducing the cause to individual blame.

checks.heading: Review and continuous learning
checks.text: OO-INC-027: Assess missed/late detection, alert noise, permission gaps, runbook accuracy, communication, and recovery friction alongside the triggering technical defect.

checks.heading: Review and continuous learning
checks.text: OO-INC-028: Assign concrete prevention/detection/recovery actions with owner, due date, expected benefit, and observable acceptance; distinguish necessary fixes from speculative expansion.

checks.heading: Review and continuous learning
checks.text: OO-INC-029: Verify completed actions using focused evidence and update scenarios/runbooks; a written postmortem alone does not resolve recurring failure.

checks.heading: Review and continuous learning
checks.text: OO-INC-030: Track repeat incidents, near misses, customer impact, unresolved action age, and response workload; avoid comparing ambiguous response averages across unlike incident classes.

checks.heading: Review and continuous learning
checks.text: OO-INC-031: Rehearse representative incidents, including absent primary responder and unavailable collaboration/monitoring; record which steps were discussed versus actually executed.

checks.heading: Review and continuous learning
checks.text: OO-INC-032: Share appropriately redacted lessons, update ownership and training, and confirm accepted residual risks have an accountable expiry/review trigger.

checks.heading: Recovery objectives and readiness
checks.text: OO-REC-001: Define important failure scenarios, acceptable recovery time, acceptable data-loss window, scope, owner, and business rationale; distinguish targets from measured rehearsal results.

checks.heading: Recovery objectives and readiness
checks.text: OO-REC-002: Map recovery dependencies including identity, DNS, certificates, secret storage, artifacts, databases, object storage, queues, providers, documentation, and billing access.

checks.heading: Recovery objectives and readiness
checks.text: OO-REC-003: Record authoritative data sources and recovery order; restored application, cache, index, queue, and external state do not silently disagree.

checks.heading: Recovery objectives and readiness
checks.text: OO-REC-004: Identify single failure domains and necessary off-host/off-account/off-region copies proportionate to scoped risk; do not assume multiple regions are mandatory.

checks.heading: Recovery objectives and readiness
checks.text: OO-REC-005: Verify backup schedules, completion, age, size plausibility, retention, access, encryption/key availability, and failure alerts from actual operational evidence.

checks.heading: Recovery objectives and readiness
checks.text: OO-REC-006: Verify backups exclude unintended secrets or contain them only under approved handling; recovery credentials/keys are not available solely inside the failed system.

checks.heading: Recovery objectives and readiness
checks.text: OO-REC-007: Track the last successful restore rehearsal and what data/components it covered separately from the last successful backup run.

checks.heading: Recovery objectives and readiness
checks.text: OO-REC-008: Include configuration, infrastructure definitions, certificates, artifacts, object data, and provider/account recovery as applicable; database backup alone may omit the usable service.

checks.heading: Recovery objectives and readiness
checks.text: OO-REC-009: Check retention/cleanup failures, full backup destinations, expired access, missing encryption keys, and provider limits are detected before restoration is needed.

checks.heading: Recovery objectives and readiness
checks.text: OO-REC-010: Document replacement-environment prerequisites, permissions, capacity, runtime versions, connectivity, and expected cost before a major recovery.

checks.heading: Practical restore and failover
checks.text: OO-REC-011: Restore representative backups into an isolated environment and validate records, relationships, files, important user journeys, and data invariants through module 09.

checks.heading: Practical restore and failover
checks.text: OO-REC-012: Record restore start/end, operator involvement, dependencies, data-loss estimate, validation evidence, and deviations from the target.

checks.heading: Practical restore and failover
checks.text: OO-REC-013: Verify restored services do not unexpectedly email customers, charge providers, replay purchases, run legacy jobs, or expose copied production data.

checks.heading: Practical restore and failover
checks.text: OO-REC-014: Test relevant point-in-time recovery, corrupt/missing backup, interrupted restore, and unavailable primary operator using safe fixtures where these risks apply.

checks.heading: Practical restore and failover
checks.text: OO-REC-015: Confirm restored identities, secrets, permissions, configuration, and feature flags are valid and do not undo later revocation or containment decisions.

checks.heading: Practical restore and failover
checks.text: OO-REC-016: For failover, verify authoritative writer/traffic ownership, fencing or equivalent safeguards, replication lag, application routing, and split-brain prevention through specialist review.

checks.heading: Practical restore and failover
checks.text: OO-REC-017: Validate degraded-mode behavior and reduced capacity during failover; users and operators know what remains unavailable or stale.

checks.heading: Practical restore and failover
checks.text: OO-REC-018: Rehearse DNS/cache/connection propagation, certificate coverage, external allowlists, callback endpoints, and monitoring changes required by recovery/cutover.

checks.heading: Practical restore and failover
checks.text: OO-REC-019: Define failback criteria, data reconciliation, operator authority, and verification; returning to the original environment does not create competing active schedulers or writers.

checks.heading: Practical restore and failover
checks.text: OO-REC-020: Verify monitoring, alerting, backups, cost controls, and support access are active in the recovered environment before declaring normal operation.

checks.heading: Queues, replay, and external effects
checks.text: OO-REC-021: Diagnose backlog using oldest age, arrival/completion rate, retry state, dead letters, dependency limits, and per-tenant fairness rather than depth alone.

checks.heading: Queues, replay, and external effects
checks.text: OO-REC-022: Define pause/drain/resume controls, allowed concurrency, backpressure, processing order, and who may replay or delete work.

checks.heading: Queues, replay, and external effects
checks.text: OO-REC-023: Inspect replay candidates for current permissions, entitlement, quota, expiry, deletion, and user cancellation; stale queued work is not automatically still authorized.

checks.heading: Queues, replay, and external effects
checks.text: OO-REC-024: Check idempotency, duplicate detection, ordering, and external-outcome reconciliation before replay through reliability/integration/payment modules as applicable.

checks.heading: Queues, replay, and external effects
checks.text: OO-REC-025: Test recovery after timeout with unknown remote outcome; operators can reconcile provider state before repeating a charge, send, purchase, or costly generation.

checks.heading: Queues, replay, and external effects
checks.text: OO-REC-026: Bound replay by rate, concurrency, cost, scope, and stop conditions; recovery does not overwhelm dependencies, trigger abuse controls, or starve new critical work.

checks.heading: Queues, replay, and external effects
checks.text: OO-REC-027: Verify partial replay, poison messages, repeated failure, skipped items, and compensating actions are visible with item-level outcome/accountability.

checks.heading: Queues, replay, and external effects
checks.text: OO-REC-028: Reconcile restored database state with newer provider effects, emails, refunds, entitlements, search indexes, analytics, and retained exports where relevant.

checks.heading: Queues, replay, and external effects
checks.text: OO-REC-029: Confirm backlog cleared means expected useful work is completed/reconciled or explicitly abandoned, not simply that queue messages were deleted.

checks.heading: Queues, replay, and external effects
checks.text: OO-REC-030: Close recovery with validated service/data state, residual customer actions, removed temporary access/resources, updated runbooks, and a follow-up owner.

checks.heading: Account ownership and emergency access
checks.text: OO-GOV-001: Inventory domain/DNS, repositories, hosting, deployment, registries, database, monitoring, alerting, email, payments, billing, secrets, and other critical provider accounts.

checks.heading: Account ownership and emergency access
checks.text: OO-GOV-002: Verify organization-controlled ownership, renewal/payment routes, recovery contacts, and at least one authorized backup administrator where needed; avoid dependence on one person's private account.

checks.heading: Account ownership and emergency access
checks.text: OO-GOV-003: Map normal operator roles to least-privilege tasks and environments; staff can diagnose and mitigate without routine untracked full-access credentials.

checks.heading: Account ownership and emergency access
checks.text: OO-GOV-004: Verify strong authentication, scoped credentials, recovery factors, and revocation through security review; record access availability without copying secret values into the audit.

checks.heading: Account ownership and emergency access
checks.text: OO-GOV-005: Rehearse emergency/break-glass access with appropriate authorization, logging, scope, expiry, and post-use review; it does not become an unaudited bypass.

checks.heading: Account ownership and emergency access
checks.text: OO-GOV-006: Test access when the primary identity provider, operator laptop, password manager, network, or main phone is unavailable where these are material dependencies.

checks.heading: Account ownership and emergency access
checks.text: OO-GOV-007: Verify operator onboarding, role changes, departure, contract expiry, and dormant access removal include provider consoles, monitoring, paging, CI, SSH, secrets, and recovery contacts.

checks.heading: Account ownership and emergency access
checks.text: OO-GOV-008: Rehearse lost/stolen operator-device response: revoke sessions/keys/device access, assess exposed credentials, preserve appropriate evidence, and restore authorized access independently.

checks.heading: Account ownership and emergency access
checks.text: OO-GOV-009: Check administrative actions and access to sensitive telemetry are attributable and reviewable; shared accounts have documented necessity and compensating accountability where unavoidable.

checks.heading: Account ownership and emergency access
checks.text: OO-GOV-010: Verify account lockout, billing suspension, provider review, expired card, lost domain, and account compromise have an escalation/recovery path proportionate to risk.

checks.heading: Documentation and knowledge continuity
checks.text: OO-GOV-011: Maintain a concise service ownership map, architecture/dependency map, deployment route, known limits, runbooks, provider contacts, and escalation expectations.

checks.heading: Documentation and knowledge continuity
checks.text: OO-GOV-012: Keep authoritative documentation versioned or otherwise change-tracked, with owner and review trigger; secrets use approved storage references.

checks.heading: Documentation and knowledge continuity
checks.text: OO-GOV-013: Verify documentation remains reachable during the relevant host, application, identity, and collaboration-tool outage with suitable confidentiality controls.

checks.heading: Documentation and knowledge continuity
checks.text: OO-GOV-014: Have an authorized backup operator follow a critical runbook without relying on the primary person's laptop or undocumented memory; record actual friction.

checks.heading: Documentation and knowledge continuity
checks.text: OO-GOV-015: Identify essential manual fulfillment, data correction, renewal, reconciliation, and support steps; define absence cover and failure detection.

checks.heading: Documentation and knowledge continuity
checks.text: OO-GOV-016: Distinguish discussion/tabletop, tool walkthrough, staging execution, and production evidence in training and rehearsal records.

checks.heading: Maintenance and resource governance
checks.text: OO-GOV-017: Assign review/patch/renewal ownership for OS/runtime, dependencies, certificates/domains, licenses, provider changes, secrets, and operator devices as applicable.

checks.heading: Maintenance and resource governance
checks.text: OO-GOV-018: Maintain versioned/reproducible infrastructure and configuration or an equivalent proportionate record; detect material drift and reconcile intentional manual changes.

checks.heading: Maintenance and resource governance
checks.text: OO-GOV-019: Review recurring jobs and external automations for necessity, schedule, owner, timezone, duplicate instances, credentials, monitoring, and cost through module 08.

checks.heading: Maintenance and resource governance
checks.text: OO-GOV-020: Retire obsolete jobs/resources with dependency checks, residual queued-work handling, restart/redeploy/reconciliation checks, and billing confirmation before declaring completion.

checks.heading: Maintenance and resource governance
checks.text: OO-GOV-021: Verify temporary debug rules, incident access, maintenance silences, migration resources, preview environments, and emergency flags have owners and expiry/cleanup evidence.

checks.heading: Maintenance and resource governance
checks.text: OO-GOV-022: Record relevant provider commitments, support tier, service limits, planned changes, renewal dates, and escalation route; no contractual requirement is assumed universally.

checks.heading: Maintenance and resource governance
checks.text: OO-GOV-023: Confirm data/log retention, deletion, preservation, audit evidence, and incident notification obligations have accountable project reviewers through modules 01 and 11.

checks.heading: Maintenance and resource governance
checks.text: OO-GOV-024: Check provider portability/exit and company handover needs against actual risk, including data export, resource inventory, credentials, recovery, and financial obligations.

checks.heading: Operating review and assurance
checks.text: OO-GOV-025: Define a risk-appropriate operating cadence covering objective breaches, incidents, noisy/missing alerts, capacity, spend, access, maintenance, and recovery evidence.

checks.heading: Operating review and assurance
checks.text: OO-GOV-026: Track accepted remediation actions with owner, date, dependency, evidence-based acceptance, and focused recheck; aging tasks and accepted risks receive explicit review.

checks.heading: Operating review and assurance
checks.text: OO-GOV-027: Review responder workload, staffing coverage, manual toil, and recurring operational mistakes; prioritize changes that reduce real risk or repeated work.

checks.heading: Operating review and assurance
checks.text: OO-GOV-028: Validate automation before expanding privileges or removing human checks; manual fallback and failure detection remain proportionate to consequence.

checks.heading: Operating review and assurance
checks.text: OO-GOV-029: Distinguish operational control effectiveness from tool adoption, document count, dashboard count, or completed training; use demonstrated outcomes and limitations.

checks.heading: Operating review and assurance
checks.text: OO-GOV-030: Trigger focused reassessment after major release, migration, ownership/provider change, incidents, new markets, new data classes, or significant workload growth.

checks.heading: Detection and diagnosis
checks.text: Capture meaningful client, server, worker, scheduled-job, integration, and payment errors. Verify a controlled failure appears in the actual monitoring system.

checks.heading: Detection and diagnosis
checks.text: Use structured logs with request/job/event correlation, stage, timing, outcome, and release version. Redact credentials and unnecessary personal data; control log access, rotation, and retention.

checks.heading: Detection and diagnosis
checks.text: Measure traffic, error rates, representative latency percentiles, queue depth/age, processing success, job freshness, and dependency failures. Add CPU, RAM, disk/inodes, I/O, connection pool, and storage/egress signals for self-hosting.

checks.heading: Detection and diagnosis
checks.text: Run an external uptime monitor from outside the VPS's failure domain. Check an appropriate user-facing path; distinguish a running process from an app able to serve useful requests.

checks.heading: Detection and diagnosis
checks.text: Monitor backup age and restore evidence, certificate/domain expiry, webhook backlog, and scheduled-task completion. A job that never runs may produce no exception, so use freshness/dead-man signals.

checks.heading: Detection and diagnosis
checks.text: Route actionable alerts for availability, job failure, spend, abuse, capacity, and security changes. Define thresholds, deduplication, recipient, acknowledgment, and escalation. Test receipt.

checks.heading: Release and configuration
checks.text: Record deployed revision, image, runtime, migration state, and critical configuration. Keep staging/test/live credentials and resources distinguishable.

checks.heading: Release and configuration
checks.text: Verify required environment values and secure defaults. A missing credential or flag should not silently enable an unsafe fallback.

checks.heading: Release and configuration
checks.text: Document the build/deploy process, health checks, migration sequence, rollback limits, and post-deploy smoke checks. Verify a known working release can be recovered.

checks.heading: Release and configuration
checks.text: Keep security updates and dependency/OS patch responsibilities explicit. Monitor failed updates and reboot requirements; rehearse upgrades proportionately.

checks.heading: Release and configuration
checks.text: Confirm cron and workers run exactly as intended across replicas and old/new environments. Check ownership, idempotency, timezone, scheduling, and alerting.

checks.heading: Release and configuration
checks.text: Reconcile deployed schedulers and external automations with the [recurring-work and cost inventory](../../cost-quotas-and-abuse/Audit/08-Cost-Quotas-and-Abuse.md#required-discovery-of-recurring-work-and-hidden-spend). Identify undeclared, ownerless, duplicate, or obsolete jobs; do not assume repository configuration lists everything that is running.

checks.heading: Release and configuration
checks.text: Verify retired jobs stay disabled after restart, redeployment, and infrastructure reconciliation, including old environments and queue repeaters. Record residual queued work and billable resources; confirm usage/billing evidence under 08 before declaring the retirement complete.

checks.heading: Incident operation
checks.text: Maintain concise runbooks for outage, compromised key/account, payment drift, queue backlog, provider outage, disk-full, restore, and unexpected spend.

checks.heading: Incident operation
checks.text: Record operator access, emergency recovery, contacts, and where documentation remains available during a server outage. Avoid sole recovery copies inside the failed server.

checks.heading: Incident operation
checks.text: Provide controlled account suspension and feature/cost kill switches where needed. Audit administrative operations and prevent recovery controls becoming an unauthorized bypass.

checks.heading: Incident operation
checks.text: Define user communication and incident review responsibilities. Security/privacy incidents may require jurisdiction-specific notification assessment under 11.

checks.heading: Incident operation
checks.text: Verify service ownership and resource attribution on shared infrastructure. Operators should know which application caused a load spike and which others were affected.

checks.heading: Supportability and organizational continuity
checks.text: Group recurring errors and tune alert deduplication and escalation using real incident patterns. Trace a slow request across service boundaries where needed; correlate traces without spreading sensitive payloads.

checks.heading: Supportability and organizational continuity
checks.text: Name primary and backup responders with realistic availability and escalation expectations. Keep customer incident communication, including a status page where warranted, available when the application is down.

checks.heading: Supportability and organizational continuity
checks.text: Track incident review actions to owners, dates, and verification; confirm recurring failure modes lead to a change rather than only a written postmortem.

checks.heading: Supportability and organizational continuity
checks.text: Capture reproducible infrastructure/configuration in code or equivalent versioned automation, excluding secrets. Record intentional environment differences and detect drift between development, staging, and production.

checks.heading: Supportability and organizational continuity
checks.text: Rehearse automated rollback, feature-flag enablement/disablement, and deployment under traffic. Verify draining and schema compatibility; test zero-downtime behavior where promised rather than treating it as a universal requirement.

checks.heading: Supportability and organizational continuity
checks.text: Verify company-controlled ownership, billing, recovery, and at least one authorized backup administrator for domains, repositories, hosting, and critical provider accounts. Rehearse handover without relying on one person's laptop or memory.

checks.heading: Supportability and organizational continuity
checks.text: Rehearse a lost/stolen operator-device response: revoke sessions, keys, and device access, assess exposed production credentials, preserve appropriate evidence, and restore authorized operator access through a separate recovery path.

checks.heading: Hosting and runtime patterns
checks.text: OO-WRK-001: For a single VPS/shared host, test external useful-service detection, per-app resource attribution, host saturation, disk/inode exhaustion, provider-console access, restart ordering, and off-host recovery evidence.

checks.heading: Hosting and runtime patterns
checks.text: OO-WRK-002: For containers or Coolify-like platforms, verify desired versus actual deployment, image identity, crash/restart loops, health routing, persistent mounts, build failures, orphan containers, and platform-control-plane recovery.

checks.heading: Hosting and runtime patterns
checks.text: OO-WRK-003: For orchestrated clusters, verify scheduling/capacity failures, rollout health, service routing, node loss, storage attachment, workload identity, control-plane dependence, and version-compatible recovery as scoped.

checks.heading: Hosting and runtime patterns
checks.text: OO-WRK-004: For managed PaaS/serverless, check invocation failure, cold start, concurrency/timeout ceilings, throttling, region/provider incident, deployment drift, and logs that survive instance disappearance.

checks.heading: Hosting and runtime patterns
checks.text: OO-WRK-005: For edge/CDN/static hosting, verify DNS/TLS, cache/invalidations, stale assets, origin failure, edge/origin disagreement, geographic degradation, and an external useful-content probe.

checks.heading: Hosting and runtime patterns
checks.text: OO-WRK-006: For multi-region or redundant systems, verify traffic steering, data authority, replication lag, split-brain safeguards, regional capacity, failover/failback, and monitoring independence only to the promised level.

checks.heading: Background work and data systems
checks.text: OO-WRK-007: For scheduled jobs, test missed start, late finish, silent zero-output success, overlap, timezone/DST, disabled scheduler, duplicate replicas, old environment, and restart/redeployment resurrection.

checks.heading: Background work and data systems
checks.text: OO-WRK-008: For queues, verify oldest age, dead letters, poison message, lease/visibility expiry, worker crash, retry amplification, fairness, safe replay, and current authorization of stale work.

checks.heading: Background work and data systems
checks.text: OO-WRK-009: For batch/ETL/reporting, check input arrival, partition coverage, schema drift, partial completion, reconciliation, lineage, late data, idempotent rerun, and downstream freshness.

checks.heading: Background work and data systems
checks.text: OO-WRK-010: For databases, test operational detection/diagnosis of connection exhaustion, locks, slow queries, replica lag, full storage, failed migration, unavailable backup, and restore validation through module 09.

checks.heading: Background work and data systems
checks.text: OO-WRK-011: For caches/search indexes, check warm-up, rebuild, stale/incorrect results, lost keys, memory eviction, source-of-truth reconciliation, and dependency overload during a cold start.

checks.heading: Background work and data systems
checks.text: OO-WRK-012: For object/file storage, check missing mount/bucket, permission expiry, full capacity, lifecycle mistakes, orphan objects, corrupt/partial upload, download failures, and separate metadata/content recovery.

checks.heading: External integrations and money flows
checks.text: OO-WRK-013: For provider APIs, verify latency, rate limit, credential expiry, schema/error changes, quota depletion, partial outage, region failure, and ambiguous timeout using safe fixtures.

checks.heading: External integrations and money flows
checks.text: OO-WRK-014: For webhooks, check delivery/retry/backlog age, signature/configuration failure, duplicate/out-of-order events, endpoint migration, dead letters, and controlled replay through module 14.

checks.heading: External integrations and money flows
checks.text: OO-WRK-015: For email/SMS/push, distinguish requested, accepted, delivered where observable, bounced/rejected, delayed, and suppressed; verify destination cost, fan-out, preference, and retry-loop monitoring.

checks.heading: External integrations and money flows
checks.text: OO-WRK-016: For payments/entitlements, detect paid-but-no-access, access-without-payment, renewal drift, pending refunds, duplicate effects, delayed callbacks, and reconciliation gaps through module 13.

checks.heading: External integrations and money flows
checks.text: OO-WRK-017: For metered/credit products, detect reservation leaks, stale usage, reset errors, bill/product-unit mismatch, spend velocity, and failed/canceled work charged against policy through module 08.

checks.heading: External integrations and money flows
checks.text: OO-WRK-018: For marketplaces/fulfillment, distinguish payment, stock/capacity, order acceptance, provider action, payout, cancellation, and actual fulfillment; monitor stranded intermediate states.

checks.heading: AI, real-time, and client applications
checks.text: OO-WRK-019: For AI/agent workloads, correlate model/provider/version, tool stages, latency, useful completion, refusals, quality signals, token/tool cost, retries, and continuation budget without unnecessary sensitive payload logging.

checks.heading: AI, real-time, and client applications
checks.text: OO-WRK-020: Test AI provider outage, model retirement/change, malformed output, retrieval gaps, context limits, slow streaming, runaway loops, and costly fallback; monitor user outcome and enforce scoped stops through modules 07-08.

checks.heading: AI, real-time, and client applications
checks.text: OO-WRK-021: For AI tool execution, distinguish generated intention from authorized action and confirmed effect; detect partial execution, unknown external outcomes, duplicate tools, failed cancellation, and missing human handoff.

checks.heading: AI, real-time, and client applications
checks.text: OO-WRK-022: For streaming/WebSocket/realtime services, monitor connection establishment, reconnect storms, dropped/late/duplicate updates, stale presence, fan-out, backpressure, draining, and partial stream failure.

checks.heading: AI, real-time, and client applications
checks.text: OO-WRK-023: For browser/mobile/desktop clients, monitor crashes, unhandled failures, release mapping, supported-version distribution, startup, deep-link failures, and API incompatibility with approved privacy handling.

checks.heading: AI, real-time, and client applications
checks.text: OO-WRK-024: For offline/background clients, check delayed telemetry, sync backlog, local/cloud conflicts, logout/account switch, stale credentials, storage exhaustion, and restored connectivity without duplicate effects.

checks.heading: AI, real-time, and client applications
checks.text: OO-WRK-025: For media/games/connected devices, check only applicable playback/session/pairing/telemetry/progression/update paths, stale device state, firmware/client compatibility, and user-visible continuity under disconnection.

checks.heading: Cross-cutting failure scenarios
checks.text: OO-WRK-026: Test monitoring backend unavailable during application failure; operators retain an adequate independent detection/diagnosis route and recognize evidence gaps.

checks.heading: Cross-cutting failure scenarios
checks.text: OO-WRK-027: Test primary paging/communication or identity outage during an incident; fallback access, contacts, documentation, and status updates remain usable.

checks.heading: Cross-cutting failure scenarios
checks.text: OO-WRK-028: Test certificate/domain expiry, DNS misconfiguration, incorrect system time, expired license, and billing suspension detection for applicable dependencies.

checks.heading: Cross-cutting failure scenarios
checks.text: OO-WRK-029: Test noisy neighbor, traffic spike, abuse burst, costly retries, and telemetry explosion using bounded fixtures; containment protects other tenants/services and useful recovery capacity.

checks.heading: Cross-cutting failure scenarios
checks.text: OO-WRK-030: Test data leak/credential compromise indicators and emergency revocation through specialist security review; audit trails and independent access remain available appropriately.

checks.heading: Cross-cutting failure scenarios
checks.text: OO-WRK-031: Test restore/rollback while old workers/schedulers/providers are still active; prevent duplicate execution, competing writers, and resurrection of retired resources.

checks.heading: Cross-cutting failure scenarios
checks.text: OO-WRK-032: Test long quiet periods followed by peak usage: expired credentials, cold caches, dormant schedulers, depleted credits, and untested response coverage are detected.

checks.heading: Cross-cutting failure scenarios
checks.text: OO-WRK-033: Test maintenance silence expiry, forgotten kill switch, stale canary metrics, and incorrect environment labels; operational tooling does not conceal an ongoing outage.

checks.heading: Cross-cutting failure scenarios
checks.text: OO-WRK-034: Test a nominally successful service that produces wrong/empty/stale results; correctness/freshness signals detect failure without relying on an exception rate.

checks.heading: Cross-cutting failure scenarios
checks.text: OO-WRK-035: For sensitive/public-service contexts, align critical availability, assisted access, data handling, incident communication, and qualified review with project-specific obligations; generic checklist completion does not establish compliance.

checks.heading: Cross-cutting failure scenarios
checks.text: OO-WRK-036: For internal tools or low-volume services, verify manual fallback, accountable working-hours response, stale-work detection, and staff continuity proportionately; absence of enterprise tooling alone is not a defect.

checks.heading: Commercial and system inventory
checks.text: PE-SCP-001: Record product, release/configuration, environment, audit period/timezone, owner, decision needed, and evidence root; distinguish sandbox results from production evidence.

checks.heading: Commercial and system inventory
checks.text: PE-SCP-002: Inventory active plans, one-time purchases, subscriptions, trials, seats, metering, credits, discounts, invoices, refunds, disputes, payouts, and sales channels; exclude unsupported models with reasons.

checks.heading: Commercial and system inventory
checks.text: PE-SCP-003: Identify seller/merchant of record, payment processors, subscription/store platforms, connected accounts, currencies, settlement accounts, and responsibilities for each supported channel.

checks.heading: Commercial and system inventory
checks.text: PE-SCP-004: Record countries actually served, approved payment methods, customer types, tax treatment, invoice obligations, and reviewer-approved policies; do not assume a provider feature establishes obligations.

checks.heading: Commercial and system inventory
checks.text: PE-SCP-005: Map buyer, payer, account owner, beneficiary, billing admin, tenant admin, support, finance, and service-account roles; one person may not own all financial and access rights.

checks.heading: Commercial and system inventory
checks.text: PE-SCP-006: Inventory provider accounts, environment-specific credentials/secrets, prices/products, endpoints, subscribed events, API versions, schedulers, and manual billing actions.

checks.heading: Commercial and system inventory
checks.text: PE-SCP-007: Define sources of truth and relationships for checkout/order, payment attempt, authorization/capture, invoice, subscription, refund, dispute, credit, payout, and entitlement.

checks.heading: Commercial and system inventory
checks.text: PE-SCP-008: Define approved amount/currency/rounding rules, effective times, grace periods, cancellation/refund policies, credit expiry, and entitlement consequences before evaluating behavior.

checks.heading: Commercial and system inventory
checks.text: PE-SCP-009: Gather current checkout terms, pricing/help, contracts, consent/notice requirements, support policies, finance procedures, and incident records; surface contradictions.

checks.heading: Commercial and system inventory
checks.text: PE-SCP-010: Document external dependency and failure boundaries, including provider acknowledgement, asynchronous settlement, bank delays, delivery, reconciliation, and staff approvals.

checks.heading: Audit evidence and classification
checks.text: PE-SCP-011: Give each selected scenario reproducible preconditions, actor/tenant/plan, synthetic data, build/configuration, environment, timestamp/timezone, and method/tool/settings.

checks.heading: Audit evidence and classification
checks.text: PE-SCP-012: Capture expected and observed provider financial status, internal financial status, entitlement state, effective time, and side effects for each lifecycle scenario.

checks.heading: Audit evidence and classification
checks.text: PE-SCP-013: Distinguish source review, mocked fixtures, provider sandbox, deployed endpoint tests, and bounded production observation; do not claim one establishes another's correctness.

checks.heading: Audit evidence and classification
checks.text: PE-SCP-014: Verify persistent records and protected operations rather than relying on a success page, frontend badge, completed ticket, or callback response.

checks.heading: Audit evidence and classification
checks.text: PE-SCP-015: Record verified sample separately from potential affected customers/amounts/currencies; explain selection and estimation without summing unlike currencies as one amount.

checks.heading: Audit evidence and classification
checks.text: PE-SCP-016: Separate confirmed defects, verification gaps, policy ambiguities, and opportunities; unsupported financial models are not automatically missing requirements.

checks.heading: Audit evidence and classification
checks.text: PE-SCP-017: Deduplicate shared causes across payment, integration, reliability, security, product, and operations audits; retain all linked checks and one primary owner.

checks.heading: Audit evidence and classification
checks.text: PE-SCP-018: Assign defect severity, current exposure, confidence, delivery priority, and launch-blocker decision separately using realistic money/access/user impact.

checks.heading: Audit evidence and classification
checks.text: PE-SCP-019: Store redacted evidence with stable relative references and approved access/retention; exclude real card data, credentials, bank details, and unnecessary customer identifiers.

checks.heading: Audit evidence and classification
checks.text: PE-SCP-020: Reconcile selected statuses, exclusions, evidence gaps, findings, and owners; an unresolved critical boundary prevents a confident readiness conclusion.

checks.heading: Safe verification and dimensions
checks.text: PE-SCP-021: Use synthetic identities and provider-approved sandbox/test methods; bound verification by target, rate, cost, duration, cleanup, and stop conditions without accidental real charges/refunds.

checks.heading: Safe verification and dimensions
checks.text: PE-SCP-022: Select success, rejection, delayed/unknown outcome, duplicate/concurrent execution, cancellation, and recovery for every material money/access flow.

checks.heading: Safe verification and dimensions
checks.text: PE-SCP-023: Cover relevant intersections such as cancellation during retry, role revocation during checkout, refund during dispute, quota expiry during a job, and restore after external payment succeeded.

checks.heading: Safe verification and dimensions
checks.text: PE-SCP-024: Add incidents, provider-specific lifecycle cases, negotiated commitments, and market/channel-specific scenarios; expand coverage after inconsistent results.

checks.heading: Catalog and trusted calculation
checks.text: PE-PRI-001: Inventory versioned products/prices, currencies, intervals, quantities, eligibility, effective dates, and legacy mappings; identify the authoritative source and owner.

checks.heading: Catalog and trusted calculation
checks.text: PE-PRI-002: Derive payable product/price/currency and beneficiary account from trusted server-side rules; reject client-supplied amounts, unauthorized plan IDs, and tenant/customer substitution.

checks.heading: Catalog and trusted calculation
checks.text: PE-PRI-003: Verify disabled, archived, draft, expired, hidden, test, and other-channel prices cannot be purchased outside their approved eligibility.

checks.heading: Catalog and trusted calculation
checks.text: PE-PRI-004: Test zero, negative, fractional, minimum, maximum, and above-limit quantities according to product rules; billable seats/items are defined unambiguously.

checks.heading: Catalog and trusted calculation
checks.text: PE-PRI-005: Check per-unit, tiered, volume, graduated, minimum-commitment, package, and hybrid calculations only where offered, using approved worked examples.

checks.heading: Catalog and trusted calculation
checks.text: PE-PRI-006: Use integer minor units or an appropriate exact decimal representation for authoritative money, with documented conversion/precision boundaries rather than binary floating-point totals.

checks.heading: Catalog and trusted calculation
checks.text: PE-PRI-007: Verify supported currency exponents, amount limits, provider-specific charge/payout representations, and rounding rules against current exact-provider documentation.

checks.heading: Catalog and trusted calculation
checks.text: PE-PRI-008: Test line/subtotal/tax/discount/final rounding boundaries and aggregation order; displayed, authorized, captured, invoiced, refunded, and reported amounts reconcile.

checks.heading: Catalog and trusted calculation
checks.text: PE-PRI-009: Store amount and currency together; prohibit accidental currency substitution, cross-currency addition, and silent default currency changes.

checks.heading: Catalog and trusted calculation
checks.text: PE-PRI-010: Check localized currency symbols, decimal/grouping separators, units, billing interval, and tax-inclusive/exclusive presentation do not misrepresent the payable amount.

checks.heading: Offers and policy boundaries
checks.text: PE-PRI-011: Test coupon/promotion validity, scope, effective time, redemption limit, first-purchase eligibility, and account/tenant binding using server-side decisions.

checks.heading: Offers and policy boundaries
checks.text: PE-PRI-012: Check promotion stacking, usage retries, concurrent last redemption, invitation/referral loops, and canceled/failed purchase treatment against the approved rules.

checks.heading: Offers and policy boundaries
checks.text: PE-PRI-013: Verify introductory prices, expiring discounts, free periods, renewal rates, and negotiated changes are shown and applied at the intended time.

checks.heading: Offers and policy boundaries
checks.text: PE-PRI-014: Test legacy/grandfathered plans and migration opt-in/out where supported; current catalog updates do not silently rewrite existing commitments.

checks.heading: Offers and policy boundaries
checks.text: PE-PRI-015: Verify custom agreements, annual prepayment, minimum quantities, purchase orders, sales-assisted quotes, and quote expiry through their own approved purchase/access path.

checks.heading: Offers and policy boundaries
checks.text: PE-PRI-016: Check gift, referral, voucher, store-credit, and prepaid offers where present; distinguish promotional value from refundable customer payment and record restrictions.

checks.heading: Offers and policy boundaries
checks.text: PE-PRI-017: Define whether credits cover tax, usage, renewals, add-ons, and upgrades; preview and final invoice apply the same allocation rules.

checks.heading: Offers and policy boundaries
checks.text: PE-PRI-018: Test price changes while cart/quote/checkout is open; honor or refresh stale quotations according to explicit policy and require appropriate customer acknowledgement.

checks.heading: Offers and policy boundaries
checks.text: PE-PRI-019: Verify currency changes, exchange-rate source/time, conversion fees, settlement presentation, and refund currency behavior where supported; disclose estimates versus locked amounts.

checks.heading: Offers and policy boundaries
checks.text: PE-PRI-020: Verify shipping, service/platform fees, deposits, tips, surcharges, minimums, and optional add-ons only where offered; final totals reflect customer choices and approved disclosure.
