checks.heading: Tax, commitments, and truthful presentation
checks.text: PE-PRI-021: Record approved tax/VAT registrations, served destinations, product classification, collection responsibilities, exemptions, and invoice treatment with reviewer/source references under module 11.

checks.heading: Tax, commitments, and truthful presentation
checks.text: PE-PRI-022: Test representative supported customer locations, business/consumer status, tax identifiers, exempt cases, and invalid/missing address against those approved configurations.

checks.heading: Tax, commitments, and truthful presentation
checks.text: PE-PRI-023: Check tax-inclusive/exclusive prices, discounted taxable base, shipping/fee treatment, rounding, refund adjustments, and effective-date changes against approved examples.

checks.heading: Tax, commitments, and truthful presentation
checks.text: PE-PRI-024: Verify before commitment the recurring amount or calculation, interval, trial conversion, renewal, cancellation, and relevant limitations are clearly presented on each supported checkout surface.

checks.heading: Tax, commitments, and truthful presentation
checks.text: PE-PRI-025: Verify required affirmative consent and terms/version evidence for the applicable transaction/channel; route exact wording, placement, timing, and retention to module 11.

checks.heading: Tax, commitments, and truthful presentation
checks.text: PE-PRI-026: Check localized, mobile, embedded, accessible, and provider-hosted experiences show consistent terms and totals; truncated layouts do not hide material conditions.

checks.heading: Tax, commitments, and truthful presentation
checks.text: PE-PRI-027: Compare marketing/pricing/help, sales quotes, checkout, portal, notices, and invoices with actual enabled products and access; identify materially false promises.

checks.heading: Tax, commitments, and truthful presentation
checks.text: PE-PRI-028: Verify trial/free labels distinguish no-cost use, card collection, authorization holds, future conversion, and usage charges according to the actual offer.

checks.heading: Tax, commitments, and truthful presentation
checks.text: PE-PRI-029: Check minimum term, pause/cancellation effect, early termination, refund eligibility, and remaining prepaid value are understandable and enforced only as approved.

checks.heading: Tax, commitments, and truthful presentation
checks.text: PE-PRI-030: Keep catalog/policy changes attributable, reviewed proportionately, effective-dated, recoverable, and traceable to affected existing/future customers.

checks.heading: Tax, commitments, and truthful presentation
checks.text: PE-PRI-031: Test unsupported destinations/currencies/payment combinations fail clearly before an unintended commitment or charge, without silently switching to another priced offer.

checks.heading: Tax, commitments, and truthful presentation
checks.text: PE-PRI-032: Reconcile sample calculations with provider sandbox results and approved finance examples; missing configuration or expertise remains a verification/policy gap.

checks.heading: Session creation and identity
checks.text: PE-CHK-001: Bind checkout/session/order to the authorized buyer, beneficiary account/tenant, catalog version, amount, currency, quantity, and environment using trusted server state.

checks.heading: Session creation and identity
checks.text: PE-CHK-002: Test unauthorized buyer/billing roles, another tenant's customer/session/order, changed membership, and suspended accounts through direct operations as well as UI.

checks.heading: Session creation and identity
checks.text: PE-CHK-003: Check guest checkout, sign-in during checkout, account creation, wrong signed-in identity, payer-versus-beneficiary, and invite acceptance only where supported.

checks.heading: Session creation and identity
checks.text: PE-CHK-004: Validate return/cancel destinations and portal links against approved routing; prevent attacker-controlled redirects and cross-account financial-session access.

checks.heading: Session creation and identity
checks.text: PE-CHK-005: Verify stale, expired, completed, reused, and another browser's sessions cannot create an unintended second purchase or attach it to the wrong customer.

checks.heading: Session creation and identity
checks.text: PE-CHK-006: Test double click, two tabs/devices, retry after timeout, refresh, and simultaneous checkout creation; documented idempotency prevents unintended duplicate commitments.

checks.heading: Session creation and identity
checks.text: PE-CHK-007: Scope operation identity to intended business action and parameters; reusing an idempotency key with another purchase/customer is rejected or handled explicitly.

checks.heading: Session creation and identity
checks.text: PE-CHK-008: Test failure before provider request, after provider acceptance, before local commit, and before response; discover actual provider state before creating a new payment.

checks.heading: Session creation and identity
checks.text: PE-CHK-009: Verify cart/price/discount/tax changes between session creation and completion obey the declared quote validity and authorization rules.

checks.heading: Session creation and identity
checks.text: PE-CHK-010: Separate test/live keys, catalogs, customers, callbacks, domains, and resources; inspect actual deployment bindings without exposing secrets.

checks.heading: Payment-method lifecycle
checks.text: PE-CHK-011: Execute successful, declined, authentication-required, user-canceled, expired, and interrupted payment attempts for supported methods using provider fixtures.

checks.heading: Payment-method lifecycle
checks.text: PE-CHK-012: Test browser back, closed tab, missing redirect, lost network, and app restart during authentication; recover status from authoritative state without false success/failure.

checks.heading: Payment-method lifecycle
checks.text: PE-CHK-013: Distinguish pending, authorized, captured, settled, failed, and canceled statuses as relevant; do not equate authorization or asynchronous initiation with final collection.

checks.heading: Payment-method lifecycle
checks.text: PE-CHK-014: For separate authorization/capture, test partial capture, repeated capture, expiry, cancellation/void, adjusted amount, and failed capture against provider-supported rules.

checks.heading: Payment-method lifecycle
checks.text: PE-CHK-015: For delayed/bank/deferred methods, test late success/failure, expiry, cancellation availability, provisional access, and reversal according to the approved method policy.

checks.heading: Payment-method lifecycle
checks.text: PE-CHK-016: For saved methods, verify customer ownership, explicit permitted use, default selection, replacement, removal, expiry, and subsequent off-session action handling.

checks.heading: Payment-method lifecycle
checks.text: PE-CHK-017: Check wallets/local methods for supported device/browser/currency/market, fallback, authentication, and completion behavior; do not assume card semantics.

checks.heading: Payment-method lifecycle
checks.text: PE-CHK-018: Verify payment-method update flow does not accidentally create a new purchase, clear arrears, or grant entitlements without the required authoritative outcome.

checks.heading: Payment-method lifecycle
checks.text: PE-CHK-019: Verify receipts/order confirmations reflect actual state and amount; an accepted or pending payment is described truthfully.

checks.heading: Payment-method lifecycle
checks.text: PE-CHK-020: Ensure a success redirect, client callback, forged session reference, or screenshot cannot independently mark payment paid or grant access.

checks.heading: Data handling and abuse
checks.text: PE-CHK-021: Identify actual card/bank-data handling boundaries and qualified compliance ownership; verify prohibited data is absent from databases, logs, analytics, support tools, and AI prompts.

checks.heading: Data handling and abuse
checks.text: PE-CHK-022: Keep privileged keys server-side, restrict provider/admin access, and verify safe errors, credential rotation, and environment-specific signing secrets through security review.

checks.heading: Data handling and abuse
checks.text: PE-CHK-023: Check checkout/portal APIs, method-setup flows, payment-status lookups, and coupon checks for cross-tenant leaks, unauthorized changes, and enumeration.

checks.heading: Data handling and abuse
checks.text: PE-CHK-024: Apply proportionate rate/abuse controls to checkout creation, failed attempts, card-testing patterns, promotion redemption, and expensive provider calls without blocking legitimate recovery/accessibility users.

checks.heading: Data handling and abuse
checks.text: PE-CHK-025: Verify client scripts, embedded frames, payment-page configuration, CSP or equivalent controls, and change monitoring meet the project's reviewed collection model and obligations.

checks.heading: Data handling and abuse
checks.text: PE-CHK-026: Prevent secrets and unnecessary payment/customer details in URLs, referrers, browser storage, error reports, test fixtures, and support exports.

checks.heading: Data handling and abuse
checks.text: PE-CHK-027: Test supported checkout accessibility, localization, virtual keyboards, autofill, validation correction, and low-connectivity recovery without losing valid form context.

checks.heading: Fulfillment and unknown outcomes
checks.text: PE-CHK-028: Define when stock/capacity, order fulfillment, entitlement, receipt, and usage allocation occur relative to authoritative payment state; partial steps have recovery paths.

checks.heading: Fulfillment and unknown outcomes
checks.text: PE-CHK-029: Test payment success with local write/entitlement/delivery failure, and local order creation with payment failure; reconcile rather than silently losing paid value.

checks.heading: Fulfillment and unknown outcomes
checks.text: PE-CHK-030: Check repeated provider payment attempts map to one intended order or subscription according to policy; failed attempts are not counted as additional purchases.

checks.heading: Fulfillment and unknown outcomes
checks.text: PE-CHK-031: Test cancellation/expiry while payment is pending and a later success arrives; explicitly resolve money, fulfillment, access, and customer messaging.

checks.heading: Fulfillment and unknown outcomes
checks.text: PE-CHK-032: Verify operators/customers can distinguish pending/unknown from confirmed failure and can locate a safe diagnostic reference without initiating another charge unnecessarily.

checks.heading: Fulfillment and unknown outcomes
checks.text: PE-CHK-033: For live cutover, verify correct live endpoint, secrets, keys, price mappings, subscribed events, and safe rejection/receipt evidence without accidental real financial actions.

checks.heading: Fulfillment and unknown outcomes
checks.text: PE-CHK-034: Retain full sandbox lifecycle evidence including final provider/internal/access state and effective time, with replay confirming no extra charge or access transition.

checks.heading: Inbound trust and account binding
checks.text: PE-EVT-001: Inventory subscribed event types, endpoint/account/environment, payload/API versions, source objects, secrets, and business transitions they may trigger.

checks.heading: Inbound trust and account binding
checks.text: PE-EVT-002: Verify provider authentication/signature with the required original bytes and metadata before state changes; reject absent/invalid/altered signatures through the actual ingress path.

checks.heading: Inbound trust and account binding
checks.text: PE-EVT-003: Test wrong endpoint secret, test/live confusion, other provider/connected account, malformed payload, unsupported event version, and unexpected content type.

checks.heading: Inbound trust and account binding
checks.text: PE-EVT-004: Apply provider-supported timestamp/replay checks with documented clock handling and secret rotation; valid delivery retries remain distinguishable from unauthorized replay.

checks.heading: Inbound trust and account binding
checks.text: PE-EVT-005: Resolve provider customer/subscription/payment ownership to trusted internal records; untrusted event metadata does not create an arbitrary tenant entitlement.

checks.heading: Inbound trust and account binding
checks.text: PE-EVT-006: Check changed/deleted customers, merged accounts, reused emails, stale membership, and connected-account scope; historical financial identity remains correctly bound.

checks.heading: Inbound trust and account binding
checks.text: PE-EVT-007: Limit payload/work, isolate parsing errors, redact event evidence, and use least-privilege provider retrieval credentials through specialist security review.

checks.heading: Inbound trust and account binding
checks.text: PE-EVT-008: Unknown/unsubscribed event types are handled according to documented policy without enabling a default privileged state transition.

checks.heading: Durable receipt and effect identity
checks.text: PE-EVT-009: Define durable receipt, acknowledgement semantics, processing state, retry ownership, and observable completion/failure according to the provider contract.

checks.heading: Durable receipt and effect identity
checks.text: PE-EVT-010: Test crash before receipt commit, after receipt commit, after acknowledgement, during business updates, and after effect but before completion marker.

checks.heading: Durable receipt and effect identity
checks.text: PE-EVT-011: Persist event identity and attempt/processing state so a duplicate is distinguishable from a previously received event whose business operation failed.

checks.heading: Durable receipt and effect identity
checks.text: PE-EVT-012: Test sequential and concurrent duplicate deliveries to multiple replicas; one intended business effect occurs without relying on process-local memory.

checks.heading: Durable receipt and effect identity
checks.text: PE-EVT-013: Check distinct event IDs describing the same underlying business effect; event-level deduplication alone does not create duplicate credits, refunds, or entitlement grants.

checks.heading: Durable receipt and effect identity
checks.text: PE-EVT-014: Scope deduplication keys to provider/account/environment and effect as needed; unrelated events with coincident identifiers are not suppressed.

checks.heading: Durable receipt and effect identity
checks.text: PE-EVT-015: Use appropriate transactions/constraints or a recoverable workflow for inbox, financial record, entitlement/outbox, and completion marker; partial commits can be repaired.

checks.heading: Durable receipt and effect identity
checks.text: PE-EVT-016: Test idempotent outbound operations with stable business identity and immutable relevant parameters; retry after an ambiguous timeout reconciles actual provider outcome.

checks.heading: Durable receipt and effect identity
checks.text: PE-EVT-017: Document provider idempotency scope, retention, parameter mismatch, error caching, and concurrent-request behavior; local durable identity covers longer business replay windows where needed.

checks.heading: Durable receipt and effect identity
checks.text: PE-EVT-018: Check deduplication/retention cleanup does not permit harmful late replay or erase evidence still needed for reconciliation and approved retention.

checks.heading: Ordering and state transitions
checks.text: PE-EVT-019: Define allowed transitions separately for order, payment, invoice, subscription, refund, dispute, credit, and entitlement; reject or reconcile impossible transitions.

checks.heading: Ordering and state transitions
checks.text: PE-EVT-020: Test reordered create/update/paid/failed/cancel/refund events, including tied timestamps; creation timestamp alone is not assumed to be a unique ordering/version key.

checks.heading: Ordering and state transitions
checks.text: PE-EVT-021: Retrieve or reconcile authoritative current state where required; stale events cannot overwrite a newer paid/canceled/refunded or otherwise authoritative state.

checks.heading: Ordering and state transitions
checks.text: PE-EVT-022: Check an event for one invoice/period/payment attempt does not incorrectly change another period's subscription or account access.

checks.heading: Ordering and state transitions
checks.text: PE-EVT-023: Test events arriving before dependent records exist; defer/reconcile safely rather than dropping accepted work or creating unbound financial objects.

checks.heading: Ordering and state transitions
checks.text: PE-EVT-024: Test delayed success after cancellation, failed payment after later recovery, refund after downgrade, and dispute after account deletion against explicit policies.

checks.heading: Ordering and state transitions
checks.text: PE-EVT-025: Distinguish event observation time, provider object version/state, billing period, effective entitlement time, and processing time in records and diagnosis.

checks.heading: Ordering and state transitions
checks.text: PE-EVT-026: Check subscription active/trial state, invoice paid, charge succeeded, and entitlement eligible are not treated as interchangeable without the defined commercial rule.

checks.heading: Ordering and state transitions
checks.text: PE-EVT-027: Verify concurrent webhook, scheduled reconciler, customer portal, support override, and API actions cannot reverse newer state or duplicate effects.

checks.heading: Recovery, replay, and endpoint changes
checks.text: PE-EVT-028: Bound retries, backoff, provider calls, queue size, and dead-letter handling; accepted but failed work is visible with an accountable repair route.

checks.heading: Recovery, replay, and endpoint changes
checks.text: PE-EVT-029: Detect missing events and stale subscriptions/invoices/entitlements via reconciliation/freshness rather than reliance on one timely callback.

checks.heading: Recovery, replay, and endpoint changes
checks.text: PE-EVT-030: Provide authorized audited replay with preview/scope/rate/cost limits; reprocessing uses current business rules/effective-time policy and preserves deduplication.

checks.heading: Recovery, replay, and endpoint changes
checks.text: PE-EVT-031: Test provider endpoint outage, WAF/proxy/body transformation, disabled event subscription, rotated secret, and delivery backlog through real deployed routing where safely authorized.

checks.heading: Recovery, replay, and endpoint changes
checks.text: PE-EVT-032: Migrate endpoint/API version/secret with explicit overlap and old/new worker behavior; both routes do not independently apply the same effect twice.

checks.heading: Recovery, replay, and endpoint changes
checks.text: PE-EVT-033: Verify replay after deployment/rollback/database restore does not forget already completed provider effects; reconcile against external authoritative records.

checks.heading: Recovery, replay, and endpoint changes
checks.text: PE-EVT-034: Correlate provider event/request/object IDs with internal operation and entitlement IDs without unnecessarily retaining full sensitive payloads.

checks.heading: Recovery, replay, and endpoint changes
checks.text: PE-EVT-035: Measure oldest unprocessed age, failures/retries, dead letters, reconciliation drift, and missing expected transitions; test alert receipt and support diagnosis.

checks.heading: Recovery, replay, and endpoint changes
checks.text: PE-EVT-036: Retain executed valid/invalid, duplicate/concurrent, reordered, missing, and crash-recovery evidence with final financial/access states, not only webhook response codes.

checks.heading: Signup, trial, and first period
checks.text: PE-SUB-001: Define subscription identity, beneficiary, billing account, plan/version, interval, anchor/timezone, trial policy, and required authoritative outcome for activation.

checks.heading: Signup, trial, and first period
checks.text: PE-SUB-002: Test no-card and card-required trials only where offered, including eligibility, verification, initial grants, end time, conversion amount, and permitted cancellation.

checks.heading: Signup, trial, and first period
checks.text: PE-SUB-003: Check repeated signup, account merge, tenant switch, repeated trial, promotions, and manual trial extension against the declared eligibility rules without automatic penalties for legitimate shared users.

checks.heading: Signup, trial, and first period
checks.text: PE-SUB-004: Test trial expiry with no payment method, failed method, authentication required, delayed callback, and scheduler outage; final access matches policy at the effective deadline.

checks.heading: Signup, trial, and first period
checks.text: PE-SUB-005: Verify trial notices and conversion disclosures/consent for applicable markets/channels with qualified review under module 11; retain required evidence and detect delivery failure.

checks.heading: Signup, trial, and first period
checks.text: PE-SUB-006: Verify incomplete/abandoned first purchase, pending invoice, delayed payment, and failed initial collection do not create an unintended indefinitely active subscription.

checks.heading: Signup, trial, and first period
checks.text: PE-SUB-007: Test two simultaneous subscriptions/checkouts for the same intended account/product; supported multiple subscriptions are explicit and accidental duplicates are prevented/reconciled.

checks.heading: Signup, trial, and first period
checks.text: PE-SUB-008: Check annual/monthly/custom terms, billing anchor changes, short/long first periods, leap dates, month-end, DST, and relevant timezone boundaries.

checks.heading: Renewal, failure, and recovery
checks.text: PE-SUB-009: Test successful renewal with correct plan, quantity, tax, discount expiry, credits, period, and access; repeated events do not extend access twice.

checks.heading: Renewal, failure, and recovery
checks.text: PE-SUB-010: Test failed/off-session/authentication-required renewal, method update, retries, and late success; users receive an accurate actionable state.

checks.heading: Renewal, failure, and recovery
checks.text: PE-SUB-011: Define dunning cadence, retry ownership, grace duration, restriction, final expiry, and who can extend/reinstate; provider defaults do not silently define the product policy.

checks.heading: Renewal, failure, and recovery
checks.text: PE-SUB-012: Verify grace access and quota/storage rules before/at/after cutoff, including direct APIs, cached sessions, active exports, and previously queued work.

checks.heading: Renewal, failure, and recovery
checks.text: PE-SUB-013: Check failed delivery of payment-recovery notices, expired links, wrong billing recipient, account owner departure, and unavailable portal access; provide a supported recovery route.

checks.heading: Renewal, failure, and recovery
checks.text: PE-SUB-014: Test payment recovery before and after final expiry, including several overdue invoices; reconcile which periods/obligations were paid and which access should return.

checks.heading: Renewal, failure, and recovery
checks.text: PE-SUB-015: Verify canceling or removing a payment method does not automatically erase an existing amount owed or initiate an unintended new billing attempt contrary to policy.

checks.heading: Renewal, failure, and recovery
checks.text: PE-SUB-016: Check price changes, expiring discounts, increased seats, changed usage rates, and annual renewal notices against approved effective dates and required notice/consent.

checks.heading: Renewal, failure, and recovery
checks.text: PE-SUB-017: Reconcile invoice/payment state with subscription state so an old failed attempt cannot revoke access after a later authoritative recovery.

checks.heading: Plan and quantity changes
checks.text: PE-SUB-018: Test immediate versus scheduled upgrade/downgrade, preview, effective date, payment requirement, access transition, and unused-value treatment.

checks.heading: Plan and quantity changes
checks.text: PE-SUB-019: Verify proration rules for interval, price, seat, credit, and mid-period changes using approved examples; unpaid time is not credited or charged incorrectly.

checks.heading: Plan and quantity changes
checks.text: PE-SUB-020: Test failed/authentication-required upgrade payment and rollback/retention of prior access; do not silently grant unpaid premium capability or destroy paid baseline access.

checks.heading: Plan and quantity changes
checks.text: PE-SUB-021: Check downgrade below current seats/storage/usage, including grace, read-only, deletion/export, excess-member handling, and future work according to policy.

checks.heading: Plan and quantity changes
checks.text: PE-SUB-022: Test simultaneous plan/quantity changes, stale previews, repeated submissions, customer-portal updates, and support changes; resulting billing and access reconcile.

checks.heading: Plan and quantity changes
checks.text: PE-SUB-023: Verify pending/scheduled changes can be inspected, amended, or canceled as promised; old schedules do not override a newer accepted change.

checks.heading: Plan and quantity changes
checks.text: PE-SUB-024: Check adding/removing seats, invited/inactive members, minimum seat count, owner transfer, and billing-admin changes against the billable-seat definition.

checks.heading: Plan and quantity changes
checks.text: PE-SUB-025: Test add-on dependencies, multiple products/intervals, bundled allowances, and removal order where supported; access is not derived solely from a single plan string.

checks.heading: Plan and quantity changes
checks.text: PE-SUB-026: Verify currency, merchant/provider, store/channel, or legacy-plan transitions use an explicit supported migration path without duplicate renewal or lost paid time.

checks.heading: Pause, cancellation, and reactivation
checks.text: PE-SUB-027: Test pause/resume collection versus pause/resume service only where supported; charges, entitlement, accumulated usage, and next period follow the distinct policy.

checks.heading: Pause, cancellation, and reactivation
checks.text: PE-SUB-028: Verify immediate and period-end cancellation, effective time, last access date, remaining invoices, refunds, and queued changes against the accepted terms.

checks.heading: Pause, cancellation, and reactivation
checks.text: PE-SUB-029: Test required online cancellation routes from all supported platforms, roles, locales, and failed-payment states; avoid unexplained dead ends or hidden extra commitments.

checks.heading: Pause, cancellation, and reactivation
checks.text: PE-SUB-030: Check cancellation confirmation, renewal date removal/update, required acknowledgement, and notices reflect authoritative state even with delayed/missing callbacks.

checks.heading: Pause, cancellation, and reactivation
checks.text: PE-SUB-031: Test cancellation during renewal, retry, pending upgrade, trial conversion, and an already initiated delayed payment; resolve final money/access/notice states explicitly.

checks.heading: Pause, cancellation, and reactivation
checks.text: PE-SUB-032: Verify undo-cancellation/reactivation before period end and resubscription after expiry; prevent duplicate subscriptions, reset-abuse, or silent loss of promised remaining access.

checks.heading: Pause, cancellation, and reactivation
checks.text: PE-SUB-033: Check account deletion versus subscription cancellation and payer/beneficiary separation; the user understands which financial obligations and retained records remain.

checks.heading: Pause, cancellation, and reactivation
checks.text: PE-SUB-034: Verify canceled/expired access is enforced when webhook or scheduler fails through reconciler/freshness checks and direct protected-operation tests.

checks.heading: Pause, cancellation, and reactivation
checks.text: PE-SUB-035: Test restoration of canceled/deleted customer records, provider reactivation, and database restore; old schedules and saved methods do not unexpectedly resume charging.

checks.heading: Pause, cancellation, and reactivation
checks.text: PE-SUB-036: Verify manual subscription/trial overrides have explicit reason, scope, actor, effective/expiry time, review, and interaction with future automatic transitions.

checks.heading: Pause, cancellation, and reactivation
checks.text: PE-SUB-037: Reconcile customer portal, UI, API, invoice, provider, notices, and support views for plan, period, cancellation, arrears, and future amount.

checks.heading: Pause, cancellation, and reactivation
checks.text: PE-SUB-038: Execute full sandbox trial/renewal/failure/cancel/reactivation scenarios with final provider, internal financial, entitlement, and effective-time evidence plus safe event replay.

checks.heading: Entitlement model
checks.text: PE-ENT-001: Inventory features, roles, products, plans, add-ons, seats, limits, flags, licenses, and entitlement sources; document the authoritative rule and beneficiary scope.

checks.heading: Entitlement model
checks.text: PE-ENT-002: Define trial, pending, paid, grace, scheduled-cancel, expired, refunded, disputed, suspended, manual, and promotional eligibility separately where applicable.

checks.heading: Entitlement model
checks.text: PE-ENT-003: Record entitlement start/end/effective time and timezone, source financial object, policy version, reason, actor, and superseding transition.

checks.heading: Entitlement model
checks.text: PE-ENT-004: Define precedence among payment, trial, manual override, bundle, multiple subscriptions, organization membership, and suspension; conflicts have deterministic policy.

checks.heading: Entitlement model
checks.text: PE-ENT-005: Distinguish payer, purchaser, assigned user, tenant owner, and current membership; purchase evidence alone does not authorize access to another tenant's resources.

checks.heading: Entitlement model
checks.text: PE-ENT-006: Define read/create/edit/export/download/costly processing separately, including retained work after downgrade/expiry and permitted correction/export routes.

checks.heading: Entitlement model
checks.text: PE-ENT-007: Verify grants and revocations are idempotent and attributable; one payment/event cannot extend a fixed license twice or duplicate an allowance.

checks.heading: Entitlement model
checks.text: PE-ENT-008: Check legacy plans, custom contracts, grandfathered allowances, and add-on dependencies against explicit mappings rather than arbitrary display names.

checks.heading: Server and client boundaries
checks.text: PE-ENT-009: Test allowed and denied direct server/API operations for protected features, not just hidden navigation or disabled buttons.

checks.heading: Server and client boundaries
checks.text: PE-ENT-010: Enforce relevant entitlement on workers, scheduled tasks, exports/imports, batch/bulk actions, integrations, and costly provider calls.

checks.heading: Server and client boundaries
checks.text: PE-ENT-011: Test another tenant/user/subscription/customer/license ID, stale role, suspended membership, and guest paths through the actual protected operations.

checks.heading: Server and client boundaries
checks.text: PE-ENT-012: Verify client-controlled role/plan flags, local storage, unsigned metadata, success redirects, and arbitrary headers cannot grant paid access.

checks.heading: Server and client boundaries
checks.text: PE-ENT-013: Check caches, JWT/session claims, replicas, edge authorization, and client refresh do not retain access beyond the documented revocation window.

checks.heading: Server and client boundaries
checks.text: PE-ENT-014: Test access immediately before/at/after trial, period, grace, credit, invite, and manual-override expiry; missing callbacks do not indefinitely preserve access.

checks.heading: Server and client boundaries
checks.text: PE-ENT-015: Verify entitlement-service/provider outage policy is explicit for reads, writes, and expensive work; fail-open/fail-closed choices match consequence and approved risk.

checks.heading: Server and client boundaries
checks.text: PE-ENT-016: Check partial propagation, conflicting caches, unavailable primary database, and stale replica; user feedback reflects actual access state rather than silently inconsistent clients.

checks.heading: Server and client boundaries
checks.text: PE-ENT-017: Test pre-signed downloads, shared links, streaming sessions, device/offline licenses, and persistent sockets for their documented revocation/expiry limits where supported.

checks.heading: Server and client boundaries
checks.text: PE-ENT-018: Revalidate queued/in-flight work after role, subscription, quota, or ownership changes according to policy; cancellation/compensation handles work already externally committed.

checks.heading: Seats, licenses, and transitions
checks.text: PE-ENT-019: Test invitation, assignment, reassignment, removal, inactive users, concurrent assignment, and seat reduction against supported seat/license rules.

checks.heading: Seats, licenses, and transitions
checks.text: PE-ENT-020: Check last-owner departure, billing-admin replacement, account merge, organization transfer/split, and domain-managed membership only where supported.

checks.heading: Seats, licenses, and transitions
checks.text: PE-ENT-021: Verify multiple workspaces/organizations do not accidentally share private paid allowances or evade user/account-scoped limits through switching.

checks.heading: Seats, licenses, and transitions
checks.text: PE-ENT-022: For device/concurrent-use licenses, test activation, deactivation, device replacement/loss, offline period, clock change, and concurrent sessions within the supported policy.

checks.heading: Seats, licenses, and transitions
checks.text: PE-ENT-023: Test upgrade grant with failed local write, delayed event, failed payment, and retry; reconcile paid-but-no-access and access-without-required-payment.

checks.heading: Seats, licenses, and transitions
checks.text: PE-ENT-024: Test downgrade/expiry beyond current storage/seats/usage; preserve, restrict, migrate, or delete only according to documented policy with appropriate notices.

checks.heading: Seats, licenses, and transitions
checks.text: PE-ENT-025: Verify partial refund, full refund, dispute, charge reversal, and dispute win affect only the intended products/periods/beneficiaries under policy.

checks.heading: Seats, licenses, and transitions
checks.text: PE-ENT-026: Test reinstatement after payment recovery, dispute resolution, manual correction, and erroneous revocation; avoid granting another reset or bonus unless intended.

checks.heading: Seats, licenses, and transitions
checks.text: PE-ENT-027: Check complimentary/support/test accounts and employee access have clear production eligibility, scope, cost controls, owner, expiry, and audit history.

checks.heading: Seats, licenses, and transitions
checks.text: PE-ENT-028: Verify gift/transfer/resale/bundle/sponsored access where offered, including redemption/revocation and payer-versus-recipient refund consequences.

checks.heading: Reconciliation and support
checks.text: PE-ENT-029: Reconcile entitlement state against authoritative current financial/contract state on a risk-appropriate schedule and after missed events/incidents.

checks.heading: Reconciliation and support
checks.text: PE-ENT-030: Detect stale grants/revocations, dangling licenses, missing effective dates, and orphaned entitlement sources; repairs are scoped, idempotent, and auditable.

checks.heading: Reconciliation and support
checks.text: PE-ENT-031: Provide authorized support an explanation of why access is allowed/denied and the relevant effective times without exposing unnecessary financial or other-tenant data.

checks.heading: Reconciliation and support
checks.text: PE-ENT-032: Require authorization, reason, scope, expiry, and audit evidence for manual access overrides; later reconciliation follows explicit precedence rather than unpredictably undoing or extending them.

checks.heading: Reconciliation and support
checks.text: PE-ENT-033: Verify restore/migration/rollback does not resurrect revoked rights, lose paid grants, forget manual overrides, or re-enable retired entitlements without reconciliation.

checks.heading: Reconciliation and support
checks.text: PE-ENT-034: Ensure denied users get truthful next steps distinguishing permission, plan, payment, quota, and temporary state; an upsell is not shown when purchase cannot fix the denial.

checks.heading: Reconciliation and support
checks.text: PE-ENT-035: Test end-to-end allowed/denied operations for every critical paid capability and meaningful transition, recording provider/internal/access state and actual persisted effects.

checks.heading: Reconciliation and support
checks.text: PE-ENT-036: Monitor entitlement drift and support recurrence with accountable alerts, repair procedures, and focused verification; do not declare alignment merely because one dashboard is green.

checks.heading: Units and ledger contract
checks.text: PE-USG-001: Define billable unit, measurement source, precision, aggregation, rounding, period/timezone, minimums, included usage, overage, and attribution to payer/tenant/product.

checks.heading: Units and ledger contract
checks.text: PE-USG-002: Specify when work is reserved, consumed, billed, released, refunded, or corrected; distinguish requested, accepted, completed, partially successful, and failed work.

checks.heading: Units and ledger contract
checks.text: PE-USG-003: Define balance categories, currency/product units, purchased/promotional origin, expiry, refund eligibility, transferability, and consumption priority.

checks.heading: Units and ledger contract
checks.text: PE-USG-004: Record immutable or appropriately auditable ledger movements with operation identity, source, amount/unit, effective time, reason, actor, and reversal reference.

checks.heading: Units and ledger contract
checks.text: PE-USG-005: Verify displayed and available balance reconcile with grants, consumption, reservations, expiry, corrections, and reversals; a cached total is not the only evidence.

checks.heading: Units and ledger contract
checks.text: PE-USG-006: Use exact supported unit/money precision and boundary rules; prevent accidental fractional truncation, negative quantities, overflow, and currency/unit confusion.

checks.heading: Units and ledger contract
checks.text: PE-USG-007: Bind usage/balance operations to trusted customer/tenant ownership and permitted product; reject client-supplied price multipliers or another account's ledger IDs.

checks.heading: Units and ledger contract
checks.text: PE-USG-008: Define authoritative source and repair policy when provider metering, internal events, and completed work disagree; retain versioned definitions for past billing periods.

checks.heading: Reservation, concurrency, and failures
checks.text: PE-USG-009: Test zero, near, exact, and above available balance/quota, including simultaneous requests across replicas; spending/reservation follows the approved overspend policy.

checks.heading: Reservation, concurrency, and failures
checks.text: PE-USG-010: Check reservation timeout, worker crash, late worker, retry, cancel, and abandoned sessions; reserved value is neither leaked forever nor released while the committed effect is still possible.

checks.heading: Reservation, concurrency, and failures
checks.text: PE-USG-011: Test failure before provider effect, timeout with unknown effect, partial success, and success followed by local write failure; reconcile before refunding or repeating work.

checks.heading: Reservation, concurrency, and failures
checks.text: PE-USG-012: Verify repeated requests, duplicated usage events, webhook replay, and concurrent finalization apply one intended debit/grant/correction.

checks.heading: Reservation, concurrency, and failures
checks.text: PE-USG-013: Check failed-request, retry, moderation/refusal, empty-output, canceled-job, and provider-error charging against the declared rule rather than an assumed universal free/fair policy.

checks.heading: Reservation, concurrency, and failures
checks.text: PE-USG-014: Handle correction/refund after reservation expiry or account closure without creating duplicate value, untracked negative balance, or a new unrelated grant.

checks.heading: Reservation, concurrency, and failures
checks.text: PE-USG-015: Test late/out-of-order usage and effective event time versus receipt time across reset, renewal, plan change, and invoice finalization boundaries.

checks.heading: Reservation, concurrency, and failures
checks.text: PE-USG-016: Verify backlog processing rechecks current entitlement/budget when required and attributes usage to the intended period/policy instead of whichever price is current at retry.

checks.heading: Grants, expiry, and top-ups
checks.text: PE-USG-017: Test included monthly/annual grants, rollover, caps, resets, carryover, and unused-value treatment as offered; period transition does not grant twice.

checks.heading: Grants, expiry, and top-ups
checks.text: PE-USG-018: Check upgrade/downgrade/trial/cancellation effects on included balances, prior purchases, and pending reservations with approved examples.

checks.heading: Grants, expiry, and top-ups
checks.text: PE-USG-019: Verify purchased top-up is granted only after the required authoritative payment state; failed/pending/duplicate purchases do not create spendable value incorrectly.

checks.heading: Grants, expiry, and top-ups
checks.text: PE-USG-020: Test partial/full top-up refund and dispute after some value has been consumed; resulting balance/access and recoverable value follow explicit policy.

checks.heading: Grants, expiry, and top-ups
checks.text: PE-USG-021: Check promotional/referral/support grants for eligibility, amount caps, redemption limits, expiry, attribution, and audit evidence.

checks.heading: Grants, expiry, and top-ups
checks.text: PE-USG-022: Test expiry before/at/after cutoff, timezone changes, oldest/earliest-expiring consumption order, held reservations, and late adjustments where supported.

checks.heading: Grants, expiry, and top-ups
checks.text: PE-USG-023: Verify automated top-up threshold, maximum amount/frequency, affirmative setup, duplicate prevention, failed charge, cancellation, and notification as applicable.

checks.heading: Grants, expiry, and top-ups
checks.text: PE-USG-024: Check mixed purchased/promotional balances, multiple units, bundle limits, and restricted credits cannot be incorrectly exchanged for cash or an ineligible product.

checks.heading: Grants, expiry, and top-ups
checks.text: PE-USG-025: Test transfer/gifting/sharing/pooling only where offered, including concurrent spend, revocation, membership changes, and correct payer attribution.

checks.heading: Grants, expiry, and top-ups
checks.text: PE-USG-026: Verify billing-method update, restore, key rotation, account merge, and tenant switching do not reset spent usage or regenerate consumed promotional value.

checks.heading: Invoices, reporting, and correction
checks.text: PE-USG-027: Reconcile measured events to billable aggregates, invoice line quantities/rates, provider usage submissions, internal ledger, and finance exports.

checks.heading: Invoices, reporting, and correction
checks.text: PE-USG-028: Check duplicate provider meter submissions, corrections, delayed acceptance, rejection, and unknown outcome; external idempotency/retention limits are documented.

checks.heading: Invoices, reporting, and correction
checks.text: PE-USG-029: Test backdated correction after finalized invoice/payment, including approved credit note or next-period adjustment; historical totals are not silently rewritten without trace.

checks.heading: Invoices, reporting, and correction
checks.text: PE-USG-030: Expose customer-appropriate usage/balance history, units, freshness, reserved amounts, resets, and explanations; unknown or delayed usage is not shown as guaranteed zero.

checks.heading: Invoices, reporting, and correction
checks.text: PE-USG-031: Restrict support balance changes with reason, source, bounds, expiry/reversal where relevant, and independent review proportionate to value.

checks.heading: Invoices, reporting, and correction
checks.text: PE-USG-032: Detect ledger invariant violations, unexpected negative balances, missing releases, unexplained grants, stale meters, and invoice mismatches with an accountable repair route.

checks.heading: Invoices, reporting, and correction
checks.text: PE-USG-033: Reconcile balances and already completed external work after backup restore, migration, replay, and pricing-version changes; purchased value and prior debits are preserved.

checks.heading: Invoices, reporting, and correction
checks.text: PE-USG-034: Execute a complete synthetic purchase/grant/reserve/consume/fail/correct/expire/refund cycle for supported paths, recording ledger, invoice, provider, and access outcomes.

checks.heading: Refund eligibility and authorization
checks.text: PE-REF-001: Define refund eligibility, amount basis, currency, time window, original payment/line, refundable balance, tax/fee treatment, owner, and entitlement consequence.

checks.heading: Refund eligibility and authorization
checks.text: PE-REF-002: Separate customer-requested, support-issued, automatic, provider-initiated, partial, and full refunds; each uses an authorized supported workflow.

checks.heading: Refund eligibility and authorization
checks.text: PE-REF-003: Verify another tenant/order/payment/customer ID, unauthorized support role, and client-supplied refund amount cannot create or redirect a refund.

checks.heading: Refund eligibility and authorization
checks.text: PE-REF-004: Check cumulative partial refunds, simultaneous requests, and the final refundable amount; prevent unintended over-refund across provider and internal channels.

checks.heading: Refund eligibility and authorization
checks.text: PE-REF-005: Test zero/negative/above-remaining amounts, currency mismatch, uncaptured authorization, pending method, and ineligible payment type with clear rejection/alternative handling.

checks.heading: Refund eligibility and authorization
checks.text: PE-REF-006: Record refund reason, source order/payment/line, actor, approval where required, business identity, requested amount, and current result without unnecessary sensitive data.

checks.heading: Refund eligibility and authorization
checks.text: PE-REF-007: Verify customer support cannot bypass refund limits or independently edit authoritative paid/refunded totals without traceable corrective movements.

checks.heading: Refund eligibility and authorization
checks.text: PE-REF-008: Clarify whether refund cancels future renewals, removes access, restores credits/stock, or affects a beneficiary; perform only the intended related changes.

checks.heading: Execution and lifecycle
checks.text: PE-REF-009: Test refund success, pending, failed, canceled/returned where supported, provider rejection, insufficient merchant funds, and delayed final result using approved fixtures.

checks.heading: Execution and lifecycle
checks.text: PE-REF-010: Handle timeout after provider acceptance by lookup/reconciliation and stable idempotency; retry does not initiate a second refund.

checks.heading: Execution and lifecycle
checks.text: PE-REF-011: Test crash before/after provider effect, internal ledger update, entitlement change, and response; all accepted work has a durable repair path.

checks.heading: Execution and lifecycle
checks.text: PE-REF-012: Replay duplicate/concurrent/out-of-order refund events and operator requests; final refunded amount, balance, and access change only once per intended effect.

checks.heading: Execution and lifecycle
checks.text: PE-REF-013: Verify a requested refund is not presented as completed before the required authoritative status; distinguish merchant action from customer bank posting where relevant.

checks.heading: Execution and lifecycle
checks.text: PE-REF-014: Test full versus line/quantity/partial-period refunds against discounts, tax, shipping/fees, consumed credits, proration, and earlier adjustments using approved examples.

checks.heading: Execution and lifecycle
checks.text: PE-REF-015: Check multiple payment attempts, split tender, installment/deferred methods, and multiple currencies only where supported; refund maps to the correct original transaction.

checks.heading: Execution and lifecycle
checks.text: PE-REF-016: Verify receipt/credit-note/customer notice, invoice status, finance export, and provider totals reflect final state and effective time; failure notices remain actionable.

checks.heading: Execution and lifecycle
checks.text: PE-REF-017: Check account deletion, payer-versus-beneficiary, removed member, and legacy/migrated order do not make a valid correction impossible or disclose another party's data.

checks.heading: Execution and lifecycle
checks.text: PE-REF-018: Ensure refund reversal/failure restores any previously provisional internal change only according to explicit policy, not by blindly regranting access or duplicating value.

checks.heading: Disputes and other reversals
checks.text: PE-REF-019: Define dispute/chargeback/inquiry, response deadline, accountable owner, evidence source, privacy controls, and escalation for supported payment methods.

checks.heading: Disputes and other reversals
checks.text: PE-REF-020: Test dispute opened, updated, won, lost, withdrawn/reversed where supported, and delayed notice; provider/internal financial/access states remain distinguishable.

checks.heading: Disputes and other reversals
checks.text: PE-REF-021: Verify provisional versus final funds movement, dispute fees, reserves, and settlement adjustments are represented in reconciliation rather than treated as ordinary sales/refunds.

checks.heading: Disputes and other reversals
checks.text: PE-REF-022: Check dispute after partial/full refund, refund during dispute, duplicate dispute events, and later reversal; avoid returning the same value through two channels.

checks.heading: Disputes and other reversals
checks.text: PE-REF-023: Test authorized access suspension, retention, and reinstatement under dispute policy; do not equate every inquiry or provisional state with final fraud/loss.

checks.heading: Disputes and other reversals
checks.text: PE-REF-024: Verify evidence submission, deadline tracking, file access, correct case binding, and review accountability; automated tools do not fabricate documents or customer consent.

checks.heading: Disputes and other reversals
checks.text: PE-REF-025: For bank returns/payment reversals, test delayed failure after provisional success, spent credits/fulfilled goods, negative balance policy, and customer remediation.

checks.heading: Disputes and other reversals
checks.text: PE-REF-026: For canceled/expired authorizations, distinguish releasing a hold from refunding captured money; customer/internal descriptions match the actual operation.

checks.heading: Reconciliation and closure
checks.text: PE-REF-027: Reconcile refunds, credit notes, ledger reversals, dispute adjustments, fees, and payouts to original payments/orders and approved reports.

checks.heading: Reconciliation and closure
checks.text: PE-REF-028: Monitor pending/stuck refunds, approaching dispute deadlines, failed notifications, cumulative anomalies, and unresolved entitlement drift with tested alert receipt.

checks.heading: Reconciliation and closure
checks.text: PE-REF-029: Provide customers/support a safe status/history with amount/currency, action date, current state, and next step without guaranteeing unsupported bank timing.

checks.heading: Reconciliation and closure
checks.text: PE-REF-030: Reconcile restore/replay/migration against provider refund/dispute history before allowing another correction or reinstating access.

checks.heading: Reconciliation and closure
checks.text: PE-REF-031: Verify risk controls for repeated refund/cancel/promotion loops proportionately, with legitimate correction and appeal paths and documented false-positive handling.

checks.heading: Reconciliation and closure
checks.text: PE-REF-032: Execute complete sandbox refund/failure/dispute/reinstatement scenarios where supported and replay relevant events; retain final provider/internal/balance/access evidence.

checks.heading: Invoice lifecycle and identity
checks.text: PE-FIN-001: Define quote/order/invoice/receipt/credit-note relationships, issuer, customer/payer, currency, period, due date, finalization, status transitions, and authoritative identifiers.

checks.heading: Invoice lifecycle and identity
checks.text: PE-FIN-002: Verify applicable invoice fields, numbering, addresses, tax identifiers, purchase orders, language, delivery, and retention against reviewer-approved requirements.

checks.heading: Invoice lifecycle and identity
checks.text: PE-FIN-003: Check draft, finalized, open, paid, partially paid, voided, uncollectible, credited, and overdue states only where supported; amount due and access consequences follow explicit policy.

checks.heading: Invoice lifecycle and identity
checks.text: PE-FIN-004: Test invoice creation/finalization retries and concurrent billing jobs; one intended period/order is not invoiced twice.

checks.heading: Invoice lifecycle and identity
checks.text: PE-FIN-005: Verify line descriptions, service periods, quantities, rates, discounts, proration, taxes, shipping/fees, credits, and final total against approved exact calculations.

checks.heading: Invoice lifecycle and identity
checks.text: PE-FIN-006: Check customer address/tax/business identity changes before/after finalization; historic documents are corrected through the approved traceable workflow.

checks.heading: Invoice lifecycle and identity
checks.text: PE-FIN-007: Test invoice download/portal/email access for correct payer/tenant/role, expired links, removed membership, and sensitive fields; direct references do not expose another customer's records.

checks.heading: Invoice lifecycle and identity
checks.text: PE-FIN-008: Verify manual/out-of-band payment recording is authorized and evidence-backed; marking an invoice paid does not independently prove cash receipt.

checks.heading: Invoice lifecycle and identity
checks.text: PE-FIN-009: Check partial payment, overpayment, underpayment, duplicate transfer, wrong reference, unallocated payment, and currency mismatch only where offered, with an accountable resolution route.

checks.heading: Invoice lifecycle and identity
checks.text: PE-FIN-010: Test invoice terms/collections, due-date changes, write-offs, void/reissue, and credit notes under approved policy with auditability and appropriate access consequences.

checks.heading: Approved tax and document configuration
checks.text: PE-FIN-011: Link each served market/product/customer category to approved tax/VAT responsibility, classification, configuration, exemption evidence, and reviewer/date under shared module 11.

checks.heading: Approved tax and document configuration
checks.text: PE-FIN-012: Verify representative destination, evidence-of-location, business/consumer, valid/invalid/missing tax identity, and exemption flows as actually supported.

checks.heading: Approved tax and document configuration
checks.text: PE-FIN-013: Check tax calculation across inclusive/exclusive price, discount, shipping/fees, proration, refunds, credits, and supported currency rounding using approved examples.

checks.heading: Approved tax and document configuration
checks.text: PE-FIN-014: Test tax service unavailable, invalid address, conflicting evidence, rate/configuration change, and missing classification; documented policy prevents silent unintended collection.

checks.heading: Approved tax and document configuration
checks.text: PE-FIN-015: Verify merchant-of-record, marketplace/platform, processor, and seller responsibilities are not confused in customer documents and internal reports.

checks.heading: Approved tax and document configuration
checks.text: PE-FIN-016: Check effective-date changes and historical corrections preserve required evidence and do not silently recalculate previously finalized documents under today's settings.

checks.heading: Approved tax and document configuration
checks.text: PE-FIN-017: Verify invoice/receipt/credit-note totals and required fields remain consistent in UI, PDF, email, exports, supported locales, and finance tools.

checks.heading: Approved tax and document configuration
checks.text: PE-FIN-018: Define handling of required tax/customer records after account deletion and after retention/hold expiry with approved access controls rather than blanket immediate deletion or indefinite retention.

checks.heading: Reconciliation and financial exports
checks.text: PE-FIN-019: Define reconciliation sources, matching keys, period/cutoff/timezone, frequency, tolerances with rationale, owner, exceptions, and completion evidence.

checks.heading: Reconciliation and financial exports
checks.text: PE-FIN-020: Reconcile orders/invoices to payment attempts, authorizations/captures, refunds, credits, disputes, fees, provider balance movements, payouts, and settlement as applicable.

checks.heading: Reconciliation and financial exports
checks.text: PE-FIN-021: Distinguish gross sales, collected amounts, fees, adjustments, net payout, outstanding receivable, prepaid product value, and accounting classifications approved by finance.

checks.heading: Reconciliation and financial exports
checks.text: PE-FIN-022: Keep currencies separate and use approved conversion rates/date/source for consolidated reports; displayed revenue is not inferred by adding unlike currencies.

checks.heading: Reconciliation and financial exports
checks.text: PE-FIN-023: Test delayed settlement, payout failure/reversal, reserve/hold, bank mismatch, negative provider balance, and account restriction where supported.

checks.heading: Reconciliation and financial exports
checks.text: PE-FIN-024: Verify timing/cutoff for late usage, refunds, delayed callbacks, disputes, credits, annual prepayment, and month/year-end; reports disclose event versus settlement periods.

checks.heading: Reconciliation and financial exports
checks.text: PE-FIN-025: Detect missing/duplicated provider objects, orphan payments, paid-without-access, access-without-required-payment, refunded-but-available credits, and unresolved pending states.

checks.heading: Reconciliation and financial exports
checks.text: PE-FIN-026: Check exports cover intended scope, full pagination, stable IDs, exact amounts/units, timezone, status, lineage, duplicates, and version changes; spreadsheet safety goes to security review.

checks.heading: Reconciliation and financial exports
checks.text: PE-FIN-027: Verify import into finance/reporting tools is idempotent or has explicit duplicate controls, rejected-row handling, correction, and traceability to the original record.

checks.heading: Reconciliation and financial exports
checks.text: PE-FIN-028: Restrict financial exports, reconciliation edits, bank/payout destination changes, and manual journal/correction operations according to approved roles and review policy.

checks.heading: Reconciliation and financial exports
checks.text: PE-FIN-029: Confirm reconciliation repairs do not create additional charges/refunds/grants merely to force a report match; financial movements retain original and corrective history.

checks.heading: Reconciliation and financial exports
checks.text: PE-FIN-030: Maintain an exception register with amount/currency, age, scope, evidence, owner, deadline, proposed action, and independent review proportionate to risk.

checks.heading: Reconciliation and financial exports
checks.text: PE-FIN-031: Verify restored/migrated/backfilled data reconciles with external financial history before reopening billing, refunds, payouts, and entitlement updates.

checks.heading: Reconciliation and financial exports
checks.text: PE-FIN-032: Test missing/stale reconciliation and anomalous variance alerts through actual receipt and support/finance investigation without exposing sensitive customer data.

checks.heading: Reconciliation and financial exports
checks.text: PE-FIN-033: Retain approved evidence/report versions and acceptance of unresolved differences; unknown financial data is not silently represented as zero or as a closed balance.

checks.heading: Reconciliation and financial exports
checks.text: PE-FIN-034: Have qualified project finance/tax owners review applicable calculations, document configuration, reconciliation coverage, and outstanding policy questions before declaring those areas verified.

checks.heading: Operations, support, and incidents
checks.text: PE-OPS-001: Name primary/backup owners and response expectations for billing, failed payment, entitlement drift, refunds, disputes, reconciliation, and provider/account outage.

checks.heading: Operations, support, and incidents
checks.text: PE-OPS-002: Correlate provider request/event/object IDs with internal customer/order/ledger/entitlement records and release/configuration without logging secrets or unnecessary payment data.

checks.heading: Operations, support, and incidents
checks.text: PE-OPS-003: Monitor callback age/failures, stale lifecycle work, duplicate-effect attempts, unknown payments, refund/dispute deadlines, ledger drift, and paid-access failures with tested alert receipt.

checks.heading: Operations, support, and incidents
checks.text: PE-OPS-004: Provide scoped support views and authorized actions for status, repair, refund, cancellation, access correction, and payment recovery; avoid routine untracked database edits.

checks.heading: Operations, support, and incidents
checks.text: PE-OPS-005: Require reason, actor, permissions, effective time, bounds, and audit evidence for manual financial/access changes; review high-impact operations proportionately.

checks.heading: Operations, support, and incidents
checks.text: PE-OPS-006: Maintain runbooks for duplicate charge, paid-no-access, unexpected renewal, missed expiry, stuck refund, dispute, provider outage, leaked key, and reconciliation failure.

checks.heading: Operations, support, and incidents
checks.text: PE-OPS-007: Verify scoped/global stops for new purchases, renewals where controllable, refunds, usage, grants, and replay; distinguish stopping local work from provider-side scheduled effects.

checks.heading: Operations, support, and incidents
checks.text: PE-OPS-008: During provider outage, preserve pending work, explain unknown status, bound retries/cost, and avoid silently routing to another provider in a way that duplicates financial effects.

checks.heading: Operations, support, and incidents
checks.text: PE-OPS-009: Reopen after containment only after checking external state, budgets, permissions, backlog, financial/access invariants, and rate-limited replay.

checks.heading: Operations, support, and incidents
checks.text: PE-OPS-010: Test required billing/consent/renewal/trial/cancellation/recovery notices with correct recipient, locale, effective time, state, approved content, delivery-failure visibility, and retention.

checks.heading: Release, recovery, and provider transitions
checks.text: PE-OPS-011: Verify sandbox/live separation and cutover of keys, prices, customers, endpoints, signatures, event subscriptions, portals, schedules, and tax settings in the actual deployment.

checks.heading: Release, recovery, and provider transitions
checks.text: PE-OPS-012: Test SDK/API/event/schema/configuration upgrades and mixed-version deployment with representative historical objects, pending work, stale clients, and rollback limits.

checks.heading: Release, recovery, and provider transitions
checks.text: PE-OPS-013: Rehearse restore after provider actions continued beyond the database snapshot; reconcile charges, refunds, grants, spent credits, cancellations, and revoked rights before enabling work.

checks.heading: Release, recovery, and provider transitions
checks.text: PE-OPS-014: Check old/new deployments, schedulers, webhook handlers, providers, and store channels do not independently renew, refund, replay, or grant the same customer value.

checks.heading: Release, recovery, and provider transitions
checks.text: PE-OPS-015: For provider/account migration, inventory portable versus nonportable customer/payment/subscription/mandate/tax/consent data and obtain approved transfer/recollection procedures.

checks.heading: Release, recovery, and provider transitions
checks.text: PE-OPS-016: Verify migration preserves billing anchors, remaining paid time, balances, discounts, arrears, cancellation, invoice/refund lineage, and customer communication without duplicate charges.

checks.heading: Release, recovery, and provider transitions
checks.text: PE-OPS-017: Define rollback/forward recovery for irreversible charges, external cancellations, migrated mandates, and issued documents; a code rollback is not assumed to reverse money movement.

checks.heading: Release, recovery, and provider transitions
checks.text: PE-OPS-018: Retire old endpoints/keys/jobs/products/accounts only after delayed-event, refund/dispute, record retention, export, payout, and residual-billing obligations are addressed.

checks.heading: Release, recovery, and provider transitions
checks.text: PE-OPS-019: Confirm organization-controlled provider/bank/admin ownership, backup access, renewal/payment contacts, and lost-device/staff-departure recovery through shared modules 01 and 10.

checks.heading: Release, recovery, and provider transitions
checks.text: PE-OPS-020: Record go/hold/limited-rollout decision with verified critical lifecycles, unresolved gaps, accepted-risk expiry, accountable owner, and focused post-release observation.

checks.heading: Conditional payment/channel models
checks.text: PE-OPS-021: For one-time digital goods, test payment-to-license/download, delivery failure, expiry/re-download, guest recovery, duplicate purchase, refund/revocation, and ownership transfer if offered.

checks.heading: Conditional payment/channel models
checks.text: PE-OPS-022: For physical commerce, test stock/price changes, split fulfillment, shipping tax/fees, partial cancellation/return/refund, and reconciliation of payment versus actual fulfillment.

checks.heading: Conditional payment/channel models
checks.text: PE-OPS-023: For bookings/services, test deposit, remaining balance, hold/authorization, no-show, reschedule, cancellation deadline/timezone, provider absence, and partial delivery against policy.

checks.heading: Conditional payment/channel models
checks.text: PE-OPS-024: For usage-based/AI products, test delayed/corrected usage, reservation leaks, failed provider work, changing unit costs, hard budgets, expensive fallback, and invoice finalization boundaries.

checks.heading: Conditional payment/channel models
checks.text: PE-OPS-025: For B2B/invoiced sales, test payer-versus-user, negotiated contracts, seats, purchase orders, payment terms, manual collection evidence, credit notes, and approved access/grace policy.

checks.heading: Conditional payment/channel models
checks.text: PE-OPS-026: For app stores/platform billing, test purchase verification, account binding, restore purchase, renewals, platform refund/revocation, grace, cross-device access, and web/store overlap using current platform guidance.

checks.heading: Conditional payment/channel models
checks.text: PE-OPS-027: For multiple providers, test routed attempt identity, unknown outcome, fallback, token/account mapping, subscription ownership, fees/currency, reconciliation, and provider-specific dispute/refund handling.

checks.heading: Conditional payment/channel models
checks.text: PE-OPS-028: For marketplaces/connected accounts, verify seller onboarding/eligibility, platform-versus-seller charges, fees, transfers, payouts, refunds, reserves, negative balance, and responsible merchant under approved contracts.

checks.heading: Conditional payment/channel models
checks.text: PE-OPS-029: For marketplace refunds/disputes, test transfer reversal, seller already paid/unavailable, partial platform fee return, cross-account scope, and recovery of unresolved liability without assuming funds are recoverable.

checks.heading: Conditional payment/channel models
checks.text: PE-OPS-030: For wallets/stored value/gift cards, obtain qualified applicability review and test issuance, redemption, transfer, expiry, refund, lost access, and ledger reconciliation within the approved model.

checks.heading: Conditional payment/channel models
checks.text: PE-OPS-031: For installments/deferred payment, test lender/provider acceptance, provisional fulfillment, partial payments, return/cancellation, late reversal, and customer/support ownership without assuming card behavior.

checks.heading: Conditional payment/channel models
checks.text: PE-OPS-032: For donations/sponsorships, test one-time/recurring designation, restricted purpose, donor-versus-beneficiary, receipts, cancellation, refunds, and approved tax-claim wording.

checks.heading: Conditional payment/channel models
checks.text: PE-OPS-033: For bundles/memberships/multiple products, test overlapping grants, mixed intervals, add-on dependencies, per-item refund, seat assignment, and cancellation that leaves other purchased rights intact.

checks.heading: Conditional payment/channel models
checks.text: PE-OPS-034: For family/team/sponsored access, test payer departure, beneficiary removal, shared allowances, role changes, refunds, privacy boundaries, and continued/revoked access under policy.

checks.heading: Conditional payment/channel models
checks.text: PE-OPS-035: For high-value/manual agreements, test approval, quote expiry, signed-term/version evidence, staged collection, provisioning, amendments, and finance/support handoff as scoped.

checks.heading: Conditional payment/channel models
checks.text: PE-OPS-036: For multiple markets/currencies, test supported method combinations, settlement/FX display, localized terms, approved tax/documents, notice timing, and clear rejection of unsupported combinations.

checks.heading: Cross-model closure
checks.text: PE-OPS-037: For each chosen model, execute at least one supported success, meaningful rejection/failure, delayed/duplicate outcome, and correction/recovery with linked final-state evidence.

checks.heading: Cross-model closure
checks.text: PE-OPS-038: Separate transaction settlement from product fulfillment/access and from accounting classification; each material boundary has an accountable source of truth and reconciliation.

checks.heading: Cross-model closure
checks.text: PE-OPS-039: Add scenarios after incidents, policy/provider changes, new markets/payment methods, pricing/model changes, or significant scale; retain failed/near-miss lessons with owners.

checks.heading: Cross-model closure
checks.text: PE-OPS-040: Close accepted actions only after focused verification of financial, ledger, entitlement, effective-time, and notice results; preserve explicit remaining gaps and next review triggers.

checks.heading: Prices checkout and credentials
checks.text: Derive product, price, currency, discount eligibility, quantity limits, and account ownership from trusted server-side rules. Reject client manipulation of amounts, plan IDs, tenant IDs, and checkout destinations.

checks.heading: Prices checkout and credentials
checks.text: Use appropriate currency units and rounding, with explicit tax/invoice requirements. Check displayed totals against authoritative charged amounts.

checks.heading: Prices checkout and credentials
checks.text: Separate test/live credentials, products, prices, callback secrets, customers, and endpoints. Do not reuse test event assumptions in production.

checks.heading: Prices checkout and credentials
checks.text: At test-to-live cutover, configure the live endpoint and its own webhook signing secret, live server/public keys, price mappings, and subscribed events in the correct deployment. Verify delivery/signature handling and safe rejection without accidental real charges; do not copy test secrets into live configuration.

checks.heading: Prices checkout and credentials
checks.text: Verify checkout creation/retry idempotency and return/cancel URLs. A client success redirect alone must not grant paid access.

checks.heading: Prices checkout and credentials
checks.text: Before subscription/trial commitment, show the applicable recurring amount or calculation, frequency, trial end/conversion, and cancellation terms clearly at the consent point. Verify the required affirmative consent and retain the accepted terms/version and evidence; cover mobile, localized, embedded, and provider-hosted checkout. Use 11 to establish jurisdiction-specific wording, placement, and recordkeeping.

checks.heading: Prices checkout and credentials
checks.text: Keep privileged keys server-side and scope administrative payment access. Use hosted/tokenized payment flows where appropriate; identify actual card-data handling obligations rather than assuming the integration removes every obligation.

checks.heading: Events and financial state
checks.text: Verify provider signatures using the required original request bytes and correct endpoint secret. Reject invalid events before state changes; support controlled secret rotation.

checks.heading: Events and financial state
checks.text: Handle duplicate and out-of-order events. Persist event identity and processing state reliably; deduplication must not suppress an event whose business update failed. Do not infer uniqueness or strict ordering from an event creation timestamp alone.

checks.heading: Events and financial state
checks.text: Acknowledge events according to the provider contract after durable acceptance, then process slow work with bounded retries and observable failures.

checks.heading: Events and financial state
checks.text: Reconcile current authoritative payment/subscription state where needed rather than letting stale events overwrite newer state. Confirm tenant/customer binding and subscribed event types. Stripe documents duplicate delivery and non-guaranteed event ordering; verify equivalent guarantees for the chosen provider. [Stripe webhook guidance](https://docs.stripe.com/webhooks)

checks.heading: Events and financial state
checks.text: Define how charge, invoice, subscription, refund, dispute, and entitlement records relate. Alert and reconcile when internal state diverges from the provider.

checks.heading: Lifecycle and access
checks.text: Test trial creation, expiry, conversion, free credits, and repeated-signup abuse. Verification requirements and grace periods must match the product's declared rules.

checks.heading: Lifecycle and access
checks.text: Verify upgrades, downgrades, proration, scheduled changes, pauses, and cancellation at period end or immediately. Access and quotas must change at the intended time.

checks.heading: Lifecycle and access
checks.text: Verify required subscription acknowledgments, renewal/trial/price-change notices, and online cancellation journeys reach the right customer and match the authoritative billing state. Test applicable notice windows and a canceled account's next billing date, including failed delivery and delayed callbacks; record consent and notice evidence under controlled retention.

checks.heading: Lifecycle and access
checks.text: Test failed charges, authentication-required payments, retries, exhausted retry windows, refunds, partial refunds, disputes, and reinstatement. Avoid granting or removing access solely from an ambiguous intermediate event.

checks.heading: Lifecycle and access
checks.text: Revoke or adjust paid entitlements when a trial/subscription lapses according to policy, including scheduled-job or webhook failure scenarios. Use reconciliation/freshness checks rather than relying on one timely callback.

checks.heading: Lifecycle and access
checks.text: Enforce entitlements on server operations, jobs, exports, and costly paths, not just navigation. Recheck work queued before a subscription change if policy requires it.

checks.heading: Lifecycle and access
checks.text: Make manual overrides, refunds, and access adjustments authorized and auditable. Customer support must not become an untracked financial bypass.

checks.heading: Monetary precision and commercial reconciliation
checks.text: Record the countries actually served and the tax/VAT registrations, collection settings, exemptions, and invoice treatment determined under 11. Test representative supported destinations in sandbox and verify configured calculations and receipts against the approved rules; switching on a provider tax feature alone does not establish the seller's obligations.

checks.heading: Monetary precision and commercial reconciliation
checks.text: Store and calculate monetary amounts with integer minor units or an appropriate exact decimal representation, never binary floating point for authoritative totals. Test supported currency exponents, rounding boundaries, tax/VAT, discounts, and displayed versus invoiced totals for the markets actually served.

checks.heading: Monetary precision and commercial reconciliation
checks.text: Verify customer tax identity, invoice address, purchase-order number, and required invoice fields where supported or contractually required. Test annual/custom agreements, negotiated prices, credits, and partial refunds against their effective dates and access rules.

checks.heading: Monetary precision and commercial reconciliation
checks.text: Reconcile billable usage, metering corrections, invoices, provider transactions, refunds/credits, and finance reports. Define rounding and aggregation so billed quantities and amounts match the agreed rules without counting retries twice.

checks.heading: Monetary precision and commercial reconciliation
checks.text: Test failed-payment recovery messages and dunning cadence through the final grace/expiry state. Explain customer action and confirm delivery failures are visible under 14.

checks.heading: Monetary precision and commercial reconciliation
checks.text: Document actual payment-card scope and verify prohibited card data does not enter databases, logs, analytics, support tools, or AI prompts. Hosted payment collection does not by itself establish compliance; coordinate obligations with 11.

checks.heading: Authority, schema, and invariants
checks.text: STATE-001 — Identify authority for each business fact and reconcile conflicting database, provider, cache and client copies; define who wins during recovery.

checks.heading: Authority, schema, and invariants
checks.text: STATE-002 — Express uniqueness, referential, balance, capacity, ownership and state-transition conditions with exact scope and permitted intermediate states.

checks.heading: Authority, schema, and invariants
checks.text: STATE-003 — Enforce applicable invariants at the authoritative boundary; application prechecks alone must not admit a concurrent violation.

checks.heading: Authority, schema, and invariants
checks.text: STATE-004 — Review null, missing, empty, soft-deleted and case-folded values against intended uniqueness and relationship rules using actual database semantics.

checks.heading: Authority, schema, and invariants
checks.text: STATE-005 — Check composite tenant/parent relationships so cross-tenant identifiers cannot create valid-looking but incorrectly owned records.

checks.heading: Authority, schema, and invariants
checks.text: STATE-006 — Validate cascade, restrict, set-null and manual cleanup behavior through deletion and rollback; optional references must not become unintended orphans.

checks.heading: Authority, schema, and invariants
checks.text: STATE-007 — Inspect direct SQL, imports, admin tools, jobs and repair scripts for bypasses of invariants enforced only in one API path.

checks.heading: Authority, schema, and invariants
