checks.text: STATE-008 — Verify generated identifiers, sequence gaps, external IDs and natural keys are interpreted correctly; do not use gap-free sequence assumptions as an integrity oracle without a requirement.

checks.heading: Transactions and isolation
checks.text: STATE-009 — Identify the exact atomic boundary of multi-record writes and whether all operations actually share the intended connection/session/transaction.

checks.heading: Transactions and isolation
checks.text: STATE-010 — Inject failures after each significant write and verify rollback or documented recoverable intermediate state, including exceptions swallowed by helpers.

checks.heading: Transactions and isolation
checks.text: STATE-011 — Test read-check-write races under the configured isolation level rather than assuming a transaction automatically prevents oversell or duplicate creation.

checks.heading: Transactions and isolation
checks.text: STATE-012 — Exercise nonrepeatable reads, changing result sets and write-skew risks where the operation depends on multiple reads or rows.

checks.heading: Transactions and isolation
checks.text: STATE-013 — Test serialization failures and deadlocks; retry the correct whole unit with bounded attempts and without repeating an unprotected external effect.

checks.heading: Transactions and isolation
checks.text: STATE-014 — Verify failed transactions are correctly rolled back/reset before pooled connections are reused; subsequent requests do not inherit broken or stale session state.

checks.heading: Transactions and isolation
checks.text: STATE-015 — Review nested transaction/savepoint behavior in the actual driver/ORM, including partial error recovery and callbacks executed before durable commit.

checks.heading: Transactions and isolation
checks.text: STATE-016 — Set and test relevant lock/statement/transaction deadlines; request timeout must not leave unbounded work or indefinite locks unnoticed.

checks.heading: Transactions and isolation
checks.text: STATE-017 — Check long transactions, idle-in-transaction sessions and large batches for contention, retained history and recovery impact at realistic volume.

checks.heading: Transactions and isolation
checks.text: STATE-018 — Inspect whether DDL, external calls, sequence operations or nontransactional tables have different rollback semantics from ordinary row updates.

checks.heading: Concurrent user and worker actions
checks.text: STATE-019 — Run simultaneous equivalent creates behind a controlled barrier and verify the number of committed records and side effects, not just returned statuses.

checks.heading: Concurrent user and worker actions
checks.text: STATE-020 — Race independent intentional creates with retries of one operation; deduplication must not merge legitimately distinct user actions.

checks.heading: Concurrent user and worker actions
checks.text: STATE-021 — Race updates from stale clients; prevent unintended lost updates through a suitable conflict/atomic-update strategy and explain conflicts to callers.

checks.heading: Concurrent user and worker actions
checks.text: STATE-022 — Race update/delete, restore/delete and child-create/parent-delete; verify the chosen lifecycle and ownership rules.

checks.heading: Concurrent user and worker actions
checks.text: STATE-023 — Test increments/decrements, balances, counters and inventory under contention; read-modify-write must not lose or manufacture value.

checks.heading: Concurrent user and worker actions
checks.text: STATE-024 — Race quota check/reservation/commit/release, including expiry and failure, and verify no double allocation or permanently leaked reservation.

checks.heading: Concurrent user and worker actions
checks.text: STATE-025 — Race uniqueness checks across tabs, replicas, API versions and background jobs; inspect final state after all attempts settle.

checks.heading: Concurrent user and worker actions
checks.text: STATE-026 — Verify optimistic concurrency tokens/version checks cover all mutable fields and channels; blind upserts must not undo newer edits.

checks.heading: Concurrent user and worker actions
checks.text: STATE-027 — Test collaborative/offline merge policies where present; conflicts, tombstones and stale synchronization do not silently resurrect deleted data.

checks.heading: Concurrent user and worker actions
checks.text: STATE-028 — Verify bulk actions and partially failed batches have explicit all-or-nothing or per-item outcomes that can be retried safely.

checks.heading: Locks, leases, and ownership
checks.text: STATE-029 — Verify job/leader/resource claims are atomic and ownership is scoped correctly; a read followed by an unguarded write is not an exclusive claim.

checks.heading: Locks, leases, and ownership
checks.text: STATE-030 — Test lease expiry while the old holder is paused; a resumed stale holder must not corrupt state after another worker takes ownership.

checks.heading: Locks, leases, and ownership
checks.text: STATE-031 — Where stale owners can write, verify fencing/version checks or an equivalent authority-side rejection rather than relying only on a lock's expiry.

checks.heading: Locks, leases, and ownership
checks.text: STATE-032 — Verify renewal, release and cancellation compare ownership tokens; an expired worker must not release another worker's new lock.

checks.heading: Locks, leases, and ownership
checks.text: STATE-033 — Test clock assumptions, process pauses, network delays and lock-store restart for ownership algorithms; record the actual guarantee boundary.

checks.heading: Locks, leases, and ownership
checks.text: STATE-034 — Review lock order and contention across resources; deadlock recovery does not leave partial allocations or retry indefinitely.

checks.heading: Locks, leases, and ownership
checks.text: STATE-035 — Test multiple replicas during scheduled/maintenance work and leader handover; exclusive ownership survives deployment and interrupted renewal as designed.

checks.heading: Locks, leases, and ownership
checks.text: STATE-036 — Verify stale/stuck-state repair distinguishes active slow work from abandoned work and does not steal or delete valid processing prematurely.

checks.heading: Replicas, failover, and consistency
checks.text: STATE-037 — Define permitted read staleness and read-your-writes behavior; replica reads after a successful update do not falsely report failure or invite duplicate work.

checks.heading: Replicas, failover, and consistency
checks.text: STATE-038 — Test replica lag, unavailable replicas and fallback routing against correctness as well as latency; critical decisions do not silently use stale authority.

checks.heading: Replicas, failover, and consistency
checks.text: STATE-039 — Record replication/write acknowledgment settings and determine what acknowledged work can be lost under the agreed failover scenario.

checks.heading: Replicas, failover, and consistency
checks.text: STATE-040 — In an isolated exercise, verify promotion/failover behavior and reconcile divergent or ambiguous writes before normal service resumes.

checks.heading: Replicas, failover, and consistency
checks.text: STATE-041 — Test old-primary fencing and clients with stale routing; topology changes must not allow unsupported concurrent authoritative writers.

checks.heading: Replicas, failover, and consistency
checks.text: STATE-042 — Verify connection pools, proxies and long-lived clients reconnect to the correct role after failover; read-only/role errors are handled explicitly.

checks.heading: Replicas, failover, and consistency
checks.text: STATE-043 — Where multi-region/multi-writer operation exists, test conflicts and convergence under partition/reconnection; document availability versus consistency choices per operation.

checks.heading: Replicas, failover, and consistency
checks.text: STATE-044 — Reconcile CDC/search/cache consumers after source failover or history discontinuity; checkpoints must not silently skip or reapply incompatible changes.

checks.heading: Persistence and externally visible outcomes
checks.text: STATE-045 — Record actual fsync/journal/WAL/write-concern settings and storage persistence; distinguish process crash survival from host/power/volume loss.

checks.heading: Persistence and externally visible outcomes
checks.text: STATE-046 — Verify a success response follows the required durable boundary; acknowledgments issued before persistence are explicitly part of the loss model.

checks.heading: Persistence and externally visible outcomes
checks.text: STATE-047 — Interrupt the connection after commit but before response and verify safe lookup/retry of the unknown outcome.

checks.heading: Persistence and externally visible outcomes
checks.text: STATE-048 — Check database/file writes on ephemeral containers, temporary directories and unmounted volumes; restart/redeploy must not discard intended persistent state.

checks.heading: Persistence and externally visible outcomes
checks.text: STATE-049 — Test disk-full, write rejection and resource exhaustion in a bounded disposable environment; failed writes do not masquerade as committed success.

checks.heading: Persistence and externally visible outcomes
checks.text: STATE-050 — Validate audit/history records and financial corrections remain traceable and consistent with business changes; auxiliary logging failure follows an explicit policy.

checks.heading: Persistence and externally visible outcomes
checks.text: STATE-051 — Verify reads after restart using independent connections and consistency checks rather than an in-memory cache or old ORM identity map.

checks.heading: Persistence and externally visible outcomes
checks.text: STATE-052 — Check invariants after fault recovery and reconciliation, including related records, provider effects and derived state; one correct main row does not prove the whole operation correct.

checks.heading: Idempotency and ambiguous outcomes
checks.text: WORK-001 — Define the logical operation identity, key scope, tenant binding, request fingerprint and retention period; transport event IDs and business operation IDs may serve different purposes.

checks.heading: Idempotency and ambiguous outcomes
checks.text: WORK-002 — Retry the same key and request sequentially and concurrently; verify one intended persisted result and allowed external effects.

checks.heading: Idempotency and ambiguous outcomes
checks.text: WORK-003 — Reuse a key with a different payload, tenant or operation and verify explicit rejection or documented semantics rather than silent result substitution.

checks.heading: Idempotency and ambiguous outcomes
checks.text: WORK-004 — Test timeout after provider success but before local persistence; resolve the ambiguous result through provider lookup/idempotency/reconciliation rather than blind duplication.

checks.heading: Idempotency and ambiguous outcomes
checks.text: WORK-005 — Test timeout after local commit but before response; retried callers can retrieve a stable outcome without executing again.

checks.heading: Idempotency and ambiguous outcomes
checks.text: WORK-006 — Verify deduplication recording and business-state changes are atomic or recoverably coordinated; an event marked done before work commits must not be lost.

checks.heading: Idempotency and ambiguous outcomes
checks.text: WORK-007 — Check pending/failed idempotency records recover after crashes; permanent “in progress” states do not block legitimate completion indefinitely.

checks.heading: Idempotency and ambiguous outcomes
checks.text: WORK-008 — Align deduplication expiry with actual provider retries, queue retention, offline clients and manual replay; expired keys must not unexpectedly duplicate old effects.

checks.heading: Idempotency and ambiguous outcomes
checks.text: WORK-009 — Test distinct events describing the same business transition and repeated business actions with different transport IDs; define the correct semantic deduplication boundary.

checks.heading: Idempotency and ambiguous outcomes
checks.text: WORK-010 — Keep idempotency results durable across restarts, replicas and topology changes; a per-process map or evictable cache must not be assumed sufficient.

checks.heading: Publish, consume, and acknowledge
checks.text: WORK-011 — Document actual broker delivery, retention, visibility, ordering and acknowledgment semantics for the configured queue/plan.

checks.heading: Publish, consume, and acknowledge
checks.text: WORK-012 — Crash a consumer before and after business commit and before and after acknowledgment; verify redelivery cannot lose or duplicate the intended effect.

checks.heading: Publish, consume, and acknowledge
checks.text: WORK-013 — Test producer interruption around send/acknowledgment; ambiguous publication is deduplicated or reconciled downstream.

checks.heading: Publish, consume, and acknowledge
checks.text: WORK-014 — Where a database update requires event publication, inspect outbox or another recoverable coordination method; publish failure must not strand committed state silently.

checks.heading: Publish, consume, and acknowledge
checks.text: WORK-015 — Test outbox insertion, publishing, marking and cleanup boundaries; publisher retries and concurrent publishers preserve required effects.

checks.heading: Publish, consume, and acknowledge
checks.text: WORK-016 — Check consumer inbox/checkpoint recording is coupled correctly to business processing; persisted offsets alone do not prove a business update succeeded.

checks.heading: Publish, consume, and acknowledge
checks.text: WORK-017 — Verify visibility/lease settings fit actual processing, renewal and worst-case pauses; overlapping consumers remain safe if a message becomes visible early.

checks.heading: Publish, consume, and acknowledge
checks.text: WORK-018 — Test message ordering assumptions per key/partition and across queues; reorder events intentionally and verify version/state-transition handling.

checks.heading: Publish, consume, and acknowledge
checks.text: WORK-019 — Check broker restart, disconnect, rebalance and partition reassignment; unfinished work and checkpoints recover without unsupported guarantees.

checks.heading: Publish, consume, and acknowledge
checks.text: WORK-020 — Verify queue retention/expiry and backlog age cannot silently remove important work before processing or recovery; alert against business deadlines.

checks.heading: Retries, dead letters, and replay
checks.text: WORK-021 — Classify transient, permanent and ambiguous errors; retry only safe operations with an explicit bounded policy.

checks.heading: Retries, dead letters, and replay
checks.text: WORK-022 — Apply a total retry/deadline budget across client, proxy, SDK, worker and provider layers; nested retries must not amplify work without bound.

checks.heading: Retries, dead letters, and replay
checks.text: WORK-023 — Check exponential or otherwise suitable backoff, jitter and provider retry guidance; synchronized workers do not repeatedly overload a recovering dependency.

checks.heading: Retries, dead letters, and replay
checks.text: WORK-024 — Test poison messages, invalid schema, oversized payloads and unavailable referenced records; one bad item does not permanently block unrelated work.

checks.heading: Retries, dead letters, and replay
checks.text: WORK-025 — Verify maximum attempts/age and dead-letter disposition are visible, retained and actionable; silently dropping failed jobs is not successful completion.

checks.heading: Retries, dead letters, and replay
checks.text: WORK-026 — Replay dead letters in a controlled sample with ownership, rate, duplicate safeguards and reconciliation; replay-all must not repeat destructive external effects.

checks.heading: Retries, dead letters, and replay
checks.text: WORK-027 — Check replay after code/schema/configuration changes; old messages still decode or have an explicit conversion/quarantine path.

checks.heading: Retries, dead letters, and replay
checks.text: WORK-028 — Verify operators can identify and recover unknown/stuck operations without clearing deduplication records or mass-resetting valid state blindly.

checks.heading: Retries, dead letters, and replay
checks.text: WORK-029 — Keep event correlation, attempt history and outcome evidence through retries while limiting sensitive payload retention.

checks.heading: Retries, dead letters, and replay
checks.text: WORK-030 — Test late success after timeout/cancellation and callbacks after local failure; terminal-state handling must not overwrite a newer valid decision.

checks.heading: Dependency failure and graceful degradation
checks.text: WORK-031 — Bound connection, read, overall request and processing time where appropriate; a single slow dependency cannot hold resources indefinitely.

checks.heading: Dependency failure and graceful degradation
checks.text: WORK-032 — Test unavailable, slow, malformed, partial and rate-limited provider responses; distinguish response parsing failure from a known business rejection.

checks.heading: Dependency failure and graceful degradation
checks.text: WORK-033 — Verify cancellation and client disconnect behavior; stopping the caller does not automatically prove external work stopped.

checks.heading: Dependency failure and graceful degradation
checks.text: WORK-034 — Inspect circuit-breaker/open/recovery behavior where used; half-open probes and retries do not create a recovery surge.

checks.heading: Dependency failure and graceful degradation
checks.text: WORK-035 — Isolate pools, concurrency and queues where necessary so a failing optional dependency does not exhaust resources for essential work.

checks.heading: Dependency failure and graceful degradation
checks.text: WORK-036 — Test fallback services for correctness, compatible data/identifiers and duplicate effects; a fallback must not execute a second charge after an unknown primary outcome.

checks.heading: Dependency failure and graceful degradation
checks.text: WORK-037 — Verify degradation communicates pending/unavailable state and preserves retry/recovery evidence instead of falsely confirming completion.

checks.heading: Dependency failure and graceful degradation
checks.text: WORK-038 — Test provider credential rotation, certificate/DNS changes, stale endpoints and revoked access as recoverable configuration failures.

checks.heading: Dependency failure and graceful degradation
checks.text: WORK-039 — Bound backlog drain and replay after outages; resource use, external quotas and live requests remain within agreed limits.

checks.heading: Dependency failure and graceful degradation
checks.text: WORK-040 — Verify dependency recovery triggers reconciliation of pending/unknown work, not merely a green health check.

checks.heading: Schedules and distributed ownership
checks.text: WORK-041 — Inventory app schedulers, host cron, provider schedules, database jobs and external automation; record owner, purpose and actual execution source.

checks.heading: Schedules and distributed ownership
checks.text: WORK-042 — Run multiple replicas and deployment overlap to verify scheduled business effects have coordinated ownership or equivalent deduplication.

checks.heading: Schedules and distributed ownership
checks.text: WORK-043 — Test missed-run behavior after downtime: skip, catch-up, coalesce or bounded replay matches the business requirement and does not create a storm.

checks.heading: Schedules and distributed ownership
checks.text: WORK-044 — Test overlapping long-running schedules, lease expiry and late prior runs; old work cannot overwrite or duplicate a newer period's result.

checks.heading: Schedules and distributed ownership
checks.text: WORK-045 — Test daylight-saving gaps/repeated hours, timezone changes and local-time recurrence; record how each logical scheduled occurrence is identified.

checks.heading: Schedules and distributed ownership
checks.text: WORK-046 — Verify schedule edits, cancellation and pause take effect for already queued work as intended; stale jobs do not ignore current authorization/state.

checks.heading: Schedules and distributed ownership
checks.text: WORK-047 — Check business-period keys and cutoffs around month/year boundaries, leap days and locale-independent dates.

checks.heading: Schedules and distributed ownership
checks.text: WORK-048 — Verify scheduler state, last-run markers and deduplication survive the intended restart/restore path; restoring old checkpoints must not blindly rerun historical effects.

checks.heading: Shutdown, compensation, and reconciliation
checks.text: WORK-049 — On graceful shutdown stop new claims, handle in-flight work and release/expire ownership correctly within actual platform termination deadlines.

checks.heading: Shutdown, compensation, and reconciliation
checks.text: WORK-050 — Hard-kill a worker at representative boundaries in isolation; process-local promises/timers must not be the only record of important work.

checks.heading: Shutdown, compensation, and reconciliation
checks.text: WORK-051 — Review cross-system workflows for explicit compensation, retry or manual reconciliation when one transaction cannot cover all participants.

checks.heading: Shutdown, compensation, and reconciliation
checks.text: WORK-052 — Test compensation success, failure and repeated execution; undo must not exceed the original effect or erase evidence of a completed external action.

checks.heading: Shutdown, compensation, and reconciliation
checks.text: WORK-053 — Verify reconciliation jobs compare authoritative states, identify drift and repair safely with limits, checkpoints and audit evidence.

checks.heading: Shutdown, compensation, and reconciliation
checks.text: WORK-054 — Race reconciliation/cleanup with normal work and late callbacks; recovery does not delete a valid upload, release a live reservation or reapply an old result.

checks.heading: Shutdown, compensation, and reconciliation
checks.text: WORK-055 — Define a maximum age for pending/unknown/stuck business states and actionable escalation; permanent limbo is not an acceptable retry strategy.

checks.heading: Shutdown, compensation, and reconciliation
checks.text: WORK-056 — Validate end-to-end outcomes after restart/replay using independent persisted records, provider receipts and invariant checks; broker metrics alone are insufficient.

checks.heading: Pagination, queries, and realistic volume
checks.text: DATA-001 — Seed above API/server/export page caps and traverse all pages; compare expected IDs and totals, not just nonempty responses.

checks.heading: Pagination, queries, and realistic volume
checks.text: DATA-002 — Use deterministic ordering with adequate tie-breaking; equal timestamps/names must not cause skipped or repeated records.

checks.heading: Pagination, queries, and realistic volume
checks.text: DATA-003 — Insert/update/delete records during traversal and verify the documented snapshot/live-list semantics, including acceptable duplicates or changes if explicitly designed.

checks.heading: Pagination, queries, and realistic volume
checks.text: DATA-004 — Check keyset/offset/cursor boundaries, empty final pages, one-record pages, invalid/expired cursors and changed filters.

checks.heading: Pagination, queries, and realistic volume
checks.text: DATA-005 — Validate tenant, role, soft-delete and status filters on every page, count, export and background batch; a complete result must also be correctly scoped.

checks.heading: Pagination, queries, and realistic volume
checks.text: DATA-006 — Verify joins, one-to-many expansion, deduplication and aggregation don't silently drop parents or inflate totals.

checks.heading: Pagination, queries, and realistic volume
checks.text: DATA-007 — Test null, missing, empty, zero and boundary values in filters/sorts; UI counts and server queries use compatible meaning.

checks.heading: Pagination, queries, and realistic volume
checks.text: DATA-008 — Inspect realistic plans and indexes for frequent filters/joins/sorts; include skew, hot tenants, long history and cold-cache behavior where relevant.

checks.heading: Pagination, queries, and realistic volume
checks.text: DATA-009 — Verify statement/client timeouts, partial responses and failed later pages produce explicit incomplete outcomes rather than successful truncation.

checks.heading: Pagination, queries, and realistic volume
checks.text: DATA-010 — Test bulk processing over more than one chunk with crash/resume; checkpoints do not skip uncommitted items or repeat unsafe effects.

checks.heading: Pagination, queries, and realistic volume
checks.text: DATA-011 — Compare list/search/export totals against a known oracle and declared snapshot; independent differences are investigated, not dismissed as pagination.

checks.heading: Pagination, queries, and realistic volume
checks.text: DATA-012 — Verify provider response caps and deployed project settings; source examples or SDK defaults are not evidence that one response covers all records.

checks.heading: Imports, exports, and materialized views
checks.text: DATA-013 — Validate import schema, encoding, required fields, type conversion and row-level errors before committing unintended data.

checks.heading: Imports, exports, and materialized views
checks.text: DATA-014 — Test duplicate files/rows, interrupted imports and resumed batches; distinguish repeated uploads from intentionally new revisions.

checks.heading: Imports, exports, and materialized views
checks.text: DATA-015 — Define atomic versus partial import semantics and provide recoverable per-row/batch outcomes; invalid rows do not silently disappear.

checks.heading: Imports, exports, and materialized views
checks.text: DATA-016 — Check large/streamed exports for complete content, finalization, failure reporting and consistent authorization while running.

checks.heading: Imports, exports, and materialized views
checks.text: DATA-017 — Avoid exposing unfinished exports as complete files; checksums/counts/manifests or equivalent verification match the actual delivered artifact.

checks.heading: Imports, exports, and materialized views
checks.text: DATA-018 — Verify reports/materialized views/warehouse pipelines maintain declared freshness and recover from missed, repeated and out-of-order changes.

checks.heading: Imports, exports, and materialized views
checks.text: DATA-019 — Test CDC snapshot-to-stream handoff, checkpoint recovery and schema evolution where present; no silent gap or double counting at the boundary.

checks.heading: Imports, exports, and materialized views
checks.text: DATA-020 — Ensure reconciliation/repair can rebuild derived aggregates and distinguish historical corrections from new business activity.

checks.heading: Files and object storage
checks.text: DATA-021 — Map object metadata to actual files, versions and ownership; detect missing objects, orphan metadata and unreferenced uploads safely.

checks.heading: Files and object storage
checks.text: DATA-022 — Test upload initiation, partial transfer, completion, metadata commit and response interruption; users are not shown a completed record for an unusable object.

checks.heading: Files and object storage
checks.text: DATA-023 — Verify multipart/chunked uploads can resume/cancel and abandoned parts expire safely; cleanup does not remove active uploads.

checks.heading: Files and object storage
checks.text: DATA-024 — Check object naming, collision and overwrite/version rules under simultaneous uploads and retries; content must not be assigned to the wrong record.

checks.heading: Files and object storage
checks.text: DATA-025 — Validate size, hash/content integrity and format as required after transfer/copy/restore; object existence or HTTP 200 alone does not establish correctness.

checks.heading: Files and object storage
checks.text: DATA-026 — Test copy/move/delete and database updates as a cross-system workflow; partial success has reconciliation rather than dangling references.

checks.heading: Files and object storage
checks.text: DATA-027 — Inspect object-store consistency and lifecycle/versioning rules for the configured provider; do not generalize one platform's read/list guarantees.

checks.heading: Files and object storage
checks.text: DATA-028 — Verify generated thumbnails, renditions, attachments and exports are either backed up or reproducible from retained source/version/tooling.

checks.heading: Files and object storage
checks.text: DATA-029 — Check signed-link expiry, storage class/archive retrieval and restored permissions against promised user access and recovery time.

checks.heading: Files and object storage
checks.text: DATA-030 — Verify local volumes, mount paths, ownership and permissions survive redeploy/host recovery; writing to an unmounted directory must not silently create a different state store.

checks.heading: Files and object storage
checks.text: DATA-031 — Exercise bounded storage exhaustion/unavailability and invalid content; errors preserve recoverable state and expose a usable retry/reconciliation path.

checks.heading: Files and object storage
checks.text: DATA-032 — Confirm retention/object lifecycle does not delete files still referenced by active, held or restored records; cleanup uses authority and appropriate safety windows.

checks.heading: Caches, search, and derived indexes
checks.text: DATA-033 — Classify each cache as rebuildable or intentionally authoritative; identify quotas, coordination, sessions and reservations that carry more than performance value.

checks.heading: Caches, search, and derived indexes
checks.text: DATA-034 — Test restart, eviction, expiry and cold rebuild under the configured persistence policy; important state is not lost under an undocumented cache assumption.

checks.heading: Caches, search, and derived indexes
checks.text: DATA-035 — Verify cache keys include the necessary tenant, role, locale, version and query scope; stale/mis-scoped data must not be returned as another user's truth.

checks.heading: Caches, search, and derived indexes
checks.text: DATA-036 — Race invalidation with writes/read-through fills; late stale fills must not indefinitely replace newer state.

checks.heading: Caches, search, and derived indexes
checks.text: DATA-037 — Check TTL, negative caching and failure caching against permitted staleness; a transient missing record must not remain invisible beyond the target.

checks.heading: Caches, search, and derived indexes
checks.text: DATA-038 — Test cache outage and stampede/rebuild behavior; fallback does not overload authority or bypass correctness checks.

checks.heading: Caches, search, and derived indexes
checks.text: DATA-039 — Verify search/vector indexes handle updates, deletes, schema/model changes and failed indexing with bounded lag and reconciliation.

checks.heading: Caches, search, and derived indexes
checks.text: DATA-040 — Rebuild indexes from authoritative data without silent omissions, wrong versions or cross-tenant mixing; record checkpoints and completeness checks.

checks.heading: Caches, search, and derived indexes
checks.text: DATA-041 — Test stale index hits pointing to deleted/unauthorized records and missing fresh hits; final access and business decisions use the appropriate authority.

checks.heading: Caches, search, and derived indexes
checks.text: DATA-042 — Coordinate index/cache rebuild after backup restore so future/stale derived entries do not resurrect invalid or deleted data.

checks.heading: Time, dates, and numeric/text representation
checks.text: DATA-043 — Distinguish instants, local dates, durations, timezone-aware recurrences and business periods; use representations fitting each meaning.

checks.heading: Time, dates, and numeric/text representation
checks.text: DATA-044 — Preserve IANA timezone identity where future wall-clock schedules depend on it; an instant or fixed UTC offset alone does not encode the future local rule.

checks.heading: Time, dates, and numeric/text representation
checks.text: DATA-045 — Test daylight-saving skipped/repeated times, timezone edits, travel and changed timezone rules; define how ambiguous/nonexistent times are resolved.

checks.heading: Time, dates, and numeric/text representation
checks.text: DATA-046 — Check UTC/local conversion, offset-bearing API input and serialization round trips across database, worker, browser and export.

checks.heading: Time, dates, and numeric/text representation
checks.text: DATA-047 — Use an appropriate monotonic elapsed-time source for durations where required; wall-clock adjustments must not corrupt timeout/lease assumptions.

checks.heading: Time, dates, and numeric/text representation
checks.text: DATA-048 — Test clock skew and time synchronization loss within a bounded environment; ordering, expiry and deduplication do not depend on impossible clock precision.

checks.heading: Time, dates, and numeric/text representation
checks.text: DATA-049 — Check month/year transitions, leap day, end-of-month recurrence and inclusive/exclusive time ranges; date-only values do not shift with user timezone.

checks.heading: Time, dates, and numeric/text representation
checks.text: DATA-050 — Preserve intended precision for money, quantities, identifiers and timestamps across API/DB/export; binary floating-point or unsafe integer conversion must not silently change business values.

checks.heading: Time, dates, and numeric/text representation
checks.text: DATA-051 — Define rounding, currency/unit conversion, overflow and negative-value rules; totals and corrections use consistent policies.

checks.heading: Time, dates, and numeric/text representation
checks.text: DATA-052 — Test Unicode normalization, collation, case sensitivity, long strings and encoding boundaries against uniqueness, search and round-trip requirements.

checks.heading: Time, dates, and numeric/text representation
checks.text: DATA-053 — Distinguish absent/null/empty/default values across JSON, forms, CSV and schema evolution; a partial update must not inadvertently erase fields.

checks.heading: Time, dates, and numeric/text representation
checks.text: DATA-054 — Validate checksums/signatures or equivalent integrity markers over a defined canonical representation when used; harmless serialization differences must not create false corruption results.

checks.heading: Time, dates, and numeric/text representation
checks.text: DATA-055 — Check compressed/encrypted/archived data has recoverable keys, format/version metadata and valid integrity checks before discarding originals.

checks.heading: Time, dates, and numeric/text representation
checks.text: DATA-056 — Compare representative end-to-end round trips after import, export, migration and restore for IDs, values, relationships, timezone meaning and file content.

checks.heading: Recovery coverage and targets
checks.text: REC-001 — Inventory every non-rebuildable state store, including database, uploads, volumes, user files, broker state, external receipts and required configuration.

checks.heading: Recovery coverage and targets
checks.text: REC-002 — Record RPO/RTO by important dataset/service and the agreed timing boundaries; include detection, access, provisioning, verification and reconciliation as specified.

checks.heading: Recovery coverage and targets
checks.text: REC-003 — Identify dependencies between records, files, encryption keys, identities, schema, application versions and queue offsets that must form a usable recovery set.

checks.heading: Recovery coverage and targets
checks.text: REC-004 — Distinguish host/process loss, accidental deletion, corruption, malicious deletion, credential loss, provider/region outage and operator absence; coverage for one does not imply all.

checks.heading: Recovery coverage and targets
checks.text: REC-005 — Verify selected provider plan, enabled features, retention, export/restore permissions and actual available recovery points; sales documentation alone is insufficient.

checks.heading: Recovery coverage and targets
checks.text: REC-006 — Confirm snapshot/control-plane coverage explicitly includes application state or is supplemented; rebuilding a server does not recreate absent uploads or keys.

checks.heading: Recovery coverage and targets
checks.text: REC-007 — Identify rebuildable caches/indexes and measure reconstruction time at realistic volume; “rebuildable” does not guarantee the RTO.

checks.heading: Recovery coverage and targets
checks.text: REC-008 — Record vendor-owned/nonexportable state and alternatives for obtaining it after outage or account loss; expose limitations in recovery promises.

checks.heading: Backup creation and completeness
checks.text: REC-009 — Verify scheduling, last successful completion and latest recoverable data point; job start time and backup-file modification time are not necessarily the recovery point.

checks.heading: Backup creation and completeness
checks.text: REC-010 — Check consistency of online backups, transactions and multi-volume/object snapshots using supported mechanisms; arbitrary file copying may not yield recoverable state.

checks.heading: Backup creation and completeness
checks.text: REC-011 — Verify full/incremental/log chains are complete and retained together; one missing segment or base backup must be detected before recovery is needed.

checks.heading: Backup creation and completeness
checks.text: REC-012 — Test PITR to a chosen safe point around a known change and record archive continuity, timeline and recovery boundary where supported.

checks.heading: Backup creation and completeness
checks.text: REC-013 — Verify object files and database references have compatible recovery coverage; metadata backups alone may omit the actual uploaded objects.

checks.heading: Backup creation and completeness
checks.text: REC-014 — Check backup inclusion/exclusion filters, new tables/buckets/volumes and large/rare objects; a legacy job may omit newly introduced state.

checks.heading: Backup creation and completeness
checks.text: REC-015 — Verify supported backup tooling/version, compression/encryption and readable manifests/checksums; file size alone is not a completeness check.

checks.heading: Backup creation and completeness
checks.text: REC-016 — Test interrupted/failed backups, overlapping jobs, unavailable destinations and exhausted quotas; incomplete copies must not replace the last usable recovery set.

checks.heading: Backup creation and completeness
checks.text: REC-017 — Verify freshness, failure and chain-gap alerts reach an accountable operator with time to act before RPO coverage is exceeded.

checks.heading: Backup creation and completeness
checks.text: REC-018 — Assess backup load and retention/storage growth against production capacity; backup success must not create recurring availability failures.

checks.heading: Protection, access, and retention
checks.text: REC-019 — Keep recovery copies outside the production failure domain with access separation appropriate to the threat model; production credentials should not erase every copy.

checks.heading: Protection, access, and retention
checks.text: REC-020 — Verify immutability/versioning/delete protection where required, including actual retention configuration and privileged bypass paths.

checks.heading: Protection, access, and retention
checks.text: REC-021 — Check backup encryption, key versions and independently recoverable access; keys lost with the primary host must not make protected copies unusable.

checks.heading: Protection, access, and retention
checks.text: REC-022 — Rehearse loss of the usual operator/device/account through approved recovery access and a second trained operator without exposing secrets in the runbook.

checks.heading: Protection, access, and retention
checks.text: REC-023 — Verify backup retention and expiry satisfy recovery needs and applicable deletion/hold policies; “keep forever” and “delete immediately everywhere” are not interchangeable defaults.

checks.heading: Protection, access, and retention
checks.text: REC-024 — Check old restore tools, credentials, extension binaries and configuration are retained or obtainable for supported historical recovery points.

checks.heading: Protection, access, and retention
checks.text: REC-025 — Verify backup evidence and restricted data remain protected during test restores, downloads, transfers and temporary-environment cleanup.

checks.heading: Protection, access, and retention
checks.text: REC-026 — Simulate source/account compromise in a tabletop or permitted isolated exercise; confirm protected recovery access and copies remain available.

checks.heading: Executed restore and validation
checks.text: REC-027 — Restore a representative recovery set into a clean environment rather than overwriting the only working production copy.

checks.heading: Executed restore and validation
checks.text: REC-028 — Block outbound payments, emails, webhooks, scheduled jobs and production writes before starting restored services; restored credentials/configuration must not escape isolation.

checks.heading: Executed restore and validation
checks.text: REC-029 — Recover schema, roles, extensions, ownership and required configuration as well as rows; the application must be able to use the restored data securely.

checks.heading: Executed restore and validation
checks.text: REC-030 — Validate representative records, counts, invariants, relationships and file hashes against the selected recovery point; a database starting successfully is insufficient.

checks.heading: Executed restore and validation
checks.text: REC-031 — Run a representative end-to-end application workflow, including authentication, file access and a controlled write where appropriate, to establish usability.

checks.heading: Executed restore and validation
checks.text: REC-032 — Measure actual recovered data boundary and loss window against RPO; include gaps between the newest file, database, log and external-state recovery points.

checks.heading: Executed restore and validation
checks.text: REC-033 — Measure elapsed recovery to the agreed usable-service boundary against RTO, including setup, access, restore, validation and required reconciliation.

checks.heading: Executed restore and validation
checks.text: REC-034 — Test missing/corrupt backup elements and older recovery points so fallback choices and resulting loss are understood.

checks.heading: Executed restore and validation
checks.text: REC-035 — Verify deletion tombstones, revocations and access changes occurring after the restored point are reapplied or otherwise handled before exposure.

checks.heading: Executed restore and validation
checks.text: REC-036 — Reconcile post-recovery provider events and operations already performed externally; old queue/idempotency state must not repeat charges or lose valid outcomes.

checks.heading: Executed restore and validation
checks.text: REC-037 — Rebuild caches/search/derived data from the chosen authority and verify no newer incompatible entries remain from the pre-restore system.

checks.heading: Executed restore and validation
checks.text: REC-038 — Record restore blockers, actual operator steps, evidence, required fixes and next exercise triggers; a failed drill stays a failure until retested.

checks.heading: Failover, disaster sequencing, and return
checks.text: REC-039 — Document service startup/recovery dependency order, including secrets, identity, storage, database, broker, workers, network and application.

checks.heading: Failover, disaster sequencing, and return
checks.text: REC-040 — Verify standby capacity, quotas, images, dependencies and access can support the promised recovery workload; a nominal standby may be empty or unusable.

checks.heading: Failover, disaster sequencing, and return
checks.text: REC-041 — Test old-writer fencing, routing and reconnect behavior during failover; the failed site must not keep accepting unsupported authoritative writes.

checks.heading: Failover, disaster sequencing, and return
checks.text: REC-042 — For regional/provider recovery, account for DNS, certificates, identity, endpoints, object locations and externally allowlisted callbacks, not only database promotion.

checks.heading: Failover, disaster sequencing, and return
checks.text: REC-043 — Define queue/event handling while unavailable: buffer, reject, persist or backfill with an explicit loss/expiry model and customer-visible status.

checks.heading: Failover, disaster sequencing, and return
checks.text: REC-044 — Drain recovery backlog at a controlled rate; live traffic, quotas and critical invariants remain protected during catch-up.

checks.heading: Failover, disaster sequencing, and return
checks.text: REC-045 — Plan failback/return to the normal site, including source of truth, divergent writes, synchronization, write freeze and validation; reversing DNS alone is not sufficient.

checks.heading: Failover, disaster sequencing, and return
checks.text: REC-046 — Keep decision authority, escalation, customer-status coordination and alternate-operator instructions available outside the failed system.

checks.heading: Failover, disaster sequencing, and return
checks.text: REC-047 — Rehearse at the agreed risk-based interval and after material changes; tabletop planning and a full restore exercise are recorded as different evidence.

checks.heading: Failover, disaster sequencing, and return
checks.text: REC-048 — After the exercise, verify isolation cleanup, temporary credentials, cost/resources, production noninterference and updates to runbooks/targets before closing it.

checks.heading: Change classification and compatibility
checks.text: CHANGE-001 — Inventory schema, data, index, extension, collation, storage-format and provider-semantic changes, not only files in the migration directory.

checks.heading: Change classification and compatibility
checks.text: CHANGE-002 — Record prerequisites, irreversible effects, expected duration, owner, stop conditions and reversal/recovery route for each material change.

checks.heading: Change classification and compatibility
checks.text: CHANGE-003 — Verify the old application works with the expanded schema and new application handles pre-backfill data during rolling deployment.

checks.heading: Change classification and compatibility
checks.text: CHANGE-004 — Check mixed-version workers, APIs, scheduled jobs and event payloads; deployment overlap must not write incompatible records or messages.

checks.heading: Change classification and compatibility
checks.text: CHANGE-005 — Use staged expand/backfill/switch/contract or another justified compatibility strategy where availability targets require it; destructive contraction waits for actual consumer retirement.

checks.heading: Change classification and compatibility
checks.text: CHANGE-006 — Verify feature flags and disabled paths do not still write/read retired structures through old replicas, admin tools or delayed jobs.

checks.heading: Change classification and compatibility
checks.text: CHANGE-007 — Check database/driver/extension upgrades and restore-tool compatibility using actual versions; supported SQL syntax alone does not settle behavior changes.

checks.heading: Change classification and compatibility
checks.text: CHANGE-008 — Document code rollback separately from schema reversal, data restoration and provider compensation; each path has its own acceptance evidence.

checks.heading: Migration execution and data backfill
checks.text: CHANGE-009 — Rehearse with production-shaped size, skew, history, tenant distribution and edge values; tiny fixtures do not measure locking or completion time.

checks.heading: Migration execution and data backfill
checks.text: CHANGE-010 — Measure lock acquisition/duration, blocked traffic and transaction impact; long waits and deadlocks have bounded stop/recovery behavior.

checks.heading: Migration execution and data backfill
checks.text: CHANGE-011 — Verify migration ownership/locking prevents duplicate concurrent execution across replicas, deployment jobs and operators.

checks.heading: Migration execution and data backfill
checks.text: CHANGE-012 — Interrupt migration/backfill before and after checkpoints; rerun/resume must not skip or duplicate transformations.

checks.heading: Migration execution and data backfill
checks.text: CHANGE-013 — Inspect actual DDL/transaction behavior, online index options and failure cleanup for the selected engine; don't assume every migration can roll back atomically.

checks.heading: Migration execution and data backfill
checks.text: CHANGE-014 — Verify batch size, throttling, checkpoints and retry bounds keep foreground traffic, storage and replica lag within agreed limits.

checks.heading: Migration execution and data backfill
checks.text: CHANGE-015 — Test concurrent old/new writes during backfill; copied data and late changes converge without overwriting newer values.

checks.heading: Migration execution and data backfill
checks.text: CHANGE-016 — Compare row/object counts, key coverage, relationships, value totals and semantic samples before/after; equal counts alone do not prove a correct transformation.

checks.heading: Migration execution and data backfill
checks.text: CHANGE-017 — Validate new constraints against legacy data before relying on them; invalid/conflicting records have an explicit repair or quarantine path.

checks.heading: Migration execution and data backfill
checks.text: CHANGE-018 — Check required indexes/constraints are valid and active after interrupted creation; a named object may exist without being usable as intended.

checks.heading: Migration execution and data backfill
checks.text: CHANGE-019 — Account for storage/log/archive growth, temporary space and replica/network load caused by changes; failure from capacity exhaustion is planned for.

checks.heading: Migration execution and data backfill
checks.text: CHANGE-020 — Record migration ledger/version only at the intended completion boundary; “applied” must not hide an incomplete backfill or failed postcondition.

checks.heading: Cutover, dual writes, and rollback
checks.text: CHANGE-021 — Define source of truth before, during and after cutover; prevent accidental independent writers on both old and new stores.

checks.heading: Cutover, dual writes, and rollback
checks.text: CHANGE-022 — If dual writing, test one-side failure, retries, reordering and reconciliation; two successful API calls are not atomicity evidence.

checks.heading: Cutover, dual writes, and rollback
checks.text: CHANGE-023 — Verify snapshot/copy plus CDC/event handoff has no untracked gap and a documented catch-up position before reads/writes switch.

checks.heading: Cutover, dual writes, and rollback
checks.text: CHANGE-024 — Rehearse final synchronization/write-freeze or equivalent boundary and measure the actual service interruption.

checks.heading: Cutover, dual writes, and rollback
checks.text: CHANGE-025 — Verify old connections, DNS caches, worker pools, webhooks and delayed jobs route to the intended authority after cutover.

checks.heading: Cutover, dual writes, and rollback
checks.text: CHANGE-026 — Reconcile provider IDs, identity/account mappings, object URLs, timestamps and sequences so new writes do not collide with imported records.

checks.heading: Cutover, dual writes, and rollback
checks.text: CHANGE-027 — Rehearse reverse migration where genuinely reversible and inspect old/new application compatibility afterward; reverse syntax is not proof of restored meaning.

checks.heading: Cutover, dual writes, and rollback
checks.text: CHANGE-028 — For irreversible changes identify lost information and execute the planned restore/fail-forward exercise; a fabricated down migration cannot recover dropped data.

checks.heading: Cutover, dual writes, and rollback
checks.text: CHANGE-029 — Check rollback after new production-format writes: preserve/reconcile those writes or explicitly document the loss/compensation boundary.

checks.heading: Cutover, dual writes, and rollback
checks.text: CHANGE-030 — Retain recovery points and compatibility routes until agreed validation completes; old-state cleanup must not prematurely remove the only fallback.

checks.heading: Cutover, dual writes, and rollback
checks.text: CHANGE-031 — Test failed deployment/startup and interrupted shutdown with the new schema; rollback must not repeatedly trigger unsafe migration side effects.

checks.heading: Cutover, dual writes, and rollback
checks.text: CHANGE-032 — Verify a fresh install and an upgrade from supported prior versions produce compatible complete state; a working long-lived database can hide missing initialization steps.

checks.heading: Deletion, retention, restoration, and repair
checks.text: CHANGE-033 — Define hard delete, soft delete, archive and cancellation distinctly, including related records, search, files, external providers and retention rules.

checks.heading: Deletion, retention, restoration, and repair
checks.text: CHANGE-034 — Test soft-deleted uniqueness, filters, references and concurrent restore/new-create; recovery does not create duplicate active identities or records.

checks.heading: Deletion, retention, restoration, and repair
checks.text: CHANGE-035 — Verify authorized restoration preserves tenant/ownership/access boundaries and does not revive expired permissions or revoked shares.

checks.heading: Deletion, retention, restoration, and repair
checks.text: CHANGE-036 — Check retention jobs use correct scope, timestamps, timezone and exclusions; dry-run samples/limits prevent broad unintended deletion.

checks.heading: Deletion, retention, restoration, and repair
checks.text: CHANGE-037 — Race cleanup with active uploads/jobs, late callbacks, restore and updates; age alone is not proof that a record/object is safe to remove.

checks.heading: Deletion, retention, restoration, and repair
checks.text: CHANGE-038 — Coordinate deletion tombstones and exceptions through backup restore, reimports, synchronization and replay; deleted data must not silently reappear.

checks.heading: Deletion, retention, restoration, and repair
checks.text: CHANGE-039 — Assess legal/operational holds with the responsible owner; holds are scoped, auditable and eventually released rather than silently disabling all retention.

checks.heading: Deletion, retention, restoration, and repair
checks.text: CHANGE-040 — Repair corrupted/inconsistent records with an explicit source of truth, bounded selection, preconditions and validation; scripts must not overwrite intervening valid changes.

checks.heading: Deletion, retention, restoration, and repair
checks.text: CHANGE-041 — Verify repair/backfill/cleanup tools support safe restart and duplicate invocation, with per-item outcomes or transactional guarantees suited to the work.

checks.heading: Deletion, retention, restoration, and repair
checks.text: CHANGE-042 — Preserve immutable business history where required; corrective entries and reconciliation are distinguishable from undocumented mutation.

checks.heading: Change completion and operational handoff
checks.text: CHANGE-043 — Compare current invariants and service/freshness targets after rollout, including delayed jobs and derived data, before declaring completion.

checks.heading: Change completion and operational handoff
checks.text: CHANGE-044 — Document residual quarantined records, manual interventions and uncertain outcomes with owners; successful majority processing must not hide untracked exceptions.

checks.heading: Change completion and operational handoff
checks.text: CHANGE-045 — Verify new backups and an appropriate restore path work with the changed schema/format/keys; old recovery evidence may no longer apply.

checks.heading: Change completion and operational handoff
checks.text: CHANGE-046 — Retire old stores, credentials, jobs and routes only after verification and retention decisions; abandoned writers can reintroduce divergence later.

checks.heading: Change completion and operational handoff
checks.text: CHANGE-047 — Update inventory, runbooks, on-call ownership, recovery sequence and evidence references for the final deployed architecture.

checks.heading: Change completion and operational handoff
checks.text: CHANGE-048 — For shutdown, acquisition or provider exit preserve required exports, history, recovery access and deletion obligations; closing a service does not automatically finish its data lifecycle.

checks.heading: State and concurrency
checks.text: REL-001 — Identify authoritative records, invariants, and multi-step writes. Use supported transactions/constraints, or an explicit recoverable workflow when one transaction cannot cover all systems.

checks.heading: State and concurrency
checks.text: REL-002 — Test simultaneous creates, edits, deletions, quota reservations, and job claims. Prevent lost updates, duplicate records, and operations against deleted or unauthorized resources.

checks.heading: State and concurrency
checks.text: REL-003 — Define idempotency keys and persistence lifetime for repeated API operations, jobs, and provider events. Verify that deduplication and business updates cannot leave an unprocessed event marked complete.

checks.heading: State and concurrency
checks.text: REL-004 — Check queue delivery guarantees, durable acknowledgment, retry bounds/backoff, dead-letter handling, and controlled replay. Jobs must survive the intended process/container restart behavior.

checks.heading: State and concurrency
checks.text: REL-005 — Recover expired leases, stuck states, orphaned files, missing objects, and partially completed external operations. Avoid cleanup that can delete valid active work.

checks.heading: State and concurrency
checks.text: REL-006 — Treat caches as rebuildable unless intentionally authoritative; document persistence and eviction assumptions for quota counters, sessions, and work coordination.

checks.heading: State and concurrency
checks.text: REL-007 — Double-click submit, retry after a timeout, and send equivalent concurrent create requests. Verify one intended order/booking/business record and one external side effect using persisted results, not only button state or HTTP status. Separate intentionally distinct submissions from retries of the same operation.

checks.heading: Query completeness and realistic data
checks.text: REL-008 — Seed more records than the configured API/page cap and traverse lists, search, exports, and background processing. Verify stable pagination, complete coverage, and no silent truncation or duplicated/skipped records. Supabase documents a default maximum of 1,000 returned rows; inspect the deployed setting and use pagination rather than assuming one response is complete. [Supabase fetch documentation](https://supabase.com/docs/reference/javascript/v1/select)

checks.heading: Query completeness and realistic data
checks.text: REL-009 — Measure frequent filters, joins, sorts, and tenant-scoped queries on realistic data volumes/distributions. Inspect query plans and relevant indexes, then verify latency against the project's target; a few dozen fixtures or an index on every column is not useful performance evidence.

checks.heading: Failure handling and migration prerequisites
checks.text: REL-010 — Bound downstream calls and use retries only when safe. Handle partial success, ambiguous provider results, timeout, disconnect, rate limits, and dependency outages without retry storms.

checks.heading: Failure handling and migration prerequisites
checks.text: REL-011 — Verify graceful shutdown, in-flight work handling, cancellation, and restart recovery. Reconcile work interrupted during deployment or host failure.

checks.heading: Failure handling and migration prerequisites
checks.text: REL-012 — Check disk-full, resource exhaustion, storage unavailability, corrupt/invalid data, and stale configuration behavior. Errors should preserve useful state and remain observable.

checks.heading: Failure handling and migration prerequisites
checks.text: REL-013 — Validate migration safety, compatibility between old/new application versions, and backup prerequisites. Code rollback and data rollback are different operations.

checks.heading: Backups and recovery
checks.text: REL-014 — Define RPO and RTO for each important dataset and service. Choose backup frequency and point-in-time recovery to meet them; daily backups are only sufficient when the tolerated data loss permits it.

checks.heading: Backups and recovery
checks.text: REL-015 — Inventory database data, uploads, objects, persistent volumes, configuration, encryption keys, and other non-rebuildable state. A VPS snapshot or control-plane backup alone may omit application state.

checks.heading: Backups and recovery
checks.text: REL-016 — Keep protected off-site copies with appropriate encryption, retention, and access separation. Consider immutable/versioned copies where the risk warrants them; avoid a production credential able to erase every recovery copy.

checks.heading: Backups and recovery
checks.text: REL-017 — Verify backup scheduling, freshness, completeness, and failure alerts. A successful job or existing file is not proof of recoverability.

checks.heading: Backups and recovery
checks.text: REL-018 — Verify the actual provider plan's backup availability, retention, and restore access. If managed recovery does not meet RPO/RTO, schedule and monitor an independent export with protected off-site retention. For Supabase Free projects, follow the documented regular export guidance rather than assuming usable managed backups; database backups do not include Storage objects. [Supabase backup documentation](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/platform/backups)

checks.heading: Backups and recovery
checks.text: REL-019 — Restore into an isolated fresh environment, inspect representative records/files, and run a representative application workflow. Measure actual loss window and restore time against RPO/RTO.

checks.heading: Backups and recovery
checks.text: REL-020 — Verify encryption-key and credential recovery through a secure external store. Align backup access, expiry, and restored deleted data with the retention/deletion process.

checks.heading: Backups and recovery
checks.text: REL-021 — Document recovery sequencing, data authority, and reconciliation of events that arrive while a service is unavailable. Test who can perform recovery if the normal operator is absent.

checks.heading: Data lifecycle and migration rehearsals
checks.text: REL-022 — Distinguish instants, local dates, and recurring wall-clock schedules. Preserve the timezone needed for future scheduling and test daylight-saving gaps/repeated hours, timezone changes, and user-visible reminder times.

checks.heading: Data lifecycle and migration rehearsals
checks.text: REL-023 — For PostgreSQL, store instants in `timestamptz` (or an equivalent instant-aware type in another database) and retain each user's IANA timezone separately for local reminders. An instant column does not preserve the user's original timezone; date-only values and future local schedules need their own appropriate representation.

checks.heading: Data lifecycle and migration rehearsals
checks.text: REL-024 — Where accidental-deletion recovery is promised, test soft delete or equivalent recovery, related records, uniqueness, retention expiry, and authorized restoration. Recovered data must preserve tenant boundaries and applicable deletion commitments.

checks.heading: Data lifecycle and migration rehearsals
checks.text: REL-025 — Rehearse forward migrations and the supported rollback or fail-forward path on representative data. Measure table-lock duration and concurrent traffic impact; use staged/backward-compatible changes where required by availability targets.

checks.heading: Data lifecycle and migration rehearsals
checks.text: REL-026 — Record a reversal/recovery plan for every schema migration. For reversible changes, keep reverse SQL or the migration tool's equivalent and run both directions on an isolated, sanitized production-shaped copy. For destructive/irreversible changes, document lost information and rehearse restore or fail-forward recovery; invented reverse SQL cannot recover dropped data. Record integrity checks and the old/new application's compatibility after recovery.

checks.heading: Data lifecycle and migration rehearsals
checks.text: REL-027 — Verify distributed scheduled jobs have coordinated ownership or equivalent deduplication so adding a replica does not duplicate business effects. Test daylight-saving changes and missed-run recovery.

checks.heading: Data lifecycle and migration rehearsals
checks.text: REL-028 — Maintain a disaster recovery plan covering dependency order, regional outage, and absence of the normal operator. Rehearse at the agreed risk-based interval (for example annually) and after material changes; add another region only when recovery/availability commitments require it.

checks.heading: Cross-cutting boundary and recovery cases
checks.text: REL-X01 — Verify correctness through client, API, database, queue, provider and generated artifact; a successful intermediate step does not establish completed business work.

checks.heading: Cross-cutting boundary and recovery cases
checks.text: REL-X02 — Repeat key cases across replicas, workers, old/new versions, tenants, roles and plan limits rather than assuming one process represents the deployed topology.

checks.heading: Cross-cutting boundary and recovery cases
checks.text: REL-X03 — Exercise the difference between graceful stop, hard process kill, host loss and persistent-volume loss in the permitted isolated scope; record which guarantees each test supports.

checks.heading: Cross-cutting boundary and recovery cases
checks.text: REL-X04 — Inspect ambiguous results after timeout/cancel/disconnect; delayed work or callbacks must not silently override a valid newer outcome.

checks.heading: Cross-cutting boundary and recovery cases
checks.text: REL-X05 — Test recovery when cache, replica, index or checkpoint is ahead of or behind restored authority; incompatible copies must not be treated as truth.

checks.heading: Cross-cutting boundary and recovery cases
checks.text: REL-X06 — Verify negative/failure responses leave explicit recoverable state; failure must not mean “nothing happened” when a side effect already completed.

checks.heading: Cross-cutting boundary and recovery cases
checks.text: REL-X07 — Reconcile old, delayed and replayed operations after cancellation, deletion, migration and restore using current lifecycle/authorization rules.

checks.heading: Cross-cutting boundary and recovery cases
checks.text: REL-X08 — Check observability reflects durable outcomes, invariant violations, backlog age and missing recovery coverage rather than only process uptime or successful HTTP responses.

checks.heading: Cross-cutting boundary and recovery cases
checks.text: REL-X09 — Validate recovery without the original operator, original host or undocumented local files; required access and instructions must exist outside the failed component.

checks.heading: Cross-cutting boundary and recovery cases
checks.text: REL-X10 — Check concurrent recovery/cleanup/reconciliation cannot duplicate effects or destroy valid slow work; repairs follow the same correctness rules as normal operations.

checks.heading: Cross-cutting boundary and recovery cases
checks.text: REL-X11 — Record workload, fault boundaries, measured outcomes and limitations; do not turn unexecuted recovery code or a mocked outage into a claim of proven disaster recovery.

checks.heading: Cross-cutting boundary and recovery cases
checks.text: REL-X12 — Reassess targets and evidence after changing providers, plans, persistence, topology, data volume, schema, keys or important background work.

checks.heading: Remediation and acceptance
checks.text: Original fault/overlap case satisfies [specific invariant/outcome].

checks.heading: Remediation and acceptance
checks.text: Relevant retry/restart/related-state cases checked: [ ].

checks.heading: Remediation and acceptance
checks.text: Affected complete workflow and durable external effects checked: [ ].

checks.heading: Remediation and acceptance
checks.text: Recovery or compatibility evidence updated if affected: [ ].

checks.heading: Identity and authorization
checks.text: Classify endpoints and operations as public, authenticated, service-only, or administrative. Enforce their policy on the server for APIs, server actions, WebSockets, jobs, and file access. Test denied requests directly rather than relying on hidden UI controls.

checks.heading: Identity and authorization
checks.text: Use two synthetic users or tenants to test read, create, update, delete, export, search, and shared-file boundaries. Derive ownership and roles from trusted identity rather than client-supplied fields. Follow least privilege and deny unspecified operations. [OWASP authorization guidance](https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Authorization_Cheat_Sheet.html)

checks.heading: Identity and authorization
checks.text: Verify password hashing through an established authentication library or provider; prefer a current Argon2id configuration for new self-managed password storage. Check reset token expiry, single use, account enumeration, OAuth redirect/state handling, and identity linking. [OWASP password storage](https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Password_Storage_Cheat_Sheet.html)

checks.heading: Identity and authorization
checks.text: Verify session expiry, revocation, logout, rotation where needed, and disabled-account behavior. For cookie sessions check Secure, HttpOnly, appropriate SameSite, narrow scope, and CSRF protection for state-changing operations; do not treat SameSite as the only control. [OWASP CSRF guidance](https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Cross_Site_Request_Forgery_Prevention_Cheat_Sheet.html)

checks.heading: Identity and authorization
checks.text: Protect sensitive admin operations with appropriate MFA or step-up authentication. Check recovery paths and avoid weakening access controls through support or demo flows.

checks.heading: Direct identity-boundary probes
checks.text: Using only the intentionally public frontend key and no login, attempt bounded reads and writes against each exposed database table/view, RPC, and storage surface. Record expected public access separately from private-data denial; never use a service key for this test. For client-accessible Supabase tables, verify RLS is enabled and policies constrain the actual anonymous/authenticated roles.

checks.heading: Direct identity-boundary probes
checks.text: As synthetic user A, replace resource/user/tenant IDs with B's in read, edit, delete, and export requests. Add `role: admin` or ownership fields to a profile update and try the equivalent direct database update. Verify no unauthorized data or privilege change, including when a response reports success.

checks.heading: Direct identity-boundary probes
checks.text: Redeem a password-reset link once, then replay it and verify the second attempt cannot reset the password. Test post-login `next`/return URLs with an external origin, protocol-relative `//` values, and `@` authority confusion; only approved destinations may be followed after URL parsing.

checks.heading: Secrets and data boundaries
checks.text: Ignore real environment files before committing; keep only placeholder examples. Inspect current source, Git history, built client assets, source maps, logs, CI artifacts, and container layers for secrets. Revoke or rotate exposed credentials; deleting a file or commit alone does not invalidate a key. [OWASP secrets guidance](https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Secrets_Management_Cheat_Sheet.html)

checks.heading: Secrets and data boundaries
checks.text: Keep privileged API, payment, signing, database, and AI credentials on trusted servers. Identify intentionally public client keys and verify their associated permissions. Missing required secrets must fail safely; no production fallback signing keys.

checks.heading: Secrets and data boundaries
checks.text: Scope service credentials per project and environment; define who can access, rotate, revoke, and recover them. Check whether OAuth refresh tokens or similar long-lived credentials need encryption with separately controlled keys.

checks.heading: Secrets and data boundaries
checks.text: Enforce tenant isolation at the appropriate database boundary. If using RLS, verify enabled policies for reads and writes using the real application roles, including roles that can bypass policies. PostgreSQL owners and privileged roles need special attention. RLS is conditional on the access model, not a universal requirement for every table. [PostgreSQL row security](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/ddl-rowsecurity.html)

checks.heading: Secrets and data boundaries
checks.text: Keep sensitive storage private by default; public assets need an explicit public-use decision. Validate access before issuing short-lived signed links; test expired and cross-tenant links.

checks.heading: Secrets and data boundaries
checks.text: Include AI chat histories and agent/tool artifacts in secret-exposure review; rotate any exposed live credentials. Verify encryption at rest for sensitive databases, files, and backups, including key access and recovery.

checks.heading: Input and request handling
checks.text: Validate types, bounds, identifiers, allowed fields, and business constraints at server boundaries. Use parameterized queries and safe process APIs; check NoSQL/operator injection, mass assignment, path traversal, and command execution too.

checks.heading: Input and request handling
checks.text: Escape output for its rendering context and sanitize deliberately supported rich HTML. Check user content, Markdown, imported content, and AI output; sanitizing input alone does not make every output context safe.

checks.heading: Input and request handling
checks.text: Constrain server-side URL fetching: block unintended private, loopback, metadata, and internal destinations, and recheck redirects and resolved addresses. Apply outbound controls to automated tools and preview/unfurl services.

checks.heading: Input and request handling
checks.text: For uploads verify size, count, allowed formats, content rather than filename alone, archive/decompression limits, controlled filenames, and safe serving headers. Store untrusted files in isolated persistent storage outside executable application paths; scan when the threat model warrants it. [OWASP file upload guidance](https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/File_Upload_Cheat_Sheet.html)

checks.heading: Input and request handling
checks.text: Configure CORS for the intended clients. Restrict credentialed and private APIs to appropriate origins; wildcard access can be valid for deliberately public unauthenticated resources. CORS does not authenticate requests or protect an API from non-browser clients.

checks.heading: Input and request handling
checks.text: Apply rate and concurrency controls to authentication, recovery, public forms, uploads, expensive endpoints, and automated requests. Trust client IP headers only from identified proxy hops; see 08 and 12.

checks.heading: Input and request handling
checks.text: Verify exported untrusted spreadsheet cells cannot unexpectedly execute formulas in the supported consumer workflow; preserve intended data and document any format-specific limitations. Apply export authorization and sensitive-data minimization independently.

checks.heading: Browser protection and privacy
checks.text: Render a harmless synthetic XSS probe such as `` in supported usernames, comments, Markdown, and imported content in an isolated browser. Verify it remains inert in each relevant rendering path, including admin views; a saved string or an HTTP success response alone proves neither safety nor execution.

checks.heading: Browser protection and privacy
checks.text: Where URL fetching exists, test loopback and metadata destinations (for example `http://localhost` and `http://169.254.169.254`) using controlled local targets or mocked egress. Correlate logs with the attempted fetch and verify rejection before any forbidden connection; do not probe a real metadata service or retrieve cloud credentials. Include redirects and address-resolution changes.

checks.heading: Browser protection and privacy
checks.text: After A visits a private page/API response, request the same URL as B and anonymously in separate sessions through the actual CDN/cache path. Verify A's content is never reused across identities; inspect cache keys and response headers as supporting evidence.

checks.heading: Browser protection and privacy
checks.text: Open hosting preview/deployment URLs in a browser without a platform session. Public previews may be intentional, but must not expose private data, secrets, admin routes, or bypass application authentication; verify access restrictions where preview privacy is required.

checks.heading: Browser protection and privacy
checks.text: Exercise the supported self-service data export and account-deletion paths. Confirm complete authorized export, session/access revocation, and erasure across active stores/vendors, with documented justified retention and backup expiry under 11. Where soft deletion is used, verify ordinary reads, searches, exports, and RLS policies hide deleted records; soft deletion alone does not fulfill an erasure promise.

checks.heading: Browser protection and privacy
checks.text: Enforce HTTPS and secure upstream connections. Test certificate renewal, redirects, mixed content, CSP, framing restrictions, content-type protection, and referrer policy. Enable HSTS only after confirming the intended HTTPS coverage; includeSubDomains/preload require separate validation.

checks.heading: Browser protection and privacy
checks.text: Return safe errors without internal stack traces, queries, or credentials. Redact secrets and unnecessary personal data from logs and monitoring; protect observability access and retention.

checks.heading: Browser protection and privacy
checks.text: Map personal data through databases, storage, analytics, exports, logs, backups, and subprocessors. Minimize collection and define lawful purpose, access, retention, export, deletion, and deletion effects on backups and derived data.

checks.heading: Browser protection and privacy
checks.text: Verify actual tracking and consent behavior against the applicable jurisdiction and privacy policy. Block consent-required tracking before consent, handle rejection and withdrawal, and distinguish essential storage. See 11 for legal interpretation and 16 for launch checks.

checks.heading: Browser protection and privacy
checks.text: Inspect session-replay/analytics payloads and recordings with synthetic inputs, including dynamically added fields, DOM text, URLs, chat, and network capture. Exclude credentials, payment data, and other prohibited content before transmission; test masking rather than trusting SDK defaults. Where consent is required, verify no capture/transmission before consent or after rejection/withdrawal, including tag-manager paths; restrict replay access and retention. Use 11 to determine permitted recording.

checks.heading: Account lifecycle and enterprise access
checks.text: Test signup, login, recovery, and identity linking with valid plus-addressed emails; avoid undocumented normalization that merges distinct identities. Verify MFA enrollment, lost-device recovery, and revocation of all sessions for one user.

checks.heading: Account lifecycle and enterprise access
