checks.text: Where enterprise identity is promised, test SSO including SAML if required, tenant binding, role/group mapping, and safe recovery access. For SCIM or other provisioning, verify offboarding revokes sessions, tokens, and downstream access within the agreed window.

checks.heading: Account lifecycle and enterprise access
checks.text: Verify fine-grained role and permission changes take effect across APIs, jobs, and cached sessions. Support impersonation, if offered, requires explicit authorization, visible operator context, bounded sessions, and an audit record of the operator, target, reason, and actions.

checks.heading: Account lifecycle and enterprise access
checks.text: Exercise login throttling and lockout recovery against password guessing and deliberate denial of access to a legitimate account. Coordinate distributed abuse controls with 08.

checks.heading: Security assurance and audit trails
checks.text: Define scoped independent security testing where warranted, a vulnerability disclosure contact and triage process, and periodic signed access reviews at the agreed interval (for example quarterly). Track remediation and retest evidence; use 11 for contractual assurance commitments.

checks.heading: Security assurance and audit trails
checks.text: For sensitive records where required, verify audit trails capture reads as well as changes, with actor, tenant, target, timestamp, and controlled retention. Protect records against unauthorized alteration and coordinate monitoring with 10.

checks.heading: Additional identity, browser and lifecycle boundaries
checks.text: Verify token issuer/audience/signature/key-source rules, refresh/revocation, MFA/step-up recovery and enterprise offboarding using the actual identity implementation. Include cached sessions, queued jobs and machine credentials.

checks.heading: Additional identity, browser and lifecycle boundaries
checks.text: Check database views/RPCs, privileged service/owner bypass and pooled tenant-context reuse, not only table-level policy toggles. Verify search/vector/analytics and export copies preserve authorization.

checks.heading: Additional identity, browser and lifecycle boundaries
checks.text: Inspect effective CSP, unpredictable response nonces, Trusted Types policies/integration and SRI where applicable. Report-only mode detects violations; browser compatibility and sanitizer configuration need explicit evidence.

checks.heading: Additional identity, browser and lifecycle boundaries
checks.text: Deliver Permissions-Policy through supported HTTP headers and intended iframe delegation. Review actual device data collection independently from browser permission prompts.

checks.heading: Additional identity, browser and lifecycle boundaries
checks.text: Verify untrusted merge/deserialization/process/path and spreadsheet/client-message handling with safe fixtures. A deep copy, public API key or hidden URL does not establish input safety or authority.

checks.heading: Additional identity, browser and lifecycle boundaries
checks.text: Inventory all personal-data sources/uses, derived AI artifacts, vendor settings/fallbacks, telemetry and support copies. Minimize collection and verify actual transmission against reviewed disclosures/choices.

checks.heading: Additional identity, browser and lifecycle boundaries
checks.text: Test export/correction/deletion completion, authorized identity, concurrent requests, delayed callbacks, soft-delete visibility and restore reconciliation. Record vendor/backup expiry and justified retention separately from UI completion.

checks.heading: Additional identity, browser and lifecycle boundaries
checks.text: Verify secret rotation at every consumer and actual old-key revocation; inspect source maps, images, CI caches, AI chats and tool artifacts. Hidden maps can remain reachable and deleting evidence of a key does not revoke it.

checks.heading: Additional identity, browser and lifecycle boundaries
checks.text: Bind dependency/build/security review to actual deployed versions and final configuration. Review updates proportionately rather than treating automatic audit-fix commands or scanner grades as assurance.

checks.heading: Additional identity, browser and lifecycle boundaries
checks.text: Rehearse scoped containment, audit/alert receipt and recovery without reactivating compromised access or deleted-account rights. Assign residual exposure and delayed confirmation to an accountable owner/date.

checks.heading: Assets, data and actors
checks.text: **SP-02-01** Record project, audit date/timezone, source/deployed revision, artifact/runtime, environments, configuration/flags, owners and current release/exposure. Identify disabled, legacy and planned features separately.

checks.heading: Assets, data and actors
checks.text: **SP-02-02** Enumerate public/private domains, APIs, server actions, WebSockets, mobile/desktop clients, databases, object stores, search indexes, queues, schedulers and administrative surfaces.

checks.heading: Assets, data and actors
checks.text: **SP-02-03** Inventory cloud/provider accounts, regions, identity systems, shared infrastructure, previews, old deployments and externally configured integrations. Mark inaccessible surfaces Not verified rather than assuming absence.

checks.heading: Assets, data and actors
checks.text: **SP-02-04** Classify sensitive business assets and personal data, including credentials, tokens, financial records, private content, location, identifiers, communications, embeddings and derived profiles where present.

checks.heading: Assets, data and actors
checks.text: **SP-02-05** Map actors and capabilities: anonymous visitor, user, member, owner, other tenant, support/admin, integration, worker, CI and provider. Include compromised low-privilege accounts and accidental operator misuse.

checks.heading: Assets, data and actors
checks.text: **SP-02-06** Identify authoritative sources for identity, role, ownership, tenant, price/entitlement and consent. Label untrusted identifiers, headers, claims, files, generated text and provider events.

checks.heading: Assets, data and actors
checks.text: **SP-02-07** Describe trust boundaries and data flows between browser/client, edge, service, worker, database, vendor and administrator. Include sync and async paths plus import/export and recovery flows.

checks.heading: Assets, data and actors
checks.text: **SP-02-08** Record per-asset owner, allowed operations, confidentiality/integrity/availability expectations, retention and recovery dependencies. Identify shared credentials and administrators with unusually broad reach.

checks.heading: Assets, data and actors
checks.text: **SP-02-09** Define intended public access explicitly for assets, database views/RPCs, storage and frontend keys. A public key's name does not establish either harmlessness or privileged access.

checks.heading: Threats and design decisions
checks.text: **SP-02-10** Model account takeover, cross-tenant access, privilege escalation, data exfiltration, injection, SSRF, insecure files, supply-chain compromise and harmful resource use relevant to the architecture.

checks.heading: Threats and design decisions
checks.text: **SP-02-11** Model accidental leaks through logs, analytics/session replay, support tickets, screenshots, CI artifacts, source maps, AI chats/tool artifacts and copied development datasets.

checks.heading: Threats and design decisions
checks.text: **SP-02-12** Consider automation/business misuse, stolen keys, malicious insiders, third-party compromise, old clients and long-delayed jobs/events. Link financial/capacity exposure to module 08.

checks.heading: Threats and design decisions
checks.text: **SP-02-13** Identify critical invariants such as no cross-tenant reads/writes, no client-assigned privileges, no unsigned event authority and no secret exposure to untrusted clients.

checks.heading: Threats and design decisions
checks.text: **SP-02-14** Document architectural defenses and limits: authorization point, service/DB roles, isolation, encryption/key control, egress controls, storage permissions and auditability. Avoid relying on one defense without testing its bypass roles.

checks.heading: Threats and design decisions
checks.text: **SP-02-15** Identify privacy purposes, sensitive populations/use cases, contractual commitments and relevant jurisdictions for accountable review. Determine whether additional privacy/security assessment is needed without inventing universal legal thresholds.

checks.heading: Threats and design decisions
checks.text: **SP-02-16** Record intentional exceptions and compensating controls, including public previews, support impersonation, shared services, offline clients and legacy integrations. Assign owner, scope, expiry and review trigger.

checks.heading: Safe, meaningful verification
checks.text: **SP-02-17** Record authorized systems/accounts, environments, techniques, data access, external effects and testing limits. Use synthetic identities and owned fixtures; follow existing authorization rather than requesting redundant permission.

checks.heading: Safe, meaningful verification
checks.text: **SP-02-18** Set request/concurrency/duration/cost and file-size ceilings, cancellation/cleanup and operator stop conditions. Avoid real metadata services, unsolicited messages, unrestricted scanning and destructive production tests.

checks.heading: Safe, meaningful verification
checks.text: **SP-02-19** Create at least two distinct synthetic users/tenants and the relevant service/admin roles for boundary tests. Use the same effective application roles and network paths as the deployed design.

checks.heading: Safe, meaningful verification
checks.text: **SP-02-20** Derive expected allowance/denial from product policy independently of current implementation. Pair denied operations with intended allowed operations so rejecting everything cannot pass.

checks.heading: Safe, meaningful verification
checks.text: **SP-02-21** Record direct sanitized requests, actual responses and resulting DB/storage/job/provider effects. A success response can hide a denied write, and an error can occur after an unauthorized side effect.

checks.heading: Safe, meaningful verification
checks.text: **SP-02-22** Distinguish source inspection, config review, local/staging execution and production evidence. Record untested scope, inaccessible providers, realistic sample sizes and relevant environment differences.

checks.heading: Safe, meaningful verification
checks.text: **SP-02-23** Select materially distinct routes, roles, tenants, policies, authentication methods, clients and failure states. Expand coverage after inconsistencies; do not infer every path from one passing endpoint.

checks.heading: Safe, meaningful verification
checks.text: **SP-02-24** Reuse meaningful tests and tools. Where material regression tests are needed, follow module 15's isolated test-sensitivity method; retain the smallest useful set, not a test mirroring every checklist sentence.

checks.heading: Safe, meaningful verification
checks.text: **SP-02-25** Protect audit evidence with redaction, restricted access and proportionate retention. Store correlation without live secrets, unnecessary personal records or portable exploit material against real targets.

checks.heading: Findings and decisions
checks.text: **SP-02-26** Distinguish verified defect, opportunity and verification gap; group shared root causes while recording all affected surfaces. Link existing specialist findings instead of duplicating them.

checks.heading: Findings and decisions
checks.text: **SP-02-27** Prioritize according to demonstrated access, data sensitivity, affected population, financial/availability impact, exploit prerequisites and confidence. A dependency severity score or missing header alone does not define business priority.

checks.heading: Findings and decisions
checks.text: **SP-02-28** Escalate active compromise/material exposure through the established incident process. Do not delay containment merely to complete an audit matrix; preserve evidence where doing so does not prolong harm.

checks.heading: Findings and decisions
checks.text: **SP-02-29** Assign remediation owner, acceptance test, dependencies, deadline and rollback/recovery approach. Risk acceptance requires an accountable decision, residual exposure and expiry, not a changed Pass status.

checks.heading: Findings and decisions
checks.text: **SP-02-30** Record ready / ready subject to recorded conditions / blocked / insufficient evidence for the audited scope. Bind it to the candidate and invalidate affected assurance after material code/config/policy/exposure changes.

checks.heading: Authentication and account lifecycle
checks.text: **SP-03-01** Inventory authentication methods, identity providers and account linking across web/native/API/admin clients. Identify authoritative subject identifiers and prevent ambiguous email/display-name mapping.

checks.heading: Authentication and account lifecycle
checks.text: **SP-03-02** For self-managed passwords, use a maintained authentication implementation and current suitable password hashing/configuration. Verify deployed storage, migration/rehash behavior and protection of reset/recovery credentials; do not invent a home-grown hash scheme.

checks.heading: Authentication and account lifecycle
checks.text: **SP-03-03** Test signup and verification for valid formats, plus-addressed emails, duplicate/racing creation and normalization rules. Do not merge distinct identities through undocumented canonicalization.

checks.heading: Authentication and account lifecycle
checks.text: **SP-03-04** Check login, signup and recovery responses/timing for material account enumeration. Balance consistent errors with usable legitimate recovery; verify logs/support do not reintroduce disclosure.

checks.heading: Authentication and account lifecycle
checks.text: **SP-03-05** Exercise guessing/throttling, distributed attempts and lockout recovery with tiny synthetic limits. Prevent both unlimited guessing and easy deliberate lockout of legitimate accounts.

checks.heading: Authentication and account lifecycle
checks.text: **SP-03-06** Verify reset/verification/magic-link tokens are appropriately generated, scoped, short-lived as policy requires and single-use where intended. Test replay, expiry, wrong account and simultaneous redemption.

checks.heading: Authentication and account lifecycle
checks.text: **SP-03-07** Check password/email/phone changes and identity linking/unlinking require appropriate current authorization or reauthentication. Verify attacker-controlled accounts cannot take over an existing subject through matching unverified attributes.

checks.heading: Authentication and account lifecycle
checks.text: **SP-03-08** Verify MFA enrollment, step-up, disablement, recovery codes, lost-device response and alternate support recovery. Protect high-impact actions without creating an easier recovery bypass.

checks.heading: Authentication and account lifecycle
checks.text: **SP-03-09** Where passkeys or hardware-backed credentials are offered, verify intended origin/RP, enrollment ownership, credential removal and recovery behavior using the provider's supported implementation.

checks.heading: Authentication and account lifecycle
checks.text: **SP-03-10** Test account suspension/deletion/reactivation for actual authentication and downstream access behavior. Retired users must not retain unintended sessions, API keys, pending invitations or background authority.

checks.heading: Sessions, cookies and tokens
checks.text: **SP-03-11** Verify session issuance, identifier rotation where needed, idle/absolute expiry and fixation protection. Record different policies for ordinary, privileged and machine sessions.

checks.heading: Sessions, cookies and tokens
checks.text: **SP-03-12** Test logout, all-session revocation, password reset and disabled-account behavior across devices, replicas, cached sessions and refresh tokens. Record actual revocation delay and any bounded exceptions.

checks.heading: Sessions, cookies and tokens
checks.text: **SP-03-13** For session cookies, verify Secure, HttpOnly, appropriate SameSite, host/domain/path scope and expiration. Choose attributes that preserve required SSO/payment flows while maintaining the intended boundary.

checks.heading: Sessions, cookies and tokens
checks.text: **SP-03-14** Verify state-changing cookie-authenticated requests have effective CSRF protection. Check origin/token validation, content types, browser cross-site behavior and alternate methods; SameSite alone is not universal assurance.

checks.heading: Sessions, cookies and tokens
checks.text: **SP-03-15** Validate bearer/JWT tokens with trusted issuer, audience, signature/algorithm policy, expiry and key source. Do not accept arbitrary token-supplied verification keys or trust decoded claims without validation.

checks.heading: Sessions, cookies and tokens
checks.text: **SP-03-16** Check signing-key rotation, unknown key IDs, stale JWKS/caches, clock skew and provider outage behavior. A verification error must not enable an authentication bypass.

checks.heading: Sessions, cookies and tokens
checks.text: **SP-03-17** Scope access/refresh/API tokens by purpose, audience, environment and permission. Inspect browser storage, URLs, logs and crash telemetry for token leakage; native clients need appropriate secure storage.

checks.heading: Sessions, cookies and tokens
checks.text: **SP-03-18** Test refresh reuse/rotation/revocation behavior according to the chosen protocol and implementation. Include parallel refresh and stolen/old credentials without exposing real tokens in evidence.

checks.heading: Federation and enterprise identity
checks.text: **SP-03-19** Verify OAuth/OIDC flow configuration, redirect allowlists, state/nonce and PKCE where required by the selected flow/client. Test login return URLs using URL parsing rather than prefix matching.

checks.heading: Federation and enterprise identity
checks.text: **SP-03-20** Test external-origin, protocol-relative, encoded and authority-confusion return URLs with controlled destinations. Approved local/partner navigation must remain usable without enabling open redirects or token disclosure.

checks.heading: Federation and enterprise identity
checks.text: **SP-03-21** For SSO/SAML, verify signed-response/assertion handling, audience/recipient, time/replay constraints and tenant binding through maintained libraries. Do not trust unverified domain/group claims.

checks.heading: Federation and enterprise identity
checks.text: **SP-03-22** Check role/group mappings, invitation acceptance, just-in-time provisioning and account linking across organizations. A user in one enterprise must not gain another tenant's membership through a shared email suffix or stale invitation.

checks.heading: Federation and enterprise identity
checks.text: **SP-03-23** For SCIM/provisioning/offboarding, verify authenticated scoped requests, group/role updates, deactivation and downstream session/token/job revocation within the agreed window.

checks.heading: Federation and enterprise identity
checks.text: **SP-03-24** Verify emergency/recovery access cannot defeat required enterprise restrictions or create permanent unmonitored superuser credentials. Record owner, audit and review of exceptions.

checks.heading: Object, role and tenant boundaries
checks.text: **SP-03-25** Classify every material operation as public, authenticated, service-only or administrative. Enforce policy server-side for APIs, server actions, workers, WebSockets, exports, search and storage.

checks.heading: Object, role and tenant boundaries
checks.text: **SP-03-26** Derive user, tenant, ownership and role from trusted context. Reject client-controlled role/admin/owner fields and mass assignment in profile, team, object-create and direct database paths.

checks.heading: Object, role and tenant boundaries
checks.text: **SP-03-27** With synthetic A/B tenants, replace IDs in read/create/update/delete/list/search/export/share requests, including nested parent/child IDs. Verify absence of forbidden records and side effects.

checks.heading: Object, role and tenant boundaries
checks.text: **SP-03-28** Verify field-level authorization for sensitive attributes, bulk operations, related objects, counts and existence checks. Filtering the main object alone may still disclose membership, secrets or private metadata.

checks.heading: Object, role and tenant boundaries
checks.text: **SP-03-29** Enforce permission changes, member removal, team/project moves and plan expiry across cached sessions, workers and queued work. State whether accepted work completes and how remaining liability is contained.

checks.heading: Object, role and tenant boundaries
checks.text: **SP-03-30** Check role inheritance, multi-membership, invitation/ownership transfer and last-owner/admin removal. Prevent accidental privilege growth or an unrecoverable tenant with no accountable owner.

checks.heading: Object, role and tenant boundaries
checks.text: **SP-03-31** Test intentional sharing/public links for scope, recipient requirements, expiry, revocation and download/derived-object behavior. Document remaining access from already issued bearer links or cached copies.

checks.heading: Object, role and tenant boundaries
checks.text: **SP-03-32** Verify least-privilege service identities, scheduled jobs and integration credentials. User initiation must not turn a privileged worker into a confused deputy for arbitrary tenant/resources.

checks.heading: Database and storage authorization
checks.text: **SP-03-33** For client-accessible database APIs, attempt bounded anonymous reads/writes using only the intentionally public client key and real public role. Separate intended public views/functions from private denial.

checks.heading: Database and storage authorization
checks.text: **SP-03-34** Where RLS is used, verify enabled policies and read/write/insert/update/delete checks for actual application roles. Inspect owners, privileged/service roles, views and functions that may bypass ordinary policy behavior.

checks.heading: Database and storage authorization
checks.text: **SP-03-35** Check pooled connection/session tenant context is set and reset safely across requests and jobs. Reused connections or elevated function execution must not inherit another tenant's authority.

checks.heading: Database and storage authorization
checks.text: **SP-03-36** For database RPCs, stored procedures and security-definer code, verify execution grants, tenant checks and relevant name-resolution/privilege settings. A protected table does not automatically protect every callable function.

checks.heading: Database and storage authorization
checks.text: **SP-03-37** Keep sensitive object stores private by default and validate access before generating signed upload/download links. Test cross-tenant keys, overwrite, completion callbacks, expiry and unintended broad prefixes.

checks.heading: Database and storage authorization
checks.text: **SP-03-38** Verify authorization for search/vector indexes, analytics queries, replicas and derived exports. Copying data from the primary store must not lose its tenant or deletion boundary.

checks.heading: Administrative and support access
checks.text: **SP-03-39** Require appropriate step-up/MFA and scoped authority for consequential admin operations, grants, exports, key access and security-setting changes. Test alternate APIs and bulk paths directly.

checks.heading: Administrative and support access
checks.text: **SP-03-40** Where support impersonation exists, require explicit permitted scope, visible operator context, bounded sessions and a protected record of actor, target, reason and actions. Prevent silent permanent takeover.

checks.heading: Administrative and support access
checks.text: **SP-03-41** Verify demo, support, break-glass and migration flows preserve material tenant/security boundaries. Exceptions require accountable ownership and expiry rather than an undocumented production bypass.

checks.heading: Administrative and support access
checks.text: **SP-03-42** Execute relevant revocation, tenant substitution, anonymous/RLS, replay and support cases from [09](09-VERIFICATION-SCENARIOS-AND-EVIDENCE.md). Record the exact application role and persisted/provider effects.

checks.heading: Validation, injection and output
checks.text: **SP-04-01** Validate schema/types, size, range, length, encoding, IDs and business constraints on the server before consequential work. Client validation improves usability but does not establish trust.

checks.heading: Validation, injection and output
checks.text: **SP-04-02** Allowlist writable properties for each role/operation and reject unexpected privilege, ownership and billing fields. Test nested objects and bulk endpoints, not only individual profile forms.

checks.heading: Validation, injection and output
checks.text: **SP-04-03** Use parameterized database queries and safe query-building APIs. Check dynamic identifiers/order/filter expressions and NoSQL/operator inputs that may fall outside parameter binding.

checks.heading: Validation, injection and output
checks.text: **SP-04-04** Avoid evaluating untrusted code/templates or constructing shell commands from input. Use safe process APIs and constrained executable/argument choices; include filenames, job options and admin tooling.

checks.heading: Validation, injection and output
checks.text: **SP-04-05** Verify path normalization and allowed-root enforcement for reads/writes/deletes, archives and exports. Include encoded paths, symlinks where relevant and cross-platform separator assumptions with safe fixtures.

checks.heading: Validation, injection and output
checks.text: **SP-04-06** Inspect unsafe deserialization, XML external entity resolution and parser features according to the stack. Disable unnecessary capabilities and bound parsing without testing against real internal services.

checks.heading: Validation, injection and output
checks.text: **SP-04-07** Prevent prototype-pollution paths in recursive merge, property assignment and configuration handling. Reject dangerous keys where appropriate; deep copying alone is not a sanitizer or authorization policy.

checks.heading: Validation, injection and output
checks.text: **SP-04-08** Encode output for its actual HTML/text/attribute/URL/JavaScript/CSS context. Prefer safe text APIs when markup is unnecessary; URL allowlists and encoding address different hazards.

checks.heading: Validation, injection and output
checks.text: **SP-04-09** Sanitize intentionally supported rich HTML with a maintained configuration. Cover Markdown, user profiles, imports, generated content, email previews and admin/support views; later unsafe mutation can undo sanitization.

checks.heading: Validation, injection and output
checks.text: **SP-04-10** Use a harmless isolated rendered probe to verify stored/reflected/DOM content stays inert on relevant paths. Inspect execution/DOM and effects, not merely that the server saved a string.

checks.heading: Validation, injection and output
checks.text: **SP-04-11** Bound expensive validation, regex, parsing, decompression, nesting and result expansion. Include malformed requests and failure paths that can exhaust CPU/memory before ordinary rate controls act.

checks.heading: Validation, injection and output
checks.text: **SP-04-12** Handle CSV/spreadsheet exports, PDFs, email headers and logs using destination-specific safety rules. Untrusted formulas, markup or control characters must not become commands or misleading audit records.

checks.heading: Browser defenses and content delivery
checks.text: **SP-04-13** Verify effective HTTP CSP and its actual enforcement/report-only state on important routes. Inventory script/style/connect/frame/worker/media dependencies and avoid a copied policy that silently allows the dangerous behavior.

checks.heading: Browser defenses and content delivery
checks.text: **SP-04-14** Where nonce-based CSP is used, generate unpredictable per-response nonces and bind them to authorized markup. Inspect cache/CDN transformations and avoid treating a literal example nonce as a production secret/control.

checks.heading: Browser defenses and content delivery
checks.text: **SP-04-15** Set appropriate frame-ancestors, base-uri and form-action explicitly where needed; they are not all covered by default-src. Deliver framing protection through a supported HTTP policy and test intended embedding.

checks.heading: Browser defenses and content delivery
checks.text: **SP-04-16** Assess unsafe-inline, unsafe-eval, broad origins, JSONP-like endpoints and user-controlled same-origin content against CSP effectiveness. Preserve required flows while addressing executable content sources.

checks.heading: Browser defenses and content delivery
checks.text: **SP-04-17** Where supported and justified, stage Trusted Types reporting, then verify enforcement and narrow policy creation. Audit policy sanitization; pass-through/default policies and unsupported browsers must not become the only XSS defense.

checks.heading: Browser defenses and content delivery
checks.text: **SP-04-18** For DOMPurify/Trusted Types integration, verify options and return types against the installed version and sink usage. Review policy callbacks rather than copying the baseline's typed-return example unchanged.

checks.heading: Browser defenses and content delivery
checks.text: **SP-04-19** Use SRI/version pinning where feasible for stable external scripts/styles and verify cross-origin CORS requirements. For dynamically changing vendors, record an alternative trust/update control instead of an unusable universal hash rule.

checks.heading: Browser defenses and content delivery
checks.text: **SP-04-20** Inventory third-party scripts, tag managers, polyfills and widgets, their administrators and data access. Self-host/vet/pin where appropriate and test failure or compromise containment within the threat model.

checks.heading: Browser defenses and content delivery
checks.text: **SP-04-21** Verify appropriate nosniff, Referrer-Policy, framing and cache headers across edge/origin/error routes. Do not equate a header-scanner grade with authorization or data-safety assurance.

checks.heading: Browser defenses and content delivery
checks.text: **SP-04-22** Deliver Permissions-Policy as an HTTP header, with deliberate iframe delegation where needed. Test actual camera/microphone/location use and denial; a meta http-equiv example is not equivalent policy delivery.

checks.heading: Browser defenses and content delivery
checks.text: **SP-04-23** Configure CORS for intended origins/credentials and inspect preflight plus actual responses. Broad access may be valid for public unauthenticated resources; CORS does not authenticate non-browser requests.

checks.heading: Browser defenses and content delivery
checks.text: **SP-04-24** Test sensitive cookie-authenticated actions against CSRF and relevant cross-origin behavior. Verify downloads, redirects and alternate content types do not create a state-changing bypass.

checks.heading: Browser defenses and content delivery
checks.text: **SP-04-25** Validate postMessage origin, source and message schema using controlled windows/frames. Avoid wildcard trust or interpreting untrusted messages as privileged commands.

checks.heading: Browser defenses and content delivery
checks.text: **SP-04-26** Check browser storage, service workers, offline caches, history/URLs and tab/shared-device behavior for sensitive persistence and account switching. Client logout must not leave another user access to private cached content.

checks.heading: Browser defenses and content delivery
checks.text: **SP-04-27** After synthetic A requests private content, repeat as B and anonymously through the actual CDN/cache path. Verify cache keys, headers and behavior prevent cross-identity reuse, including error and redirect responses.

checks.heading: Server-side fetches and integrations
checks.text: **SP-04-28** Inventory URL-fetch, unfurl, import, screenshot, webhook-test, conversion and agent-tool fetchers. Define permitted schemes, hosts, ports and destination classes according to actual product needs.

checks.heading: Server-side fetches and integrations
checks.text: **SP-04-29** Reject unintended loopback/private/link-local/metadata/internal destinations after parsing and resolution. Include IPv4/IPv6 and address forms supported by the runtime; verify through mocks or owned local fixtures.

checks.heading: Server-side fetches and integrations
checks.text: **SP-04-30** Revalidate redirect destinations and address-resolution changes at the effective connection boundary. Include proxy/egress routing and prevent leaking credentials across redirected origins.

checks.heading: Server-side fetches and integrations
checks.text: **SP-04-31** Bound outbound duration, redirects, response size, concurrency and content processing. Apply network/egress defenses where feasible without relying solely on a URL-string blacklist.

checks.heading: Server-side fetches and integrations
checks.text: **SP-04-32** Authenticate incoming callbacks before privileged processing using the provider's intended signature/token mechanism. Test duplicate/replayed/out-of-order events and enforce tenant/operation scope independently.

checks.heading: Server-side fetches and integrations
checks.text: **SP-04-33** Validate outbound webhook destination ownership and scoped secrets where needed, protect delivery logs and bound retries. A user-configured integration must not expose arbitrary internal endpoints.

checks.heading: Files and media
checks.text: **SP-04-34** Enforce upload count/bytes, allowed content, names, destination and processing policy server-side. Inspect actual content/metadata rather than trusting extension or client MIME alone.

checks.heading: Files and media
checks.text: **SP-04-35** Store untrusted files outside executable application paths and serve them with suitable content types/disposition/isolation. Review active HTML/SVG/documents according to permitted features and origin trust.

checks.heading: Files and media
checks.text: **SP-04-36** Authorize upload initiation, multipart completion, download, overwrite and deletion against actual tenant/object ownership. Constrain signed URLs and credentials by scope/expiry/platform capabilities.

checks.heading: Files and media
checks.text: **SP-04-37** Bound archive expansion, nesting, file count, media dimensions/duration and conversion work using small safe fixtures. Prevent traversal and resource exhaustion before durable writes or expensive processing.

checks.heading: Files and media
checks.text: **SP-04-38** Where scanning/content disarm is warranted, isolate/quarantine until the verdict and define unavailable/timeout behavior. A scanner result does not replace authorization or safe rendering.

checks.heading: Files and media
checks.text: **SP-04-39** Clean abandoned uploads, rejected files and failed derivatives under retention/recovery rules. Ensure processing errors do not leak paths, payloads or provider credentials.

checks.heading: API, realtime and client-specific edges
checks.text: **SP-04-40** Apply authorization and work-weight/complexity limits to GraphQL aliases/nesting, batch APIs, search, pagination, exports and bulk actions. One request may contain many expensive or privileged operations.

checks.heading: API, realtime and client-specific edges
checks.text: **SP-04-41** Authenticate/authorize WebSocket handshakes, subscriptions and individual consequential messages. Check origin, tenant changes, token expiry/revocation, reconnect and message-size/rate behavior.

checks.heading: API, realtime and client-specific edges
checks.text: **SP-04-42** Check API versions, route aliases, methods, content types and edge/origin parsing differences for bypassed controls. Use bounded owned fixtures for proxy/request-parsing assessments.

checks.heading: API, realtime and client-specific edges
checks.text: **SP-04-43** For native/desktop/mobile clients, validate deep links, IPC/plugin messages, update sources and local permissions relevant to the product. Client attestation or hidden endpoints do not replace server authorization.

checks.heading: API, realtime and client-specific edges
checks.text: **SP-04-44** Treat AI output, retrieved documents and tool responses as untrusted at rendering/action boundaries. Tool permissions and sensitive action authorization must remain independent of generated instructions.

checks.heading: API, realtime and client-specific edges
checks.text: **SP-04-45** Execute applicable browser, upload, injection, fetch, cache and API scenarios from [09](09-VERIFICATION-SCENARIOS-AND-EVIDENCE.md). Record allowed flows as well as denial and downstream effects.

checks.heading: Collection, purposes and exposure
checks.text: **SP-05-01** Map personal/sensitive data through forms, clients, APIs, databases, files, search/vector stores, analytics, logs, support, vendors and backups. Include identifiers, inferred attributes and derived outputs, not just explicit profile fields.

checks.heading: Collection, purposes and exposure
checks.text: **SP-05-02** Record purpose, accountable owner, collection source, necessity, recipients, access, region, retention and applicable commitments for each material data category. Flag unknown-purpose fields and unused exports/datasets.

checks.heading: Collection, purposes and exposure
checks.text: **SP-05-03** Minimize collection, precision, default visibility and retention to product needs. Examine hidden form fields, auto-collected SDK data, URLs, device IDs and unnecessary third-party enrichment.

checks.heading: Collection, purposes and exposure
checks.text: **SP-05-04** Verify privacy notices, user settings and product claims reflect actual flows and provider configuration. Compare runtime requests and stored data with reviewed disclosures, not only a policy-page checklist.

checks.heading: Collection, purposes and exposure
checks.text: **SP-05-05** Identify high-impact/sensitive use cases, vulnerable populations, children or special contractual restrictions for accountable assessment. Define product scope/exclusions and tailored review without assuming a universal age or legal threshold.

checks.heading: Collection, purposes and exposure
checks.text: **SP-05-06** Distinguish anonymization from pseudonymization and reversible identifiers. Document linkage/reidentification risks and access to lookup tables; hashing an email does not automatically make it anonymous.

checks.heading: Collection, purposes and exposure
checks.text: **SP-05-07** Restrict personal data in public profiles, shared links, directories, search snippets and notifications. Test default visibility, previews, counts and account-discovery behavior with synthetic identities.

checks.heading: Collection, purposes and exposure
checks.text: **SP-05-08** Review production-data use in development, QA, demos, screenshots, issue trackers and AI assistance. Prefer synthetic/minimized fixtures and control any justified copies with access, retention and deletion ownership.

checks.heading: Tracking, consent and device permissions
checks.text: **SP-05-09** Inventory cookies, local/session storage, pixels, beacons, analytics, replay, advertising, attribution and tag-manager rules across pages, clients and authenticated states.

checks.heading: Tracking, consent and device permissions
checks.text: **SP-05-10** Classify essential and optional processing with the project's reviewer. Where consent or another specific user choice is required, verify the actual pre-choice behavior and vendor calls, not merely a banner's presence.

checks.heading: Tracking, consent and device permissions
checks.text: **SP-05-11** Test accept/reject/selective choice, withdrawal, expiry and cross-device/account behavior against documented rules. Prevent a tag-manager, embedded widget or server-side relay bypassing the choice.

checks.heading: Tracking, consent and device permissions
checks.text: **SP-05-12** Keep collection/preferences coherent across login, logout, account switching, new SDK versions, locale and mobile/native clients. Do not silently merge unrelated users' identities or settings.

checks.heading: Tracking, consent and device permissions
checks.text: **SP-05-13** Request location/camera/microphone/contact/notification permissions in context with understandable purpose. Handle denial/revocation and avoid collecting or retaining more precise data than needed.

checks.heading: Tracking, consent and device permissions
checks.text: **SP-05-14** Verify device/iframe capabilities through effective Permissions-Policy and platform permissions. Permission to access a device feature is separate from permission to transmit or retain its data.

checks.heading: Tracking, consent and device permissions
checks.text: **SP-05-15** Inspect fingerprinting, persistent IDs, cross-site links and server-side tracking/enrichment against disclosed scope and reviewed requirements. Removing one cookie does not prove tracking stopped.

checks.heading: Telemetry, replay and communications
checks.text: **SP-05-16** Inspect actual analytics/error/replay payloads using synthetic secrets and personal fields in forms, DOM text, URLs, chat, dynamic components and network capture. Mask/exclude before transmission, not only in the vendor UI.

checks.heading: Telemetry, replay and communications
checks.text: **SP-05-17** Test replay masking on late-loaded fields, rich editors, attachments and account-switch states. Verify failure/default configuration does not record passwords, payment data or prohibited content.

checks.heading: Telemetry, replay and communications
checks.text: **SP-05-18** Verify consent-required capture/transmission stops before choice and after rejection/withdrawal, including buffer flushes, retries, tag-manager and server-side paths. Document any justified essential telemetry separately.

checks.heading: Telemetry, replay and communications
checks.text: **SP-05-19** Bound telemetry retention/cardinality, recipients and staff access. Check downloadable recordings, shared dashboards, support links and vendor administrator roles.

checks.heading: Telemetry, replay and communications
checks.text: **SP-05-20** Review emails/SMS/push notifications, receipts and support messages for sensitive content, lock-screen exposure, wrong recipients, reply threading and tenant context. Use approved synthetic recipients in tests.

checks.heading: Telemetry, replay and communications
checks.text: **SP-05-21** Restrict exports, reports, attachments and customer-support data to the appropriate operator/tenant. Check signed-link lifetime, logs, cached copies and external sharing defaults.

checks.heading: Vendors and AI processing
checks.text: **SP-05-22** Record processors/subprocessors, purpose, data sent, hosting/processing regions, retention, deletion capability, contractual/security commitments and accountable vendor owner.

checks.heading: Vendors and AI processing
checks.text: **SP-05-23** Verify actual provider account/settings and SDK defaults for training/reuse, logging, retention and regional routing where material. A marketing statement or another plan's guarantee is not evidence for this account.

checks.heading: Vendors and AI processing
checks.text: **SP-05-24** Check data transferred through middleware, proxies, integrations, backup providers and support tools. Include fallback providers and failover regions so outage behavior does not silently alter approved data flows.

checks.heading: Vendors and AI processing
checks.text: **SP-05-25** For AI features, inspect prompts, attachments, chat history, memory, embeddings, retrieval snippets, tool inputs/outputs and evaluation datasets for necessary scope and tenant isolation.

checks.heading: Vendors and AI processing
checks.text: **SP-05-26** Treat embeddings, summaries, derived profiles and model/provider logs as potentially sensitive where linkable. Define export/deletion/retention effects and avoid assuming deleting the source removes all derived data.

checks.heading: Vendors and AI processing
checks.text: **SP-05-27** Verify vendor offboarding, access revocation, data export/deletion and residual-retention confirmation under actual commitments. Distinguish a sent request from completed erasure.

checks.heading: Access, export, correction and deletion
checks.text: **SP-05-28** Define supported privacy/account requests, identity verification, authorized-agent handling where applicable, scope, ownership and required response timelines with accountable review.

checks.heading: Access, export, correction and deletion
checks.text: **SP-05-29** Test self-service/admin export as the legitimate synthetic subject and another tenant. Include relevant messages, files, settings and derived categories without exposing secrets or other users' data.

checks.heading: Access, export, correction and deletion
checks.text: **SP-05-30** Protect export generation, download, expiry and delivery channels. Avoid an unauthenticated permanent archive or a background job that runs with the wrong tenant authority.

checks.heading: Access, export, correction and deletion
checks.text: **SP-05-31** Test correction/deletion across active databases, object stores, indexes, caches, analytics, integrations and vendors. Record eventual processing and failures with retry/reconciliation ownership.

checks.heading: Access, export, correction and deletion
checks.text: **SP-05-32** Where soft deletion is used, verify ordinary reads/search/exports/RLS and unique-key/recreation behavior hide or handle retired records as intended. Soft deletion alone does not fulfill an erasure promise.

checks.heading: Access, export, correction and deletion
checks.text: **SP-05-33** On account deletion/offboarding, revoke sessions, refresh/API tokens, shares, integrations and pending work as policy requires. Protect shared/organization-owned data and explain retained records.

checks.heading: Access, export, correction and deletion
checks.text: **SP-05-34** Test duplicate, concurrent and interrupted export/delete requests plus late provider callbacks. Prevent re-created records, unbounded retries and a race that restores access after deletion.

checks.heading: Access, export, correction and deletion
checks.text: **SP-05-35** Verify privacy requests cannot be abused for account takeover, cross-tenant deletion, insider access or unauthorized disclosure. Support recovery must not be an easier path than normal identity checks.

checks.heading: Retention, backups and evidence
checks.text: **SP-05-36** Define retention/deletion schedules by data category and system with justified exceptions, legal holds and accountable owners. Verify actual lifecycle tasks and vendor settings rather than policy text alone.

checks.heading: Retention, backups and evidence
checks.text: **SP-05-37** Check backups, replicas, object versions, logs and disaster-recovery copies for access and bounded expiry. Document why immediate removal may differ from active-store deletion under reviewed commitments.

checks.heading: Retention, backups and evidence
checks.text: **SP-05-38** Prevent restored backups, replayed imports or delayed sync from silently resurrecting deleted users/data contrary to policy. Maintain a proportionate reconciliation/deletion mechanism for restored state.

checks.heading: Retention, backups and evidence
checks.text: **SP-05-39** Verify encryption/access control for retained sensitive stores and exports, including key recovery and authorized use. Encryption does not remove purpose, access or retention responsibilities.

checks.heading: Retention, backups and evidence
checks.text: **SP-05-40** Record evidence of actual completion, justified retention and unresolved vendor/backup expiry. Assign an owner/date to delayed confirmation; a UI success message is not proof of system-wide erasure.

checks.heading: Retention, backups and evidence
checks.text: **SP-05-41** Reassess data flows after new SDKs/providers, regions, AI features, collection fields, user populations or product purposes. Update notices/settings/reviews before relying on earlier assurance.

checks.heading: Retention, backups and evidence
checks.text: **SP-05-42** Execute applicable consent, replay-payload, export/delete, vendor and restore cases from [09](09-VERIFICATION-SCENARIOS-AND-EVIDENCE.md). Keep sanitized evidence separate from real personal data.

checks.heading: Secret discovery and lifecycle
checks.text: **SP-06-01** Inventory privileged API/database/payment/signing/AI credentials, OAuth refresh tokens, SSH/deploy keys, webhook secrets and recovery material. Record owner, consumers, environment, privilege, rotation and revocation route without copying values.

checks.heading: Secret discovery and lifecycle
checks.text: **SP-06-02** Inspect current source, relevant history, real environment files, examples, built frontend assets, source maps, CI artifacts, package archives and container layers for secret exposure.

checks.heading: Secret discovery and lifecycle
checks.text: **SP-06-03** Inspect logs, errors, monitoring/replay, support exports, screenshots, AI chats and agent/tool artifacts for credentials or unnecessary sensitive payloads. Review artifacts outside the repository as part of scope.

checks.heading: Secret discovery and lifecycle
checks.text: **SP-06-04** Keep intentionally public client keys separate from privileged secrets and verify their associated roles. A public key is safe only within an enforced permission design, not because it is labeled public.

checks.heading: Secret discovery and lifecycle
checks.text: **SP-06-05** Verify real environment/secret files are excluded from new commits and placeholders contain no working credentials. Ignoring a file does not remove an existing historical exposure.

checks.heading: Secret discovery and lifecycle
checks.text: **SP-06-06** Revoke/rotate exposed credentials, update all consumers and confirm the old credential is ineffective through safe verification. Deleting a file/commit, rewriting history or hiding a source map does not invalidate a stolen key.

checks.heading: Secret discovery and lifecycle
checks.text: **SP-06-07** Scope service secrets per environment/project/role and restrict who can read, issue, rotate, revoke and recover them. Check shared accounts and long-lived keys for excessive blast radius.

checks.heading: Secret discovery and lifecycle
checks.text: **SP-06-08** Use appropriate secret storage/injection rather than distributing secrets in clients, images or downloadable configuration. Verify permissions on temporary files, process/environment exposure and CI output.

checks.heading: Secret discovery and lifecycle
checks.text: **SP-06-09** Ensure missing required production secrets fail safely, with no fallback signing/password keys, debug bypass or accidental live/test provider substitution.

checks.heading: Secret discovery and lifecycle
checks.text: **SP-06-10** Rehearse proportionate rotation/revocation with scoped fixtures, including queued jobs, cached connections and rollout overlap. Document how emergency revocation affects service and recovery.

checks.heading: Cryptography and key access
checks.text: **SP-06-11** Use maintained platform/library cryptography appropriate to the data and protocol; avoid custom algorithms, static nonces/IVs and embedded master keys. Verify implementation-specific configuration with current primary guidance.

checks.heading: Cryptography and key access
checks.text: **SP-06-12** Verify encryption in transit and at rest for sensitive databases/files/backups and long-lived credentials where required by the threat model. Record actual provider settings, key ownership and trust boundary.

checks.heading: Cryptography and key access
checks.text: **SP-06-13** Separate encrypted data from unnecessary key access; restrict decrypt/export/admin privileges and protect audit records. Disk encryption alone does not isolate authorized application roles or compromised accounts.

checks.heading: Cryptography and key access
checks.text: **SP-06-14** Verify key generation, versioning, rotation, recovery and destruction against data lifetime. Test old/new key readability and recovery without destroying the sole usable key or production copy.

checks.heading: Cryptography and key access
checks.text: **SP-06-15** Identify risks from URL/bearer tokens, signatures, hashes and pseudonymous IDs. Do not treat encoding/hashing as encryption or assume secrets remain safe merely because the database disk is encrypted.

checks.heading: Build and dependency integrity
checks.text: **SP-06-16** Bind release artifacts to source/build/runtime/configuration and verify deployed versions. Inspect application packages, base images, OS/runtime components, plugins, SDKs and client-bundled code.

checks.heading: Build and dependency integrity
checks.text: **SP-06-17** Run suitable dependency/image/security checks with recorded tool/database dates and scope. Triage affected versions, reachability and exposure; a scanner's empty output or severity score is incomplete assurance.

checks.heading: Build and dependency integrity
checks.text: **SP-06-18** Verify maintained/supported dependencies and update ownership. Evaluate fixes using compatibility/relevant tests; do not run automatic dependency upgrades merely because the baseline lists an audit-fix command.

checks.heading: Build and dependency integrity
checks.text: **SP-06-19** Review lockfiles, registry/source selection, install/build hooks, downloaded binaries and dependency-confusion/typosquatting risks where applicable. Protect publishing and organization/package ownership.

checks.heading: Build and dependency integrity
checks.text: **SP-06-20** Protect CI/workflow definitions, runners, caches and artifacts from untrusted contribution execution or privilege escalation. Scope workflow tokens and production secrets; inspect alternate/manual release paths.

checks.heading: Build and dependency integrity
checks.text: **SP-06-21** Verify promotion/signing/update verification appropriate to distributed packages and containers. Mutable tags, public download links or an unsigned manifest must not silently replace the reviewed release.

checks.heading: Build and dependency integrity
checks.text: **SP-06-22** Inventory third-party JS/CSS/polyfills and tag-manager changes alongside backend dependencies. Record version/integrity/trust/update controls and administrators who can inject code into production.

checks.heading: Build and dependency integrity
checks.text: **SP-06-23** Review production source-map policy and actual reachability on CDN/origin/build artifacts. Hidden maps can still be served; restrict sensitive original sources/secrets while retaining approved debugging capability.

checks.heading: Build and dependency integrity
checks.text: **SP-06-24** Check artifact retention, access and cleanup for secrets and personal data. Include old releases, failed builds, preview bundles, caches and deleted-branch environments.

checks.heading: Transport and deployed configuration
checks.text: **SP-06-25** Verify TLS/certificates, redirects, renewal and intended upstream encryption for actual domains, callbacks, APIs, database connections and management interfaces. Inspect mixed content and insecure failover paths.

checks.heading: Transport and deployed configuration
checks.text: **SP-06-26** Enable HSTS only after required HTTPS coverage and recovery implications are verified. includeSubDomains and preload need separate domain-wide review; copied values are not universally appropriate.

checks.heading: Transport and deployed configuration
checks.text: **SP-06-27** Restrict exposed ports, database/cache/admin consoles, debug endpoints and management APIs. Check previews, old deployments, origin IPs and alternate IPv4/IPv6 routes within permitted scope.

checks.heading: Transport and deployed configuration
checks.text: **SP-06-28** Verify trusted proxy hops, forwarded identity/host/scheme handling, allowed hosts and edge/origin rules. Untrusted headers must not grant internal trust, bypass limits or poison links/caches.

checks.heading: Transport and deployed configuration
checks.text: **SP-06-29** Verify runtime/container privileges, user identity, mounts, filesystem access, service isolation and resource limits against actual application needs. A non-root image alone does not prove host isolation.

checks.heading: Transport and deployed configuration
checks.text: **SP-06-30** Check remote administration, SSH/access gateways, firewall/egress controls and provider dashboard MFA/recovery. Preserve a separately controlled emergency access path with accountable ownership.

checks.heading: Transport and deployed configuration
checks.text: **SP-06-31** Isolate production/staging/local credentials, provider callbacks, data and networks where required. Verify tests/previews cannot write real customer data, send unintended messages or invoke production privileges.

checks.heading: Transport and deployed configuration
checks.text: **SP-06-32** Validate effective feature flags, safe defaults, diagnostics and security configuration after clean install, restart, deploy, rollback and failover. Record drift from code-defined intent.

checks.heading: Recovery and ownership
checks.text: **SP-06-33** Protect backups/snapshots/configuration exports and recovery accounts with appropriate access, retention and off-host availability. Verify restore can recover required keys without exposing them to ordinary users.

checks.heading: Recovery and ownership
checks.text: **SP-06-34** Check restore/rollback cannot reintroduce exposed keys, permissive policies, deleted-account access or outdated vulnerable artifacts. Reconcile old credentials and security state explicitly.

checks.heading: Recovery and ownership
checks.text: **SP-06-35** Confirm organization-controlled domain/repository/provider ownership, billing/recovery contacts, primary/backup administrators and patch responsibilities. Avoid a sole recovery path tied to one person's device or memory.

checks.heading: Recovery and ownership
checks.text: **SP-06-36** Execute applicable secret, artifact, transport, source-map, configuration and recovery scenarios from [09](09-VERIFICATION-SCENARIOS-AND-EVIDENCE.md). Retain sanitized proof of old-key rejection and deployed state where claimed.

checks.heading: Security records and detection
checks.text: **SP-07-01** Define material audit events: authentication/recovery, role/tenant changes, admin/support access, credential changes, exports/deletes, policy/config changes and consequential denied attempts.

checks.heading: Security records and detection
checks.text: **SP-07-02** Where sensitivity/commitments require read auditing, capture important record reads as well as writes. Record trusted actor/service, tenant, target, operation, outcome, time and correlation without unnecessary payloads.

checks.heading: Security records and detection
checks.text: **SP-07-03** Protect event integrity, access and retention. Restrict deletion/alteration, prevent untrusted text from forging events and retain appropriate time synchronization and correlation across services.

checks.heading: Security records and detection
checks.text: **SP-07-04** Verify logs/errors/traces do not expose credentials, session tokens, personal payloads or private queries. Test redaction with synthetic markers before transmission and inspect real telemetry paths.

checks.heading: Security records and detection
checks.text: **SP-07-05** Detect meaningful account/privilege changes, unusual exports, repeated boundary violations, suspicious credential use and relevant data/vendor access. Choose signals based on actual exposure and operator capacity.

checks.heading: Security records and detection
checks.text: **SP-07-06** Exercise controlled relevant alerts through actual delivery, acknowledgement and escalation. Record accountable recipients, response availability and an accessible runbook; configuration alone is not receipt evidence.

checks.heading: Security records and detection
checks.text: **SP-07-07** Bound event/alert volume, key cardinality, retention and ingestion cost during abuse. Preserve useful aggregated evidence while preventing security monitoring from becoming an availability/spend problem.

checks.heading: Security records and detection
checks.text: **SP-07-08** Restrict observability, support/replay and audit-dashboard access by role/tenant. Check shared links, downloadable exports, vendor staff access and offboarding of former responders.

checks.heading: Access and vulnerability management
checks.text: **SP-07-09** Review actual user/service/admin/provider access at an agreed risk-based cadence and after important personnel/architecture changes. Record reviewer, date, exceptions and completed revocations.

checks.heading: Access and vulnerability management
checks.text: **SP-07-10** Verify offboarding removes sessions, keys, group membership, provider consoles, repositories, support tools and downstream integrations within the agreed window. Check dormant and emergency accounts.

checks.heading: Access and vulnerability management
checks.text: **SP-07-11** Maintain a vulnerability disclosure/contact and triage route appropriate to the product. Test accountable receipt with a synthetic harmless report; do not solicit or perform unauthorized third-party testing.

checks.heading: Access and vulnerability management
checks.text: **SP-07-12** Track security advisories, dependency/runtime/provider changes and patch ownership. Define severity/response based on affected scope, business exposure and relevant commitments.

checks.heading: Access and vulnerability management
checks.text: **SP-07-13** Commission scoped independent testing where risk/commitments warrant it. Record scope, permission, exclusions and final-revision applicability rather than treating an old penetration-test label as blanket assurance.

checks.heading: Access and vulnerability management
checks.text: **SP-07-14** Track remediation with owner, acceptance criteria, deadline and focused retest. Preserve original findings and root-cause reasoning; suppressions/risk exceptions need rationale, accountability and expiry.

checks.heading: Access and vulnerability management
checks.text: **SP-07-15** Review security-relevant changes independently through the established process. Verify effective review/gate execution on the final revision; installing a review plugin does not establish that a review happened.

checks.heading: Incident preparation and containment
checks.text: **SP-07-16** Assign incident lead, technical responder, privacy/legal reviewer and communication duties proportionate to team size. Record primary/backup availability, authority and emergency contacts.

checks.heading: Incident preparation and containment
checks.text: **SP-07-17** Keep runbooks for exposed keys, account takeover, cross-tenant access, sensitive telemetry, malicious files, provider compromise and data loss relevant to the system.

checks.heading: Incident preparation and containment
checks.text: **SP-07-18** Ensure runbooks, recovery references and incident communication remain accessible during host/app/provider failure. Rehearse authorized emergency access without printing credentials in evidence.

checks.heading: Incident preparation and containment
checks.text: **SP-07-19** Verify scoped containment: revoke keys/sessions, disable vulnerable features, suspend accounts, block unsafe egress, pause queues and stop costly tools. Include retries, child tasks and old deployments.

checks.heading: Incident preparation and containment
checks.text: **SP-07-20** Record residual exposure from already downloaded data, cached content, signed links, uncancellable remote work and delayed revocation. A kill switch cannot retract every earlier disclosure or external action.

checks.heading: Incident preparation and containment
checks.text: **SP-07-21** Preserve relevant redacted evidence, timeline, affected versions, identities and provider records while avoiding unnecessary duplication of sensitive material. Do not let evidence collection delay urgent containment.

checks.heading: Incident preparation and containment
checks.text: **SP-07-22** Assess actual/potential data, integrity, availability and financial impact with explicit unknowns. Distinguish confirmed access from possible exposure and use accountable review for notification/contractual duties.

checks.heading: Incident preparation and containment
checks.text: **SP-07-23** Prepare internal/customer/vendor communication and support handling as appropriate. Any actual messages follow task authorization and the established incident process; the audit itself does not send them.

checks.heading: Recovery, release and closure
checks.text: **SP-07-24** Verify recovery restores safe permissions, current keys, deletion/offboarding state and data integrity. Prevent rollback or restore from reactivating compromised access or replaying forbidden effects.

checks.heading: Recovery, release and closure
checks.text: **SP-07-25** Restore service gradually after containment with monitored limits and known-good state. Define re-engagement conditions for stops and check delayed retries/callbacks cannot reopen the exposure.

checks.heading: Recovery, release and closure
checks.text: **SP-07-26** Reconcile vendor copies, exposed credentials, customer requests and incomplete cleanup. Assign owner/date to delayed confirmation instead of claiming complete eradication from code changes alone.

checks.heading: Recovery, release and closure
checks.text: **SP-07-27** Capture lessons and verified corrective actions after material incidents. Track recurring root causes and procedure failures, not merely a completed postmortem document.

checks.heading: Recovery, release and closure
checks.text: **SP-07-28** Bind release/security decisions to code, artifact, runtime/config/policies, exposure and evidence time. Unverified critical controls and material active exposure may prevent a confident release decision.

checks.heading: Recovery, release and closure
checks.text: **SP-07-29** Reassess after new features, data categories, AI tools, vendors, regions, roles and client platforms. Review expired exceptions and inherited infrastructure evidence before carrying assurance forward.

checks.heading: Recovery, release and closure
checks.text: **SP-07-30** Execute applicable audit, alert, offboarding, containment/restore and regression cases from [09](09-VERIFICATION-SCENARIOS-AND-EVIDENCE.md). Record residual gaps, accepted risk and operational handoff explicitly.

checks.heading: Security (critical)
checks.text: HTTPS enabled, no mixed content

checks.heading: Security (critical)
checks.text: No vulnerable dependencies (`npm audit`)

checks.heading: Security (critical)
checks.text: CSP headers configured (with `frame-ancestors`, `base-uri`, `form-action`)

checks.heading: Security (critical)
checks.text: `require-trusted-types-for 'script'` enforced (or report-only during rollout)

checks.heading: Security (critical)
checks.text: Third-party `<script>`/`<link rel="stylesheet">` pinned with SRI hashes

checks.heading: Security (critical)
checks.text: Security headers present (HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy)

checks.heading: Security (critical)
checks.text: No exposed source maps (and `sourcesContent` stripped from uploaded ones)

checks.text: Valid HTML5 doctype

checks.heading: Compatibility
checks.text: Charset declared first in head

checks.heading: Compatibility
checks.text: Viewport meta tag present

checks.heading: Compatibility
checks.text: No deprecated APIs used

checks.heading: Compatibility
checks.text: Passive event listeners for scroll/touch

checks.heading: Code quality
checks.text: No console errors

checks.heading: Code quality
checks.text: Valid HTML (no duplicate IDs)

checks.heading: Code quality
checks.text: Semantic HTML elements used

checks.heading: Code quality
checks.text: Proper error handling

checks.heading: Code quality
checks.text: Memory cleanup in components

checks.heading: UX
checks.text: No intrusive interstitials

checks.heading: UX
checks.text: Permission requests in context

checks.heading: UX
checks.text: Clear error messages

checks.heading: UX
checks.text: Appropriate image aspect ratios

checks.heading: Release boundaries and accountable expectations
checks.text: **PLN-01 — Release identity.** Compare intended source revision, build artifact, configuration, schema, flags, and deployment targets.

checks.heading: Release boundaries and accountable expectations
checks.text: **PLN-02 — Change impact map.** Trace changed code, configuration, dependencies, data shape, infrastructure, interfaces, and shared consumers.

checks.heading: Release boundaries and accountable expectations
checks.text: **PLN-03 — Core outcomes and invariants.** Ask product/domain owners for required journeys, forbidden effects, and important state/financial/data rules.

checks.heading: Release boundaries and accountable expectations
checks.text: **PLN-04 — Exposure and consequence.** Inventory audiences, roles, tenants, data sensitivity, costly work, public surfaces, and indirect affected people.

checks.heading: Release boundaries and accountable expectations
checks.text: **PLN-05 — Independent expected results.** Review the source of expected values, reference calculations, policy examples, and defect reproductions.

checks.heading: Release boundaries and accountable expectations
checks.text: **PLN-06 — Owner competence and availability.** Identify implementation, review, verification, go/no-go, recovery, and incident responsibilities.

checks.heading: Release boundaries and accountable expectations
checks.text: **PLN-07 — Supported environment contract.** Record supported browsers/devices, operating systems, regions, languages, protocols, provider versions, and accessibility requirements.

checks.heading: Release boundaries and accountable expectations
checks.text: **PLN-08 — Verification authority and limits.** Record permitted environments, test identities, allowed operations, data classes, load budgets, and prohibited effects.

checks.heading: Smallest useful verification portfolio
checks.text: **PLN-09 — Existing assurance inventory.** Review current manual records, tests, checks, monitors, contract fixtures, and prior valid defect evidence.

checks.heading: Smallest useful verification portfolio
checks.text: **PLN-10 — Risk to evidence mapping.** Map each critical behavior and boundary to method, environment, actor, sample, expected outcome, and artifact.

checks.heading: Smallest useful verification portfolio
checks.text: **PLN-11 — Appropriate check level.** Compare pure-rule, component, integration, end-to-end, exploratory, and deployed checks for each material risk.

checks.heading: Smallest useful verification portfolio
checks.text: **PLN-12 — Durable test admission.** For each proposed automated check identify distinct risk, likely recurrence, existing equivalent checks, owner, and maintenance cost.

checks.heading: Smallest useful verification portfolio
checks.text: **PLN-13 — Duplicate and implementation-coupled checks.** Inspect assertions, mocks, snapshots, helper code, and overlapping cases for equivalent assurance.

checks.heading: Smallest useful verification portfolio
checks.text: **PLN-14 — Regression value.** Review meaningful fixed defects, failure modes, and safe reproduction evidence against retained checks.

checks.heading: Smallest useful verification portfolio
checks.text: **PLN-15 — Sampling and combinatorial scope.** Select representative boundaries, pairwise combinations where useful, high-consequence interactions, and known incident cases.

checks.heading: Smallest useful verification portfolio
checks.text: **PLN-16 — Coverage metric interpretation.** Compare line/branch metrics with missing behaviors, dead code, assertion quality, and excluded files.

checks.heading: Planning and scope evolution
checks.text: **PLN-17 — Time and budget constraints.** Estimate execution, environment setup, review, reconciliation, cleanup, and recovery reserve.

checks.heading: Planning and scope evolution
checks.text: **PLN-18 — Third-party and inherited assurance.** Review vendor reports, shared infrastructure results, component ownership, and the conditions under which evidence applies.

checks.heading: Planning and scope evolution
checks.text: **PLN-19 — Specialist routing.** Identify AI, payments, accessibility, migrations, safety-critical, regulated, and platform-specific risks.

checks.heading: Planning and scope evolution
checks.text: **PLN-20 — Acceptance gates before execution.** Agree critical invariants, success measures, error budgets, tolerances, and escalation authority before collecting results.

checks.heading: Planning and scope evolution
checks.text: **PLN-21 — Plan drift and change triggers.** Compare the approved plan with subsequent commits, flags, provider changes, and environment drift.

checks.heading: Planning and scope evolution
checks.text: **PLN-22 — Exclusions and unresolved scope.** Review unsupported features, unavailable access, ambiguous requirements, and accepted risks.

checks.heading: Functional boundaries and state transitions
checks.text: **FUN-01 — Essential journey completion.** Run scoped create/read/update/delete and other core tasks with required artifacts and persisted state.

checks.heading: Functional boundaries and state transitions
checks.text: **FUN-02 — State-machine transitions.** Exercise valid, invalid, repeated, skipped, terminal, and reversed transitions against independently reviewed rules.

checks.heading: Functional boundaries and state transitions
checks.text: **FUN-03 — Input validation and business rules.** Use missing, extra, null, incorrectly typed, malformed, negative, boundary, and conflicting values.

checks.heading: Functional boundaries and state transitions
checks.text: **FUN-04 — Empty large and sparse data.** Exercise empty lists, absent optional data, maximum supported sizes, sparse records, and many related objects.

checks.heading: Functional boundaries and state transitions
checks.text: **FUN-05 — Numeric and monetary semantics.** Compare rounding, decimal precision, percentages, units, large identifiers, currency, and aggregation against reference examples.

checks.heading: Functional boundaries and state transitions
checks.text: **FUN-06 — Date time and reset boundaries.** Test time zones, daylight-saving changes, leap/day/month boundaries, expiry, scheduled resets, and clock differences where relevant.

checks.heading: Functional boundaries and state transitions
checks.text: **FUN-07 — Search filter sort and pagination.** Use duplicates, stable tie values, changing datasets, escaped queries, empty pages, and repeated cursors.

checks.heading: Functional boundaries and state transitions
checks.text: **FUN-08 — Persistence and refresh.** Write data then reload, change device/replica, restart a disposable process, and read through supported paths.

checks.heading: Concurrency and interrupted workflows
checks.text: **FUN-09 — Concurrent mutation conflicts.** Issue competing updates and versioned writes from synthetic users to the same scoped record.

checks.heading: Concurrency and interrupted workflows
checks.text: **FUN-10 — Duplicate request handling.** Repeat identical requests concurrently and after timeout using the intended operation identity.

checks.heading: Concurrency and interrupted workflows
checks.text: **FUN-11 — Stale tabs and optimistic UI.** Act from old tabs, undo local previews, and fail a server mutation after optimistic rendering.

checks.heading: Concurrency and interrupted workflows
checks.text: **FUN-12 — Partial multi-step operations.** Fail between durable workflow steps and resume using recorded progress.

checks.heading: Concurrency and interrupted workflows
checks.text: **FUN-13 — Session interruption and resume.** Disconnect or expire a session during upload, draft edit, checkout, or other supported task.

checks.heading: Concurrency and interrupted workflows
checks.text: **FUN-14 — Cancellation and final outcome.** Cancel before work starts, during execution, and after an external system accepts the operation.

checks.heading: Concurrency and interrupted workflows
checks.text: **FUN-15 — Background ownership and backlog.** Run multiple workers/schedulers and restart one amid representative queued work.

checks.heading: Concurrency and interrupted workflows
checks.text: **FUN-16 — Cache and replica consistency.** Exercise cache misses/stale entries, replica lag, invalidation, and read-after-write paths.

checks.heading: Contracts imports and specialized variants
checks.text: **FUN-17 — Consumer and provider contract accuracy.** Compare deployed schemas, errors, event versions, compatibility promises, and official provider documentation.

checks.heading: Contracts imports and specialized variants
checks.text: **FUN-18 — Malformed and partial upstream results.** Return wrong types, unknown enums, incomplete pages, partial batches, bad encodings, and oversized responses.

checks.heading: Contracts imports and specialized variants
checks.text: **FUN-19 — Callback ordering and reconciliation.** Deliver valid/invalid, duplicate, delayed, missing, and out-of-order synthetic provider events.

checks.heading: Contracts imports and specialized variants
checks.text: **FUN-20 — Import export and transformation fidelity.** Round-trip representative records/files with permissions, Unicode, units, encoding, version metadata, and relationships.

checks.heading: Contracts imports and specialized variants
checks.text: **FUN-21 — Property and metamorphic checks.** Where suitable, define independent invariants or transformations such as round trips, monotonicity, conservation, and order independence.

checks.heading: Contracts imports and specialized variants
checks.text: **FUN-22 — Bounded fuzz and parser verification.** Use controlled generated malformed/edge inputs for exposed parsers and structured boundaries with explicit budgets.

checks.heading: Contracts imports and specialized variants
checks.text: **FUN-23 — Mobile desktop and offline variants.** If supported, test application lifecycle, permission prompts, upgrade compatibility, local storage, offline edits, and later synchronization.

checks.heading: Contracts imports and specialized variants
checks.text: **FUN-24 — AI and probabilistic output variants.** If AI or probabilistic decisions are present, route representative tasks, repeats, human scoring, and forbidden outcomes through module 07.

checks.heading: Actors authorization and denied effects
checks.text: **ADV-01 — Actor and permission matrix.** Exercise anonymous, ordinary, same-tenant, other-tenant, disabled, removed, and administrator actors where relevant.

checks.heading: Actors authorization and denied effects
checks.text: **ADV-02 — Direct object and nested resource access.** Substitute synthetic record, file, conversation, export, child-resource, and list/filter identifiers.

checks.heading: Actors authorization and denied effects
checks.text: **ADV-03 — Role changes and authorization freshness.** Revoke membership, downgrade roles, disable accounts, and expire sessions while work is queued or paused.

checks.heading: Actors authorization and denied effects
