checks.text: **ADV-04 — Alternative path parity.** Attempt the same restricted operation through UI, API, mobile, batch, legacy endpoint, callback, and internal worker paths.

checks.heading: Actors authorization and denied effects
checks.text: **ADV-05 — Forbidden-data absence.** Use unique synthetic private canaries and inspect responses, exports, logs, traces, model context, cache, and outbound requests as relevant.

checks.heading: Actors authorization and denied effects
checks.text: **ADV-06 — Forbidden side-effect absence.** Attempt denied writes, messages, payments, jobs, and destructive actions with stubbed effect ledgers.

checks.heading: Actors authorization and denied effects
checks.text: **ADV-07 — Session identity and account mixing.** Swap session/account context, callback transaction identifiers, device profiles, and tab identities under synthetic users.

checks.heading: Actors authorization and denied effects
checks.text: **ADV-08 — Positive controls for denials.** Pair each material denial test with a matching permitted operation through the same feature path.

checks.heading: Input trust and abuse scenarios
checks.text: **ADV-09 — Untrusted input execution boundaries.** Use harmless injection-shaped text in supported HTML/SQL/command/template/formula/file inputs and downstream outputs.

checks.heading: Input trust and abuse scenarios
checks.text: **ADV-10 — Network and file destination control.** Exercise controlled URL redirects/DNS changes, unsupported schemes, path traversal, and file ownership cases.

checks.heading: Input trust and abuse scenarios
checks.text: **ADV-11 — Credential and secret exposure.** Seed synthetic secret canaries into approved protected fixtures and inspect builds, client output, error paths, and evidence exports.

checks.heading: Input trust and abuse scenarios
checks.text: **ADV-12 — Replay and consequential authorization.** Replay callbacks, approvals, verification tokens, payment intents, and action identifiers using altered targets where relevant.

checks.heading: Input trust and abuse scenarios
checks.text: **ADV-13 — Quota and budget enforcement.** Exercise bounded repeated requests, parallel accounts, large inputs, retries, recursive tools, and bulk actions.

checks.heading: Input trust and abuse scenarios
checks.text: **ADV-14 — Enumeration and information differences.** Compare supported response/timing behavior for existing and nonexistent synthetic accounts/resources.

checks.heading: Input trust and abuse scenarios
checks.text: **ADV-15 — Privacy lifecycle and deletion.** Delete/revoke synthetic data and inspect histories, caches, indexes, exports, pending work, and isolated restored backups.

checks.heading: Input trust and abuse scenarios
checks.text: **ADV-16 — AI and untrusted instruction surfaces.** If AI exists, place harmless hostile instructions in retrieved files, media, history, or tool results.

checks.heading: Controlled faults and sensitivity
checks.text: **ADV-17 — Dependency outage and degraded mode.** Fail a scoped provider/database/cache/queue connection with bounded stubs or disposable infrastructure.

checks.heading: Controlled faults and sensitivity
checks.text: **ADV-18 — Timeout after effect commit.** Let a stub commit an operation then suppress the response and trigger recovery.

checks.heading: Controlled faults and sensitivity
checks.text: **ADV-19 — Worker crash and restart.** Kill a disposable worker at receipt, persistence, effect, and acknowledgment checkpoints.

checks.heading: Controlled faults and sensitivity
checks.text: **ADV-20 — Storage pressure and resource exhaustion.** Apply bounded disposable disk/memory/connection/quota pressure with explicit stop conditions.

checks.heading: Controlled faults and sensitivity
checks.text: **ADV-21 — Clock randomness and race control.** Control clocks, randomness, and concurrency where needed to reproduce expiry, retry, reset, and race defects.

checks.heading: Controlled faults and sensitivity
checks.text: **ADV-22 — Known-bad fixture sensitivity.** Use a safely recorded bad fixture or known vulnerable pre-fix revision for an important regression check.

checks.heading: Controlled faults and sensitivity
checks.text: **ADV-23 — Safe targeted mutation.** If needed, introduce one meaningful defect in an isolated disposable copy with no production credentials or live consequences.

checks.heading: Controlled faults and sensitivity
checks.text: **ADV-24 — Fault cleanup and uncertainty.** Inspect stopped processes, test flags, altered policies, fixture data, budgets, and missing observability after each fault rehearsal.

checks.heading: User experience and supported platforms
checks.text: **EXP-01 — Representative browser and device matrix.** Choose supported engine/browser/OS/device combinations from commitments, usage, known incidents, and feature risk.

checks.heading: User experience and supported platforms
checks.text: **EXP-02 — Older supported hardware.** Run relevant journeys on a constrained older supported laptop/mobile device or a documented representative approximation.

checks.heading: User experience and supported platforms
checks.text: **EXP-03 — Responsive layout and content extremes.** Use narrow/wide viewports, long labels, translations, empty/large data, zoom, and orientation changes.

checks.heading: User experience and supported platforms
checks.text: **EXP-04 — Interaction and input methods.** Exercise keyboard, mouse, touch, pointer alternatives, paste, autofill, and virtual keyboard where supported.

checks.heading: User experience and supported platforms
checks.text: **EXP-05 — Loading error and interrupted states.** Induce slow/failed requests, offline transitions, partial results, empty data, and permission changes.

checks.heading: User experience and supported platforms
checks.text: **EXP-06 — Navigation and session continuity.** Test deep links, refresh, browser back/forward, multi-tab behavior, session expiry, and return after login.

checks.heading: User experience and supported platforms
checks.text: **EXP-07 — Localization and time presentation.** Exercise supported languages, right-to-left layout, local dates/numbers, time zones, and translated errors/actions.

checks.heading: User experience and supported platforms
checks.text: **EXP-08 — Native and installable application lifecycle.** Where relevant, test install/update/rollback, startup, permission prompts, backgrounding, suspension, and local storage upgrade.

checks.heading: Accessibility and human review
checks.text: **EXP-09 — Keyboard focus and semantics.** Manually traverse critical journeys including dialogs, menus, forms, async updates, and errors.

checks.heading: Accessibility and human review
checks.text: **EXP-10 — Screen-reader core journeys.** Use supported assistive-technology/browser combinations for forms, tables, generated/streaming content, and recovery.

checks.heading: Accessibility and human review
checks.text: **EXP-11 — Visual perception and motion.** Check contrast, zoom/reflow, text scaling, reduced motion, high-contrast settings, and color-independent meaning.

checks.heading: Accessibility and human review
checks.text: **EXP-12 — Accessible authentication and failure recovery.** Exercise login, verification challenges, session timeout, payment errors, opt-out, and human/non-AI alternatives.

checks.heading: Accessibility and human review
checks.text: **EXP-13 — Manual versus automated evidence.** Compare static/automated results with observed keyboard, screen-reader, responsive, and representative-user review.

checks.heading: Accessibility and human review
checks.text: **EXP-14 — Usability and domain review.** Have representative users or competent reviewers attempt high-consequence or confusing workflows with realistic tasks.

checks.heading: Accessibility and human review
checks.text: **EXP-15 — Visual regression meaning.** Review screenshot differences for user impact and layout behavior against the actual rendered target.

checks.heading: Accessibility and human review
checks.text: **EXP-16 — Browser privacy and storage policies.** Test relevant cookie restrictions, storage denial, private browsing, third-party contexts, and permission rejection.

checks.heading: Performance network and bounded capacity
checks.text: **EXP-17 — Poor network and intermittent connectivity.** Run relevant core journeys under constrained bandwidth, latency, loss, and disconnection using controlled profiles.

checks.heading: Performance network and bounded capacity
checks.text: **EXP-18 — User-perceived performance.** Measure appropriate real/user-visible milestones and task completion alongside request latency.

checks.heading: Performance network and bounded capacity
checks.text: **EXP-19 — Representative load model.** Define arrival pattern, concurrency, dataset, cache state, background work, duration, and critical paths before a load run.

checks.heading: Performance network and bounded capacity
checks.text: **EXP-20 — Authorized capacity execution.** Run only bounded permitted workloads with quotas, monitoring, cost limits, and stop conditions.

checks.heading: Performance network and bounded capacity
checks.text: **EXP-21 — Shared contention and cold states.** Include relevant builds, backups, workers, cache misses, startup, and neighboring host workloads.

checks.heading: Performance network and bounded capacity
checks.text: **EXP-22 — Endurance and resource leaks.** Where risk justifies it, run a bounded longer-lived representative workload while watching memory, disk, handles, pools, and queues.

checks.heading: Performance network and bounded capacity
checks.text: **EXP-23 — Failure and recovery under load.** Within scope, introduce controlled throttling or worker interruption while load remains bounded.

checks.heading: Performance network and bounded capacity
checks.text: **EXP-24 — Performance comparison limits.** Compare baseline/candidate samples with equivalent workload and configuration, including variability and saturation.

checks.heading: Required check execution
checks.text: **PIP-01 — Required gate inventory.** List required build, lint, type, test, dependency, container, signing, and other checks for the actual stack.

checks.heading: Required check execution
checks.text: **PIP-02 — Discovery and zero-test detection.** Inspect executed test discovery, filters, sharding, skipped suites, and expected critical test selection.

checks.heading: Required check execution
checks.text: **PIP-03 — Exit status and failure propagation.** Force a safe known failing fixture in a disposable pipeline copy and inspect wrappers, shell pipes, allow-failure settings, and report upload steps.

checks.heading: Required check execution
checks.text: **PIP-04 — Conditions paths and workflow triggers.** Compare PR, merge, push, release, manual, scheduled, path-filtered, and reusable workflow execution.

checks.heading: Required check execution
checks.text: **PIP-05 — Skipped canceled and stale checks.** Review intentionally skipped, canceled, timed-out, quarantined, and older-revision check results.

checks.heading: Required check execution
checks.text: **PIP-06 — Parallel shard completeness.** Interrupt one shard, fail setup, and inspect aggregate results from matrix jobs and merged reports.

checks.heading: Required check execution
checks.text: **PIP-07 — Dependency and container findings.** Review actual scan/build results, reachability context, exceptions, and base-image/dependency versions.

checks.heading: Required check execution
checks.text: **PIP-08 — Independent review freshness.** Bind required security/domain review to the final source/configuration/artifact and introduce a relevant later change.

checks.heading: Untrusted code and execution environment
checks.text: **PIP-09 — Untrusted contribution isolation.** Review fork/PR builds, external contributions, install hooks, test scripts, and artifact consumption paths.

checks.heading: Untrusted code and execution environment
checks.text: **PIP-10 — CI credential scope.** Inspect token permissions, cloud identities, registry access, signing/deployment rights, and secret exposure paths.

checks.heading: Untrusted code and execution environment
checks.text: **PIP-11 — Runner cleanup and trust.** Compare isolated/ephemeral and reused runner behavior with workspace, caches, containers, credentials, and concurrent jobs.

checks.heading: Untrusted code and execution environment
checks.text: **PIP-12 — Cache poisoning and dependency trust.** Attempt a harmless controlled cache/artifact substitution across trust boundaries in isolation.

checks.heading: Untrusted code and execution environment
checks.text: **PIP-13 — Tool and action provenance.** Inspect downloaded scripts, CI actions/plugins, package registries, pinned references, integrity records, and actual permissions.

checks.heading: Untrusted code and execution environment
checks.text: **PIP-14 — Dependency resolution and lockfiles.** Build from a clean environment with recorded lockfiles, registry configuration, runtime and tool versions.

checks.heading: Untrusted code and execution environment
checks.text: **PIP-15 — Build versus runtime configuration.** Change build-time/public and runtime/private variables in a disposable environment and inspect resulting behavior/assets.

checks.heading: Untrusted code and execution environment
checks.text: **PIP-16 — Reproducibility and retrieval.** Retrieve the exact evaluated build or rebuild under the documented process in a clean controlled environment.

checks.heading: Artifact and deployment identity
checks.text: **PIP-17 — Artifact manifest and digest.** Record package/image/binary digest, source revision, dependencies, config/schema references, and generation process.

checks.heading: Artifact and deployment identity
checks.text: **PIP-18 — Artifact provenance and verification.** Where selected, verify trusted producer/build provenance, signatures/attestations, and deployment admission policy.

checks.heading: Artifact and deployment identity
checks.text: **PIP-19 — Build once promote evidence.** Trace how tested artifacts reach staging and production, including any rebuild or packaging change.

checks.heading: Artifact and deployment identity
checks.text: **PIP-20 — Platform and native dependency parity.** Run the release artifact on actual supported OS/CPU/runtime combinations and required native binaries.

checks.heading: Artifact and deployment identity
checks.text: **PIP-21 — Production-like topology.** Compare proxy/network, environment injection, filesystem, worker startup, database pools, persistence, and replicas.

checks.heading: Artifact and deployment identity
checks.text: **PIP-22 — Schema configuration and flag bundle.** Associate migration state, feature flag values, tool/provider settings, and secrets references with the release manifest.

checks.heading: Artifact and deployment identity
checks.text: **PIP-23 — Evidence artifact integrity and access.** Inspect result manifests, reports, traces, uploads, permissions, retention, and links to immutable revisions.

checks.heading: Artifact and deployment identity
checks.text: **PIP-24 — Rollback artifact availability.** Retrieve the last compatible approved artifact and its configuration/migration requirements through recovery access.

checks.heading: Deployment mechanics and readiness
checks.text: **DEP-01 — Versioned deployment rehearsal.** Execute the actual intended deployment process using the recorded candidate bundle on isolated infrastructure.

checks.heading: Deployment mechanics and readiness
checks.text: **DEP-02 — Readiness and liveness behavior.** Delay dependencies and simulate a sick process while observing routing, health checks, and restart decisions.

checks.heading: Deployment mechanics and readiness
checks.text: **DEP-03 — Graceful drain and shutdown.** Redeploy during active requests, uploads, streams, and background work in a disposable environment.

checks.heading: Deployment mechanics and readiness
checks.text: **DEP-04 — Mixed-version compatibility.** Run old and new app/worker/client versions together against supported schema/message/cache states.

checks.heading: Deployment mechanics and readiness
checks.text: **DEP-05 — Scheduler and worker activation.** Deploy multiple replicas and transition old/new schedules, queue consumers, and event handlers.

checks.heading: Deployment mechanics and readiness
checks.text: **DEP-06 — Feature flag activation.** Change flags, targeting, defaults, dependencies, and cached values with synthetic users across roles/tenants.

checks.heading: Deployment mechanics and readiness
checks.text: **DEP-07 — Origin and public path proof.** Use traceable requests through final DNS/TLS/edge/proxy paths and correlate destination artifact and logs.

checks.heading: Deployment mechanics and readiness
checks.text: **DEP-08 — Post-deploy smoke scope.** Run a small useful set of read/write, identity, permission, integration, and operational journeys for the changed release.

checks.heading: Data-safe recovery and failure rehearsal
checks.text: **DEP-09 — Backup inventory and access.** Identify database/files/keys/configuration/provider settings needed for recovery and verify protected alternate access.

checks.heading: Data-safe recovery and failure rehearsal
checks.text: **DEP-10 — Representative isolated restore.** Restore a representative selected backup to a disposable environment and run data/permission/core-journey checks.

checks.heading: Data-safe recovery and failure rehearsal
checks.text: **DEP-11 — Recovery time and loss measurement.** Measure critical-path restore/redeploy/reconcile time and committed state checkpoints under the rehearsed failure.

checks.heading: Data-safe recovery and failure rehearsal
checks.text: **DEP-12 — Rollback before new state.** Rehearse returning to the known compatible release before destination/new-version writes or effects occur.

checks.heading: Data-safe recovery and failure rehearsal
checks.text: **DEP-13 — Rollback after new writes.** Create synthetic new records, files, queued work, and external effects then rehearse reversal or reconciliation.

checks.heading: Data-safe recovery and failure rehearsal
checks.text: **DEP-14 — Schema and irreversible boundary.** Test rollback compatibility after additive/backfill/destructive schema phases and identify no-return transitions.

checks.heading: Data-safe recovery and failure rehearsal
checks.text: **DEP-15 — Restart outage and regional scope.** Where required, simulate process/host/provider loss and relevant recovery dependency order with approved stubs or isolation.

checks.heading: Data-safe recovery and failure rehearsal
checks.text: **DEP-16 — Rollback and recovery cleanup.** Inspect restored writers, jobs, credentials, test flags, temporary environments, and reconciliation after rehearsal.

checks.heading: Controlled exposure and operational decision
checks.text: **DEP-17 — Rollout population and stages.** Define who receives a canary/staged release, its duration, traffic representativeness, and activation prerequisites.

checks.heading: Controlled exposure and operational decision
checks.text: **DEP-18 — Baseline and candidate comparison.** Compare error, latency, task success, important slice behavior, backlog, cost, and invariants under comparable conditions.

checks.heading: Controlled exposure and operational decision
checks.text: **DEP-19 — Pause and recovery thresholds.** Predeclare journey, unauthorized-effect, data, financial, latency, error, backlog, and capacity triggers as relevant.

checks.heading: Controlled exposure and operational decision
checks.text: **DEP-20 — Monitoring and alert readiness.** Trigger scoped synthetic new-version failures and inspect metric labels, dashboards, alert routing, and runbook links.

checks.heading: Controlled exposure and operational decision
checks.text: **DEP-21 — Disablement and queued work.** Turn off the feature/release while jobs, callbacks, retries, streams, or offline clients remain active.

checks.heading: Controlled exposure and operational decision
checks.text: **DEP-22 — Hotfix and emergency release.** Rehearse the reduced emergency verification/approval path against actual high-consequence boundaries.

checks.heading: Controlled exposure and operational decision
checks.text: **DEP-23 — Observation and delayed effects.** Select an observation window covering relevant user cycles, schedules, renewals, caches, and delayed provider events.

checks.heading: Controlled exposure and operational decision
checks.text: **DEP-24 — Operational handover.** Have a backup operator diagnose, pause, recover, and locate the final evidence/runbook using documented access.

checks.heading: Execution evidence and result integrity
checks.text: **EVD-01 — Run identity and prerequisites.** Capture actor, environment, source revision, artifact/config/schema versions, UTC time, inputs, prerequisites, and method.

checks.heading: Execution evidence and result integrity
checks.text: **EVD-02 — Expected actual and effect evidence.** Record independent expected allowed/denied behavior, response, persisted state, and external/stub effects.

checks.heading: Execution evidence and result integrity
checks.text: **EVD-03 — Status classification.** Review Pass, Fail, Not verified, and Not applicable assignments against artifacts and scope.

checks.heading: Execution evidence and result integrity
checks.text: **EVD-04 — Product failure versus harness failure.** Inspect failing setup, fixtures, credentials, network, test runner, assertions, and application behavior.

checks.heading: Execution evidence and result integrity
checks.text: **EVD-05 — Skipped checks and quarantine.** Review every required skip, ignored failure, timeout, quarantine, and temporarily disabled assertion.

checks.heading: Execution evidence and result integrity
checks.text: **EVD-06 — Flakiness diagnosis and retries.** Repeat only as justified to examine races, environment variability, nondeterminism, or unreliable assertions and retain all outcomes.

checks.heading: Execution evidence and result integrity
checks.text: **EVD-07 — Samples uncertainty and populations.** Record tested cases/actors, counts, dataset selection, repetitions, failure frequencies, and estimated affected population derivation.

checks.heading: Execution evidence and result integrity
checks.text: **EVD-08 — Evidence provenance and contradiction.** Compare raw logs/traces, reports, screenshots, source/configuration, external outcomes, and conflicting runs.

checks.heading: Release decision and independent review
checks.text: **EVD-09 — Independent security review at final revision.** Verify required security-relevant review happened after implementation and remains valid for final material changes.

checks.heading: Release decision and independent review
checks.text: **EVD-10 — AI and tool claim verification.** Inspect commands, exit codes, artifacts, check selection, versions, and findings behind generated test/review claims.

checks.heading: Release decision and independent review
checks.text: **EVD-11 — Severity confidence and exposure.** Assess realistic consequences and prerequisites separately from confidence, current exposure, priority, and blocker status.

checks.heading: Release decision and independent review
checks.text: **EVD-12 — Root-cause deduplication.** Group related observations by verified root cause across controls and shared modules.

checks.heading: Release decision and independent review
checks.text: **EVD-13 — Critical verification gaps.** Identify missing executed evidence for required access, integrity, financial, safety, recovery, or other high-consequence boundaries.

checks.heading: Release decision and independent review
checks.text: **EVD-14 — Risk acceptance and conditions.** Review named owner, rationale, compensating controls, monitored limits, expiry, and authority for each accepted issue.

checks.heading: Release decision and independent review
checks.text: **EVD-15 — Go no-go record.** Consolidate failed/passed controls, gaps, inherited evidence, scope limitations, recovery, and observations.

checks.heading: Release decision and independent review
checks.text: **EVD-16 — Action ownership and retest.** Give accepted actions owners, dates, independent acceptance, dependencies, and fix evidence.

checks.heading: Retention reduction and lifecycle
checks.text: **EVD-17 — Session-created artifact review.** Review every new test, helper, fixture, snapshot, mock, recording, screenshot, output and test-only dependency.

checks.heading: Retention reduction and lifecycle
checks.text: **EVD-18 — Small useful regression placement.** Place retained necessary checks in the project's existing test structure with owner, fixtures, safe instructions, and expected outcomes.

checks.heading: Retention reduction and lifecycle
checks.text: **EVD-19 — Evidence retention and confidentiality.** Apply scoped access, redaction, expiry, integrity, and records obligations to reports, traces, data, and recordings.

checks.heading: Retention reduction and lifecycle
checks.text: **EVD-20 — Unresolved finding preservation.** Before deleting temporary artifacts, identify proof needed for unresolved issues, accepted exceptions, incidents, or required records.

checks.heading: Retention reduction and lifecycle
checks.text: **EVD-21 — Obsolete test and dependency retirement.** Review removed features, changed contracts, duplicate coverage, brittle snapshots, stale fixtures, and unused test-only packages.

checks.heading: Retention reduction and lifecycle
checks.text: **EVD-22 — Review tool and plugin adoption.** Evaluate optional review/test plugins for compatibility, provenance, permissions, cost, outputs, and actual configured triggers.

checks.heading: Retention reduction and lifecycle
checks.text: **EVD-23 — Incident and change feedback.** Turn meaningful production defects, support patterns, provider changes, and newly exposed risks into bounded review items.

checks.heading: Retention reduction and lifecycle
checks.text: **EVD-24 — Audit closure and next review.** Reconcile the final revision, evidence, blockers, conditions, cleanup, operational owners, and next change/review triggers.

checks.heading: Meaningful coverage
checks.text: Link core user outcomes and important business invariants to existing automated or manual checks. Identify missing evidence for authentication, permissions, data writes, costly work, and payments where present.

checks.heading: Meaningful coverage
checks.text: First reuse existing checks. Where an uncovered material risk requires a durable test, prefer unit checks for complex pure rules, integration checks for real boundaries, and a small useful end-to-end set for essential journeys. Delete tests that merely repeat implementation details or duplicate equivalent assurance; do not add tests automatically for every session or reversible low-impact edit.

checks.heading: Meaningful coverage
checks.text: Test allowed and denied role/tenant operations directly. Include anonymous, normal user, another tenant, disabled account, and admin behavior where applicable.

checks.heading: Meaningful coverage
checks.text: Cover validation, empty/large data, duplicate requests, concurrent actions, stale state, timezone/reset boundaries, and interrupted sessions according to the feature.

checks.heading: Meaningful coverage
checks.text: Verify timeout, external outage, exhausted budget, failed payment, invalid callback, job restart, and other meaningful failure paths using controlled faults.

checks.heading: Meaningful coverage
checks.text: Combine automated UI checks with manual keyboard/screen-reader and responsive journeys under 02/03. Include a constrained mobile device/network when relevant.

checks.heading: Release environment and tooling
checks.text: Run the relevant build, lint, type, dependency, and container checks for the actual stack. Inspect CI configuration to confirm required gates execute and cannot be silently skipped.

checks.heading: Release environment and tooling
checks.text: Keep fixtures/accounts synthetic, isolate test/live resources, and prevent tests from sending real messages or charges without explicit authorized scope.

checks.heading: Release environment and tooling
checks.text: Reproduce the production build/runtime closely enough to expose platform differences: environment injection, proxy headers, network, filesystem, worker startup, database pools, and persistence.

checks.heading: Release environment and tooling
checks.text: Keep necessary release results, revision, configuration differences, and skipped/flaky checks visible in the designated evidence location with bounded retention. Delete disposable local test outputs and recordings after review unless needed for an unresolved finding or required record. A permanently ignored failing check contributes no assurance.

checks.heading: Release environment and tooling
checks.text: Check that critical contract tests reflect provider schemas and event delivery behavior; add project-specific official documentation to the report.

checks.heading: Recovery and deployment evidence
checks.text: Rehearse deployment, health checks, worker/job ownership, post-deploy smoke journeys, and relevant restart recovery on isolated infrastructure.

checks.heading: Recovery and deployment evidence
checks.text: Verify a representative restore and data-safe rollback according to 09/12/17. Do not test destructive restore against the only production copy.

checks.heading: Recovery and deployment evidence
checks.text: Use bounded authorized capacity tests when needed to assess expected traffic and shared VPS contention. Record load, duration, environment, and stop conditions.

checks.heading: Recovery and deployment evidence
checks.text: After a relevant fix, rerun the changed control and affected flows. Broaden testing only for observed failures, new changes, or unresolved dependencies.

checks.heading: Independent expectations and representative users
checks.text: Derive expected results from product rules and independently reviewed examples rather than copying implementation behavior or accepting an AI claim that tests passed. Preserve regression checks for meaningful fixed defects.

checks.heading: Independent expectations and representative users
checks.text: Cover critical third-party contracts with controlled integration tests and representative recorded/synthetic failures. Keep test data realistic in size and shape without copying personal production data.

checks.heading: Independent expectations and representative users
checks.text: Include older supported laptops/browsers and poor Wi-Fi conditions in relevant core-journey checks. Test accessibility obligations and enterprise-specific flows selected in project scope, not only the developer's current device.

checks.heading: Extended release controls
checks.text: Identify the final source/artifact/configuration/schema/flag bundle and keep all required gate/review evidence current for that bundle. Check zero-test discovery, excluded shards, masked exit codes, conditional skips, and stale prior-revision results.

checks.heading: Extended release controls
checks.text: Protect CI/deploy credentials and release artifacts from untrusted contribution code, runner reuse, caches, install hooks and unsafe tooling. Verify selected provenance/signature policies without equating a signature with correctness.

checks.heading: Extended release controls
checks.text: Test state transitions, precision, transformations, concurrency conflicts, cache/replica behavior, partial remote outcomes and cancellation using independent expectations and real durable effects.

checks.heading: Extended release controls
checks.text: Include representative actual supported environments, manual accessibility tasks, poor network and meaningful load only where relevant and authorized. Record approximation, sample and capacity limits.

checks.heading: Extended release controls
checks.text: Rehearse health/drain behavior, mixed versions, flags, job ownership, post-deploy origin proof, isolated restore, rollback after accepted writes, fail-forward boundaries, and queued-work disablement.

checks.heading: Extended release controls
checks.text: Keep flaky, skipped, canceled, quarantined, infrastructure-failed and unexecuted required checks visible. Retries do not erase intermittent failures; critical gaps need an explicit decision.

checks.heading: Extended release controls
checks.text: Complete a separate project report, coverage matrix and execution ledger with owner/date/acceptance for actions. Preserve required unresolved-finding evidence and remove unnecessary session-created tests and disposable artifacts.

checks.heading: Identify the foundation
checks.text: INF-SCOPE-001 — Record hosting account, instance IDs, regions, OS/kernel, CPU architecture, Docker, Coolify, proxy, DNS/CDN, and relevant versions/plans; distinguish installed, configured, and running state.

checks.heading: Identify the foundation
checks.text: INF-SCOPE-002 — Identify physical/virtual hosts, control/build/remote servers, public/private IPv4 and IPv6, interfaces, VPNs, floating addresses, load balancers, and provider firewalls.

checks.heading: Identify the foundation
checks.text: INF-SCOPE-003 — Map domains, registrar, authoritative DNS, delegated subzones, certificates, proxy routes, mail providers, and application/administrative hostnames to owners.

checks.heading: Identify the foundation
checks.text: INF-SCOPE-004 — Inventory applications, listeners, published container ports, private services, workers, schedules, volumes, databases, object stores, and externally configured triggers.

checks.heading: Identify the foundation
checks.text: INF-SCOPE-005 — Identify critical journeys, sensitive data, tenant/project boundaries, allowable downtime/data loss, restoration targets, capacity expectations, and budget.

checks.heading: Identify the foundation
checks.text: INF-SCOPE-006 — Define provider/customer responsibilities and who owns OS, Docker, Coolify, proxy, application, DNS, backup, monitoring, and incident response in the actual service model.

checks.heading: Identify the foundation
checks.text: INF-SCOPE-007 — Map privileged dependency chains across hosting, recovery email, registrar, DNS, identity, source control, registry, Coolify, servers, and backup accounts.

checks.heading: Identify the foundation
checks.text: INF-SCOPE-008 — Name every application inheriting a shared control and what remains app-specific; separate shared-host risk from per-app authentication and authorization.

checks.heading: Define evidence and permitted verification
checks.text: INF-SCOPE-009 — Record allowed target addresses/domains, methods, source networks, synthetic accounts, request/rate/time bounds, side effects, and stop conditions before live verification.

checks.heading: Define evidence and permitted verification
checks.text: INF-SCOPE-010 — Separate read-only configuration review, ordinary bounded connection checks, restore rehearsals, access changes, and load/fault tests; authorization for one does not establish the others.

checks.heading: Define evidence and permitted verification
checks.text: INF-SCOPE-011 — Capture expected allowed/denied paths for each exposed service, address family, ingress mode, and administrative source using the exposure matrix.

checks.heading: Define evidence and permitted verification
checks.text: INF-SCOPE-012 — Distinguish provider configuration, host/container rules, actual listeners, external reachability, and application response; a screenshot of one layer does not verify the others.

checks.heading: Define evidence and permitted verification
checks.text: INF-SCOPE-013 — Use a controlled allowed request alongside a denial check where feasible; a failed connection alone can reflect an outage, routing failure, or wrong destination.

checks.heading: Define evidence and permitted verification
checks.text: INF-SCOPE-014 — Record timestamps/timezone, environment, resource/revision/version, source vantage point, tools/settings, exact target, observed result, and evidence limitations.

checks.heading: Define evidence and permitted verification
checks.text: INF-SCOPE-015 — Sample each materially different host, firewall attachment, Docker network mode, proxy path, address family, record type, role, and persistent-data class; expand after inconsistent results.

checks.heading: Define evidence and permitted verification
checks.text: INF-SCOPE-016 — Inspect actual deployed configuration and account capabilities rather than assuming upstream defaults or a guide written for another release apply.

checks.heading: Define evidence and permitted verification
checks.text: INF-SCOPE-017 — Redact evidence and keep credential/key values out of reports; record secure custody references and demonstrated retrieval without displaying secrets.

checks.heading: Define evidence and permitted verification
checks.text: INF-SCOPE-018 — Mark missing dashboard access, absent IPv6 vantage, unexecuted restore, unavailable provider telemetry, and uncertain external consumers Not verified with the required follow-up.

checks.heading: Triage and complete
checks.text: INF-SCOPE-019 — Assign each finding one root cause, primary module/owner, related check IDs, affected hosts/apps, severity, confidence, current exposure, priority, and blocker rationale.

checks.heading: Triage and complete
checks.text: INF-SCOPE-020 — Separate active exposure, latent enablement risk, verification gap, accepted limitation, and optional improvement; lack of a paid product is not itself a defect.

checks.heading: Triage and complete
checks.text: INF-SCOPE-021 — Propose the smallest effective fix with legitimate-traffic impact, lockout prevention, compatibility, dependencies, acceptance checks, and rollback/forward recovery.

checks.heading: Triage and complete
checks.text: INF-SCOPE-022 — Record accepted risk with accountable person, reason, compensating controls, expiry, and revisit trigger; acceptance does not turn an unmet control into Pass.

checks.heading: Triage and complete
checks.text: INF-SCOPE-023 — Recheck changed controls and directly affected apps after implementation; preserve actual results and unresolved gaps rather than marking planned mitigation verified.

checks.heading: Triage and complete
checks.text: INF-SCOPE-024 — Report selected/assessed/status counts with an explicit denominator and sample coverage; do not present a checklist completion percentage as a security guarantee.

checks.heading: Provider and identity accounts
checks.text: INF-HOST-001 — Confirm accountable ownership of hosting, registrar, DNS, CDN, identity, source control, registry, billing, and backups; remove abandoned personal or former-contractor control.

checks.heading: Provider and identity accounts
checks.text: INF-HOST-002 — Use available strong MFA and protect enrollment/recovery; verify that privileged account recovery cannot bypass the intended boundary through an insecure mailbox or shared credential.

checks.heading: Provider and identity accounts
checks.text: INF-HOST-003 — Maintain off-host recovery methods, trusted contacts, alternate billing/renewal alerts, and emergency access independent of the failing VPS or hosted domain where practicable.

checks.heading: Provider and identity accounts
checks.text: INF-HOST-004 — Review members, roles, service accounts, sessions, API keys, authorized OAuth apps, and last use; revoke obsolete access with consumer-aware sequencing.

checks.heading: Provider and identity accounts
checks.text: INF-HOST-005 — Scope automation tokens to necessary accounts/resources/actions and supported expiry/IP constraints; give integrations separate identities so revocation is attributable and bounded.

checks.heading: Provider and identity accounts
checks.text: INF-HOST-006 — Verify audit/change notifications reach a monitored recipient and that sensitive account, domain, and billing changes can be investigated.

checks.heading: Provider and identity accounts
checks.text: INF-HOST-007 — Record provider support authentication, console/rescue access, identity verification, service suspension, and escalation procedures; do not rely on an unreachable dashboard as the only incident route.

checks.heading: Provider and identity accounts
checks.text: INF-HOST-008 — Check renewal dates, payment failures, service limits, domain expiry, abuse contacts, and resource cancellation responsibilities; accidental suspension is an availability risk.

checks.heading: SSH and privileged administration
checks.text: INF-HOST-009 — Inventory SSH users, keys/certificates, authorized-key sources, automation accounts, forwarding, jump hosts, listening addresses, and alternate administrative protocols.

checks.heading: SSH and privileged administration
checks.text: INF-HOST-010 — Use attributable individual administrative access and protected private keys; distinguish interactive operators from unattended Coolify and backup automation.

checks.heading: SSH and privileged administration
checks.text: INF-HOST-011 — Review effective SSH configuration including include files, Match blocks, cloud-init/provider changes, authentication methods, root access, and user restrictions rather than one edited file.

checks.heading: SSH and privileged administration
checks.text: INF-HOST-012 — Verify a second working authorized session and provider console/rescue access before changing SSH authentication, listening ports, routing, or firewall sources; preserve a tested recovery path.

checks.heading: SSH and privileged administration
checks.text: INF-HOST-013 — Limit administrative reachability to required operators/VPN/jump hosts and controller addresses; account for dynamic home IPs, remote controllers, and IPv6.

checks.heading: SSH and privileged administration
checks.text: INF-HOST-014 — Review sudo, Docker-group/socket access, service-unit editing, writable privileged scripts, cron, and mount permissions as privilege paths; a non-root username may still have host-equivalent powers.

checks.heading: SSH and privileged administration
checks.text: INF-HOST-015 — Check SSH host-key verification for operators and automation, especially after rebuild/IP reuse; investigate a changed fingerprint rather than disabling verification globally.

checks.heading: SSH and privileged administration
checks.text: INF-HOST-016 — Restrict agent/TCP/X11 forwarding and tunneled access according to actual use; ensure a narrow SSH allowlist cannot still expose unintended internal services through an overly privileged account.

checks.heading: SSH and privileged administration
checks.text: INF-HOST-017 — Revoke stale keys, shared credentials, rescue passwords, temporary users, and emergency access after use; check every relevant host and automation consumer.

checks.heading: SSH and privileged administration
checks.text: INF-HOST-018 — Detect failed/suspicious authentication and unexpected privileged sessions; optional blocking tools require observed effectiveness and false-lockout recovery.

checks.heading: Operating system and service hygiene
checks.text: INF-HOST-019 — Verify OS/kernel/packages remain supported using actual versions and primary advisories; plan patches, reboots, maintenance windows, and urgent fixes with an owner.

checks.heading: Operating system and service hygiene
checks.text: INF-HOST-020 — Review package repositories, signing/trust configuration, third-party installers, unattended updates, and unsupported pinned packages for avoidable compromise or upgrade failures.

checks.heading: Operating system and service hygiene
checks.text: INF-HOST-021 — Inventory enabled services, systemd timers, cron, startup scripts, remote agents, shells, and unexpected privileged processes; remove obsolete components only after confirming purpose.

checks.heading: Operating system and service hygiene
checks.text: INF-HOST-022 — Check ownership/mode of secrets, environment files, SSH material, backup config, service files, sockets, and privileged executables; include inherited group and ACL access.

checks.heading: Operating system and service hygiene
checks.text: INF-HOST-023 — Review temporary directories, shared writable locations, symlink handling, and privileged scripts that process untrusted paths or filenames.

checks.heading: Operating system and service hygiene
checks.text: INF-HOST-024 — Verify time synchronization, timezone, hostname, local DNS, and certificate trust; clock drift can break authentication, TLS, schedules, and incident correlation.

checks.heading: Operating system and service hygiene
checks.text: INF-HOST-025 — Inspect disk bytes, inodes, mount health, filesystem errors, read-only remounts, swap/OOM behavior, and persistence of critical paths; capacity monitoring must cover the volume actually used.

checks.heading: Operating system and service hygiene
checks.text: INF-HOST-026 — Review host audit/auth/system logs, rotation, retention, off-host export, and privacy; diagnose without filling disk or recording secrets.

checks.heading: Operating system and service hygiene
checks.text: INF-HOST-027 — Check restart policies, service dependencies, boot ordering, and recovery after a real reboot where authorized; runtime state is not proof configuration survives restart.

checks.heading: Operating system and service hygiene
checks.text: INF-HOST-028 — Evaluate AppArmor/SELinux/seccomp and kernel controls supported by the installed stack; document necessary exceptions rather than blindly applying a generic sysctl/hardening script.

checks.heading: Operating system and service hygiene
checks.text: INF-HOST-029 — Confirm provider agents, guest tools, cloud-init, rescue images, and console functionality are understood and appropriately secured; provisioning metadata and credentials need explicit ownership.

checks.heading: Operating system and service hygiene
checks.text: INF-HOST-030 — Review access to instance metadata, local credential services, and private management endpoints from workloads; enforce applicable boundaries without breaking required platform operation.

checks.heading: Isolation and lifecycle
checks.text: INF-HOST-031 — Identify workloads that share a kernel, host account, filesystem, registry credential, backup identity, or control plane; document the resulting compromise blast radius.

checks.heading: Isolation and lifecycle
checks.text: INF-HOST-032 — Separate production and untrusted build/preview workloads where needed by trust level, not only by project labels or container names.

checks.heading: Isolation and lifecycle
checks.text: INF-HOST-033 — Document baseline provisioning, secure configuration sources, drift detection, and owner; avoid manual-only settings that disappear during host replacement.

checks.heading: Isolation and lifecycle
checks.text: INF-HOST-034 — Preserve required recovery/license/evidence assets while retiring obsolete accounts, daemons, keys, packages, and instances; verify dependencies and retained billing.

checks.heading: Isolation and lifecycle
checks.text: INF-HOST-035 — Treat suspected host compromise as a trust failure: plan isolation, evidence preservation, clean rebuild, and credential rotation from a trusted system rather than assuming a restart removes persistence.

checks.heading: Isolation and lifecycle
checks.text: INF-HOST-036 — Validate operator handover when the original maintainer is absent, including safe credential retrieval, console access, patching, and restoration ownership.

checks.heading: Effective ingress policy
checks.text: INF-NET-001 — Inventory public/private interfaces, routes, listeners, provider firewalls, host rules, Docker mappings, reverse proxies, tunnels, and alternate direct paths on every host.

checks.heading: Effective ingress policy
checks.text: INF-NET-002 — Confirm provider policies are active and attached to the correct instance/interfaces, with intended direction, protocol, source range, address family, and effective rule precedence.

checks.heading: Effective ingress policy
checks.text: INF-NET-003 — Apply default-deny ingress where appropriate and justify every exception by consumer/owner; do not confuse a saved rule template with an attached effective policy.

checks.heading: Effective ingress policy
checks.text: INF-NET-004 — Compare runtime and persistent firewall state; verify rules survive supported reboots, daemon restarts, deployments, and provider-side interface/IP changes.

checks.heading: Effective ingress policy
checks.text: INF-NET-005 — Identify the actual iptables/nftables/backend integration and forwarding path before changing Docker rules; policies must match the installed engine/backend.

checks.heading: Effective ingress policy
checks.text: INF-NET-006 — Verify Docker-published ports externally rather than assuming UFW's normal input policy covers their traffic; use a supported policy at the effective filtering layer.

checks.heading: Effective ingress policy
checks.text: INF-NET-007 — Do not disable Docker firewall management without a complete supported replacement and validation; check container routing and intended isolation after network-policy changes.

checks.heading: Effective ingress policy
checks.text: INF-NET-008 — Inspect wildcard/loopback/specific-address binds, Compose ports versus expose declarations, host networking, direct routing, and extra port mappings for unintended public paths.

checks.heading: Effective ingress policy
checks.text: INF-NET-009 — Keep database, cache, Docker API/socket, registry administration, metrics, debug, development, and internal API listeners private unless a justified protected integration needs access.

checks.heading: Effective ingress policy
checks.text: INF-NET-010 — Verify management access from allowed and disallowed sources, including Coolify controllers, backup agents, monitoring, and temporary maintenance paths.

checks.heading: Address families and packet behavior
checks.text: INF-NET-011 — Test IPv4 and IPv6 independently across provider rules, host rules, public binds, Docker publishing, DNS A/AAAA, and VPN routes; one passing family does not establish the other.

checks.heading: Address families and packet behavior
checks.text: INF-NET-012 — If IPv6 is intentionally unused, verify actual interfaces, routes, records, and exposure match that decision; deleting AAAA alone does not close an IPv6 listener.

checks.heading: Address families and packet behavior
checks.text: INF-NET-013 — Preserve necessary ICMP/ICMPv6 and path-MTU behavior according to the network design; blanket blocking can break diagnostics, neighbor discovery, or larger transfers.

checks.heading: Address families and packet behavior
checks.text: INF-NET-014 — Check TCP and UDP separately for services that use both, including DNS, VPN, game/media traffic, and HTTP/3 where enabled.

checks.heading: Address families and packet behavior
checks.text: INF-NET-015 — Review connection tracking capacity, established/related rules, fragment handling, asymmetrical routing, and rate rules where relevant; verify legitimate connections under the supported topology.

checks.heading: Address families and packet behavior
checks.text: INF-NET-016 — Check NAT/hairpin behavior, loopback exposure, public-to-private routing, and access from neighboring hosts/workloads; a public denial does not prove east-west isolation.

checks.heading: Address families and packet behavior
checks.text: INF-NET-017 — Validate MTU/MSS and encapsulation overhead for VPN/tunnel paths using bounded checks; investigate size-dependent or streaming failures rather than disabling TLS verification.

checks.heading: Address families and packet behavior
checks.text: INF-NET-018 — Record intended protection and recovery for floating/additional IPs, failover interfaces, load balancer health probes, and IP changes; ensure old policies do not become a bypass.

checks.heading: Private networks, VPNs, and egress
checks.text: INF-NET-019 — Map private/overlay networks, memberships, routes, ACLs, DNS search domains, exit nodes, and advertised subnets; private addressing alone is not authorization.

checks.heading: Private networks, VPNs, and egress
checks.text: INF-NET-020 — Restrict cross-project traffic to required flows and test denied paths where authorized; shared Docker/VPN membership may permit lateral access despite separate dashboard projects.

checks.heading: Private networks, VPNs, and egress
checks.text: INF-NET-021 — Scope VPN/device identities, admin rights, enrollment, expiry, revocation, and lost-device response; verify removal takes effect on active paths.

checks.heading: Private networks, VPNs, and egress
checks.text: INF-NET-022 — Check split/full tunnel behavior, DNS leakage, route conflicts, client-IP attribution, and management reachability during VPN/control-plane outage.

checks.heading: Private networks, VPNs, and egress
checks.text: INF-NET-023 — Inventory required egress for DNS, NTP, package/registry access, ACME, OAuth, payments, email, object storage, backups, and provider APIs.

checks.heading: Private networks, VPNs, and egress
checks.text: INF-NET-024 — Where egress restrictions are required, verify the effective outbound layer and actual allowed/denied traffic; do not infer outbound filtering from an inbound-only provider firewall.

checks.heading: Private networks, VPNs, and egress
checks.text: INF-NET-025 — Account for changing provider IPs/CDNs, DNS resolution, IPv6, TLS endpoints, and proxy exclusions in egress policy; avoid brittle IP lists without update ownership.

checks.heading: Private networks, VPNs, and egress
checks.text: INF-NET-026 — Review access to link-local metadata, host services, private control planes, and other tenants from untrusted workloads; pair network restriction with application SSRF controls.

checks.heading: Private networks, VPNs, and egress
checks.text: INF-NET-027 — Confirm DNS resolution and time sync have appropriate redundant/available paths and are not accidentally blocked during policy tightening.

checks.heading: Private networks, VPNs, and egress
checks.text: INF-NET-028 — Detect unexplained outbound traffic, scanning, mail, exfiltration, and bandwidth growth; identify the originating workload and response owner.

checks.heading: Non-web protocols and validation
checks.text: INF-NET-029 — Do not expose inbound DNS merely to permit outbound lookups; deliberate DNS hosting needs explicit authoritative/resolver role, recursion policy, transfer access, and amplification review.

checks.heading: Non-web protocols and validation
checks.text: INF-NET-030 — For mail hosting, inventory protocol/port exposure, authentication, relay policy, provider restrictions, reverse DNS, abuse handling, and availability separately from the web proxy.

checks.heading: Non-web protocols and validation
checks.text: INF-NET-031 — For game/voice/media/VPN services, verify required UDP/TCP ranges, identity, per-protocol limits, upstream mitigation, and client compatibility; ordinary HTTP WAF rules may not apply.

checks.heading: Non-web protocols and validation
checks.text: INF-NET-032 — For intentionally external databases or replication, require justified clients, narrow sources, authentication, encryption/identity validation, monitoring, and revocation/recovery procedures.

checks.heading: Non-web protocols and validation
checks.text: INF-NET-033 — Check public container registries, artifact servers, object gateways, and management agents for anonymous write/admin routes and direct-port bypasses.

checks.heading: Non-web protocols and validation
checks.text: INF-NET-034 — Use ordinary bounded connection/application checks from authorized external vantage points; record source, destination, family, protocol, expected result, and actual response.

checks.heading: Non-web protocols and validation
checks.text: INF-NET-035 — Pair denied tests with allowed service checks and confirm the intended origin, not a cached edge response or a different instance, was observed.

checks.heading: Non-web protocols and validation
checks.text: INF-NET-036 — Revalidate exposure after deploying a new service, publishing ports, switching Docker backend, enabling IPv6, adding a tunnel, or replacing a firewall policy.

checks.heading: Privileged management plane
checks.text: INF-CTL-001 — Inventory Coolify instance/version, control-plane host, remote servers, build servers, teams, projects, credentials, and administrative entry points; map compromise reach across them.

checks.heading: Privileged management plane
checks.text: INF-CTL-002 — Protect dashboard access with HTTPS, strong authentication and available MFA, deliberate registration policy, and an appropriate restricted-access boundary.

checks.heading: Privileged management plane
checks.text: INF-CTL-003 — Review actual team roles, invitations, removed members, service identities, and resource visibility; confirm intended boundaries with scoped accounts where authorized.

checks.heading: Privileged management plane
checks.text: INF-CTL-004 — Keep API access deliberate and tokens appropriately scoped, attributable, revocable, and protected; verify installed-version permissions and access restrictions.

checks.heading: Privileged management plane
checks.text: INF-CTL-005 — Review Git/source integrations and deployment hooks for caller authentication, target authorization, credential scope, and revocation without leaving stale triggers.

checks.heading: Privileged management plane
checks.text: INF-CTL-006 — Distinguish the dashboard domain from direct management ports; restricting one route must not leave another public administrative path.

checks.heading: Privileged management plane
checks.text: INF-CTL-007 — Verify required dashboard, realtime, terminal, remote validation, hooks, and certificate behavior before closing direct ports; account for self-hosted/controller/remote topology.

checks.heading: Privileged management plane
checks.text: INF-CTL-008 — Secure remote-server SSH identities and verify effective sudo/Docker powers, trusted host identity, allowed sources, rotation, and recovery if the controller is lost.

checks.heading: Privileged management plane
checks.text: INF-CTL-009 — Keep control-plane state, updates, encryption material, and recovery ownership explicit; losing access to its stored credentials can affect every connected server.

checks.heading: Privileged management plane
checks.text: INF-CTL-010 — Separate untrusted builds/previews from sensitive workloads and management credentials; assess isolation at host, process, filesystem, identity, and network layers.

checks.heading: Workload privileges and networks
checks.text: INF-CTL-011 — Inventory actual running container images/digests, users, capabilities, security options, mounts, networks, published ports, device access, and restart policies rather than only source Compose files.

checks.heading: Workload privileges and networks
checks.text: INF-CTL-012 — Identify privileged containers, broad capabilities, host PID/IPC/network namespaces, host devices, and writable host mounts; justify or reduce each privilege through required behavior.

checks.heading: Workload privileges and networks
checks.text: INF-CTL-013 — Restrict Docker socket/API access and equivalent control endpoints; read-only mounting or an application label alone may not create an effective privilege boundary.

checks.heading: Workload privileges and networks
checks.text: INF-CTL-014 — Use an appropriate non-root workload identity and bounded writable locations where supported; verify file ownership, low-port needs, temp files, and health checks still work.

checks.heading: Workload privileges and networks
checks.text: INF-CTL-015 — Review seccomp/AppArmor/SELinux and no-new-privileges/readonly constraints where compatible; document exceptions and validate the actual runtime rather than prescribing incompatible flags.

checks.heading: Workload privileges and networks
checks.text: INF-CTL-016 — Check network membership and cross-project reachability; project separation in a dashboard does not establish denied container-to-container traffic.

checks.heading: Workload privileges and networks
checks.text: INF-CTL-017 — Inspect external/shared networks, host aliases, direct database routes, and manually published ports that bypass domain routing or intended access controls.

checks.heading: Workload privileges and networks
checks.text: INF-CTL-018 — Verify container DNS, outbound access, metadata/host access, and service discovery against intended workload authority and SSRF risk.

checks.heading: Workload privileges and networks
checks.text: INF-CTL-019 — Bound CPU, memory, process counts, file descriptors, connections, storage, and log growth as required; inspect actual effective limits and their failure behavior.

checks.heading: Workload privileges and networks
checks.text: INF-CTL-020 — Validate health/readiness, graceful shutdown, stop timeout, restart/backoff behavior, and service dependencies after deployment, crash, and host reboot.

checks.heading: Secrets, build inputs, and deployment
checks.text: INF-CTL-021 — Trace secrets through source integrations, build args, build context, environment files, image layers, logs, runtime environment, and frontend bundles; keep them out of public artifacts.

checks.heading: Secrets, build inputs, and deployment
checks.text: INF-CTL-022 — Separate production, staging, previews, and build identities/data; preview URLs and environment copies must not grant access to production providers or tenant data.

checks.heading: Secrets, build inputs, and deployment
checks.text: INF-CTL-023 — Review registry/source trust, image pinning, build tooling, install scripts, dependency updates, and native architecture; coordinate build provenance checks with module 05.

checks.heading: Secrets, build inputs, and deployment
checks.text: INF-CTL-024 — Verify the artifact and environment actually deployed, including configured branch/tag, build cache, runtime variables, and rollback image availability.

checks.heading: Secrets, build inputs, and deployment
checks.text: INF-CTL-025 — Inspect deployments that overlap old/new replicas for migration compatibility, concurrent startup jobs, duplicate consumers/schedules, and local-state assumptions.

checks.heading: Secrets, build inputs, and deployment
checks.text: INF-CTL-026 — Check proxy/route generation and manual overrides for drift, unexpected labels, wildcard collisions, stale routes, and configuration overwritten by the next deployment.

checks.heading: Secrets, build inputs, and deployment
checks.text: INF-CTL-027 — Verify failure/cancel paths leave an understood serving version and resource state; a successful build is not proof that startup, routing, or migrations succeeded.

checks.heading: Persistent state and housekeeping
checks.text: INF-CTL-028 — Map every stateful path to a named volume, bind mount, external store, or intentional ephemeral path; identify data currently living only in a container layer.

checks.heading: Persistent state and housekeeping
checks.text: INF-CTL-029 — Check volume ownership, UID/GID, mount location, permissions, disk/inode capacity, backup coverage, and behavior after container recreation or host replacement.

checks.heading: Persistent state and housekeeping
checks.text: INF-CTL-030 — Verify cleanup jobs exclude required images, volumes, backups, deployment evidence, and rollback assets; never assume an unused label proves an artifact has no recovery purpose.

checks.heading: Persistent state and housekeeping
checks.text: INF-CTL-031 — Monitor build/cache/image/log/volume growth and failed backup residue; prune only classified candidates with dependency and recovery evidence.

checks.heading: Persistent state and housekeeping
checks.text: INF-CTL-032 — Detect orphaned preview environments, containers, routes, schedules, credentials, and billable resources; retire dependencies and external references together.

checks.heading: Persistent state and housekeeping
checks.text: INF-CTL-033 — Establish a supported Coolify/Docker/proxy update process with backup, compatibility checks, maintenance impact, rollback limits, and post-update functional verification.

checks.heading: Persistent state and housekeeping
checks.text: INF-CTL-034 — Demonstrate recovery of the management layer separately from application data; restoring a dashboard does not establish restored databases, uploads, or job ownership.

checks.heading: Ownership and delegation
checks.text: INF-DNS-001 — Confirm registrar/account ownership, contacts, strong authentication, recovery, transfer/registry locks where available, renewal payment, expiry, and external alert recipients.

checks.heading: Ownership and delegation
checks.text: INF-DNS-002 — Verify parent delegation, authoritative nameservers, zone availability, and agreement among authoritative servers; a correct record in an inactive dashboard is not effective DNS.

checks.heading: Ownership and delegation
checks.text: INF-DNS-003 — Review delegated subzones, in-bailiwick nameserver glue where relevant, abandoned secondary providers, and account ownership for each dependency.

checks.heading: Ownership and delegation
checks.text: INF-DNS-004 — Maintain a sanitized zone inventory/export and change history independent of a single dashboard; identify the authoritative configuration when UI/API/IaC can all modify records.

checks.heading: Ownership and delegation
checks.text: INF-DNS-005 — Scope DNS API credentials to required zones/actions and renewal/automation consumers; prevent unrelated workloads from changing production authority.

checks.heading: Ownership and delegation
checks.text: INF-DNS-006 — Review who can change nameservers, DS records, mail routing, ownership proofs, and certificate-validation records; those paths can bypass ordinary application controls.

checks.heading: Ownership and delegation
checks.text: INF-DNS-007 — Check availability dependencies and actual provider/service capabilities; several nameservers under one failing control plane are not automatically independent redundancy.

checks.heading: Ownership and delegation
checks.text: INF-DNS-008 — Review wildcard zones, internal split-horizon records, and search-domain behavior for accidental catch-all routing or private-name disclosure.

checks.heading: Record integrity and routing
checks.text: INF-DNS-009 — Reconcile A and AAAA with intended origins/edges and active firewall policy; remove stale/reassigned addresses only after checking legitimate consumers and recovery needs.

checks.heading: Record integrity and routing
checks.text: INF-DNS-010 — Inspect CNAME chains, dangling cloud/SaaS targets, abandoned verification records, and unclaimed resources for takeover or misrouting risk.

checks.heading: Record integrity and routing
checks.text: INF-DNS-011 — Verify apex/alias/flattening behavior and restrictions in the actual DNS service; do not assume one provider's pseudo-record semantics transfer unchanged.

checks.heading: Record integrity and routing
checks.text: INF-DNS-012 — Distinguish DNS-only and proxied records per hostname, supported protocol, certificate, and client; ordinary web proxying does not cover every port or non-web workload.

checks.heading: Record integrity and routing
checks.text: INF-DNS-013 — Evaluate origin disclosure through historical records, DNS-only subdomains, mail, certificate names, and alternate services; hiding the current A record is not an access control.

checks.heading: Record integrity and routing
checks.text: INF-DNS-014 — Verify wildcard, www/apex, administrative, preview, API, upload, and webhook hostnames each route to the intended protected service and TLS identity.

checks.heading: Record integrity and routing
checks.text: INF-DNS-015 — Check TTL and negative caching against failover/cutover expectations; changing a TTL does not retroactively expire answers already cached.

checks.heading: Record integrity and routing
checks.text: INF-DNS-016 — Validate from authoritative and selected recursive vantage points, including IPv4/IPv6 where relevant; explain caching, split-horizon, and geolocation differences rather than assuming immediate global agreement.

checks.heading: Record integrity and routing
checks.text: INF-DNS-017 — Verify SRV/TXT and other service-discovery records, ownership tokens, ACME delegation, and third-party verification still have a current owner and purpose.

checks.heading: Record integrity and routing
checks.text: INF-DNS-018 — Review CAA where selected for certificate-issuance policy, including subdomains, delegated challenges, wildcard issuance, and CA account/provider changes.

checks.heading: DNSSEC and migration
checks.text: INF-DNS-019 — Where DNSSEC is selected and supported, verify signing, valid signatures, DNSKEY/DS chain consistency, algorithm support, and behavior with validating resolvers.

checks.heading: DNSSEC and migration
checks.text: INF-DNS-020 — Monitor signature/key lifecycle and DS/signing drift; document accountable ownership for renewal, rollover, and incident correction.

checks.heading: DNSSEC and migration
checks.text: INF-DNS-021 — Plan DNS-provider/nameserver changes with current DS/signing state and cache windows; stale parent trust can make an otherwise populated new zone fail validation.

checks.heading: DNSSEC and migration
checks.text: INF-DNS-022 — Sequence key rotation, enabling/disabling signing, and registrar DS changes using provider-supported procedures; preserve a recovery path and validate externally after each relevant phase.

checks.heading: DNSSEC and migration
checks.text: INF-DNS-023 — Keep DNSSEC's role distinct from encryption, registrar-account security, WAF filtering, and DDoS capacity; do not claim it prevents an authenticated malicious zone change.

checks.heading: DNSSEC and migration
checks.text: INF-DNS-024 — Before transfer/cutover, export all required records and zone options, verify new authority, maintain required old service paths, and define rollback limits for cached/delegated state.

checks.heading: Resolution and intentional DNS hosting
checks.text: INF-DNS-025 — Verify the host/container resolver path, upstream availability, search domains, local cache, DNSSEC expectations, and timeouts under intended network policy.

checks.heading: Resolution and intentional DNS hosting
checks.text: INF-DNS-026 — If hosting an authoritative server, review zone transfer permissions, update authentication, recursion policy, TCP/UDP availability, response size, and upstream flood mitigation.

checks.heading: Resolution and intentional DNS hosting
checks.text: INF-DNS-027 — If running a recursive resolver, restrict authorized clients and review cache poisoning, forwarding, resource limits, and amplification exposure; ordinary applications need no public resolver.

checks.heading: Resolution and intentional DNS hosting
checks.text: INF-DNS-028 — Check large responses, truncation/TCP fallback, fragmentation/MTU effects, and resolver-specific failures with bounded queries where applicable.

checks.heading: Mail and ownership dependencies
checks.text: INF-DNS-029 — Verify MX targets, priorities, address resolution, provider ownership, and retained mail routing; mail should not unintentionally expose a protected web origin or land on retired infrastructure.

checks.heading: Mail and ownership dependencies
checks.text: INF-DNS-030 — Review SPF policy and include chains for actual senders and evaluation limits using current mail-provider guidance; remove obsolete authorizations without breaking legitimate delivery.

checks.heading: Mail and ownership dependencies
checks.text: INF-DNS-031 — Verify DKIM selectors/keys, provider rotation, and alignment with the intended sending domains; distinguish configured DNS from actual signed message evidence.

checks.heading: Mail and ownership dependencies
checks.text: INF-DNS-032 — Assess DMARC alignment, policy, reports, subdomain handling, and staged enforcement against legitimate senders; inspect real delivery before tightening policy.

checks.heading: Mail and ownership dependencies
checks.text: INF-DNS-033 — For self-hosted mail, verify PTR/reverse DNS, forward identity, hostname/HELO, TLS, relay controls, blocked provider ports, reputation, and deliverability with module 14.

checks.heading: Mail and ownership dependencies
checks.text: INF-DNS-034 — For non-sending domains, consider explicit non-sending mail policies according to actual domain/subdomain use and provider guidance; do not blindly apply a sending-domain template.

checks.heading: Mail and ownership dependencies
checks.text: INF-DNS-035 — Keep account recovery and incident contacts reachable during a DNS/mail/hosting outage; test alternate access without exposing recovery secrets.

checks.heading: Mail and ownership dependencies
checks.text: INF-DNS-036 — After changes, verify mail, OAuth ownership, ACME renewal, verification tokens, and service discovery as well as ordinary website resolution.

checks.heading: Certificates and renewal
checks.text: INF-TLS-001 — Inventory certificate names, issuers, termination points, private-key custody, expiry, automation, ownership, and dependent services; include dashboard, APIs, and non-web TLS.

checks.heading: Certificates and renewal
checks.text: INF-TLS-002 — Validate hostname/SAN, chain, trust, expiry, SNI, and certificate actually served at each required hop; a valid edge certificate does not prove origin validation.

checks.heading: Certificates and renewal
checks.text: INF-TLS-003 — Verify supported protocol/cipher policy against actual client requirements and current primary guidance; avoid hardcoded universal settings that break needed clients or age unnoticed.

checks.heading: Certificates and renewal
checks.text: INF-TLS-004 — Document the ACME challenge method, DNS/API credentials, renewal path, egress, ingress, and propagation prerequisites; certificate issuance and renewal must both work.

checks.heading: Certificates and renewal
checks.text: INF-TLS-005 — For HTTP-01, preserve the required port-80 validation path through all active proxies/firewalls and all answering origins; redirects and access gates must not break the challenge.

checks.heading: Certificates and renewal
checks.text: INF-TLS-006 — For DNS-01, verify TXT/delegation behavior, API scope, propagation, concurrent challenges, and cleanup; protect the automation credential as authority over relevant DNS.

checks.heading: Certificates and renewal
checks.text: INF-TLS-007 — Check wildcard versus explicit names, apex coverage, CAA policy, chosen CA limits, and staging/test issuance behavior against the actual ACME client/provider.

checks.heading: Certificates and renewal
checks.text: INF-TLS-008 — Monitor renewal execution and externally served expiry, including failed reloads, wrong storage permissions, full disk, lost account keys, and replicas serving different certificates.

checks.heading: Certificates and renewal
checks.text: INF-TLS-009 — Test supported certificate reload and key replacement paths where authorized; avoid assuming files on disk match the in-memory listener.

checks.heading: Certificates and renewal
checks.text: INF-TLS-010 — Prepare recovery for expired/revoked certificates, compromised keys, lost DNS credentials, and unavailable CA/provider without normalizing disabled verification.

checks.heading: Trusted ingress and origin bypass
checks.text: INF-TLS-011 — Declare which hostnames permit direct origin traffic and which require trusted edge/tunnel ingress; record necessary health, ACME, administrative, and machine-client exceptions.

checks.heading: Trusted ingress and origin bypass
checks.text: INF-TLS-012 — Validate encryption and identity checking on edge-to-origin connections; do not silently downgrade origin verification to solve a misconfiguration.

checks.heading: Trusted ingress and origin bypass
checks.text: INF-TLS-013 — Enforce the chosen origin restriction at an effective layer, covering IPv4/IPv6, alternate ports, historic IPs, DNS-only names, and newly attached addresses.

checks.heading: Trusted ingress and origin bypass
checks.text: INF-TLS-014 — Verify direct-IP/Host/SNI combinations and alternate names cannot reach protected apps outside intended ingress; a hidden origin address is not sufficient evidence.

checks.heading: Trusted ingress and origin bypass
checks.text: INF-TLS-015 — If allowing an edge provider's IP ranges, update them through an owned validated process and recognize whether the rule identifies the provider network or the specific intended tenant.

checks.heading: Trusted ingress and origin bypass
checks.text: INF-TLS-016 — Where specific origin authentication is required, verify the selected per-origin certificate/token/tunnel identity and its rotation/revocation; distinguish shared-provider identity from your own ingress authority.

checks.heading: Trusted ingress and origin bypass
checks.text: INF-TLS-017 — For tunnels, inventory connector credentials, replica routing, local service binds, private routes, egress, access policy, and behavior when the connector or its control plane fails.

checks.heading: Trusted ingress and origin bypass
checks.text: INF-TLS-018 — Reject unintended/default host routes and route collisions; distinguish legitimate SNI/Host rewrites from spoofed routing into another application.

checks.heading: Proxy semantics and application behavior
checks.text: INF-TLS-019 — Trust forwarded client-IP/protocol/host headers only from verified proxy hops; strip or normalize caller-supplied variants before using them for limits, logs, redirects, or secure cookies.

checks.heading: Proxy semantics and application behavior
checks.text: INF-TLS-020 — Inspect proxy-chain order, duplicate/conflicting forwarded values, PROXY protocol where used, and application trusted-proxy configuration; verify actual client attribution through every hop.

checks.heading: Proxy semantics and application behavior
checks.text: INF-TLS-021 — Validate redirects, external URL generation, cookie secure/domain attributes, OAuth callbacks, CORS, CSRF, and webhook destinations behind the real proxy topology.

checks.heading: Proxy semantics and application behavior
checks.text: INF-TLS-022 — Check HSTS host/subdomain/preload consequences only after all required names support the intended HTTPS behavior; define recovery implications before irreversible client caching commitments.

checks.heading: Proxy semantics and application behavior
checks.text: INF-TLS-023 — Review cache keys and cache-control for authenticated/personalized responses, tenant/locale variation, errors, redirects, cookies, and invalidation after access changes.

checks.heading: Proxy semantics and application behavior
checks.text: INF-TLS-024 — Verify WebSocket upgrades, SSE/AI streaming, response buffering, idle/total timeouts, compression, and disconnect behavior through the complete serving chain.

checks.heading: Proxy semantics and application behavior
checks.text: INF-TLS-025 — Check upload/body/header limits, request buffering, temporary disk, download/range requests, and large or slow clients against legitimate product requirements.

checks.heading: Proxy semantics and application behavior
checks.text: INF-TLS-026 — Inspect path normalization, encoded separators, duplicate headers, request framing, and HTTP-version translation where ambiguity could bypass routing/authentication or create request-smuggling risk.

checks.heading: Proxy semantics and application behavior
