checks.text: INF-TLS-027 — Keep access/identity gates compatible with signed webhooks, bots, APIs, ACME, monitoring, and health probes; machine clients need deliberate protected paths rather than blanket browser challenges.

checks.heading: Proxy semantics and application behavior
checks.text: INF-TLS-028 — Verify edge/proxy error pages and maintenance modes do not disclose secrets, hide origin failure, cache privileged content, or report a healthy application when only an edge response works.

checks.heading: Change and validation
checks.text: INF-TLS-029 — Version/record proxy configuration, middleware, labels, certificates, and external rules; identify which manual changes will be overwritten by Coolify or a later deployment.

checks.heading: Change and validation
checks.text: INF-TLS-030 — Validate routing/config reload before and after proxy upgrades; define recovery for invalid configuration, conflicting routes, or lost certificate state.

checks.heading: Change and validation
checks.text: INF-TLS-031 — Run bounded allowed/denied checks from appropriate paths and identify which edge/origin/version served the response; do not infer full-chain health from cached content.

checks.heading: Change and validation
checks.text: INF-TLS-032 — Recheck TLS, origin restrictions, forwarded headers, renewal, and critical machine/user flows after DNS, CDN mode, IP, firewall, or ingress changes.

checks.heading: Distinguish protection layers
checks.text: INF-ABUSE-001 — Separate registrar/DNS takeover, DNS amplification, network/transport floods, HTTP floods, credential abuse, scraping, expensive valid actions, and workload compromise in the threat model.

checks.heading: Distinguish protection layers
checks.text: INF-ABUSE-002 — Verify the hosting account's actual upstream DDoS service, covered IPs/protocols, exclusions, detection/mitigation behavior, null-routing policy, contacts, and support escalation.

checks.heading: Distinguish protection layers
checks.text: INF-ABUSE-003 — Record uncertainty in provider capacity and response guarantees; marketing descriptions and an enabled dashboard control are not evidence of surviving a specific attack.

checks.heading: Distinguish protection layers
checks.text: INF-ABUSE-004 — Identify where a link, provider interface, host, proxy, database, worker pool, or paid provider saturates first; a local firewall cannot recover bandwidth already exhausted upstream.

checks.heading: Distinguish protection layers
checks.text: INF-ABUSE-005 — Map protection by hostname, address family, port, and protocol; an HTTP edge/WAF may leave direct IP, UDP, mail, SSH, or other services outside its coverage.

checks.heading: Distinguish protection layers
checks.text: INF-ABUSE-006 — Verify resilient authoritative DNS and no unintended public recursion/amplification service; web WAF configuration does not establish DNS-layer protection.

checks.heading: Distinguish protection layers
checks.text: INF-ABUSE-007 — Determine whether origin restrictions prevent bypassing edge controls, including alternate names/ports/IPs and permitted exceptions.

checks.heading: Distinguish protection layers
checks.text: INF-ABUSE-008 — Record actual WAF/bot/rate features and plan limits; do not assume a rule template or vendor feature name is available or enabled in this account.

checks.heading: Application-aware controls
checks.text: INF-ABUSE-009 — Apply limits at appropriate identity levels: source network, account, tenant, session, token, route, expensive feature, and global budget; consider shared IPs and IPv6 address rotation.

checks.heading: Application-aware controls
checks.text: INF-ABUSE-010 — Derive rate identities from verified proxy context; spoofed forwarding headers must not create unlimited fresh identities or ban innocent clients.

checks.heading: Application-aware controls
checks.text: INF-ABUSE-011 — Bound authentication, password recovery, invitation, search, export, upload, image/media processing, AI, and other expensive paths according to cost and legitimate usage.

checks.heading: Application-aware controls
checks.text: INF-ABUSE-012 — Verify quotas/concurrency remain effective across replicas, workers, retries, queues, and direct endpoints; process-local counters alone may not enforce a global budget.

checks.heading: Application-aware controls
checks.text: INF-ABUSE-013 — Bound request bodies, headers, decompression, connection duration, idle clients, and simultaneous requests without breaking explicitly supported streaming or large-transfer routes.

checks.heading: Application-aware controls
checks.text: INF-ABUSE-014 — Review cache-miss amplification, unique query strings, broad search/filter combinations, origin fetches, and unauthenticated cache bypass for disproportionate backend work.

checks.heading: Application-aware controls
checks.text: INF-ABUSE-015 — Authenticate and validate webhooks/machine clients with deliberate protected exceptions; do not replace their verification with a blanket WAF bypass or browser-only challenge.

checks.heading: Application-aware controls
checks.text: INF-ABUSE-016 — Check deny/challenge/rate responses, retry hints, account recovery, and accessible alternatives; false positives must be diagnosable and reversible.

checks.heading: Application-aware controls
checks.text: INF-ABUSE-017 — Confirm limits preserve legitimate crawlers, login/OAuth, payments, uploads, ACME, monitoring, and assistive/client workflows using bounded representative checks.

checks.heading: Application-aware controls
checks.text: INF-ABUSE-018 — Keep application authorization, input validation, and per-tenant controls behind the edge; passing a WAF does not confer authority or prove safe business behavior.

checks.heading: Capacity, spend, and response
checks.text: INF-ABUSE-019 — Define finite resource pools, queue bounds, admission control, backpressure, and shedding priorities; avoid unlimited buffering when a dependency slows down.

checks.heading: Capacity, spend, and response
checks.text: INF-ABUSE-020 — Measure relevant baseline latency/error distributions, bandwidth, connections, CPU, memory, disk/I/O, backlog, and provider spend; record dataset and workload context.

checks.heading: Capacity, spend, and response
checks.text: INF-ABUSE-021 — Account for builds, backups, log export, database maintenance, image pulls, and recovery competing with production; scheduled internal work can trigger the same saturation as external load.

checks.heading: Capacity, spend, and response
checks.text: INF-ABUSE-022 — Configure alerts and budgets for egress, paid API calls, autoscaling, storage/log growth, and retry storms; coordinate consequential spend controls with module 08.

checks.heading: Capacity, spend, and response
checks.text: INF-ABUSE-023 — Define an owned emergency sequence for tightening rules, disabling expensive features, queueing/read-only mode, or suspending abusive accounts with legitimate-user checks and rollback.

checks.heading: Capacity, spend, and response
checks.text: INF-ABUSE-024 — Keep provider escalation, off-host contacts, current instance/IP details, and a sanitized incident evidence procedure usable when the server is unreachable.

checks.heading: Capacity, spend, and response
checks.text: INF-ABUSE-025 — Compare edge/origin/application telemetry to locate the failing layer; distinguish blocked malicious traffic from origin outage and successful-but-expensive valid requests.

checks.heading: Capacity, spend, and response
checks.text: INF-ABUSE-026 — If capacity testing is explicitly authorized, define owned targets, source, maximum concurrency/rate/duration/cost, success criteria, stop conditions, and provider constraints before execution.

checks.heading: Capacity, spend, and response
checks.text: INF-ABUSE-027 — After mitigation, verify legitimate journeys, data/financial effects, backlog recovery, lasting rules, and credential/compromise concerns; do not close merely because traffic dropped.

checks.heading: Capacity, spend, and response
checks.text: INF-ABUSE-028 — Document residual risk, review triggers, and control ownership after real incidents, new expensive features, protocol changes, or material growth.

checks.heading: Coverage and independent custody
checks.text: INF-REC-001 — Define RPO/RTO and retention per critical data/service class, including what constitutes restored usable service; record accountable owners and accepted loss/downtime.

checks.heading: Coverage and independent custody
checks.text: INF-REC-002 — Inventory Coolify state, instance encryption material, application databases, uploads, named volumes, bind mounts, object stores, proxy/certificate state, DNS, infrastructure config, and required artifacts.

checks.heading: Coverage and independent custody
checks.text: INF-REC-003 — Distinguish control-plane backup from workload data backup; verify actual included files/databases, exclusions, job locations, and consumer expectations for each mechanism.

checks.heading: Coverage and independent custody
checks.text: INF-REC-004 — For self-hosted Coolify, preserve the matching APP_KEY securely outside the host separately from the instance database backup; verify custody without displaying its value.

checks.heading: Coverage and independent custody
checks.text: INF-REC-005 — Verify each application's engine/version supports the selected backup procedure; use appropriate native tools where the orchestration UI does not cover the required data.

checks.heading: Coverage and independent custody
checks.text: INF-REC-006 — Check backup consistency across live database transactions, files/blobs, multiple stores, and related application versions; a raw copy or VM snapshot is not automatically application-consistent.

checks.heading: Coverage and independent custody
checks.text: INF-REC-007 — Keep usable copies outside the source server/failure domain and review account/provider/region independence against the required disaster scenario.

checks.heading: Coverage and independent custody
checks.text: INF-REC-008 — Restrict backup credentials and deletion authority; consider versioning/immutability or independent custody when protection against malicious deletion is required and supported.

checks.heading: Coverage and independent custody
checks.text: INF-REC-009 — Protect encryption keys, password managers, recovery accounts, and decrypt permissions with an available off-host recovery path; encrypted backups without keys are not a recovery plan.

checks.heading: Coverage and independent custody
checks.text: INF-REC-010 — Review backup transport, storage access, retention, privacy, and access logging; avoid placing public backups, dumps, or temporary restore files behind a web route.

checks.heading: Execution, retention, and failure detection
checks.text: INF-REC-011 — Verify schedules, timezone, overlap, duration, timeouts, skipped jobs, database/container downtime, and resource competition under actual deployment conditions.

checks.heading: Execution, retention, and failure detection
checks.text: INF-REC-012 — Monitor creation, completeness, remote upload, freshness, remote availability, and failure/warning outcomes independently; local success does not establish an off-site copy exists.

checks.heading: Execution, retention, and failure detection
checks.text: INF-REC-013 — Inspect size/content anomalies, exclusions, command exit codes, compression/encryption failures, partial files, and backup jobs that appear successful after doing no work.

checks.heading: Execution, retention, and failure detection
checks.text: INF-REC-014 — Define retention across local and remote stores, versioning/lifecycle, failed residues, and deletion permissions; ensure no policy removes the last useful recovery generation unexpectedly.

checks.heading: Execution, retention, and failure detection
checks.text: INF-REC-015 — Verify storage/disk/inode/egress costs and capacity for backup growth, download, decompression, restore, and temporary copies; recovery may need more space than the archive size.

checks.heading: Execution, retention, and failure detection
checks.text: INF-REC-016 — Test failure/alert reception through an authorized bounded method and confirm an off-host recipient/owner responds; an enabled notification toggle is not delivered evidence.

checks.heading: Isolated restore and recovery order
checks.text: INF-REC-017 — Rehearse on an isolated fresh host or equivalent clean environment using actual documented tools, versions, keys, backups, and available credentials rather than cached source-server state.

checks.heading: Isolated restore and recovery order
checks.text: INF-REC-018 — Prevent restored jobs, webhooks, mail, payments, and external writes from running against production during rehearsal; isolate identities, endpoints, and recipients as well as networks.

checks.heading: Isolated restore and recovery order
checks.text: INF-REC-019 — Document restore order and prerequisites for accounts, network/firewalls, OS/runtime, control plane, keys, volumes, databases, apps, proxy, DNS, monitoring, and jobs.

checks.heading: Isolated restore and recovery order
checks.text: INF-REC-020 — Verify restored secrets can be used through safe functional checks, not secret printing; check decryption, credentials, image/source access, and remote-server identity after replacement.

checks.heading: Isolated restore and recovery order
checks.text: INF-REC-021 — Validate row/entity relationships, business invariants, uploaded files, permissions/tenants, application behavior, and version compatibility; row counts or a running dashboard alone are insufficient.

checks.heading: Isolated restore and recovery order
checks.text: INF-REC-022 — Measure actual restore and verification times, last recoverable committed state, external dependencies, and gaps against RPO/RTO; do not substitute schedule frequency for achieved RPO.

checks.heading: Isolated restore and recovery order
checks.text: INF-REC-023 — Reconcile data and external effects after restore, including queue replay, payment state, mail/webhook delivery, deleted accounts, and events newer than the recovered snapshot.

checks.heading: Isolated restore and recovery order
checks.text: INF-REC-024 — Establish one intended writer and scheduler/consumer owner before restoring service; prevent old/new hosts from concurrently performing consequential work.

checks.heading: Isolated restore and recovery order
checks.text: INF-REC-025 — Verify post-recovery DNS/TLS/routing, origin restrictions, alerts, new backups, and ordinary deployment operation; retain old evidence/assets until their recovery purpose ends.

checks.heading: Isolated restore and recovery order
checks.text: INF-REC-026 — Record rehearsal results, artifact/key references, actual versions, isolated cleanup, failures, owners, and next triggers without embedding recovery secrets in the report.

checks.heading: Incident containment and clean rebuild
checks.text: INF-REC-027 — Distinguish DNS/delegation failure, upstream network saturation, host outage, storage exhaustion, proxy/TLS failure, application failure, and suspected compromise using layer-specific evidence.

checks.heading: Incident containment and clean rebuild
checks.text: INF-REC-028 — Maintain an off-host incident sequence with authority, provider contacts, safe restrictions, legitimate-traffic checks, sanitized evidence preservation, and communication dependencies.

checks.heading: Incident containment and clean rebuild
checks.text: INF-REC-029 — For suspected compromise, plan controlled isolation and clean provisioning from trusted inputs; do not assume restoring the latest system snapshot removes persistence or compromised keys.

checks.heading: Incident containment and clean rebuild
checks.text: INF-REC-030 — Scope credential rotation to hosting, registrar, DNS, control plane, SSH, source/registry, app providers, database, and backups as affected; perform rotation from a trusted system with consumer sequencing.

checks.heading: Incident containment and clean rebuild
checks.text: INF-REC-031 — Assess backup contamination and select a defensible recovery point; preserve necessary incident evidence separately and validate repaired data/financial consequences.

checks.heading: Incident containment and clean rebuild
checks.text: INF-REC-032 — Complete post-incident review, permanent fixes, risk/ownership updates, and focused rechecks; report unknown compromise scope or unverified restore as an unresolved gap.

checks.heading: Detection and operating ownership
checks.text: INF-OPS-001 — Monitor external DNS, TLS, HTTP/application journeys, control-plane access, host health, and dependency health separately; a running container or ping response is not product availability.

checks.heading: Detection and operating ownership
checks.text: INF-OPS-002 — Check CPU/steal, memory/OOM, swap, disk bytes/inodes, I/O, bandwidth, connection tracking, file descriptors, queue age, and relevant provider quotas against actual failure risks.

checks.heading: Detection and operating ownership
checks.text: INF-OPS-003 — Keep monitoring and alert reception sufficiently independent of the VPS, hosted DNS/mail, and critical identity dependencies to detect their failure.

checks.heading: Detection and operating ownership
checks.text: INF-OPS-004 — Verify alert delivery, thresholds, recovery notices, ownership, and escalation with bounded evidence; avoid noisy alerts that are never acted upon.

checks.heading: Detection and operating ownership
checks.text: INF-OPS-005 — Maintain useful correlation/time synchronization across edge, proxy, host, containers, jobs, and provider logs without recording unnecessary secrets or private payloads.

checks.heading: Detection and operating ownership
checks.text: INF-OPS-006 — Bound log/metric/trace retention, label cardinality, disk use, access, and export costs; logging must not become the cause of storage exhaustion or a privacy leak.

checks.heading: Detection and operating ownership
checks.text: INF-OPS-007 — Detect drift in firewall attachment, listeners, DNS, routes, memberships, credentials, images, volumes, and backup status against an owned configuration source.

checks.heading: Detection and operating ownership
checks.text: INF-OPS-008 — Assign routine patch/reboot, certificate/credential renewal, capacity, backup/restore, domain/billing, and incident responsibilities; cadence should reflect actual risk.

checks.heading: Lockout-safe change and updates
checks.text: INF-OPS-009 — Record current/desired configuration, affected hosts/apps, scope, prerequisites, owner, maintenance window, success metrics, and stop/rollback triggers before consequential changes.

checks.heading: Lockout-safe change and updates
checks.text: INF-OPS-010 — Establish a verified alternate admin/rescue path and known-good configuration before changing SSH, routing, VPN, provider firewall, or host network policy.

checks.heading: Lockout-safe change and updates
checks.text: INF-OPS-011 — Sequence add/validate/restrict/remove where appropriate so the new path is proven before the old one is retired; avoid combining unrelated access changes that obscure recovery.

checks.heading: Lockout-safe change and updates
checks.text: INF-OPS-012 — Validate configuration syntax/version compatibility and persistent versus runtime state using supported methods before reload/restart; do not deploy unreviewed generic hardening commands.

checks.heading: Lockout-safe change and updates
checks.text: INF-OPS-013 — Include Docker/Coolify/proxy updates, OS/kernel reboots, and dependency changes in the recovery plan; code/image rollback may not reverse data/config migrations.

checks.heading: Lockout-safe change and updates
checks.text: INF-OPS-014 — Recheck administrative, web, database, webhook, streaming, backup, DNS, certificate, and monitoring paths affected by the change, including legitimate denied/allowed outcomes.

checks.heading: Lockout-safe change and updates
checks.text: INF-OPS-015 — Remove temporary broad rules, test hostnames, tokens, preview containers, debug listeners, and bypasses after their purpose ends; verify cleanup without deleting required evidence/recovery assets.

checks.heading: Lockout-safe change and updates
checks.text: INF-OPS-016 — Record actual result, changed version/config, rollback/forward repair if used, residual risk, and handover; planned success is not a verified completed change.

checks.heading: Availability and topology
checks.text: INF-OPS-017 — Identify single points in host, control plane, proxy, DNS authority, identity, registry, backups, region, and human ownership; compare with agreed availability/recovery requirements.

checks.heading: Availability and topology
checks.text: INF-OPS-018 — Distinguish a multi-host management dashboard from a tested highly available application/control plane; document which components actually fail over.

checks.heading: Availability and topology
checks.text: INF-OPS-019 — For multiple replicas/hosts, verify shared sessions/uploads, database authority, queue/cron ownership, cache/limit scope, health routing, and consistent configuration.

checks.heading: Availability and topology
checks.text: INF-OPS-020 — For failover, validate IP/DNS movement, certificate identity, provider policy attachment, private routing, replication lag, stale readers, and prevention of split writers.

checks.heading: Availability and topology
checks.text: INF-OPS-021 — Ensure spare/replacement capacity and recovery transfer time match the target; theoretical failover without deployable resources or usable credentials is a gap.

checks.heading: Availability and topology
checks.text: INF-OPS-022 — For remote/build servers, test intended behavior during controller loss, SSH failure, registry outage, failed builds, and reconnection without assuming running apps require a healthy dashboard.

checks.heading: Workload and deployment profiles
checks.text: INF-OPS-023 — For shared multi-project VPSs, check cross-project network/volume/secret access, resource fairness, build/backup contention, and the maximum acceptable host-wide blast radius.

checks.heading: Workload and deployment profiles
checks.text: INF-OPS-024 — For preview/staging environments, isolate data/credentials/recipients and public access, label owners/expiry, and remove orphaned resources and DNS safely.

checks.heading: Workload and deployment profiles
checks.text: INF-OPS-025 — For external/managed databases, verify private/TLS routing, egress addresses/allowlists, pools, region latency, credentials, backups, and provider outage behavior.

checks.heading: Workload and deployment profiles
checks.text: INF-OPS-026 — For local SQLite/file-backed stores, check actual persistent path, concurrent writer limits, permissions, backup consistency, and behavior on redeploy/recreation.

checks.heading: Workload and deployment profiles
checks.text: INF-OPS-027 — For object/NFS/shared storage, verify mounts, identity, encryption, permissions, locking/consistency semantics, outage behavior, backup, and deletion/recovery expectations.

checks.heading: Workload and deployment profiles
checks.text: INF-OPS-028 — For game/voice/VPN/mail/DNS workloads, audit non-HTTP ports, protocols, clients, upstream protection, and provider restrictions without assuming the web proxy secures them.

checks.heading: Workload and deployment profiles
checks.text: INF-OPS-029 — For tunnels/private-only origins, review connector/device enrollment, credentials, access policy, routing, resolution, recovery, and whether a direct public bypass still exists.

checks.heading: Workload and deployment profiles
checks.text: INF-OPS-030 — For IPv6-only, NAT-constrained, or mixed-architecture hosts, verify package/image/provider compatibility, outbound dependencies, published services, and real client reachability.

checks.heading: Workload and deployment profiles
checks.text: INF-OPS-031 — For high-volume transfers, streaming, or AI workloads, check proxy buffering/timeouts, temporary storage, egress, concurrency, worker lifetime, and expensive-feature shutdown.

checks.heading: Workload and deployment profiles
checks.text: INF-OPS-032 — For sensitive or regulated workloads, record applicable data location/access/retention requirements and accountable specialists; this general infrastructure checklist cannot establish compliance.

checks.heading: Migration and retirement
checks.text: INF-OPS-033 — Before provider/IP/DNS moves, map source/destination authority, records, secrets, certificates, allowlists, callbacks, jobs, data, and rollback constraints; use module 17 for the full cutover.

checks.heading: Migration and retirement
checks.text: INF-OPS-034 — Preserve supported old paths during cache/consumer transition while preventing duplicate writers/jobs; reversing DNS alone is not data-safe rollback.

checks.heading: Migration and retirement
checks.text: INF-OPS-035 — Retire old instances, IPs, volumes, snapshots, DNS, tokens, tunnels, deployments, and paid services only after dependency, retention, recovery, and observation requirements are satisfied.

checks.heading: Migration and retirement
checks.text: INF-OPS-036 — Have another maintainer follow the operating/recovery instructions and document gaps; finish with owned findings, verified controls, unresolved evidence, and explicit review triggers.

checks.heading: Provider accounts and administrative access
checks.text: INF-CORE-001 — Protect hosting, registrar, DNS, source control, registry, and backup accounts with available MFA, controlled ownership, scoped tokens, and externally stored recovery methods. Verify domain/service renewal and payment-failure notifications.

checks.heading: Provider accounts and administrative access
checks.text: INF-CORE-002 — Use individual SSH keys and a documented administrative path. Validate key access and the provider console/rescue recovery path before disabling password or root login, changing ports, or narrowing firewall rules.

checks.heading: Provider accounts and administrative access
checks.text: INF-CORE-003 — Separate routine operator accounts from automation credentials. If Coolify needs elevated access, document the actual sudo/Docker powers; a non-root account with broad elevation is still privileged.

checks.heading: Provider accounts and administrative access
checks.text: INF-CORE-004 — Restrict SSH to necessary administrator/VPN and Coolify-controller sources, including a separate controller if used. Avoid assuming the user's home IP is the only legitimate SSH source.

checks.heading: Provider accounts and administrative access
checks.text: INF-CORE-005 — Review stale users, keys, access logs, and suspicious authentication. Optional intrusion-blocking tools complement key access and perimeter controls; they do not replace upstream mitigation.

checks.heading: Effective firewall and public ports
checks.text: INF-CORE-006 — Configure the actual provider perimeter and host/container filtering together. Contabo's documented firewall blocks inbound traffic unless allowed and does not restrict outbound traffic; verify attachment to the correct instance and effective address-family coverage. [Contabo firewall](https://help.contabo.com/en/support/solutions/articles/103000390430-firewall-what-is-it-and-how-does-it-protect-my-vps-vds-)

checks.heading: Effective firewall and public ports
checks.text: INF-CORE-007 — Inventory listeners and Docker-published ports against approved services. Ordinary UFW rules may not filter Docker-published ports because Docker routes this traffic before UFW's normal chains. Use the provider perimeter or an appropriately supported Docker-aware policy and verify externally. Do not disable Docker's firewall integration blindly. [Docker firewall behavior](https://docs.docker.com/engine/network/packet-filtering-firewalls/)

checks.heading: Effective firewall and public ports
checks.text: INF-CORE-008 — Identify the deployed iptables/nftables backend and maintain compatible rules. Do not assume a rule intended for one backend or forwarding chain works on another.

checks.heading: Effective firewall and public ports
checks.text: INF-CORE-009 — Verify IPv4 and IPv6 independently, including AAAA records, public interfaces, container exposure, and any private/VPN route. Do not accidentally create an unfiltered IPv6 bypass.

checks.heading: Effective firewall and public ports
checks.text: INF-CORE-010 — Keep databases, Redis/caches, internal APIs, Docker API/socket, debug ports, and metrics endpoints private unless a justified integration explicitly requires protected access.

checks.heading: Effective firewall and public ports
checks.text: INF-CORE-011 — Do not open inbound TCP/UDP 53 merely because the apps use DNS. Outbound DNS resolution and serving DNS are different. If deliberately hosting DNS, separately verify authoritative/resolver role, restricted recursion, and flood/amplification defenses.

checks.heading: Effective firewall and public ports
checks.text: INF-CORE-012 — Preserve required outbound resolution, time sync, updates, certificate flows, provider APIs, and backup uploads. Where outbound restrictions are used, test them and account for dynamic provider endpoints.

checks.heading: Coolify and container separation
checks.text: INF-CORE-013 — Treat Coolify as a privileged control plane. Protect its dashboard with HTTPS, verified authentication/MFA capabilities, limited membership, and an appropriate VPN/private-access or identity-gateway boundary. Closing direct ports alone does not restrict the dashboard domain. [Coolify security model](https://coolify.io/docs/core/security-model)

checks.heading: Coolify and container separation
checks.text: INF-CORE-014 — Verify necessary machine webhooks and automation still function through any administrative access gateway. Authenticate endpoints; avoid globally bypassing dashboard protection to make callbacks work.

checks.heading: Coolify and container separation
checks.text: INF-CORE-015 — Scope Git/registry/deployment tokens and stored SSH keys; review user invitations, administrative sessions, API tokens, deploy hooks, and audit records.

checks.heading: Coolify and container separation
checks.text: INF-CORE-016 — Separate production/staging, credentials, volumes, and container networks. Check whether apps can reach another project's database or files; do not rely on project labels alone for isolation.

checks.heading: Coolify and container separation
checks.text: INF-CORE-017 — Avoid privileged app containers, unnecessary capabilities, host namespace use, Docker socket mounts, and broad host mounts. Apply non-root execution, resource limits, and filesystem restrictions where compatible. Isolate higher-risk workloads on separate hosts when shared-host risk is unacceptable.

checks.heading: Coolify and container separation
checks.text: INF-CORE-018 — Budget CPU, memory, disk, inodes, logs, build cache, I/O, database pools, and worker concurrency per project. Rehearse a deploy/build while other apps are serving traffic.

checks.heading: Coolify and container separation
checks.text: INF-CORE-019 — Keep OS, Docker, proxy, Coolify, and images patched. Plan security update/reboot windows and verify restart policies, health checks, graceful shutdown, and service recovery.

checks.heading: DNS TLS and origin protection
checks.text: INF-CORE-020 — Inventory A/AAAA/CNAME/MX/TXT/CAA records, nameservers, TTLs, credentials, wildcard records, and stale/dangling references. Record ownership and change/expiry monitoring.

checks.heading: DNS TLS and origin protection
checks.text: INF-CORE-021 — Enable and validate DNSSEC where supported; ensure the registrar DS record matches the authoritative provider. Rehearse DNS provider changes to avoid stale delegation breaking resolution. [DNSSEC activation](https://developers.cloudflare.com/registrar/get-started/enable-dnssec/)

checks.heading: DNS TLS and origin protection
checks.text: INF-CORE-022 — If using an edge proxy, confirm the intended web records are actually proxied and audit DNS-only records, mail services, and historical IP exposure. Test a known origin IP with the real Host/SNI; it should not bypass the intended edge restrictions.

checks.heading: DNS TLS and origin protection
checks.text: INF-CORE-023 — Choose an origin design: allowlisted trusted ingress with suitable origin authentication, or an outbound tunnel where appropriate. Account for health checks, callbacks, certificate renewal, range updates, and IPv6. Shared proxy IP ranges alone do not prove that a request belongs to your specific site/account. [Origin protection options](https://developers.cloudflare.com/fundamentals/security/protect-your-origin-server/)

checks.heading: DNS TLS and origin protection
checks.text: INF-CORE-024 — Encrypt and authenticate edge-to-origin traffic. For Cloudflare use a correctly configured Full (strict) equivalent with a valid trusted origin certificate; verify renewal and certificate compatibility with any direct access. [Cloudflare Full strict TLS](https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/origin-configuration/ssl-modes/full-strict/)

checks.heading: DNS TLS and origin protection
checks.text: INF-CORE-025 — Reject unintended Host values/default routes and secure proxy forwarding. Trust client-IP/protocol headers only from verified proxy hops and prevent spoofed headers affecting limits, logs, redirects, or secure cookies.

checks.heading: DNS TLS and origin protection
checks.text: INF-CORE-026 — Validate HTTPS redirects, renewal automation, WebSockets, SSE/AI streaming, upload limits, and sensible route-specific timeouts. Apply HSTS only after validating its hostname/subdomain scope.

checks.heading: Bad traffic and operational defenses
checks.text: INF-CORE-027 — Select WAF/rate/bot controls based on actual plan capabilities and observed traffic. Combine edge controls with server-side per-user/tenant limits, global budgets, and bounded expensive jobs under 08.

checks.heading: Bad traffic and operational defenses
checks.text: INF-CORE-028 — Test that rules do not break login, APIs, signed webhooks, search indexing, uploads, or accessibility. Use documented verification exceptions instead of blanket challenges on machine clients.

checks.heading: Bad traffic and operational defenses
checks.text: INF-CORE-029 — Prevent slow/oversized requests and connection exhaustion with bounded request bodies, connections, and appropriate timeouts. Keep streaming/long jobs on explicitly supported paths.

checks.heading: Bad traffic and operational defenses
checks.text: INF-CORE-030 — Monitor edge versus origin requests, errors, latency, bandwidth, connection counts, CPU/RAM, disk, queue age, authentication failures, and billing signals. Place uptime/alert reception outside this VPS.

checks.heading: Bad traffic and operational defenses
checks.text: INF-CORE-031 — Define controlled abuse suspension, emergency rate tightening, and expensive-feature shutdown. Operators need a safe rollback for false positives.

checks.heading: Recovery and incident readiness
checks.text: INF-CORE-032 — Back up Coolify configuration/state independently from app databases, uploads, volumes, and other persistent data. Preserve the instance APP_KEY securely outside the server; a database backup cannot recover encrypted stored secrets without the key. Never print it into audit logs. [Coolify instance backup](https://coolify.io/docs/core/backup-and-recovery/instance-backup)

checks.heading: Recovery and incident readiness
checks.text: INF-CORE-033 — Verify engine-specific application backup/restore support, off-site destinations, freshness, retention, encryption, and alerts. Coolify backup support differs by database type; use native procedures where needed. [Database backups](https://coolify.io/docs/databases/backups), [database restoration](https://coolify.io/docs/databases/restore)

checks.heading: Recovery and incident readiness
checks.text: INF-CORE-034 — Rehearse restoring onto an isolated fresh host or equivalent environment. Restore control plane, keys, networks, apps, databases, files, and jobs in a documented order; measure RPO/RTO and inspect real application behavior.

checks.heading: Recovery and incident readiness
checks.text: INF-CORE-035 — Prepare an incident sequence: identify network/DNS/web/application symptoms, contact the relevant upstream provider, apply proportionate restrictions, preserve sanitized evidence, suspend expensive work, and assess compromise. A compromised host may require clean rebuild and credential rotation rather than an in-place restart.

checks.heading: Recovery and incident readiness
checks.text: INF-CORE-036 — During mitigation check legitimate traffic and shared-project effects; after recovery review the cause, data/financial consequences, and remaining controls. Keep the runbook and contacts available off-host.
